issues.title: Standardize B.U.N.N.Y. diagnostics and evaluate local logs and traces
issues.body:
## Diagnose B.U.N.N.Y. with consistent logs and connected request traces

- Establish one shared format for every owned component.
- Evaluate Pino and OpenTelemetry on one synthetic command route.
- Use Grafana locally to inspect the evaluation evidence.
- Expand only after the evaluation supports the chosen approach.
- Keep remaining component coverage visible until it is delivered.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can investigate B.U.N.N.Y. through shared log and trace fields, beginning with the explicitly selected Pino/OpenTelemetry evaluation and then covering all owned components. This parent tracks the complete source outcome; completion of the pilot alone cannot close it. One operator, the current Linux/WSL development setup, and existing configured-component architecture are the operating assumptions.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required children, in input order:

1. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/703 defines the versioned shared record and trace profile and proves TypeScript/Python compatibility.
2. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/704 consumes that artifact and evaluates one synthetic hub-to-controller operation with local Grafana inspection.
3. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/705 consumes a supported evaluation and coordinates repository-owned adoption across the full inventory.

The native child relationship expresses parent acceptance; blocked-by links express contract -> pilot -> adoption required inputs. No phase, commitment, priority, dates or Project membership are assigned by this plan. Existing #425 content capture, #504 assistant evaluation and Pixoo #114 build identity remain separate related work and are not new prerequisites.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one state owner and one device writer; retain authentication, Origin checks, queues, request identities, no automatic write retries, and truthful uncertain outcomes. Telemetry is best-effort diagnostic evidence, never admission authority, an audit ledger, a replay source, or proof of physical success. Preserve journal retention and silent bounded fail-open hooks. Exclude credentials, tokens, request/response bodies, transcripts, prompts, media, session titles, private paths and raw URLs by default; the separate content policy in [Hub #425](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/425) does not implicitly enable telemetry capture. No installation, personal configuration, live state migration, model spending or physical device calls are authorized by this planning record.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] All three required child outcomes are accepted with their own evidence, and the final adoption inventory has no unresolved required producer coverage.
- [ ] One shared query vocabulary retrieves the same semantic fields across the covered components; logs correlate to available spans without inventing missing context or physical success.
- [ ] The pilot records actual safety/query/overhead results and its proceed/revise/stop recommendation. Refuted or inconclusive results retain unfinished adoption work and prevent false parent completion.
- [ ] Native relationships and consumer ownership are read back and reconciled at child completion or changed prerequisites. Source, installed, client, physical and viewer evidence remain distinct.

Delivery target: source contracts, synthetic evaluation and source adoption. No installation or permanent observability backend is approved by this plan. The child evidence, not a parent checklist alone, establishes acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

Always-running hosting, remote/cloud export, alerts, continuous profiling, session replay and LLM prompt/response capture are not required for this source outcome. Revisit only when the measured pilot or an actual diagnostic need warrants them. The existing work guide is not regenerated or publicly published by tracker planning.

## Work assessment

Complexity high: shared contract plus coordinated consumer adoption. Uncertainty medium for the first evaluation and high for the later rollout until the pilot reports. Impact high: shared privacy and command-evidence boundaries. Readiness: parent backlog; start only the ready contract child. Alignment: aligned with the owner-selected tools and shared-form requirement, current Hub architecture and independent related work. This parent is coordination, not permission to deliver every child in one session.

Planning baseline: Hub `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` (remote main read 2026-10-01); [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/architecture.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/sdlc.md), controller/lifecycle contracts, owning package guides and current related tracker reads. The local checkout is older; planning used remote-main files without changing the checkout. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated). All checks below are planned, not executed.

## Guide

**Topic:** hosting-migrations

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Child delivery evidence and the pilot disposition. This parent has no single implementation session; each ready leaf carries its own two-host recommendation.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** Shared telemetry crosses language, process, privacy and command-evidence boundaries. Contract fixtures, consumer checks and negative cases govern acceptance; source evidence does not establish installed coverage.
**Reassess when:** The contract, component inventory, privacy policy, upstream instrumentation compatibility or pilot result changes.

issues.title: Adopt the shared diagnostic contract across B.U.N.N.Y. components
issues.body:
## Give every B.U.N.N.Y.-owned runtime the same queryable diagnostics

- Apply the accepted contract after the first evaluation supports adoption.
- Cover the hub, dashboard, shared libraries and local controllers.
- Include Pixoo and Nanoleaf through their existing repository owners.
- Keep hooks silent and device writes in their current queues.
- Track source coverage separately from installed and physical evidence.

## Outcome and real setup

Parent: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/706

Complete source adoption across the current B.U.N.N.Y. component inventory. This coordinating backlog item remains blocked and requires bounded repository-owned child stories after the pilot results are accepted; it is not ready for blanket implementation. New components must consume the same contract or an explicitly reviewed version extension.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/703 and a supported https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/704 result. Preserve one coordinating writer for common artifacts and one owner per repository deliverable. The shared contract stays Hub-owned. Pixoo and Nanoleaf consume versioned artifacts rather than local source imports; create/refine their implementation children in their own repositories at refinement, after fresh instructions, current main, seam and ownership reads.

Required inventory and adoption boundaries:

| Component group | Required coverage and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Hub HTTP/MCP and background services | Request/admission/dispatch/outcome, startup/shutdown, automation/moments and feed reconnect/freshness; Hub owner |
| Shared MCP, agent-state, agent-status and contract libraries | Host-injected/no-op instrumentation and shared scope names; keep reducers/pure validation deterministic, add no autonomous exporter |
| Provider hooks and adapters | Preserve silent bounded fail-open behavior; report allowlisted ingestion/rejection/health through the receiving owner where hooks cannot safely emit; no transcript reader for telemetry |
| Local controller host, LIFX and Tidbyt runners | Admission, queue wait/execution, transport and typed receipt; preserve one designated writer and cloud/LAN boundaries; no per-frame INFO flood |
| Dashboard | Bounded operation/error diagnostics and correlation with its authenticated hub; no browser exporter credentials, raw DOM/user text, blanket console capture or session replay; qualify browser transport separately |
| Pixoo backend and owned UI/worker processes | Common fields across media/player/monitor/controller boundaries; source-owned admission and receipt identity preserved; Pixoo repository owns changes |
| Nanoleaf Python bridge/worker and owned wall UI | Matching Python JSON/OTLP mapping, explicit context handoff across threads/queues, epoch/source and scene restoration evidence; Nanoleaf repository owns changes |
| Owned executable helpers and diagnostic tooling | Inventory includes startup, verification and maintenance helpers that emit operational records; normalize those records, while test-runner/compiler output remains external tooling output |

Do not force pure functions to manufacture telemetry or claim collection from external Codex/Claude internals, third-party tools, vendor services or firmware. Record these boundaries explicitly in the coverage inventory. A record emitted on behalf of another component must retain observed-versus-source identity and provenance.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one state owner and one device writer; retain authentication, Origin checks, queues, request identities, no automatic write retries, and truthful uncertain outcomes. Telemetry is best-effort diagnostic evidence, never admission authority, an audit ledger, a replay source, or proof of physical success. Preserve journal retention and silent bounded fail-open hooks. Exclude credentials, tokens, request/response bodies, transcripts, prompts, media, session titles, private paths and raw URLs by default; the separate content policy in [Hub #425](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/425) does not implicitly enable telemetry capture. No installation, personal configuration, live state migration, model spending or physical device calls are authorized by this planning record.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] After pilot acceptance, refresh each repository's main/instructions and create non-overlapping child work with exact seams, packaging pins, acceptance and current validation commands. Record required inputs separately from shared-file coordination and preferred ordering. Implementation remains blocked until those children are ready.
- [ ] The inventory accounts for every owned executable and shared library: adopted, pure/no-op with a justified host boundary, or still outstanding with an owning child. No executable diagnostic producer silently uses an incompatible second format. Required outstanding work prevents this item closing.
- [ ] TypeScript, Python and browser-owned producers pass the shared conformance cases. Representative multi-component queries find service/event/outcome/ticket/trace fields using identical semantics, including a mixed-version transition and a Python queue handoff.
- [ ] Relevant consumer regression checks verify redaction, concurrent context isolation, telemetry outages, bounded retention/volume, restart and no duplicated device effects. Device-facing transport tests remain fake; no physical-success claim is inferred.
- [ ] Each child supplies actual source/CI evidence. The coordinator reconciles the parent against its own coverage criteria and records source adoption separately from installed runtime, live client and physical evidence.

Planned validation: shared contract conformance and packaging checks plus each owning package's current development/CI commands, refreshed during child refinement. Dashboard modifications also require its existing browser checks; actual visible UI changes retain current-candidate human approval under the owning policy. Privacy/concurrency review is mandatory coverage within independent reviews. No specific future command is represented as existing or executed.

Delivery target: source adoption in the owned repositories. Installing on the personal system requires a separately selected owner and explicit authorization; a source-complete inventory is not an installed-coverage claim.

## Meaningful deferrals

Detailed consumer implementation is deliberately deferred until the pilot identifies working adapters and their limits. Existing local logs/receipts remain the manual alternative meanwhile. Actual runtime installation, always-running storage/retention and remote access remain separate decisions. Planned PC-lighting and later assistant/voice/device components adopt this contract when their own executable slices are defined; no speculative platform adapter is required now. [Hub #504](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/504) keeps LLM evaluation separate.

## Work assessment

Complexity high: multiple languages, queues and separately owned repositories. Uncertainty high: accepted adapter behavior and fresh consumer implementation boundaries depend on the pilot. Impact high: privacy and async context across the device command path. Readiness: blocked, not implementation-ready; refine repository-owned children after a supported pilot. Alignment: aligned at the Hub architecture/ownership level; detailed Pixoo/Nanoleaf implementation alignment remains pending their child refinement. Reassess on pilot disposition and inventory changes.

Planning baseline: Hub `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` (remote main read 2026-10-01); [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/architecture.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/sdlc.md), controller/lifecycle contracts, owning package guides and current related tracker reads. The local checkout is older; planning used remote-main files without changing the checkout. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated). All checks below are planned, not executed.

## Guide

**Topic:** hosting-migrations


## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Accepted contract/artifact and pilot result, then current repository-specific implementation scopes and owner handoffs. Recommend both-host execution settings per child after those inputs exist; do not launch this umbrella as a single delivery.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** Shared telemetry crosses language, process, privacy and command-evidence boundaries. Contract fixtures, consumer checks and negative cases govern acceptance; source evidence does not establish installed coverage.
**Reassess when:** The contract, component inventory, privacy policy, upstream instrumentation compatibility or pilot result changes.

issues.title: Evaluate Pino and OpenTelemetry on one synthetic hub-to-controller route
issues.body:
## Follow one command from the hub to a controller in local logs and traces

- Use the shared diagnostic contract with Pino and OpenTelemetry.
- Exercise a fake controller through the hub using synthetic data.
- Inspect correlated logs and timing in Grafana’s development bundle.
- Check rejection, uncertain timeout and telemetry-outage behavior.
- Measure overhead and record whether broader adoption should proceed.

## Outcome and real setup

Parent: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/706

Produce repeatable evidence that standard logs/traces help one operator diagnose the existing hub-to-controller command path. Run an isolated Linux/WSL development harness with synthetic credentials, disposable state, a fake controller and a pinned `grafana/otel-lgtm` development image. This is a source evaluation, not an installed daily-use service or a backend-production recommendation.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required input: reviewed, packaged https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/703. Start from `apps/hub/tests/fake-controller.mjs` and existing hub controller/MCP fixtures. Select one existing brightness command with its actual ticket semantics; no physical network target. Instrument the hub HTTP boundary, controller client, fake controller queue/execution and terminal receipt. Use Pino structured logs, manual OTel spans and narrowly selected HTTP/Undici instrumentation. Qualify Node 24 ESM startup order and exact package versions; do not assume stable OTel tracing makes every instrumentation package stable.

Use the shared log adapter for JSON output and trace correlation; route logs through one Collector ingestion path and spans through OTLP. Disable a duplicate Pino-to-OTel sending path. Pin the image and Collector mapping configuration. Bind published listeners to loopback; use synthetic resources only. Keep persistent test output under ignored disk-backed `.local/`, preserve final evidence in the main checkout, and clean only resources owned by the run. Do not alter a system Docker installation, runtime service, personal environment, device or global log configuration. Missing execution prerequisites leave the run pending.

Provide executable query checks and accompanying Grafana Explore instructions for service, operation, severity, outcome, command ticket and trace ID. Use the existing viewer; a new custom dashboard or product UI is outside this slice. No automatic agent session launch, remote model call or tracing of third-party internal work.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one state owner and one device writer; retain authentication, Origin checks, queues, request identities, no automatic write retries, and truthful uncertain outcomes. Telemetry is best-effort diagnostic evidence, never admission authority, an audit ledger, a replay source, or proof of physical success. Preserve journal retention and silent bounded fail-open hooks. Exclude credentials, tokens, request/response bodies, transcripts, prompts, media, session titles, private paths and raw URLs by default; the separate content policy in [Hub #425](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/425) does not implicitly enable telemetry capture. No installation, personal configuration, live state migration, model spending or physical device calls are authorized by this planning record.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Success, rejected admission, duplicate ticket, concurrent operations, queued work and a timeout after fake write admission produce contract-valid logs/spans. Log-to-trace lookup finds the expected operation and service, with no cross-request context leak or second fake side effect.
- [ ] Canonical fields survive Pino -> local JSON -> Collector -> Loki and OTLP -> Tempo. The same query keys find the cross-language contract fixture; no language-specific message parser is required. Backend IDs/labels do not create unbounded streams.
- [ ] Paused/absent Collector, bounded-queue saturation, exporter errors and shutdown preserve command results and existing service timeouts; safe drop/failure evidence is observable. Bounded shutdown must finish without an indefinite exporter flush.
- [ ] Negative fixtures place secrets/private values in payloads, headers, URL queries and thrown errors. Neither local captured logs nor exported records contain them. Unknown context and malformed trace headers do not bypass authentication or change admission.
- [ ] Run the same bounded synthetic workload with telemetry disabled and enabled, with healthy and unavailable collection. Record p50/p95 request latency, throughput, process/collector CPU and RSS, dropped records, output bytes and shutdown duration with raw measurements, workload and versions. Use three paired measured runs per condition after warm-up; no unbounded tuning loop. Select explicit pass thresholds in the issue-linked design before running, grounded in existing host limits; evidence that misses them is refuted, not a pass.
- [ ] A reproducible report includes query results and viewer evidence, original failed attempts, resource cleanup proof, and a supported/refuted/inconclusive decision. Failure to execute Grafana is recorded as unexecuted, not replaced by unit-test claims. A positive result recommends adoption; a negative or inconclusive result blocks expansion pending a scoped revision or owner decision.

Use an issue-linked OpenSpec change and the owning repository's PR, independent Standards/Specification review and CI gates. Planned shared checks on Node 24: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`; use supported Python 3.12 or 3.14. Add any new telemetry test commands and package-consumer checks to `docs/development.md` and CI before implementing product behavior. Retain all additional owning-package checks required by the final diff.

Additionally plan `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package` and `npm run test:hub:mcp`; any shared MCP change adds `npm run test:mcp`, `npm run test:mcp:protocol`, `npm run test:mcp:package`. Register the new bounded evaluation entrypoint in development documentation and appropriate CI; it is not an existing command today. Use owned supervised app verification if an existing adapter fits; otherwise document and qualify this bounded harness through the project's procedure.

Delivery target: source plus isolated synthetic evaluation evidence. Installed-client and physical behavior remain unqualified.

## Meaningful deferrals

Broader instrumentation is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/705 and does not hold this evaluation open. The bundled Grafana image is documented for development/testing, not qualified as an always-running backend. Production retention, alerts, remote/cloud export, custom dashboards, profiling and LLM content inspection wait for a concrete need. Manual local queries are the initial operator workflow.

## Work assessment

Complexity medium: Node instrumentation, Collector mappings and a reproducible local query harness. Uncertainty medium: Node/ESM instrumentation and workload overhead require this bounded evaluation. Impact high: redaction and context propagation run next to authenticated command handling. Readiness: blocked on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/703; contract versions and pre-run performance thresholds must be frozen before evaluation. Alignment: aligned with the fake-controller boundary and current ownership/no-retry rules. No live installation is needed to answer this source-level question.

Planning baseline: Hub `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` (remote main read 2026-10-01); [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/architecture.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/sdlc.md), controller/lifecycle contracts, owning package guides and current related tracker reads. The local checkout is older; planning used remote-main files without changing the checkout. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated). All checks below are planned, not executed.

## Guide

**Topic:** hosting-migrations


## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot. Claude Code: Opus at high effort; Codex: Sol 6.1 at high reasoning. Paste the matching host prompt after required inputs are accepted.
**Work surface:** Backend

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol 6.1 (`gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Astra (`gpt-6-astra`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: installed policy checked 2026-10-01; verify alias, high effort and reviewer inheritance in Claude Code at pickup. | Verified: current Codex tool schema exposes gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra and high reasoning on 2026-10-01; starting-session access remains a pickup check. |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
Required input: reviewed, packaged https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/703. Start from `apps/hub/tests/fake-controller.mjs` and existing hub controller/MCP fixtures. Select one existing brightness command with its actual ticket semantics; no physical network target. Instrument the hub HTTP boundary, controller client, fake controller queue/execution and terminal receipt. Use Pino structured logs, manual OTel spans and narrowly selected HTTP/Undici instrumentation. Qualify Node 24 ESM startup order and exact package versions; do not assume stable OTel tracing makes every instrumentation package stable.

Use the shared log adapter for JSON output and trace correlation; route logs through one Collector ingestion path and spans through OTLP. Disable a duplicate Pino-to-OTel sending path. Keep persistent test output under ignored disk-backed `.local/`, preserve final evidence in the main checkout, and clean only resources owned by the run. issues.title: Define a shared observability contract for B.U.N.N.Y. logs and traces
issues.body:
## Query every B.U.N.N.Y. component using the same diagnostic fields

- Define one versioned log format and one trace attribute vocabulary.
- Map TypeScript and Python records to the same OpenTelemetry fields.
- Correlate activity using trace IDs and the existing command identities.
- Keep private content out and bound telemetry failures.
- Prove the format with shared fixtures before instrumenting services.

## Outcome and real setup

Parent: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/706

One operator can query the same fields across B.U.N.N.Y.-owned services and correlate logs with traces. This is the common contract for the hub, MCP, state/status packages, local controller host, Tidbyt/LIFX runners, dashboard, Pixoo and Nanoleaf. Third-party software and device firmware remain external; their allowlisted boundary observations use this contract without claiming access to their internals. Pure libraries inherit the host's resource identity and open no exporter or listener.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: none. This produces the reviewed contract and language fixtures consumed by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/704 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/705. Use a small shared observability artifact with TypeScript/Python types, validation and conversion helpers, following existing private-package conventions. Keep exporter startup in executable hosts. Final package/path choices belong in the issue-linked design; do not turn logging into a new service framework.

Define a concrete B.U.N.N.Y. profile of the [OpenTelemetry log data model](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/), [resource conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/resource/), [non-OTLP trace context](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/compatibility/logging_trace_context/) and [W3C Trace Context](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). Pin the semantic-convention version independently from the B.U.N.N.Y. schema version.

The contract must settle these fields and mappings:

- Canonical local output is UTF-8 NDJSON, one object per record. Common keys: `schema_version`, `timestamp`, `observed_timestamp` when applicable, `severity_number`, `severity_text`, `event_name`, `body`, `resource`, `scope`, `attributes`; optional valid `trace_id`, `span_id`, `trace_flags` appear at top level. Specify required/optional fields, primitive types, bounds, omission versus null, truncation/drop rules, and exact OTLP mappings. Raw default Pino and Python formats are not separate supported dialects.
- Local timestamps use a single UTC RFC3339 format at declared millisecond precision; OTLP conversion must preserve that precision without unsafe JavaScript nanosecond integers. Measure duration with each process's monotonic clock. Never derive cross-process durations by subtracting unrelated clocks. Preserve unknown source time and observed time separately.
- Use the same OTel severity values in both languages, with explicit Pino/Python mappings: TRACE 1, DEBUG 5, INFO 9, WARN 13, ERROR 17, FATAL 21. Severity and trace status are distinct from domain outcomes: denial, cancellation, partial delivery, transport acknowledgment and uncertainty retain their meanings.
- Resources use registered `service.namespace` (`bunny`), `service.name`, `service.version`, neutral `service.instance.id` and environment values. Preserve an authoritative available build identity; unknown stays unknown. Existing build metadata work, including [Pixoo #114](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/114), remains independent and is not duplicated or required just to emit logs.
- `scope` identifies the library/component. Registered stable event/span names describe operations, not IDs or user content. Domain attributes under `bunny.*` carry only typed, bounded approved metadata. Keep controller ID/device ID/source ID, request epoch/sequence, operation identity and state revision distinct. Map an application `request_id` separately from a controller ticket; no lossy generic request-ID replacement.
- Trace IDs and span IDs follow W3C/OTel encoding. Untraced logs remain valid and do not invent parents. Define short request spans, queue/execution spans, links for deferred work or lifecycle observations, and rules for background work/SSE/reconnects so a session is not one indefinitely open span. Async context cannot bleed across concurrent requests.
- Propagate only qualified trace context on authenticated owned service boundaries. Incoming trace context is untrusted metadata, never authorization. Define malformed/absent-header handling and external-destination suppression. Do not add fields to closed controller/lifecycle envelopes or send tracing headers to device/cloud vendor endpoints by default. No personal data in baggage; initially disable baggage propagation.
- Provide one documented ingestion path for each signal, field-to-query mappings, low-cardinality index/label choices, and log-to-trace links. Trace IDs, tickets, sessions and instance IDs are searchable metadata, not unbounded metric labels or Loki stream labels. Queries select fields, not free-text message parsing.
- Version the B.U.N.N.Y. profile and registered extensions. Unknown fields never silently become exported private content. State additive/breaking rules and explicit old/new projections for strict consumers; test mixed supported versions. Libraries have a no-op default, bounded work, no import-time I/O and no failure propagation into product behavior.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one state owner and one device writer; retain authentication, Origin checks, queues, request identities, no automatic write retries, and truthful uncertain outcomes. Telemetry is best-effort diagnostic evidence, never admission authority, an audit ledger, a replay source, or proof of physical success. Preserve journal retention and silent bounded fail-open hooks. Exclude credentials, tokens, request/response bodies, transcripts, prompts, media, session titles, private paths and raw URLs by default; the separate content policy in [Hub #425](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/425) does not implicitly enable telemetry capture. No installation, personal configuration, live state migration, model spending or physical device calls are authorized by this planning record.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A reviewed normative field dictionary, resource/event/span catalog, privacy allowlist and compatibility policy specify the mappings above. Contract review is accepted before dependent instrumentation consumes it.
- [ ] Shared positive/negative fixtures validate in TypeScript and Python and yield equivalent normalized records and OTLP fields. Cases include every severity, timestamp precision, valid/malformed IDs, missing context, unsupported versions, bounded extensions, oversize data and forbidden fields.
- [ ] Contract examples cover command admission/rejection, queue delay, success, timeout with uncertain write outcome, cancellation, lifecycle processing and process startup. They keep transport and physical proof separate.
- [ ] An executable synthetic query fixture finds the same operation across TypeScript/Python log records and corresponding trace identities without message parsing; mappings preserve names/types and avoid duplicate export.
- [ ] Packaged consumer tests verify immutable artifact use outside the source checkout; all affected existing contract consumers remain compatible. Document the component adoption inventory with status `not yet adopted`, owner and planned seam; a schema alone is not system coverage.
- [ ] Sanitization/conversion failures fail open with bounded, safe diagnostics; no secret or payload reaches either local output or export in negative fixtures. Independent reviewers explicitly cover privacy and context isolation.

Use an issue-linked OpenSpec change and the owning repository's PR, independent Standards/Specification review and CI gates. Planned shared checks on Node 24: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`; use supported Python 3.12 or 3.14. Add any new telemetry test commands and package-consumer checks to `docs/development.md` and CI before implementing product behavior. Retain all additional owning-package checks required by the final diff.

Delivery target: source-only contract, fixtures and packaged helpers. No installed service or physical acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

Runtime instrumentation and actual Grafana queries belong to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/704 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/705. Metrics/profiling conventions, hosted backends and LLM content/evaluation products are deferred until a concrete consumer needs them; this contract reserves no speculative data collection. No changes to durable domain journals or audit semantics.

## Work assessment

Complexity medium: shared schema, language mappings and exporter seams. Uncertainty medium: exact adapter/package compatibility is bounded by fixtures and design inspection. Impact high: a bad allowlist can disclose credentials or content across every consumer. Readiness: ready for source-only contract delivery, unselected. Alignment: aligned with current local ownership, strict contracts and private-artifact distribution; this is a new diagnostic profile, not a change to controller semantics. Search found no existing shared logging/tracing story; #425, #504 and Pixoo #114 retain separate scope.

Planning baseline: Hub `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` (remote main read 2026-10-01); [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/architecture.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/sdlc.md), controller/lifecycle contracts, owning package guides and current related tracker reads. issues.title: Define shared B.U.N.N.Y. event contracts and component responsibilities
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Define one shared event contract for B.U.N.N.Y.'s existing and future components on the current single-operator Windows/WSL installation. Components can publish their owned facts and consume other components' facts without inventing a new envelope, naming convention or reliability meaning at each integration. The contract remains usable from TypeScript and Python.

The owner accepted staged adoption, a B.U.N.N.Y. CloudEvents profile, an optional bounded Effect evaluation, latest-state status displays, and durable delivery for actionable notifications after confirmed durable acceptance. Reliable history and notification delivery remain separate capabilities.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use the Hub's existing ownership of shared contracts. Publish a language-neutral B.U.N.N.Y. profile of CloudEvents 1.0, typed payload schemas, TypeScript/Python validation fixtures and a current-interface inventory. CloudEvents is the envelope standard, not a selected broker, storage system or Effect runtime: https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md.

Internal tasks form one source-contract deliverable:

1. Define the envelope/profile rules: required `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `type`; profile-required schema/content metadata; typed `data`; stable retry identity; qualified correlation/causation references; known occurrence time versus observation/receipt time; ordering provenance; payload/version compatibility; finite bounds; privacy and authorization. Distinguish CloudEvents spec version, B.U.N.N.Y. profile version and payload schema version. A locally assigned record ID must not manufacture native provider identity or ordering evidence. CloudEvents context attributes have their own type limits; do not silently narrow existing safe-integer revisions.
2. Define three delivery classes. Current-state delivery may coalesce and recovers from the latest authoritative snapshot. Actionable notifications guarantee recoverable delivery only after explicit durable acceptance, tolerate duplicates, distinguish delivery acknowledgment from human acknowledgment, and remain recoverable until handled or explicitly expired. Time-sensitive effects have an explicit validity window and are not replayed after reconnect/restart. Declare retries, bounded capacity, saturation, expiry, observable failed/pending handling and deduplication scope; do not claim exactly-once delivery or lossless upstream hook capture.
3. issues.title: Verify daily activity measurements and a permitted companion response in the apartment
issues.body:
## Compare activity estimates with real apartment timings

- Start with couch-area measurements from mapped presence sensing.
- Compare kitchen and pacing estimates with manual reference intervals.
- Exercise guests, Yoshi, coverage gaps and moved furniture.
- Demonstrate one configured response and its suppression rules.
- Test future pressure or Bluetooth inputs only when acquired and selected.

## Outcome and real setup

Required installed/physical child of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/696. Prove staged real measurement accuracy and one complete observation→history→pattern/context→eligible companion response. Couch is the first independently runnable stage; kitchen/cooking and pacing are separate required measurement stages for this story's final acceptance, not blockers for the first couch observation.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required source inputs for the whole finish line: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/697, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/698 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/699, plus #634 qualified sensor/map definitions. Before each stage, verify only its inputs, pinned artifacts, exact sensors/targets/areas, named installation/trial owner, selected collection/retention/destinations, permitted effects and restoration/stop procedure. Select manual-reference tolerances, false-positive/missed-episode/coverage measures and response expectations before testing; do not invent an accuracy target. Reuse #643's trial discipline, not its whole robot/navigation dependency chain. Use an existing screen/endpoint where sufficient. #694 additions and exact robot/controller baselines are conditional on the selected trial targets; future hardware and navigation do not block the initial mapped-presence slice.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep observations, person association, activity inference, corrections, learned patterns and generated dialogue distinct. Missing/stale/disagreeing evidence means unknown; memory is not current location or command authority. Keep personal data private, with selected sources/destinations and inspect/correct/delete/export controls covering derived records. Reuse one authoritative owner per state domain and one designated device writer. #642's explicit hold on implementing ambient audio/video recording and passive transcription remains in force; structured sensor history does not release it. Manual written timestamps and device receipts are sufficient trial evidence; do not record ambient audio/video or passive transcripts. Physical sequence/installation authorization must explicitly name actual targets. Preserve manual takeover and restore the authorized baseline without replay.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Couch-stage manual reference covers sitting, standing nearby, zone entry/exit, boundary crossings, sensor/map movement, guests/Yoshi and dropout; report zone time separately from sitting and association confidence.
- [ ] AC2: Kitchen/cooking and pacing stages compare source estimates against independent manually labelled intervals, ordinary trips/non-cooking stays and unknown coverage. Each requested activity has supported/refuted/inconclusive findings and a next action; missing evidence remains unfinished.
- [ ] AC3: Compare measured error and coverage with preselected thresholds; a synthetic fixture or transport receipt cannot establish apartment accuracy. Any claimed seated cue also needs actual sitting qualification.
- [ ] AC4: At least one complete selected context/pattern/response trace shows one eligible endpoint, mode/override/snooze/call-media suppression, outage/uncertain send and restart with preserved history and no replay. Retain real elapsed-time evidence separately from accelerated clocks.
- [ ] AC5: If later pressure/Bluetooth sources are acquired and selected, compare against the presence-only baseline, including disagreement/dropout and a Bluetooth device left behind; unselected future hardware is not required to close the initial baseline scope.
- [ ] AC6: Close only after all three required measurement stages and the configured response meet accepted evidence or the owner explicitly revises the scope. Record versions, manual references, results/limitations, privacy/correction checks and restoration.

Delivery target: separately authorized installation and physical acceptance; no live work in planning.

These are planned checks, not executed evidence. Source delivery follows current AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: issue-linked OpenSpec, versioned interface definitions before consumers, package/consumer checks added to docs/development.md and CI, independent Standards and Specification review of the same committed comparison, applicable current-candidate UI approval, guarded PR merge and merged-main checks. No implementation, installation, live model spending, device activation or physical sequence is authorized by this planning update.

## Meaningful deferrals

Existing #633/#643 guest, relationship, TV and navigation stages retain their own finish lines. Future hardware remains conditional #694 scope. If sensor evidence cannot establish posture/cooking/pacing, report that limit and refine the producer instead of claiming accuracy; owner labels can demonstrate the query path but not automatic recognition.

## Work assessment

Complexity: high. Uncertainty: high. Impact: high for private movement history and activity-informed interaction. Status: backlog; not implementation-ready.

Missing: Pinned accepted source; qualified sensor/map and selected behavior; owner-selected accuracy/reference plan, exact targets, named owner and explicit installation/live-trial authorization.

Scope: one operator and the existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation. Prefer existing ingestion, personal memory, policy and authenticated query surfaces. No new platform, database technology, Project commitment or delivery order is selected. Reassess after accepted producer definitions, retention/activity decisions and selected hardware evidence. Planner reasoning setting is unknown. Planning baseline: 2026-10-01, live source/issues and owner-authorized North Star reconciliation.

issues.title: Learn revisable activity patterns and coordinate permitted companion responses
issues.body:
## Use activity patterns to choose helpful companion responses

- Learn revisable patterns from permitted activity history.
- Show the observations and coverage behind each pattern.
- Let corrections and deletions change what companions remember.
- Send response proposals through the existing companion policy.
- Use explicit feedback without treating silence as approval.

## Outcome and real setup

Required source child of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/696. Connect measured history to companion context and one owner-selected response behavior, using shared permitted knowledge while retaining companion personalities. Start with couch-history fixtures; cooking/pacing become consumers of the same boundary once https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/698 is accepted and need not block that first fixture.

## Smallest useful implementation

## Show how much supported time I spend in the couch area

- Map qualified presence readings to my couch footprint.

Select retention of samples/intervals/summaries and permitted model/query destinations. Use one existing authenticated query surface; a new dashboard is not required. issues.title: Give the Hub a saved mode and allow individual device overrides
issues.body:
## Choose one mode for the Hub, then make exceptions for individual devices

- Select Work, Free, or Quiet to request that mode from every participating device.
- Change one device's mode without changing the Hub or the other devices.
- Select a Hub mode again to replace all individual overrides.
- See each device's result, even when another device fails.
- Start in Free and remember later choices without sending commands on startup.

## Outcome and real setup

The Hub has its own selected mode. Devices normally use that selection, but the owner can give an individual device a different mode. A saved choice records what the owner requested; it does not prove a device has reached that mode.

The first delivery covers one operator, the existing Windows/WSL Hub, its dashboard and authenticated HTTP/MCP interfaces, and explicitly configured Nanoleaf lights and Pixoo displays. LIFX and companions join through their existing stories after this shared interface is available. This story does not require every device family to be implemented before it closes.

| What the owner does | Hub selection | Nanoleaf choice | Pixoo choice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Select Work in the Hub | Work | Work | Work |
| Set Nanoleaf individually to Free | Work | Free, individual override | Work |
| Restart the Hub | Work | Free, remembered | Work, remembered |
| Select Quiet in the Hub | Quiet | Quiet, override removed | Quiet |

These are saved choices. The restart row sends no commands. Device responses and fresh observations are separate evidence.

This fills the gap between https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67's explicit device requests and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635's companion behavior rules. This story owns selected-mode state; those stories must not create competing copies.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use the existing Hub process, private persistence boundary, authenticated routes, MCP composition, dashboard controls and controller clients. Keep one coordinating writer for this deliverable. Deliver one complete source story with these internal steps; layer-only steps are not separate completed features.

1. **Define and save choices (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6, AC8, AC10).** Define a versioned Hub-mode snapshot and guarded selection operations in issue-linked OpenSpec before coding. Store one Hub selection, optional per-participant overrides, revisions and bounded current request/result metadata. Distinguish first initialization from unreadable or damaged existing state. Seed Free once without commands; restore later choices without commands. Keep this state separate from coding-agent lifecycle state and private controller databases. Specify persistence/migration, duplicate identity, interruption and response-deadline behavior at this boundary before consuming it.
2. **Connect explicit requests (AC2-AC8).** Use #67's fixed mappings, controller clients and independent results. Once a valid Hub-wide request is admitted and its choices are saved, clear overrides and attempt every configured participant independently. An individual request saves only that participant's choice and sends only its command. Selecting the Hub's mode individually removes that participant's override. An explicit same-mode Hub reapply counts as a new selection and clears every override; refreshes, reconnects and duplicate submissions do not. Route dashboard, HTTP and MCP Hub-mode operations through one owner. Preserve #67's public compatibility while making its Hub-wide preset entry points delegate to this owner after this feature lands; do not leave a state-bypassing path.
3. **Expose controls and verify the complete journey (AC1-AC10).** Add the Hub selector and individual Work/Free/Quiet controls to existing dashboard surfaces. Reuse existing direct-selection interactions and command-status components. Read-only callers see permitted state without receiving controls. Show the Hub selection, individual exceptions, last request outcomes and native observations separately. Retain existing native controls and content/brightness behavior; a native observation alone cannot manufacture a Hub override. Supply HTTP/MCP snapshot access so a caller can inspect current choices and request evidence after a lost response without resending. Define the consumer interface for future companions and test it synthetically; do not implement companion behavior here.

Required source input: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67's delivered dispatcher, native API mapping, guards and result contract. Review that input before dependent implementation; issue closure alone is not compatibility evidence. No reverse dependency is introduced: #67 can deliver without this story.

| Hub-facing choice | Nanoleaf native request | Pixoo native request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work | Work | Monitor |
| Free | Free | Media |
| Quiet | Quiet | Monitor |

Pixoo Quiet adds no dimming or animation change. Work and Quiet both use Monitor, so a Monitor observation cannot establish which Hub-facing choice was selected. These are Hub concepts mapped to native APIs, not a new common controller-native enum.

Later integrations: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/415 adds LIFX participation; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635 consumes each companion's effective choice (its override, otherwise the Hub selection). https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634 retains sensing, freshness and endpoint qualification. None is a prerequisite for this first delivery. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267 retains coordinated colors/scenes; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/443 retains before-apply preview. Neither blocks these controls or after-request results.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- **Save intent without claiming device success.** Once admitted and saved, the Hub keeps its choice even if one or all device calls fail. A 404, unsupported capability, offline device or timeout produces that participant's result and does not block healthy participants. Failed calls do not restore the previous selection or override.
- **Reject before changing anything.** Invalid input/configuration, no configured participants, missing control authority, stale request revision, busy admission or failure to save choices leaves previous choices intact and sends no commands. Hub-wide requests require authority for every configured participant; individual requests require authority for their target. Read access does not expose unauthorized device details.
- **Keep existing ownership and truthful receipts.** The Hub uses registered aliases and existing controller services/queues, never arbitrary destinations or a second physical writer. Preserve queued, sent, failed, partially-applied, uncertain and cancelled meanings, request guards, manual takeover, private credentials and observation freshness. Transport acknowledgment is not physical proof.
- **Bound concurrent work.** Serialize conflicting Hub-wide and individual selections under a shared admission rule and reject overlaps as busy rather than queueing them. Keep downstream revision/generation conflicts truthful. Duplicates, late results and a lost client response cannot clear a newer override, replace newer intent or start another device command. Specify finite snapshot/command/outer-response deadlines; a disconnected caller does not cancel an already admitted effect or make retry safe.
- **Restart and reconnect never replay commands.** Restore saved choices; retain historical results with their age and mark interrupted attempts uncertain. Fresh observations may resolve evidence but must not enforce a saved choice. Existing unreadable state is not a new-install Free default. No background retry, rollback, restoration baseline or unbounded operation history is added.
- **Preserve individual control.** Native/vendor-app changes remain observed device state and persist under their existing ownership rules until another explicit supported request. Do not automatically correct them or invent a Hub-recorded override. Brightness, scene and media operations are not implicit Hub-mode selections.
- **Preserve companion policy boundaries.** The future companion consumer reads its effective choice without owning another selected-mode store. Individual Free still respects permissions, snooze, call/media suppression and safety rules in #635. Unknown/stale policy cannot become Free permission, and startup cannot initiate speech or motion. Ambient recording and passive transcription holds remain unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. Installation, real-client acceptance and visible-device effects require separate authorization, a named owner and explicit targets. This story changes no installed service or device during planning or source delivery.

| Criterion | Observable result | Planned evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: First startup | A new store displays Hub Free without sending commands or claiming devices are Free. | Fresh-store integration test with controller call counters; dashboard browser check. |
| AC2: Global selection | Work saves the Hub choice and attempts the configured Nanoleaf/Pixoo mappings through the same HTTP/MCP operation. | Fake-controller integration tests for all three mappings and entry points. |
| AC3: Individual override | Nanoleaf Free leaves Hub Work and Pixoo unchanged; selecting the Hub's mode individually clears only that override. | State/API/MCP tests and dashboard browser journey. |
| AC4: Next global selection | A later Hub selection clears every override, including explicit same-mode reapply. Duplicate submission or view refresh does not. | State-transition and browser tests with request identities. |
| AC5: Independent failures | A device 404, unsupported operation, offline service or timeout does not block the other device; the Hub choice remains saved even if every device fails. | Bounded fake-controller failure tests preserving typed/uncertain receipts. |
| AC6: Restart and storage | Restart restores selections without commands; interrupted attempts stay uncertain; unreadable saved state is not overwritten with Free. Existing unrelated Hub state survives the change. | Persistence, migration, interrupted-request and restart tests with disposable state. |
| AC7: Rejection | Invalid, empty, unauthorized, busy, stale or unsaved requests preserve previous choices and send no commands. | Negative admission tests, including partial device authority and a failing store. |
| AC8: Ordering and lost responses | Overlaps, duplicates, late responses and client timeouts cannot overwrite newer choices or cause replay; current choices/results can be reread. | Focused HTTP/MCP/individual-operation ordering and response-deadline tests. |
| AC9: Honest UI | The dashboard distinguishes choice, override, native state, stale evidence and request result, including Pixoo's shared Monitor mapping and external native changes. | Keyboard/pointer browser checks, component/home consistency, partial-failure journey and current-candidate human UI approval. |
| AC10: Future consumer | A synthetic companion reads its override or Hub fallback from the versioned owner interface; no second mode store or robot behavior is required. | Contract tests for fallback, override, global reset, restart and unavailable/stale policy. |

All evidence above is planned, not executed. Before implementation, create the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, capability scenarios, design/failure/recovery notes and tasks. Update affected architecture, API/MCP/dashboard guides, feature-map checks and CI validation within the delivery branch. Explain the new Hub-level choice alongside retained native mode semantics; do not silently replace those semantics.

Run the applicable shared build/type, controller contract, workflow, Hub, dashboard and MCP checks from current AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, covering persistence, authentication, concurrency, compatibility and every acceptance criterion. Preserve current-candidate UI approval, current-head CI, guarded merge and merged-main checks. Provide the required short PR walkthrough of state ownership, timeouts, duplicates, restart and the failure/recovery test. Fake/source results never establish installed or visible-device acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

- **Additional device families (deferred capability):** LIFX remains in #415 and companions in #635 with their own prerequisites and acceptance. Use their existing individual controls until integrated; this first release does not claim their support.
- **Physical cycling control (deferred capability):** https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68 remains deferred until the owner requests a requirements reevaluation. It is not a prerequisite. Dashboard/API/MCP selection supplies explicit control here; binding-specific installation and acceptance remain held in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/69.
- **Automatic retries/enforcement (unnecessary capability for this outcome):** an owner explicitly reapplies after inspecting a failure. Revisit only for a separately accepted recovery requirement; do not add a scheduler now.
- **Restoration of prior scenes/media (deferred capability):** Free uses native Free/Media behavior, with manual content selection where needed. Coordinated looks remain with #267; no saved baseline is promised here.
- **Custom modes, discovery and participation editing (unnecessary capability for this outcome):** use Work/Free/Quiet and configured aliases. Revisit when a selected integration needs another mode or participation workflow.
- **Unbounded history and a general device framework (unnecessary capability):** retain bounded current choice/request evidence and existing adapters. Revisit only for a concrete second requirement that the current boundary cannot serve.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-10-01. Product decisions are settled by the owner: Free on first-ever startup; persist Hub choice and individual overrides; no startup commands; the next explicit Hub selection replaces all overrides; independent device failures; Nanoleaf/Pixoo first; #68 deferred.

Complexity: high. Persistent selections, dashboard/API/MCP entry points and independent device requests share ordering and restart invariants.

Uncertainty: medium. The behavior is settled; #67's delivered native API/receipt composition is not yet available. Verify that producer contract before dependent coding. Exact Hub-mode schemas, finite deadlines and safe persistence/migration mechanics are bounded design work in this story, not unanswered product choices.

Impact: medium. Incorrect behavior could change device modes or lose saved preferences. Preserve existing authorization, ownership and data protections; device calls remain explicit and recovery is manual.

Readiness: backlog, blocked by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67. Publication does not select #67 for implementation or remove its deferred label. No dependency on #68, #634, #635 or #415 blocks this first delivery.

Alignment: authorized extension of the existing per-request preset design, without expanding #67's source scope. Reuse the existing Hub storage owner, component controls and controller writers. Sources inspected at Hub main `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949`: [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/architecture.md), [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/controller-contract.md), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md), Hub/dashboard guides and the integration seams. Live #67/#68/#267/#415/#633/#634/#635 bodies, comments and relevant relationships were inspected on 2026-10-01; targeted open/closed mode searches and open PRs found no dedicated saved-mode implementation. Search was limited to these ownership and integration boundaries.

This shared story remains standalone; companion parent membership and unrelated ownership are preserved. No Project membership, Phase, Commitment, guide refresh or public-site publication is selected. Planner reasoning setting is unknown. Reassess when #67 is delivered, scope/ownership changes, a supported consumer requires a different contract, or verification contradicts the proposed state model.

## Guide

**Topic:** desktop-controls
**Note:** Save the Hub's mode and allow individual exceptions until the next Hub selection.
**Highlight:** idea, The owner wants one remembered Hub choice with temporary device and companion overrides.
**Extends:** H67

## Shared event foundation coordination — 2026-10-01

https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/701 defines common envelope/payload/version, ownership and delivery rules for event adoption. This issue remains the sole owner of saved Hub mode, per-participant overrides, revision and guarded dashboard/HTTP/MCP selection operations.

A selection command expresses a request. A committed selection event reports saved authoritative choice after admission/persistence; it does not claim device success. Device request outcomes and fresh native observations are separate facts, owned by their existing components. Same-mode explicit reapply remains a new accepted selection; duplicate submissions, refreshes and reconnects do not become new selections. Restart restores choices without commands or replay of old effects.

Use the foundation's accepted rules when defining a mode-event publication interface, and record any required adapter or scoped adoption change. This coordination note does not add a universal publisher/runtime rollout to the first Nanoleaf/Pixoo delivery. The existing required #67 dispatcher input, future LIFX/companion ownership, UI acceptance and all restart/override/failure criteria remain. Preferred contract/adoption order is distinct from a new blocked-by link; no new implementation prerequisite is selected by this note.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The delivered #67 dispatcher, native request guards and result contract. Inspect that producer input before selecting the final implementation session; the owner has settled the product choices.
**Work surface:** UI

**Why:** The saved mode/override outcome and restart policy are settled, but the required #67 dispatcher is unfinished. The #701 event coordination preserves mode ownership and adds no new first-delivery implementation prerequisite; publication cannot supply the missing producer evidence.
**Reassess when:** #67 is delivered and its request/guard/result evidence is inspected, or mode/event-adoption scope and ownership change.

| AC4: Next global selection | A later Hub selection clears every override, including explicit same-mode reapply. Duplicate submission or view refresh does not. | State-transition and browser tests with request identities. |
| AC5: Independent failures | A device 404, unsupported operation, offline service or timeout does not block the other device; the Hub choice remains saved even if every device fails. | Bounded fake-controller failure tests preserving typed/uncertain receipts. |
| AC6: Restart and storage | Restart restores selections without commands; interrupted attempts stay uncertain; unreadable saved state is not overwritten with Free. Existing unrelated Hub state survives the change. | Persistence, migration, interrupted-request and restart tests with disposable state. |
| AC7: Rejection | Invalid, empty, unauthorized, busy, stale or unsaved requests preserve previous choices and send no commands. | Negative admission tests, including partial device authority and a failing store. |
| AC8: Ordering and lost responses | Overlaps, duplicates, late responses and client timeouts cannot overwrite newer choices or cause replay; current choices/results can be reread. | Focused HTTP/MCP/individual-operation ordering and response-deadline tests. |
| AC9: Honest UI | The dashboard distinguishes choice, override, native state, stale evidence and request result, including Pixoo's shared Monitor mapping and external native changes. | Keyboard/pointer browser checks, component/home consistency, partial-failure journey and current-candidate human UI approval. |
| AC10: Future consumer | A synthetic companion reads its override or Hub fallback from the versioned owner interface; no second mode store or robot behavior is required. | Contract tests for fallback, override, global reset, restart and unavailable/stale policy. |

All evidence above is planned, not executed. Before implementation, create the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, capability scenarios, design/failure/recovery notes and tasks. Update affected architecture, API/MCP/dashboard guides, feature-map checks and CI validation within the delivery branch. Explain the new Hub-level choice alongside retained native mode semantics; do not silently replace those semantics.

Run the applicable shared build/type, controller contract, workflow, Hub, dashboard and MCP checks from current AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, covering persistence, authentication, concurrency, compatibility and every acceptance criterion. Preserve current-candidate UI approval, current-head CI, guarded merge and merged-main checks. Provide the required short PR walkthrough of state ownership, timeouts, duplicates, restart and the failure/recovery test. Fake/source results never establish installed or visible-device acceptance.

issues.title: Add apartment hardware inputs: ESPresense, Yoshi tracking and door events
issues.body:
<!-- bunny-hardware-backlog-20261001 -->

Lightweight backlog capture requested on 2026-10-01. Hardware choices, implementation slices and acceptance need refinement.

## Outcome and real setup

Extend B.U.N.N.Y. with apartment hardware inputs so it can build a useful history of room presence, Yoshi's likely location, and doors opening and closing. Start with one operator and the existing Windows/WSL installation.

Capture these candidates:

- **Everything Presence Pro / ESPHome:** the owner plans to get two Pros. Evaluate their available presence, zone and tracking observations; purchase, installation and physical performance are unverified.
- **ESPresense:** add BLE room/proximity observations, with M5Stack AtomS3 Lite receivers as a candidate. Keep ESPresense and ESPHome firmware/integration paths distinct.
- **Yoshi tracking:** combine stationary room, doorway and bed observations, including low-mounted sensors where useful. Preserve the owner's preference for collar-free indoor tracking; a BLE tag is optional. Validate detection of a small dog, including when resting, instead of assuming human presence sensors can identify him.
- **Door open/close events:** capture contact-sensor state, transition timestamps and history. A door opening alone does not establish who crossed it.

## Smallest useful implementation

Refine a first slice of one room, one sensor source, local ingestion and durable observation history; retain the other hardware inputs in this backlog scope for subsequent slices. Then combine sources where measured results justify it.

Reuse #634 for sensor capability/identity qualification and #11 for Home Assistant/MQTT evaluation. Home Assistant is a candidate integration route, not a settled requirement. Follow #637 for person identity and reacquisition rather than adding a competing identity system. Related to #633 without adding a required outcome to that epic. Delivery prerequisites remain to be settled during refinement.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep observations separate from inferred identity/location and coding-agent lifecycle state. Preserve source, timestamps, freshness and uncertainty; stale or missing readings mean unknown, not absence. Use the existing state owners and designated device writers. Define storage, retention and access before collecting movement history.

The ambient recording/transcription hold in #642 remains in force. This item does not authorize installation or physical trials.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Not fully defined yet. Desired examples are: show the last observed door transition; explain which observations support Yoshi's likely room; and show unknown when sources expire or disagree.

At refinement, select the first hardware/room, observation contract, retention and delivery target. Define source checks for event ingestion and stale data, then a separately authorized physical trial for door transitions, room changes, Yoshi moving/resting and sensor coverage. Simulated data cannot establish tracking accuracy.

## Meaningful deferrals

Camera identity remains with #634/#637; ambient capture remains held by #642. Precise positioning, automatic calibration and broader hardware purchases need evidence from the first selected sensors. Until then, use bounded room-level observations with uncertainty. Interpret door scope here as sensing open/closed state; powered opening/closing requires a separately selected actuation scope.

## Future pressure sensing and activity history — 2026-10-01

Add pressure sensors as a future hardware candidate alongside the existing ESPresense/Bluetooth scope. The owner has no pressure-sensor hardware today. Qualify available pressure/load observations, placement, calibration, dropout, false occupancy and whether any source supports person association; pressure alone does not identify a person. Keep existing Presence Pro, Yoshi, collar-free tracking and door-event outcomes.

The daily activity follow-on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/696 initially uses qualified presence positions or zones mapped to the apartment and couch footprint. It need not wait for purchasing pressure sensors or Bluetooth receivers. Later acquired sources can corroborate occupancy/identity estimates only after #634 qualification and a separately authorized trial. Compare the combined estimate with the presence-only baseline, including a Bluetooth device left behind and disagreeing sensors. Hardware selection, procurement and activation remain future decisions; #694 is related work, not a mandatory prerequisite for the initial couch slice.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-10-01. Complexity: medium, with several sensor interfaces and observation fusion. Uncertainty: high, because exact hardware support, placement, dog detection and acceptance remain unverified. Impact: high for personal movement/identity history; privacy and data integrity need explicit treatment when implementation is scoped. Status: backlog, needs refinement.

Alignment checked against #11, #633, #634, #637 and #642 and the repository's local ownership boundaries. Next step: use #634's qualification to select one useful sensor slice, then reassess contracts, evidence and prerequisites. This issue captures the request without making it implementation-ready.

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Highlight:** idea, Add apartment hardware observations for room presence, Yoshi and door history.
**Extends:** H634

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Selected first sensor/room, actual hardware/interfaces/placements, accepted observation/storage/retention contract, refined source and physical acceptance, and delivery prerequisites. Pressure sensors are future candidates, not current hardware; choose the first source/room and retention before implementation.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** The activity-history/response follow-on is now scoped and linked to the existing sensing, memory and policy owners. Required definitions, producer evidence or physical authorization remain unresolved; tracker publication does not establish implementation readiness. Existing stories retain their acceptance and holds.
**Reassess when:** Accepted producer/activity/retention definitions, selected hardware or trial findings, ownership/scope changes, or explicit authorization of the named physical work. A model choice cannot resolve missing product or sensor evidence.
