issues.title: Epic: Bring active agents to life in animated isometric workshops
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Give active agents a small animated world: a grid of isometric workshops where a worker arrives when an agent starts working. Workers could be people, bunnies, robots or other characters. At a glance, the owner can see activity, who needs attention and which observations are uncertain, with more personality than status cards alone.

This epic preserves the September 28 brainstorm for later refinement, as requested on October 1, 2026. It is a **deferred concept placeholder**, not an implementation specification or a selected delivery commitment. One operator, the existing B.U.N.N.Y. installation and its supported agent clients are the starting scope. Browser/dedicated-screen presentation, Pixoo, Tidbyt or a combination remain open choices. The original discussion placed the idea around Jev; its exact role is still to be defined.

The owner proposed workshops appearing as agents become active. The alternatives and mappings below are brainstorming candidates, not approved requirements.

## Smallest useful implementation

**Candidate first slice:** a browser workshop view over the existing shared session observations, initially explored with simulated states. A fixed isometric perspective can use layered 2D artwork: floors, walls, furniture, character sprites and small effects. PixiJS was suggested as one possible renderer; no library or art pipeline is selected. True 3D is an alternative if camera rotation or exploring a connected world becomes important.

The dashboard already has shared-session observations and a widget catalog; inspect those current interfaces again at pickup. Presentation rules would map observed state to scenes without adding another collector or lifecycle reducer. Local animation does not require ongoing model inference. Jev could eventually help choose an approved presentation or theme, but its involvement is an open design question rather than a prerequisite.

### Scene directions to revisit

| Direction | Experience |
| --- | --- |
| Individual dioramas | One compact isometric room per session; easy comparison across a grid. |
| Bunny burrow | A cutaway hillside of connected rooms, potentially grouped by project. |
| Workshop village | Persistent project buildings with workers arriving and leaving. |
| Shared maker space | Several agents at benches in one room, showing evidenced collaboration. |
| Space station | Labs, engineering bays and control rooms for a more technical aesthetic. |

Individual dioramas with a cozy burrow style were the initial suggestion. Cozy inhabited world, busy factory and interactive command center remain distinct directions to compare.

### Candidate visual vocabulary

| Observation | Possible visual |
| --- | --- |
| Active | Worker uses a bench; task lamp is on. |
| Needs input | Raised hand or question marker, visible from the overview. |
| Blocked attention | Paused work with a clear obstruction marker. |
| Turn ended / retained notice | Envelope in an outbox; no automatic success trophy. |
| Idle | Worker sits or tidies the bench. |
| Stale or uncertain | Work animation pauses with an explicit uncertainty marker. |

Signals can coexist: a retained envelope may remain when another turn starts. Exact precedence, transitions and labels need later design.

### Twists worth keeping

- Persistent project rooms with visiting session workers, versus temporary rooms per session.
- Stable placement and dimmed quiet rooms to preserve spatial memory; bounded retirement still needs a policy.
- Extra helper benches for agents with evidenced parent/child relationships; never infer relationships from shared project names.
- An attention bell or consistent marker that remains legible when zoomed out; selecting a room opens precise status.
- Decorative personality through mugs, goggles, tools, furniture and small gestures without changing state meanings.
- A calm or reduced-motion mode, with readable static poses.
- Compact companion scenes: Pixoo's 64×64 surface could show one workshop or simplified stations; Tidbyt's 64×32 surface could show a side-view bench or single worker. Compose for each device instead of shrinking the browser grid.
- A possible explicit control to show a selected room's miniature on a device, subject to its existing mode and writer policy.

**Related work, not declared blockers:** [Jev/Guide epic #509](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509), [semantic look gallery #535](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/535), and [B.U.N.N.Y. art epic #677](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677). At refinement, check whether their components, assets or theme work can be reused. Preserve their scope, parents and acceptance. No required children or native prerequisites are established by this placeholder.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Animation expresses observed activity, not measured productivity or task success. Keep activity, attention, retained notices, acknowledgment, evidenced relationships and freshness distinct. A moving worker is not a progress percentage; turn end is not success, and silence is not completion.

Retain one authoritative state owner and each device's designated writer. Any physical presentation goes through the owning controller and respects manual choices, modes and queued work. Preserve precise status access, readable labels, contrast, reduced motion and stable controls. Decorative themes must fit the application's current UI rules.

Use only fields allowed by the selected versioned contracts and owner policy; preserve explicit-label precedence and neutral fallbacks. Credentials and secrets remain excluded. This concept does not require prompt/transcript capture or expand its authority.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

**Current delivery target: this durable tracker placeholder only.** Product acceptance is intentionally undefined. Filing the epic neither completes the feature nor authorizes implementation, installation or device operation.

When selected for refinement, agree on the target surface, session-versus-project grouping, visual direction and smallest useful release before creating delivery children. Distinguish required work from optional themes, world-building, 3D and device companions.

Candidate evidence for that later decision: compare one-agent, six-agent and crowded scenes using simulated active, input-needed, idle, retained-notice and stale states. Check whether the owner can identify who needs attention and inspect exact status without losing the spatial layout. Review arrival, departure, reconnect and reduced-motion behavior. These are proposed questions, not completed tests or adopted acceptance criteria.

Later source/browser evidence, explicit approval of the current UI candidate, installed-client evidence and any separately authorized physical observations remain distinct. Define the epic's end-to-end closure criteria during refinement; do not close it merely because this note exists.

## Meaningful deferrals

The entire feature is deferred until the owner chooses to revisit it further into project delivery. Existing monitoring remains the practical alternative. No date, phase, delivery slot or automatic promotion is assigned.

Open decisions to revisit together:

- Primary screen and whether workshops supplement or replace status cards.
- Cozy world, factory or command-center feel; characters and art style.
- Session rooms versus project rooms; identity, grouping, overflow and room retirement.
- Ambient display versus interactive controls; exact role of Jev.
- Asset authoring/reuse, 2D versus 3D, performance and accessibility needs.
- Which device companions, if any, belong in the first release.

Detailed architecture, contracts, estimates, implementation tasks and child issues wait for those choices. Physical integration waits for selected targets and explicit authorization. Revisit when the owner selects this experience or related art/widget work provides a concrete reusable foundation; availability alone does not select it for delivery.

## Assessment

Placeholder capture, 2026-10-01. Complexity: unknown until surfaces and interaction are selected. Uncertainty: high because product shape, Jev's role and acceptance remain open. Impact: unknown for the eventual feature; a browser presentation and physical display control have different consequences. Readiness: deferred backlog, not implementation-ready.

Scope fit: one operator and the existing installation; no additional service, host, general game platform or continuous generation is required by the concept. Current dashboard/architecture guides and live #509/#535/#677 were checked for relevant ownership and overlap. The workshop concept can fit as a presentation consumer; its final style and integration remain unassessed. Reassess on owner selection or material changes to those interfaces and related work.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Deferred epic placeholder for animated isometric agent workshops; refine when selected for later delivery.
**Highlight:** idea, Turn observed agent activity into expressive workshop scenes while retaining precise status and uncertainty.

issues.title: Add Mario Kart Live control and camera access to B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Give B.U.N.N.Y. deliberate control of the owner's Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit Mario car, with supervised movement and access to its onboard camera. Start with one operator, one kart and the existing B.U.N.N.Y. installation; the kart's Linux host and Wi-Fi adapter are still to be selected.

This is a coarse design placeholder requested on 2026-10-01. Keep it in the backlog and refine it when selected; this record does not authorize implementation, installation, pairing or physical movement.

## Smallest useful implementation

Proposed path: **B.U.N.N.Y. UI/MCP → owning kart controller → OpenKart/mk-live on a Linux host → Wi-Fi → Mario kart**.

Evaluate [OpenKart SDK](https://github.com/OpenKart-SDK/openkart) and [mk-live](https://github.com/xmrius/mk-live) before building a driver. The earlier source assessment found pairing/status support in OpenKart and driving/video support in mk-live; compatibility with the owner's kart remains unverified. A Linux host with an access-point-capable Wi-Fi adapter is the candidate setup, with a dedicated host as an option alongside Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y.

Start with a separately authorized hardware qualification: establish pairing, camera access, bounded movement and reliable stopping. If supported, refine a controller integration exposing short movement requests, stop, status and deliberate camera viewing. The local controller owns motor timing and command expiry independently of model response time. The current [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md) has no steering/throttle operations; define a typed interface before adding consumers.

No required native issue dependency is established yet. [Robot companions #627](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627) and [sensing/map qualification #634](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634) are related work, not prerequisites or parent assignments.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One designated writer per kart; explicit configured target; bounded speed and duration; manual takeover and stop; no motion replay after reconnect/restart. Verify stopping on expired commands and loss of control. Keep camera access deliberate and credentials/private imagery out of Git. This item includes no ambient recording or passive transcription; preserve the owner hold recorded in #634. Returning to Switch control needs a documented handoff/pairing path.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target to refine: source integration plus separately authorized installed-client and physical acceptance.

At pickup, turn these evidence goals into concrete criteria: the selected host can pair with the actual kart; a B.U.N.N.Y. request produces bounded supervised movement and a verified stop; camera/status information has clear freshness; timeout, disconnect, restart and manual takeover do not resume stale motion. Use source tests for command/ownership rules and owner-observed hardware trials for real movement, stopping and camera behavior. No tests or device trials have run for this item.

## Meaningful deferrals

Defer detailed APIs, UI, package layout and child stories until hardware qualification and selection of the first useful controls. Autonomous navigation, room finding, person following and mapping remain later possibilities: initial use requires supervision/manual direction. Revisit them only after the control/video pilot works and the owner selects a navigation use case. No new robotics framework or multi-kart support is selected.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-10-01. Complexity: medium (controller, radio host and video integration). Uncertainty: high (host/adapter, kart compatibility and runtime behavior unverified). Impact: high (physical motion and private camera imagery). **Backlog; not implementation-ready.** Next refinement selects the host, confirms upstream capabilities and defines a bounded hardware trial. Reassess after qualification, host/firmware changes or a scope change.

Alignment: follows the existing controller ownership boundary and scope defaults. Live Hub title search and kart search found no duplicate; related #627/#634 were read. No portfolio Phase, Commitment or implementation priority is assigned.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Explore supervised Mario Kart Live control and deliberate camera access through a local controller.

outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
Give B.U.N.N.Y. deliberate control of the owner's Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit Mario car, with supervised movement and access to its onboard camera. Start with one operator, one kart and the existing B.U.N.N.Y. installation; the kart's Linux host and Wi-Fi adapter are still to be selected.

This is a coarse design placeholder requested on 2026-10-01. Keep it in the backlog and refine it when selected; this record does not authorize implementation, installation, pairing or physical movement.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
Proposed path: **B.U.N.N.Y. UI/MCP → owning kart controller → OpenKart/mk-live on a Linux host → Wi-Fi → Mario kart**.

Evaluate [OpenKart SDK](https://github.com/OpenKart-SDK/openkart) and [mk-live](https://github.com/xmrius/mk-live) before building a driver. The earlier source assessment found pairing/status support in OpenKart and driving/video support in mk-live; compatibility with the owner's kart remains unverified. A Linux host with an access-point-capable Wi-Fi adapter is the candidate setup, with a dedicated host as an option alongside Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y.

Start with a separately authorized hardware qualification: establish pairing, camera access, bounded movement and reliable stopping. If supported, refine a controller integration exposing short movement requests, stop, status and deliberate camera viewing. The local controller owns motor timing and command expiry independently of model response time. The current [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md) has no steering/throttle operations; define a typed interface before adding consumers.

No required native issue dependency is established yet. [Robot companions #627](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627) and [sensing/map qualification #634](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634) are related work, not prerequisites or parent assignments.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text: One designated writer per kart; explicit configured target; bounded speed and duration; manual takeover and stop; no motion replay after reconnect/restart. This item includes no ambient recording or passive transcription; preserve the owner hold recorded in #634. Returning to Switch control needs a documented handoff/pairing path.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text: Defer detailed APIs, UI, package layout and child stories until hardware qualification and selection of the first useful controls. Autonomous navigation, room finding, person following and mapping remain later possibilities: initial use requires supervision/manual direction. Revisit them only after the control/video pilot works and the owner selects a navigation use case. No new robotics framework or multi-kart support is selected.

issues.title: Explore a library of creative art formats for B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
<!-- bunny-art-creative-library-20261001 -->

## Outcome and real setup

Give B.U.N.N.Y. a reusable library of creative art formats it can pull from randomly for the UI, Tidbyt and Pixoo. Keep these ideas together for future exploration; individual formats do not need separate stories or detailed designs yet.

Optional deferred child of #677. This library does not block the initial art release.

## Smallest useful implementation

When this work is selected, choose a small first set of formats and connect their reusable prompts or scene recipes to the existing art catalog and scheduling work (#680 and #684). The library should support variety across repeated appearances. Selection rules, repeat avoidance and storage details remain open for later refinement.

## Creative formats to explore

1. **Little visual conversations:** A door offers choices such as open, knock or leave a snack; the artwork responds at the viewer's pace.
2. **Two windows into one place:** Related views across Pixoo, Tidbyt and the UI show characters or events moving through a shared imaginary setting.
3. **Creative constraints:** Four colors, a suspicious duck or a world made of rectangles gives each piece a playful constraint and develops B.U.N.N.Y.'s recognizable creative voice.
4. **Art from your doodles:** Turn an intentionally supplied rough sketch into artwork, keeping the original alongside B.U.N.N.Y.'s interpretation.
5. **Cabinet of imaginary objects:** Invent a pocket thunderstorm, a moonlight-folding machine or an impossible-snack vending machine, with short fictional descriptions.
6. **Tiny performances:** Short visual comedy with a beginning, payoff and ending, such as a magician and rabbit or a robot watering a stubborn flower.
7. **Milestone art souvenirs:** Make collectible posters or stamps for selected, verified achievements, building an illustrated history.
8. **Private art festivals:** Explore a theme over several days, such as underwater transit, monster cafes or impossible architecture, ending with a finale or collection sheet.
9. **Explain through a picture:** Answer a requested explanation visually in the UI, with symbolic miniatures on the displays where useful.
10. **Optional visual riddles and hidden details:** Offer playful puzzles with hints or a reveal on request, without deadlines or penalties for not watching.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Random selection chooses only formats whose required inputs, context and interaction are available. Preserve the art epic's owner controls, generation-call allowance, privacy, factual provenance and display priorities. A fictional scene must not invent a real achievement; personal inputs remain opt-in. Reuse the existing art and device owners.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Detailed delivery criteria and evidence are deferred until a first set of formats is selected. At that point, define how eligible formats are chosen and replayed, how each selected format works on its target surfaces, and how viewers can dismiss or interact with it. Filing this idea does not constitute implementation or acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

Per-format specifications, individual delivery stories, interaction design, selection algorithms and implementation estimates. Desktop art and room-presence behavior retain their separate stories (#685 and #686).

## Work assessment

Deferred idea collection. Uncertainty is high; implementation complexity and impact depend on the formats selected. Scope remains one operator and the existing B.U.N.N.Y. surfaces. Reassess when the owner selects this library for refinement; related foundation stories are not a newly imposed delivery sequence.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Highlight:** idea
**Extends:** H677, H680, H684
**Note:** Future library of creative art formats for random, context-appropriate appearances.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The first creative formats, their inputs and interactions, and implementation boundaries remain deliberately unrefined.
**Work surface:** UI

**Why:** Deferred idea collection for later selection; it does not expand the initial art release.
**Reassess when:** The owner selects this library and a small first set of formats for refinement.

At pickup refresh exact released revisions, selected subscription host/account route, controller owners, explicit Tidbyt/Pixoo targets and existing display state. Run https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678's accepted bounded generation trial only with the applicable session/model-execution authorization. Use existing installation/verification procedures, a recoverable configuration change and one writer per target.

Before physical writes obtain explicit targets and permission for the display sequence. Capture source/install/browser/transport/optical evidence separately. Check readable stills and supported gentle animation, gallery/favorites, pins and attention precedence, theme lock/reset, generation count readback and return to the current display base. Observe one agreed waking-day schedule; do not claim between-session monitoring or invisible future evidence.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No guessed device address, firmware change, private database sharing, provider credential exposure or second writer. Stop and reconcile uncertainty rather than resending. Restore the prior configuration/content through the existing owner if the trial fails; retain source completion even when installed acceptance remains pending.

- [ ] AC3: The UI, 64×32 Tidbyt and 64×64 Pixoo show appropriate compositions, with accurate animation support and restoration.
  Planned evidence: Browser evidence plus owner-visible optical observations on explicit targets.

- [ ] AC4: An agreed waking-day trial records the three-to-five appearance policy, generation allowance, pins/attention and saved-art fallback.
  Planned evidence: Dated actual observations and missing-window disclosure; no fabricated continuous acceptance.

- [ ] AC5: Failure/stop and recovery leave ordinary controls usable and no delayed art replay.
  Planned evidence: Bounded stop/recovery sequence and final readback.

Delivery target: installed/browser/physical acceptance on explicitly authorized targets.

Planning publication only. Any new executable surface must first have documented build/type/test coverage and CI. All tests here are planned, not run. Installation and device contact remain separately authorized through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

Desktop wallpapers and occupancy gating remain optional deferred children, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/685 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/686, and do not block this first installed trial. No host migration or new always-on machine is required.

Complexity: high (cross-surface state and integration). Uncertainty: high (Released source children, qualified subscription route, named installation owner and explicit physical targets/sequence permission are not yet available.). Reuse existing state/layout/palette/media owners. Search was limited to these art, automation, UI and occupancy seams, including relevant open/closed work and the preview merge.

Scope fit: one operator, existing installation and configured surfaces. Desktop and presence are accepted deferrals with owning children; no extra host, generic job platform or second general memory/scheduler is introduced. Required data/ownership/queue protections remain. Reassess after producer/contract changes, provider findings, owner policy changes, or contradictory installed evidence.

**Note:** Install and verify the B.U.N.N.Y. art experience on the selected host and displays.

issues.body:
<!-- bunny-art-planning-20261001:presence -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677. Optional deferred follow-on.

## Outcome and real setup

Deferred: once proximity and room presence are configured, show art on room-assigned surfaces when anybody is in the room. Occupancy is sufficient; recognizing the owner or any named person is not required.

## Smallest useful implementation

Consume a qualified occupancy observation and explicit room-to-surface mapping from the existing presence effort https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. The first implementation needs fresh occupied/vacant/unknown evidence, not identity, cameras, robot navigation or the whole companion epic. If that effort does not provide a reusable occupancy producer, define the minimal owning producer gap at promotion rather than pretending a consumer is ready.

On confirmed vacancy, remove art through the normal presentation handoff and postpone generation intended solely for that room. Shared generation may proceed for another occupied target. Ordinary status/base behavior continues; no display-power changes. Unknown/stale evidence pauses new art presentation and does not fabricate a departure. On re-entry select something currently relevant, without replaying a missed-event backlog. Missed pieces already created remain subject to ordinary gallery retention.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Presence changes presentation eligibility only; they do not enable personal sources or authorize sensitive content for guests. No personal identity prerequisite, passive recording, new tracking database or raw sensor capture. Preserve one device writer, fresh cancellation guards, current-base restoration and truthful unsupported/uncertain removal results.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/684, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634. The linked accepted output, not a closed label alone, is the prerequisite.

- [ ] AC1: Any person, including an unnamed guest without the owner, permits art in the correctly mapped occupied room.
  Planned evidence: Synthetic occupancy tests; no identity lookup occurs.

- [ ] AC2: Vacancy retires pending art, removes active art via its owning path and postpones room-only generation while other eligible rooms continue.
  Planned evidence: Fake room/surface/controller traces with no power or mode-change writes.

- [ ] AC3: Unknown, stale, conflicting or rapidly changing observations do not create repeated requests or false presence; return shows current art once.
  Planned evidence: Freshness, debounce/cancellation, restart and re-entry tests using the qualified observation semantics.

- [ ] AC4: Actual occupied/vacant transitions match source evidence and observed display behavior on named targets.

<!-- bunny-art-planning-20261001:desktop -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677. Optional deferred follow-on.

## Outcome and real setup

Deferred: request a still wallpaper composed for a selected monitor's resolution and aspect ratio, preview it and export/save it. A favorite tiny scene can be reinterpreted as richer desktop artwork while retaining B.U.N.N.Y.'s taste, themes and explicit feedback.

## Smallest useful implementation

Extend https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680 through a distinct desktop output profile and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682 preview/export controls. At promotion, define desktop-specific generation settings and a separate allowance before dispatching any desktop generation. Ask/configure the actual monitor dimensions then; do not guess them or simply enlarge a pixel rendition. Native pixel-art scaling remains an intentional user choice, not the only composition method.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve originals and favorites, approved source/destination privacy, provenance and explicit export paths. Creating an image does not change the operating system's wallpaper. No desktop call silently consumes or bypasses the initial surfaces' allowance.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682. The linked accepted output, not a closed label alone, is the prerequisite.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: A selected scene produces a still with the configured pixel dimensions/aspect ratio and a preview before export.
  Planned evidence: Fake-generator/profile and browser tests; later authorized generation provides visual acceptance.

- [ ] AC2: Export preserves the selected image and creates no wallpaper-setting or device operation.
  Planned evidence: File/export readback and an OS/device-operation spy.

- [ ] AC3: Separate desktop call settings are visible and enforced, including failure and regeneration.
  Planned evidence: Fixed-clock accounting tests after the owner selects the deferred allowance.

Planned validation (not executed): Node 24: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow` (Python 3.12 or 3.14 for Python checks). `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:dashboard`, `npm run test:dashboard:browser` after promotion. If MCP changes, also run `npm run test:mcp`, `npm run test:mcp:protocol`, `npm run test:mcp:package` and the hub MCP checks. Refresh the exact applicable suite from docs/development.md at pickup.

Delivery target: source-only; installation and optical acceptance are tracked in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

Planning publication only. Implementation follows the owning repository's live AGENTS.md/SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec, applicable package/consumer tests and CI, independent Standards and Specification review of the same committed comparison, and current UI policy. Any new executable surface must first have documented build/type/test coverage and CI. All tests here are planned, not run. Installation and device contact remain separately authorized through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

## Meaningful deferrals

Deferred from the first art release. Automatic wallpaper changing, animated wallpaper and multi-monitor compositions need later owner selection. Revisit after the initial art experience is accepted or the owner explicitly selects desktop work; use manual wallpaper selection after export.

## Work assessment

Complexity: medium (bounded interfaces and evidence). Uncertainty: high (Deferred desktop output settings and separate generation allowance have not been selected; refine them at promotion.). Impact: medium (bounded private state or reversible UI behavior).

Readiness: deferred; not selected for the first release.

Alignment: aligned. Inspected Hub main `782f25cb201d60947ec2526bf6cdfb89acc11bbd`, controller contract 1.1, ADRs 0004/0006/0007, app/controller guides and the directly linked live backlog on 2026-10-01 UTC. Main advanced during planning through Pixoo preview PR #676; its merged widget/media interfaces were reread before final publication. Flexible art sizing and runtime themes are owner-selected extensions of earlier fixed-layout/single-skin scope; update their owning specifications during delivery. Reuse existing state/layout/palette/media owners. Search was limited to these art, automation, UI and occupancy seams, including relevant open/closed work and the preview merge.

Scope fit: one operator, existing installation and configured surfaces. Desktop and presence are accepted deferrals with owning children; no extra host, generic job platform or second general memory/scheduler is introduced. Required data/ownership/queue protections remain. Reassess after producer/contract changes, provider findings, owner policy changes, or contradictory installed evidence.

Planning evidence: 2026-10-01 UTC; user decisions in the art grilling session; live linked issues and source reads. Shared policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be`. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated). Tracker-only publication; no model trial, test, install or physical action ran.

## Guide

**Topic:** desktop-controls
**Note:** Deferred art extension; revisit after its named trigger.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Deferred desktop output settings and separate generation allowance have not been selected; refine them at promotion.
**Work surface:** UI

**Why:** Assessment and named producer boundaries above govern this start. Implementation and review cross the interfaces and invariants listed in the acceptance criteria; prerequisite acceptance is required before coding.
**Reassess when:** Producer acceptance, changed scope/contracts, provider/host availability, new UI policy or failed evidence changes the next step.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-30 · policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be` · evidence: Owner art decisions; current linked issues; Hub main 782f25cb201d60947ec2526bf6cdfb89acc11bbd; planning reads 2026-10-01 · fingerprint: `1f87acef3b88`

issues.body:
<!-- bunny-art-planning-20261001:schedule -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677. Required first-release outcome.

## Outcome and real setup

B.U.N.N.Y. offers roughly three to five art appearances per waking day: morning, a spontaneous daytime gift and evening, with additional selected moments. The UI, Tidbyt and Pixoo share an artistic idea but receive their own readable composition. New generation is optional for an appearance; saved art remains useful.

## Smallest useful implementation

Extend the existing Hub automation owner, using https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/359 for host-local scheduling and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/358 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/335 for event arbitration and moment dispatch. Keep model-driven creation separate from deterministic due-time scheduling. Request art through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680 and consume https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/681 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/93 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682. Reuse https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/295 for agent-proposed moments and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/297 for shared cross-device choreography rather than creating alternate owners.

Consume the exact-art handoff published by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/679 and implement hub routing through the existing moment/media owners; the existing closed 1.1 moment payload cannot receive arbitrary asset IDs. Reuse supported content-mode rendition operations where suitable, while event interludes retain current-base restoration and status precedence. Do not change device modes to make art play.

Enable the owner's accepted art policy through the existing permission/rule controls. Make waking hours and frequency configurable on the host-local clock, without adding a timezone platform. Select varying times within eligible windows, drop expired opportunities and schedule only future ones after restart. Pinning/manual interaction/attention may delay or suppress a showing without causing repeated generation. Show truthful per-surface outcomes; best-effort coordination is enough. Informative art carries explicit factual meaning and fresh source provenance; celebrations require evidence of the event.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep the shared eight-attempt generation allowance separate from appearance counts and existing moment budgets. Retain rules, quiet hours, one writer per device, fresh guards, bounded queues, no replay after uncertain effects and no inference of completion from a turn ending. A missing surface does not prevent other eligible surfaces from working. User-approved personal sources remain individually scoped.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/681, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/93, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/359, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/295, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/297, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/679. The linked accepted output, not a closed label alone, is the prerequisite.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Fixed-clock examples produce morning/daytime/evening opportunities and the configured three-to-five rhythm, using saved art without model calls where appropriate.
  Planned evidence: Automation tests with injectable choice/clock; quiet hours, empty windows and unavailable generation have bounded fallback.

- [ ] AC2: One idea yields independently legible UI/64×32/64×64 compositions and typed per-target results.
  Planned evidence: Real-consumer fixture contract tests, including missing targets and unsupported exact-art references.

- [ ] AC3: Pins, attention and manual changes prevent inappropriate replacement; interludes return to each current base, never a captured stale screen.
  Planned evidence: Controller/automation interleaving tests with zero mode-changing writes.

- [ ] AC4: Restart, duplicate events, expired work, concurrent triggers and lost responses cause no stale catch-up or automatic resend.
  Planned evidence: Negative scheduling and identity tests; ninth generation attempt remains blocked by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680.

- [ ] AC5: An approaching meeting/rain notice has a factual label and evidence, while imagined scenes stay decorative; milestones are not fabricated.
  Planned evidence: Synthetic enabled-source/freshness cases, disabled-source zero reads and UI inspection.

Planned validation (not executed): Node 24: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow` (Python 3.12 or 3.14 for Python checks). `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:dashboard`, `npm run test:dashboard:browser`; real controller-consumer fixtures. If MCP changes, also run `npm run test:mcp`, `npm run test:mcp:protocol`, `npm run test:mcp:package` and the hub MCP checks. Refresh the exact applicable suite from docs/development.md at pickup.

Delivery target: source-only; installation and optical acceptance are tracked in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

Installation and device contact remain separately authorized through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

## Meaningful deferrals

Desktop wallpapers are https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/685; occupancy gating is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/686. Broad Jev ranking/composition experiments remain https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/530, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/531 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/517; this bounded art feature does not require those optional experiments. Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677. Required first-release outcome.

## Outcome and real setup

A displayed scene can bring matching backgrounds, accents, borders and decorative textures to the B.U.N.N.Y. interface. The owner can lock the theme or restore its default at any time.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680 palette/provenance and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682 presentation lifecycle with the existing skin/token layer. Update that decision documentation and relevant OpenSpec during delivery. A supplied validated palette is enough for the first implementation.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep attention/error/success distinguishable and fixed-meaning device colors truthful. Theme changes never move controls, alter permissions, activate devices or undo a user lock. Preserve dark/light behavior, reduced motion and accessible focus. Typography and structural redesign are not included.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682. The linked accepted output, not a closed label alone, is the prerequisite.

## Outcome and real setup

On the owner's hub, request an original scene or a variation, inspect the result, save a favorite, dismiss it, or ask for more like it. B.U.N.N.Y. has recognizable taste, warm/playful/occasionally surreal expression, recurring characters and room to experiment. A piece can succeed purely by being enjoyable.

## Smallest useful implementation

Implement one adapter qualified by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678 and a private art catalog using the existing hub authentication/storage boundaries. Keep asset identity separate from target renditions and generation attempts. Persist bounded recent art, permanent favorites until deletion, provenance and explicit creative feedback. Configure a finite retention bound; do not silently expire favorites or referenced renditions. Reuse scoped preference/memory interfaces from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/501 if available; otherwise keep art-specific feedback in the art domain rather than creating a second general memory runtime.

Enforce eight generation attempts per host-local calendar day shared across UI, Tidbyt and Pixoo. Reserve before starting, count dispatched failures/retries and all extra model requests for art/styling, and reconcile in-flight/uncertain attempts after restart without resetting or refunding unknown effects. Manual requests share the allowance unless the owner explicitly overrides it for a bounded request. Expose used/remaining/uncertain usage. Local composition, resizing, palette application, animation playback and replay of saved assets consume no generation attempts. No application dollar budget; do not silently switch to separately billed API access.

Support newly generated images, procedural art, short gentle animations and reused favorites. Imagination/time/weather/seasons are eligible inspirations; external source data must be configured and fresh. Personal sources are individually enabled, and permitted cloud destinations are separate from permission to read those sources. Store explicit preferences, not inferred dislikes or diagnoses. issues.body:
<!-- bunny-art-planning-20261001:epic -->

## Outcome and real setup

B.U.N.N.Y. creates playful, personal and occasionally informative art for Tidbyt, Pixoo and its own UI. Delight and recognizable personality lead; informative art, celebrations, recurring characters and evolving fictional worlds broaden the experience. The operator can request, save, dismiss, revisit and steer art. One operator, the selected existing hub installation, configured displays and browser; no additional host or general art platform.

Accepted in the owner's grill-me session, completed 2026-09-30 America/New_York. Cloud creation uses an approved Codex/Claude subscription route without an application dollar budget. Eight generation attempts per local calendar day are shared across UI/Tidbyt/Pixoo, including failures, retries and extra model requests for art/styling. Manual requests share the limit unless explicitly overridden. Local rendering and replay do not count.

## Smallest useful implementation

The smallest complete release includes one qualified subscription route; a private art catalog and feedback; validated device renditions; daily and event presentation; flexible UI art widgets; theme adaptation; and an installed trial. Each is separately verifiable. One scene may yield a moon bakery in the UI, its storefront on Pixoo and its baker on Tidbyt; every composition works alone.

Required new children: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/679, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/681, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/684, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/683 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687. Reuse the existing Pixoo generated-art child https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/93. Optional deferred children: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/685, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/686 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/688. Parent grouping does not imply serial execution, and optional children do not block the initial release.

Existing shared work keeps its owner/parent: layouts https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/366; routines https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/359; agent moments https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/295; choreography https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/297; Tidbyt interludes https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/337; Pixoo interludes https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92. General Jev explorations https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/517, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/530 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/531 remain related optional work, not duplicate implementations or automatic prerequisites. Native prerequisites on children identify actual required inputs. Phase and Commitment remain unassigned; filing this epic selects no delivery slot.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Respect pins, manual interaction, attention, quiet hours, selected content modes, one writer per device and truthful receipts/freshness. Never claim task success or infer personal emotions without evidence. Ordinary contexts (imagination/time/weather/seasons) need no personal-data enrollment; personal sources and cloud destinations require individual enablement. Preserve originals, favorites and referenced renditions. Assets/context remain private; no passive capture or new credential grants.

Allow three to five appearances during configured waking hours, including morning/daytime/evening, using saved art when appropriate. Recurring art and new styles are both welcome. Keep a bounded recent gallery and favorites until deletion; explicit feedback shapes future choices, silence does not.

UI artwork fits available space without moving active controls or pinned widgets. Themes change decorative colors/textures while preserving contrast, state meanings and navigation. Pin/dismiss/restore layout and theme lock/reset remain available.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Subscription-backed creation produces inspectable art under an enforced shared eight-attempt allowance, including concurrent/failure/restart cases.
  Planned evidence: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680 evidence; installed route verified in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

- [ ] AC2: Still/procedural/short animated art and reused favorites produce appropriate UI, Tidbyt and Pixoo compositions.
  Planned evidence: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/681 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/93 source fixtures plus https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687 optical evidence; unsupported animation is not silently accepted.

- [ ] AC3: Daily surprises and verified event art respect waking hours, pins, attention, budgets and current-base restoration.
  Planned evidence: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/684 source/failure tests and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687 actual waking-day observations.

- [ ] AC4: The owner can retrieve/save/steer art and enjoy adaptive widgets/themes without losing control usability.
  Planned evidence: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/682 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/683 browser/accessibility/UI evidence plus installed readback.

- [ ] AC5: Every required child has its own accepted evidence, and the integrated installed trial succeeds.
  Planned evidence: Reconcile source, installed and physical acceptance before epic closure; closed issue state alone is insufficient.

Delivery target: integrated first release with source and installed/physical acceptance.

These optional children do not block the first release. Future personal context sources keep their own producer stories. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/688 collects ten future creative formats in a reusable library for random selection; individual formats remain unrefined.

Ask both companions for their take on a lighthearted everyday choice. Reachy offers a considered, diplomatic view; Duck offers an adventurous perspective in quacks, which Reachy faithfully translates. The owner hears both characters and makes the choice.

issues.title: Repair the local hub verify compose tests: stale Nanoleaf core pin and intermittent Pixoo aggregate-reset cases
issues.body:
> Filed 2026-09-30 from the close-work sweep after the #576, #335, #358 and #336 delivery. Observed during that delivery, not caused by it; the delivery writers reported it and did not fix it.

### Failure and reproduction

`npm run test:hub:verify` (`apps/hub/verify/tests/compose.test.mjs`) fails locally on clean `main` at `6654d02`, which already includes #651:

- `a pin mismatch or a dirty checkout fails identity-mismatch before anything is created` fails every run. It expects `nanoleaf: core 1.2.0, pinned 1.0.0; …` and gets `nanoleaf: core 1.3.0, pinned 1.0.0; …` plus an extra `scenario no-such-scenario does not require input hub-feed` message, so the assertion's regular expression no longer matches the current Nanoleaf core version.
- `aggregate reset failure in pause/pixoo preserves evidence and remains stoppable` and `aggregate reset failure in consumer/pixoo preserves evidence and remains stoppable` failed on main in one run (`actual: 'nanoleaf', expected: 'pixoo'` and `actual: 'pause', expected: 'consumer'`). On the #336 branch a different pair failed once and the next run passed, so these two look order-dependent or intermittent.

Reproduce from the worktree root with Node 24: `TMPDIR=/home/jimmie/.cache/adh<short> fnm exec --using=.nvmrc -- npm run test:hub:verify`. The suite skips on Depot (no user manager), so CI stays green while the local suite is red. Logs: the canonical checkout's `.local/evidence/gh-336-try-a-moment/compose-main.log` and `hub-verify-final.log`.

### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] The identity-mismatch case asserts on the pinned and detected versions without hard-coding a Nanoleaf core release that the runtime has moved past, or the pin fixture is updated deliberately with the reason recorded.
- [ ] The two aggregate-reset Pixoo cases pass on three consecutive local runs of the full suite, or the order dependence is found and fixed.
- [ ] `npm run test:hub:verify` exits zero locally on main.

### Dependencies, verification and delivery target

Relates to #651 (composed reset repair) and the hub verification runs in `apps/hub/verify`. Source-only; no installation or device access. Verification is the local suite above plus the Depot jobs that do run.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Highlight:** next step, the local verify suite is red on main while Depot skips it

issues.title: Let Reachy and MicroDuck banter within one shared social allowance
issues.body:
<!-- reachy-duck-relationship-20260930:banter -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. Required source outcome after explicit conversation works.

## Outcome and real setup

Reachy and MicroDuck occasionally start a short, affectionate exchange in Free mode. Either may initiate, Duck remains a capable quack-speaking peer, and the owner can join or interrupt. The pair shares the casual-check-in allowance rather than adding another stream of interruptions.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/661 for messages, voice and stationary expression, and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635 for one authoritative policy and social-episode budget. Casual check-ins in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/641 consume the same budget: at most three combined unsolicited episodes per local day, separated by at least three hours, including across midnight. These are maxima, never quotas. One episode may contain at most four alternating robot turns or 20 seconds, whichever ends first. Admit bounded audio that can stop at that time; do not merely stop generating new turns while old audio continues.

The owner joining ends the unsolicited exchange and continues an ordinary user-led conversation; existing admission remains counted. Explicitly requested conversations do not consume the unsolicited allowance. Spontaneous behavior follows existing per-behavior enablement, Free-mode, call/meeting/media suppression and one-hour “not now” snooze. Work/Quiet or stale policy suppress initiation. Mode restrictions and user interruption cancel pending unsolicited turns without replay.

Use immediate permitted context and harmless shared experiences/running jokes. Keep personal information out of unsolicited speech around guests or an uncertain audience; missing context can produce a neutral exchange or none. No passive microphone capture is needed to trigger banter. Stationary gestures never grant movement authority.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/661, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/641 is another consumer of the same policy budget, not a prerequisite for banter's basic implementation. Coordinate and test both consumers without creating a dependency cycle or a second counter.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One operator, the existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, one Reachy Mini Lite over USB and one configured MicroDuck. Reuse the assistant/voice, companion policy, private memory and robot controllers; preserve one authoritative owner for each state domain and one designated writer per robot. Device actions use the existing authenticated routes and vendor runtime, with explicit targets, bounded work, manual takeover and truthful queued/sent/uncertain results.

The ambient audio/video recording and passive-transcription implementation hold in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/642 remains in force. This story adds no passive listening, recorder, pre-roll or capture pipeline, even default-disabled. Deliberately activated speech and intended outgoing companion messages are separate from room recording. Credentials and private data stay out of Git. Translation of an intended message is not proof that audio played or that a person heard it.

One speaker per turn; user speech yields priority through the deliberately active voice session. Unanswered exchanges do not repeat. Restart, a more permissive mode or restored connectivity cannot produce catch-up chatter. Uncertain admission/output does not grant a new budget slot. Quack translations retain the same intended message; fiction remains attributed dialogue, never a real memory.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Synthetic Free-mode scenarios let either robot begin and preserve alternating turns, personality and quack-only Duck output. At the fourth turn or 20-second bound no further unsolicited audio/gesture starts or continues beyond its qualified stop behavior.
- [ ] AC2: Fixed-clock and concurrent-admission tests mix casual check-ins and banter: never more than three episodes per local day and never less than three hours between admitted episodes. Cover midnight, restart, ambiguous output, simultaneous consumers and exhausted allowance. A two-behavior fixture verifies the same owner/interface even before all sitting-reminder work ships.
- [ ] AC3: Work/Quiet, calls, meetings, active media, snooze, disabled behavior, unknown/stale policy and unavailable endpoints prevent the relevant unsolicited output. No repeated unanswered exchange, reconnect burst or replay after returning to Free.
- [ ] AC4: Joining the exchange transfers to user-led conversation; interruption cancels pending robot replies without duplicating playback or cancelling an unrelated admitted task. Extended explicit conversation is outside the unsolicited turn/time cap.
- [ ] AC5: Guest/uncertain-audience fixtures disclose no private facts. Missing memory is not filled with invented experience, and a joke cannot become an event fact in later retrieval. Reads of widget/history do not count as starting a social episode.
- [ ] AC6: Complete policy/conversation consumer, fixed-clock, restart and applicable shared/hub checks, with independent review of concurrency, privacy and cancellation. Hand off real timing and eligible-day observations to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/643; accelerated tests are not a physical full-day record.

Delivery target: source-only; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/643 owns separately authorized timing, personality and physical acceptance.

Planned source validation: issue-linked OpenSpec; meaningful behavior tests and affected-consumer checks; Node 24 build/type/contract/workflow checks and the owning hub/dashboard/MCP/package checks from [development.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd/docs/development.md). Add feature-specific executable checks to the owning guide and CI before product implementation. Applicable checks must exit zero. Independent Standards and Specification reviews inspect the same committed base/head; UI changes need explicit approval of the current candidate; current-head and merged-main CI must pass. No check has run in this planning session. Source delivery is separate from the staged installed/physical acceptance in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/643.

## Meaningful deferrals

Free-running conversations, separate per-robot allowances, learned timing optimization and walking choreography are excluded. Explicit conversation remains available while unsolicited output is suppressed. Tune the accepted starting limits only after an explicit owner decision informed by the pilot.

## Work assessment

Complexity: high (shared persistent admission, two endpoints, interruption and timing). Uncertainty: high (policy/budget and conversation producers are unaccepted). Impact: high (private speech and unsolicited physical/audio effects). Status: backlog; blocked on the named interfaces. One shared budget is required; broader automation is not selected.

Alignment: aligned with the owner's accepted relationship decisions, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633 and its voice/policy/memory/robot work, current [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd/docs/architecture.md), [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd/docs/controller-contract.md), [dashboard widget catalog](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd/apps/dashboard/src/widgets.ts) and SDLC. This specializes Duck's selected voice as quacks; it does not replace the first robot pilots or their ownership. Relevant open/closed issue and open-PR searches found no existing quack-language story. Search was limited to these affected seams. No Project membership, Phase or Commitment is selected; no guide refresh is required for this tracker-only task.

Planning evidence: 2026-09-30, Hub main `9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd`, installed policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be`; live issue bodies/comments and native relationships were read. Planner reasoning setting: unknown, not exposed or user-stated. Installation, live model use, microphone activation and device sequences require their separately applicable authorization and named owner/target.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Note:** Brief companion banter shares the existing casual-check-in allowance.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Accepted conversation implementation and companion-policy admission/budget interface shared with casual check-ins. Consumer tests must establish one budget before proactive output is enabled.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** The accepted product outcome is captured, but the named producer interfaces and acceptance evidence are not available. Choose implementation and independent review settings after those inputs are accepted; publication does not establish readiness.
**Reassess when:** Producer definitions or qualification findings are accepted, scope/ownership changes, or the selected host/device interface changes.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-30 · policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be` · evidence: Owner-accepted relationship/widget/input/completion decisions; live issue bodies, comments, native parent/dependency reads and Hub main 9ba4edd111f08631a24f7dfda07c0a15648126cd inspected on 2026-09-30. Active Codex schema inspected; no Claude session or future worker was launched. · fingerprint: `3c367d77148f`

issues.title: Show MicroDuck’s latest meaning in a B.U.N.N.Y. widget with separate history
issues.body:
<!-- reachy-duck-relationship-20260930:widget -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. Required source outcome.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can look at B.U.N.N.Y. whenever desired and read MicroDuck's latest intended meaning. The home widget shows exactly one Duck message, not an inline transcript. A “View conversation” option opens older messages elsewhere, including Reachy's replies and speaker/time labels.

## Smallest useful implementation

Register a read-only widget in the existing dashboard catalog and reuse its navigation, authenticated hub reads and shared UI tokens. Consume https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/661's accepted latest/history interface over https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/636's private record owner. Keep the latest Duck meaning visible without a reveal button or a request to Reachy. Show its timestamp and relevant connection/delivery evidence. Reachy's reply must not overwrite the latest Duck message.

Use the existing conversation/history surface when one exists; otherwise add a bounded separate history view in the existing shell. Do not create a second archive or widget framework. The owner explicitly rejected the earlier 20-message inline suggestion: no 20-message display or retention limit is implied. History retrieves available permitted records through the producer's bounded/paginated interface and inherits its correction/deletion policy.

Required input: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/661. Owner-arranged layouts (https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/366) and the broader widget inventory (https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/287) are related independent work, not prerequisites for adding this catalog widget.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One operator, the existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, one Reachy Mini Lite over USB and one configured MicroDuck. Reuse the assistant/voice, companion policy, private memory and robot controllers; preserve one authoritative owner for each state domain and one designated writer per robot. The ambient audio/video recording and passive-transcription implementation hold in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/642 remains in force. This story adds no passive listening, recorder, pre-roll or capture pipeline, even default-disabled. Deliberately activated speech and intended outgoing companion messages are separate from room recording. Credentials and private data stay out of Git. Translation of an intended message is not proof that audio played or that a person heard it.

Viewing the widget/history is read-only and never activates a microphone, synthesizes speech, replays a quack or commands a robot. Latest means latest available Duck message by the accepted producer order, not an inference of current thoughts. Missing meaning, emotional expression, stale content, empty history and denied access must remain distinguishable. Keep private data out of URLs and browser diagnostics.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Synthetic browser scenarios show exactly one latest Duck meaning directly on the home widget. New Duck messages replace it; Reachy's subsequent reply does not. No inline list, reveal control or mandatory spoken translation is needed.
- [ ] AC2: “View conversation” opens a separate surface with older available Duck and Reachy messages, speaker labels and times. Back navigation restores the home. Long messages and narrow layouts remain readable; keyboard and assistive-technology access work without focus-stealing on each update.
- [ ] AC3: Reload/restart restores available retained history from the authoritative owner. Deletion or correction of the latest message is reflected without resurrection or a stale browser copy. No separate retention policy or hard 20-message cap is introduced.
- [ ] AC4: Empty, emotional-only, unknown-meaning, interrupted/uncertain playback, offline and stale fixtures show honest states. A pending intended message is not labelled as heard or played; Reachy's absence does not prevent reading available history.
- [ ] AC5: Denied/revoked access hides private content, and widget/history reads cause no speech, capture or device command. Exercise these negative cases alongside the producer's contract tests.
- [ ] AC6: Run applicable dashboard unit/browser, hub/read-contract and shared checks, obtain explicit human approval of the current UI candidate, and hand off the installed widget checks to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/643.

Select a companion in the existing conversation UI or name it during an active conversation; ambiguous addressing requests clarification rather than producing two replies.

## Smallest useful implementation

Inspect pinned primary sources for Reachy audio playback/capture and interruption, MicroDuck quack synthesis/playback and supported stationary gestures, and the selected Windows/WSL routes. Reuse https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/619, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/620 for motor/host boundaries; do not repeat or expand their first pilots. Define one conversation/turn identity and intended-message representation shared by the voice controller, Reachy translation and the widget. Specify speaker/addressee, literal intended utterance versus emotional expression, provenance/time, ordering, interrupted/failed/uncertain delivery, latest-message/history reads and correction/deletion behavior. This is intended communicative content, not private model reasoning and not audio decoding. An unassociated vendor quack has unknown meaning; no fabricated translation. Specify how the same meaning reaches Reachy across rooms without acoustic hearing or new room-map requirements.

Name one owner for the shared social-episode budget in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635, consumed by casual check-ins in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/641 and the new banter behavior. Settle its admission, local-day, restart, ambiguity and spacing semantics without a second counter or scheduler. Review existing automation facilities before choosing reuse; generic moment budgets do not automatically satisfy this social budget.

Required native prerequisites: none for source investigation. Before a consumer is implementation-ready, accept the relevant producer contracts and this proposal. Current missing hardware observations must remain unknown.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One operator, the existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, one Reachy Mini Lite over USB and one configured MicroDuck. No product code, new wire value, installation, live provider call or physical experiment is delivered here. Interface approval does not qualify a device. Preserve quack-only Duck output, faithful Reachy translation and typed/explicitly activated spoken input.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Return a source-pinned capability matrix for both robots: audio input/output, quack variation, bounded stationary gestures, interruption/stop, available receipts and host route. Separate documented, simulated, physically observed, refuted and unknown findings.
- [ ] AC2: Provide caller examples and a versioned interface proposal for the normal conversation, emotional quack, unassociated quack, cross-room translation, missing endpoint, duplicate/out-of-order turn, interrupted/ambiguous playback, restart and forbidden English output on Duck. Review the proposal against existing controller and voice boundaries before consumers implement it.
- [ ] AC3: Define latest Duck message and history retrieval through the same private record owner. Include reload/restart, deletion of the latest message, unavailable history, permitted companion-generated dialogue and the rule that a fictional joke is not a remembered fact.
- [ ] AC4: Define the shared three-per-local-day and three-hour-spacing budget with fixed-clock examples that combine check-ins and banter, including midnight, restart, concurrent admission and uncertain output. Preserve separate sitting-reminder policy.

- [ ] AC6: Reconcile consumers from the findings and identify any implementation-changing owner decision. No unresolved producer, physical claim or scope change may be disguised as accepted. The definition completes only when the required proposal decisions are accepted or the owner explicitly narrows its outcome.

## Outcome and real setup

Hub delivery uses fewer duplicate instructions and repeated approval steps while retaining independent evidence where mistakes matter. A bounded pilot tests whether routine Guide changes can use one independent review covering both required axes.

## Smallest useful implementation

First align the source policy with the owner's effective 2026-09-30 instruction: no project UI requires human UI approval, including Hub, dashboard, device-facing UI, Guide and Ask. Remove obsolete current-candidate UI approval requirements, Guide/path exemptions and approval-evidence gates from AGENTS.md, docs/sdlc.md, docs/development.md, the delivery ADR, other active guidance, preflight and its fixtures. Do not fabricate approval evidence to satisfy obsolete checks. Preserve automated/browser/accessibility verification and the existing independent review and CI requirements. This UI-rule alignment can proceed independently of agent-skills #113 and the reviewer pilot; the owner decision itself needs no further approval.

After https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/113 is accepted and its installed readback is available, reconcile the remaining planning/review rules and matching shared instructions. Keep GitHub as the delivery/status authority and each normative rule in one owning place, with links from other entry points.

Define narrow pilot eligibility for the first three future routine Guide changes after policy adoption. Exclude policy/CI, security/authentication, contracts, state/device ownership, high-impact work and unresolved uncertainty. One fresh independent reviewer must still inspect Standards and Specification; the implementer cannot self-review. This policy change itself uses the existing two-reviewer gates.

Human UI approval is removed for both new interfaces and changes to existing ones, regardless of path or size. This does not authorize device operations, installation, external configuration, publication or a contract change. Preserve each separately scoped decision, including the Guide root-cutover acceptance.

Bind contract approval to the canonical schema and normative behavior, with renewed approval for material definition changes rather than unrelated editorial bytes. Preserve compatibility, exact version provenance and current approvals until the new rule is accepted. Reconcile this proposal with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542 and agent-skills #87; do not silently close or bypass their still-applicable obligations.

Use conditional planning detail and selective recommendations consistently with #646 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/113. Full OpenSpec remains appropriate where behavior, uncertainty or a project rule requires it. Remove blanket editorial-pass requirements for routine clear prose while keeping substantive editing available. The duplicated machine-level AGENTS instruction must be coordinated with its canonical dotfiles source; changing only a local copy would leave the effective rule unchanged.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep exact source/review provenance, current checks, guarded merge, unresolved findings and merged-main readback. Source, installation, live UI and physical evidence remain distinct. Runtime permissions, credentials, designated device writers and explicit physical authority are unchanged.

The owner's removal of human UI approval is effective now and supersedes the older UI-approval guidance. Other proposed rule changes stay pending until their replacement is accepted. Readiness never selects a Project commitment. Simplification does not remove an issue's observable outcome, real blocker or owner-held decision.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Active instructions and preflight agree that no project UI needs human UI approval. Fixtures cover Guide and non-Guide UI, including new/material UI changes, passing the UI gate without an approval record while still enforcing applicable validation, independent review and CI. The remaining pilot rules agree on eligibility, review evidence, contract approval and planning detail; negative fixtures reject ineligible single-review work, self-review, missing axes, stale evidence, unresolved findings and missing CI.
- [ ] AC2: Source policy alignment uses the existing independent review and CI gates, with no human UI approval gate. Affected central/shared instructions receive a named coordinated update and readback. Report the owner's effective UI decision separately from source/preflight and installed-policy alignment; do not claim those artifacts changed before they do.
- [ ] AC3: Record the first three eligible future Guide deliveries using existing PR evidence: reviewer rounds, human interventions, corrections and observed escaped defects, with dates and observation limits. Do not invent a measured result before those deliveries exist.
- [ ] AC4: After those three cases, record retain/adjust/stop and the evidence behind it. A disqualifying finding stops the affected use immediately; the pilot does not waive normal blockers.
- [ ] AC5: Run affected preflight/workflow tests and all applicable source checks. Record source acceptance separately from the later pilot outcome and any installed-instruction change.

Delivery target: accepted Hub/central policy adoption and an honestly evaluated three-change pilot. Consumers may rely on the accepted policy revision after its required installation/readback; they do not wait for this issue's final pilot evaluation to close. Pilot deliveries still need their own ordinary authorization.

## Meaningful deferrals

No automatic merge service, broad device/security relaxation, mandatory organization-wide rollout or indefinite measurement program. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/654 provides hosted Guide CI independently; the browser, preview and cutover do not wait for this policy pilot.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium; impact high for delivery policy. The reviewer/planning pilot is blocked on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/113 source and installed acceptance; the UI-rule alignment is independently actionable under the owner's decision. Alignment: current Hub AGENTS/SDLC/ADR/preflight, machine-level instructions, #542, #646 and the shared skill policy. Scope is bounded adoption plus three observed cases, not a new process platform.
