issues.title: Document B.U.N.N.Y.’s productive-companion product vision
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Give the owner and agents building B.U.N.N.Y. one short, durable statement of the intended product: productive companions that help with work and everyday life. Keep it plain enough for a reader outside the project to understand.

## Smallest useful implementation

Add `docs/product-vision.md` and a short README link. Use the agreed draft below, editing for clarity without changing its promises. This is documentation of product direction, not a new roadmap or authorization to implement the capabilities it describes. No product prerequisite is required.

Alignment references: the accepted local-first assistant direction in ADR 0004; assistant foundation https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498; Jev and adaptive interfaces https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/517; robot pilots https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627; apartment-aware companions and portable memory https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. These are related work, not prerequisites or a selected delivery order.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub issues own scope, priority, acceptance and status. Architecture decisions and versioned contracts own implementation boundaries. Preserve user control of knowledge, observation-versus-inference distinctions, model/harness portability and existing permissions. The separate owner hold in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/642 still prohibits implementing ambient audio/video recording or passive transcription without subsequent explicit approval.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: The document leads with productive companions and describes useful initiative, completing work and dependable follow-through within established permissions. Evidence: review the opening and definition of productive against the owner-approved draft.
- [ ] AC2: Digital-only, voice, screen and embodied companions are included; shared permitted knowledge and distinct personalities/voices survive changes of model, tools or harness. Evidence: direct document review.
- [ ] AC3: Comprehensive owner-selected digital/physical observation, evidence-backed activity history, revisable learned patterns, permitted responses, continuity across rooms/devices, adaptive interfaces and user ownership of personal knowledge are clear. Inspection, correction, deletion and export are explicit; observations, remembered facts and inferences remain distinct. Evidence: direct document review.
- [ ] AC4: Intended experience is distinguished from delivered behavior, and the recording/transcription hold is preserved. The document contains no copied issue/status ledger, dependency chain or delivery commitment. Evidence: compare with ADR 0004 and current linked issues at pickup.
- [ ] AC5: The README links to the committed document with a valid relative path. Evidence: source/link inspection and required repository workflow checks.

Delivery target: source documentation, merged through the normal issue/PR, independent Standards and Specification review, CI and merged-main readback gates. Use Node 24 and run `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` from the assigned isolated worktree; report the actual specification inventory. These are planned checks, not executed evidence. Record the docs-only/no-product-behavior explanation for omitting an OpenSpec product proposal. No installation or physical acceptance is involved.

## Meaningful deferrals

Feature delivery, architecture changes, epic reprioritization, Project selections, guide regeneration/publication and marketing collateral are outside this document. Existing capability issues retain their acceptance and sequencing. Revisit the vision when the owner changes the product promise, audience or ownership principles; create focused follow-up work for any resulting product change.

## Agreed vision draft

### B.U.N.N.Y. — Product vision

B.U.N.N.Y. is a personal system for productive companions that help me build, think, and manage everyday life. They combine capable task assistance with personality, lasting knowledge, and continuity across the places and devices where I spend my time.

A productive companion helps turn intentions into outcomes. It can help develop an idea, coordinate coding agents, organize a project, prepare for the day, discuss dinner, or follow through on an accepted routine. It can take appropriate initiative within established permissions and recognize when staying quiet is more useful.

Companions can appear through conversation, voice, adaptive interfaces, and physical robots. They share permitted knowledge and conversation context while retaining distinct personalities and selected voices. Their usefulness and identity should survive changes to the underlying models, tools, or agent harnesses.

B.U.N.N.Y. should build a comprehensive, owner-controlled history of my day-to-day life from the digital and physical sources I choose. It should measure where I spend time and what activities the evidence supports, keep uncertainty and corrections visible, and learn revisable patterns from that history. Companions should use current context and learned patterns to choose useful, permitted responses across rooms and devices, while I control both collection and initiative. This context also includes what I am working on, my preferences, and the routines I have taught it. Its interface should bring forward useful information and controls for the current activity. Moving between rooms or devices should preserve continuity.

Personal knowledge remains under my control. I should be able to inspect, correct, delete, and export it. B.U.N.N.Y. must distinguish remembered facts, inferred patterns, and current observations. Local operation is the foundation, with cloud services used within selected boundaries. Recording and passive transcription retain their separate approval requirements.

We will build toward this experience through small, useful releases. Each should demonstrate a complete interaction and report its limitations honestly. Success means useful outcomes, dependable follow-through, and companions I want to work and live alongside.

This document describes the intended product. GitHub issues own delivery scope and priorities; architecture decisions and versioned contracts own implementation boundaries.

## North Star clarification — 2026-10-01

The owner selected the daily activity context amendment above for tracker publication. The intended loop is observe, estimate, remember, learn, respond and improve. Couch time, cooking and pacing are examples for the related daily activity follow-on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/696, not delivered capabilities or a delivery ledger to copy into the vision. Initial couch estimates use qualified presence/position or zones mapped to the apartment and couch footprint; pressure and Bluetooth sensors are future additions in #694. The short vision should describe the purpose and owner control without prescribing sensors or architecture. The existing source-document/README deliverable and its readiness remain unchanged.

## Assessment

Complexity low: one short document and a README link. Uncertainty low: promise, audience, companion forms and boundaries were settled with the owner. Impact low: no product behavior or contract changes. Ready for source delivery; not selected into a Project commitment.

Scope fit: one owner's existing repository and workflow; no additional service, platform, registry or publication process. issues.title: Offer mode-aware sitting reminders and three spaced personal check-ins
issues.body:
<!-- apartment-companions-planning-20260930:checkins -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. Required outcome; parent membership is not itself a prerequisite.

## Outcome and real setup

B.U.N.N.Y. gently notices prolonged sitting and checks in with personal context at varied appropriate times. A sitting reminder becomes eligible after 90 minutes of supported continuous sitting. Casual check-ins are capped at three per day, at least three hours apart; these are maxima, not a quota that must be filled.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/637's current posture/seat evidence, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/636's permitted daily context and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635's mode, busy/media and snooze rules through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/500 voice. Reuse applicable local automation clock facilities rather than model-driven polling or a second scheduler. Define the local-day timezone and evidence gaps using the selected installation and qualify the sitting signal; lack of movement alone cannot prove sitting.

Work uses a gentle nonverbal sitting cue; Free can speak when appropriate; Quiet suppresses it. Calls, meetings and active playback suppress unsolicited conversation; a reminder can wait for a natural break. Casual check-ins occur only in Free. "Not now" pauses unsolicited social prompts for one hour; ignored prompts are not repeated. Select varied eligible moments and wording from actual permitted context without inventing events or trying to meet a quota after downtime.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/637, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/635, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/636, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/500.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

**Owner hold — 2026-09-30 UTC:** Ambient audio recording, ambient video recording and passive conversation transcription may be planned, but must not be implemented without the owner's subsequent explicit approval naming that work. This backlog publication, acceptance of behavioral defaults, a general implementation request for another story, model access, multiple-person presence and enabling a companion are not that approval. No default-disabled recorder, passive transcription pipeline, pre-roll buffer, persistence path or live trial is included through another story. Deliberate conversation and qualified transient perception are separate scopes; if a proposed perception path needs a held capability, stop that path and return for the explicit decision.

Persist/reconcile the minimum budget and timing evidence needed to enforce daily cap/spacing across restart and mode changes; uncertainty must not grant another prompt. Do not bridge unknown sitting intervals as confirmed sitting. Keep sitting reminders distinct from casual check-ins and define the one-reminder-per-supported-sitting-session rule in refinement. This is a user-selected conversational reminder, not a medical assessment.

One operator and the owner's existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, with explicitly configured devices. Preserve one authoritative owner for each state domain and one designated writer per physical device, existing authenticated Hub API/MCP routes, bounded queues, manual takeover, private credentials and truthful stale/partial/uncertain results. Personal memory is not current location evidence or command authority. New schemas, APIs and persistence boundaries require definition and review before dependent implementation; no speculative robotics framework is selected.

The owner has selected https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/663 as another consumer of the casual social allowance. The existing three-per-local-day maximum and three-hour spacing apply to the combined total of casual check-in and unsolicited banter episodes. They are not separate allowances. ## Outcome and real setup

In Free mode, after roughly 30 seconds of supported sustained kitchen presence, one available companion may ask what the owner is doing and continue a natural conversation about cooking. Passing through does not trigger a prompt, and being in the kitchen is not evidence that the owner is cooking.

Implement a bounded once-per-visit trigger with a defined visit/exit/re-entry boundary from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634. On track loss, Reachy may perform one bounded look-around attempt and ask if still uncertain. issues.body:
<!-- apartment-companions-planning-20260930:policy -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/633. Required outcome; parent membership is not itself a prerequisite.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner selects Work, Free or Quiet in the Hub and may override an individual companion through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695; this issue applies each companion's effective choice to its behavior and retains enable/disable controls for individual proactive behaviors. Companions with distinct personalities share conversational continuity while one selected endpoint speaks a turn. The mode matrix below is the accepted product policy.

## Smallest useful implementation

Build a bounded companion-policy path inside the owning Hub/assistant services using https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634's accepted qualification and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695's shared mode interface. The latter owns the saved Hub selection, per-participant overrides, revision and restart semantics: first-ever startup selects Free; later restarts remember choices; neither startup path sends commands. An individual companion override lasts until the next explicit Hub selection, including a same-mode reapply. Consume the companion override when present, otherwise the Hub selection; do not keep a second selected-mode store. #67 remains the fixed device-request dispatcher and #267 retains colors/scenes. This issue owns behavior rules and future companion participation, not another native-controller enum or Hub selector.

Own standing permissions, per-behavior settings, prompt cancellation, one-hour social snooze and selection of an available robot/audio endpoint. Consumers provide their own triggers and use existing controllers. Reuse applicable rules/permission/voice interfaces in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/500; do not create another device scheduler or a second writer. Availability of those interfaces must be checked before readiness. Losing an endpoint does not prove its speech or motion never occurred; no duplicate greeting on another endpoint after an ambiguous send.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695. This issue does not block the Nanoleaf/Pixoo first delivery of that shared-mode story.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

| Behavior | Work | Free | Quiet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guest greeting | Brief, subdued gesture | Expressive gesture and speech | No unsolicited greeting |
| Kitchen conversation and casual check-ins | Suppressed | Enabled at appropriate moments | Suppressed |
| Sitting reminder | Gentle nonverbal cue | Gentle spoken prompt | Suppressed |
| Automatic TV power | Disabled | Enabled under the seating rule | Disabled |
| Automatic guest approach | Disabled | Available only when separately enabled | Disabled |
| Explicit conversation or movement request | Available | Available | Available when explicitly requested |

Calls, meetings and active media playback suppress unsolicited conversation. A sitting reminder may wait for a natural break; it is not a media-interruption exception. More restrictive modes cancel pending unsolicited actions; returning to Free never replays missed prompts or greetings. "Not now" pauses unsolicited social prompts for one hour. Unanswered prompts are not repeated. A restrictive mode cancels a pending approach and requests the qualified safe stop for admitted autonomous motion; it must not cut motor power as an assumed safe stop. An explicit request remains subject to device safety, authority and availability.

**Owner hold — 2026-09-30 UTC:** Ambient audio recording, ambient video recording and passive conversation transcription may be planned, but must not be implemented without the owner's subsequent explicit approval naming that work. This backlog publication, acceptance of behavioral defaults, a general implementation request for another story, model access, multiple-person presence and enabling a companion are not that approval. No default-disabled recorder, passive transcription pipeline, pre-roll buffer, persistence path or live trial is included through another story. Deliberate conversation and qualified transient perception are separate scopes; if a proposed perception path needs a held capability, stop that path and return for the explicit decision.

Modes govern outward behavior independently of any later recording eligibility. Keep explicit stop-speaking, stop-recording, task cancellation and robot safe-stop meanings distinct. An unknown/stale policy suppresses unsolicited behavior until fresh authority is available; it is not automatically Free.

One operator and the owner's existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, with explicitly configured devices. Preserve one authoritative owner for each state domain and one designated writer per physical device, existing authenticated Hub API/MCP routes, bounded queues, manual takeover, private credentials and truthful stale/partial/uncertain results. Personal memory is not current location evidence or command authority. New schemas, APIs and persistence boundaries require definition and review before dependent implementation; no speculative robotics framework is selected.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Fixed-clock/table tests cover every Work/Free/Quiet matrix cell, per-behavior enablement, call/meeting/media suppression and explicit requests in all modes.
- [ ] AC2: Race tests change mode or disable a behavior while a prompt/approach is pending: no prohibited new effect starts. Admitted motion follows the qualified safe-stop path and reports already-sent effects truthfully.
- [ ] AC3: Snooze, ignored prompt, restart and return to Free produce no repeated or catch-up prompt. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695 supplies remembered mode/override choices without startup commands; this issue must define snooze recovery and apply fresh permission/availability checks before behavior. Restart cannot authorize speech or new autonomous movement.

| Guest greeting | Brief, subdued gesture | Expressive gesture and speech | No unsolicited greeting |

## Outcome and real setup

As the apartment's owner, I want Reachy Mini Lite and MicroDuck to know rooms and people, converse at appropriate moments and share durable knowledge across models and harnesses. Reachy starts with a stationary guest greeting; MicroDuck later navigates to named rooms or people. Each companion keeps a distinct personality and selected voice while sharing household knowledge and conversation continuity.

Configured setup: existing Windows/WSL hub, Reachy Mini Lite over USB, MicroDuck, Roborock S8 MaxV Ultra and LG OLED G4. Sensor models, camera placement/coverage, robot localization and usable map interfaces remain unqualified. Home Assistant is not installed and is not a prerequisite.

## Smallest useful implementation

This is follow-on work, not an expansion of the first robot pilots in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627. issues.title: Control the LG OLED G4 locally from B.U.N.N.Y. without additional hardware
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

One operator controls the existing LG OLED G4 from B.U.N.N.Y.: power on/off, volume/mute, HDMI inputs and installed-app launching. The owner selected everyday controls and a software-first Wi-Fi investigation. Home Assistant is not running. Direct local webOS control is the first candidate to qualify; no hardware purchase or Home Assistant deployment is selected.

## Smallest useful implementation

Three required children, with separate finish lines:

1. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/628 — qualify actual Wi-Fi behavior and decide the host, API ownership and consumer surfaces.
2. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/629 — deliver the qualified commands, observed state and selected B.U.N.N.Y. interfaces through one owner.
3. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/630 — install and verify the pinned artifact with the real TV under explicit authorization.

Required order is qualification → source → installed acceptance. Parent membership is not a dependency. Keep this device capability independently useful; apartment-aware seating triggers and conversational watch selection are later consumers, not prerequisites. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11 remains related Home Assistant research; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/345 remains a separate Sony IR idea. Neither blocks this Wi-Fi investigation.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One designated TV writer; correct configured target; private pairing credentials; bounded command admission and no unsafe replay. Manual control, independent devices and existing audio ownership remain intact. Commands and observations stay distinct; stale or unreachable is not proof of TV power-off. Automatic behavior requires its own accepted trigger and standing-permission policy.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Accept https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/628's supported/unsupported/inconclusive capability results and implementation boundary, preserving the coordinated apartment-aware robotics boundary.
- [ ] AC2: Accept https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/629's source, selected consumer integration, compatibility and delivery evidence for all five control groups; do not infer installed or physical acceptance from fake tests or CI.
- [ ] AC3: Accept https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/630's installed-interface and owner-observed real-TV results, including Wi-Fi wake after extended standby and reversible removal.
- [ ] AC4: Reconcile all required child criteria before parent closure. Failed wake or a missing requested control remains unfinished unless the owner explicitly revises scope. Closing a child as not planned does not satisfy it.

Delivery target: qualified source plus separately authorized installed and physical acceptance. Start with qualification, not an epic-wide implementation.

## Meaningful deferrals

No IR hardware is purchased or integrated now. If a required software capability fails, revisit an open-firmware, cloud-free IR option with the owner; the temporary alternative is the physical remote. Playback/navigation, TV notifications, content search and playback deep links, viewing history, automatic routines and robot/voice experiences are deferred until explicitly selected. The apartment-aware planning owner retains automatic seating triggers, standing permissions and asking what to watch.

## Work assessment

Complexity: high (TV/host/contract/consumer integration and installed acceptance). Uncertainty: high (Wi-Fi wake, firmware/audio behavior and final API surfaces are unqualified). Impact: high (credential and command ownership across shared consumers). Backlog; not implementation-ready. Required evidence comes from all three children. Reassess at each accepted child, changed owner scope, shared contract decision, or conflicting physical result.

Planning baseline: 2026-09-29 America/New_York (2026-09-30 UTC), Hub main `dd1d984f6667e567da1a751fd9819f658f8a2c6e`; current docs/architecture.md, docs/controller-contract.md, docs/sdlc.md and live LG/webOS/apartment issue searches. No existing LG/webOS issue was found. Home Assistant is not installed, confirmed by the owner. This backlog publication authorizes no implementation, installation, TV commands, network/settings changes or purchase. Installation and physical checks need the owner's explicit target and approved sequence. One coordinating writer owns each deliverable; coordinate shared contract, host, dashboard, manifest and CI edits at pickup.

Coordination received through an owner-relayed response from the “Clarify apartment-aware robotics” planning chat on 2026-09-29. This TV planning chat owns these four LG issues. The apartment-aware planning chat owns shared presence, mode and automation planning edits once authorized; neither writer independently rewrites the other's records.

The LG work owns local control and its evidence limits. One TV controller owns credentials and the command queue. Hub API/MCP expose supported operations against a registered TV alias; dashboard, assistant and future automation use the same owning service. Reuse `power.set` where its semantics fit; use a typed, versioned device profile for volume/mute, inputs and apps, with exact API placement and supported consumer surfaces settled during qualification. No arbitrary webOS commands or caller-supplied destinations. The apartment work owns presence/identity, seating intent, mode eligibility, interruption rules and standing permissions. Conversation/voice asks what to watch and requests qualified actions; app launch is not proof that a particular programme is playing.

Related independent work, reread during this coordination: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45 owns event rules/routines, but presence-triggered TV commands need an explicit extension; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67 has fixed desk presets with no durable selected household-mode state; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267 is broader mode/presentation planning; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/500 own conversation and voice; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627 owns the initial robot pilots. Exact mode eligibility, seating triggers and automation manual-override policy remain unsettled in the apartment-aware work. None is a prerequisite for explicit LG controls. Existing shared issues are linked, not edited or reparented; link the apartment-aware follow-on story when its owner publishes it.

No Project membership, Phase or Commitment is selected. Existing shared issues retain their parents. No guide refresh or publication is included. All acceptance below is prospective; no local TV behavior has been verified.

issues.title: Qualify LG G4 local Wi-Fi control and define its B.U.N.N.Y. integration
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Determine whether the owner's existing LG OLED G4 can provide power on/off, volume/mute, HDMI selection and installed-app launching over its existing Wi-Fi connection from the selected B.U.N.N.Y. Windows/WSL installation, without additional hardware or a cloud control dependency. Record exact model/firmware, host, network path and normal sound output; private addresses, MAC and pairing credentials stay outside Git.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with read-only API/host/contract investigation, then a separately authorized bounded physical qualification. Direct local webOS control through an existing open-source client is the first candidate. Compare the existing Home Assistant integration before custom transport work, but do not install Home Assistant or assume it is selected. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11 is related research, not a required prerequisite.

Home Assistant 2026.9.4 pins `aiowebostv==0.10.0`; use it as a candidate baseline, not automatic package selection. Record the chosen version and dependency/runtime fit. Current controller v1 supports power but lacks typed volume/mute, HDMI and app-launch operations. Decide the owning service, versioned API/profile, observation fields, target/app allowlist, selected dashboard/MCP surfaces and exact validation entrypoints before dependent source work. No raw webOS command or arbitrary destination escapes the owner boundary. Prefer existing hosts when technically suitable; the current Node local-controller host does not by itself establish compatibility with a Python client.

Starting sources: [Home Assistant webOS](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/webostv/), [2026.9.4 dependency](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.9.4/homeassistant/components/webostv/manifest.json), [aiowebostv](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/aiowebostv), and [LG mobile wake guidance](https://www.lg.com/us/support/help-library/how-to-set-up-the-lg-thinq-app-on-your-lg-smart-tv--20152745625356). LG's Wi-Fi wake feature is not proof that wake works from this WSL host. Pairing is owner-approved local registration, not TV rooting or firmware replacement.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One automated writer per TV; explicit configured target; private credential storage; bounded calls and no blind command retry. Preserve manual TV/receiver control and current audio routing. Distinguish API transmission, observed state and physical effect. A dropped connection does not prove power-off; stale/missing observations remain unknown. Do not infer user intent, occupancy or watch duration from TV power alone.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Produce a versioned capability matrix for pairing/reuse, state readback, power-off, Wi-Fi wake, volume/mute with normal sound output, configured HDMI inputs and installed apps. Every row records supported/unsupported/inconclusive, source versus observed evidence, host/model/firmware, limits and next action.
- [ ] AC2: Agree API/host ownership and consumer scope, carrying the coordinated apartment-aware automation boundary into the exact interface. Document any necessary versioned contract extension and existing-consumer checks. Choose and document a qualification entrypoint; none is supplied by this planning issue.
- [ ] AC3: After explicit authorization, pair with the named TV, reuse the private credential after client restart and observe manual remote changes. Exercise only approved volume values, inputs and apps. If HDMI-CEC/eARC affects the Sony system, record the actual behavior and retain its separate ownership; do not silently route duplicate commands through both devices.
- [ ] AC4: Bound wake qualification to at most three short-standby attempts and one overnight-standby attempt from the intended host, with the TV retaining mains power. Agree timing and maximum wait before execution. Record settings already enabled, packet send, subsequent TV observation and owner-visible effect separately. No automatic overnight monitor is created. Stop on an unexpected effect, a decisive failure or the agreed bound; refuted/inconclusive findings require reassessment, not unlimited retries.
- [ ] AC5: Verify reconnect makes no unsolicited power/input/app/volume change, record whether local control needs internet services, and distinguish app launching from internet-dependent content playback. Provide teardown/revocation steps and the minimum repeatable evidence for the source child.
- [ ] AC6: Return a supported/refuted/inconclusive decision. Keep failed Wi-Fi wake visible; do not silently replace full power control with manual wake. The owner decides any revised scope or open-firmware IR fallback before dependent implementation is declared ready.

Delivery target: qualification report and accepted integration definition, including separately authorized real-device evidence. Initial read-only investigation may proceed independently; full qualification needs the explicit target/sequence and resolved implementation interfaces.

No IR purchase, Home Assistant installation, TV firmware/root/service-menu changes, router/firewall changes, new sensors or network migration. The physical remote is the temporary fallback. Revisit IR only after a required Wi-Fi capability fails and the owner selects that route. Presence-triggered actions and conversations belong to the apartment-aware follow-on story; no automatic actions are enabled here.

Compare direct aiowebostv with [HA webOS](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/webostv/) under [#11](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11). Preserve direct local control as the first candidate.

implementation.text:

issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/627.

## Outcome and real setup

Let the owner deliberately arm and operate limited MicroDuck walking controls in B.U.N.N.Y. during a supervised session, using the stationary findings from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/624.

## Smallest useful implementation

Define and obtain acceptance of conservative speed, duration and command-expiry bounds from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/624's evidence. Add explicit arming, supervised movement and a priority stop path through the existing owning controller. Keep balance and the robot-side watchdog/stopping mechanism onboard; a browser or model cannot be the sole stopping mechanism. Refine this story before implementation once the physical inputs exist.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No walking from lifecycle events, background rules or unsolicited agents. Reconnect/restart cannot rearm or resume. Expired or stale-armed commands do not move the robot. Stop must not wait behind ordinary queued movements. A network stop request is not a guaranteed physical emergency stop; preserve the observed manual recovery procedure.

## Outcome and real setup

Give the owner a Reachy Mini Lite component view with truthful connection/USB status, explicit bounded controls and opt-in agent-status gestures. The selected host and behavior contract come from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/619.

Implement the owning adapter/controller, hub registration and routing, existing component-view controls and MCP status inspection. Source delivery is separate from installation batched in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/622.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One B.U.N.N.Y. command owner calls the vendor daemon. Reads never move the robot. Daemon health does not imply USB connectivity or physical pose. Repeated unchanged state does not restart gestures; stale input never means success. Manual takeover suppresses status gestures until explicit restoration. Bound work and reject unsafe replay; report a lost response as uncertain. No unsolicited agent motion through MCP.

issues.title: Record VOLCANO HYBRID manual usage in private local history
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Record private local usage for the enrolled VOLCANO HYBRID when the owner uses its physical buttons, without requiring a B.U.N.N.Y. control command. Expose the observed state and retained usage through an authenticated read interface for the dashboard.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required input: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/614, with an accepted host/transport, telemetry contract, session definition and retention/deletion policy. This issue is a bounded dependent outline; choose package paths and detailed algorithms only after that input exists.

Implement the qualified observation path, durable history and read API as one usable backend slice. Reuse the accepted BLE or Home Assistant route and the existing host/authentication facilities. Keep one history owner and one observer connection policy; do not introduce another agent-state reducer. Register the device through the selected typed contract and keep existing controllers compatible. Capture measured heater/pump/temperature/counter fields only to the extent qualification supports them; unsupported values stay explicit.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No heater, pump, setpoint, auto-off, workflow or firmware commands. Connecting, polling, restarting and opening the dashboard must not start or extend heating. Preserve physical controls and the qualified S&B-app handoff. Credentials, device identity and actual usage stay private; no transcript or material/consumption capture. Preserve existing read authorization and origin checks. Product scope changes need the owner's decision.

A missed observation is unknown. Never infer off, a complete session or an exact event timestamp from a Bluetooth gap. Repeated samples and restart must not duplicate sessions or accumulated time. A counter decrease/reset or changed device identity starts an explicit discontinuity, not a negative or huge usage delta. Recover aggregate missed heating time only if qualification establishes a persistent counter and a valid continuous baseline; do not invent session boundaries within the gap.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Fake transport/fixture replay of physical-button state changes records the accepted usage metrics and returns them through the authenticated read route, without any B.U.N.N.Y. actuation command. Record source and observation times separately. This proves software behavior, not actual manual-button reporting.
- [ ] AC2: Source tests reject duplicate accumulation and fabricated continuity for repeated/out-of-order samples, first connection mid-session, dropped updates, reconnect, logger restart and counter reset/decrease. Simulated counter-gap recovery follows only the qualified rule.
- [ ] AC3: A transport spy fails if the read path emits actuator/settings/firmware operations; authentication tests reject unauthorized or wrong-device reads. Include necessary BLE subscription setup in the explicit permitted transport operations.
- [ ] AC4: Durable-store tests demonstrate history survives an ordinary restart and follows the accepted retention/deletion policy without damaging unrelated hub state. Use synthetic usage data and the existing practical recovery facilities; define persistence examples before implementation.
- [ ] AC5: API/contract checks verify bounded data, truthful freshness/availability and existing consumers. Add the selected adapter's exact checks to docs/development.md and CI before product implementation. Run the owning hub/package checks and applicable shared build/type/contract/workflow checks. No test command or source check is claimed executed by this planning issue.

Delivery target: source-only backend, with installation and manual-device acceptance tracked by the linked Volcano verification issue. Source completion cannot establish that the owner's firmware emits the expected events.

## Meaningful deferrals

The dashboard is a separate consumer issue; authenticated fixture/API readback is the source acceptance here. Actual installation and manual-use verification remain separate; source delivery grants neither. Remote device control and automation are deferred until explicitly requested; the owner continues using physical controls. A broad telemetry platform, all-host matrix and long-running performance study are unnecessary for the first device; revisit only for an observed failure or another selected consumer.

## Work assessment

Complexity: medium (transport, durable usage state and authenticated reads). Uncertainty: high (qualification and history semantics unresolved). Impact: high (private usage history and durable state; read-only intent must also be proven at the transport boundary). Blocked on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/614 and needs the owner decisions recorded there. Not implementation-ready; execution settings for either host remain insufficient until the route, contract and storage scope are accepted. Later reviews must cover private data, continuity and unintended command paths at the high-impact floor.

Planning assessment: 2026-09-29. One operator, one explicitly enrolled VOLCANO HYBRID and the existing B.U.N.N.Y. installation. The requested outcome is usage tracking even when the owner operates the physical buttons. Scope is observation and history; publication of this backlog does not authorize implementation, installation or device activity.

Current controller kinds do not include Volcano, and controller v1 does not define its usage telemetry. No existing integration is claimed. Live all-state searches for Volcano, vaporizer and Storz found no duplicate; relevant Bluetooth issues and open PR titles were inspected. [Home Assistant #11](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11) and [BB-8 host qualification #603](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/603) are related independent work, not prerequisites unless their accepted artifacts are actually selected. No repository-wide audit was performed.

The owner chooses product semantics, installation host and physical-test scope; one coordinating writer is assigned at pickup. Preserve existing owners of shared contracts, manifests, CI and running services. Source delivery retains issue-linked OpenSpec, documented checks/CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, current-candidate human approval for UI, guarded merge and merged-main readback. Source, installation and physical acceptance remain separate. No Project membership, Phase or Commitment is selected; no guide rebuild or public publication is included.

Evidence limits: planning reads only; no product tests, Bluetooth scans, device connections or installations ran. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated). Reassess when the qualifying evidence, owner decisions, firmware, host, storage or consumer scope changes.

issues.title: Qualify VOLCANO HYBRID manual-use telemetry and define usage tracking
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Determine whether B.U.N.N.Y. can reliably observe a VOLCANO HYBRID operated from its own HEAT/AIR/temperature buttons, and define the smallest local usage-tracking slice. Deliver an evidence-backed route and usage contract, with unknown physical behavior clearly marked.

## Smallest useful implementation

This is an investigation/design item. Select a candidate Bluetooth host and explain how it reaches the WSL hub through existing authenticated boundaries. Bluetooth access from WSL is unqualified; native Windows or another host is only a candidate.

Define device identity, supported observed fields, units, sample time, freshness, missing/error values and counter continuity. Keep device readings separate from optimistic local command state. Establish what heating-hours/minutes measure and their granularity, rollover/reset behavior and persistence; source evidence alone cannot prove the owner's firmware behavior.

Resolve owner choices before dependent implementation: what counts as a usage session (a heater-on interval is a proposal, not an accepted definition), whether pump runs and temperature history belong in the first slice, history retention/deletion, and the selected host. Record accepted choices in this issue and refine dependent acceptance after those decisions. Evaluate the smallest typed telemetry route; do not disguise heating as lighting power or put it into agent-lifecycle/session state.

Source starting points, inspected 2026-09-29:

Required inputs: none for read-only source investigation. Owner decisions and any needed hardware evidence gate dependent implementation, not this initial investigation.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No discovery, connection, device command, personal configuration change or installation during this investigation. Preserve manual operation and S&B app handoff. Observation must not change heater, pump, setpoint, auto-off or firmware. BLE subscription setup, if required, must be distinguished from actuator/settings writes. Identify any unavoidable side effect before a live trial. Usage records stay private and local; do not put actual usage, Bluetooth identifiers or raw device dumps in GitHub.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC3: Owner-approved usage/session definitions and retention/deletion policy have concrete examples for manual operation, first connection mid-session, a missed interval and a counter decrease. A disconnect never means off; usage does not mean consumption, dose or inhalation.

No automatic retries beyond that bound. No test is executed here.
- [ ] AC5: Reassess dependent issues and native blockers against the result. Identify exact owning packages, issue-linked OpenSpec and package/consumer checks to add to docs/development.md and CI before implementation. Unresolved choices remain holds; a closed investigation with an unsupported result does not unblock a consumer.

Delivery target: accepted investigation/design and tracker record. Initial investigation is read-only; record accepted decisions only within the tracker authority granted at pickup. Live behavior remains for separately authorized verification.

Heater/pump control, workflows, remote start and firmware updates are deferred capabilities: use the physical controls or S&B app; revisit only after an explicit control request. Consumption/dose or inhalation estimates are excluded because the examined telemetry does not establish them. Wider device/host compatibility is unnecessary for this one-device outcome; revisit for a second selected device or host. Detailed dependent implementation waits for this result rather than inventing a generic telemetry framework.

issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Decide whether concentrating existing device profiles would reduce the protocol knowledge shared by Hub controller routing and MCP tool registration. The result is an evidence-backed recommendation, including a supported no-change result. Scope: the current single-operator Linux/WSL Hub and its configured Pixoo, Nanoleaf, Tidbyt and LIFX clients; the device controller packages and owning repositories keep their current responsibilities.

This is observed knowledge spread; no failure or expected performance saving was demonstrated. The existing PlaybackSource interface is a useful comparison, not a mandate to adopt another pattern.

## Smallest useful implementation

One bounded read-only investigation using current source, callers, tests, authoritative contracts and relevant history. Compare keeping the current composition with concentrating native routing, validation and command construction in existing per-device modules. Identify exactly which branches or duplicated knowledge disappear, where each responsibility moves and what HTTP/MCP callers must still know. Do not prescribe a plugin framework, class hierarchy or shared native-mode enum.

Required issue prerequisites: none for investigation. [#576](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/576) owns contract-1.1 reads and the 1.0 fallback and must not be absorbed here. [#335](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/335) owns later moment submission. Coordinate any subsequent implementation touching their client/MCP paths; shared paths alone create no dependency. [Playback-retirement repair](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/608) is independent. An actual refactor proposal depends on this investigation's supported result and a separate implementation request; do not pre-create speculative implementation chores.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

The common client retains one bounded transport slot per configured device, independent health/timeouts, fixed target and credential binding, no redirects with credentials and no automatic retry of ambiguous writes. Preserve native identity/revision/generation/ticket validation, optional-route handling, capabilities and device-specific errors. HTTP and MCP keep their current authorization and observable outcomes. Device-owned databases, queues, physical writers and wire contracts remain private and unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Keep the one-slot transport owner intact. A smaller file count or naming a GoF pattern does not establish improvement.
- [ ] Account explicitly for the approved contract-1.1 fallback from #576 and moment work from #335 without redesigning either. Distinguish required producer inputs from shared-file coordination and preferred order.

Proposed checks are unexecuted; source evidence does not prove installed behavior.

If supported, provide one bounded candidate with interface ownership, migration order and acceptance coverage for a separately authorized implementation issue; if refuted or inconclusive, record that outcome and stop.

Broad formatting cleanup and a whole-repository architecture audit remain outside this bounded investigation; revisit only on separate request or concrete friction beyond this seam.

issues.title: Retire browser playback replay entries with their session
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

After a B.U.N.N.Y. browser session sends a playback command and retires, the single-operator Linux/WSL Hub releases that session's playback replay state as well as its monitor ledger and streams. Work admitted before retirement runs once and remains accounted for until settlement.

The review at `88dc56f8df1ec5a2a56bd3429bece5bf77e7d6a6` found that [retireBrowser](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f8df1ec5a2a56bd3429bece5bf77e7d6a6/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L145) calls only the monitor replay store, while [playback](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f8df1ec5a2a56bd3429bece5bf77e7d6a6/apps/hub/src/playback.ts#L34) keeps a separate principal-keyed receipt cache without retirement. An instrumented in-process synthetic probe retained one playback entry after monitor retirement reported zero, and after playback close. The cache is capped at 64 entries; this is a cleanup and accounting defect, not measured unbounded memory growth. HTTP/logout reproduction was unavailable because this review runner refused local sockets, including `listen EPERM` on the launcher socket, even after an expanded-access retry.

## Smallest useful implementation

Extend the existing local retirement coordinator to retire playback replay ownership. Keep monitor and playback request formats and replay policies distinct; use existing storage structures unless focused tests justify a small shared primitive. Include playback ownership in private lifecycle accounting so the established resource tests observe every Hub-owned browser replay entry. No public diagnostics route or persistent session store.

Required issue prerequisites: none. This is a bounded playback follow-up to [#244](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244), delivered through PR #270 and merged revision `7d9251a`. [#430](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/430) owns future session-list UI, not this correction; [#438](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/438) and [#571](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/571) are related playback extensions. These are shared-file coordination, not blocked-by dependencies. Fixing cleanup first is preferred order only.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Follow the [browser retirement contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f8df1ec5a2a56bd3429bece5bf77e7d6a6/openspec/specs/standalone-hub-host/spec.md#L87): retire only the intended principal, reject late new work, preserve configured credentials and other browser sessions, keep pending work charged until it settles, and release it exactly once. Retirement never cancels admitted work or resends it. Preserve configured targets, scopes, Host/Origin protections, bounded receipts, cross-HTTP/MCP replay for configured credentials, source selection at admission, and failed versus uncertain outcomes. Controller-owned replay and device queues remain with their owners.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. Installation and physical acceptance require a separate request and named owner. No UI change.

- [ ] Reproduce browser launch/sign-in -> playback command -> retirement through the HTTP boundary against synthetic loopback sources before the fix. Cover logout, expiry, oldest-session eviction, credential replacement and host shutdown; settled playback entries return to the documented bound alongside monitor entries and streams. Private counts include playback without exposing identifiers or credentials.
- [ ] A deferred playback write survives retirement, response timeout and repeated retirement without cancellation or another source call. Success and rejection/uncertainty settle and release accounting once. Pending work cannot be evicted to admit additional work.
- [ ] Retired tokens and requests whose body arrives after retirement contact no source. Another browser session remains usable. Configured credentials retain their permitted HTTP/MCP replay behavior and original request identity; a conflicting duplicate never becomes a new write.
- [ ] Preserve the distinct algorithm and negative cases in `apps/hub/tests/replay.test.mjs`, `browser-sessions.test.mjs`, `playback.test.mjs` and `mcp.test.mjs`. Extend those owning tests rather than replace them with assertions of private structure alone.
- [ ] At pickup prepare an exact issue-linked OpenSpec change with lifecycle/concurrency design and targeted `standalone-hub-host` and `hub-playback` scenarios, reconciling existing requirements rather than weakening them. Synchronize affected specs and archive on the delivery branch before final review.
- [ ] Planned Node 24 validation: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:mcp`, `npm run test:hub:package`, and the shared controller, lifecycle, agent-state, MCP and workflow gates required by `AGENTS.md` and `docs/development.md`. Run dashboard browser regressions if the browser integration boundary changes. These checks have not run for a repair candidate; the review's build and 12 focused passing tests are baseline evidence only. Socket-dependent tests need a runner that supports the existing fake services; do not replace that evidence with in-process probes.
- [ ] One coordinating writer, isolated branch/worktree, independent Standards and Specification reviews of one committed base/head, applicable successful current-head and merged-main CI, and a PR walkthrough of ownership, duplicates, timeout, shutdown and recovery. Reviews must explicitly cover authorization and pending replay accounting.

## Meaningful deferrals

Process-wide RSS/performance measurement stays in [#123](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123); this correction proves retirement ownership, not a memory-budget improvement. Session-management UI stays in #430. The [controller-profile investigation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/609) is independent and does not block this repair. Multi-operator/remote session support is outside the actual setup and triggers reassessment if selected. Installed services and physical displays remain unchanged until separately authorized.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-29. Source review: `88dc56f8df1ec5a2a56bd3429bece5bf77e7d6a6`; live main `fb411f7de8771ef03e591fec53f5f998a967defd` also inspected. Its server change adds preview-proof mounting and does not change retirement or playback. Live relevant issue bodies and open PRs checked on this date; no matching open fix was found.

- **Complexity: medium.** Browser, playback, replay and shutdown lifetimes interact.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The contract and retained cache are explicit; the exact release scheduling must be established through the end-to-end regression on a socket-capable runner. No production incident or RSS saving is claimed.
- **Impact: high.** An incorrect repair can weaken authorization or replay and duplicate a device-facing command. This rating follows the prior #244 assessment.
- **Readiness:** scope and criteria are settled for separately requested source delivery; retain `status:backlog` until selected. Socket-dependent evidence remains a delivery prerequisite, not evidence that the product failed.
- **Alignment: aligned.** Existing architecture/ADR 0001 keeps one state owner and controller-owned writers; the host retirement requirement already covers playback. Preserve #244's accepted monitor correction, #430's UI scope and #123's profiling scope. No wire contract or ownership departure. Search was limited to relevant Hub issues, open PRs, worktrees and source paths.
- **Review:** independent Standards and Specification axes must cover concurrency, retirement and authorization; add specialist review only if the candidate exposes risk those axes cannot cover. No UI approval unless UI scope expands.
- **Reassess:** session authorization, replay identities, source-selection semantics or active ownership changes, or an end-to-end reproduction refutes the source diagnosis.

issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Refine this placeholder after evidence. Owner selects conservative command limits, aiming reference, arming/disarming and recovery.

Extend the same app/writer. Define heading validity after reconnect, restart or manual repositioning; require re-aiming when that reference is invalid. Treat aiming/stabilization as physical operations. Implement bounded intent, stop priority and cancellation around queued writes. Assess timeout units, enable conditions and refresh behavior; do not silently write persistent options. Any approved option change must preserve unrelated bits and support verified restoration. Present measured sensor values separately from command targets and estimates.

issues.title: Integrate original Sphero BB-8 controls into B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Let one owner control the original Sphero BB-8, ASIN B0107H5FJ6, through the existing B.U.N.N.Y. app. Required outcome: connection/power status, LEDs, aiming/calibration, bounded manual rolling and useful qualified sensor feedback. Confirm the actual unit and BLE identity before physical work. A standalone CLI is not the finish line.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required native children:
1. [#603](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/603): protocol/library assessment, host/contract decisions and finite hardware briefs.
2. [#604](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/604): deliver app-connected LEDs, power/status and selected telemetry against fake BLE.
3. [#605](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/605): qualify installation, charging/battery condition and the first app-to-robot slice.
4. [#606](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/606): deliver aiming, calibration, bounded rolling and stop handling in the app.
5. [#607](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/607): qualify actual direction, stop/loss behavior and recovery.

New controller source belongs in this monorepo. Each child consumes the previous child's named evidence; parent membership adds no dependency. Preserve one writer per physical device. Reuse a host or shared contract only after its suitability and ownership are accepted in [#603](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/603).

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Exact enrolled target, authenticated commands, bounded work and no reconnect replay. Keep commanded speed/heading separate from observed motion. A collision event is not obstacle avoidance; a motion-timeout command is not proof of stopping. Aiming or stabilization may cause physical effects and belongs to the motion gate.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: [#603](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/603) supplies accepted host/contract decisions and bounded test briefs with evidence limits.
- [ ] AC2: [#604](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/604) and [#605](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/605) prove the first B.U.N.N.Y. slice, with separate source, installation and physical receipts.
- [ ] AC3: [#606](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/606) and [#607](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/607) prove operator aiming/calibration, manual rolling, observed stopping/recovery and the selected motion/sensor feedback within accepted bounds.
- [ ] AC4: Owner can repeat setup and teardown. Unqualified actions remain unavailable; failed or missing physical evidence keeps the affected outcome open. Child counts alone do not close this epic.

Delivery target: B.U.N.N.Y. integration plus separately authorized installed and physical acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

No onboard sound: this model has no speaker. Host/external-speaker sound is a later explicit feature, with manual playback as the alternative. Autonomous roaming, obstacle avoidance, mapping, agent-triggered motion, Force Band support, holographic effects, firmware updates, remote access and multiple robots are outside this release; revisit on a new owner-selected use case. MCP and automatic status reactions are deferred; manual app controls are required.

## Existing evidence and limits

- [Linked product](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0107H5FJ6) identifies the original Sphero BB-8. [Sphero compatibility](https://help.sphero.com/sphero-support/sphero-edu-device-compatibility) lists BB-8 in native iOS/Android/Windows/macOS Edu apps, not the web app. An owner-run Edu baseline is optional and needs its own installation/device authority; do not trigger firmware updates implicitly.
- Inspected [spherov2.py revision 4252ddb](https://github.com/artificial-intelligence-class/spherov2.py/tree/4252ddb1a12a25db725257d66e3e8ec3057dd48b), which declares MIT licensing. Its BB8 class inherits Ollie/Sphero commands, including roll, heading, LEDs, power queries, sensor streaming, collision notifications and motion timeout. Check dependency/reuse terms and the exact supported hardware path at qualification. The package name does not mean every model uses the same packet version: the inspected BB-8 inheritance uses the legacy PacketV1 path.
- [Command source](https://github.com/artificial-intelligence-class/spherov2.py/blob/4252ddb1a12a25db725257d66e3e8ec3057dd48b/spherov2/commands/sphero.py) includes a motion-timeout command and an `enable_motion_timeout` persistent-option bit. Units, enabling behavior and firmware effects need qualification; changing persistent settings requires an explicit approved plan that preserves unrelated bits and supports restoration.
- [Drive control source](https://github.com/artificial-intelligence-class/spherov2.py/blob/4252ddb1a12a25db725257d66e3e8ec3057dd48b/spherov2/controls/v1.py) changes stabilization during heading reset. Do not call aiming/calibration a passive read. Adapter close alone is not evidence of physical stop.
- [Sphero sound documentation](https://sites.google.com/sphero.com/sphero-edu-javascript-wiki/sounds) states BB-8 has no speaker; its sounds play through the app device.

These are documentation/source findings, not tests on the owner's robot. No library installation, BLE scan/connection or physical test has occurred. Keep device addresses, captures, credentials and proprietary assets outside Git. Do not expose the reference library's general TCP relay as the B.U.N.N.Y. control boundary without a separately accepted authenticated design.

## Work assessment

Complexity: high (app/hub/BLE writer and physical state). Uncertainty: high (host, contract, firmware and battery condition unqualified). Impact: high (physical rolling and command authority). Backlog; only the bounded investigation is ready.

Planning assessment: 2026-09-29 against [Hub fb411f7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/fb411f7de8771ef03e591fec53f5f998a967defd), docs/architecture.md, docs/controller-contract.md, docs/sdlc.md and live #536/#537. BB-8/Sphero backlog searches found no duplicate. [R2-D2 #594](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/594) and [Claptrap #588](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/588) are related independent integrations. No Project membership, Phase or Commitment is selected.

The requesting owner decides scope, host and physical-test choices; assign one coordinating writer at pickup. This backlog grants no implementation, installation, configuration change or device activity. Later delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: isolated work, applicable OpenSpec and documented checks/CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, current-candidate UI approval, guarded merge and merged-main acceptance. Reassess after changed decisions, reference revisions or contradictory observations.

issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Observe the owner operating the real R2-D2 from B.U.N.N.Y. for [#594](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/594), including head movement, driving/turning, selected routines and return to rest within accepted bounds.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required input: accepted [#598](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/598) revision, [#597](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/597) receipt and the approved motion brief. Confirm operator, BLE target, host, exact sequence permission, conservative duration bounds, containment and immediately accessible physical power-off.

Run the finite sequence: small head/drive/turn operations and selected routines, normal stop/release/expiry, then controlled link loss, claim lapse and controller-failure cases only where the approved setup contains continued or autonomous motion. Observe cam/head transitions rather than trusting disputed enum labels. Unexpected movement or a missed stop aborts to the agreed physical recovery; do not extend or retry automatically.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One writer and supervised operator. Connection, claim freshness and physical rest remain different observations. A loss test that cannot be contained stays pending. No firmware/network changes or speculative emergency-stop guarantee.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Record actual head positions, drive/turn direction and allowed routine effects through the approved app controls, attributed to source/host/target/sequence.
- [ ] AC2: Observe physical rest after release, stop and intent expiry within approved bounds, including cancellation around cam transitions. For permitted loss/claim/controller-failure tests, record stopping, continued or autonomous behavior and distinguish firmware action from writer action.
- [ ] AC3: Reconnect/restart does not replay motion or re-arm the app. Record any independent factory movement; demonstrate practical power-off/teardown and repeatable recovery.
- [ ] AC4: Issue a supported/refuted/inconclusive disposition for each required function and the supervised-use outcome. Unsafe-to-run, failed or missing required stop/loss evidence blocks a usable-motion claim. Reconcile [#594](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/594)'s own acceptance; only an explicit owner scope revision retires a requirement.

Delivery target: separately authorized physical acceptance and operational handoff.

## Meaningful deferrals

Unattended motion, long-running reliability, every built-in routine and additional hosts are outside this release. Revisit on an explicit use case after supervised acceptance; retain the accepted first slice if motion remains unqualified.

## Work assessment

Complexity: medium (finite physical sequences and evidence). Uncertainty: high (firmware and cam behavior unobserved). Impact: high (motion may persist or resume autonomously). issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Produce the accepted host/contract decisions and bounded experiment briefs for [#594](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/594). B.U.N.N.Y. controls are in scope; the open question is how to connect them to the one BLE writer.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: the pinned sources and evidence limits in [#594](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/594), current hub/controller contracts and owner preferences. Inspect protocol and reference-code provenance, licensing, notification parsing, routine effects, application-mode behavior, cam sequencing and cancellation. Distinguish source facts, third-party observations and unknown firmware behavior.

Compare the smallest viable BLE host choices for the existing Windows/WSL setup. A native Windows helper is a candidate; qualify adapter access and authenticated WSL-to-helper reachability before selecting it. Do not assume Windows loopback is reachable from WSL or alter network policy. Record owner decisions for the host, app controls, permitted routines and manual stop/recovery.

Define identity, capabilities, explicit commands, observations/freshness and failure semantics across UI, hub and writer. Current controller v1 and the hub kind allowlist do not automatically admit R2-D2. Identify the smallest approved contract/routing changes; do not disguise robot motion as a lighting or moment command. Refine/split dependent source work only where the accepted design warrants it.

Write finite lights/sounds and motion trial briefs: setup, allowed effects, attempts/duration, observations, abort/power-off recovery and supported/refuted/inconclusive next decisions. Host selection and code planning do not authorize running them.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve one writer, explicit BLE target enrollment, authentication, local exposure boundaries and existing consumers. Treat autonomy suppression separately from link health and command expiry. A source-derived sound/routine name is not proof of no motion.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: A cited protocol table records frame/notification validation, supported operations, unknowns and the independent report's conflicts; check code reuse terms before choosing reuse or reimplementation.
- [ ] AC2: The owner-approved host and UI/hub/writer contract has a concrete setup path, failure semantics and a comparison against existing consumer contracts. Unresolved decisions remain holds.
- [ ] AC3: Both physical briefs have finite bounds, a confirmed-target requirement and result-to-decision mapping; no physical observation is invented.
- [ ] AC4: Refine the children, native blockers and readiness using these decisions. Before implementation, name the issue-linked OpenSpec and exact build/type/test/consumer checks in the delivery plan and docs/development.md/CI as required.

issues.title: Integrate Hasbro Smart R2-D2 controls into B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Let the owner control one Hasbro Smart R2-D2 from the existing B.U.N.N.Y. app. The shared Amazon link resolves to ASIN B01LY1JOKV; Hasbro's Smart R2-D2 documentation identifies product B7493. Confirm the actual unit and BLE identity during qualification. App integration is required, not an optional follow-up or a standalone CLI finish line.

The first usable increment provides lights, selected built-in sounds/volume and truthful status. The full outcome adds supervised head movement, manual driving/turning and selected routines whose effects are qualified.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required native children:
1. [#595](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/595): qualify protocol evidence and select the host and integration contract.
2. [#596](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/596): deliver the first app-to-controller lights/sounds/status slice with fake BLE.
3. [#597](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/597): qualify that slice on the installed host and actual robot.
4. [#598](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/598): add bounded manual head/drive controls and selected routines in the app.
5. [#599](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/599): qualify physical motion, stop, loss and recovery from B.U.N.N.Y.

Each child consumes the preceding child's stated evidence. Native parent membership is not an additional dependency. New controller source belongs in this monorepo; retain one designated physical writer and the existing hub owner. Exact helper process/language and any shared-contract changes await [#595](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/595).

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Explicitly enrolled target; bounded commands; no replay after disconnect/restart. Preserve authorization and existing controllers. Distinguish sent, observed, stale, unknown and externally controlled state. A BLE connection does not prove exclusive app control, and a stop packet does not prove physical rest. Built-in routines may move the robot and need the motion gate.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: [#595](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/595) records accepted host/contract choices, protocol uncertainties and bounded physical briefs.
- [ ] AC2: [#596](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/596) and [#597](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/597) prove the owner can use B.U.N.N.Y. for the selected lights/sounds/status functions, with separate source, installed and physical receipts.
- [ ] AC3: [#598](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/598) and [#599](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/599) prove approved head, drive/turn and selected routine controls, including observed stopping and loss/reconnect behavior within accepted bounds.
- [ ] AC4: The handoff lets the owner start, stop and recover the setup; unsupported or unqualified actions stay unavailable. Epic closure requires this outcome, not child counts or source-only completion.

Delivery target: app integration plus separately authorized installation and physical acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

Autonomous navigation, agent-triggered motion, multi-robot support, remote exposure, firmware changes and replacement mobile apps are outside this release. Manual supervised control is the alternative; revisit on a new owner-selected use case. Custom speech/audio streaming, camera feeds and calibrated distance claims have no supporting evidence here and remain excluded pending capability research. MCP exposure and automatic agent-status reactions require an explicit later use case; the B.U.N.N.Y. UI is required now.

## Existing evidence and limits

- [Hasbro product documentation](https://instructions.hasbro.com/en-au/instruction/star-wars-smart-r2-d2) describes app-controlled movement, sounds and music routines. [Product link](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01LY1JOKV).
- [Community controller revision 79d55e4](https://github.com/elitistphoenix/r2d2-robot-apps/tree/79d55e41b87e6cecf169afcd96a78873cee32359/linux-controller) was inspected, not installed or run against hardware. It implements direct BLE using service `DAB91435-B5A1-E29C-B041-BCD562613BE4`, write characteristic `DAB91383-B5A1-E29C-B041-BCD562613BE4` and notify characteristic `DAB91382-B5A1-E29C-B041-BCD562613BE4`. Names `Kipps`/`2ndHeroD` are discovery hints, not verified identity.
- [Protocol source](https://github.com/elitistphoenix/r2d2-robot-apps/blob/79d55e41b87e6cecf169afcd96a78873cee32359/linux-controller/r2d2cli/protocol.py) defines head/motor/LED commands, indexed onboard audio, sequences, volume and input/IR/voltage notifications. `cam` means a mechanical cam, not a camera. No arbitrary audio-streaming or camera capability was established.
- [Client source](https://github.com/elitistphoenix/r2d2-robot-apps/blob/79d55e41b87e6cecf169afcd96a78873cee32359/linux-controller/r2d2cli/client.py) sends `50 8d` every two seconds; drive/turn selects a cam then waits 0.4 seconds before a motor write. Disconnect does not itself send motor-stop. These source behaviors are evidence to assess, not an accepted stop/reconnect design.
- An [independent builder's hardware report](https://mikefentonnz.github.io/projects/casio-calculator-r2d2-droidx.html) says `50 8d` suppresses autonomous behavior and its lapse can return the toy to its own behavior while BLE stays connected. It also disputes head-position decoding and reports an IR relationship. These are third-party observations, not verified on the owner's unit; do not treat the reported five-second interval as an accepted watchdog guarantee.
- [Bleak Windows backend](https://bleak.readthedocs.io/en/latest/backends/windows.html) supports native Windows Bluetooth. A Windows helper is a candidate, not a selected installation. WSL access, helper reachability and authentication need qualification without weakening the hub's loopback rules. Check the reference project's licensing/provenance before reusing code; original Hasbro binaries/assets are outside its stated license.

No APK recovery, installation, BLE scan, connection or physical test has been performed for this integration. Keep private device addresses, captures and credentials out of Git.

## Work assessment

Complexity: high (app, hub, BLE host and device state). Uncertainty: high (host/contract choices and physical behavior unqualified). Impact: high (moving hardware and cross-host command authority). Backlog; only the bounded qualification child is ready.

Planning assessment: 2026-09-29, [Hub revision a94b1ed](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a94b1ede0ef9b221311ee6e89718b7628c1f4dc3), docs/architecture.md, docs/controller-contract.md, docs/sdlc.md and live portfolio policy #536/#537. Searches for R2-D2 and Hasbro found no existing integration. Claptrap [#588](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/588) is related independent work, not a required prerequisite. Coordinate any overlapping contract, hub, dashboard, manifest or CI edits with their active owner; shared files alone create no dependency. No Project membership, Phase or Commitment is selected here.

The requesting owner owns scope and physical-test decisions; assign one coordinating writer at pickup. This planning record authorizes no implementation, installation, settings change or device command. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md for later delivery, including isolated work, applicable OpenSpec/build/type/test/CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, current-candidate UI approval, guarded merge and merged-main readback. Reassess after host/contract decisions or contradictory protocol or hardware evidence.
