issues.title: Qualify supervised Claptrap driving, stopping and recovery
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Observe the actual robot performing bounded manual movements and returning to rest under the agreed controls. Determine whether normal stop, lost connection and controller failure behavior are acceptable for supervised use; this is the final physical gate of [#588](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/588).

## Smallest useful implementation

Required source input: accepted [#592](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/592) revision, the stationary receipt from [#591](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/591), and the owner-approved motion brief. At pickup confirm exact device/IP, test operator, selected host, permission for motion/display changes, conservative speed/duration bounds, clear test area/containment and immediately accessible physical power-off.

Run only the brief's finite sequence: small forward/back and steering inputs, operator release/explicit stop, then controlled connection and controller-failure cases if the agreed setup can contain continued movement. Record measured or owner-observed results with their limits. Do not attempt a loss test if its consequence cannot be safely contained. Unexpected motion or a missed stop aborts the sequence; use the agreed physical recovery. No automatic retry or expanded test sequence.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One writer and one supervised operator; no background autonomy or reconnect replay. Keep uncertainty explicit when a camera view or transport response cannot establish physical rest. Stop the trial at its bound, on unexpected motion or when a physical stop cannot be confirmed. No firmware or network-infrastructure changes to force acceptance.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Record source/host/target/owner/sequence identities and observed direction/magnitude behavior for each authorized bounded input.
- [ ] AC2: Observe and record physical rest following release, explicit stop and intent expiry within the owner-approved bound. For permitted link-loss/controller-failure tests, record actual stop or continued-motion behavior; distinguish writer action from firmware action.
- [ ] AC3: Reconnect/restart is disarmed and produces no unrequested movement. Demonstrate recovery to manual/off state and preserve stationary controls.
- [ ] AC4: Issue a supported/refuted/inconclusive disposition for supervised driving, with limitations and evidence. Missing, unsafe-to-run or failed loss/stop acceptance remains pending and blocks a usable-motion claim; scope changes require the owner's decision. Reconcile the epic's own required finish line rather than closing it from child counts.

Delivery target: separately authorized physical acceptance and operational handoff. Offline or simulator checks do not satisfy these criteria.

## Meaningful deferrals

Unattended operation, navigation and repeated long-running reliability trials are outside this release. Revisit only after supervised acceptance and a new owner-selected use case. A refuted or inconclusive result keeps movement unqualified and allows the accepted stationary capability to remain useful.

## Work assessment

Complexity: medium (a bounded manual sequence and evidence reconciliation). Uncertainty: high (firmware motion/stop behavior unobserved). Impact: high (moving hardware and potentially ineffective software stop). Blocked on [#592](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/592) plus the explicit physical inputs and approved sequence at pickup. The owner can hold the trial without losing stationary acceptance.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-29. Alignment checked against [repository revision a94b1ed](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a94b1ede0ef9b221311ee6e89718b7628c1f4dc3), docs/architecture.md, docs/controller-contract.md, docs/sdlc.md, ADR 0003 and live #536/#537. Searches for Claptrap and robot work found no duplicate Claptrap issue. Existing device controllers and the shared state owner keep their responsibilities. Reassess on a protocol mismatch, changed owner scope, host selection, or failed physical observation.

This backlog record authorizes no implementation, installation, personal configuration changes or device commands. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md at pickup. Source work requires an isolated worktree, issue-linked OpenSpec where behavior changes, documented build/type/test commands and CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, guarded merge and merged-main evidence. A UI candidate, if introduced, needs the repository's human approval. Each physical trial additionally requires an identified owner, confirmed device IP and explicit permission for its exact sequence.

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Physical driving and stop qualification; keep unsafe or unobserved behavior unqualified.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Reviewed movement source from #592, accepted stationary receipt and exact physical target/operator/bounds/sequence authorization.

**Why:** The named prerequisite supplies decisions or evidence needed to choose a delivery strategy; planned checks do not establish readiness.

issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Provide the owner-approved stationary control surface from [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589): play a bounded local audio clip, obtain decoded camera output and inspect fresh/unknown status for one configured robot. Implement the accepted device writer and operator entrypoint with separate TCP control/status, paced UDP audio and bounded HTTP/frame decoding. Keep movement unavailable in this increment; send only the accepted neutral control state if the protocol needs a control session. Use synthetic audio/video/status fixtures and fake transports. Add the package's actual build/type/tests, documented verification entrypoints and applicable CI before product implementation. Scope the issue-linked OpenSpec to the selected stationary contract.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One explicitly configured robot and one writer. No scan, guessed IP, arbitrary destination tool argument or implicit networking on startup. Bound audio duration/buffering, camera frame sizes and pending work. Handle TCP fragmentation/coalescing and malformed input; a connection heartbeat does not refresh status. Cancel pending audio/video on stop or disconnect and never replay on reconnect. No microphone capture or recording retention by default. Keep current controller clients and APIs unchanged unless [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589) explicitly selects and links their expansion.

issues.title: Qualify the Claptrap protocol and define the first local-control release
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Produce a reviewable first-release contract and a bounded hardware-test plan for [#588](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/588). Ready for investigation and owner decisions only. The Android recovery and offline decoding work already exists; build on it instead of repeating an open-ended APK search.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: the pinned APK and offline receipts recorded in [#588](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/588), current architecture/SDLC and the owner's release preferences. No unresolved source issue blocks investigation.

Inspect the evidence and trace each supported operation to code/instruction locations. Define command frame fields, checksum, TCP framing, status interpretation and freshness, UDP PCM framing/pacing, and the video transform with size/error bounds. Record unsupported fields and unknown firmware behavior.

Settle with the owner: standalone first versus B.U.N.N.Y. in the first release; the initial host and manual Wi-Fi routing arrangement; the operator-facing control surface; camera output/retention and allowed audio inputs. Propose the smallest host and package using the monorepo's existing Node 24/TypeScript conventions. A robot-specific API is not automatically supported by controller v1: examine the current command union and identify any separately approved integration work instead of hiding drive/audio/video in lighting or moment commands.

Write the smallest later experiment briefs: stationary connectivity/audio/video and, separately, bounded manual movement/stop behavior. Each brief names the question, allowed effects, finite attempt/content bounds, owner observations, abort/recovery steps and supported/refuted/inconclusive outcomes. Explicit IP and device permission are required when those trials are picked up; no physical discovery runs here.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve one device writer, exact-target configuration, neutral initial state, no reconnect replay and privacy boundaries. Do not assume the direct Wi-Fi network is reachable from WSL or alter the current network to make it so. Distinguish a client timeout from a firmware watchdog and a neutral command from a verified stop. Treat the app as evidence, not code to vendor into the repository.

issues.title: Restore local control of the Claptrap-in-a-Box robot
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Restore useful control of the owner's Borderlands: The Handsome Collection Claptrap-in-a-Box robot after the original iPhone app became unavailable. One operator and one explicitly identified robot. The proposed first usable increment is stationary audio, camera and status; the full outcome includes supervised manual driving. Standalone local control versus B.U.N.N.Y. integration in the first release remains an owner decision in [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589).

## Smallest useful implementation

Required children, each with its own finish line:

1. [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589): preserve and qualify the Android protocol evidence; settle the first-release contract and experimental questions.
2. [#590](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/590): deliver the stationary controller against fake transports and synthetic fixtures.
3. [#591](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/591): qualify installation, routing, audible output and camera/status on the actual stationary robot.
4. [#592](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/592): deliver bounded, explicitly armed manual movement and stop handling after the stationary findings.
5. [#593](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/593): qualify supervised movement, stopping and recovery on the actual robot.

These are native sub-issues. Required-input edges are recorded on the children; parent membership is not an extra dependency. A first stationary release does not satisfy the driving finish line. New source belongs in this monorepo under the accepted new-controller direction; exact package/host/API choices are settled in [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589). One coordinating writer owns shared manifest/lockfile/CI work; do not change another controller's ownership. No portfolio Phase, Commitment or Project membership is selected by this backlog addition.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One designated device writer; an explicit target; bounded commands and buffers; manual control and power-off; no replay of audio or motion after reconnect/restart. Keep transport transmission, fresh status, audible/visible results and physical stopping distinct. Camera/audio stay local; do not capture microphones, retain recordings or expose services remotely by default. No firmware, router or firewall changes.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589) has an accepted scoped contract, evidence limitations and owner decisions; dependent implementation uses that version.
- [ ] AC2: [#590](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/590) and [#591](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/591) establish a repeatable stationary session with owner-selected audio, decoded camera output and truthful status. Source, installation and physical receipts are separate.
- [ ] AC3: [#592](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/592) and [#593](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/593) establish supervised manual driving and observed normal-stop/loss/restart behavior within accepted bounds. Sending neutral bytes alone is not physical-stop evidence.
- [ ] AC4: The owner can stop the controller, return to manual/off state and repeat the setup from its handoff. Unfinished or unsafe capabilities remain unavailable with a recorded limitation; they cannot be silently checked off.

Delivery target: source plus separately authorized installation and physical acceptance. The epic remains open until its own required outcome is evidenced or the owner explicitly revises it.

## Meaningful deferrals

Autonomous roaming, agent-triggered driving, obstacle avoidance, mapping, remote access, multiple robots, firmware replacement and a replacement mobile app are outside this outcome; manual supervised control is the alternative. Revisit only for an explicit new use case after acceptance. B.U.N.N.Y./MCP/dashboard inclusion is pending the first-release decision in [#589](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/589), not an assumed deletion of requested scope. Live microphone passthrough is a later explicit input/privacy choice; bounded local audio playback is the initial speaker path.

## Existing evidence — 2026-09-29

Android package `com.ych.standrobot`, version `3.0.2` / code `13`, recovered through [APKCombo](https://apkcombo.com/claptrapp/com.ych.standrobot/), 8,491,982 bytes. APK SHA-256: `681b487fbd569ed2c09b962af6831757f6dd23495573a63a127d915d29ddce7a`. Its legacy SHA-1 JAR signature verifies and all 187 payload digests match; there is no trusted publisher fingerprint comparison. This establishes internal consistency, not publisher authenticity or installation safety.

Static code identifies TCP control on the app's default `192.168.10.123:2000`, 22-byte frames about every 150 ms, UDP audio on 8081, and HTTP camera on 8080 with custom frame decoding. These are app defaults, not the owner's verified device address. The app streams its 15 bundled phrases; it does not merely send a phrase-selection command. Offline reconstruction matched 1,000 checksum cases and 100 valid/100 invalid synthetic video cases against ARM instruction blocks. This is neither full-app execution nor firmware or physical qualification.

Local evidence is retained under the canonical checkout's ignored `.local/evidence/claptrap-android/`: `apk-inspection.json`, `native-verification.json`, `verify_native.py`, `requirements-analysis.txt`, `libData-disassembly.txt`, the APK and decompiled classes. It is not publicly hosted or a tracked dependency; verify availability and the hash at pickup. Keep APKs, decompiled vendor implementation, voice assets, device identifiers and recordings outside Git. Publish authored protocol findings and synthetic fixtures only. [Original operation manual](https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1531651/Hyperion-Cl4p-Tp.html).

## Work assessment

Complexity: high (three transports, installed routing and a moving device). Uncertainty: high (no hardware observations, host and first-release boundary unselected). Impact: high (physical motion and private camera/audio). Status: backlog, not selected for execution. The qualification child is independently ready for bounded investigation; product work remains gated.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-29. Alignment checked against [repository revision a94b1ed](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a94b1ede0ef9b221311ee6e89718b7628c1f4dc3), docs/architecture.md, docs/controller-contract.md, docs/sdlc.md, ADR 0003 and live #536/#537. Searches for Claptrap and robot work found no duplicate Claptrap issue. Existing device controllers and the shared state owner keep their responsibilities. Reassess on a protocol mismatch, changed owner scope, host selection, or failed physical observation.

This backlog record authorizes no implementation, installation, personal configuration changes or device commands. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md at pickup. Source work requires an isolated worktree, issue-linked OpenSpec where behavior changes, documented build/type/test commands and CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, guarded merge and merged-main evidence. A UI candidate, if introduced, needs the repository's human approval. Each physical trial additionally requires an identified owner, confirmed device IP and explicit permission for its exact sequence.

**Note:** Claptrap control: stationary audio/video first, then supervised movement with separate physical acceptance.

## Execution recommendation

**Missing:** Accepted first-release boundary and host/interface choices from #589, followed by source and physical evidence from the required children.

issues.title: Diagnose intermittent owner startup timeout in Hub migration CI
issues.body:
## Failure and reproduction

P2: an intermittent startup timeout prevents a migration protection test from reaching its assertion and blocks shared CI. Observed during #543 / PR #581 merged-main validation at `69c02b5bd994ff4dfb5bf33b037d5db274178aa3` on 2026-09-29, in the Python 3.12 matrix job.

`apps/hub/tests/migration.test.mjs:134`, “activation rejects the host masquerading as a missing Pixoo consumer,” failed with `Error: owner-start-timeout` at `apps/hub/dist/migration.js:48:49` after about 8.75 seconds. The suite reported 157 tests, 156 passed and one failed. First attempt `bh9pv2805l` failed; retry `bj7z907n03` passed on the identical SHA with no source change.

[Depot job and attempts](https://depot.dev/orgs/0kwdkp3sc9/workflows/z84cjqn3wd?job=04bqqbcvzp&repo=jimmie-potts%2Fagent-device-hub). Raw failure/retry logs are retained privately with #543 evidence. Whether this is CI contention, fixture lifetime, or a runtime startup defect is unknown. No installed-runtime failure is established.

After the normal Node 24 build, begin with the named migration test and the same shared CI command/environment. Capture child startup/exit evidence, readiness timing and cleanup before deciding whether a test or product change is needed.

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish why the owner did not become ready, using a reproducer or attributable startup/process evidence.
- [ ] Preserve the missing-Pixoo-consumer rejection and bounded startup failure behavior; do not disable the protection, blindly inflate the timeout or rely on unconditional retries.
- [ ] Demonstrate the intended test reaches its rejection assertion, with a meaningful failure control, then run affected Hub/shared checks and normal PR/main CI.
- [ ] Record actual repeat-run count and residual uncertainty. Confirm no child processes remain after the fixture.

## Dependencies, verification and delivery target

Source/test reliability investigation. No installation, migration of live state or device contact. No new required prerequisite identified. Check current Hub migration and shared-CI owners before editing; #543 introduced no change to this test or runtime.

Scope assessment: complexity medium (child process/readiness protocol), uncertainty medium (cause unknown), impact medium (shared gate and migration protection). Keep in backlog until picked up; changes to actual migration ownership or timing require the repository's contract and review gates. No broad runtime redesign is authorized by this report.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Note:** Diagnose why the Hub migration protection test timed out before its assertion in CI.
**Workaround:** Preserve failure evidence and use only the existing bounded retry procedure; a passing retry does not diagnose startup behavior.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Add everyday controls for qualified Twinkly Generation I strings to the existing B.U.N.N.Y. device experience. This is a future source deliverable, to be refined after [qualification #573](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/573) selects a viable owner and per-model capabilities. Do not add Home Assistant solely for this feature if the direct local route qualifies.

## Refine before implementation

- Give each configured set a neutral device identity and one designated writer. Keep addresses and credentials private. Route commands through the Hub's guarded controller boundary and the existing B.U.N.N.Y. component view; inspection and reconnect must send no light commands.
- Expose power and brightness only where #573 verifies support. Consider static color and saved-effect selection only when their model/firmware behavior and contract mapping are qualified. Twinkly's newer [Scenes feature excludes Generation I](https://help.twinkly.com/hc/en-gb/articles/31045049635485-What-is-the-Scene-Feature-and-How-to-Use-It); do not equate it with a saved effect or silently reuse `scene.activate`.
- Preserve separate desired, observed, stale, pending, failed and uncertain states. Serialize writes per set, bound retries, and never treat a transport acknowledgment as visible success. Show unsupported or unavailable controls with an explanation.
- Define issue-linked OpenSpec work and proportionate build/type/product tests in docs/development.md and CI before implementation. Cover different firmware capabilities, offline sets, concurrent commands, app changes, reconnect and ambiguous replies with fakes. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md, including independent reviews, applicable CI, and approval of the current UI candidate.

## Outside the first release

Automatic agent-status lighting, synchronized multi-set effects, per-LED streaming, Twinkly app group control, music mode, firmware changes and installation. Add bounded follow-up issues only if qualified and wanted.

issues.title: Migrate the runtime from WSL to the Mac mini
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-28 from the Mac mini hosting plan (#44). Deferred until the owner has the Mac and the stories below are done. Publishing authorizes no installation or device change; the cutover itself needs the owner's explicit request.

### Outcome and real setup

The six runtime services run in the Mac mini's Linux machine, the WSL units are stopped and disabled, and every device shows agent status and music from the Mac.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Pre-check:** #565, #566, #567, [codex-nanoleaf#200](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/200) and [divoom-app-upgrade#14](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/14) are done, and #44's ADR is merged.
2. **Stop and disable** the WSL units first, so each device keeps one writer.
3. **Install and move state** in the Mac machine:
   - **Hub:** a stopped copy of its state. Use [#427](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/427)'s release layout if it has landed, otherwise the current install procedure. Hub state is inside the Nanoleaf state directory today, so coordinate the layout with [codex-nanoleaf#200](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/200).
   - **Local controller host:** Tidbyt credentials copied privately, and the LIFX leases.
   - **Nanoleaf:** its procedure in [codex-nanoleaf#200](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/200).
   - **Pixoo:** its offline export and import bundle (Pixoo ADR 0016).
4. **Keep the hook producers in WSL** (the hook scripts). Only the owner moves.
5. **Start the tunnel** and check each device with the owner present.
6. **Rollback:** stop the Mac units and re-enable the WSL units ([#356](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/356)'s keep-alive).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One agent-state owner and one writer per device at every step.
- No SQLite file is opened on two hosts.
- Credentials are copied privately, never through Git or issue text.
- Manual control keeps working.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- With the owner present, the Nanoleaf, Pixoo, Tidbyt, LIFX and HT-A9 source each respond from the Mac.
- A Claude session and a Codex session on the PC appear on the devices.
- After a Mac restart and the owner's sign-in, all six units are active.
- One closing comment is the acceptance record.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Removing the WSL runtime:** the owner's choice after a quiet week.
- **Tronbyt:** #23 and #24.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-28.

- **Complexity: high.** Six services, three state moves, one writer per device.
- **Uncertainty: medium.**
- **Impact: high.** A wrong order could produce two writers or lost device state; rollback is re-enabling the WSL units.
- **Readiness:** deferred until the hardware arrives and the listed stories are done.

issues.title: Push Codex Desktop read state from the PC to the Mac-hosted hub
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-28 from the Mac mini hosting plan (#44). Deferred until the Mac hosts the runtime; the hub keeps reading the mounted Codex home while it runs in WSL.

### Outcome and real setup

Codex Desktop unread and read evidence keeps reaching the hub after it moves to the Mac mini. Today the hub reads `.codex-global-state.json` from the mounted Windows Codex home every 2 seconds. On the Mac it can't see `/mnt/c`, and the PC is the only place Codex Desktop runs.

### Smallest useful implementation

- A small relay mode of the hub package runs in WSL. It reuses the hub's existing Codex Desktop reader on the same file and interval, and pushes only changes to the hub through the tunnel (#566) on an authenticated route.
- When configured for relay, the hub accepts the pushed state instead of reading a path.
- An issue-linked OpenSpec change covers the new route.
- Later PC-only inputs reuse the relay: [#380](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/380) (the Steam client), PC lighting and desktop controls.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Freshness stays distinct from read evidence. If the relay stops, the hub marks the source stale; it never treats the thread as read or unread.
- No inference from missing evidence.
- Only allowlisted metadata is pushed, never transcript content.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Hub tests with a fake file and a fake relay:
  - a change is pushed once;
  - an unchanged file is not re-sent;
  - a stopped relay becomes stale, not read;
  - an unauthorized push is rejected.
- After the cutover, reading a thread in Codex Desktop clears its attention on a device.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Hook-triggered pushes:** read state changes without a Codex hook, so the relay keeps the existing 2-second local poll.

issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-28 from the Mac mini hosting plan (#44). Deferred until the Mac hosts the runtime; current PC hooks and browsers keep using the WSL runtime unchanged.

### Outcome and real setup

After the cutover (#568), everything on the PC keeps reaching B.U.N.N.Y. at the same `127.0.0.1` ports, while the runtime runs on the Mac mini. That covers:
- Claude and Codex hooks in WSL;
- Codex Desktop hooks through `wsl.exe`;
- the Windows browser, through WSL's localhost forwarding;
- MCP clients.

### Smallest useful implementation

- One documented WSL systemd user unit that keeps an SSH tunnel open to the Mac's Linux machine, with automatic restart:
  - `ssh -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -L 127.0.0.1:<port>:127.0.0.1:<port> ...`
  - Forward the loopback ports PC clients use today: hub 8788, Nanoleaf map 8765 and MCP 41230, Pixoo 8787. Confirm the list at pickup.

- Docs in `apps/hub/SETUP.md`.
- [#378](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/378) (Steam Deck) can reuse the same pattern.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The hub, hooks, and Host and Origin checks stay loopback-only, and no LAN listener is added.
- Hooks fail open and never delay an agent: with the tunnel down, or the Mac off, a hook returns within its existing timeout.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- With the tunnel up, a Claude session and a Codex session on the PC show in B.U.N.N.Y. on the Mac.

issues.title: Decide whether a prefetched Hub page may sign in
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The Hub's trusted-loopback sign-in (#276, #419) admits a page request with `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` and no `Origin`. That is how a typed address, a bookmark or a system-browser open arrives.

Chromium sends a speculation-rules prefetch of a document (`<script type="speculationrules">{"prefetch":…}</script>`) the same way. When the user activates the prefetched page, the dashboard runs same-origin and signs in. So a cross-site page, including a public-address-space page, can lead the owner into a signed-in dashboard even though a direct cross-site navigation is refused. The Standards review of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/562 (S2) reproduced this with a `localhost` page linking to `127.0.0.1`, and with a page overridden to the public address space.

This predates #561, which leaves the `none` admission unchanged. #562 corrects the docs to state the actual boundary, and adds `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

## Smallest useful implementation

This needs the owner's decision: legitimate bookmarks and system-browser opens also send `none`. Options:
- Refuse prefetch and prerender requests for the page (`Sec-Purpose: prefetch` or `Purpose: prefetch`), so a prefetched copy never exists and the activation becomes a direct navigation the Hub judges normally. Verify what Chromium and Edge send.
- Also add `Supports-Loading-Mode` or cache headers so an activation cannot reuse a prefetched response.
- Or accept the residual risk and record it: the local-only exposure is one signed-in tab, with COOP severing the opener.

## Observable acceptance

A cross-site page's speculation-rules prefetch and activation no longer yield a signed-in session, while a bookmark and a typed address still sign in. A Chromium test covers both.

## Evidence

The round 1 Standards review on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/562.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The owner must choose whether to accept sign-in exposure during prefetch or use a different cache/prefetch design, with the browser evidence and acceptance checks for that choice.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** The issue records a deferred or unsettled definition. This assessment preserves that gap and does not change readiness, labels, scope or existing ratings.

The Standards review of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/562 (S2) reproduced this with a `localhost` page linking to `127.0.0.1`, and with a page overridden to the public address space.

This predates #561, which leaves the `none` admission unchanged. #562 corrects the docs to state the actual boundary, and adds `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
This needs the owner's decision: legitimate bookmarks and system-browser opens also send `none`. Options:
- Refuse prefetch and prerender requests for the page (`Sec-Purpose: prefetch` or `Purpose: prefetch`), so a prefetched copy never exists and the activation becomes a direct navigation the Hub judges normally. Verify what Chromium and Edge send.
- Also add `Supports-Loading-Mode` or cache headers so an activation cannot reuse a prefetched response.
- Or accept the residual risk and record it: the local-only exposure is one signed-in tab, with COOP severing the opener.

issues.title: Make the guide's B.U.N.N.Y. Local entry open or stop linking to a refused page
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The work guide's Places link **B.U.N.N.Y. · Local** (`docs/skins/places.json:8`, `localUrl` `http://127.0.0.1:8788/`) still shows the Hub's Forbidden error. That is true whether the guide is opened from a `file://` path or from the public Pages edition. Chromium sends both as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. The #561 worker confirmed this with a logging-server probe (`chromium-fetch-metadata-probe.txt` under the canonical `.local/evidence/gh-561-hub-navigation/`).

#561 (PR #562) admits only same-site navigations from other local apps. It deliberately keeps cross-site refused, because such a request carries nothing that tells the guide apart from any website. This link therefore stays broken and has no failing check.

## Smallest useful implementation

This needs the owner's decision on the approach first. Options:
- Show the guide's local B.U.N.N.Y. entry as a copyable address or bookmark hint instead of a link. The guide cannot be told apart from any website.
- Serve the guide's local edition from a loopback origin (for example, from the Hub itself or another local app on 127.0.0.1), so the link becomes same-site.
- Leave it, but mark the entry in the guide as "open from a bookmark", and add a check that fails while it is a live link that cannot open.

## Observable acceptance

The guide's B.U.N.N.Y. · Local entry either opens the signed-in dashboard, or no longer presents a link that returns Forbidden. A check fails if the broken form comes back.

## Evidence

issues.title: Close the remaining app-verify redaction edges
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The `@jimmie-potts/app-verify` 1.1 `redact()` replaces absolute paths outside a run's two roots in failure details and in check and capture reasons. The final #554 reviews left small edges that don't break the documented rule but could keep sensitive text.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **URL userinfo (S10):** URLs are kept whole, including userinfo (`https://user:tok@host/...`) and absolute paths embedded in a query. Replace userinfo with `<credentials>@`, and apply the path rule inside queries, or redact query values.
- **Colon-joined lists (S11):** a colon-joined list such as `PATH=` is judged by its first segment only. Split on `:` and judge each segment.
- **Trailing dot and home paths (P-S7):** a trailing `.` is taken into a path. Home-relative `~/…` paths are kept.
- **Assertion names:** these are written as given. Document that, or redact them.
- **Windows paths:** Windows `C:\…` paths are kept. This matters once #497 runs Windows-side checks.

## Behavior to preserve

Paths inside the roots, full http and ws URLs without credentials, linear performance on large inputs, and the 1000-character cap.

## Observable acceptance

Unit cases for each form above; each is redacted, and in-root paths and plain URLs are kept.

## Evidence

Final review reports on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/554.

issues.title: Define the Ask v1 request, ranked-result and failure contract
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509. Owner-authorized reconciliation, 2026-09-30. This defines backlog work, not implementation or contract acceptance.

## Outcome and real setup

One approved Ask boundary connects the local signed-in Hub to Jev and the shared Guide records/components. A submitted question returns ranked existing epic/issue references with source-backed template reasons, or a useful no-match/clarification/failure result. This consolidates the v1 obligations previously split across #544, #546 and #548; #545 continues to own records and component inputs.

## Smallest useful implementation

Define request identity, question and optional explicit repository scope, dataset/release/catalog binding, the minimal allowlisted model projection and a bounded ranked result. Use #545's accepted projection, stable IDs, closure/acceptance distinctions and compatible release rules. Resolve trusted links, exact counts and graph facts in code. Results contain existing references, supported reason codes and typed evidence; they contain no arbitrary layouts, HTML/JSX/code, URLs or invented facts. One result schema serves the ordinary shared card renderer.

Include the existing Hub origin/authentication boundary, server-side credentials and fixed provider endpoints. Specify concrete request/candidate/result bounds, timeout, bounded retry and usage-limit semantics before implementation. Distinguish valid empty/no good match, clarification, missing data, unavailable configuration/provider, denied access, incompatible dataset/catalog, invalid decision, timeout, superseded request and usage-limit outcomes. issues.title: Adopt separate contract issues and a verifiable human approval gate
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make Hub contract changes separately traceable and require Jimmie's approval of the exact definition before adoption and dependent implementation. Apply the shared rule from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/87 to the SDLC, agent instructions and delivery checks. This issue plans the rule; creating it does not enable enforcement.

## Smallest useful implementation

Update docs/sdlc.md, AGENTS.md and the relevant issue/PR guidance to identify a dedicated contract issue, canonical artifact/version, producers/consumers, compatibility and approval evidence. Link dependent stories with native blocked-by relationships. Apply the rule during ordinary assessment and explicitly invoked planning/delivery methods without requiring implicit skill invocation. Reuse the shared procedure instead of copying its full implementation into Hub.

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240 for GitHub/Depot capabilities, approval identity/trusted-publisher qualification and guide-only CI handling. This issue consumes those findings, selects the contract approval mechanism and implements the smallest testable local validator/check wiring the qualified mechanism supports. Do not duplicate #240's platform investigation. If the platform cannot enforce human provenance under shared credentials, keep adoption blocked on an owner-selected mechanism; never describe an agent-editable approval field as a human gate.

Require the validator to bind the contract issue, artifact/version/digest, approval actor/evidence and consumer references to the candidate actually being adopted. Missing, stale, withdrawn, mismatched or unreadable evidence blocks adoption. Candidate PR content must not execute with approval-publisher credentials or manufacture success. Register known contract paths and declarations; independent review must also detect undeclared semantic boundary changes. A path filter cannot prove that all contract changes were declared.

Contract definitions can be drafted and reviewed before approval. Merge/adoption and dependent behavior wait for human approval of that exact definition plus the existing source gates. Reapproval follows definition changes; unchanged approved reuse retains evidence. Issue closure follows merged canonical content, approved-content comparison, main checks and tracker readback. A separate implementation story must not bypass this by declaring its own contract already accepted.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep independent Standards/Specification review, applicable Depot checks, guarded merge, merged-main verification and explicit installation/device authority. Preserve the guide UI exemption, while stating that it does not exempt contracts. Reconcile a required contract check with the guide-only CI filter through #240; do not bypass a pending required check or emit dummy success. Workflow/policy changes receive full applicable CI.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Shared guidance https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/87 and #240's qualification are accepted inputs, with native blocked-by links and no dependency cycle.
- [ ] The SDLC, AGENTS and issue/PR instructions describe the same lifecycle, approval evidence, unchanged reuse and closeout rules. They identify how to handle a contract discovered mid-delivery and how to keep consumers blocked.
- [ ] The selected approval mechanism demonstrably distinguishes owner approval from an agent assertion under shared credentials, binds exact approved content, and rejects amended content. The owner approves the concrete policy/mechanism before activation.
- [ ] Meaningful negative checks cover absent contract issue, missing/stale/withdrawn approval, wrong actor/source/version, unreadable evidence, candidate-created proof, altered contract content and skipped/failed required checks. Positive checks cover unchanged approved reuse and a properly approved new version.
- [ ] Planned required-check behavior covers ordinary, guide-only and mixed changes and uses trusted inputs. Record what source tests establish and what still needs a separately authorized GitHub configuration/trial.
- [ ] Use Node 24, npm ci, npm run check:workflow and npm run test:workflow; report the actual specification inventory and add any focused validator checks to docs/development.md and CI. Follow current local instructions at pickup and preserve independent review/main-CI gates.
- [ ] Read back a representative contract/consumer chain, including the Jev contract issues under #509. Keep unapproved contracts pending and do not close them through this policy issue.

Delivery target: source-only policy, templates and qualified validator/check integration. Live account, ruleset, credentials, check-publisher setup or skill installation requires separately authorized named work; source success is not proof that GitHub currently prevents a merge. If no enforceable mechanism is qualified, keep that acceptance open and report the procedural boundary.

## Meaningful deferrals

No new general contract registry service, external governance platform or automatic rewrite of old contracts. Record existing accepted versions for reuse only when evidence exists; changed or previously unapproved definitions need review. issues.title: Epic: Adopt outcome-based phase planning with GitHub Projects
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make the growing B.U.N.N.Y. backlog manageable through outcome phases while keeping a small, explicit near-term commitment. Use one GitHub Project across Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo, existing repository issues for delivery, and the work guide for explanation and discovery. One owner chooses priorities; agents maintain the agreed records during authorized work.

## Smallest useful implementation

Adopt the planning contract, configure a bounded Project pilot, define routine SDLC maintenance and evaluate actual delivery-and-replanning cycles. Use themes for enduring areas, epics for bounded outcomes, delivery issues for independently verifiable increments and checklists for implementation details. Native parent/sub-issue membership and native prerequisites remain distinct. GitHub Project Phase and Commitment fields add portfolio intent without replacing issue scope or workflow authority.

A phase describes a capability outcome with a bounded set of required epics, known entry conditions and observable exit evidence. Phase membership is separate from workflow state and from Now/Next/Later/Ideas commitment. Replenish a small Now queue when capacity opens; reassess on accepted increments, blockers, material learning and phase decisions. Independent work can cross phase boundaries when its real prerequisites permit. Dates record evidence or genuine external deadlines, not automatic start/finish gates. Tests and acceptance remain part of each delivered increment.

Required delivery work:
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536 — agree outcome phases, entry/exit evidence, Now/Next/Later selection and field ownership.
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/537 — qualify access, configure/reuse the Project and seed a bounded pilot.
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/538 — maintain Project state through the existing SDLC with truthful readback.

Additional required source input through #539: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/646 — deliver and accept the epic issue template before the pilot review closes. This is a prerequisite link, not a change to the existing native parent/child grouping.

The required order is rules → setup → SDLC → observed pilot review. Source inspection and drafting can overlap, but downstream acceptance needs the named inputs. No new issue is required for every backlog idea. #498 and #509 are pilot examples, not a promise to deliver both first.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Issues remain authoritative for scope, acceptance, dependencies and delivery status. Project fields own only agreed planning intent; the work guide/Jev are consumers. Ready is not Selected, no blockers is not Ready, and issue closure is not installed or physical acceptance. Keep one coordinator for writes and all existing delivery gates. Creating this epic authorizes neither Project/account configuration nor product implementation.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] EP4: Actual pilot observations support an explicit keep/simplify/change decision and a continue/revise/advance decision for the phase and queue. - [ ] EP5: All required children meet their own acceptance; optional work remains separately visible. Evidence: native child/readback inspection and the accepted pilot decision. Closing this epic does not close #498/#509 or imply their product delivery.

Use manual agent maintenance and GitHub editing first; revisit automation or more repositories only after observed need. Public guide refresh/publication remains separately authorized.

## Owner planning selection — 2026-09-27 UTC

The owner accepted the detailed [#536 decision record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536): current Ask the guide phase anchored by #509 and its required acceptance; coarse later development-activity Status-page direction anchored by the first history-based slice of #283; one #509 child in Now (#543); #545 then #544 as preferred order once ready; #498 visible without a near-term commitment; private owner-only pilot across Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo with Nanoleaf #162 and Pixoo #96 as unselected examples. Only Phase and Commitment are custom planning fields. Priority and Size are omitted for the pilot. #540 and optional Jev ideas remain outside closure. This is planning and Project-setup authority, not authorization for product or device work.

## Pilot setup status — 2026-09-27 UTC

#536 and #537 are accepted and closed. The owner approved the current five-view layout after inspecting all saved views. [B.U.N.N.Y. Portfolio](https://github.com/users/jimmie-potts/projects/1) is private with Phase and Commitment as its two custom planning fields and 28 bounded pilot issue items; #543 alone is Now. #537 records field, membership, visibility, saved grouping, mobile screenshot and owner approval evidence. The earlier discovery/setup uncertainty is resolved. The next action is the bounded read-only pilot-evidence review under #539, without changing selection or restarting optional work.

issues.title: Publish the portfolio Project and show Phase and Commitment in the Guide
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The public Guide displays the owner's portfolio choices alongside the same issue facts used elsewhere. The existing B.U.N.N.Y. Portfolio becomes public during this story's later authorized delivery, after checking its current contents. This extension is selected for the Guide rebuild; it no longer waits for the broader delivery-cycle pilot.

Named Project: https://github.com/users/jimmie-potts/projects/1, owner `jimmie-potts`, currently identified as `PVT_kwHOAu24Wc4Bkz2N`. Refresh identity, audience and content at pickup. Publishing this issue does not change Project visibility or membership.

## Smallest useful implementation

Reuse accepted setup https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/537 and the shared browser/records from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511. Show epic summaries, a read-only Commitment board and an ordered, date-free Phase view using the same components and IDs. Keep all issues available, including nonmembers and unassigned work.

Built-in GitHub fields and native issue state, labels, parents and blockers retain their authority. Phase and Commitment are the only custom planning fields. Phase order is owner intent, not a fabricated dependency; readiness does not choose Commitment. Honor the accepted inheritance rule from the native parent and show unavailable/conflicting ancestry rather than guessing. Show phase outcome/entry/exit evidence when recorded; do not infer phase completion from closed cards.

Read the Project outside the browser with a qualified credential and explicit allowed fields. A public Project does not make the repository-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN sufficient for the Projects API. Choose and document the least-privilege working access path during delivery, with no token values in artifacts or logs. Update private-Project wording in the owning procedure after the verified visibility change.

Review all current Project items, draft content and field values immediately before making it public. Confirm the intended public audience and then verify anonymous viewing. If that review finds unapproved content, keep the visibility change pending and report the specific decision needed; do not silently publish it.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Project selection is a projection of owner choices, not a second issue store or an approval. Preserve native readiness, blockers, closure reason and source/installed acceptance. No auto-replenishment or inferred priority. Private repository/draft content and unapproved fields must not enter public outputs merely because another referenced issue is public.

Pagination failure, denied access, renamed/missing fields, stale values and a verified empty result are distinct. Project enrichment is optional for issue browsing and publication under #545/#317: its failure must not freeze an otherwise valid complete issue inventory. A failed Project read retains the last complete permitted snapshot with its original observation time, or reports unavailable; it cannot silently clear owner selections or make cached values appear newly collected. An optional parse failure is represented explicitly before validation; it never excuses invalid required records or an unsafe public artifact. Do not merge partial Project pages into cached or current values.

Recheck that cached fields remain allowed for the public output. Known private/unapproved data or withdrawn publication permission cannot be republished from cache. Keep build time, issue collection time and Project observation time distinct. Preserve the owner's phase sequence through normalization, hashing and rendering using #545's order-sensitive identity rules.

An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: A current content/audience audit, explicit named visibility action and anonymous readback establish public Project access. Existing item selection and Phase/Commitment values are preserved; no new custom fields are created.
- [ ] AC2: Every displayed field traces to its named native or Project source. Fixtures cover field/option changes, missing parents, mixed fresh/stale reads, not-planned closure and unassigned/nonmember issues.
- [ ] AC3: Board, phase and epic views reuse the browser's components and IDs. Unique counts agree, cross-repository children work, phase order does not create blockers, and absent exit evidence never marks a phase complete.
- [ ] AC4: Complete, partial, denied and verified-empty API fixtures prove safe fallback without erasing selections. Public-artifact/network inspections contain no credentials or unapproved data.
- [ ] AC5: Keyboard/mobile/print/search/brief checks pass. Run relevant browser/adapter and normal applicable source checks. Record source acceptance and Project configuration/anonymous readback separately.

- [ ] AC6: An unavailable/partial/denied Project read with a complete valid issue inventory still permits a browsable candidate and publication eligibility. Fixtures exercise both a permitted older snapshot (original timestamp and stale status visible) and no permitted cache (explicit unavailable); neither creates a fresh or empty selection. A permission/audience change prevents replay of disallowed cached data. Reordering Phase options changes the owning content identity and displayed order without inventing dependencies; API item enumeration alone does not.

Delivery target: source views and the named Project visibility/access setup with readback, subject to the checkpoint above. #317 owns public Guide deployment. No credential configuration or Project change occurs in this planning pass.

## Meaningful deferrals

No editing or drag-to-change-state controls, new Project, priority/size fields or background write synchronization. Use GitHub for edits. #521/#522 retain semantic selection and saved-question ideas. This story does not require Jev or the full assistant.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium; impact high because visibility and credentials cross a public boundary. Blocked on #511; #537 is the accepted setup input. issues.title: Evaluate and qualify ranked Ask v1 against ordinary search
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509. Owner-authorized reconciliation, 2026-09-30. This defines backlog work, not implementation or contract acceptance.

## Outcome and real setup

Decide from evidence whether ranked Ask v1 helps the owner find work more reliably or easily than ordinary search. Qualify the useful request/result experience independently of later pins, undo and motion.

## Smallest useful implementation

Run #510's frozen 20-development/20-held-out corpus against #512's implemented ranked-results flow. Tune only with development cases; freeze model/configuration, retrieval, #545 dataset/catalog and #547 contract revisions before held-out evaluation. Use #510's local receipt format. Compare relevance, required-item coverage, factual/graph errors, clarification/no-match behavior, latency, reported cost and manual corrections against the same ordinary-search baseline. Keep failed and slow cases, realistic data defects and adversarial issue text; separate data, retrieval, model-selection and renderer failures.

Required inputs: #510 and #512. #514/#515 are later extension evaluations, not prerequisites. Any live paid trial requires explicit authorization, credentials and a spending cap before it runs. Missing live access keeps model quality pending; offline source checks alone do not establish it. Prepare setup/disable/recovery guidance and a named installed-trial handoff; do not install as part of source work.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub owns work facts and native relationships. Use #545 records, public projection and evidence rules; source, installed/client and physical acceptance stay distinct. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. Missing/stale data stays visible. An incomplete seven-day completion read is a visible partial-history gap, not a failure of an otherwise valid publication; required open inventory and relationship reads retain #545's fatal rules. Render issue text literally and treat it as data, never model instructions. No GitHub mutations, device commands, credentials or private runtime/session data enter the model projection. Ground truth is independently labeled; Jev does not grade itself. Usability observation is evidence about usefulness, not a reinstated UI-approval gate.

No project UI requires human UI approval under the owner's 2026-09-30 decision. UI/browser/accessibility validation, independent review and CI remain. Contract approval and separately scoped installation, publication, paid-trial and device decisions retain their own gates. #657 aligns the remaining source instructions.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: The implemented v1 source/browser and contract regressions pass at recorded revisions, including explicit submission, no ordinary-use inference, public projection and failure/reset behavior. Use the new generator's checks; retired topic/no-drift machinery is not a requirement.
- [ ] AC2: A reproducible held-out comparison reports every case, required-item omissions, factual errors, acceptable alternative rankings, latency and known/unknown cost. Do not tune on held-out outcomes or silently exclude failures.
- [ ] AC3: Pixoo GIF requests and at least two other domains exercise question, ranked shared cards, evidence/links, ambiguity, reset and outage fallback. #510's alternatives and scoped limitations are preserved. Pins/undo and spatial motion are not required.
- [ ] AC4: Record proceed/revise/stop against the predeclared rubric, with honest limits. Paid trial authorization and spend cap are recorded separately; absent live evidence cannot be called model-quality acceptance or epic completion.
- [ ] AC5: Trace representative results through #511's inventory audit and #545's evidence rules, including missing acceptance, cancelled prerequisites, optional enrichment gaps, stale sources and version mismatches. Data limitations remain distinct from selection errors.
- [ ] AC6: #510 receipts reproduce case/split, source/catalog/candidate/model/configuration versions and actual outcomes. Source, installed-client and live-provider acceptance are separate; before this issue closes, its coordinating writer records or links the installed Ask follow-up issue and names the trial owner, selected source revisions, observable live acceptance, setup/disable/recovery steps, separate installation and any paid-trial authority, and next action. Link the follow-up under #509 as required installed acceptance; it remains open until evidenced or explicitly revised by the owner. Do not claim installation from the evaluation report or close #509 while that obligation is unresolved.

Delivery target: source-only unless a separately authorized trial is named. These checks are planned, not executed. Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change where behavior/contracts change, the owning Hub/Guide checks in docs/development.md and applicable shared checks. Keep independent Standards/Specification review, current-revision CI and merged-main readback. No installation, public publication, device operation or paid inference is authorized by this planning update.

## Meaningful deferrals

No workflow-skill benchmark, LangGraph qualification, general dashboard adoption, mandatory production telemetry or evaluation of undelivered motion/refinement. Those extensions receive their own scoped validation if selected.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty high until real model usefulness/latency are measured; impact medium for adoption and misleading recommendations. Blocked on #510 and #512. Choose trial settings only after those inputs and the authorized budget are known.

Planning evidence: live issue bodies/comments, native relationships and scoped Project fields read on 2026-09-30; owner-selected browser-first and ranked-results direction. Reassess at pickup, when accepted inputs change, or if ownership, audience or operational scope expands.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Measure ranked Ask against search using frozen cases; richer motion and refinement are later.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Approved #547 boundary, delivered #512 experience, frozen #510 corpus and authorized live-trial settings/budget are required before choosing the qualification session.
**Work surface:** UI

**Why:** High uncertainty is live usefulness, not missing coding effort; offline fixtures cannot qualify the provider.
**Reassess when:** The active owner or required acceptance evidence changes.

One Ask contract, ranked v1, later independent motion/refinement and optional-enrichment cutover rules assessed. No planned product behavior or trial was implemented by these tracker edits. Alignment correction readback: accepted #545 prerequisite and partial-history semantics clarified; original scope, capability ratings and session strategy retained. No implementation, installation or trial performed. · fingerprint: `a4793e87909d`

issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509. Owner-authorized reconciliation, 2026-09-30. This defines backlog work, not implementation or contract acceptance.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner submits a question on the local signed-in Hub and gets ranked existing epics/issues with template reasons and links into the ordinary Guide. The result uses #511’s reusable issue-card and epic components.

## Smallest useful implementation

Deliver one vertical slice through the existing Hub: protected route, server-side provider adapter, validated request/result boundary and shared renderer. Required inputs are #547's approved Ask v1 contract and #511's accepted browser/data adapter/components. Consume #545's compatible records/catalog and #317's artifact interface; use fixture artifacts before live hosting, with no second GitHub collector. #544/#546/#548 are consolidated into #547 and no longer separate prerequisites.

Open with a useful complete ordinary browser or direct access to it; page load, navigation, filters and refresh make no model call. Only explicit submission invokes Jev. Rank existing references; render code-owned template reasons and trusted links. Show no good match/clarification, missing evidence and unavailable-provider states without inventing work. A new question or reset invalidates older replies. Reset returns to the ordinary complete browser without inference, and a late reply cannot replace it. Keep credential/auth/origin checks, fixed endpoints and bounded usage server-side. #510's corpus is frozen before tuning; offline fake-provider implementation does not wait for corpus freeze.

The work canvas is a later interaction design reference, not a requirement that v1 opens empty or rearranges itself. Pins, undo and richer composition/motion are separate later work.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub owns work facts and native relationships. Use #545 records, public projection and evidence rules; source, installed/client and physical acceptance stay distinct. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. Missing/stale data stays visible. An incomplete seven-day completion read is a visible partial-history gap, not a failure of an otherwise valid publication; required open inventory and relationship reads retain #545's fatal rules. Render issue text literally and treat it as data, never model instructions. No GitHub mutations, device commands, credentials or private runtime/session data enter the model projection.

No project UI requires human UI approval under the owner's 2026-09-30 decision. UI/browser/accessibility validation, independent review and CI remain. Contract approval and separately scoped installation, publication, paid-trial and device decisions retain their own gates. #657 aligns the remaining source instructions.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Fake-provider integration traces a typed question through allowed public records to ranked references, validated template reasons and the same issue-card/epic implementations used by the browser. No invented URLs, graph facts or authoritative model prose are rendered.
- [ ] AC2: Reject injected instructions, unknown IDs, unsupported evidence, duplicate/excessive results and dataset/catalog mismatch before display. A payload test proves the provider sees only the submitted question and the approved public projection.
- [ ] AC3: Missing configuration, denied auth, timeout, provider errors, invalid decisions, no match and incomplete evidence yield distinct truthful states with ordinary search/browser fallback. A failed request preserves the last valid view with its actual provenance.
- [ ] AC4: Loopback auth/origin/limit checks show no browser-visible provider secret, no GitHub/device writes and no paid API requirement for source validation.
- [ ] AC5: Browser checks show zero model calls on open/browse/filter/reset, explicit submission only, and no late response after reset or a newer question. Keep keyboard, mobile, reduced-motion and task-brief access.
- [ ] AC6: Data fixtures cover optional Project/recommendation gaps, unsupported schema versions, cancelled/not-planned prerequisites, accepted replacements and missing required acceptance. Missing evidence never becomes ready or selected.
- [ ] AC7: Share the approved #547 valid/invalid fixtures across adapter and renderer, including request bounds, no-fit versus missing data, sanitized failures and honest retry/cancellation/usage. The renderer never consumes raw provider output.
- [ ] **AC8.** An older Hub and an outstanding request remain safe across a Guide deployment. Consume #545's release/version contract and #317's published artifact without a second collector. Pin one validated supported dataset/catalog for the request and result. Fake-provider/integration fixtures cover unsupported records versions, mixed release IDs, deployment during a pending reply, unavailable retained assets and a newer question/reset. Retain a still-valid compatible view with its actual age or show an explicit update/unavailable state; reject incompatible data before a model call and discard replies whose request/release binding is obsolete. Ordinary browser links remain usable without inference. Browser release acceptance does not depend on this later Ask work.

Delivery target: source-only unless a separately authorized trial is named. These checks are planned, not executed. Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change where behavior/contracts change, the owning Hub/Guide checks in docs/development.md and applicable shared checks. Keep independent Standards/Specification review, current-revision CI and merged-main readback. No installation, public publication, device operation or paid inference is authorized by this planning update.

## Meaningful deferrals

No pins/undo, multi-turn refinement, general composition engine, motion system, persistent conversation, public inference endpoint, LangGraph dependency or live paid trial. #514/#515 retain later interactions and #516 qualifies actual model usefulness.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium; impact high at the credential/network boundary. Source implementation waits for #547 and #511. Reconciliation of ranked v1 scope is complete; approval and delivery of its actual inputs remain pending. Focused auth/data-exposure review is required alongside the two independent axes.

Planning evidence: live issue bodies/comments, native relationships and scoped Project fields read on 2026-09-30; owner-selected browser-first and ranked-results direction. Reassess at pickup, when accepted inputs change, or if ownership, audience or operational scope expands.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Return ranked work references after a question using the shared cards, with safe failure and reset.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot after the named input gates. Claude Code: Opus at high effort; Codex: Sol at high reasoning. Use the host prompt for the current issue scope.
**Work surface:** UI

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |

| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Astra (`gpt-6-astra`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: verify the Claude Code model picker, effort and reviewer profiles at pickup; no Claude session was inspected. | Verified 2026-09-30: current host schema exposes the selected GPT-6 models and reasoning levels. Future host/reviewer access must be rechecked at pickup; no implementation session was launched. |
| Checkpoints | Verify #547 contract approval and #511 source acceptance; obtain separately applicable authority for installation or paid trials | Verify #547 contract approval and #511 source acceptance; obtain separately applicable authority for installation or paid trials |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/512. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Opus reviewers at high effort for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: Verify #547 contract approval and #511 source acceptance; obtain separately applicable authority for installation or paid trials. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-10-01) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/512. I started this session on gpt-6.1-sol at high reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6.1-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-astra reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: Verify #547 contract approval and #511 source acceptance; obtain separately applicable authority for installation or paid trials. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-10-01) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; High-impact credential/network work retains the implementation floor; no host unavailability is evidenced.

**Why:** The bounded scope crosses records, evidence and consumer behavior, warranting Sol implementation and review judgment; Claude Opus high covers edge-case verification. The credential/network boundary requires high implementation settings and stronger independent reviews.
**Reassess when:** Scope, prerequisites, approval, source ownership, installed policy, public audience or actual host availability changes.

One Ask contract, ranked v1, later independent motion/refinement and optional-enrichment cutover rules assessed. No planned product behavior or trial was implemented by these tracker edits. Alignment correction readback: accepted #545 prerequisite and partial-history semantics clarified; original scope, capability ratings and session strategy retained. No implementation, installation or trial performed. · fingerprint: `92008a68404e`
