issues.title: Build the epic Guide browser from shared records and components
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner can browse all public Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo issues through a compact epic-based Guide. Ordinary browsing, search and work commands are useful on their own. The same cards, lists and widgets provide a tested foundation for later Jev views.

## Smallest useful implementation

Build the vertical slice fetch → normalize → validate → render. Consume the new definition from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/545; #543 is its accepted historical baseline, not approval for a changed version. Audit the complete current in-scope issue inventory and produce actionable missing/conflicting-data findings, including legacy body shapes and bugs.

The home page shows epic summaries and Current work, Newly added and Open defects panels. Each short epic page shows its outcome, in-progress and next eligible work, blocked work, later ideas and work completed in the preceding seven days, measured against the dataset's as-of time. Include All issues and Not in an epic views, deeper grouping as the contract defines, one canonical primary placement per issue and stable URLs. Repeated cards do not inflate unique counts. Persistent desktop navigation makes every epic one click away; mobile navigation provides the same destinations without a long page.

Build reusable issue-card, epic, row/list, dependency-list and task-brief components. The issue card accepts any issue kind through the same normalized input; the epic component accepts epic data and child references and composes those shared issue components. Components receive records and view configuration, with no GitHub fetching, body parsing or model calls. Use the same implementation in ordinary pages and the deterministic composed fixture, with a reusable renderer entry point for the later Hub/Ask consumer. Jev will select validated references and allowed components after a user request, causing these existing cards to appear. Leave clear inputs for #540's board and phase views without building a generic widget editor.

Keep large epics compact: use compact rows or a small initial card set, visible total counts and Show more/pagination. Search and shareable filters reach the full issue set; collapsed or unrendered items must not disappear from inventory counts. Test the largest realistic epic, not only small examples.

Collect all open issues, the seven-day completed-issue slice and older parent/dependency records required by #545. Apply the display window using UTC closure timestamps and the dataset's as-of time; reopening or closing as not planned must not make an issue Recently done.

Task briefs keep Explain, Plan, Implement and Review commands. Generic prompts work when recommendations are missing, stale or insufficient; a valid optional Execution recommendation supplies extra guidance. Copying a command never executes it. Keep client-side search/filtering, Back/navigation state, theme, keyboard access, reduced motion and per-page print.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Owner instruction, 2026-09-30: no UI candidate needs human UI approval, including shared components later used by Hub/Ask. Keep browser/accessibility validation, independent review and CI. #657 aligns the remaining instructions and preflight; that cleanup is not a prerequisite for this UI decision.

Issues/native relationships own work facts. Phase and Commitment are Project-owned; readiness is computed only from established evidence and never invents owner selection or phase-based blockers. Explicit labels, closure reasons, unknown dependencies and incomplete reads retain their meanings. Treat issue text as data, render it safely and keep credentials/model calls out of the public browser.

One validated dataset has recorded source provenance and collection time. Complete required issue pagination and whole-attempt consistency are mandatory; a failed core inventory refresh preserves the last accepted dataset. Optional enrichment follows #545's explicit failure classification: missing/stale recommendations, malformed optional sections or an unavailable Project leave issues browsable with visible gaps and generic briefs. #540 may supply a complete permitted cached Project snapshot with its original observation time, or unavailable; never splice partial Project pages or relabel old values as fresh. Invalid required records or unsafe projection still block the candidate. Do not require a hand-maintained topic or next-step narrative.

Consume #545's separate native-blocker and required-outcome evidence. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. A cancelled/not-planned or unresolved duplicate prerequisite does not make work ready; show the missing acceptance or replacement evidence. Preserve source versus installed/physical gates. Consume the declared array ordering and identity rules, and carry one release binding through pages, records and assets. A browser open across deployment must retain its validated release or offer a coherent reload/update state rather than combine versions.

An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545.

The old Guide remains usable during construction. Its manually maintained Direction, global roadmap/timeline, topic prose and leverage table are not parity requirements for the new browser. Architecture stays in the atlas. Useful source facts and brief commands survive the migration.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: A complete live inventory audit accounts for every open issue exactly once in primary placement, under an epic or standalone view. Fixtures cover cross-repository/deep parents, missing ancestors, duplicates, closed-not-planned issues, legacy forms and incomplete pagination; unresolved gaps are visible.
- [ ] AC2: Home, epic, standalone and composed-example views resolve the same canonical identities and use the same component implementations. Search and repeated cards cannot change unique counts or invent dependencies.
- [ ] AC3: Browser checks demonstrate epic navigation, compact laptop pages, mobile, keyboard/focus, Back and shareable filter retention, light/dark, reduced motion and print. Include a large-epic fixture proving bounded initial display, accurate totals and access to every issue through filters and Show more/pagination. Test the seven-day Recently done boundary, a partial closed-issue read with visible partial history that permits publication, and older required ancestry/dependencies. Task briefs work with valid, missing, stale and insufficient recommendations and clipboard fallback.
- [ ] AC4: Fresh open makes no model request. Literal-text and public-artifact negative tests prevent script/link injection and disallowed fields. Recorded freshness and unknown/unavailable states remain visible.
- [ ] AC5: Fixture rendering, adapter tests and the applicable Guide, workflow and shared checks pass; validate the actual new generator and browser. The accepted source candidate is consumable by #540 and #317. Planned checks are recorded in docs/development.md/CI before delivery.

- [ ] AC6: With the same complete issue inventory, missing recommendations, malformed optional sections and unavailable/partial Project enrichment still produce a browsable candidate with explicit gaps. A cached permitted Project snapshot displays its original date. Contrast with truncated required inventory, invalid required records and unsafe projection, which fail the candidate and preserve last-good data.
- [ ] AC7: Browser/adapter fixtures show no-open-blocker separately from required-outcome acceptance. Cancelled/not-planned prerequisites, unresolved duplicates and missing required acceptance cannot populate Ready/Up next as accepted work. A completed prerequisite accepts its own stated scope; missing further acceptance is represented by a separate open native gate issue. A reconciled accepted replacement satisfies only the gates its evidence establishes. Reuse #545's canonical identity fixtures and preserve meaningful phase order.
- [ ] AC8: Keep a browser open while the fixture server changes releases. Navigate, search and open a task brief; every view resolves against one supported release, or shows an explicit update/unavailable state. Missing old assets, mixed identities and unsupported schema versions cannot silently replace or corrupt the current view. #317 repeats the relevant scenario against the deployed artifact.

Delivery target: source implementation and a verified generated candidate. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/654 supplies hosted Guide validation; #317 owns scheduled public preview publication. No installation, model trial or root-site cutover is implied by this story.

## Meaningful deferrals

No Jev endpoint, paid inference, Project editing, new server, full widget editor, pins/undo or composed-view motion system. Full backlog epic mapping is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/655 and is not a prerequisite: standalone issues remain browsable. #510/#512/#516 retain later Ask qualification.

## Assessment

Complexity medium: the collector, canonical records, release binding and shared browser components interact. Uncertainty medium: live inventory shapes and browser behavior need the planned fixtures and inventory audit. Impact medium: incorrect projection can misstate work or disrupt the public browser; literal-text and public-artifact checks remain required.

Ready for source implementation. #543 is the accepted historical baseline; #545's owner-approved guide-records/2.0, guide-views/1.0 and guide-release/1.0 definitions are accepted in [PR #645](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/645), merged as `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949`. Its [source closeout](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/545#issuecomment-5935329208) records approval and validation. The obsolete prerequisite hold is retired. The owner selected #511 as Now on 2026-10-01; selection does not start implementation.

Alignment: #509's browser-first release, the accepted #545 definitions, this issue's AC1–AC8 and existing Guide/architecture/SDLC boundaries. Preserve one collector-to-browser slice, all current acceptance criteria and the separate #540 Project, #654 hosted-validation, #317 publication and #656 cutover work. Planned inventory, fixture, negative-projection and browser/release checks supply acceptance evidence; none ran for this tracker refresh. Recheck source ownership and applicable delivery policy at pickup. No open Hub PR was found during this review.

Planning reassessment, 2026-10-01: live issues, native prerequisites, Project and Hub main `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` inspected. Reassess if contract, scope, ownership, public audience, inventory assumptions or delivery policy changes. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated).

Each short epic page shows its outcome, in-progress and next eligible work, blocked work, later ideas and work completed in the preceding seven days, measured against the dataset's as-of time. Include All issues and Not in an epic views, deeper grouping as the contract defines, one canonical primary placement per issue and stable URLs. Repeated cards do not inflate unique counts. Persistent desktop navigation makes every epic one click away; mobile navigation provides the same destinations without a long page.

Build reusable issue-card, epic, row/list, dependency-list and task-brief components. The issue card accepts any issue kind through the same normalized input; the epic component accepts epic data and child references and composes those shared issue components. Components receive records and view configuration, with no GitHub fetching, body parsing or model calls. Use the same implementation in ordinary pages and the deterministic composed fixture, with a reusable renderer entry point for the later Hub/Ask consumer. Jev will select validated references and allowed components after a user request, causing these existing cards to appear. Leave clear inputs for #540's board and phase views without building a generic widget editor.

Keep large epics compact: use compact rows or a small initial card set, visible total counts and Show more/pagination. Search and shareable filters reach the full issue set; collapsed or unrendered items must not disappear from inventory counts. Test the largest realistic epic, not only small examples.

Collect all open issues, the seven-day completed-issue slice and older parent/dependency records required by #545. Apply the display window using UTC closure timestamps and the dataset's as-of time; reopening or closing as not planned must not make an issue Recently done.

Task briefs keep Explain, Plan, Implement and Review commands. Generic prompts work when recommendations are missing, stale or insufficient; a valid optional Execution recommendation supplies extra guidance. Copying a command never executes it. Keep client-side search/filtering, Back/navigation state, theme, keyboard access, reduced motion and per-page print.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
Owner instruction, 2026-09-30: no UI candidate needs human UI approval, including shared components later used by Hub/Ask. Keep browser/accessibility validation, independent review and CI. #657 aligns the remaining instructions and preflight; that cleanup is not a prerequisite for this UI decision.

Issues/native relationships own work facts. Phase and Commitment are Project-owned; readiness is computed only from established evidence and never invents owner selection or phase-based blockers. Explicit labels, closure reasons, unknown dependencies and incomplete reads retain their meanings. Treat issue text as data, render it safely and keep credentials/model calls out of the public browser.

One validated dataset has recorded source provenance and collection time. Complete required issue pagination and whole-attempt consistency are mandatory; a failed core inventory refresh preserves the last accepted dataset. Optional enrichment follows #545's explicit failure classification: missing/stale recommendations, malformed optional sections or an unavailable Project leave issues browsable with visible gaps and generic briefs. #540 may supply a complete permitted cached Project snapshot with its original observation time, or unavailable; never splice partial Project pages or relabel old values as fresh. Invalid required records or unsafe projection still block the candidate. Do not require a hand-maintained topic or next-step narrative.

Consume #545's separate native-blocker and required-outcome evidence. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. A cancelled/not-planned or unresolved duplicate prerequisite does not make work ready; show the missing acceptance or replacement evidence. Preserve source versus installed/physical gates. Consume the declared array ordering and identity rules, and carry one release binding through pages, records and assets. A browser open across deployment must retain its validated release or offer a coherent reload/update state rather than combine versions.

An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545.

The old Guide remains usable during construction. Its manually maintained Direction, global roadmap/timeline, topic prose and leverage table are not parity requirements for the new browser. Architecture stays in the atlas. Useful source facts and brief commands survive the migration.

issues.title: Define and freeze Ask v1 evaluation cases and receipts
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509. Owner-authorized reconciliation, 2026-09-30. This defines backlog work, not implementation or contract acceptance.

## Outcome and real setup

Freeze an independent evaluation of ranked Ask results before Jev tuning, using real public work and ordinary search as the baseline. This issue also owns the small case/receipt format formerly in #549 and the Pixoo scenario obligations from #513.

## Smallest useful implementation

Define case IDs, frozen dataset/catalog/release and candidate-selection versions, input hashes, independently labeled required/relevant/excluded references, graph facts, acceptable alternative rankings, expected no-match/clarification/failure outcomes and development/held-out membership. Define bounded local receipts with model/configuration, validated results, observed failures, latency, corrections and reported usage/cost; missing usage stays unknown. Do not add production logging of arbitrary questions/provider payloads.

Freeze 40 cases as 20 development and 20 held-out. Cover domain/goal questions, prerequisites versus downstream work, no-match, ambiguity, deferred ideas, legacy bodies, missing acceptance, stale/incomplete sources, optional enrichment gaps, unsafe issue text and new-question/reset. Include Pixoo and at least two other domains. Pins/undo/multi-turn refinement and rich motion are extension cases for #514/#515, not v1 gates. Layout need not have a single correct answer.

Preserve the Pixoo GIF distinctions from #513: curated mood tags https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/91, moment playback https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92, generated media https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/93 and staged external GIFs https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/94 are alternatives, not a mandatory four-step chain. Timing qualification https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/55 and transition defect https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/52 are scoped limitations, not universal blockers. Include existing completed capability evidence where available. Ambiguous “GIFs” yields concrete choices such as playback, event reactions or importing media. Native prerequisites and downstream dependents answer different questions; suggestions never invent edges, effort estimates or readiness. Refresh these source issues when freezing the corpus.

Predeclare must-not-fail factual/security invariants, relevance and required-item coverage, clarification quality, latency/cost reporting, baseline comparison and the proceed/revise/stop rubric. Freeze labels before tuning; do not tune on held-out failures. A changed corpus gets a new version and an honest account of held-out contamination. Required inputs for the final freeze: #547's approved Ask boundary and #511's validated dataset/audit. Draft independent questions while those are underway. #545 owns data/component definitions; #547 owns runtime/provider limits; #510's local evaluation format adds no separate human contract-approval gate.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub owns work facts and native relationships. Use #545 records, public projection and evidence rules; source, installed/client and physical acceptance stay distinct. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. Missing/stale data stays visible. An incomplete seven-day completion read is a visible partial-history gap, not a failure of an otherwise valid publication; required open inventory and relationship reads retain #545's fatal rules. Render issue text literally and treat it as data, never model instructions. No GitHub mutations, device commands, credentials or private runtime/session data enter the model projection. Ground truth is independently labeled from recorded sources; Jev cannot grade itself.

No project UI requires human UI approval under the owner's 2026-09-30 decision. UI/browser/accessibility validation, independent review and CI remain. Contract approval and separately scoped installation, publication, paid-trial and device decisions retain their own gates. #657 aligns the remaining source instructions.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Exactly 40 independently labeled cases, 20 development and 20 held-out, cover Pixoo and at least two other domains, with valid alternative rankings and explicit no-match/unknown outcomes.
- [ ] AC2: Offline validation covers case/receipt identity, split membership, source/catalog/candidate hashes, required/relevant/excluded IDs, graph facts, unknown usage and invalid examples. Candidate omissions are distinct from model and renderer failures.
- [ ] AC3: The Pixoo examples preserve the alternative branches and scoped limitations above. Cases cover shared prerequisites, closed/not-planned records, accepted replacements, missing/external references, cycles and incomplete reads without invented readiness.
- [ ] AC4: Ordinary search/filter baselines and the quality/adoption rubric are reproducible and fixed before tuning. Runtime ceilings come from #547; any later paid trial has an explicit separately authorized budget.
- [ ] AC5: V1 tests cover explicit submission, complete ordinary browsing and late-response rejection after new question/reset. Pins/undo and motion do not block the freeze. #516 can reproduce every tested input and receipt without a separate #549 contract.

Delivery target: source-only unless a separately authorized trial is named. These checks are planned, not executed. Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change where behavior/contracts change, the owning Hub/Guide checks in docs/development.md and applicable shared checks. Keep independent Standards/Specification review, current-revision CI and merged-main readback. No installation, public publication, device operation or paid inference is authorized by this planning update.

## Meaningful deferrals

Live quality and adoption are #516; endpoint/UI implementation is #512. #514/#515 own later interaction evaluation additions. No new analytics service, provider call or installation is needed for this offline work.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium for independent labels and representative cases; impact low for offline artifacts. Drafting can start now; final freeze waits for #547 and #511. The case schema and corpus form one testable outcome, not separate approval tickets.

Planning evidence: live issue bodies/comments, native relationships and scoped Project fields read on 2026-09-30; owner-selected browser-first and ranked-results direction. Reassess at pickup, when accepted inputs change, or if ownership, audience or operational scope expands.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Freeze ranked-result cases, Pixoo distinctions and a reproducible search baseline before tuning.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot after the named input gates. Claude Code: Opus at high effort; Codex: Sol at medium reasoning. Use the host prompt for the current issue scope.
**Work surface:** Backend

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: verify the Claude Code model picker, effort and reviewer profiles at pickup; no Claude session was inspected. | Verified 2026-09-30: current host schema exposes the selected GPT-6 models and reasoning levels. Future host/reviewer access must be rechecked at pickup; no implementation session was launched. |
| Checkpoints | Freeze independent labels and held-out membership before tuning; wait for the accepted #547 and #511 inputs | Freeze independent labels and held-out membership before tuning; wait for the accepted #547 and #511 inputs |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/510. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Opus reviewers at high effort for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: Freeze independent labels and held-out membership before tuning; wait for the accepted #547 and #511 inputs. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-10-01) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/510. I started this session on gpt-6.1-sol at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6.1-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6.1-sol reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: Freeze independent labels and held-out membership before tuning; wait for the accepted #547 and #511 inputs. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-10-01) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** The same source scope, as a one-shot session in Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) `high`. Codex: none. Codex has no stated model or budget constraint; no cheaper Codex start is selected. Preserve both recommended reviewers and every acceptance gate.

**Cheaper prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver the same source scope of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/510. I started this session on Sonnet at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Opus reviewers at high effort for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: Freeze independent labels and held-out membership before tuning; wait for the accepted #547 and #511 inputs. If acceptance exposes a capability gap, return to the recommended start. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-10-01) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Why:** The bounded scope crosses records, evidence and consumer behavior, warranting Sol implementation and review judgment; Claude Opus high covers edge-case verification. Fixture/browser checks bound the work; two fresh independent reviewers retain both axes. No weaker-reviewer exception.
**Reassess when:** Scope, prerequisites, approval, source ownership, installed policy, public audience or actual host availability changes.
**Assessed:** 2026-10-01 · policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be` · evidence: Owner-authorized Ask reconciliation and demo preservation; live bodies/comments, native graph and scoped Project values read 2026-09-30. One Ask contract, ranked v1, later independent motion/refinement and optional-enrichment cutover rules assessed. No planned product behavior or trial was implemented by these tracker edits. Alignment correction readback: accepted #545 prerequisite and partial-history semantics clarified; original scope, capability ratings and session strategy retained. No implementation, installation or trial performed. · fingerprint: `19696d67d9e1`

issues.title: Epic: Rebuild the work Guide around epics and reusable Jev-ready components
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner can browse all Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo work through a compact public Guide organized by epics, with GitHub issues and the portfolio Project supplying current facts. Explain, Plan, Implement and Review commands remain useful. Reusable cards, lists and widgets support a later local, signed-in Ask the Guide experience without building another renderer.

Owner-selected revision, 2026-09-30: deliver the browser first, remove hand-maintained guide bookkeeping, connect the public portfolio, and simplify development rules through a separate bounded policy track. This tracker publication defines work; it does not implement it, approve contract candidates, change Project visibility or publish a site.

## Smallest useful implementation

**Release 1 — Epic browser.** One normalized dataset feeds a home index, short epic pages, a persistent navigator, All issues/Not in an epic views and shared task briefs. Epics are explicit; native parents own membership. Deep relationships and standalone work remain visible. A deterministic composed example proves that ordinary browsing and later Jev requests reuse the same issue-card and epic component implementations. Each issue card accepts a normalized record of any issue kind; epic components accept epic data and child references. Large epics use bounded initial display, accurate counts, shareable filters and Show more/pagination. Recently done covers the preceding seven days; collection also retains older records needed for parent/dependency resolution.

The public build produces artifacts from live GitHub and the approved Project projection on an hourly target, manual dispatch and generator-change events. No operational snapshots or generated pages are committed. Collection time and incomplete/unavailable evidence are visible. Incomplete required issue inventory or invalid/unsafe artifacts block publication; optional enrichment failures leave issues browsable with explicit gaps and honest source dates. An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545. Failed publication keeps the last good site. Build at /next, obtain owner acceptance, then switch the root with a recovery path.

**Release 2 — Ask.** Keep the local signed-in Hub surface, server-side model access only after submission, ranked existing records with template reasons/evidence displayed through the shared issue-card and epic components, visible failures and a reset/new-question rule that discards older replies. The reconciled sequence is #547’s single Ask v1 contract, #510’s case/receipt definitions and frozen corpus, #512’s ranked-result implementation, then #516’s qualification. #547/#510/#512 use #545’s accepted records/component boundary. Draft corpus work can run alongside contract drafting; offline #512 implementation does not wait for corpus freeze. No live model quality is claimed from fake-provider fixtures. Composed interactions can follow using the same catalog; browser delivery does not require pins, undo or motion.

Phase and Commitment stay owner-selected Project values. Native issue state, labels, blockers and closure reason own delivery facts. Do not add a competing priority field or derive selection from readiness.

## Required browser work

- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/545 — new records and reusable component definitions, including their own exact-candidate approval.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/646 — consistent Epic, Work item and Bug forms; preserve the existing #539 template obligation.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511 — complete collector, inventory audit and usable browser.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/540 — public portfolio setup and read-only Phase/Commitment views.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/654 — hosted Guide validation and removal of the manual CI exception.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/317 — scheduled artifact build and verified public /next.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/656 — accepted root cutover and retirement of obsolete machinery.

https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/655 maps the backlog in reviewed batches, in parallel. It is not a release gate when all issues remain reachable under an epic or standalone view. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/113 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/657 are related shared-policy and Hub-adoption work, not prerequisites for browser publication.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub remains authoritative. Use one canonical issue record and primary placement; repeated cards do not inflate counts. Native blockers, suggested order, parent membership and related ideas retain distinct meanings. Unknown required evidence never means ready, unblocked or selected. The remaining safeguard work is assigned within the existing children: #545 owns required-versus-optional collection, prerequisite acceptance evidence, set-versus-sequence identity and release compatibility; #511 implements those browser behaviors; #540 preserves permitted Project fallback and phase order; #317 prevents deployment regression and mixed releases; #512 verifies old-Hub and pending-request compatibility later. Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. These additions keep the seven-day window and shared components, require no human UI approval and add no 60-day inactivity work.

Keep task briefs, generic commands, optional execution recommendations, search/filtering, themes, keyboard/mobile access and per-page print. Copying a prompt never executes it. Ordinary use makes no model request, and a failed Ask request leaves ordinary browsing available. Public artifacts and model projections exclude credentials, private data and unapproved fields.

The old Guide remains live until cutover. Its manually maintained Direction, global timeline/roadmap, topic prose and leverage table are retired as navigation requirements. Architecture stays in the atlas. Preserve useful issue-owned content through migration. The old Guide metadata is removed only when its builder has retired.

Source, CI, installed/client, public publication and physical evidence remain separate. Owner instruction, 2026-09-30: all project UI changes, including Hub and Ask, no longer require human UI approval. UI validation, independent review and CI remain. Contract approval and separately scoped external actions/root cutover remain distinct. #657 aligns source instructions and preflight with this effective decision; the decision does not wait for its reviewer pilot.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] EP1: Every open in-scope issue has exactly one canonical primary placement and is reachable through the browser, including ungrouped and deep/cross-repository work. Inventory and fixture evidence establish coverage.
- [ ] EP2: Compact pages, epic navigation, search, keyboard/mobile, print and all four work commands pass browser checks, including missing/stale recommendation cases.
- [ ] EP3: Browser, board, phase and deterministic composed example reuse the same validated records and components. Field provenance, unknowns, counts and reason evidence remain consistent.
- [ ] EP4: Approved source definitions and normal source/CI evidence are available before consumer acceptance. A closed child or green CI alone does not establish owner contract approval.
- [ ] EP5: An observed automated build updates the public preview without generated-file PRs. Required collection/publication failures keep the last good artifact; optional enrichment can degrade visibly. implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
**Release 1 — Epic browser.** One normalized dataset feeds a home index, short epic pages, a persistent navigator, All issues/Not in an epic views and shared task briefs. Epics are explicit; native parents own membership. Deep relationships and standalone work remain visible. A deterministic composed example proves that ordinary browsing and later Jev requests reuse the same issue-card and epic component implementations. Each issue card accepts a normalized record of any issue kind; epic components accept epic data and child references. Large epics use bounded initial display, accurate counts, shareable filters and Show more/pagination. Recently done covers the preceding seven days; collection also retains older records needed for parent/dependency resolution.

The public build produces artifacts from live GitHub and the approved Project projection on an hourly target, manual dispatch and generator-change events. No operational snapshots or generated pages are committed. Collection time and incomplete/unavailable evidence are visible. Incomplete required issue inventory or invalid/unsafe artifacts block publication; optional enrichment failures leave issues browsable with explicit gaps and honest source dates. An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545. Failed publication keeps the last good site. Build at /next, obtain owner acceptance, then switch the root with a recovery path.

**Release 2 — Ask.** Keep the local signed-in Hub surface, server-side model access only after submission, ranked existing records with template reasons/evidence displayed through the shared issue-card and epic components, visible failures and a reset/new-question rule that discards older replies. The reconciled sequence is #547’s single Ask v1 contract, #510’s case/receipt definitions and frozen corpus, #512’s ranked-result implementation, then #516’s qualification. #547/#510/#512 use #545’s accepted records/component boundary. Draft corpus work can run alongside contract drafting; offline #512 implementation does not wait for corpus freeze. No live model quality is claimed from fake-provider fixtures. Composed interactions can follow using the same catalog; browser delivery does not require pins, undo or motion.

Phase and Commitment stay owner-selected Project values. Native issue state, labels, blockers and closure reason own delivery facts. Do not add a competing priority field or derive selection from readiness.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve

Under #545's accepted contract, a native prerequisite closed as completed accepts only that issue's stated scope. Any further required acceptance gate must be a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent. Not-planned, duplicate and unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until the native links are reconciled; absence of open blockers alone does not establish readiness. These additions keep the seven-day window and shared components, require no human UI approval and add no 60-day inactivity work.

Keep task briefs, generic commands, optional execution recommendations, search/filtering, themes, keyboard/mobile access and per-page print. Copying a prompt never executes it. Ordinary use makes no model request, and a failed Ask request leaves ordinary browsing available. Public artifacts and model projections exclude credentials, private data and unapproved fields.

issues.title: Install and verify the first B.U.N.N.Y. assistant daily-use workflow
issues.body:
Installed acceptance follow-up to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498; separate from that epic's source-delivery completion. Creating this issue does not authorize installation, account connection, agent launch, spending or physical actions.

## Outcome and real setup

On a named Windows/WSL installation, the owner uses B.U.N.N.Y. to resume a conversation, recall an explicit preference, hear an accurate response and review a bounded coding result. Record actual daily-use observations rather than inferring them from source tests.

## Required inputs and authorization

Requires delivered conversation https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46, voice https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/500, preferences https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/501, coding delegation https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/502 and the applicable baseline evaluation https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/504, including their underlying runtime. Before execution, name the installation owner/machine, reviewed package revisions, selected model/voice and worker interface, permitted repository/workspace, account/data scope and usage allowance. Agree on installation, private-state backup and rollback. Existing installations and device owners must be preserved.

A physical-device sequence is optional and separately gated by explicit targets/IPs and permission for the sequence/content replacement. The first workflow can use a read-only status request and an explicitly authorized isolated coding change. Source closure of the epic does not claim this milestone is complete.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Install the selected reviewed revisions under the named owner's authority; record actual service/client versions and a usable rollback path, without credentials in receipts.
- [ ] Start a conversation, store an explicit preference, pause a task, restart the assistant service and reopen the same conversation/task with its pending decision intact.
- [ ] Recall the preference, answer a current status question, and hear a spoken result that matches the evidence. Observe microphone/speaker behavior and response latency on the named client.
- [ ] Delegate one bounded coding task to the qualified interface in the selected isolated workspace. Inspect its progress/question and review the resulting diff or PR, checks, limitations and remaining approvals. No unattended merge authority is implied.
- [ ] Observe model/audio unavailability and recovery without repeated admitted actions. Confirm speech interruption and task cancellation have the documented distinct effects.
- [ ] The owner records whether the workflow is usable, with reproducible failures and follow-ups. Distinguish installed behavior, real-client interaction, transport receipts and any separately authorized visible-device result.

## Meaningful deferrals

Phone/ambient access, every device, every model and every connector are not prerequisites. Native lifecycle, personal-knowledge retrieval and portability can receive later installed observations after their own delivery; do not hold the first daily-use workflow for all future capabilities.

## Assessment and delivery boundary

Complexity medium; uncertainty high (selected installation/interfaces); impact high (live setup and coding). Backlog; refine the selected interfaces, bounds and acceptance before implementation. Planning baseline: Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, 2026-09-26. This update authorizes planning records only. Install only source revisions that have passed their applicable SDLC delivery gates; any repair remains a separately scoped source change. Installation, model spending, live clients and physical tests require their separately applicable authority. All acceptance evidence below is prospective.

issues.title: Retrieve owner-selected personal knowledge through authorized B.U.N.N.Y. tools
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

## Outcome and real setup

B.U.N.N.Y. can answer a useful personal/project question using owner-selected notes or documents and one selected structured source, with inspectable references and dates. This extends explicit preferences; it does not duplicate source-owned databases or assume access to every connected service.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/501 for identity, tool access and memory policy. Select a small local notes/document collection, supported file formats, bounds and one structured-source question during refinement. Implement bounded ordinary search and retrieval first, with stable source IDs, provenance, observation/update times, access scope and a distinction between source facts, user statements and generated inferences. Keep transient observations separate from durable preferences or goals.

Reuse applicable source owners: calendar reminders https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298, email events https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/352, Wispr aggregates https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/470 and private history https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282. Select one available owner and define the additional authenticated read-tool boundary it actually supports. These are alternatives/related work, not a blanket prerequisite chain. Add the selected owner's source issue as a native dependency only when chosen. Reminder/event metadata is not full calendar/email search; aggregate access is not transcript access. Do not reopen the closed umbrella https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/49 as a delivery prerequisite.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Choose which content may be sent to each model or displayed on each surface; access to a source is not permission to export all of it. Retrieved content is evidence, not authority to widen tools or actions. Credentials and secrets remain excluded. A missing, stale or revoked source stays visibly unavailable; the assistant does not silently substitute outdated material. Corrections, deletion and revocation invalidate derived retrieval copies according to a documented retention policy. Source owners retain their own storage, collection and mutation rules.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A fixed personal/project question is answered using selected notes and the chosen structured source, with inspectable source references and actual timestamps.
- [ ] Updating or deleting a source record changes subsequent retrieval; revoked access and corrected preferences are respected, including derived copies.
- [ ] Stale, missing, contradictory and unsupported data are reported accurately. Text embedded in a document cannot grant tool scope or override the owner.
- [ ] Fixtures prove content marked local-only is not sent to a hosted model, and only authorized fields reach the chosen tool/model/display surface.
- [ ] The source API/adapter and its consumer tests agree on freshness, limits and permissions. Actual personal-data connection and installation remain separately authorized.

## Meaningful deferrals

Automatic background ingestion, automatic learning from all conversations, broad calendar/email access, embeddings/vector databases and model training wait for a specific retrieval need. Start with the selected question and sources.

## Assessment and delivery boundary

Complexity high; uncertainty high (first source and retrieval question); impact high (personal data). Backlog; refine the selected interfaces, bounds and acceptance before implementation. Planning baseline: Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, 2026-09-26. This update authorizes planning records only. Source delivery requires issue-linked OpenSpec, applicable package and consumer checks, current-candidate UI approval where applicable, independent reviews, PR delivery and merged-main checks under the current SDLC. Installation, model spending, live clients and physical tests require their separately applicable authority. All acceptance evidence below is prospective.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The initial notes collection and supported formats/bounds, one structured-source question and owner/API, and retention, freshness and data-destination rules.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** The source owners listed are alternatives, not approved access or a dependency chain. The initial retrieval contract must follow the selected question and permissions.

issues.title: Qualify B.U.N.N.Y. model portability with a hosted and an open-weight model
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can choose a qualified hosted or local open-weight model for the native B.U.N.N.Y. assistant without depending on Codex or Claude Code as its execution harness. Conversation/task identity, tool permissions and available personal preferences remain owned by B.U.N.N.Y.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46. Define model adapters separately from coding-worker adapters: model calls return text/structured results/tool requests; worker adapters own dispatch, progress, questions, cancellation and reviewable results. Qualify one hosted provider and one locally served open-weight model on the same small text/tool scenario set. Select the actual models, serving software, hardware fit, context/tool support, credentials and trial budget during refinement; do not install or spend as part of planning.

Use the native LangGraph runtime as the first execution path independent of Codex/Claude. Add a capability record for each model/worker and explicit behavior when a capability is unsupported. Reuse https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/504's fixtures and receipts. Voice, memory and native lifecycle scenarios join as their source stories are delivered, without blocking initial text/tool qualification.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Select models at a new task/turn or a documented safe handoff boundary; do not promise transparent migration of an in-flight tool call or a harness's private state. Stable B.U.N.N.Y. identity survives selection; native model histories may need a structured context handoff. Enforce data-destination and tool permissions outside the model. A local-only task never falls back to a cloud endpoint without the owner's applicable authorization. Unknown usage/cost stays unknown, and existing subscriptions do not imply custom-client API coverage.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Both selected providers complete the same fixed status/read and permitted-tool cases through B.U.N.N.Y., with model-specific limitations recorded.
- [ ] Provider substitution preserves task/conversation association and tool scopes; denied targets stay denied. Existing memory and lifecycle features, when present, remain attached to the same B.U.N.N.Y. identity.
- [ ] Unsupported tool/context features and unavailable providers return explicit outcomes. A local-only fixture produces no cloud fallback and no duplicate effect after interruption.
- [ ] Mock-adapter/source compatibility is reported separately from actual budgeted provider trials and local serving/hardware qualification. Record exact tested versions, settings, latency, outcomes and attributable usage.

## Meaningful deferrals

A third-party coding harness beyond Codex/Claude is a later bounded adapter when a named coding use case warrants it; the initial independent harness is B.U.N.N.Y.'s own runtime. Broad model benchmarks, automatic routing and live arbitrary-session migration are deferred. Jev is optional: only add a routing/classification experiment with a fixed comparison and demonstrated benefit; it never grants permission.

## Assessment and delivery boundary

Complexity high; uncertainty high (model and serving choices); impact high (tools and data routing). Backlog; refine the selected interfaces, bounds and acceptance before implementation. issues.title: Report native B.U.N.N.Y. assistant tasks through shared agent state
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

## Outcome and real setup

A task run directly by B.U.N.N.Y.'s LangGraph assistant appears in shared monitoring and drives the existing device status consumers even when no Codex or Claude process is involved. Delegated workers remain distinguishable from their parent task.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499 for stable assistant task/run identities. Define and implement a versioned lifecycle identity extension for the native assistant, a bounded emitter and the necessary owner/API/consumer compatibility changes. Current contracts explicitly enumerate Codex/Claude identities; do not impersonate either provider or merely widen an enum without validating its consumers.

Map evidenced start, waiting-for-input/approval, interruption, resumption and end to the existing activity/attention/notice concepts. Define whether a persistent task keeps a session identity across runtime restarts and how execution attempts are identified. Select one ingestion path per observed worker session, with deduplication and parent relationships based on explicit adapter evidence. Reuse https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/502 for delegated-worker integration when available; basic native task reporting does not depend on coding delegation. Coordinate observed model metadata with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/305 rather than making model names into provider identities.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One shared agent-state owner and the existing device writers remain authoritative. LangGraph checkpoints own task execution, not device state. Observation delivery is bounded and fail-open; its failure does not change task permissions or stall work. Preserve freshness, unknown parentage, notices and readership semantics; task end is not proof of successful delivery. Follow the selected contract's session-content policy, including https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/424 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/425, while keeping credentials and secrets excluded.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A synthetic native task reaches the shared snapshot as active, waiting, interrupted/resumed and ended without a Codex/Claude identity; existing consumer adapters receive the intended status transitions.
- [ ] A fake delegated run has a correlated parent only when evidence exists. Duplicate emitter/hook observations and reconnect do not duplicate sessions or status effects.
- [ ] Restart preserves the selected identity rules; stale/delayed events do not revive an ended run. Unsupported old readers fail or degrade according to the documented version strategy.
- [ ] Lifecycle/state fixtures, TypeScript/Python validators, hub/MCP/dashboard and affected downstream consumer checks cover the selected revision. Synthetic device output is reported separately from installed/visible-device acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

No new device renderer or writer, personal-memory broadcast, full transcript archive or installed hook migration. Conditional delegation cases join when https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/502 is delivered; they do not block the native-task slice.

## Assessment and delivery boundary

Complexity high; uncertainty high (identity/version compatibility); impact high (all shared consumers). Backlog; refine the selected interfaces, bounds and acceptance before implementation. Planning baseline: Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, 2026-09-26. This update authorizes planning records only. Source delivery requires issue-linked OpenSpec, applicable package and consumer checks, current-candidate UI approval where applicable, independent reviews, PR delivery and merged-main checks under the current SDLC. Installation, model spending, live clients and physical tests require their separately applicable authority. All acceptance evidence below is prospective.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Versioned native-assistant lifecycle identity and compatibility strategy; persistent-task versus execution-attempt identity; selected ingestion/deduplication boundary.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** The issue requires defining these shared contracts before changing owners, validators or consumers; widening a provider enum is explicitly insufficient.
**Reassess when:** The owner settles the listed definitions and the required inputs are available; preserve the existing readiness and separate installation, spending and physical-action gates.

issues.title: Evaluate the LangGraph assistant with bounded B.U.N.N.Y. scenarios
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

Lightweight backlog placeholder. Refine contracts, acceptance and operational choices before implementation. The owner selected LangGraph as the planned personal-agent engine on 2026-09-26.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can judge whether the assistant is useful and trustworthy on the actual supported tasks before expanding its scope.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46 for the first executable assistant slice. Prepare synthetic cases earlier, then add scenarios as voice, memory, coding and computer tools become available. Measure correctness, wrong-target attempts, false success, duplicate effects, response latency and attributable usage. Start with local receipts; consider LangSmith only if it materially improves inspection.

## Evaluation as capabilities arrive

Deliver the baseline scenario runner/report with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/46, then extend the same fixed expectations in each capability's delivery. The baseline may close after its own acceptance; sibling implementations own adding and running their new cases, so evaluation is neither delayed until the end nor left as an unowned follow-up.

The combined scenario asks B.U.N.N.Y. about an active project, retrieves an explicit preference, uses an authorized tool or coding worker, presents the evidence and speaks an accurate result. Interrupt/restart at a selected boundary and verify that conversation, pending decisions and admitted-effect identity survive. Source/fake evidence is separate from real model, microphone, client and device evidence.

Add provider substitution and local-only/no-cloud-fallback cases through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/506; native lifecycle/deduplication through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/505; and source update/deletion/freshness/revocation through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/507. These are conditional extensions, not prerequisites for the first report. The installed daily-use observation is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/508, not implied by a synthetic pass.

Jev remains optional. If a concrete routing/classification decision warrants an experiment, compare it against the existing approach on fixed cases with a separate trial allowance. Record decision quality, latency, usage and failure behavior. A classifier never grants tool or data permission, and the experiment does not block core assistant delivery.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep failed and interrupted attempts, preserve immutable fixture expectations, and never weaken permissions or controller evidence semantics for a pass. Keep private content out of hosted traces and mark unknown usage as unknown.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A fixed small scenario set covers status explanation, permitted control, stale state, denied action, restart after ambiguous write and model outage.
- [ ] Record per-scenario outcomes and limitations; obtain a specific model-trial budget/allowance and separate installed/device authority before those trials.

- [ ] The baseline includes a reusable combined-scenario fixture with explicit capability requirements; unavailable later features are recorded as not yet evaluated, never passed.
- [ ] Each delivered capability adds and runs its applicable combined/failure cases at its reviewed revision; reports identify provider/version/settings and actual attributable usage or unknown values.

Delivery target: source-only unless a later request explicitly names installation or live qualification. These checks are planned, not executed. Current SDLC, UI approval and physical-device authorization still apply.

## Meaningful deferrals

Large benchmarks, mandatory hosted tracing and broad model comparison are deferred; the first report assesses the selected LangGraph implementation and its chosen model.

## Assessment

Planning refinement, 2026-09-26: expanded acceptance and integration boundaries at the owner's request. Remains backlog, not implementation-ready; select the bounded first case and settle the listed choices before delivery.

issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

Lightweight backlog placeholder. Refine contracts, acceptance and operational choices before implementation. The owner selected LangGraph as the planned personal-agent engine on 2026-09-26.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can ask B.U.N.N.Y. to hand a bounded coding task to a qualified Codex or Claude interface and receive progress, questions and a result while conversation remains available.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499. Reuse relevant interface/authentication findings from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199; select one supported SDK/app-server/CLI path first and qualify the second separately within this story or a later split. Bind each task to an explicit repository/workspace and preserve the coding harness’s approvals. Related phone-workspace integration https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205 retains its own scope.

## Reviewable coding results

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499's stable task/run/effect identities and bind each question to the exact task, proposed action and current approval target. Return a structured handoff/result containing the selected repository/workspace, base/head revisions where available, changed-file/diff or PR references, checks actually performed and their results, unresolved findings, limitations and remaining approvals. Unavailable fields are explicitly unknown; process exit or a worker's final message is not delivery evidence.

The first useful finish line is that the owner can inspect a tested candidate or an accurately reported incomplete result through B.U.N.N.Y. Preserve the repository's current review/CI/UI gates; this story adds no unattended merge authority. A replacement worker receives a bounded structured handoff rather than an assumed copy of private live harness state. The first non-Codex/Claude assistant execution path and model-adapter qualification belong to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/506; an additional coding harness can be a later named adapter.

Coordinate parent/worker lifecycle and deduplication with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/505 when available. A missing native-parent integration does not authorize inventing parentage or duplicating a worker's existing hook feed. Reuse the future workspace's task/question references from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/204 through the runtime's documented mapping; remote-workspace delivery is not a prerequisite.

## Smallest useful implementation

No other open source-delivery issue is a prerequisite for this initial slice; model/storage and interface choices still need refinement.

## Runtime identity and bounded execution

Define stable conversation, task, worker-run and external-effect identities. A model/provider choice is configuration for a run, not the identity of the owner's task. Separate model adapters from worker adapters, with one initial model path sufficient here; hosted/open-weight qualification belongs to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/506. Keep durable domain records accessible through versioned application interfaces rather than treating an opaque framework checkpoint as the only record.

Persist the user-visible conversation and pending questions needed to reopen the same task after a service restart. Define retention and what is reconstructed versus explicitly unavailable. Set concrete bounds at refinement for model/tool iterations, elapsed execution, concurrent work and permitted usage. Stop at the applicable limit with an inspectable outcome; unavailable usage reporting is not an invented cost value. Cancellation, approval validity and effects already admitted must be reconciled separately.

issues.title: Epic: Build B.U.N.N.Y.’s personal assistant on LangGraph
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Give the owner a B.U.N.N.Y. personal assistant for conversation, voice, supported device/dashboard actions, personal preferences and selected knowledge, coding delegation and selected computer actions. Use LangGraph as the planned coordination engine, initially alongside the existing Hub on the owner's Windows/WSL setup.

This is a lightweight backlog epic, not an implementation-ready specification. The owner selected this direction on 2026-09-26. Model, voice provider, persistence backend and exact hosting remain refinement decisions. LangGraph is the task runtime, not the language model or an operating-system controller.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with a bounded LangGraph runtime and the existing conversational-assistant story #46. Add voice, memory, coding delegation and computer tools as separately deliverable capabilities. Plan native assistant lifecycle reporting, model portability and selected knowledge retrieval as explicit source stories. Evaluation begins with the first slice and expands with delivered features. Native sub-issues below track this work; their order is not a blanket dependency chain.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Keep one shared agent-state owner and the existing device writers, queues and MCP/API boundaries. Assistant conversation/task state and personal memory remain separate from operational state.
- Retain Codex/Claude harnesses and their hooks for independently used sessions. B.U.N.N.Y. can delegate through qualified interfaces; deduplicate lifecycle ingestion for any session observed through more than one path.
- Existing controls and accepted routines remain usable when the model is unavailable. The assistant may propose a recurring rule; the owner accepts it before the existing automation runtime executes it.
- Enforce scoped tools, permissions, current-target checks and truthful partial/uncertain outcomes in code. Checkpoints cannot authorize duplicate writes or reuse stale approval.
- B.U.N.N.Y. owns stable conversation/task identities; model adapters and coding-worker adapters have separate responsibilities. Future phone-workspace records reference or map to those identities.
- Preserve local-first boundaries. Cloud conversation is an option; account/API usage and costs require qualification, not an assumption that existing subscriptions cover a custom client.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A resumable local LangGraph task has defined stop, restart and approval behavior.
- [ ] Conversation reads status and performs explicitly permitted device/dashboard actions through existing services.
- [ ] Local voice, inspectable personal memory, bounded coding delegation and selected computer tools each meet their own child acceptance.
- [ ] A bounded evaluation covers useful tasks, stale evidence, interrupted writes and model/tool outages, with separate source and installed evidence.

- [ ] Native assistant tasks reach the shared owner and device-status consumers with evidenced worker relationships and no duplicate ingestion.
- [ ] Hosted/open-weight model qualification demonstrates the selected portability scope, and selected knowledge retrieval preserves provenance, freshness and destination permissions.

Source-child completion is assessed against refined criteria. Epic closure does not imply installation, daily-use, phone/ambient access or physical acceptance. The separately tracked installed acceptance follow-up is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/508; it is not a prerequisite for source closure. All evidence is prospective; this request creates planning records only.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Phone access remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47; ambient/wearable access remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/48. Use the local interface first.
- Deterministic routines remain https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45 and its existing follow-ups; this epic does not introduce another scheduler.
- Native-app qualification and the private phone workspace remain https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203 through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205. Reuse their applicable findings; local SDK delegation does not require the entire remote workspace.
- Personal knowledge retrieval is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/507. Select sources individually and reuse existing calendar/email/Wispr/history owners through explicit authorized tools. No broad calendar/email integration or background personal-data ingestion is implied.
- Home Assistant remains an optional integration evaluation in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11. LiveKit or an OpenAI voice SDK can supply voice without replacing LangGraph; LangSmith is optional evaluation tooling. No paid platform is selected here.

## Delivery order and independent paths

Start with runtime #499, then conversation #46. Explicit preferences #501 and spoken replies/the remaining voice slice #500 can follow without waiting for all connectors. Coding delegation #502 supplies the first build-through-B.U.N.N.Y. workflow. Native lifecycle #505 and evaluation #504 progress alongside the relevant slices; computer actions #503 follow a selected daily need. Portability #506 and knowledge #507 have their own bounded qualification. Use native dependency links for actual prerequisites; this order is guidance, not a serial chain.

#504 delivers baseline evaluation first. Each later capability owns adding its cases to that suite, including the combined conversation/memory/tool-or-worker/spoken-result scenario. Jev is optional and only merits a bounded routing/classification experiment when a measurable decision warrants it; it cannot grant permissions and blocks no core slice.

The installed workflow in #508 requires its selected source capabilities and separate installation/live-use authority. It can proceed before every optional epic capability is delivered.

## Assessment

Planning refinement, 2026-09-26: the owner authorized these tracker updates after review. LangGraph remains the selected engine; this does not authorize implementation or runtime changes.

Complexity high (conversation, persistent tasks and multiple tool boundaries); uncertainty high (providers and concrete interfaces remain open); impact high (private data and computer/device actions). Status: backlog. Refine each slice before implementation, preserving the existing review and authorization gates. Baseline: Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, 2026-09-26.
