outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
Give the owner a B.U.N.N.Y. personal assistant for conversation, voice, supported device/dashboard actions, personal preferences and selected knowledge, coding delegation and selected computer actions. Use LangGraph as the planned coordination engine, initially alongside the existing Hub on the owner's Windows/WSL setup.

This is a lightweight backlog epic, not an implementation-ready specification. The owner selected this direction on 2026-09-26. Model, voice provider, persistence backend and exact hosting remain refinement decisions. LangGraph is the task runtime, not the language model or an operating-system controller.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text: Start with a bounded LangGraph runtime and the existing conversational-assistant story #46. Add voice, memory, coding delegation and computer tools as separately deliverable capabilities. Plan native assistant lifecycle reporting, model portability and selected knowledge retrieval as explicit source stories. Evaluation begins with the first slice and expands with delivered features. Native sub-issues below track this work; their order is not a blanket dependency chain.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- Keep one shared agent-state owner and the existing device writers, queues and MCP/API boundaries. Assistant conversation/task state and personal memory remain separate from operational state.
- Retain Codex/Claude harnesses and their hooks for independently used sessions. B.U.N.N.Y. can delegate through qualified interfaces; deduplicate lifecycle ingestion for any session observed through more than one path.
- Existing controls and accepted routines remain usable when the model is unavailable. The assistant may propose a recurring rule; the owner accepts it before the existing automation runtime executes it.
- Enforce scoped tools, permissions, current-target checks and truthful partial/uncertain outcomes in code. Checkpoints cannot authorize duplicate writes or reuse stale approval.
- B.U.N.N.Y. owns stable conversation/task identities; model adapters and coding-worker adapters have separate responsibilities. Future phone-workspace records reference or map to those identities.
- Preserve local-first boundaries. Cloud conversation is an option; account/API usage and costs require qualification, not an assumption that existing subscriptions cover a custom client.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
- [ ] A resumable local LangGraph task has defined stop, restart and approval behavior.
- [ ] Conversation reads status and performs explicitly permitted device/dashboard actions through existing services.
- [ ] Local voice, inspectable personal memory, bounded coding delegation and selected computer tools each meet their own child acceptance.
- [ ] A bounded evaluation covers useful tasks, stale evidence, interrupted writes and model/tool outages, with separate source and installed evidence.

- [ ] Native assistant tasks reach the shared owner and device-status consumers with evidenced worker relationships and no duplicate ingestion.
- [ ] Hosted/open-weight model qualification demonstrates the selected portability scope, and selected knowledge retrieval preserves provenance, freshness and destination permissions.

Source-child completion is assessed against refined criteria. Epic closure does not imply installation, daily-use, phone/ambient access or physical acceptance. The separately tracked installed acceptance follow-up is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/508; it is not a prerequisite for source closure. All evidence is prospective; this request creates planning records only.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- Phone access remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47; ambient/wearable access remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/48. Use the local interface first.
- Deterministic routines remain https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45 and its existing follow-ups; this epic does not introduce another scheduler.
- Native-app qualification and the private phone workspace remain https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203 through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205. Reuse their applicable findings; local SDK delegation does not require the entire remote workspace.
- Personal knowledge retrieval is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/507. Select sources individually and reuse existing calendar/email/Wispr/history owners through explicit authorized tools. No broad calendar/email integration or background personal-data ingestion is implied.
- Home Assistant remains an optional integration evaluation in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11. LiveKit or an OpenAI voice SDK can supply voice without replacing LangGraph; LangSmith is optional evaluation tooling. No paid platform is selected here.

issues.title: PStack phase 4: maintain verification, qualify adoption and measure outcomes
issues.body:
## Codex qualification complete — 2026-10-01

#613 is accepted: Desktop/WSL, normal-terminal interactive CLI and codex exec each passed Hub/wall/Pixoo/integrated qualification. Two independent Desktop sessions passed the scoped Hub and two-composition isolation cases. CLI/exec use ordinary per-command escalation; this does not establish unattended approval-free execution. The owner accepted the final previews, screenshot and annotated mouse-highlight walkthrough. Final owned services, leases, runtime directories and temporary video player are stopped; frozen proof checksums and installed-service readback passed. The owner attributes the stopped installed Pixoo service and prior settings resaves to intentional actions.

Source acceptance remains #610/#611/#612 and repair #649; historical #497 and postponed agent-skills #44 remain unchanged. The qualification pins and focused current-main smoke at a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949 are recorded in #613. Private receipts and the supported-client runbook remain in the canonical local delivery evidence directory.

Disposition: retain this issue open for the independently scoped manual follow-up. Its coordinator/owner must identify the actual first-10-deliveries (or available deliveries after 14 days) cohort, give each delivery an equal 14-day repair-observation window, record missingness and obtain selected/deferred case dispositions. Actual cohort/window dates are still unknown, so no maturity date or completed observational outcome is claimed. No new trial, automatic monitor, Project membership expansion or public guide refresh is started.

## Outcome

Verification remains usable after feature changes, known failures are detected, review evidence survives the chat, and the owner can use the installed workflow with clickable app proof and previews. Retain operational observations through the bounded manual follow-up below; the formal workflow comparison is postponed.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488

## New delivery work

- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/86
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/496
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/610 — diagnose Codex access and obtain the launch-boundary decision.
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/611 — deliver the approved launch configuration and setup.
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/612 — check preview prerequisites before launch.
- [x] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/613 — activate and qualify fresh and parallel Codex sessions.

## Existing deliveries retained under their current parents

- [x] [Retained actual reviewer results — agent-skills #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/54). Require its applicable current-candidate evidence; do not duplicate review extraction or host adapters.
- Deferred related work: [agent-skills #44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/44). Its discovery, calibration, manifest, fixture expansion and model trials are not scheduled or required for this phase. A later owner decision must reassess the question, scope and allowance; the historical 32-attempt design is not an active target or approved future budget.

## Codex preview follow-up — planned 2026-09-29

The owner requested backlog work to make the existing previews usable from the supported Codex development sessions on this PC, including parallel sessions. This is a new required adoption outcome; it preserves #497's completed mixed result and the separately scoped manual observation follow-up below.

Sequence: #610 produces the access diagnosis and owner-accepted boundary. #611 and #612 consume that decision and may proceed in parallel with coordinated shared-file ownership. #613 consumes their accepted sources and separately authorized host activation. Native sub-issue and blocked-by links carry these relationships. The initial targets are Desktop/WSL, interactive WSL CLI and `codex exec`; delegated launch behavior is resolved in #610. Read-only/reviewer restrictions remain intact.

Disposition: proceed with scoped planning and read-only diagnosis; hold implementation, permission changes and host trials until their named prerequisites and authority exist. No launch method, broader access, new permanent service, Portfolio commitment or #44 study is selected by this plan. The Codex branch need not wait for the manual cohort's observation window; neither branch completes the other.

## Operational follow-up ownership — updated 2026-09-28

This phase retains its separately scoped bounded manual follow-up after the workflow is adopted. It uses ordinary delivery and adoption evidence without waiting for, preparing or substituting for the postponed discovery sample, calibration or comparison in [agent-skills #44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/44).

For the initial follow-up, inspect the first 10 subsequent deliveries, or all available deliveries after 14 days if fewer have completed. Record the actual cohort and give each delivery the same 14-day repair-observation window; immature windows remain pending. Record known failed, blocked or abandoned attempts separately so a completed-delivery cohort does not hide them. Do not delay unrelated source closure while observing the cohort.

Use existing Execution records and attributed Fixes delivery links directly, or through [Hub #307](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/307) when available, plus adoption findings from [#497](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497), and authorized issue/PR evidence. Capture user corrections, unnecessary stops, manual intervention and later defects where evidenced. Missing records, ambiguous attribution and unobserved human time remain unknown; no recorded repair is not proof of no defect.

The owner reviews whether each recurring or consequential failure warrants a new case, a revised criterion or an owned repair. Route selected prevention work through [agent-skills #86](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/86); preserve unrelated scope boundaries. Retain the case's source revision, expected/observed behavior and selection or deferral reason. Discovery examples used for tuning must not silently become holdout evidence.

Retain one concise readback in existing phase/evaluation evidence: cohort, observation windows, missingness, repeated failure modes, selected cases and owned follow-ups. Compare recurrence only for comparable observed cohorts and label the result observational. This is one manual follow-up, not a scheduled scanner or a model study; a later cadence can be proposed from its usefulness. It grants no model-trial allowance or private transcript access and does not restart #44's postponed preparation.

## Phase acceptance

- [x] The owner-selected Codex development entrypoints have a delivered launch path, actionable readiness checks and fresh/parallel Windows/WSL acceptance under #610–#613. Unsupported paths remain explicit; permission or scope changes need the owner decision.
- [x] Feature maps and verification recipes change with affected behavior; missing harness capability is distinguished from a product failure.
- [x] Focused negative controls demonstrate that a relevant known defect fails and the reference behavior passes; avoid a blanket mutation-testing project.
- [x] Preflight reports source/check/review/acceptance gaps without changing approval or merge authority.
- [x] The named owner-host workflow can start, exercise, capture and hand off all three apps, then stop or expire its owned previews. Preserve failed or unsupported host results.
- [ ] Reviewer evidence, host qualification and the operational follow-up readback are linked with exact scope and source identity. Report defects, rework, elapsed time, human effort and attributable usage with their limits; do not infer dollar cost from tokens or elapsed time.
- [x] Completion reporting identifies #44 as postponed and makes no claim of comparative workflow improvement from app verification or host qualification.
- [ ] The bounded manual follow-up records equal repair-observation windows, missing evidence and selected or deferred regression cases. Unavailable adoption or incomplete windows remain pending.

Preparation for this phase's active deliverables can proceed independently. Applicable source and qualification receipts gate each actual runtime step; the entire review-work initiative need not close first. No benchmark, installation or service launch is authorized by this issue's creation. Pending owner-host acceptance or the retained manual follow-up keeps this phase open; postponed #44 evidence does not.


## Acceptance reconciliation — 2026-09-29

Maintenance, preflight and review-retention source work are delivered; host qualification is recorded. The bounded manual follow-up remains incomplete, so phase 4 stays open.

- [agent-skills #86](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/86) supplies the maintenance checkpoint. Adapter deliveries supply reference and negative-control evidence; [Hub #561](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/561#issuecomment-5881250492) is a later observed failure turned into a browser regression check.
- [#496](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/496#issuecomment-5854890365) delivered read-only preflight. [agent-skills #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/54#issuecomment-5853669112) delivered retained review results. Actual returns are inspectable on Hub [#552](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/552#issuecomment-5855275779) and [#553](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/553#issuecomment-5856277544). Broader review-work host qualification remains separately owned by agent-skills #80.
- [#497's 2026-09-29 readback](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497#issuecomment-5881256819) qualifies Claude Code CLI 2.1.283 for single-app and integrated previews on the named Windows/WSL host. Codex CLI 0.156.0 with the default profile failed. Preserve that result and untested paths; closing qualification does not mean both hosts passed.
- That readback records twelve candidate adoption findings, source identities, proof retention and lifecycle observations. It supplies inputs for the follow-up, not the follow-up itself. The subsequent-delivery cohort and equal 14-day repair-observation windows have not been assembled and accepted. Closed source children and elapsed agent time cannot establish them.

Next action: the phase follow-up coordinator selects the existing bounded cohort after adoption, records each actual observation window and missingness, preserves known failed/blocked attempts, and returns the owner-selected regression cases or deferrals. Incomplete windows stay pending. Use existing authorized delivery records; no scheduler, new model study or transcript access is added.

Agent-skills #44 remains postponed and is not a completion blocker. App qualification is not a comparative workflow-improvement result. Phase 2's #557/#560 repairs stay with that phase; relevant later repair evidence can feed this follow-up without being counted as completed acceptance twice.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

## Work assessment

Assessment for Hub #341 on 2026-09-28. These ratings apply to the next read-only acceptance audit, not implementation of the entire initiative or its remaining qualification work. Existing scope, readiness and owner gates are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** Reconcile acceptance evidence across linked deliveries and distinguish source from host and adoption claims.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Closed child issues do not by themselves establish every parent acceptance criterion.
- **Impact: medium.** An incorrect reconciliation could misstate operational qualification or resume explicitly postponed work.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** Actual delivery cohort identities and dates, equal 14-day repair-observation windows, missingness and attributed case dispositions for the separate manual follow-up. #613 has no remaining delivery gate.
**Work surface:** Backend

**Why:** Host qualification is accepted. A mature cohort and supported observations are needed before assessing the remaining phase outcome; absent dates cannot be treated as elapsed observation windows.
**Reassess when:** The owning coordinator records the actual cohort, per-delivery observation dates and available outcomes, or the owner explicitly changes the follow-up scope.
**Assessed:** 2026-10-01 · policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be` · evidence: #613 closed completed after selected client matrices, independent-session isolation, owner preview and annotated-video acceptance, cleanup, proof checksums and installed-service readback. The remaining parent gate is its separate bounded manual observation follow-up; actual cohort and window dates are not yet recorded. · fingerprint: `ccfc1c97ed35`

## Codex source delivery checkpoint — 2026-09-29

[#611 / PR #618](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/618) is accepted at `0c1d0867b0d8dc3562f66cf8363c641e8c80ca0b`. [#612 / PR #632](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/632) is accepted at `da5e4794d45f461bc583b1092b8ee1edeac07a94`. Both source changes have satisfied independent Standards/Specification review and seven successful exact merged-main Depot jobs with no annotations. The #612 source patch is unchanged by the concurrent preflight-parser merge; [both review applicability readbacks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/632#issuecomment-5902703614) are retained.

The diagnostic reports local facts without claiming launch, capture or Windows acceptance. Its custom-module and adapter trust limits are documented; missing and unknown capabilities remain distinct. The pinned wall/Pixoo core1.1.0 adapters explicitly report the new diagnostic unsupported through help. Hub core1.3.0 is prepared in two clean, separate build checkouts. Local build/browser files are present; manager access, writes and runtime/browser qualification remain unknown or unproven.

#613 remains open and blocked on the owner’s concrete operational checkpoint and actual qualification. The prepared brief covers Desktop/WSL, interactive WSL CLI, codex exec, isolated synthetic previews, two-session overlap, Windows/chat observations, lifecycle checks and exact owned cleanup. No personal configuration edit is proposed; no preview, fresh model session or device action has occurred. Prepared checkouts and proof storage are retained for that qualification.

#492’s bounded manual cohort and equal observation windows remain pending. #497’s mixed result remains historical; agent-skills #44 stays postponed. Native dependency edges remain as provenance, and no Project membership expansion is selected.

## Codex operational progress — 2026-09-29

The owner approved the #613 operational brief. The current Desktop coordinator passed standalone Hub, wall and Pixoo reference captures and handoffs through the explicit host route. Hub extension, stop, restart, short-lease expiry and a deliberate failing-start cleanup passed. The owner confirmed the Hub Windows preview, screenshot and video; the video was too fast to follow, so a slower viewing copy and assertion explanation were retained without changing frozen proof.

#613 remains in progress. Fresh Desktop evidence, normal-terminal CLI/exec launches, integrated qualification, independent-session overlap and remaining owner browser observations are pending. Fresh CLI/exec attempts from the enclosing Desktop tool environment failed before model initialization because Codex state directories were read-only; these are recorded failures, not preview acceptance. No personal configuration, permanent grant, installed service or physical device changed. The existing operational approval remains valid; no repeated approval is needed for its scope.

#492's separate manual cohort and equal observation windows remain pending. #497's mixed result and the postponed agent-skills #44 study remain unchanged.

## Reset repair accepted — 2026-09-29

The owner approved the prepared repair. [#649 / PR #651](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/651) is accepted at `13fb6310f49d7c909744afc7db8dfdf77cb93ced`. [Independent Standards and Specification review](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/651#issuecomment-5903626917) found no defects in the reviewed comparison. All seven exact-head PR and seven merged-main Depot jobs succeeded with zero annotations. The merged tree matches the reviewed candidate.

Real core-written default and explicit-root receipt regressions passed, as did 37 focused tests, 24 broad validation commands, and seven actual-manager reset/failure/interruption cases. At the clean candidate, the actual pinned Hub/wall/Pixoo composition completed 14 host operations: captures, handoff, two resets, loss/replay/second-owner controls, doctor and owner-first stop. Seeded state returned without replay; IDs, ports, pairing, lease expiry and all 20 frozen-file hashes stayed unchanged. Installed service states match the baseline. Runtime cleanup and copied-proof checksum checks passed; evidence remains in the canonical local delivery directory. The repair made no personal configuration edit, installation or physical-device change.

#613 remains open: selected fresh-client launches, independent-session overlap and Linux Codex configuration metadata attribution are still required. The fresh Desktop ordinary approval-path retry returned supervisor-unavailable before any host command launched; zero starts and verified evidence checksums do not constitute preview success. Normal-terminal CLI/exec evidence is still missing. The source repair does not waive or replace those obligations. Existing operational approval remains valid.

#492's separate first-10-deliveries/14-day manual cohort and equal 14-day observation windows remain pending; actual cohort/window dates are not yet recorded, so no next maturity date can be asserted. #497's historical mixed qualification remains unchanged and agent-skills #44 stays postponed. Native dependency edges remain as provenance. No Project membership or publication expansion is selected.

## Fresh Desktop Hub qualification — 2026-09-30

A new independent Desktop/WSL chat passed exact-launcher manager preflight twice using normal execution, then launched Hub at accepted repair revision `13fb6310f49d7c909744afc7db8dfdf77cb93ced`, passed all five task-appears assertions and froze its handoff. No escalation was needed. The previous fresh-chat failure did not reproduce; its historical cause remains unknown.

After the launching chat finished its turn, the coordinator verified the same healthy Hub process and lease. A separate coordinator-owned checkout launched a concurrent Hub. Rebuilding, reseeding and stopping A left B's health, process identity, listeners, build digest, synthetic revision/question state, zero fake-controller commands and frozen proof hashes unchanged. A's positive control returned from revision 2 with a question to seeded revision 1 without one. Snapshot comparison excludes only the advancing timestamp and observation age; raw snapshots are retained. This establishes the scoped two-Desktop Hub preview overlap, not integrated or unlimited concurrency, nor survival after closing Desktop or restarting WSL.

The owner confirmed the new preview, screenshot and video all opened and the tested change was clear. Post-handoff extension passed, then both Hub runs stopped cleanly; frozen checksums passed after runtime cleanup. Installed service names/states still match baseline. Configuration stat metadata differs for both Linux and Windows from the earlier checkpoint; attribution is unknown and metadata alone does not establish changed contents. Neither coordinator edited personal configuration.

#613 remains open: fresh Desktop wall/Pixoo/composition and integrated isolation, normal-terminal interactive CLI/exec qualification, and configuration-change attribution remain pending. The next bounded fresh-chat handoff is prepared under the existing operational approval. Earlier source acceptance, #497's historical mixed result, #492's separate manual cohort/observation windows and postponed agent-skills #44 are unchanged. No guide/publication or Project expansion.

## Fresh Desktop matrix and integrated isolation — 2026-09-30

The same independent Desktop/WSL chat completed standalone wall (7 assertions), Pixoo (10) and pinned integrated lifecycle (11), all through normal execution without escalation. Together with the earlier Hub case, all four Desktop launch/capture/handoff paths passed. The core1.1.0 consumer adapters explicitly lack the new prerequisites operation; their help and actual launch checks remain recorded separately. Both standalone consumers stopped cleanly with copied frozen proof retained.

Two independent Desktop chats launched separate integrated compositions: six services total, with distinct run identities, checkouts, units, timers, ports, runtime and proof directories. Rebuilding A's Hub/Pixoo, resetting A twice and stopping A left B's synthetic state, owner/feed revision and session, zero consumer-writer counters, process/build identities and frozen proof hashes unchanged. Wall serves source assets directly and has no build operation. A's positive reset control returned from revision 2 with one task to revision 0 with none; both B consumers stayed on B's task and revision 2. B survived the launching chat's completed turn. This establishes the scoped two-composition Desktop case, not unlimited capacity or Desktop/WSL restart survival.

The owner confirmed all three integrated previews and proof opened and the shared task was clear. The owner also attributed the observed Linux/Windows Codex configuration metadata changes to an intentional settings change or resave. Attribution is owner-reported, not a byte-level comparison; neither qualification coordinator edited settings and no contents were read. The previous attribution question is resolved on that basis.

Post-handoff composition extension passed. Both compositions were stopped cleanly after acceptance, and retained frozen proof passed checksums. Installed service names/states match the baseline. #613 stays open for actual normal-terminal interactive WSL CLI and codex exec qualification, their applicable owner observations and final runbook/readback. Earlier nested CLI initialization failures remain historical; a prepared normal-terminal interactive handoff uses the already approved controls. #492's separate manual cohort/observation windows, historical #497 and postponed agent-skills #44 remain unchanged.

## Interactive WSL CLI qualification — 2026-09-30

An actual interactive WSL Codex CLI 0.159.1 session, launched by the owner from a normal terminal, passed Hub (5 assertions), wall (7), Pixoo (10) and integrated lifecycle (11): 33 assertions across all four launch/capture/handoff cases at Hub `13fb6310f49d7c909744afc7db8dfdf77cb93ced` and the accepted consumer pins. Normal host access was refused with supervisor-unavailable; ordinary per-command escalation then succeeded. Requested workspace-write/on-request flags, stated restricted-network/auto_review policy and observed host authority are recorded separately. This qualifies the approval-mediated interactive route, not unattended exec. No persistent permission or personal settings change was made.

issues.title: Retry transient issue-inventory drift in nightly guide refresh
issues.body:
## Defect

A nightly guide refresh can stop when an issue opens or closes between its REST and GraphQL inventory reads. The collector rejects the inconsistent counts, which protects the saved snapshot, but the workflow does not retry the transient read and leaves the rolling guide PR unchanged for that run.

On 2026-09-26, [run 36272105772](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/36272105772) failed in `docs/work-guide/work/refresh_backlogs.py` with `('agent-device-hub', 188, 188, 187)`: the GraphQL open-issue total and nodes were 188, while the REST count was 187. `nightly_run.py` then reported `Input refresh failed; no partial snapshot was published`. Concurrent issue activity is the likely cause; the log proves the count mismatch, not which issue changed during the reads.

This is separate from [run 36270661492](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/36270661492), where H478–H485 lacked Guide topics. Those topics were added and [run 36271295316](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/36271295316) passed.

## Expected behavior

- Retry the complete input collection a small, bounded number of times when REST and GraphQL open-issue inventories disagree. Each attempt must use fresh reads rather than mixing pages or counts from different attempts.
- Preserve the current fail-closed rule: after persistent mismatch, publish no partial snapshot or rolling PR update, and report the repository, counts, attempts, and run evidence.
- Add a test for a one-time mismatch followed by a consistent inventory and a test for persistent mismatch. Keep incomplete pagination and other validation failures fail-closed.
- Do not change guide publication or automatic merge policy; [#317](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/317) owns those decisions.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Make the nightly guide input refresh resilient to transient cross-API issue-count drift while preserving complete-snapshot validation.

## Work assessment

Assessment for Hub #341 on 2026-09-26. Adds the missing ratings for the defined source-only tooling fix; scope, readiness labels and authorization are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** Retry orchestration must preserve whole-attempt collection, typed failure discrimination and atomic publication boundaries.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The observed mismatch is proven; concurrent issue activity is only the proposed explanation. The retryable error contract and bounded attempt count need explicit implementation choices and tests.
- **Impact: medium.** Incorrect retries could mix snapshots or hide a persistent validation failure; existing fail-closed and rolling-PR boundaries must remain intact.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: implement the bounded retry fix with whole-attempt and fail-closed regression tests. Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.
**Work surface:** Backend

| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: Claude Code host controls were not inspected; confirm alias and effort before starting | Provisional: Codex tool metadata lists this model and reasoning; starting-session availability remains unverified |
| Checkpoints | choose and test a small retry bound and explicit mismatch classification; retry only complete fresh collection on the specified inventory disagreement, never other validation failures; coordinate current guide-tooling ownership and preserve no partial publication; do not change guide automatic-merge or public-publication policy | choose and test a small retry bound and explicit mismatch classification; retry only complete fresh collection on the specified inventory disagreement, never other validation failures; coordinate current guide-tooling ownership and preserve no partial publication; do not change guide automatic-merge or public-publication policy |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

issues.title: Review and clean the accumulated local delivery artifacts
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Reduce the existing local branch/worktree/temporary-clone backlog for the three source repositories, using a freshly reviewed and owner-approved candidate list. Leave every ineligible or uncertain artifact intact with a reason and next action.

The 2026-09-26 Hub audit observed 124 local branches associated with merged PRs, nine linked worktrees at merged PR heads, and four standalone clones under its worktree storage. These observations are evidence of a backlog, not current eligibility or approval. Refresh all facts at execution.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Required inputs: merged local-cleanup policies in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/476, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/192 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/117. Their reviewed rules and acceptance evidence define eligibility.
- Inventory only the three named canonical source repositories and their task-owned temporary locations, including embedded standalone clones. The read-only audit utility https://github.com/jimmie-potts/dotfiles/issues/5 is a preferred convenience, not a blocker; manual inspection can supply equivalent evidence.
- Produce a private candidate list identifying repository/resource, task/owner or unknown, current branch/head, merged PR/head, merged-main verification, worktree/session usage, ignored evidence, surviving evidence destination, proposed action and retention reason.
- Have independent read-only Standards and Specification reviewers inspect that fixed candidate list and the applicable policies. Present the exact eligible actions to the owner and obtain approval before any deletion. An issue being marked ready, this planning session, or approval of future automatic cleanup is not approval of the historical list.
- Revalidate each approved resource immediately before action. A changed head, new consumer, unknown owner, dirty/locked worktree or unresolved evidence causes that resource to be retained. Remove only approved eligible resources through their proper Git/tool lifecycle; do not force removal.
- Read back every result and reconcile the list. Separate local branch, worktree, scratch and clone outcomes. Retain evidence of exclusions and failed/refused operations.

Remote-branch deletion and GitHub settings remain [Hub #309](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/309). The two maintenance passes must coordinate ownership; neither consumes the other's unverified candidate list. Public agent-device-guide publish/* refs remain excluded. Do not remove canonical installed skill/dotfiles checkouts, device runtime data, shared caches or another active task's workspace.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No age-based deletion, blanket git clean, forced worktree removal, unknown-owner cleanup, unreviewed tip removal or private evidence publication. A clean worktree alone does not establish that ignored content is disposable. Native tool-managed worktrees use the owning tool's supported exit flow; unavailable flow remains a pending owner action.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: approved local maintenance completed or explicitly retained resource-by-resource, with private before/after receipts and a sanitized tracker summary. This operational task does not invent a source PR when no source file needs to change.

1. The three policy prerequisites are read at their merged revisions and their required acceptance evidence is available before removal.
2. The candidate list is current, reviewed and explicitly approved. The receipt records which exact actions that approval covered.
3. Each attempted removal has an immediate identity/ownership/evidence recheck and a readback; skipped or refused actions remain visible. No unapproved target changes.
4. Reinventory distinguishes remaining eligible candidates from retained or newly created work. Reclaimed storage is measured where practical and never guessed; a nonempty retained list is not called a cleanup failure.
5. Record a follow-up owner/action for each unresolved artifact. No user approval means no destructive action and the issue stays pending.

## Meaningful deferrals

No periodic janitor, evidence-retention expiry, remote prune, global checkout refresh, runtime installation or host configuration change. Revisit retained entries only when the recorded owner releases them or the missing evidence/approval becomes available.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26. Complexity: medium; multiple repositories and resource lifecycles require serial revalidation. Uncertainty: medium; exact ownership and ignored-file disposability must be established in the bounded inventory. Impact: high; deletion could lose unmerged/private work. Readiness: blocked on the three local-policy issues; afterward ready for the inventory stage, with deletion gated by approval of the fresh list. The audit utility is preferred order only. Planning-session reasoning: unknown.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Keep the procedure in docs/sdlc.md. Add only a short completion requirement and conditional pointer in AGENTS.md, using writing-for-agents.
- Separate remote and local branch lifecycle. [Hub #309](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/309) owns GitHub automatic deletion and the old remote-branch prune. A missing remote branch does not prove local cleanup or authorize deleting local work.
- After the repository's existing merge, merged-main CI (or applicable documented exception), issue readback and evidence gates, remove the delivery's eligible owned worktree through its designated lifecycle. Remove its local branch only when it still points exactly at the reviewed merged PR head, no worktree or session uses it, and no remaining consumer needs it.
- Establish squash-merge delivery from the merged PR and exact reviewed head, not commit ancestry or git branch --merged. A moved tip is unfinished/unknown work and must be retained.
- Recheck branch identity, expected tip and worktree/ownership state immediately before removal. Use an exact-ref expected-head guard for branch removal; never perform a broad forced branch sweep. Any refusal or changed state retains the resource and records the next action.
- Account for owned scratch, independent temporary clones, review copies and staging directories, including locations outside the registry. Preserve required ignored/private evidence in a surviving private location before cleanup.
- Require a concise cleanup result in existing delivery evidence: removed with readback, retained with reason and owner/next action, or not applicable. A tool exit flow that this session cannot run is retained, not completed.
- Extend docs/work-guide/README.md only at its publication procedure: account for the owned public checkout, export/archive and staging directories after authorized publication and live verification finish. This is procedure text only; do not refresh guide inputs or generated HTML. Preserve public agent-device-guide publish/* refs, which #309 explicitly excludes.

Required inputs: none; the accepted local-branch policy is specified here. Coordinate shared docs/sdlc.md edits with Hub #309 and sibling cleanup-policy deliveries. Remote deletion need not be enabled to verify and clean an eligible local branch.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep other sessions' branches, worktrees and installations untouched. Never force worktree removal, reset, clean or discard files to make cleanup pass. Unknown ownership, locks, dirty state, unreviewed commits, unavailable CI, needed ignored files and active consumers all retain the affected resources. A lack of visible processes is not proof that a session has released a worktree. Failed/abandoned work and the historical backlog keep their separate owner-decision boundary. Source delivery does not install hooks, change live state or contact devices.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: reviewed documentation/instruction PR merged to this repository's main, with required local checks, hosted CI and issue readback. No product behavior delta or invented OpenSpec capability.

1. A completed ordinary delivery and an explicitly invoked deliver-work both produce a cleanup outcome. An eligible squash-merged local branch is removed only after its worktree is gone and the exact-head/ownership checks pass.
2. Read-only simulations cover a moved branch tip, another registered worktree, an active/unknown session, ignored evidence, lock/dirty state, incomplete CI and a remaining installation/publication consumer. Each retains the resource and names the next action.
3. A clean tool-managed worktree uses its exit flow; unavailable flow is reported pending. A standalone clone is discovered through task ownership rather than the Git worktree registry.
4. Source/CI completion and cleanup outcome remain distinct; no claim of removed resources without a current readback. Public receipts do not expose private paths, configurations or runtime metadata.
5. With Node 24, run npm ci, npm run check:workflow and npm run test:workflow from the isolated delivery root; both checks must exit zero and report the actual specification inventory. Preserve all applicable current-head and merged-main CI and independent Standards/Specification reviews. Because docs/sdlc.md and AGENTS.md change, the guide-only CI exception cannot qualify this PR.
6. The publication procedure accounts for its local clones/staging after live verification while preserving the public publication branch history and leaving generated guide artifacts unchanged.

## Meaningful deferrals

No retroactive artifact deletion, GitHub setting changes, scheduled cleanup, evidence expiry, runtime/cache cleanup or installation. The existing remote-branch backlog remains Hub #309; a separate approved local-maintenance issue handles old local artifacts. Manual retention with a named next action is the fallback when safe cleanup cannot be established.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26, against agent-device-hub main 55f11cb and the owner's accepted local-branch policy. Complexity: medium, because Git refs, worktree lifecycles, evidence and consumers interact. Uncertainty: low; the decision and existing retention gates are explicit. Impact: high, because incorrect removal can lose unmerged or private work. Readiness: ready. Shared-file coordination is not a required-input dependency. Reassess on policy/head changes, tool-lifecycle differences, or new cleanup consumers. Planning-session reasoning: unknown.

issues.title: Investigate Wispr mobile usage exports and optional iPhone Shortcut capture
issues.body:
### Outcome and scope

Determine which supported Wispr Flow routes can supply this owner's phone usage to the private B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard, and recommend a bounded implementation or document why a route is unavailable. Investigate historical aggregates first, then prospective capture through iPhone Shortcuts if the owner uses an iPhone.

Owner: agent-device-hub. This is a research issue, independent of the Windows collector/dashboard milestone [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467). The owner authorized this issue on 2026-09-26. Phone platform, OS/Flow version, plan, admin/export eligibility and preferred dictation workflow are not yet confirmed. Planning does not authorize phone access, installation, recurring collection or contacting Wispr.

**Current evidence, checked 2026-09-26**

- Wispr documents synced usage statistics but device-local dictation history. Phone transcripts must not be assumed to appear in the Windows history database. [Device sync documentation](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/5284722493-sync-flow-across-your-devices).
- Desktop Insights can include mobile usage. Establish exactly which figures combine platforms, their reporting windows and whether supported export or programmatic access exists. A visible counter alone is not an integration contract. Resolve the difference between the sync article's local daily counts and the usage article's combined heatmap before selecting a daily series. [Your usage documentation](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/8760230576-your-usage-tab-track-your-dictation-stats-in-wispr-flow).
- Eligible organization administrators can export daily UTC usage. Plan and organization controls restrict export; documented columns do not establish a platform identifier. Specific-app filtering excludes mobile. Verify mobile separability rather than interpreting App type as operating system. [Usage export documentation](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2356896572-admin-usage-v2-team-members-table-and-words-dictated-csv-export).
- On iPhone, Quick Dictation to Clipboard and some Dictate a Flow Note invocations can return a Shortcuts result. With the Flow keyboard active, output can go into the current text field instead. Quick Dictation to Notes returns no result for subsequent steps. This suggests selective future capture, not access to all keyboard dictation or historical records. [iPhone Shortcuts documentation](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/1986921789-How-to-Set-Up-Flow-Shortcuts-for-iPhone).

### Investigation plan

1. **Confirm the actual setup.** Record platform, OS/app versions, ordinary keyboard versus Shortcut usage, whether devices use the same account, applicable plan/export role, and relevant retention settings. Keep account identity and personal settings evidence private. Do not change settings to make a route work. Continue public-document research while owner facts or device authorization are pending.

2. **Qualify aggregate access first.** Inventory supported desktop Insights, admin CSV and any documented consumer analytics API/export. Separate a supported recurring feed, owner-initiated export and manually transcribed counter. For each route record eligibility, available history, refresh delay, reporting timezone, granularity, dimensions and reset/deletion behavior. Inspect only an owner-supplied export or explicitly authorized account surface, limited to the owner's usage. Determine whether it identifies mobile-only data, a particular phone, or combined usage. Distinguish recorded counts from forecasts, omitted rows from confirmed zeros, and cumulative snapshots from daily increments. No plan upgrade or organization-control change is part of this investigation.

3. **Assess the iPhone Shortcut route conditionally.** If applicable and separately authorized, use deliberate synthetic phrases in a temporary owner-approved test. Check the return value with the Flow keyboard inactive and active, cancellation/no result, repeated invocation and retry. Record precisely what is returned and where text lands. Evaluate whether local processing could produce counts and optional word/phrase aggregates before transfer. A locally generated capture timestamp is not evidence of the original speech start or duration. Do not infer raw recognition, cleanup pairs, later corrections, source app or speaking rate from a final transcript alone. Label coverage as Shortcut-mediated dictations only. If Android is used, examine documented Android export/share/automation facilities and record any missing equivalent; do not assume iOS behavior applies.

4. **Check export fallbacks.** Determine whether an owner-requested account data export could contain useful retained mobile data and whether it is historical-only or repeatable. Prepare specific unanswered questions for Wispr if needed; sending them requires explicit authorization. Do not promise an export contains local history or change cloud-retention/model-sharing preferences. [Wispr security and export information](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/3467817258-security-and-compliance-faq). Manual copying of selected history may be a limited fallback, but must not be described as a complete structured export.

5. **Define the integration boundary.** Propose a source mapping for the format owned by [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468) and the consumer owned by [#470](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/470). Include source/platform, capture scope, metric definition, reporting window, timezone, granularity, observation time, coverage and provenance. Describe a deduplication/replacement rule for repeated exports and late revisions. Never add an account-wide desktop/mobile total to the collector's desktop totals. Deriving mobile as combined minus desktop is acceptable only if identical definitions, complete coverage and aligned windows are demonstrated; otherwise show separate series. Identify proposed storage, transport, authentication, retention and schema changes for a later implementation without selecting an unverified transport or changing the desktop contract here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dated capability matrix covers synced statistics, supported CSV/API export, conditional phone automation and account-export fallback. Each row distinguishes documented behavior, observed behavior, untested assumptions and unavailable capabilities.
- [ ] For each route, the matrix addresses historical versus future coverage, words, dictations, daily/hourly activity, duration/rate, apps, words/phrases, automatic cleanup and later edits. Unsupported metrics stay unavailable; aggregate fix counts are not correction pairs or evidence of speaking improvement.
- [ ] Eligibility and platform assumptions are resolved or explicitly recorded as owner-input gaps. Device-dependent claims have a versioned, reproducible synthetic observation; missing access cannot be reported as successful qualification.
- [ ] Synthetic reconciliation examples cover desktop-only, phone-only and mixed usage; overlapping windows; repeated imports/snapshots; late updates; UTC/local-date boundaries; and missing versus zero values. They demonstrate the proposed counting rules without requiring an ingestion implementation.
- [ ] The recommendation states whether each route is suitable for automatic integration, manual import, limited prospective capture, or currently unavailable/unqualified, with concrete reasons and operating limitations.
- [ ] Any recommended implementation has a bounded proposed scope, required schema/storage changes, privacy controls, remaining prerequisites and acceptance checks. No implementation is declared ready while its required data-access or coverage evidence is missing.

### Dependencies

No blocking dependency on the desktop milestone. #467, #468 and #470 are related contract owners, not prerequisites for public-document research. This investigation must not delay or broaden their Windows-only delivery.

Phone/account observations depend on the owner identifying the target and authorizing the specific access or test. Export eligibility may rule out a route without blocking the remaining research. If access is unavailable, deliver the documented findings and name the unresolved qualification work; do not silently turn assumptions into findings.

### Verification and delivery target

Deliver a sanitized findings record linked from this issue, the capability matrix, synthetic reconciliation examples and a recommended next step. Cite official sources with verification dates. Record the exact test method and platform/app versions for observations, keeping personal evidence private. Distinguish research completion from qualification on the owner's phone. A supported negative finding is a valid outcome; closing with outstanding device checks must name those limits and the condition for reopening or follow-up.

This issue ends at investigation and implementation planning. No collector, database migration, dashboard feature, recurring task or permanent Shortcut is delivered. Tracker-only planning needs no product test run; any temporary prototype later authorized must report what was actually tested and remove its own temporary data.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Raw transcripts, audio, credentials, account identifiers and personal usage examples stay out of public issues, source control and public screenshots. Use synthetic examples. Aggregate text remains sensitive and requires the separate opt-in already planned for desktop; that planning approval does not enable mobile collection.
- No reading private app/session files, extracting credentials, replaying undocumented authenticated endpoints, broad clipboard monitoring, sandbox bypass, rooting/jailbreaking or whole-phone backup extraction.
- No sign-out, reinstall, history deletion, retention changes or unrelated settings changes to test a hypothesis. No access to other organization members' records.
- Speaking-improvement interpretation remains [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473); dictionary/snippet suggestions remain [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474). Neither becomes part of this investigation's implementation scope.

## Work assessment

- Complexity: medium; several access routes and overlapping metric scopes, bounded to one owner's usage.
- Uncertainty: high; phone setup, export eligibility, field availability and reliable mobile separation need evidence.
- Impact: low for public-document research; high if later access touches personal text or account exports. Keep those activities explicitly scoped and authorized.
- Readiness: ready for research. Owner-specific observations are conditional on setup facts and applicable authorization; no implementation readiness is implied.
- Reassess if Wispr changes export/API contracts, the owner selects another platform, or a proposed route requires broader retention or account permissions.

issues.title: Install and verify the private Wispr collector and dashboard on the owner PC
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

After source delivery, one named owner explicitly installs and verifies [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467) on the selected Windows PC and its existing WSL hub. Required input: [#471](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/471) and its transitive collector/language/hub source dependencies, merged-revision CI, package receipts and current-candidate UI approval.

Planning this issue authorizes no installation, personal settings change, scheduled task, service restart or recurring read. It is the separate installed finish line for the source-only issues.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. On explicit request, identify the owner, exact Wispr source, Windows Node runtime, collector output/private-state directory, WSL hub configuration and installed hub/dashboard revision. Read the currently applicable install procedure; use its plan/status facilities. Do not assume #465/#427 are already delivered or install from a development worktree.
2. Verify the immutable release/package checksums and supported Windows runtime. Preserve the previous hub package/config through existing backup/rollback facilities. The collector needs its own private state backup; a numeric-only backup omits all text derivatives. No backup of the complete Wispr source database is required by this integration.
3. Run one explicitly authorized read-only collection, initially numeric-only. Verify source preservation and compare a bounded known period with the app/direct local metadata. Built-in lifetime/mobile totals may differ from retained/captured desktop data; explain the difference instead of forcing equality. Keep actual usage/content evidence private outside Git.
4. Ask the owner to explicitly enable language collection and hub text sharing if wanted; the planning choice is not an installed opt-in. Compare a small owner-chosen set of raw/cleaned/edited records locally without publishing them; confirm unknown edit finality stays labelled. Verify the installed dashboard and exported numeric/text counts.
5. Install one per-user Windows scheduled task for a five-minute run, same owner, explicit absolute executable/config paths, no concurrent starts and no catch-up queue after sleep. This is an integration-specific Windows task; it does not modify the WSL keep-alive or device runtimes. Record exact task identity privately. Reboot/sign-in qualification may use an owner-performed restart; never restart the PC implicitly.
6. Verify the task for a day, including a normal dictation, later edit, collector stop, WSL restart/reconnect and resume after sleep. Confirm freshness reflects collection rather than dashboard polling. Source pruning behavior is tested with synthetic data; do not delete the owner's Wispr history to test it.
7. Exercise stop/uninstall on the collector's own task/files only. Preserve analytics by default; offer an explicit clear as a separate action. Roll back the hub package/config through its existing procedure if needed. No change to Wispr installation, settings, account, dictionary or history.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

One source reader/analytics writer on Windows, read-only JSON consumer in WSL; no mounted SQLite coordination. Credentials and public device APIs stay unchanged. Raw transcripts stay with Wispr on Windows; no personal metrics or phrases in public issues, CI or guide screenshots. Disabling text sharing removes text from responses immediately even if the collector is stopped. An all-data clear must remove pending exports/managed text-bearing backups and advance the generation so reconnect cannot restore old output.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: separately authorized installed collector plus real private dashboard, not physical-device acceptance.

- [ ] Record named-owner authorization, source identity without private path disclosure, release hashes, Windows/Node/Wispr versions, hub/dashboard revision, task cadence and selected privacy/retention settings.
- [ ] Native read-only collection and actual dashboard comparison establish correct words/count/time buckets and metric coverage for an agreed period. Differences from official lifetime/mobile/WPM totals are accounted for.
- [ ] With opt-in, an owner-reviewed private phrase/change sample matches the aggregate; source does not change and no network upload occurs.
- [ ] Repeat runs, restart, same-record late edits, stale/unavailable source and resume have no duplicate counts or fabricated freshness. Credentials lacking the source grant cannot read data.
- [ ] Text opt-out, explicit clear/reset and stop/uninstall have private receipts; source records/settings are preserved, old text cannot return from caches or managed backups, and default uninstall preserves retained analytics.
- [ ] One-day task evidence and the owner's current installed UI acceptance are recorded separately from source tests. Public closure records only outcomes and versions; sensitive evidence stays private.

### Meaningful deferrals

Always-on headless pre-sign-in collection, remote/server deployment, more Windows users and mobile history are not required for this one-owner task. Missed periods are visible; source rows still retained can be imported on resume. Dictations deleted before capture cannot be recovered. Revisit on a concrete missed-data problem or new host request.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-26. Exact installed paths/versions will be refreshed at pickup.

- Complexity: medium; one Windows task and the existing hub installation.
- Uncertainty: medium until source native-Windows qualification and the installed readback exist.
- Impact: high; live private data, scheduled execution and a hub update require explicit installation authority and recovery evidence.
- Readiness: blocked by [#471](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/471) and its transitive dependencies, then the owner's explicit installation request. Source issue closure alone does not grant that request.

issues.title: Show Wispr usage, phrase and correction trends in the B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

One Wispr page plus a compact home widget shows all first-milestone metrics from [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467). It uses [#470](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/470) and [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469), the existing React dashboard, hash routes, widget registry, application skin and authenticated session. No separate dashboard app or data collector in the browser.

### Smallest useful implementation

Add a distinct route such as `#/wispr/<sourceId>` and a `wispr-summary` read-only widget registered in `src/widgets.ts`; source IDs cannot collide with component routes. Navigation and the widget appear only when the context grants this source. Keep one shared filter/revision state across the widget and page. Page controls are date range (today/7d/30d/all/custom), app/category and the visible configured timezone. Language-specific unsupported filter combinations are disabled with a short reason, not applied only to some charts silently.

| Section | Required view and interaction |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Words, dictations, speech/recording minutes, weighted WPM, average dictation length/duration, active days and descriptive activity runs; daily volume with previous equal-length period where available |
| When & where | Hour × weekday heatmap with words/count/time selector; daily/weekly/monthly series; app/category ranked bars/table; distinguish Unknown app and metric coverage |
| Words & phrases | Separate raw-recognition/cleaned-output/observed-text views, top words (all/useful-word filter) and repeated 2–5-word phrases; counts, distinct dictations, minimum-support rule and ranking limits |
| Changes | Flow cleanup versus observed later edits; stored correction/replacement counters separate from derived change rates; common added/removed/replaced phrases; edit-observation coverage and unknown finality |
| Dictionary & snippets | Active entry/snippet counts, separate local/remote counter snapshots, permitted repeated labels; no sum over snapshots, auto-edit buttons or invented date attribution |
| Data & coverage | Last successful collection, latest source activity, date span, reporting zone, current source versus archived aggregates, per-field missing/skipped counts, gaps, schema/algorithm version and text-sharing status |

The home widget shows today's words and speaking minutes plus a seven-day numeric sparkline, last-success age and link to the page. Do not place words/phrases/change pairs on home automatically. These remain on the dedicated opt-in page. Reuse delivered #283 chart primitives if present; otherwise implement only simple local SVG line/bar/heatmap components with shared scale/axis helpers, matching the existing CSP and asset rules. No external chart service, web fonts, analytics or CDN dependency.

A table alternative accompanies every graph. Keyboard focus reveals the same values as hover; touch is supported; state is not color-only. Provide 390 px, intermediate and wide layouts, reduced motion and accessible text labels. Use the existing dense page layout, not a long stack of oversized tiles. Filters survive route changes without rereading Wispr or sending commands.

**Truthful presentation:**

- Missing/unavailable values use a reason, never zero. Unknown source coverage draws a gap; a genuinely observed zero can show zero. Month-to-date is partial; compare equivalent elapsed windows and show the denominator. No percentage change from a zero or unknown baseline.
- A successful hub fetch does not refresh collection time. Show stale and last-good data together. Configured-but-unavailable, disabled, opt-in-off, empty, low-sample and unsupported-schema states have distinct copy.
- Call raw text “recognized speech,” cleaned text “Flow output” and later differences “observed edits.” Avoid “mistakes,” “accuracy,” “sent text,” “better speaker” or an overall communication score. A reduction in cleanup alone is not improvement.
- Coverage is visible next to edit rates, WPM and language ranks. Streak/activity runs are descriptive history, not goals or gamified scoring; they are separate from #283's development-velocity policy.
- Vocabulary ranks use the four exact supported presets. Choosing a numeric custom date range keeps those numeric charts working and shows language views as unsupported for that range, with a one-click switch to a supported preset; it must not silently show different dates.
- Numeric CSV/JSON download is available for the current selection; adding text is explicit and allowed only when both opt-ins permit it. Logout/grant removal clears in-memory data and stops polling. No localStorage, IndexedDB, service-worker cache or hidden DOM retention of text after opt-out.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Use hub source permissions for every read and export. Opening, filtering, navigation and refresh send no commands and never start a collector, change settings, enable sharing or operate devices. Display aggregate strings as text; no transcript drill-down or raw utterance examples. Public screenshots and browser fixtures are synthetic.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source with explicit approval of the current UI candidate; installed comparison is [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472).

- [ ] A synthetic end-to-end dataset drives collector → hub → dashboard and all sections above, including top phrase and separate cleanup/edit pairs. Each displayed total and export matches hand-calculated fixtures and source revision.
- [ ] Date/app/timezone labels, DST-derived heatmap, equivalent-period comparison, zero baseline, missing fields, observed versus unobserved edits, low support, capped exact preset ranks and unsupported custom lexical ranges have unit/browser scenarios.
- [ ] Browser tests cover no configured source, wrong grant, opt-in off, first load, empty data, stale last-good data, malformed/unavailable source, source clear, source replacement and logout. No stale text remains after opt-out or permission loss.
- [ ] Home/page navigation, deep links, filters, keyboard/touch access and table alternatives work at desktop/intermediate/390 px, with no clipped labels or overlaps. Axe WCAG 2.1 AA and reduced-motion checks pass.
- [ ] Run shared build/type/controller/workflow suites, `build:dashboard`, `typecheck:dashboard`, `test:dashboard`, `test:dashboard:browser`, and the applicable hub/package suites. Extend existing matrix and CI tests; record synthetic screenshots and current-candidate human approval.
- [ ] Two independent read-only Standards/Specification reviewers assess the same committed base/head; applicable PR/main CI passes. Source tests do not claim live installed usage or improved speaking.

### Meaningful deferrals

Coaching and practice goals: [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473). Dictionary/snippet recommendations: [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474). Custom home placement stays with [#366](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/366); the default compact widget is sufficient here. Public sharing, physical-display output and raw history browsing have no first-milestone requirement. Owner uses Wispr itself for an individual transcript.

- Uncertainty: low after [#470](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/470)/[#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469) provide fixtures; UI approval remains an acceptance gate.

issues.title: Serve private Wispr aggregates through source-authorized hub routes
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The existing WSL hub reads the Windows collector's aggregate JSON and serves only authorized private dashboard metrics. Parent [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467); required input [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468). Language tables are optional in that producer's schema; [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469) is a related producer extension, not a reason to block numeric delivery.

### Smallest useful implementation

Add a bounded file-reader service under `apps/hub/src/wispr.ts` and an optional private `wispr` configuration block: opaque `sourceId`, explicit aggregate path, diagnostics path, freshness threshold (10 minutes), `exposeToDashboard` and `shareTextAggregates` (both false by default). Paths stay server-side and outside Git/cloud-synced folders. Read only the allowlisted JSON files over the mount, never SQLite or Wispr/session/config files. The operator selects these files; request parameters cannot name paths or URLs. No new socket/listener, ingest API, polling of Wispr or general history store.

Use the existing read scope plus the configured source ID in the credential's existing `devices` grants, following the playback source pattern. Validate collision with every controller/playback source ID. Generic `read` without that grant gets 403. Launcher/trusted-loopback browser sessions gain this source only with explicit `exposeToDashboard=true`; static tokens still need their source grant. Disabling exposure/removing grants invalidates access; text also requires `shareTextAggregates=true` and the collector manifest's text-enabled flag. Never add Wispr to global agent-session snapshots or MCP tool results implicitly.

Proposed routes under `/api/wispr/v1`:

- `status`: configuration availability, source/generation/revision, last-success/source-event times, freshness, coverage, bounds and whether text is allowed; no private paths.
- `summary?from=<date>&to=<date>&app=<id>`: words, dictations, durations, weighted rate components, corrections, dictionary usage and coverage.
- `series?...&bucket=day|week|month` and `heatmap?...`: numeric buckets and local-hour/weekday cells from the same snapshot revision.
- `apps?...`: words/count/duration by safe app/category label.
- `language?period=today|7d|30d|all&app=<id>&corpus=raw|cleaned|observed`: bounded rankings/change pairs and suppression/coverage; custom lexical dates are unsupported in this milestone and return a typed reason. Reject unsupported filter combinations rather than ignore them.
- `export?...&format=csv|json&includeText=false|true`: the same authorized aggregate selection, numeric by default; text requires both opt-ins and explicit inclusion. Correct quoting/formula neutralization; never a database download.

Coordinate exact names in the issue-linked OpenSpec delta and consumer fixture; no browser-supplied timezone rebucketing unsupported by the producer. The report's configured IANA zone is visible. A range is inclusive calendar dates, at most the captured period; reject reversed/invalid dates and excess filters. One cached immutable validated snapshot per source; retain only current revision and sanitized health. Protect event-loop responsiveness with bounded reads/parsing (16 MiB input, bounded nesting/arrays), no more than one read in flight and coalesced 30-second refreshes. Cap route responses to 1 MiB and numeric rows to 10,000; page or request a coarser bucket, never silently drop rows.

Validate the producer schema, algorithm compatibility and source identity before swapping the cache. Missing/invalid/stale input retains last-good numeric data with its true age and a reason; first-ever failure returns unavailable, not empty success. Reject older revisions within a generation. An expired preset retains its actual as-of date and becomes stale/unavailable for today rather than being relabelled. A generation/clear manifest replaces the entire dataset and invalidates old exports. Partial writes are never served. Opt-out takes effect even when the last good snapshot still contains text: evict/suppress all text before responding. Responses and exports use `Cache-Control: no-store`; text is not logged. Browser logout removes client copies.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Same bearer/session, Host/Origin/Fetch-Metadata checks as other hub reads. The grant is checked on every request and after session retirement; filesystem access is not authorization. No change to agent-state, device queues or the generic history contract. An unavailable or oversized Wispr file cannot make device/session routes unavailable. No API can start collection, enable sharing, change Wispr settings or clear source data.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only; install under [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472).

- [ ] Synthetic collector output validates through the real hub; summary/series/app/heatmap/export values and snapshot identity agree. Unknown optional language support shows unavailable.
- [ ] No token, generic read token, wrong-source token, retired session, unapproved Origin and disabled exposure/text-sharing cases return no unauthorized data. Launcher source grants appear only when configured. Existing device/agent grants remain unchanged.
- [ ] Truncated/malformed/oversized file, unknown schema, missing path, locked file, old revision and clear-generation fixtures never serve invented zero/fresh state or resurrect cleared content.
- [ ] Slow file and simultaneous-client tests show bounded work and continued hub health/device responses. Source file path and injected secret fields never reach a response or diagnostic.
- [ ] CSV/JSON uses the identical filter/coverage policy; text remains absent by default and CSV formulas/HTML are safe.
- [ ] Run shared build/type/controller/lifecycle/state/MCP/workflow checks, `test:hub`, `test:hub:package` and setup checks required by current docs/development; existing offline hub archive tests include producer schema fixtures. Add cases to applicable CI and owning guides. No live data in tests.
- [ ] Same-commit Standards and Specification reviews explicitly assess the new authorization and private-file boundary. Current PR/main checks pass before source closure.

### Meaningful deferrals

MCP analytics tools, remote ingestion, arbitrary source files, database replication and integration into #282's future history store are unnecessary for this dashboard. Revisit only for a named second consumer or transport requirement. The current file bridge keeps one producer and one read-only consumer.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-26 at [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467)'s source baseline. Existing `server.ts` uses read scope plus device/source grants for playback and browser sessions.

- Complexity: medium; one file reader and route family using existing authorization.
- Uncertainty: low after the producer contract is delivered; fixed-input validation and fixture math are testable.
- Impact: high; new access to private analytics and optional text makes authorization and cache eviction consequential.
- Readiness: blocked by [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468); shared file edits coordinate with other hub work but do not consume #282/#283.
- Reassess on remote hosting, new users, changed session policy or aggregate schema changes.

## Guide

**Note:** Source-authorized hub reads expose private Wispr aggregate metrics without opening its database.
