issues.title: Add opt-in Wispr word, phrase and text-change aggregates
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Extend [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468) so the owner can see frequently dictated words/phrases, how Wispr cleans them up and how observed later edits differ. This provides descriptive evidence for [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473) and [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474), not a speaking-quality score. Parent: [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467).

Required input: the collector's reviewed schema, private-store/retention behavior and synthetic Windows reader. Native source text interpretation remains bounded qualification here; a field's name alone does not establish that a message was sent or that an edit fixed an error.

### Smallest useful implementation

Keep analysis in `apps/wispr-collector`; reuse the reader, store, publisher and algorithm-version mechanism. Off by default. Numeric-only runs do not select text columns. With `language.enabled=true`, select only qualified raw-recognition, formatted/pasted and observed-edited fields plus the minimal provenance/status/counter fields. No audio, surrounding text, URLs, screenshots or user prompts from other tables.

**Three independent corpora:** raw recognition (`asrText`), Wispr's cleaned output (`formattedText`), and observed later text (`editedText`) when its metadata is usable. Missing edited text is unobserved, not unchanged. At pickup, qualify edited-text status/observation-end fields against source behavior or a controlled synthetic/personal opt-in comparison; until then label it observed text with unknown finality and exclude uncertain fields from confident edit measures. Never call it sent text.

**Words and phrases:** versioned English tokenizer using Unicode normalization, case folding and a documented apostrophe rule; preserve a safe display spelling. Keep both all-word counts and a useful-words view with a visible, versioned stopword filter. Repeated phrases use contiguous 2–5 tokens within one dictation only, with occurrence counts and distinct-dictation counts. No cross-dictation concatenation. Initial analysis supports English; unsupported/unknown-language text has explicit coverage and is not silently parsed as English. Numeric analytics still cover every qualified language.

**Text changes:** deterministic bounded token alignment computes insertions, deletions and substitutions for raw→formatted and formatted/pasted→observed-edited separately. Pair endpoints are at most five tokens each, shown as added/removed/replaced when one side is empty. Longer changes contribute only numeric counts and a long-change exclusion count; never emit entire utterances. Keep source `numWordsCorrected` and `numDictionaryReplacements` separate from algorithm-derived change counts; do not sum overlapping measures or classify them as grammar mistakes. Report changed-dictation share only over records with both qualified stages. Editing rate uses observed edits as its denominator, not all dictations.

**Aggregation and limits:**

- Output contains only group aggregates for fixed range presets (today, 7 days, 30 days, all captured), per safe app/category and corpus. Numeric custom-date filters remain exact. Language rankings support those four presets initially; arbitrary custom lexical ranges are unavailable with an explanation rather than an approximate ranking. Compute each supported preset's exact top entries from all eligible private contributions before filtering/capping. Never sum daily top-N lists and claim a global top-N. Apply the minimum-support rule within each exported subgroup, not just across the entire corpus.
- A term/phrase/change pair must appear in at least three distinct dictations in the requested preset before its text leaves the collector; count repetitions within one utterance separately. Maximum displayed preset ranking: 100 entries per kind/corpus; response says how many qualified candidates were omitted. No complete transcript, event ID, event timestamp, per-event text map or examples leave Windows.
- Bound tokenization/alignment work: at most 2,000 tokens per compared stage and a fixed edit-work budget; oversize text is skipped for language metrics with coverage, not truncated into plausible pairs. Preserve numeric counts.
- Treat text aggregates as sensitive. Exclude URLs, email/phone patterns, file paths and token-like secrets before grouping; allow owner exclusions for apps/terms. These filters reduce exposure but are not a guarantee of anonymity. Render all strings as text, never markup; text exports neutralize spreadsheet formulas. No external AI or telemetry.
- Retention follows [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468). Store no copied raw/cleaned transcript strings. Language derivatives are private data even when unordered. Turning language collection off clears its local derivatives, pending outputs and any text-bearing managed backup; numeric data remains. Publish a text-disabled generation immediately. Hub-side opt-out independently blocks and evicts text even if the collector is offline. Reenablement analyzes only text still available; deleted text cannot be regenerated.

**Dictionary/snippets:** report active entry and snippet counts, local and remote usage counters separately, and their availability. Snapshot counters are cumulative/undocumented-window until qualified; never sum successive snapshots. Show optional aggregate entry/replacement labels only under text opt-in and the same repeat/sensitivity rules. Deleted entries are excluded. Source reset or decreasing counters starts a new comparison segment, not negative usage. Do not edit Wispr's dictionary.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Mechanical changes describe what happened, not why. Recognition errors, cleanup preferences, snippets, style changes and user reconsideration can all cause a difference. Fewer edits or faster speaking do not prove better everyday communication. Empty/failed observations and missing provenance remain visible coverage limits.

No raw utterance drill-down, audio recording, speech diagnosis, automatic rewriting or account manipulation. The owner can use numeric-only mode without sharing language data.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only; installation is [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472).

- [ ] Synthetic examples distinguish raw recognition, Flow cleanup and observed user editing, including an unchanged observed edit, absent edit, partial observation, snippet expansion and ambiguous change. A full rewrite emits numeric counts, not its sentences.
- [ ] Token/phrase fixtures cover case, Unicode/apostrophes, stopwords, repeated phrase in one versus three dictations, language mismatch, deletion/insertion/substitution, long input and deterministic results.
- [ ] Exact preset top-N fixtures include a term that is never daily top-N but is globally frequent. Custom lexical ranges reject as unsupported; the numeric custom range stays available. Counter snapshots are not double-counted.
- [ ] Repeat/restart, late edit, source pruning, algorithm version, exclusions and opt-out fixtures preserve [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468)'s retention rules. A text-disabled report contains no text derivatives, including in caches/managed backups.
- [ ] Canary secrets/paths, HTML and CSV-formula inputs are suppressed or safely encoded; tests assert no raw source strings in logs, fixtures generated from personal data, output files or errors. Use synthetic text only.
- [ ] Run collector build/type/unit/package suites and shared checks; add the new fixtures to existing collector CI. Independent same-head Standards/Specification review covers interpretation and privacy. Planned checks do not establish the owner's speaking habits.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Explaining why a phrase changed, grammar judgments and coaching: [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473). First release labels changes mechanically.
- Actionable dictionary/snippet proposals: [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474); manual Wispr editing remains available.
- Other-language tokenization: revisit when the owner requests a language or coverage shows a material excluded corpus. No unsupported language score.
- Arbitrary custom-date language rankings: use the exact supported presets first; revisit when the owner needs a specific custom lexical range. Numeric custom-date analysis is included. No raw-record API is added to work around this limit.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-26, same source baseline as [#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467).

- Complexity: medium; bounded local text algorithms and aggregation within the existing collector slice.
- Uncertainty: medium; raw/formatted fields are present, but later-edit provenance and dictionary counter windows need qualification.
- Impact: high; words/change pairs may reveal private content despite aggregation.
- Readiness: blocked by [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468). That story's accepted envelope/retention is the required input. Unqualified edit provenance remains an explicitly labelled limitation, not invented finality.
- Reassess for external AI, raw examples, automatic writes, new language support or materially changed source fields.

## Guide

**Note:** Opt-in words, repeated phrases and separate Flow-cleanup versus observed-edit patterns, computed on Windows.

issues.title: Collect Wispr usage locally on Windows and publish private aggregate snapshots
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Produce reliable numeric analytics from one configured Windows Wispr Flow database for the private B.U.N.N.Y. integration ([#467](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/467)). This slice is useful on its own as an on-demand local report; it does not install a task or touch the owner's live data during source tests.

A 2026-09-26 inspection confirmed the relevant source columns and mixed record statuses. It did not qualify a native Windows reader, duration semantics under every source version, or a recurring collector. Personal counts and content are not part of the public fixture corpus.

### Smallest useful implementation

**Ownership and code:** one TypeScript/Node 24 workspace at proposed `apps/wispr-collector`, with pure aggregation functions, a native Windows SQLite reader, a private local analytics store, CLI and versioned aggregate JSON schema/fixtures. Share the pure schema/validator with the hub through the existing workspace/package conventions; no controller-v1 profile, lifecycle events or general ingestion platform. Coordinate root manifest, lockfile and CI edits with their current owners. Create the issue-linked OpenSpec proposal/design/tasks and owning README in this delivery.

**Read algorithm:**

1. Load owner-selected source and output paths from a private config outside Git; no discovery beyond the explicitly configured Wispr source. Establish an opaque source namespace that survives restarts. Refuse UNC/network SQLite paths and reparse/symlink redirection outside the configured owner directory.
2. Acquire one collector lease. Open the Wispr source on Windows with SQLite read-only/query-only semantics and extensions disabled. Use a consistent read transaction and explicit selected columns, including the WAL through SQLite itself. Do not use a live `immutable` connection, copy only the main file, checkpoint, change journal mode, or open it from WSL. Use `node:sqlite` read-only and timeout support after native qualification ([Node 24 docs](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/sqlite.html), [SQLite WAL rules](https://sqlite.org/wal.html)).
3. Inspect required columns and compatible types. Unknown optional fields are ignored; missing required fields make this run unsupported, preserve the last complete aggregate snapshot and publish only a sanitized diagnostic. Known optional fields contribute their own coverage; SQL NULL is not zero.
4. Read only the needed metadata and, when the separate language opt-in is enabled, the text fields owned by [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469). Source record IDs stay local. Release the source transaction promptly, then aggregate outside it. Budget: 1-second busy wait, 10-second source-read limit, 60-second total run deadline, 512 MiB working-memory ceiling, 100,000 input rows and 256 MiB selected input bytes. A supervisor must interrupt a blocked synchronous read. Exceeding a bound produces a capacity diagnostic, never an unlabelled truncated report. These initial bounds are tested, not performance claims about the owner's installation.
5. Commit local analytics changes atomically and publish one validated versioned aggregate JSON using same-directory temporary file + atomic replacement. Flush before rename; failed publication keeps the previous valid file. One successful data revision represents one consistent source read. No network requests.

**Metrics and time model:**

- Eligible rows: formatted, positive `numWords`, valid zoned timestamp. Retain diagnostic totals for all other known/unknown statuses; never call raw/empty/dismissed rows successful dictations.
- Record words, dictation count, recording seconds, speech seconds, duration-valid word totals, automatic correction/replacement counters and each denominator. Invalid negative/nonfinite counts/durations are excluded with reasons. Unknown counters remain unknown.
- Bucket numeric data by calendar date, local hour, weekday and sanitized destination app. Initial reporting timezone is `America/New_York`, stored as an IANA zone; parse the observed timestamp form with a space before `+00:00`, normalize UTC and apply DST correctly. Retain source offset as provenance. Numeric source times remain local in the private store so an explicit reporting-zone change can rebuild numeric buckets without shifting old data silently.
- Weighted rate uses matching rows' words and speech duration; recording-duration fallback is separate. Sum durations in seconds, render minutes/hours in the consumer. Distinguish wall-clock recording duration from speech duration; do not infer session length from timestamp gaps.
- Include daily totals, weekly/monthly rollups, active days, observed consecutive active-day runs, hourly/weekday heatmaps, app totals and category totals. An incomplete collection period is not an observed zero. App categories use one versioned local mapping (AI prompts, email, messaging, documents, other/unknown); app labels never include paths, URLs or document titles.
- Dictionary/snippet metadata and counters use the separate rules in [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469); dictionary totals never add to word totals.

**Retention and late changes:** Keep already captured contributions until explicit clear; source deletion is not a collector clear. Use a separate private Windows SQLite store with a unique `(source namespace, source record ID)` contribution key. Persist only numeric metadata needed for exact bucketing/deduplication and, under the language opt-in, unordered token/phrase/change-count contributions: never a transcript string, token sequence or raw source row. Per-record derivatives stay on Windows and are treated as sensitive, not anonymous; group output is the only WSL boundary.

On every complete source scan, insert unseen keys and replace an existing key's entire contribution when its currently observable metadata/text fingerprint changes. Recompute affected aggregate groups transactionally, subtracting the old contribution before adding the new. A repeated scan is a no-op for counts. Previously seen keys now absent from a complete successful scan become archived/unavailable-source contributions and retain their last observed values; absence during failed/partial scans changes nothing. Reappearing same-namespace keys update the existing contribution, never insert a duplicate. Numeric and language coverage are independent: a source row can lack enough data for one and still contribute to another.

Distinguish records currently retained by Wispr from aggregates captured earlier, with captured/retained date bounds, archive flags and observation gaps. A row deleted before first capture is unknowable, and an archived record's later edits cannot be inferred. Archived contributions preserve their metric/algorithm version; if a new algorithm needs deleted source text, retain visibly separate version segments or mark the derived metric unavailable rather than silently recomputing or mixing definitions. Dictionary/snippet counters are snapshot measures, not row contributions.

Collector state is recoverable from an owner-managed private backup; source data cannot restore archived contributions. Define and test a bounded backup/restore procedure in the runbook before clear or schema migration. No automatic backup rotation framework is required. Clearing all analytics advances a generation and records a capture-after boundary so the next run does not immediately reimport old source rows; historical reimport must be explicit. Clearing text removes local text contributions, current/pending aggregate text and any collector-managed text-bearing backup, while leaving numeric history. Owner-created exports/unmanaged backups cannot be recalled and the clear receipt says so. Language reenablement backfills only still-available text within the current capture policy.

The initial private-store cap is 1 GiB. Approaching it reports capacity; reaching it stops new commits without deleting captured history or publishing partial totals. Keep the last valid report. A conscious retention/size change belongs to the owner; an alert is preferable to losing archived aggregates silently. The source observation and analytics store remain entirely separate.

**Aggregate format:** fix `schemaVersion`, `algorithmVersion`, source namespace/generation, monotonic revision, generated/last-success times, latest source event time, earliest/latest retained/captured coverage, per-field coverage and exclusion counts, source health, collection-gap intervals and truncation state. Include numeric daily/hour/app rows; declare optional language tables and dictionary counters now so [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469) can extend the implementation without an incompatible envelope. Never publish event IDs, private paths, per-event timestamps or raw transcript rows. Carry each preset's as-of/valid-until timestamp; a preset computed yesterday must never be labelled today. Bound a snapshot to 16 MiB; aggregate capacity failure is explicit. Correctness cannot depend on `mtime` as the observation clock.

CLI: `collect --config <private-file>` (one run), `status --config <private-file>` (sanitized), `export --config <private-file> --format json|csv --output <private-file>`, and explicit clear/reset operations. Numeric exports are default; text needs a separate choice. A clear stops overlapping work, advances the dataset generation and publishes empty aggregates so hub caches cannot resurrect old data. Clearing can start a new capture epoch at now; a full historical reimport is a separate explicit choice. Never clear Wispr history.

Default scheduling will be one per-user Windows task every five minutes, installed only under [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472); one run after resume, not a catch-up queue. A stopped collector remains stopped until manually run or its task is reenabled.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Wispr owns its database. No write-capable source connection, update, migration, vacuum, repair, setting change or login/session read. SQLite's normal native reader locks are allowed; no attempt to bypass them.
- The collector's private state/output use owner-restricted Windows ACLs and live outside Git and cloud-synced folders. No copied full transcripts, audio, screenshot or context fields in its own store, logs, reports or exceptions. Text derivatives are sensitive and follow the separate opt-in.
- Last-good aggregate data survives a read failure; a status file/manifest records the failed attempt without refreshing last-success or source-event time. Successful empty read and missing/unreadable source are different states. A replaced database requires explicit source-namespace reconciliation; never merge it silently. No session/account file is read to infer identity. The runbook requires disabling/rebinding the collector when the owner switches Wispr accounts; an account switch inside the same source file is not automatically detectable from this allowlist.
- Existing hub/device/agent behavior is unchanged. The collector does no device work and cannot block ordinary dictation waiting on hub availability.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source and reproducible offline collector package; install is [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472).

- [ ] Synthetic SQLite fixtures cover mixed statuses, missing and zero values, malformed timestamps, unsupported schema, duplicate IDs, repeated runs, delayed formatting/counters, timezone offsets, midnight and both DST transitions. Hand-calculated aggregates match output exactly.
- [ ] Run/restart/late-change/source-pruning/clear fixtures prove the documented retention behavior, no duplicate counting and atomic revisions. A restored source and source-namespace change cannot silently double counts.
- [ ] A native Windows synthetic WAL test runs a writer concurrently with the read-only collector, confirms a coherent snapshot, no source mutation by the collector, prompt lock release and bounded busy/deadline failure. An unavailable native runner is a remaining acceptance gap, not Linux proof of Windows compatibility.
- [ ] Crash-before/after local commit and output rename, locked destination, capacity and missing-source tests preserve last-good data and expose truthful health. Re-running completes pending publication without adding contributions twice.
- [ ] Fixtures contain synthetic canary secrets, URLs, paths, audio/context fields and transcript strings; numeric snapshots, logs and CLI diagnostics contain none of them. Permissions, symlink/reparse redirects and unsafe paths reject.
- [ ] Add proposed `test:wispr`, `test:wispr:package` and their built variants to the root scripts, `docs/development.md` and applicable CI before implementation. Run Node 24 `npm ci`, build/typecheck, the new suites and shared controller-contract/workflow suites. Offline package extraction and a synthetic collect run pass. These commands are planned, not executed evidence.
- [ ] Independent Standards and Specification review cover the same committed candidate; private-state/concurrency review explicitly checks the native read and retention algorithm. PR/main CI follow SDLC.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Language analysis: [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469); numeric-only mode remains usable and never reads text.
- HTTP transport/cloud APIs, additional OSes and multiple accounts/devices: revisit on a second source request. The local JSON bridge avoids another listener and credential.
- Incremental source queries and a durable event archive: full bounded rescans handle late edits simply; optimize only after a measured capacity problem. No claim that dictations deleted before the first successful capture can be recovered.
- Automatic installation/update/rollback framework: [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472) uses existing release/runbook facilities and explicit manual recovery, not a new service manager.

## Work assessment

Planning at hub `55f11cb0b785e2123711b3e8720489205c02dec4`, 2026-09-26. One Windows source, one owner, existing WSL consumer.

- Complexity: medium; one native reader, private persistence and atomic exported contract, with no network protocol.
- Uncertainty: medium; Windows packaging/locking and duration units get bounded synthetic qualification before consumers rely on them.
- Impact: high; a live private database is the eventual input, requiring read-only operation and content-exclusion evidence.
- Readiness: ready for source delivery under the explicit planning retention default above; no implementation or live recurring read is authorized by this planning issue.

issues.title: Plan Wispr analytics: local collection, private dashboard and future speaking insights
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Give the owner a private Wispr Flow page and home widget in B.U.N.N.Y. for dictation volume, time of day, speaking duration and rate, apps, vocabulary, repeated phrases, automatic cleanup and observed later edits. This is one operator's Windows Wispr installation and the existing Linux/WSL hub. No Wispr cloud account or device-control integration is needed.

The owner authorized these GitHub planning issues on 2026-09-26, including aggregate words, phrases and common text-change pairs with a separate opt-in. This authorizes planning, not implementation, installation, recurring collection or personal data publication. A same-day read-only schema/coverage check found the required History timestamps, timezone offsets, counts, durations, app fields, raw recognition text, formatted text and partially populated later-edit fields, plus Dictionary usage counters. Exact personal totals, dates of dictation, phrases, paths and transcripts stay out of these public issues. Native Windows collector behavior remains unqualified.

### Smallest useful implementation

Windows Wispr SQLite → native Windows collector and its private analytics store → atomically published aggregate JSON → existing authenticated hub → B.U.N.N.Y. Wispr page and widgets.

The hub reads the configured JSON file through the mounted Windows filesystem. It never opens Wispr's database or the collector's database across Windows/WSL. There is no new listener, cloud service, browser database access or lifecycle-event ingestion. Wispr remains the sole writer of its source database; the collector owns its own analytics store and output; the hub is a read-only consumer.

**Delivery sequence and criterion coverage**

| Work | Outcome | Required input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#468](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/468) | Windows reader, numeric metrics, retention, versioned aggregate format, private publication and package | None; bounded native-Windows synthetic qualification is part of this story |
| [#469](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/469) | Opt-in word/phrase frequencies, cleanup pairs, observed later-edit pairs and dictionary/snippet usage | Collector and its tested schema |
| [#470](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/470) | Configured aggregate reader, source-specific authorization, bounded read/export routes and freshness | Collector format and package contract |
| [#471](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/471) | All numeric and opted-in language views, home widget, accessible tables, filters and empty/stale states | Language metrics and hub routes |
| [#472](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/472) | Separately authorized installation, scheduling and real-client verification | All source slices and current UI approval |

The source-only slices are complete only with their repository review and CI gates. The milestone's installed finish line is owned by the installation issue. Future [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473) and [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474) are placeholders and do not block this milestone.

**Metric vocabulary and scope**

| Metric | Definition and limit |
| --- | --- |
| History record | Any source row; not necessarily a useful dictation or successful paste |
| Eligible dictation | `status=formatted`, positive stored word count and valid timestamp; other statuses remain separate diagnostic counts |
| Words | Sum Wispr's stored `numWords` over eligible rows; tokenized word counts for language analysis are separate |
| Recording / speech time | Separate sums of finite positive `duration` / `speechDuration`, in qualified seconds; show coverage, never fill missing values with zero |
| Speaking rate | 60 × sum(words) / sum(speech seconds) over the same eligible records; use recording duration only in a separately labelled fallback series; not Wispr's rolling WPM formula |
| Activity | Daily words and dictations, active days, observed consecutive active-day runs, local-hour × weekday heatmap; no productivity score |
| App usage | Words, dictations and durations by sanitized app name and fixed local category; unknown remains Unknown; no URL/title extraction |
| Vocabulary | Separate counts from raw recognition and cleaned output; raw recognition is an ASR result, not verified verbatim speech |
| Repeated phrase | A normalized contiguous 2–5-token sequence recurring across distinct dictations; no utterance examples |
| Flow cleanup | Mechanical raw-recognition → formatted-text changes, plus Wispr's own counters as a separate measure; not proof the original was wrong |
| Observed later edit | Formatted/pasted output → observed edited text, only where provenance is qualified; missing observation is unknown, not unchanged or finally sent |
| Dictionary/snippet usage | The source's recorded usage counters and substitutions; not additional dictated words; counter windows must not be invented |
| Coverage | Available versus excluded/unknown input for each metric, observation periods, retention and archive status, collection gaps and algorithm version |

UI layout: a persistent date filter (today, 7 days, 30 days, all captured, custom), app filter and explicit timezone; Overview, When & where, Words & phrases, Changes, and Data & coverage sections on one dedicated Wispr route. Language views distinguish raw/cleaned output and automatic/later changes. The home has one compact numeric summary linking to the page. Full text aggregates are never placed on home by default. Numeric CSV/JSON export is included; text exports require the same separate opt-in and an explicit export choice.

**Operating defaults**

- Disabled until configured. One native Windows process, run on demand or every five minutes by one explicitly installed per-user scheduled task. No overlapping runs or backlog replay after sleep. Ten-minute freshness threshold; data age is independent of hub health and file reads.
- Language collection and hub text sharing are independently off by default; both must be on to display text. The owner's planning decision permits an explicit opt-in at installation, not automatic enablement.
- Planning default, pending any owner change: keep captured aggregates until the owner explicitly clears them, even when Wispr later deletes source rows. The collector persists numeric contributions and, only with language opt-in, unordered token/phrase/change-count contributions in its private Windows analytics store. It stores no copied raw/cleaned transcript fields. These derivatives are sensitive and can reveal wording; only grouped aggregates leave Windows. This retention choice is shown explicitly during installation.
- One source namespace and one analytics algorithm version. No cross-device deduplication, remote endpoint, LLM call or microphone capture in this milestone.

**Related work, not blockers:** [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) delivered the widget shell. [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) owns general hub metrics history; Wispr owns its external-source data and supplies aggregates without adding rows to agent-state. [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) owns general chart widgets; reuse helpers if delivered, otherwise add only the small shared chart/table primitives needed here. Coordinate shared dashboard paths with [#287](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/287). Neither unfinished inventory nor general history is a prerequisite.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- No Wispr settings, account/session files, source database writes, checkpoints, migrations or dictionary edits. No device commands, personal hook changes or reinterpretation of agent-state.
- Private data stays out of Git, issues, the public guide, screenshots used for public review, telemetry and external AI. Public tests use synthetic text. Aggregate words and change pairs are still sensitive data, not anonymized by counting.
- The collector queries only an explicit column allowlist; never audio, screenshots, surrounding textbox/window content, URLs, account identity or tokens. The hub sees only validated group aggregates and sanitized diagnostics, never per-dictation IDs or exact event timestamps.
- Unknown, missing, stale, disabled and genuine zero are distinct. Coverage and data provenance travel with metrics. No causal claim that edits measure speaking quality, correctness or understanding.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: five source/installation slices above; future insights are not part of completion.

- [ ] Every metric and dashboard view maps to a child issue's fixture and acceptance check.
- [ ] A synthetic end-to-end dataset passes from Windows collector to authorized hub read and dashboard; totals, time buckets, edits, suppression and exports agree.
- [ ] Repeated runs/restarts, late changes, missing fields, source pruning, collector failure and sharing opt-out preserve the documented outcomes.
- [ ] Unauthorized reads and text opt-out expose no metric/text payload; retained last-good data is clearly dated.
- [ ] Current-candidate UI approval, independent Standards/Specification reviews and applicable PR/main CI are recorded on the delivery PRs.
- [ ] The installed issue records package identities, named owner authorization, scheduling, a real read-only comparison and stop/uninstall results separately from source tests.

Each feature delivery creates its exact issue-linked OpenSpec change; lasting decisions go to the architecture/owning guides through that delivery PR. These tracker plans do not create or archive OpenSpec artifacts, refresh the work guide or change the accepted general history design.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Speaking-improvement goals and coaching: [#473](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/473). First release provides descriptive trends, not diagnoses or a communication-quality score.
- Reviewed dictionary/snippet suggestions: [#474](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/474). First release observes only; use Wispr's own editor manually.
- Mobile usage sources, supported exports/API access and conditional iPhone Shortcut capture: investigate in [#475](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/475). Mobile implementation remains outside this desktop milestone and does not block it; additional sources need qualified coverage and deduplication.
- Estimated typing time saved: revisit when the owner supplies a typing baseline; no invented baseline or productivity claim.
- Live recording indicators, hardware displays and automation: revisit only on a separate request after this dashboard is qualified.

## Work assessment

Planning baseline: hub `55f11cb0b785e2123711b3e8720489205c02dec4`, live related issues and private schema-only/aggregate inspection on 2026-09-26. Repository scope defaults: one operator, one Windows source and existing WSL hub.

- Complexity: high overall; split into independently verifiable producer, analysis, consumer, presentation and installation slices.
- Uncertainty: medium. Data fields exist; Windows locking/packaging, edit provenance and source-version changes need bounded qualification.
- Impact: high. Private text derivatives and new data access require explicit opt-in, source grants and disclosure tests.
- Readiness: planning umbrella; source prerequisites and installation authorization remain with the children. No implementation was performed.
- Reassess when source schema/field meaning, retention, host topology or sharing policy changes. Do not widen to another user, device or cloud service silently.

## Guide

issues.title: Define the shared install contract and receipt schema for installed runtimes
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-26 from an owner-requested review of how the hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo runtimes are installed. Publishing it authorizes no implementation, installation or device change.

### Outcome and real setup

The hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo runtimes install, upgrade, roll back and report their running build the same way, defined once in this repository. Each project then implements the contract in its own command, and agents find each procedure through one short `AGENTS.md` pointer.

Setup: one operator on one Linux/WSL host. The installed runtimes are the standalone hub (`codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service`), the Nanoleaf wall, controller and MCP units, and the Pixoo user service.

What the review found on 2026-09-26:

- **Hub:** the upgrade is reconstructed from old receipts because `apps/hub/SETUP.md` still describes the 0.2.0 GitHub release (#427). Archives are named by version, and two different builds were both installed as 0.3.10 (receipts gh276 from `f69d6f4` and gh355 from `3bdbb7c`). Health does not report the running build (#428).
- **Nanoleaf:** `bridge/install_linux.py` only does fresh installs, and `docs/linux-install.md` says "there is no upgrade or rollback mechanism here". Upgrades are hand-run file swaps with no revision stamp ([codex-nanoleaf#140](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/140)).
- **Pixoo:** installs already use one `git archive` copy per SHA and an `ExecStart` repoint, but `docs/local-operations.md` still describes an in-place checkout. The running revision is not visible ([divoom-app-upgrade#114](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/114)).
- **All three:** receipt formats differ between runs, and the hub and Pixoo keep backups under `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/install-backups/`.

### Smallest useful implementation

Add `docs/install-contract.md` beside `docs/controller-contract.md` and `docs/agent-lifecycle-contract.md`. It defines:

1. **Release identity:** the full commit SHA of a clean, merged revision. Package versions are informational. A dirty tree or unknown provenance is refused.
2. **Layout:** each release in `<project state>/releases/<sha>/`. The path the service and hooks already use becomes a symlink to the current release, switched atomically (create the new link, then rename it over the old one). Upgrades do not edit units or hook paths.
3. **Commands** each runtime provides:
   - `plan`: read-only. Names the target, the current release, the changed components and the units that will restart. Agents may run it without approval.
   - `upgrade <sha>`.
   - `rollback [<sha>]`.
   - `status`: compares the installed link, the running build and merged `main`.
4. **Upgrade sequence:**
   - Build and verify the release beside the running one (manifest hashes) before any outage.
   - Take one lock per installation.
   - Back up the mutable state the project names.
   - Switch the link and restart only the named units.
   - Poll health until it reports the target `build.sourceRevision`.
   - On failure, switch back, restart, and record the rollback.
5. **Retention:** keep the current release and the previous three. Prune older ones only after a successful upgrade.
6. **Receipts:** one JSON document per operation under `<project state>/receipts/`, valid against the schema below. Existing `install-backups/` folders stay untouched as history.
7. **Running identity:** health reports `build: {sourceRevision, version}` for the running process, with `sourceRevision` set to `unknown` when provenance is untrusted. The `build` name keeps it apart from agent-state's `sourceRevision` (divoom-app-upgrade#114).
8. **Authority:** every command except `plan` and `status` needs the owner's approval at a checkpoint or an explicit request. The commands never send device commands and never change credentials, hooks or `host.json` unless a story names that change. Physical acceptance stays separate.
9. **Declaring the procedure to agents:** the declaration and placement rules below.

**Declaration.** Each repository adds this text to the existing `Runtime boundaries` section of its root `AGENTS.md`:

```text
Installation: a merged change to <installed runtime source> is complete only
after <upgrade command> installs it on the owner's installation and its receipt
passes, unless the issue marks the change source-only with a reason and links
the install issue that batches it. Offer the upgrade at a checkpoint after merge
and post-merge CI; run it only on the owner's approval there or an explicit
request. Before planning, running or checking an install, upgrade or rollback,
read <procedure doc>#<section> and run <plan command> first.
```

**Placement rules**, with the reason for each:

- The root `AGENTS.md` keeps only rules that apply on every matching task: the completion condition, the authority rule and one pointer that names its trigger. `CLAUDE.md` imports it with `@AGENTS.md`, so both hosts load the same text. Codex caps the combined project instructions at 32 KiB, and the hub file is 9 KiB today.
- The procedure lives in one project document, and `docs/sdlc.md` links to it instead of restating it. This prevents drift such as Nanoleaf's `sdlc.md`, which points at a section saying no mechanism exists.
- No nested `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` holds install rules. Codex builds its instruction chain once at launch, from the root to the launch directory. Claude Code reads a nested `CLAUDE.md` only when it reads files beneath it. Install requests start from the repository root, so a nested file would be missed.
- Project documents pin this contract with a commit link. `AGENTS.md` points only at the local procedure, which keeps always-loaded context small.
- Mechanical safety (the clean-tree check, hash verification, the lock and rollback) lives in the command and its tests, not in prose.

Add `packages/contracts/schemas/install-receipt-v1.schema.json` with valid and invalid fixtures and TypeScript and Python validation, following the existing controller schema. Then publish contracts 1.2.0 through the existing archive-and-receipt procedure in `docs/development.md`, so Nanoleaf and Pixoo can vendor and pin it.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One authoritative state owner and one writer per device. The contract adds no device commands.
- Adopting the contract modifies or deletes no existing receipt, backup or runtime folder.
- Private paths, credentials and tokens stay out of Git and out of health responses.
- The controller and agent-lifecycle contracts are unchanged.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] `docs/install-contract.md` covers items 1–9. A reviewer maps each item to the evidence above and to its consumer stories: #427, #428, [codex-nanoleaf#140](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/140), [divoom-app-upgrade#114](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/114) and [the Pixoo upgrade story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/115).
- [ ] The schema rejects a receipt with a missing, short or non-hex `sourceRevision`, or with no outcome. It accepts upgrade, rollback and failed-then-rolled-back fixtures. Checked by the contracts TypeScript and Python tests.
- [ ] The PR maps the gh417 and gh355 receipts to the schema field by field. No private values are committed.
- [ ] Contracts 1.2.0 is published with its receipt, and its SHA-256 is recorded on this issue for consumers.
- [ ] The shared build, type, contract and workflow checks pass, and the applicable Depot jobs pass on the PR and the merged revision.

Delivery target: source and the published contracts archive. No installation.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **A shared installer library:** declined on 2026-09-26 in favor of per-repository commands, because Nanoleaf is Python. Revisit if the three commands diverge in behavior the contract requires.
- **Moving the hub runtime out of `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf`:** deferred, because the stable-path symlink keeps the unit and hook paths unchanged. Revisit when either changes for another reason.
- **Not covered:** the local-controllers service, producer hooks (#371) and boot start (#356). Revisit at each one's next install change.
- **#313:** its installed-versus-merged view can read these receipts once they exist.

### Dependencies

- **Required inputs:** none.
- **Required by:** #427, #428, [codex-nanoleaf#140](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/140), [divoom-app-upgrade#114](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/114) and [the Pixoo upgrade story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/115).
- **Preferred order:** [agent-skills#69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/69) makes `deliver-work` offer a declared procedure at a checkpoint and lets `plan-work` record the source-only opt-out. Consumer stories can land before it; their declarations then guide ordinary delivery.

## Work assessment

issues.title: Repaint LIFX and Tidbyt status on each hub change notice
issues.body:
Originally filed as a backlog placeholder during the #22 final sweep on 2026-09-26. The owner clarified its source-only outcome on 2026-10-01 through the shared-event planning discussion. Installation and device changes remain separate work.

## Outcome and real setup

The existing LIFX status bulb and Tidbyt status tile reevaluate current Hub status promptly after a change notice rather than waiting for the next 30-second poll. This covers the current Windows/WSL Hub and local controller host, `pendant-1` and the configured Tidbyt.

Measure notice-to-evaluation latency separately from device writes. Latest-state delivery may coalesce brief states. Tidbyt retains its 15-second minimum write interval, so this story does not promise every transient state will appear or every device will change within two seconds.

## Smallest useful implementation

Add optional `HubStatusFeed.subscribe()` in `packages/agent-status`, reading the existing authenticated `GET /api/monitor/v1/changes` SSE route with the same read-only token, validated owner/connection identity, bounded parsing and permitted loopback origin. Interpret the route's existing `state`/`resync` notices and heartbeat behavior; do not change its public wire contract.

Connect LIFX's publisher to feed subscriptions and its existing `EvaluationLoop`. Tidbyt already consumes optional subscriptions; verify its integration and shutdown/reconnect behavior rather than assuming both publishers are wired. Retain the 30-second polling path while connected and disconnected for recovery/reconciliation, plus bounded snapshot reads. Each valid notice requests evaluation; requests during an evaluation coalesce into at most one rerun that reads latest state.

Use cancelable subscriptions, finite stream/frame limits, incremental parsing and bounded reconnect scheduling. Preserve existing authentication, redirect/origin and snapshot-version rules. Coordinate the shared package and controller owners before overlapping edits.

https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/701 defines the common delivery/ownership rules. Preferred order is accepted rules before this story's final review. No new CloudEvents runtime envelope, Effect adoption or reliable-history implementation is a required input for this existing-wire change. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139 remains separate history work; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/702 is an independent investigation. Existing source interfaces are the implementation inputs.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve controller queues/designated writers, current Work/Free/Quiet behavior and manual control. LIFX remains transition-only and does not change power. Preserve Tidbyt's write gate and existing refresh policy. An unavailable feed causes no fresh status paint and does not manufacture idle/connection success; existing last-good presentation policies remain.

A dropped stream must not stop polling. Heartbeats/unchanged snapshots cause no new LIFX transition or excess Tidbyt write. Reconnect/resync reads authoritative current state rather than replaying historical effects. Maintain one evaluation at a time and bounded reads/resources. Stop prevents new evaluation/submission; an already admitted controller write reports its own outcome. Startup behavior remains the publishers' current lifecycle, without replaying commands merely because a stream reconnects.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- [ ] AC1: With a connected fake SSE stream and an idle evaluator, a valid notice starts evaluation within one second of receipt. Use a controlled clock and inspect evaluation invocation separately from snapshot completion and physical write time. Do not claim an end-to-end physical latency bound from this check.
- [ ] AC2: Notices arriving while an evaluation is running create at most one queued rerun. The rerun retrieves current state; storm tests establish no overlapping evaluations or unbounded pending work.
- [ ] AC3: Closed/failing streams, stalled reads, malformed/oversized frames and authentication failure leave polling operational. Fake-clock tests advance through the configured 30-second poll and inspect current-snapshot reads without new paints from unavailable data.
- [ ] AC4: Reconnect and `resync` retrieve authoritative current state under existing owner/auth/snapshot-version checks. Historical/repeated notices do not replay old effects; a freshly observed current-state transition retains ordinary publisher behavior.
- [ ] AC5: Stop aborts/closes the stream and prevents new evaluations/submissions or reconnect attempts. Pending reads settle/cancel within declared bounds; already admitted controller writes keep their independent receipts.
- [ ] AC6: Fake LIFX/Tidbyt consumer tests preserve mode restrictions, manual control, transition-only LIFX writes, Tidbyt's 15-second gate/refresh behavior and last-good/unavailable-feed semantics. Multiple notices cannot bypass device cadence.

Planned source checks: Node 24; `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:agent-status`, `npm run test:lifx`, `npm run test:tidbyt`, `npm run test:tidbyt:python`, `npm run test:local-controllers`, plus the shared controller-contract TypeScript/Python/package and workflow checks required by current AGENTS.md. Use current `docs/development.md` for affected consumer/package validation and update its coverage where needed. Add Hub/server tests if that scope changes; preserving today's server wire is the baseline. Independent Standards and Specification reviewers must inspect the same committed comparison, including parsing, cancellation, concurrency, credentials and recovery, before normal PR/CI/merge gates. Commands and checks are planned, not executed by this tracker update.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Every intermediate state visibly displayed: deferred capability. This is latest-state status; brief attention may disappear before a permitted write. Retained actionable notifications have a separate lifecycle/acknowledgment policy under https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/701 and its identified follow-on work.
- Effect dependency, new event envelope and reliable complete history: unnecessary for this outcome. Use native primitives/existing SSE; revisit only for accepted evidence from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/702 or a concrete consumer/recovery requirement. #139 remains independent.
- Installation and physical latency acceptance: separate explicitly authorized work. Source/fake-stream results do not qualify the installed host, cloud path or visible devices.

## Evidence

In the #22 trial (2026-09-26) every repaint trailed its transition by up to 30 s, for example working at 05:59:25 and the blue paint at 05:59:50.

The current source confirms the gap: `HubStatusFeed` has no concrete subscription; Tidbyt supports the optional feed subscription; LIFX has mode callbacks and polling but needs the feed-subscription wiring. The owner accepted prompt reevaluation with device write limits and polling preserved. Current main: `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949`.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-10-01. One operator, the current installed Windows/WSL setup and explicitly configured LIFX/Tidbyt. Installation is not part of this source-delivery story. The accepted outcome corrects the placeholder's blanket two-second physical promise and its assumption that both consumers already subscribe.

Complexity: medium, because SSE parsing, reconnect/cancellation and two publishers share evaluation invariants. Uncertainty: medium, because exact stream bounds and shutdown integration need bounded source design; observable acceptance is settled. Impact: medium, because incorrect handling could bypass modes, flood writes or misstate status; existing auth, queues and cadence remain required protections.

Readiness: ready for source implementation after this definition is published; remains unselected backlog work. Alignment: reuse existing Hub SSE, shared feed/cadence machinery and controller-owned writers; add no new wire/runtime dependency. Sources inspected: main above, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/controller-contract.md`, `docs/development.md`, current feed/publisher implementations/tests and live #455/#139/#695. Reassess on changed stream/auth semantics, unsupported lifecycle bounds, controller cadence changes or changed delivery target. No tests, source delivery, installation or physical acceptance are inferred from this publication. Planner reasoning setting is unknown.

- [ ] AC6: Fake LIFX/Tidbyt consumer tests preserve mode restrictions, manual control, transition-only LIFX writes, Tidbyt's 15-second gate/refresh behavior and last-good/unavailable-feed semantics. Multiple notices cannot bypass device cadence.

Planned source checks: Node 24; `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:agent-status`, `npm run test:lifx`, `npm run test:tidbyt`, `npm run test:tidbyt:python`, `npm run test:local-controllers`, plus the shared controller-contract TypeScript/Python/package and workflow checks required by current AGENTS.md. Use current `docs/development.md` for affected consumer/package validation and update its coverage where needed. Add Hub/server tests if that scope changes; preserving today's server wire is the baseline. Independent Standards and Specification reviewers must inspect the same committed comparison, including parsing, cancellation, concurrency, credentials and recovery, before normal PR/CI/merge gates. Commands and checks are planned, not executed by this tracker update.

issues.title: Undo the last device change from its card
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 during the #277 final sweep. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome

After a device control sends a change the owner did not mean (a select stepped one option too far, a slider released at the wrong place, the wrong Power button), the card offers one explicit "Undo" that sends the previous known value back as one more guarded command, and the status line says what was sent. ### Starting points

- #277 removed the Apply buttons (owner decision 2026-09-25): a select sends on change, a slider on release, Power on a button press. That makes an unintended send cheaper to cause than before, and the old draft-and-discard step no longer exists.

### Open questions

- How long the Undo stays offered: until the next change on that control, until the snapshot shows a different value, or for a fixed time.
- Whether a mode Undo on Nanoleaf should say that it reapplies that mode's brightness policy (the same wording as Reapply).
- Whether scene and playlist choices get an Undo at all, since the previous state may be unknown.

### Related

- #277 (no-Apply controls), #231 (one-step settings), #245 (shared command lifecycle), #288 (keyboard and D-pad navigation, where a wrong step is likeliest).

**Readiness:** backlog. It needs the owner's answer on how long an Undo stays offered.

issues.title: Report the running hub version and source revision in health and on the Connections page
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-26 during the #417 final sweep; defined the same day to follow the [install contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/465). It does not authorize installation.

### Outcome and real setup

The owner and agents can see which hub build is running, meaning its package version and the source revision it was built from, in the hub's health response and on B.U.N.N.Y.'s Connections page. Today `GET /api/hub/v1/health` lists devices but no version. #417 verified the 0.3.9 install from `runtime/hub-gh30/package.json` on disk, which says nothing about whether the running process was restarted. The archive's `manifest.json` records the version and file hashes, but not the source revision. Setup: the installed monitor, one operator.

### Smallest useful implementation

- `scripts/package-hub.mjs` stamps the source revision into `manifest.json` when the tree is clean at a known commit, and `unknown` otherwise. The hub reads its own manifest once at startup.
- Health and the dashboard context report the contract's `build: {sourceRevision, version}` for the running process, read-scoped and with no paths.
- The Connections page shows the version and the short revision, with the full revision copyable.
- #313's installed-revisions view and #427's upgrade check read this instead of hand-copied receipts.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- No private paths, credentials or host details in the response.
- An unknown revision (for example a build from a dirty tree) is reported as unknown, never guessed.
- Existing health fields and the agent-state `sourceRevision` keep their meaning.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Packaging from a clean tree stamps its `HEAD`; a dirty tree stamps `unknown` (package test).
- [ ] Health returns `build` with the stamped values, and a process started from an older manifest keeps reporting its own build after a newer one lands on disk (service test).
- [ ] The Connections page shows the build, and the owner approves the current candidate per the UI approval scope in `docs/sdlc.md`.
- [ ] The shared checks and applicable Depot jobs pass. The next hub install (#427) shows the new build in health.

### Meaningful deferrals

- The B.U.N.N.Y. home widget for build identity: revisit if the Connections page proves too hidden.

### Dependencies

- **Required input:** [the install contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/465), which fixes the `build` field names.
- **Required by:** #427, whose health check waits for the target revision.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26, from hub `c5ae6af`, codex-nanoleaf `da5f9d3` and divoom-app-upgrade `9467f90` read 2026-09-26, with read-only inspection of the installed runtimes and their receipts.

- **Complexity: low.** A manifest stamp, one health field and one presentation change.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Field names come from the contract; the rest is settled above.
- **Impact: medium.** Health is read by the dashboard and will gate the upgrade command's rollback decision.
- **Readiness:** blocked by the install contract.
- **Reassess when:** the contract changes the `build` shape.

## Guide

issues.title: Upgrade and roll back the installed hub with one command under the install contract
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-26 during the #417 final sweep as a documentation story. Rescoped the same day at the owner's request: the deferred upgrade command is now in scope and follows the [install contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/465). Publishing authorizes no installation.

### Outcome and real setup

The owner, or an agent the owner approves at a checkpoint, upgrades or rolls back the installed hub with one command that implements the install contract. Agents find the command through one pointer in `AGENTS.md`. Hub upgrades #330, #357 and #417 each reconstructed the steps from the previous `install-backups/*/receipt.json`. The #276 and #355 installs both shipped "0.3.10" from different sources, because archives are named by version. Setup: the single Linux/WSL installation, with `codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service` running `runtime/hub-gh30` inside `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf`.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Command.** Add `plan`, `upgrade <sha>`, `rollback [<sha>]` and `status`, run from a clean checkout, following the contract. The command:
   - builds the release from the named merged revision in a disposable checkout (`npm ci`, `npm run package:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package:built`);
   - extracts it into `releases/<sha>/` and checks every `manifest.json` hash before any outage;
   - takes the installation lock and backs up `shared-monitor` (excluding sockets), refusing if `host.json` differs from the recorded hash;
   - switches the link, restarts the monitor, and waits until health reports the target `build.sourceRevision` (#428) and `bunny-launch.sock` returns;
   - rolls back automatically on failure;
   - writes the receipt under `~/.local/share/agent-device-hub/hub/receipts/` and prunes releases per the contract.
2. **One-time migration.** Move the current `runtime/hub-gh30` folder into `releases/<its sha>/` and replace it with a symlink, so the unit and the Codex hook paths stay unchanged. Existing `hub-gh30.prev-*` folders and `install-backups/` stay as history until the owner chooses to remove them.
3. **Procedure document.** Replace the stale "update" section in `apps/hub/SETUP.md` (L67-121) with the command, what it touches and how to roll back. `docs/sdlc.md` "Installation and evidence" links to it.
4. **Declaration.** Add the contract's declaration to `AGENTS.md`.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The upgrade stays an explicit, owner-authorized step. No credential is printed. `host.json` changes only when a story names the change.
- One agent-state owner. The collector's revision keeps advancing across the restart.
- The unit name, its `ExecStart` path and the Codex hook paths are unchanged.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] `plan` changes nothing and names the target, the current release and the monitor restart. `upgrade`, `rollback`, a hash mismatch, a changed `host.json`, a dirty checkout and a failed health check (which must roll back automatically) are covered with fake service control in an isolated state directory (hub tests).
- [ ] At the owner's checkpoint, the migration and one real upgrade to a revision containing #428 produce a schema-valid receipt, health reports the target build, and a real `rollback` followed by a re-upgrade succeeds.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries the contract's declaration for hub in its existing `Runtime boundaries` section: the completion condition with the source-only opt-out, the checkpoint and authority rule, and one pointer to `apps/hub/SETUP.md` that names its trigger. It adds no procedure steps and no nested `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` still imports `AGENTS.md` unchanged. The procedure appears only in `apps/hub/SETUP.md`, and `docs/sdlc.md` links to it instead of restating it (inspection in the PR).
- [ ] In a fresh read-only Claude Code session started at the repository root, the request "upgrade the installed hub to main" reads `apps/hub/SETUP.md` through the pointer, runs or proposes only the plan command, and stops at the checkpoint without effects. The same check in Codex is recorded, or reported pending when no Codex session is available.
- [ ] The shared checks and applicable Depot jobs pass on the PR and the merged revision.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Removing old `hub-gh30.prev-*` folders and `install-backups/`: the owner's choice after the first successful upgrade.
- Moving the hub runtime out of the Nanoleaf state directory: see the contract's deferral.

### Dependencies

- **Required inputs:** [the install contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/465) and #428 (`build` in health).
- **Related:** #444 can use this command once it lands; it is not blocked by it. #313 can read the receipts.
- **Preferred order:** [agent-skills#69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/69).

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26, from hub `c5ae6af`, codex-nanoleaf `da5f9d3` and divoom-app-upgrade `9467f90` read 2026-09-26, with read-only inspection of the installed runtimes and their receipts.

- **Operating assumptions:** one operator and one Linux/WSL host (hub `docs/sdlc.md` Scope defaults). The hub runs from `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/runtime/hub-gh30` under `codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service`, and Codex hooks point into that folder (read-only inspection, 2026-09-26). Claude Code auto mode has blocked `systemctl --user stop/start` and a post-swap receipt write (hub #417, codex-nanoleaf#169), so the owner may need to run or approve the final step.
- **Complexity: medium.** Build, verify, switch, restart, health-gated rollback and a one-time migration of the live runtime.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The steps come from the #417, #355 and #22 receipts and swap script. The owner decided on 2026-09-26: a hub-owned contract with a receipt schema; per-repository commands; each release in `releases/<sha>` behind the path the service already uses; receipts and backups under each project's own state directory; installation included by default, with a source-only opt-out that names a batching install issue.
- **Impact: high.** It restarts the shared agent-state owner and migrates the live runtime folder. A wrong switch stops monitoring for every device until rollback.
- **Readiness:** blocked by the install contract and #428.
- **Reassess when:** the contract changes, #428's field changes, or the monitor unit or hook paths move.

issues.title: Carry the latest prompt and agent response in shared agent state for devices
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-25 from the divoom-app-upgrade#98 follow-up, at the owner's request. The owner wants agent responses to reach the devices eventually. This issue does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes on its own.

### Outcome and real setup

The shared state carries the latest prompt and the latest agent response for each session, so a device or B.U.N.N.Y. can show what was asked and what the agent answered. For example, a Pixoo card or a Tidbyt tile could show the agent's last reply when a turn ends or a question is waiting. This covers the hub's shared owner and its Codex and Claude Code producers. Drawing the text on a specific device belongs to that device's own issue.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **Prerequisite:** #424 (policy change and contract 1.1).
- **Prompt:** the prompt text on `turn.started`. `UserPromptSubmit` payloads carry it.
- **Response:** the agent's final message on `turn.ended`.
  - Qualify the available fields per client version, such as a Stop-hook last-message field where one exists.
  - Otherwise read the last assistant entry from `transcript_path` (Claude) or the rollout (Codex).
- **Questions:** the text of a pending question or approval request, so an attention card can show what is being asked.
- **Bounds:**
  - Store each text as an optional, bounded field, trimmed to a stated maximum with a truncation marker. Raise the 8192-byte envelope bound, or carry text beside the envelope, as the design decides.
  - Keep only the latest prompt and response per session, not the full history.
- **Access:** expose the fields in `hub_sessions`, the monitor snapshot and SSE, and a hub MCP read tool, so agents and devices can read them.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Hooks stay fail-open. A long or unreadable response never blocks or slows a turn beyond the existing hook bounds.
- Credentials and tokens stay excluded. Qualify whether prompts or responses echo secrets from tool output, and redact recognizable secret formats if the owner wants that.
- Existing consumers ignore the new fields.
- Storage and journal growth stay bounded: latest values only, with retention matching session retirement.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- After a Codex turn and a Claude Code turn, `hub_sessions` shows each session's last prompt and final response. Verified by fixtures per client version and an installed observation.
- A waiting question or approval shows its text in the snapshot.
- Long responses are trimmed at the stated bound with a marker, and the hook stays within its timing bound. Covered by unit tests.
- The delivery target is source-only unless the owner asks for installation.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Device rendering belongs to per-device issues. A text-scrolling Pixoo card and Tidbyt text follow when the owner wants them.
- Full conversation history and search: revisit if a consumer needs more than the latest turn.

## Guide

**Topic:** shared-codex
**Highlight:** idea, Shared state carries each session's latest prompt, question and agent reply so devices can show what the agent said.
**Extends:** H424, H372

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-09-25 (read 2026-09-26 03:46 UTC). Complexity medium: text fields, bounds, storage and exposure through snapshot, SSE and MCP. Uncertainty high: which hook fields or transcript reads carry the final response and question text per client version is unqualified, and the envelope bound needs a design decision. Impact medium: hooks run on every turn and storage grows with text, bounded to the latest turn. Blocked by #424. Needs the investigation's answer before implementation.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** Investigate first: a read-only session establishes the text sources and the envelope shape, then the story is reassessed. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

issues.title: Offer to register each device a connected controller lists, as one explicit setup step
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 during the #323 final sweep. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or configuration changes.

### Outcome and real setup

Adding another device on a controller that already serves several (the NL22 Panels next to the Lines, a LIFX Beam next to the bulbs) is one explicit hub setup step instead of a hand-written `host.json` entry. Today each device needs its own `controllers` entry that copies the endpoint and credential of its sibling. codex-nanoleaf#167 did this by hand for `nanoleaf-panels`, and #323 then had to make the hub accept that device's read-only snapshot. The Nanoleaf controller already lists every configured device on `GET /controller/v1/devices`. Setup: one operator and the installed hub.

### Smallest useful implementation

Not yet defined. Starting points:
- A read-only setup operation that asks a registered controller for its device list and shows which devices have no hub entry.
- An explicit add step that writes one entry with an owner-chosen alias, reusing the sibling's endpoint and credential reference, then prints the health check from apps/hub/SETUP.md "Connect device controllers for B.U.N.N.Y.".
- The local controller host (#289) and a future Beam (#319) are the second and third consumers.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Nothing registers by itself. Every new alias is an explicit owner action, and the change is a configuration edit with a backup.
- One writer per device. The hub still calls each device through its owning controller.
- Credentials stay in private configuration and are never printed.
- The per-credential `devices` lists still decide which callers reach a new alias.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Not yet defined. Delivery target: source only.

### Meaningful deferrals

None yet.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Highlight:** idea, #323 and codex-nanoleaf#167 added the Panels by hand-copying the Lines' endpoint and credential into a second host.json entry, though the controller already lists its devices.
**Extends:** H323, H232, H289

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient

issues.title: Fade LIFX status changes and pulse once when attention starts
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 from the #20 reassessment at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome

### Observation

#20 paints each status as one zero-duration `LightSetColor`. - A per-bulb `transitionMs` in the host's status configuration, applied to every status paint; 0 keeps #20's behavior.

- Fake transport tests assert the duration field and the single waveform message; nothing polls.

### Protections

- One writer per bulb through the host's queue; a waveform is one queued request with the same bounded retries and cancellation.
- ADR 0006 precedence is unchanged: attention still wins over a #337 moment, and a moment returns to the painted base.
- A manual change in the LIFX app is still left alone; the pulse fires only on a transition #20 would paint anyway.

An installation owner registers or removes a device controller with one hub command. The command reads the controller's identity, writes the owner-only entry from a token file, restarts or reloads the hub and reports the verification. Each new device kind stops repeating the manual steps.

issues.title: Keep a session's label when the same session resumes
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 from the #312 closeout at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

A session keeps its task label on every device when the same session resumes. After `claude --resume`, `codex resume` or an in-session `/resume`, the Pixoo, the Nanoleaf Lines and B.U.N.N.Y. show the same name the row had before it ended, not a bare ID fragment. The setup is the installed shared owner with its existing Claude Code and Codex CLI producers.

### Observation

#312 showed on the installed hub that both clients' resume keeps the session ID but returns it as a fresh record. The retirement rule (#241) deliberately forgets labels, overrides and notices when a session ends. So a label set by the owner, or by an agent through #372 or #374, disappears every time a session is resumed, which is when the owner most wants to recognize it. Claude `/clear` is harder: it starts a new session ID with no link to the old one.

### Smallest useful implementation

- The owner keeps the last user-set label per retired identity for as long as that identity's retirement guard is kept, which is at most 24 hours and within the existing bound.
- It reapplies that label when the same identity is admitted again as a fresh record.
- There is no linking across different IDs.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Retirement still removes the record and releases device placement.
- Labels stay within the label bound that #424 settles. Credentials and tokens stay out.
- The owner can clear a remembered label.
- A retired identity that never returns loses the label at guard expiry.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Owner tests: label, end, resume and label restored; label, end, expiry and label gone; a label is never copied to a different identity.
- One installed resume per client shows the label back on B.U.N.N.Y.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Carrying a label across Claude `/clear` needs positive evidence linking the old and new IDs, which the hook input does not provide. Revisit if a client adds it.

issues.title: Stop showing a Claude Code session as working before its first prompt and after /resume
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 from the #312 closeout at the owner's request. It records an observed defect until the expected behavior is decided. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Failure and reproduction

This was observed on the installed Hub 0.3.7 (Agent State 3.2.0) with Claude Code 2.1.280 and 2.1.283 on WSL, during the #312 qualification. The per-path times are in `docs/provider-qualification.md`, "Installed CLI and Claude observation".

1. **At launch.** Start `claude` and don't type anything. The SessionStart hook creates the owner record with activity `active` and an unknown turn. The row reads as working until the first prompt's Stop. In the exit run it read `active` for 27 s before any prompt (00:09:34 to 00:10:01 UTC).
2. **After `/clear`.** The new session ID starts as `active` in the same way and stays so until its first prompt ends.
3. **After in-session `/resume <id>`.** The SessionStart for the resumed session carries the `/resume` command's `prompt_id`, which `normalizeHook` turns into a known turn. No Stop follows, so the re-created row stayed `active` with that turn for 68 s, until the session exited, and never showed idle.

The cause is `packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts:140`: `session.started` sets activity `active`, the same as `turn.started`. Codex CLI is unaffected, because its first event arrives with the first prompt.

The effect: a Claude session sitting at its prompt shows as working on B.U.N.N.Y. and on devices that follow activity, such as the Nanoleaf Lines and the Pixoo Monitor rows.

### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

Decision needed before implementation. The candidates are:

- A start with no turn evidence leaves activity `unknown` or `idle` rather than `active`.
- A SessionStart's `prompt_id` no longer creates a known turn.

Acceptance, once decided:

- A launched, cleared or resumed Claude session that has not been prompted is not shown as working.
- A prompt still shows `active` until its Stop.
- Codex Desktop and CLI start behavior is unchanged, or any change is recorded.
- Fixture tests cover launch, `/clear` and in-session `/resume` starts, plus a Desktop start.

### Dependencies, verification and delivery target

- Related: #241 (retirement rule, unchanged) and #312 (evidence).
- Source delivery, with owner tests in `packages/agent-state`.
- An installed check repeats one Claude launch and one in-session `/resume` against the owner snapshot.
- Visible device checks need their own authorization.
