issues.title: Add the LIFX Beam to the LIFX controller and B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner's LIFX Beam appears in B.U.N.N.Y. next to the LIFX bulbs, with power, brightness, color and temperature controls, and in `hub_devices` over MCP. Setup: one operator, the installed hub, and the Beam at an IP the owner supplies, owned by the same local controller host that [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) adds for the bulbs.

Today `controllers/lifx` qualifies only vendor 1/product 27/firmware 2.90 (the A19 from [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/17)). Any other model is reported unsupported. The [pinned product catalog](https://github.com/LIFX/products/blob/8adbe485db11621639f693f3a1510603f029c902/products.json) lists four Beam product IDs (38, 56, 119, 120). All are color and multizone, and their temperature range and extended-multizone support depend on product and firmware. The owner's Beam has not been identified yet.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Identify the Beam (read-only, at pickup).** With the owner's IP and permission, send only `GetVersion` (32), `GetHostFirmware` (14), `LightGet` (101) and `GetExtendedColorZones` (511) to UDP 56700, as in #17. Record product, firmware, zone count and catalog capabilities in a comment. No broadcast, no `Set` messages.
2. **Qualify that exact product and firmware** in the controller's qualification table. Keep the A19 entry unchanged. Report the temperature range the catalog gives for that firmware.
3. **Whole-Beam controls.** Power uses `DeviceSetPower`. Color and temperature set every zone to one HSBK, which is what "set the Beam to blue" means.
4. **Brightness keeps the zone pattern.** A plain `LightSetColor` sets all zones to one color, so today's brightness path would flatten a multi-color scene set in the LIFX app. For a multizone device, brightness reads the zones with `GetExtendedColorZones`, scales each zone's brightness, and writes them back in one `SetExtendedColorZones` (510), inside the same queue turn. If the qualified firmware lacks extended multizone, stop and ask the owner before using the legacy zone messages.
5. **Profile and snapshot.** Report zone count and whether the device is multizone in the `lighting` snapshot, and add them to the `lifx-light` profile with a minor version if the owner-facing view needs them. Controller v1 is unchanged. Read `docs/controller-contract.md` before changing any wire value.
6. **Hub and dashboard.** Nothing new beyond #289, since the Beam is another device in the same host configuration. Check that the LIFX component view renders it with the right controls available.

Dependencies: #289 for the hub, dashboard and MCP path. Steps 1-4 touch only `controllers/lifx` and can start before #289 merges. #289 is in progress in another worktree, so coordinate with its owner before editing `controllers/lifx` in parallel.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer: the Beam is owned by the #289 host through the existing per-device queue. No second process talks to it, and nothing polls or scans the LAN.
- The A19's qualification, commands and tests stay unchanged.
- A brightness change never flattens the zone pattern. A zone read that fails before the write reports no write effects; an unacknowledged write stays `uncertain`, as it does today.
- Manual changes in the LIFX app are left alone until the next explicit command. Nothing here adds automatic status painting.
- The Beam's IP stays in private host configuration, never in Git, issues or the browser.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installation and the physical check are the companion hardware issue.

- The qualification comment records product, firmware, zone count and catalog capabilities, without the IP or serial.
- Fake-transport tests cover: the qualified Beam accepted and other Beam IDs or firmware rejected; power, color and temperature on all zones; brightness preserving a mixed zone pattern with an exact packet fixture; a failed zone read with no write; an unacknowledged zone write reported `uncertain`; the A19 unchanged.
- With fakes, the dashboard shows a Beam component with the right controls, and `hub_devices` lists it.
- `npm run build`, `typecheck`, `test:lifx`, the contract suites, and the hub, MCP and dashboard suites pass.
- Any dashboard change beyond #289's LIFX view needs the owner's UI approval under the SDLC UI scope.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Per-zone gradients and scenes from B.U.N.N.Y.** Use the LIFX app for now; the controller leaves app scenes alone. Revisit when the owner asks for zone control or [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) defines coordinated looks.
- **Firmware effects (move, etc.).** Stay off, as for the A19. Revisit with #267 or a moments story under [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292).
- **Agent status on the Beam.** Belongs to [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20)'s choice of which lights show status.
- **Other Beam product IDs or firmware.** Unsupported until qualified; a firmware update needs a new read-only check.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: medium.** Two new protocol messages and a multizone read-modify-write inside the existing queue, plus a profile addition.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The product ID, firmware and extended-multizone support are unknown until the read-only check.
- **Impact: medium.** Commands change a physical light. Effects are reversible, and a wrong brightness write could flatten an app scene the owner would have to reapply.

**Readiness:** blocked on the owner's Beam IP and read-only permission for step 1. Hub visibility also needs #289. This issue does not authorize installation or `Set` messages to the Beam.

issues.title: Build and publish the Guide automatically without generated-file PRs
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Issue or Project updates reach the public Guide on the next successful build without a repository edit, rolling generated-file PR or hand-written status update. Publish the new browser at `/next` in `jimmie-potts/agent-device-guide` while the accepted root Guide and atlas remain usable.

This replaces the old auto-merge plan based on #315. It does not implement an unattended source-PR merge path or bypass source review.

## Smallest useful implementation

Build in the public Guide repository from a recorded Hub generator commit and a complete required issue inventory, with Project enrichment classified under #545/#540. Trigger hourly as a target, manually, and through an explicit cross-repository trigger when the Hub generator changes. Qualify token permissions and event delivery; changing a file in Hub does not itself trigger a workflow in another repository.

Produce validated `records.json`, HTML and assets as build/deployment artifacts, never committed operational snapshots or generated output. A visible “as of” time reports actual collection, not an hourly freshness guarantee. Keep dataset/schema identity, generator commit and per-source completeness evidence. Ask can later consume this dataset without another GitHub collector.

Validate the entire candidate before deployment. Use bounded whole-attempt retries for transient core inventory drift, preserving the useful requirement from #487. An incomplete required issue inventory, invalid required dataset, unsafe public projection, failed render or failed deploy retains the last good site and exposes failed CI plus visible data age. Discard failed core attempts rather than combining their pages. Missing/stale recommendations, malformed optional sections and unavailable Project enrichment are explicit gaps, not publication blockers. A complete permitted cached Project snapshot is an allowed fallback with its original timestamp; a partial or disallowed snapshot is not.

Use one deployment writer and a durable ordering check at the promotion boundary. A delayed older build, retry or run from another trigger must not overwrite a newer accepted release; a concurrency group alone is not proof of ordering. Define the ordering key and eligibility check for scheduled, manual and generator-change runs. A deliberate authorized rollback is recorded separately from routine promotion.

Publish pages, records, catalog and assets as one coherent release under #545's release binding. Define the cache/asset retention or explicit reload behavior so an open browser cannot mix releases. Preserve the full Pages artifact, including the old root and atlas during preview, since a Pages deployment replaces the deployed artifact.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/540 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/654. #240's relevant qualification informs https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/654; delivery does not wait for every wider governance mechanism in #240. #315 remains historical evidence of the old rolling workflow, not a producer of this new deployment.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Reviewed source changes still use normal independent reviews, applicable exact-revision CI and guarded merge. Once explicitly enabled during delivery, routine data rebuilds use their standing schedule authority and automated validation; they need no per-refresh PR or two-agent review.

Keep all credentials out of browser artifacts and model payloads. Project API access is qualified separately from public issue access. Preserve atlas routes, old URLs until the cutover plan handles them, last-good deployment and rollback evidence. No inference runs during generation.

An incomplete seven-day closed-issue read is an optional collection gap: publish the otherwise valid candidate with Recently done visibly partial. Incomplete required open-issue inventory or required relationship reads still block publication, as defined by #545.

issues.title: Publish a daily five-repository delivery and closeout digest
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Produce one daily GitHub digest across jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub, codex-nanoleaf, divoom-app-upgrade, agent-skills and dotfiles. Consolidate delivered work, unfinished work, actionable blockers, overlapping follow-ups and acceptance gaps so the owner does not have to reconcile every session's closeout.

The owner selected a daily run at 9 a.m. America/New_York, with one comment on a dedicated tracking issue when meaningful changes exist. The actual tracking issue is chosen or created during authorized activation. Reports use GitHub evidence by default. They do not depend on a nightly guide PR: #315's historical rolling-PR mechanism is superseded by #317's separate guide publication design.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Build a bounded collector and digest renderer using current issue, PR and closeout records. Reuse existing GitHub collection and Markdown rendering where suitable. Include opened/closed/updated issues, merged PRs and relevant closeout comments across the explicit five-repository allowlist.
- Record exact window boundaries, successful collection watermark, source links and coverage. Handle pagination and overlap between runs, DST, missed schedules and partial failures without silently omitting records or re-emitting the same findings. A failed source remains visibly incomplete; it does not advance that source's successful watermark.
- Separate merged/source-accepted, installed/activated, physical acceptance pending, unfinished and blocked work. A PR merge alone is not full delivery. A run still active at 9 a.m. is reported as active, even when its 10-hour deadline falls later.
- Attribute proposals to existing Session labels where present. Missing labels stay unattributed. Use exact issue links, repository identity, labels/topic IDs and linked comment text for duplicate/overlap candidates; distinguish exact repeated references from semantic suggestions and cite the evidence. Do not read transcripts to improve attribution.
- Complement existing per-session closeout and authorized P1/P2 filing. Consolidate cross-session duplicates, likely overlapping stories, untracked deployment gaps and incomplete new placeholders. Do not suppress urgent session closeout while waiting for the next digest.
- Publish a compact comment with completed work, required owner actions/blockers, and proposed follow-up consolidation. It files, edits or closes no candidate issues itself. Use a stable window/run identifier and authoritative readback to avoid duplicate comments after uncertain publication; do not assume a retry is safe.
- Stay quiet when the completed collection shows no meaningful change. Surface collection/publishing failure or newly required action through the configured failure-notification path; do not post repeated unchanged status. A quiet run is not proof that a failed source had no changes.

Source and on-demand rendering have no incoming dependency on a scheduler. Recurring activation consumes the exact host/account route qualified by [agent-skills #77](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/77) and [dotfiles #9](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/dotfiles/issues/9). #317 and #328 are related guide outputs, not source prerequisites. Preserve the current closeout record contract, including [agent-skills #120](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/120)'s accepted compatible output.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

The digest reads GitHub data and writes only its authorized report destination. No local history, credentials, private paths or transcript excerpts enter it. Content from comments is evidence, not agent instructions. Keep one report publisher and reconcile uncertain writes before retry. No issue selection, automatic backlog filing, Project membership/Phase/Commitment change, merge or device operation follows from a report.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: reviewed collector/renderer source merged with applicable checks, plus explicitly authorized recurring activation and a verified destination comment. A source-only delivery retains its linked activation obligation.

- [ ] Fixtures cover all five repositories, complete pagination, repeated/late events, missing labels, exact duplicates versus uncertain overlap, time-window/DST boundaries, first run and recovery after missed/partial runs.
- [ ] Reports distinguish merged from accepted/installed/physical outcomes and cite the precise supporting comments/revisions. Missing evidence remains explicit.
- [ ] Dry-run output produces no GitHub mutation. A publishing fixture proves one comment per completed run/window under retry and leaves unrelated issue content intact.
- [ ] Secret markers and instruction-like source text cannot cause commands, broader collection or private-data publication. No automatic issue filing/closure occurs.
- [ ] A no-change run is quiet; a partial or failed collection is not mislabeled no change. Failure notifications are bounded and do not repeat unchanged noise.
- [ ] A live read-only collection matches representative GitHub records. Later authorized activation records destination issue, exact daily schedule/timezone, run ownership, failure route and pause procedure; verify one authorized posted digest and its next scheduled run.
- [ ] Run focused tests, the applicable repository checks and independent current-revision Standards/Specification reviews. Update development/CI validation only where the implementation requires it; no product-controller or physical testing is implied.

## Meaningful deferrals

No report dashboard, automatic dedupe/closure, continuous local-history capture or public usage ranking. Human review of proposed backlog changes remains possible without requiring human PR review of delivered source. [agent-skills #128](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/128) owns weekly private Codex/Claude insights; the weekly guide page stays with #328. When semantic overlap cannot be established from permitted evidence, report a candidate or omit it rather than guessing.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium in collection compatibility and semantic suggestions; impact medium because writes are confined to the configured report. Planning defines behavior and evidence only; it does not start a schedule or publish an actual digest.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Enable "Automatically delete head branches" on agent-device-hub, codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade (owner action or `gh api -X PATCH repos/<r> -f delete_branch_on_merge=true`).
- One-off prune: list remote branches whose PR is merged and whose head is the merged PR's head, show the list for approval, then delete them. Keep any branch with an open PR, an unmerged commit, or a registered worktree.
- `docs/sdlc.md` cleanup step 4: replace "Do not delete the delivery branch yourself" with "GitHub deletes the head branch on merge; if it did not, report it". Drop the branch line from the session closeout checklist.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Squash merge, head guard, review gates and worktree rules are unchanged. Deleting a merged branch loses nothing: the squash commit is on `main` and the PR keeps the history.
- Branches with unmerged commits, open PRs or registered worktrees are never touched by the prune.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: repository settings plus one docs-only hub PR.

1. The setting reads back `true` on all three repositories.
2. The prune list was approved before deletion; the receipt (branch, merged PR, head SHA) is kept outside Git; a rerun finds nothing to prune.
3. The next merged PR in each repository leaves no head branch behind.
4. `docs/sdlc.md` step 4 updated; workflow checks pass.

- A scheduled prune: unnecessary once the setting is on.

issues.title: Read delivery execution records into the guide and show deliveries by model
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The guide's history chart shows one mark per merged PR with title and time only. After agent-skills#60 defines the `## Execution record` PR section, PR bodies carry the actual model, level and review effort per delivery with provenance. Read that into the saved history so the guide shows, per delivery, model, level and review effort, and per story the recommended-versus-actual drift, without anyone re-reading PR bodies. The owner uses this on the guide page; the comparison itself stays with agent-skills#44. Real setup: the maintainer's dated `gh api` history refresh and guide rebuild.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `docs/work-guide/work/execution_record.py`: a strict parser on `story_sections.py`, like `recommendations.py`, pinned to the agent-skills revision that merges agent-skills#60. A section that breaks the convention renders "record unavailable"; a PR without one renders "no record".
- The history refresh keeps the parsed record for each merged PR in `work/history/github-history.json`, not the PR body. Fix attribution comes only from the record's `Fixes delivery` line.
- `timeline.py`: each PR mark's tooltip adds model, level, provenance and review rounds when recorded.
- A "Deliveries by model" table in the timeline section: for each coordinator model and level, count of deliveries, median lines changed, review rounds, corrections and attributed post-merge fixes, with unknown shown as unknown and the record count as the denominator.
- Each task brief's Start with block adds one line: the last delivery for that story and whether it matched the recommendation.
- `docs/sdlc.md`: require the Execution record section in delivery PRs and the `Fixes delivery` line on repairs, pointing at the catalog reference rather than copying it.
- Tests in `test_maintenance.py` for the parser and the table; `check_guide.cjs` coverage for the tooltip and the table.

Dependencies: agent-skills#60 merged and its revision known; #304 merged so the recommended side is current.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

History remains a dated snapshot read with `gh api`; nothing is fetched live in the browser for records. No prompts, transcripts, private paths or raw session ids enter the snapshot. Existing chart marks, milestones and roadmap are unchanged. The table ranks nothing and states its denominators.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. The docs/sdlc.md change is outside docs/work-guide, so the guide-only CI filter exception does not apply; the full applicable CI runs.

- [ ] Parser tests cover a complete record, an unknown-heavy record, a broken record and a PR without one.
- [ ] After a history refresh, the deliveries recorded since agent-skills#60 show model and level in their tooltips and appear in the table with correct counts.
- [ ] A story with a recorded delivery shows the drift line in its brief; a story without one shows nothing.
- [ ] `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, independent reviews, PR and merged-main CI.

No human UI approval: the change is guide UI. No OpenSpec change.

## Meaningful deferrals

Backfilling records for the existing merged PRs is excluded; their models are mostly unknown and the table says so. Cost or usage columns wait for a host that exposes them. The hub-to-PR join is story #305's session label plus this record's Session label row, not a new service.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `f94e1f4`. Complexity medium: parser, refresh, three widgets and a docs rule. Uncertainty low to medium: the shape is fixed by agent-skills#60; the table's value depends on how many records exist. Impact low: guide presentation and a documentation rule. issues.title: Investigate host-observed model sources for Codex and the Claude Code model id
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

#305 captures Claude Code's thinking level from the hook's documented `effort.level` field. Two sources remain unqualified: the Codex hook input, whose documented fields do not mention model or reasoning, and a Claude Code model id, which the hook input does not document but the status line JSON does (`model.id`, `model.display_name`, `effort.level`). Codex rollout files record `model` and `effort` in every `turn_context` line and `cli_version` in `session_meta`, but the hub deliberately refuses to open rollout files (`apps/hub/src/codex-desktop.ts`, `docs/provider-qualification.md`). Answer, read-only, which host records can supply model and level for each provider without reading conversation content, and which of them the owner is willing to have the hub read. Real setup: the installed Codex CLI and Desktop and Claude Code on this host.

## Smallest useful implementation

None; this is an investigation. Question: for Codex CLI and Desktop and for Claude Code, which host-provided record gives the session's model and level, at what event, with what stability guarantee, and what does capturing it require: a hook field, a status-line emitter installed separately, or a bounded read of `turn_context` metadata lines from the rollout file?

Evidence to return:

- The documented Codex hook input fields at the current reference, with model and effort presence per event.
- The documented Claude Code status line input and the installation it needs, kept separate from the hub's hook installation.
- Whether reading only `session_meta` and `turn_context` lines from a rollout is compatible with the hub's transcript rule, and what bound it would need.
- A recommendation per provider and the decision the owner must make before #305's deferrals are picked up.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Read-only. No hook, setting or installation change. No transcript or prompt content quoted; field names only.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: a report on this issue, then reassessment of #305.

## Meaningful deferrals

issues.title: Carry observed model and thinking level in shared agent state and show it in B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The lifecycle envelope rejects every property outside its schema, so the model and level a host already reports never reach the hub. Claude Code's hook input carries `effort.level` as a documented common field on every event, which is exactly the value agents cannot self-report reliably. Add an optional, allowlisted `settings` field so the shared owner keeps the last observed model and level per session, and the B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard shows it on the session card. Real setup: the installed standalone hub with its Claude Code and Codex hooks, one operator.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `packages/lifecycle-contracts`: add optional `settings: {model?: string, level?: string, source: 'hook' | 'statusline' | 'rollout' | 'user'}` to the envelope in `src/index.ts` and `schemas/lifecycle-v1.schema.json`, bounded like `label`, with fixtures and both contract test suites. Keep `apiVersion` `1.0`; the field is optional and ignored by older readers.
- `packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts`: `normalizeHook` copies Claude Code's `effort.level` into `settings.level` with `source: 'hook'`; no model, since hook input does not document one. Codex hook input is unknown until the investigation in #306 answers it; pass nothing for Codex.
- `packages/agent-state`: `Session.settings` keeps the last observed value with its observation time; snapshot 1.1 exposes it; the README's privacy section lists model and level as allowlisted metadata. Format version stays 2.0 with the field optional; startup from a store that lacks it needs no migration.
- `apps/hub`: pass the field through the snapshot the dashboard reads; `bin/monitor-hook.mjs` needs no change beyond the normalizer.
- `apps/dashboard`: a small model and level chip on each session card, `unknown` when absent, provenance in its title. This is application UI and needs human approval of the candidate.
- The existing `setLabel` operation is the join to deliveries: the delivery record convention in agent-skills#60 asks the coordinator to label its session with the issue key. No new API.

Dependencies: none for source. Installed capture needs the hub upgrade and hook re-qualification as a separate installation task with a named owner.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Hooks still fail open within their time budget. Missing settings never imply anything. Transcripts and rollout files are not read by this story. One owner, one writer, unchanged retirement, attention, read and freshness semantics. No raw session ids, paths or prompts in the field or the dashboard.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installed and physical acceptance are separate.

- [ ] Contract tests in TypeScript and Python accept the field with each `source`, reject an unknown source, an oversized value or a second unknown property, and still accept envelopes without it.
- [ ] Agent-state tests show a session keeping its last observed settings across turns, surviving restart from a store without the field, and exposing it in snapshot 1.1 only.
- [ ] A fake Claude Code hook payload with `effort.level` reaches the snapshot as `level: high, source: hook`; a payload without it leaves settings absent.
- [ ] The dashboard browser test shows the chip for a session with settings and `unknown` without.
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run test:agent-state`, `npm run test:agent-state:python`, `npm run test:agent-state:package`, `npm run test:mcp`, the Dashboard checks, the workflow checks, independent reviews, PR and merged-main CI.
- [ ] Human approval of the dashboard chip candidate, renewed after any change to it.

OpenSpec: the agent-state-core spec gains the settings requirement; sync and archive on the delivery branch.

## Meaningful deferrals

issues.title: Dashboard browser job flakes in the keyboard-submit brightness scenario
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The Depot job "Checks / Dashboard browser and contracts on ubuntu-latest" passes on the first attempt for a change that does not touch the dashboard. Today it fails intermittently in one Playwright scenario and passes on retry, which blocks routine merges until someone reruns it.

## Evidence

- `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, scenario "accepted brightness and power changes leave their forms ready for the next change without another action" in `apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs`. At line 189 the test sets the fake to uncertain, fills Brightness with 25, focuses the slider, presses Tab and Enter, then waits for the form's status "Result unknown: this may have reached the device (uncertain-result). Check the device, then reload current values before trying again." The wait times out after 12 seconds; the page log shows the Pixoo view rendered normally up to that point.
- Failed then passed on retry on 2026-09-25, all with `depot-code-access` check runs:
  - `main` at `5cdc7fd`: failure started 18:07:53Z, success 18:11:51Z.
  - `main` at `e4135fb`: failure 07:35:29Z, success 07:39:08Z.
  - PR #302 (docs only, two markdown files) at `354ab50`: failure 19:08:51Z (check 108212800527, Depot attempt `mk01pwk080`), success on `depot ci retry` at 19:14:28Z (check 108214705294). The same job passed first time on the identical tree at `43053e5`.
- The attempt 1 log excerpt is kept outside Git in the owner's `.local/evidence/gh-242-resume/pr302-depot-dashboard-flake-mk01pwk080.log`.

## Smallest useful implementation

Reproduce locally by looping `npm run test:dashboard:browser` on the scenario, then find why the keyboard submit sometimes does not produce the uncertain status: whether Tab lands on a different control, whether Enter submits before the fake's uncertain mode applies, or whether the status renders and is replaced before the locator sees it. Fix the cause in the dashboard or make the test drive the same behavior deterministically without weakening what it asserts. No new tooling.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

The assertion set stays: an uncertain result locks the form, nothing retries within 5.5 seconds, focus lands on "Reload current values", and reload restores the controller's desired value. A possibly related pre-existing focus gap was seen during #245: after an uncertain Resume in a busy Media group, focus can fall to the page body. It is not filed and may or may not share a cause.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- The scenario passes 20 consecutive local runs and the Dashboard job passes first time on the delivery PR and on the merged `main` revision.
- If a dashboard behavior changes, the existing UI approval scope applies.

## Meaningful deferrals

- A general retry policy for flaky jobs: none. The merge rules keep requiring a green run; this issue removes the cause.

issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner drives the dashboard without touching the everyday mouse: a command palette opens with one shortcut and jumps to any component, mode, scene or page, and the widget grid is navigable with up, down, left and right. The 8BitDo N30 mouse becomes a dedicated B.U.N.N.Y. controller: its D-pad moves between widgets, a press enters one, another press backs out. The everyday mouse and its driver stay untouched. This runs on the Windows PC with the dashboard open in the browser.

What exists today: the dashboard has keyboard order, focus restoration and ArrowDown, Tab and Enter behavior inside forms, all covered by tests. The N30 emits PageUp, PageDown, Back and Forward from its D-pad, as the [N30 qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-input-qualification.md) recorded, and [#65](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/65) plans an app-scoped AutoHotkey mapper that binds those outputs to Codex actions while Codex is in the foreground. Nothing routes them to B.U.N.N.Y.

**Owner direction (2026-09-25):** the N30 is the dedicated widget controller for the hub. #65's Codex mapping is not withdrawn; the two coexist as foreground-scoped profiles, which is what [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70) already intends.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Widget focus model in the dashboard.** Widgets form a roving-focus grid: one widget holds focus at a time, arrow keys and PageUp or PageDown move by grid position, Enter enters the widget and focuses its primary control, Escape returns to the widget level, Home and End jump. Inside a widget, the existing form keyboard behavior is unchanged. Focus is visible and announced. Hash routes from [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) let the palette and the grid deep-link.
2. **Command palette.** `Ctrl+K` opens a palette listing pages, components, modes per component, scenes, saved playlists and the Places links from [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278). Selecting a control action fills and focuses the matching widget's control; it does not apply it. Applying stays an explicit press, so the palette never sends a command by itself.
3. **N30 as controller.** The browser already receives PageUp and PageDown, so up and down work with no extra software once the dashboard maps them. Back and Forward arrive as browser history buttons, which Chromium may act on before the page can cancel; the first spike checks that. If the page cannot cancel them, the app-scoped mapper from #65 gains a second profile, active only while the B.U.N.N.Y. browser window is in the foreground, that turns Back and Forward into Left and Right and one chosen button into Enter and Escape. No mapping applies outside that window, and unassigned controls keep their normal behavior.

Dependencies: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) for the widget grid. Part 3's mapper profile depends on #65's mapper existing; until then up and down work and left and right wait. Related: [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70) (profiles), [#66](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/66) (installed verification pattern).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- No input ever applies a device command by itself. The palette and the grid move focus and fill controls; a separate explicit press applies, as today.
- The everyday mouse, its driver and the keyboard A/B and Super Buttons stay outside B.U.N.N.Y., as [docs/desktop-controls.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-controls.md) records.
- Mapper rules from #65: foreground scope, no duplicate dispatch from held input, no replay of input received while the window was not in front, explicit enable and disable, and normal behavior on unassigned controls.
- Existing keyboard tests: Tab order, focus restoration after refresh and reconnect, ArrowDown inside forms, and reduced motion.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only for parts 1 and 2; part 3's mapper profile is installed only on explicit request with a named owner, following #66's pattern.

- Browser tests: arrow and PageUp or PageDown keys move focus across a fake widget grid in grid order and wrap at edges as decided; Enter and Escape enter and leave a widget; the palette opens, filters, and focuses the right control without sending a command (a command spy stays at zero).
- Spike result recorded here: whether Chromium lets the page cancel the Back and Forward buttons.
- If the mapper profile is built: injected-input tests for foreground scope, held input and disable, and a short trial on the PC with the N30, recorded as installed acceptance.
- axe passes at desktop and 390 px; the owner approves the candidate before merge.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Custom button mappings and saved profiles: [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70).
- Desk preset cycling from a button: [#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68).
- A dedicated gamepad or keypad instead of the N30: revisit if the N30's four directions and two buttons prove too few.

- For each external source, record the API, its auth model, the read-only scope, what is stored (counts and states only) and the revisit trigger.
- Write one follow-up story per widget group in the feature form, and link them here.

issues.title: Show a read-only wall miniature widget on the dashboard home
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The dashboard home shows a read-only miniature of the Nanoleaf wall: which Lines are lit, in which project color, and why (working, question, blocked, unread, free, held by a stale task). The owner reads the wall's state without opening the wall map on port 8765, and one click opens the full wall map or the wall component page. This runs on the installed hub with the registered `nanoleaf-wall` controller. It sends no commands.

What exists today: the hub's Nanoleaf integration snapshot already carries `mode`, `projects[{id, color}]`, `tasks[]`, `elements[{id, projectId, signature}]` (the Line assignments) and `wallPending`. The wall map draws the physical layout from geometry that lives only in codex-nanoleaf (`layout.json`, the Prism material scripts). The style guide §10 keeps that imagery Nanoleaf's, and [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) leaves shared device art as an open question.

### Smallest useful implementation

Two phases.

1. **Schematic wall widget from the existing snapshot.** A widget in the [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) widget interface draws one cell per Line in a fixed 15-cell strip: fill from the project color, a status mark from the task's state, dimmed for free, hatched for a stale holder. A legend and counts (assigned, free, waiting for a Line) sit under the strip, matching the wall map's "Tasks" summary. Hover or focus on a cell names the Line, project and task label. Clicking the widget opens the wall component page; a secondary link opens the wall map at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through the numeric-loopback link rule the advanced editor already uses. The widget refreshes with the existing 5-second poll and shows the snapshot's freshness.
2. **Physical layout.** codex-nanoleaf exposes the wall's element geometry read-only on its integration route (an issue in that repository), the hub passes it through the integration snapshot, and the widget draws the real shape with the same cells. Until then the strip stays schematic and says so.

Dependencies: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) for the widget interface. Phase 2 needs a codex-nanoleaf issue for geometry. Related independent work: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) (device pages and shared art), [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Read-only: the widget issues no controller command, reservation, assignment or read acknowledgment. Opening it changes nothing on the wall.
- Fixed-meaning status colors from the shared skin; project colors come from the snapshot, never guessed. A stale or unavailable snapshot shows as stale, not as an empty wall.
- Task names are the user label, then the session title and project from #424, then a neutral ID.
- The Nanoleaf controller remains the wall's only writer. [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-bunny-shell.md) (2026-09-25) decided the shell question: the dashboard is the shell and the wall map is Nanoleaf's advanced editor until it retires; this widget is the first user of the shared device art in #355.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- With the fake Nanoleaf controller fixtures, the widget shows the assigned Lines in project colors with correct status marks, free Lines dimmed, and counts matching the snapshot; a stale snapshot shows the stale state.
- Keyboard: cells are reachable and announced; axe passes at desktop and 390 px, where the strip wraps.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the widget on the home grid.
- The owner approves the candidate before merge, renewed after changes.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Physical layout: phase 2, after the codex-nanoleaf geometry route exists (codex-nanoleaf#169), drawn through the shared device art of #355.
- Controls on the widget (assign, clear, locate): stay on the wall map and the component page; ADR 0007 routes them through the integration extension (codex-nanoleaf#170) before the shell offers them, and #271 still decides the group page.
- The Panels device: add a second strip when the Panels register as a controller ([codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113)).

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match.

issues.title: Render playback artwork on the Pixoo and Tidbyt now-playing cards
issues.body:
Follow-up from [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38), which delivered text-only now-playing cards:

- Tidbyt: [#280](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/280).
- Pixoo: [divoom-app-upgrade#90](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/90).

#38 required this open follow-up for artwork rendering before it closed, and [#229](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) (AC6) links it.

## Outcome and real setup

Once #229 exposes optional, source-scoped artwork through the authenticated playback boundary, each display's owning controller sizes and renders it on its card:

- the Tidbyt runner in `controllers/tidbyt`;
- the Pixoo app in divoom-app-upgrade.

The setup is the same as #38: one operator, the installed hub with the HT-A9 source, and the installed Tidbyt runner and Pixoo service.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Read the artwork reference that #229 defines, with the displays' existing credentials and read cadence.
- Scale artwork to each display (64×32 Tidbyt, 64×64 Pixoo) inside the owning renderer, next to the existing text layout.
- Keep writes on each device's existing queue and presentation gates.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep everything #38 settled:

- the Tidbyt rotation tile;
- the Pixoo Monitor pop-up and the Media Off, Pop-up and Whole song setting;
- the 15 s Tidbyt gate and the 2 s Pixoo poll;
- the stale and removal rules;
- one writer per device.

The text-only card stays the fallback. Artwork from an earlier track or source is never shown on the current one.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Each renderer shows correctly sized, readable artwork for the current track: golden or exact-pixel tests with fake artwork.
- Artwork updates after a track change and after a source change, and delayed artwork from an earlier track is discarded: fake-feed tests.
- The text fallback appears when artwork is missing, invalid or unavailable: fake-feed tests.
- Renderer checks are recorded separately from physical display acceptance. Physical checks need a separately authorized trial on each device.
- Delivery target: source merged in both repositories.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Scrolling, rotation slots and foreground Tidbyt takeover stay out of scope, as in #38.

Blocked by #229.

issues.title: Add a Status page with velocity and live graph widgets to the dashboard
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The dashboard gets a Status page and a set of graph widgets. The owner sees development velocity for the three repositories (issues opened and closed per day, PRs merged per week, median issue cycle time, median PR open-to-merge time, commits per day) and live graphs that move through the day: tasks seen and finished, attention waiting on the owner, device mode timelines, brightness, minutes of music, hub memory and health. The widgets use the same widget system as the dense dashboard, so any of them can sit on the home grid.

This is the owner's own view of the owner's own work. It shows counts and trends, never scores, streaks or comparisons, which [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198) already excludes for the guide timeline.

What exists today: `docs/work-guide/work/history/github-history.json` already holds merged PRs, closed issues with created and closed times, commits and issues created per day for the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repositories, refreshed by hand. The guide draws one static SVG of merge dots from it. The dashboard has four count tiles and no charts. The hub records no time series.

### Smallest useful implementation

Two phases. The first needs no new data capture.

1. **Velocity from the saved GitHub history.**
   - Add `scripts/refresh-github-history.mjs`, a read-only paginated `gh api` fetcher that reproduces the saved file byte-for-byte for unchanged entries (the guide refresh needs the same script; today there is none). Extend the entries with PR closed-without-merge and issue label snapshots only if cheap.
   - The hub reads an optional private configuration field `githubHistory: <absolute path>` and serves it at `GET /api/status/v1/velocity` with `read` scope, computing per-day and per-week buckets, medians and the snapshot age. A stale or missing file shows its date, never a guess.
   - Velocity widgets: issues opened versus closed per day (line), PRs merged per week (bar), cycle-time distribution (small multiples per repo), commits per day (sparkline), with the snapshot time visible.
2. **Live graphs from the history store.** Once the [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) route lands, add widgets for tasks seen and finished today (line, updated with the 5-second poll), attention waiting (step line), per-device mode timeline (horizontal bands), brightness (line), music minutes (bar per hour), RSS and collector state (sparkline with the budget line).

Charts are hand-drawn inline SVG React components (line, bar, step, band, sparkline) with a shared axis and scale helper, drawn from the application skin's tokens with the fixed status colors for status series. No charting library, because the CSP allows only `'self'` scripts and many chart libraries need `eval`. Each chart has a text alternative (a table toggle) and honors reduced motion.

Dependencies: phase 1 needs [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277)'s widget interface or lands as the first widgets of it. Phase 2 needs [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282). Related independent work: [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198) (guide timeline scrubber over the same history file), [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Opening or refreshing the Status page sends no device command and marks nothing read.
- The velocity route reads a file the owner configured; it never calls GitHub from the hub, and the refresh script stays read-only and outside the hub process.
- No private data on the page: labels come from user-chosen session labels and repository issue titles, which are already public; playback titles appear only with the store's opt-in.
- Style guide §9: text cues as well as color, reduced motion, no decorative motion beyond 5 seconds, 390 px layouts without overflow, axe WCAG 2.1 AA.
- The dashboard CSP and the three-asset rule stay as they are.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only for phase 1; phase 2 after [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) is installed.

- Phase 1: with the saved history file configured, the Status page shows the five velocity widgets with the snapshot time; with no file, it says so. Unit tests cover bucket math on a fixture with month boundaries and a day with zero activity; the refresh script reproduces the checked-in file for unchanged entries.
- Phase 2: with fake series, each live widget renders, updates on poll, and shows its table alternative; a day with a gap draws the gap, not a line across it.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the new page; axe passes at desktop and 390 px.
- The owner approves the design candidate and then the implemented candidate, renewed after later UI changes.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Review timing, label transitions and in-progress start times: not in the saved history; add to the fetcher only when a widget needs them.
- Achievement scores, streaks and productivity comparisons: excluded on purpose, as in [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198).
- Showing velocity in the public guide: the guide keeps its own timeline; revisit if the owner wants the same widgets there.

**Coordination with [#293](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/293) (checked 2026-09-25):** the two GitHub readers serve different needs and stay separate. This story's read-only snapshot refresh gives history back to each repository's creation, which a poller that starts today cannot. #293's bounded poller gives live PR and CI events for rules and moments. Once #293 emits into [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282), phase 2 adds a "merged today" live widget from those events, and the snapshot refresh may reuse #293's repository allowlist and credential so there is one GitHub configuration.

## Guide

**Note:** Status page with velocity widgets from the saved GitHub history first, then live graphs from the history store.
**Highlight:** idea, A Status page with velocity and live graph widgets.
**Extends:** H282, H277

issues.title: Record a private local history of tasks, devices, music and hub health for graphs
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The hub keeps a private, timestamped history of what B.U.N.N.Y. sees and does, so dashboard widgets can draw graphs that move through the day: tasks seen and finished, attention raised and cleared, device modes and brightness over time, minutes of music played, hub health. Everything stays on the PC in the hub's private directory. Nothing enters Git, the public guide or any service.

What exists today: the hub stores current state only. The agent-state journal keeps 24 hours of change summaries in memory and on disk, no route exposes it, and retirement and expiry leave no journal row. Controller, integration and playback snapshots carry no wall-clock timestamps and nothing samples them. Playback holds only the latest title. Performance receipts are one-off runs. There is no time series anywhere in the hub.

### Data catalog (brainstorm, 2026-09-25)

Everything below is counts, states and durations with neutral IDs or user-chosen labels. Session titles and project names from #424 may be recorded. Credentials and tokens never are.

| Area | Capture | Why it helps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent tasks | Session started, turn started and ended, attention raised (input, approval) and resolved, read observed, retired or expired; per provider (Codex, Claude) and per user-chosen label | Tasks seen and closed per hour and day, time waiting on the owner, time blocked, sessions alive at once |
| Lights and displays | Mode per device over time (Work, Quiet, Free), power and brightness samples, commands issued with outcome, external-control takeovers, observation freshness gaps, wall Line occupancy (Lines assigned, free, held by stale tasks), scene activations, Pixoo playlist generation advances | Time in each mode, how often a manual change overrides B.U.N.N.Y., how full the wall is, which scenes get used |
| Music | Playing, paused and stopped minutes per day, play and pause commands, track changes; optionally artist and album counts when the owner turns on `history.playbackTitles` | Listening time through the day, top artists; titles are private listening data and stay opt-in and local |
| Hub health | Collector state, loss count, admission rejections, feed clients, browser sessions, process RSS, uptime and restarts, hook receipt latency samples | Spot leaks and outages before they show on the wall; compare with the performance budgets |
| Development | Issues opened and closed per day, PRs merged, issue cycle time, PR open-to-merge time, commits per day, from a refreshed GitHub history snapshot | Velocity widgets; owned by the status screen story |
| Later | Tidbyt installation presence, LIFX per-bulb state once connected, PC lighting, room or desk presets, Sonos as a second source | Same series shapes; add when the device joins the hub |

### Smallest useful implementation

- **One private store.** `history.sqlite` beside `state.sqlite`, owner-only, single writer (the hub process), two append-only tables: `events(at_ms, kind, subject, label, value)` and `samples(at_ms, series, subject, value)`. Raw rows kept 30 days; hourly and daily rollups kept indefinitely in a third table. Bounded size with oldest-first pruning.
- **One recorder in the hub.** It mirrors every journal commit, retirement and expiry into `events`; samples each configured controller snapshot, the Nanoleaf and Pixoo integration snapshots and the playback snapshot every 30 seconds, stamping hub wall-clock time and writing only when a value changes; and records each command outcome. Playback titles are stored only when `history.playbackTitles` is true in the private configuration; otherwise only status and counts.
- **One read route.** `GET /api/history/v1/series?series=<name>&from=<ms>&to=<ms>&bucket=<minute|hour|day>` with `read` scope, returning buckets for one or more series, plus `GET /api/history/v1/catalog` listing available series and their subjects. No write route; no MCP tool yet.
- **One export.** `cli.js history-export <config> --csv <dir>` for the owner's own analysis, written outside Git.

Dependencies: none required. Related independent work: [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139) (reliable event history, which this does not claim to be), [#123](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123) (performance), [#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222) (push notifications). [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) (Status page) consumes the route.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- This is a metrics store, not an event archive. It is never presented as complete history, never feeds current-status calculation, and never replays anything to a device. The agent-state journal rules from the core spec stay as they are.
- One state owner and one writer per device are untouched; the recorder only reads snapshots the hub already fetches and the journal the hub already writes.
- Privacy allowlist enforced in the recorder with a test: no field outside the allowlist reaches the store; playback titles absent unless opted in. The store, exports and rollups stay out of Git and out of the public edition.
- Bounded resources: sampling adds no controller polling beyond what the dashboard already causes; the recorder writes in batches; the store has a size cap and the hub keeps serving when the store is unavailable.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then the owner's installation on explicit request.

- Fake-controller and fake-playback tests show events and samples appear with wall-clock stamps, change-only sampling, rollups, pruning at the cap and the 30-day boundary, and route buckets that match the raw rows.
- A test injects a credential-like field into every source and shows it never reaches the store. Session titles and project names do; playback titles do only with the opt-in.
- The hub serves normally with the store read-only or missing, with a health flag in the context route.
- Memory and hook latency stay within `docs/performance/linux-budgets.json` in the standalone measurement.
- Installation gate: a named owner updates the hub package and confirms series accumulate on the installed hub for a day.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Reliable, ordered, gap-aware event history: [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139). Consequence: counts here can miss events the journal missed.
- Read versus unread transitions per chat: the journal does not record the direction, so waiting-to-be-read time stays approximate until [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139) or a journal change.
- Tidbyt, LIFX and PC lighting series: when those devices join the hub ([#16](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/16), [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/17), [#53](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/53)).
- MCP access to history: add when an agent needs it.

**Coordination with the moments work (checked 2026-09-25):** [#296](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/296)'s moment log is a bounded local log "alongside" this store. Prefer one file: moments become `events` rows with kind `moment.*` (trigger, target device, receipt, pre-empted) so the Status page and the moment-log widget read one route. Events from [#293](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/293) (GitHub) and [#298](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298) (calendar) enter the same table deduplicated by their stable event IDs, and a restart never re-emits them. Commands that moments send through the hub are already covered by the command-outcome rows.

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match.

## Guide

**Note:** Private local history store with a data catalog: agent tasks, lights, music, hub health, sampled by the hub and read through one series route.
**Highlight:** idea, A private local history so widgets can graph the day.

### Outcome and real setup

issues.title: Let devices join or leave one shared task pool
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It records a long-term direction until it is clarified and split into stories. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

In Work mode, the operator decides how tasks spread across devices. The owner set this direction on 2026-09-25:

- A device can show tasks on its own. That includes showing every task, as the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels each do today.
- Devices can join one shared pool, so each task is placed once across all pooled devices, like one extended display.
- The operator can pull a single device out of the pool, for example to put it in Free, and add it back later.
- Any device can take part: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and qualified PC lighting.

This is not needed for the first or second version. Near-term stories should avoid choices that block it. The B.U.N.N.Y. pages that show and control these devices are [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- [codex-nanoleaf#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) designs a combined Lines-and-Panels pool inside Nanoleaf. It is the natural first pool and should use the membership model decided here.
- Nanoleaf already stores a mode per device. A device in Free or Quiet shows no tasks, so "Lines only" or "Panels only" needs no pool.
- [#262](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/262) evicts a task across devices through the shared owner. Pooled devices must reconcile that the same way.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The shared monitoring owner stays the single task source, and each device keeps one writer. A pool is a placement decision, not a new writer or a merged controller device.
- Each device keeps its own identity in the hub and controller APIs ([codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113)).
- Reservations, unread tracking, active comets and effect epochs survive a device joining or leaving the pool.
- Red and yellow alerts keep their priority on every pooled device.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined after clarification.

### Open questions for clarification

1. **Placement across different devices:** a Line has two zones, a triangle one, a Pixoo a screen and a LIFX bulb one color. Can a bulb or screen hold one task, several, or only a summary?
2. **Allocator:** does the hub owner allocate tasks across the pool, or does one device controller allocate for the whole pool?
3. **Leaving:** what happens to a device's placed tasks when it leaves the pool, goes offline or changes mode?
4. **Projects:** how project reservations and Shared overflow work across devices.
5. **Pools:** can several pools exist at once, or only one?

### Meaningful deferrals

None yet; decide during clarification.

Related: #271, #262, #267, codex-nanoleaf#44, codex-nanoleaf#47, codex-nanoleaf#113.

issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It records a long-term direction until it is clarified and split into stories. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

One operator sees and controls every device from one B.U.N.N.Y. interface: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and, once qualified, PC lighting. The owner set this direction on 2026-09-25:

- The device projects move into this repository under the B.U.N.N.Y. name ([#25](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/25), [#26](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26)). The interface with controls for every device is the dashboard; the wall map's art moves into it and the wall map becomes Nanoleaf's advanced editor (ADR 0007, 2026-09-25; this line originally said the wall map grows into the interface).
- The interface has several pages. A device page covers one product, for example a Nanoleaf page with today's wall-map art. A group page shows every device together, using the same art alongside LIFX, Pixoo and other device graphics.
- Designs, graphics and images are shared components that any page reuses, not per-page copies.
- Each device runs its own mode. Some devices can be in Work while others are in Free, and in Free each device can be controlled differently.
- In Work, the operator chooses which devices show tasks. Devices can share one task pool ([#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272)) or be pulled out and shown on their own.

This is not needed for the first or second version. Near-term stories should avoid choices that block it.

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- [codex-nanoleaf#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44) adds a device selector to the wall map, giving the Lines and the Panels one view each. It is the first device page, and it draws each device through a reusable renderer.
- [codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113) makes the Panels a second controller device, so the hub and dashboard control each Nanoleaf device separately.
- `apps/dashboard` already lists devices and changes their modes. [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) gives it the B.U.N.N.Y. name and Neon skin. Section 10 of the [application UI style guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/application-ui-style-guide.md) keeps the wall map a separate application for now.
- [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) owns shared colors and coordinated Free looks across devices. [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) puts PC lighting controls in the shared UI.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Each device keeps one light writer, through its owning controller service. Pages and the hub route requests; they never write to devices directly.
- Credentials stay with their owning services. The browser never receives device tokens.
- Alert priority stays keyed by status. No page layout or device mode hides a red or yellow alert on a device that shows tasks.
- Task placement, reservations, unread tracking, scenes and mode selections survive the move into this repository.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined after clarification.

1. **Codebase:** answered on 2026-09-25 by [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-bunny-shell.md). The dashboard in `apps/dashboard` is the shell. issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

One operator controls all participating devices from B.U.N.N.Y. (the hub) as one system: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and, once qualified, PC lighting.

- **Work:** every device shows the same colors for the same meaning. Each status (working, question, blocked, unread) uses the same color everywhere, and each project uses the same project color on every device.
- **Free:** the hub can start a coordinated look, so that every participating device plays something in the same colors, instead of each device being set separately in its own app.
- **Quiet** follows the same idea at low intensity.

To be defined. Starting points:

This issue retains coordinated colors/scenes and builds on those boundaries rather than defining another selected-mode store.
- jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#139 delivered a configurable status palette for Nanoleaf. One palette is stored in the Nanoleaf installation and shared by the Lines and Panels, and only the Nanoleaf wall map edits it. Project colors are also stored and edited per installation there.

- Each device keeps one light writer, through its owning controller service. The hub routes requests; it does not write to devices directly.
- Alert priority stays keyed by status, never by color.
- Manual control in vendor apps keeps working, with the existing ownership handoff.
- Credentials stay with their owning services.

issues.title: Evict a task across devices through the shared owner
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

For one operator and the selected shared Hub owner, provide an explicit **Evict everywhere** action that removes a selected task's shared monitoring record and its known descendants. Every connected consumer reconciles the resulting owner snapshot, removing its row, status and task effects through its existing queue and cadence. Codex/Claude conversations and agent execution are untouched. Offline consumers reconcile on recovery; this is not a promise of simultaneous physical output.

The user requested eventual eviction across devices during [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218), accepted device-only eviction as the first version, and on September 25 explicitly chose shared-record removal rather than presentation-only hiding. This is distinct from [Hub #138](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/138), which resets an activity indicator while preserving the session.

## Smallest useful implementation

Build on #218's durable atomic retirement and fresh-generation behavior after [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) provides the same retirement/late-event rules for all supported provider/client paths. Add a deliberate guarded owner command through the existing monitor command boundary. Record manual eviction as a user command, never as a fabricated provider `SessionEnd`.

The existing Nanoleaf wall task control is the first caller. Add an explicitly named Evict everywhere action alongside the current device-only eviction, using a protected server-side call to the selected Hub. The local action retains its existing meaning. Do not silently broaden a saved device-only request or fall back to local-only removal after a failed global command. Reuse the existing private provisioning path for an appropriately authorized Hub credential; a read-only feed credential gains no control rights automatically and no credential reaches the browser.

Keep one coordinating writer across the Hub change and a linked Nanoleaf companion PR under this issue. Sequence owner command/contract tests, independent review of that shared boundary, then Nanoleaf adoption and end-to-end consumer checks. These are tasks within one delivered behavior, not unrelated layer tickets. No new daemon, event bus, device broadcast or direct controller-database access.

Required input: #241's accepted provider-neutral retirement and delayed-event contract. #218 is delivered. Native end qualification in [#253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253) and Work/Free automation in [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) are related independent work, not prerequisites. #110 must not depend on this feature: it already consumes owner presence.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Use exact owner/session identity and observed revision/generation/turn guards so an old click cannot evict a fresh incarnation or a different selected source. Reuse bounded replay, authentication and Host/Origin protections. Repeated matching commands are idempotent; a timeout or lost response does not authorize a new request identity or optimistic success.

Like accepted retirement, eviction may discard that task tree's labels, notices, attention, task-project overrides, placement and animation state. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects/colors/reservations/scenes/settings and all conversations. It is not acknowledgment, readership, completion, cancellation or approval. Keep one authoritative state owner and one existing writer per physical device.

An eligible new start may create a fresh generation with defaults, without old-effect replay. Recognizable late events and current-turn noise must not immediately resurrect the evicted record. Retain documented unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits rather than promising permanent suppression.

Evicting the last record produces a healthy empty owner snapshot. That allows #110's future explicitly enabled automation to select Free. Eviction itself sends no mode command; disabled automation, manual precedence and unavailable-feed hold behavior remain #110's responsibility. Device-only eviction keeps owner presence and therefore does not produce this result.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: coordinated source delivery in Hub and Nanoleaf; installation and physical qualification remain separately authorized.

- [ ] A guarded command removes the exact known session tree atomically, releases capacity and publishes one owner revision. Unknown/duplicate targets do not create records. Core/storage tests cover unrelated records and preserved global state.
- [ ] API tests reject unauthorized, read-only, wrong-owner, stale revision/generation/turn and replay-conflict requests without removal. A lost-response/duplicate case does not remove a replacement task or execute twice. Persisted retirement guards survive restart.
- [ ] Lifecycle tests cover all supported providers, read/acknowledgment and known late/current-turn events after eviction, plus an eligible new start with fresh defaults and no old effects. Document limits when evidence cannot distinguish old and new work.
- [ ] Real owner snapshots drive focused dashboard, Nanoleaf, Pixoo and Tidbyt consumer tests: rows/allocations/effects disappear, disconnected consumers reconcile later, and a consumer that misses the absent interval still resets the recreated generation where supported. Preserve the documented snapshot1.0/1.1 compatibility limits and normal device queues/cadence.
- [ ] Nanoleaf browser/API tests distinguish device-only eviction from Evict everywhere, preserve selection/focus, reject stale controls, and show unavailable/uncertain outcomes without falsely reporting global removal. User approval covers the concrete changed UI before merge.
- [ ] A fake-owner/presence scenario shows the last global eviction produces zero records while a local eviction does not. If #110 is delivered, run its first/last presence and manual-override tests against the compatible owner; otherwise keep this assertion at the snapshot boundary and carry the integration example into #110.
- [ ] Prepare issue-linked OpenSpec changes at delivery pickup for the owner command, lifecycle state and Nanoleaf control. Assess package/contract compatibility; run required owner/Hub/contract/MCP/workflow checks and Nanoleaf Python/browser/workflow/MCP checks as applicable. Both repositories require independent Standards/Specification reviews, matching CI, guarded merges and merged-main readback. The PR walkthrough covers ownership, duplicate/stale/timeout behavior and recovery limits.

These are planned checks, not completed acceptance. Source work changes no installed credentials, service, hooks, live database or physical device.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Multi-owner/remote installations and multi-operator policy: no requirement in this setup; revisit before adding another owner/operator.
- Additional device-specific eviction UIs or a new Hub dashboard/MCP control: the existing Nanoleaf action is the first caller. Future callers reuse the same owner operation when requested; do not add a separate suppression system per device.
- Bulk clear, undo/restoration history and agent cancellation: excluded. Fresh eligible work can appear with defaults; previously discarded task presentation metadata is not restored.
- Native quit/idle end reliability remains #253; manual global eviction does not qualify it. Automatic Work/Free behavior remains #110.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded` and the delivered #218/Nanoleaf #116 contracts. Complexity medium: one owner command, durable state transition and one existing cross-repository UI caller. Uncertainty medium: product behavior is settled; command schema, credential provisioning and compatibility need bounded design at pickup. Impact high: an authorized action deliberately discards shared monitoring metadata across consumers, so stale-target, authorization and durable no-replay coverage are mandatory. Deferred/backlog, blocked on #241. Reassess after #241 lands or if support expands beyond the selected owner and existing clients.
