Native end qualification in [#253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253) and Work/Free automation in [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) are related independent work, not prerequisites. #110 must not depend on this feature: it already consumes owner presence.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
Use exact owner/session identity and observed revision/generation/turn guards so an old click cannot evict a fresh incarnation or a different selected source. Reuse bounded replay, authentication and Host/Origin protections. Repeated matching commands are idempotent; a timeout or lost response does not authorize a new request identity or optimistic success.

Like accepted retirement, eviction may discard that task tree's labels, notices, attention, task-project overrides, placement and animation state. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects/colors/reservations/scenes/settings and all conversations. It is not acknowledgment, readership, completion, cancellation or approval. Keep one authoritative state owner and one existing writer per physical device.

An eligible new start may create a fresh generation with defaults, without old-effect replay. Recognizable late events and current-turn noise must not immediately resurrect the evicted record. Retain documented unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits rather than promising permanent suppression.

Evicting the last record produces a healthy empty owner snapshot. That allows #110's future explicitly enabled automation to select Free. Eviction itself sends no mode command; disabled automation, manual precedence and unavailable-feed hold behavior remain #110's responsibility. Device-only eviction keeps owner presence and therefore does not produce this result.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
Delivery target: coordinated source delivery in Hub and Nanoleaf; installation and physical qualification remain separately authorized.

- [ ] A guarded command removes the exact known session tree atomically, releases capacity and publishes one owner revision. Unknown/duplicate targets do not create records. Core/storage tests cover unrelated records and preserved global state.
- [ ] API tests reject unauthorized, read-only, wrong-owner, stale revision/generation/turn and replay-conflict requests without removal. A lost-response/duplicate case does not remove a replacement task or execute twice. Persisted retirement guards survive restart.
- [ ] Lifecycle tests cover all supported providers, read/acknowledgment and known late/current-turn events after eviction, plus an eligible new start with fresh defaults and no old effects. Document limits when evidence cannot distinguish old and new work.
- [ ] Real owner snapshots drive focused dashboard, Nanoleaf, Pixoo and Tidbyt consumer tests: rows/allocations/effects disappear, disconnected consumers reconcile later, and a consumer that misses the absent interval still resets the recreated generation where supported. Preserve the documented snapshot1.0/1.1 compatibility limits and normal device queues/cadence.
- [ ] Nanoleaf browser/API tests distinguish device-only eviction from Evict everywhere, preserve selection/focus, reject stale controls, and show unavailable/uncertain outcomes without falsely reporting global removal. User approval covers the concrete changed UI before merge.
- [ ] A fake-owner/presence scenario shows the last global eviction produces zero records while a local eviction does not. If #110 is delivered, run its first/last presence and manual-override tests against the compatible owner; otherwise keep this assertion at the snapshot boundary and carry the integration example into #110.
- [ ] Prepare issue-linked OpenSpec changes at delivery pickup for the owner command, lifecycle state and Nanoleaf control. Assess package/contract compatibility; run required owner/Hub/contract/MCP/workflow checks and Nanoleaf Python/browser/workflow/MCP checks as applicable. Both repositories require independent Standards/Specification reviews, matching CI, guarded merges and merged-main readback. The PR walkthrough covers ownership, duplicate/stale/timeout behavior and recovery limits.

These are planned checks, not completed acceptance. Source work changes no installed credentials, service, hooks, live database or physical device.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- Multi-owner/remote installations and multi-operator policy: no requirement in this setup; revisit before adding another owner/operator.
- Additional device-specific eviction UIs or a new Hub dashboard/MCP control: the existing Nanoleaf action is the first caller. Future callers reuse the same owner operation when requested; do not add a separate suppression system per device.
- Bulk clear, undo/restoration history and agent cancellation: excluded. Fresh eligible work can appear with defaults; previously discarded task presentation metadata is not restored.
- Native quit/idle end reliability remains #253; manual global eviction does not qualify it. Automatic Work/Free behavior remains #110.

issues.title: Report documentation drift against pinned sources in CI
issues.body:
Owner: Hub documentation tooling and CI.

## Outcome and real setup

Every non-guide PR and main push reports where documentation has fallen behind the code it describes, so staleness is visible instead of unknown. Three checks:

1. **Pinned sources.** For each diagram, atlas document and API or database reference, list the pinned source files that changed between the recorded pin and the current head. Hub files come from the checkout; Nanoleaf and Pixoo files come from the public GitHub compare API.
2. **Documented commands.** Every `npm run <script>`, `python3 <path>` and `node <path>` named in AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/development.md, docs/sdlc.md and docs/work-guide/README.md exists in `package.json` scripts or on disk.
3. **Atlas reference.** `python3 docs/system-design/build.py --check` and `python3 docs/system-design/reference/check_reference.py` run in CI, so the generated API and database reference cannot drift silently.
4. **Documented paths.** Every repository path cited in code spans in AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/development.md, docs/sdlc.md, docs/work-guide/README.md and docs/application-ui-style-guide.md exists on disk. Added 2026-09-25: the style guide kept naming `apps/dashboard/src/style.css` as the token layer after #269 moved it to the skin file, and two independent reviews missed it.

Setup: the existing Depot `Checks` workflow, the hub checkout, and anonymous or `GITHUB_TOKEN` reads of the two public device repositories.

Excluded: rewriting or re-pinning any document, re-rendering diagrams, a documentation dashboard, and the work guide's own snapshot age, which its freshness line already shows.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `docs/check_docs_drift.py`, standard library only. It reads the diagram receipts under `docs/work-guide/work/architecture/` (`sourceRevisions`, `viewRevisions`, each diagram's `sources` and `revisions`), `docs/system-design/design.json` source baselines and `docs/system-design/reference/sources.json`, then prints one Markdown report: per diagram or document, the pin revision, the count of pinned files changed since, and the file list. Drift is a warning, never a failure, because lag is documented on purpose; the guide says A2 does not draw Tidbyt, LIFX or shared playback yet.
- The command check, the documented-paths check and the atlas reference check are hard failures that name the file and line. The paths check treats a backticked span as a path when it contains a `/` and matches a tracked-file prefix; a span may opt out with a following `(retired)` note.
- One step in the `Checks` workflow: write the report to the job summary and emit `::warning` annotations for drift and `::error` annotations for hard failures. The same script runs locally with `--report <path>`.
- One paragraph in docs/development.md: what the check reports, how to read it, and that drift is not a merge gate.

Dependencies: none required. Shared-file coordination with [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) on docs/development.md and with [#240](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240) on workflow policy. A workflow change receives full CI.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- The check modifies no document, pin, receipt or rendered file and never re-renders a diagram.
- Job identities, timeouts, matrices and the guide-only path filters stay as they are; `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` still pass.
- Reads are GET only. A failed compare read reports "not checked" for that repository instead of failing the job.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

1. Unit tests for the script with fixtures: a pin with changed files reports them; an unchanged pin reports none; a documented command missing from `package.json` fails with the file and line; a missing path fails; a failed compare read reports not checked; the report is deterministic.
2. On the delivery PR, the job summary shows the report for the real pins (A2 and S4 pin hub `5db67a09`, so drift is expected) and the annotations appear on the PR's checks tab.
3. `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` pass with the new step. All six Depot jobs succeed on the PR head and on the merged main revision.
4. Independent Standards and Specification reviews and a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The workflow and docs paths sit outside the guide folder, so normal CI applies. No OpenSpec change: tooling with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Failing CI on drift: not done. Lag is intentional and documented. Revisit if reviewers keep missing drift shown in the summary.
- Checking prose claims beyond commands and pins, such as statements in docs/architecture.md: not done; there is no reliable mechanical check. Revisit when one claim goes stale twice.
- A PR comment: not done, because it needs `pull-requests: write`. The job summary and annotations are enough. Revisit if they prove too hidden.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24, against Hub `main` [`73166b2`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/commit/73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d).

- **Complexity: low.** One script, two existing checks called, one workflow step.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The pins live in three files with known shapes and the compare API is public. Whether Depot renders job summaries and annotations like GitHub Actions is confirmed on the first hosted run.
- **Impact: low.** Read-only reporting. A wrong hard failure blocks a PR until a documentation line is fixed.
- **Readiness: ready.** Placed in the backlog by the owner on 2026-09-24.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `medium` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258. I started this session on Sonnet at medium effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258. I started this session on gpt-6-luna at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-luna; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; the low-effort row fits only trivial, mechanical work.

**Why:** One standard-library script, three existing checks and one workflow step, with unit tests and a visible CI summary on the delivery PR itself. Policy row: bounded implementation with settled requirements.
**Reassess when:** #240 moves the step to a different workflow, or the pin files change shape.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text, comments and dependencies re-read 2026-09-25 after the documented-paths check was added; ratings as recorded in the story · fingerprint: `7afec9dd783e`

## Guide

issues.title: Add a trading-card skin to the guide and atlas, with art shared by issue label
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide and atlas source.

## Outcome and real setup

Add a second, just-for-fun skin to the cross-project work guide and the B.U.N.N.Y. atlas. It draws on trading card games like Magic: The Gathering. Each issue appears as a card, and each card's art comes from its issue's type label, so every `bug` shares one piece of art, every `enhancement` another, and so on, the way basic lands share art. Atlas component pages get the same card treatment, with art chosen by component category. Readers pick Neon or Cards with a skin picker, and the page remembers the choice.

This is the alternate skin and skin picker that [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) postponed "to a separate issue". Neon Geometry Wars stays the default.

Real setup: the generated guide (`docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html`) and atlas (`docs/system-design/`), read on a phone and a desktop. The guide covers Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo issues. No other hosts or services.

## Smallest useful implementation

**Satisfied required input: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85)** (merged PR [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251)). The card skin uses its role tokens, skin template and "how to add a skin" section, with the reduced-motion and five-second one-shot limit delivered by [#264](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/264). Read the current merged tokens and template at pickup.

- **Art mapping.** One small data file maps art keys to images and gives the precedence order. Issues are keyed by type label. The starting set covers every type label in the three repos' current snapshots, and the owner can rename or reassign any of it:

  | Label | Card "land" | Color |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `enhancement` | Forest | green |
  | `bug` | Mountain | red |
  | `documentation` | Island | blue |
  | `maintenance` | Swamp | black |
  | `accessibility` | Plains | white |
  | `hardware` | Artifact | colorless |

  Workflow labels (`status:*`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `priority:*`) never pick art. An issue with several type labels uses the first in precedence order. An issue with no mapped label gets a default card art. Atlas components are keyed by their category prefix (`API`, `CORE`, `DB`, `DEV`, `DEP`, `CH`, `ADR`, ...), and an unmapped prefix also gets the default.
- **One markup, two skins.** The generators (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`) write the art key into each issue link, brief and component panel, for example as a `data-art` attribute. The skins differ only in CSS, tokens and assets. Neon ignores the art key. Live GitHub status updates (#197) also update the art key when an issue's labels change.
- **Card anatomy.** In the Cards skin, the task brief dialog (#196) becomes a full card:
  - **Name line:** the issue title.
  - **Art box:** the label art.
  - **Type line:** type label and repository, for example "Enhancement - Hub".
  - **Set symbol:** a repository glyph. `priority:high` gets a "rare" treatment.
  - **Text box:** the existing brief content and copy buttons.

  Issue links in the guide tables become small mini-cards, using a type-colored frame and an art thumbnail or glyph. Atlas component panels use the card frame and category art. The table and page structure stays the same.
- **Art.** Original art made for this project and bundled in the repository, one piece per art key plus the default. Agent-drawn SVG is the default, and the owner can swap in raster images through the mapping later. Use no Wizards of the Coast art, card frames, mana symbols or logos, and do not use the Magic: The Gathering name in the UI. Record where each piece came from, and its license, in a short credits file beside the art. Keep all art to about 1 MB or less and make no remote requests.
- **Skin picker.** A small control in the guide and atlas headers switches between Neon and Cards. It stores the choice in `localStorage` (wrapped in try/catch) and applies it in the head script before first paint. If storage is unavailable, the page falls back to Neon.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Status stays readable as text in both skins. Art and frame color never replace the status label, the blocked qualifier or the issue number. Text always sits on a solid panel, never directly on art.
- Fixed-meaning colors (the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repository colors and the status colors) come from #85's non-overridable token set. The card "land" colors are skin decoration only.
- Decorative motion in the Cards skin plays once and ends within five seconds of load; `prefers-reduced-motion` stops it. A skin introducing longer or repeating motion must supply an accessible motion control, as the shared style guide requires. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls. Print shows no decoration.
- The guide's issue totals, links, brief prompts, live GitHub status and existing checks behave as they do now. Change the generators and assets, not the generated output.
- The public guide carries only public issue data. Art and credits contain nothing private.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

1. **Cards render.** In the Cards skin at 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide's issue mini-cards, the brief card and the atlas component cards show the mapped art, type line, repository symbol and readable status text. Evidence: screenshots in the PR. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md#ui-approval-scope) requires. The guide needs no approval.
2. **Art is shared by label.** Two issues with the same type label use the same art. An issue with several type labels follows the precedence order. An unmapped label or category falls back to the default art. When a live status update changes an issue's labels, the art changes with them. Evidence: a guide check that every type label in the current snapshots, and every atlas category prefix, maps to art or explicitly to the default. The check must also cover a fixture issue with several labels and one with an unknown label.
3. **Picker works.** Switching skins changes the whole page without a reload and saves the choice. A seeded preference applies before first paint, and when storage is unavailable the page renders Neon. Evidence: browser check assertions. Seed the stored choice with `addInitScript`; do not assert storage across `page.reload()` (see the #85 CI lesson).
4. **Protections hold.** Status stays identifiable without color or art. Decorative motion runs once and ends within five seconds of load; with reduced motion enabled, nothing moves. Text contrast is checked on the card text panels. Nothing in the Cards skin adds a remote request. The color-literal check from #85 covers the new skin's files. Evidence: extended `check_guide.cjs` and `docs/system-design/check.cjs` assertions.
5. **Docs and credits.** The guide README's skin section lists the Cards skin, the mapping file and how to add or reassign art. The credits file lists each art piece's source and license.
6. **Existing checks pass:** `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`, `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`.

Delivery: follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas is outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies. There are no product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change is needed. Public publication follows the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md) and is separate from source delivery.

## Meaningful deferrals

- **B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard, Nanoleaf and Pixoo apps.** They keep Neon only. Revisit after [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) lands the dashboard token layer.
- **Markdown documents rendered by GitHub** (READMEs, docs/*.md) and the nine Archify architecture viewers. These can't be skinned from our generators and stay as they are.
- **Deck view** (a card grid in place of each guide table), a rotated "tapped" look for blocked issues, gold frames for issues with several type labels, and flavor text. Revisit if the owner wants them after seeing the first candidate.
- **Per-issue custom art** (art keyed by issue rather than label). Revisit if the owner asks for it; the mapping file can grow an issue-key column.

## Assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24. Hub `main` is at `73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d`, and #85's PR #251 head is at `92423ae4970d4fc3c94bd9c288bea939abc9907b` (open, in review).

- **Operating assumptions:** a personal project with one owner, the public guide and atlas as the only consumers, and reversible styling. The owner chose guide plus atlas and original bundled art on 2026-09-24.
- **Complexity: medium.** Two generators, one mapping, a picker with pre-paint application, live-status art updates and the art itself.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** #85's final token names and skin template haven't merged yet. Whether mini-cards read well at 390 px, and whether the art looks good, are for the owner to judge on the candidate. The label set and generator paths are known.
- **Impact: low.** Reversible, per-viewer styling on documentation pages. Neon stays the default. No device, state or credential effects.
- **Readiness: blocked** on #85 merging. The requirements are otherwise settled. At pickup, refresh the token and template names from the merged #85, and refresh the label set from the current snapshots.
- **Reviews:** independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI, per sdlc. The owner approves the atlas candidate. No specialist review is needed beyond the accessibility checks in AC4.
- **Reassess if** #85 merges with a different skin mechanism, if the owner wants the dashboard included, or if the art source changes to supplied or licensed images.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: implement directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.
**Work surface:** UI

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: Claude Code host controls were not inspected; confirm alias and effort before starting. | Provisional: collaboration tools offer gpt-6-sol and high reasoning on 2026-09-26; confirm availability in the starting-session picker. |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/254. I started this session on Sonnet at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-26) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

## Guide

outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
Add a second, just-for-fun skin to the cross-project work guide and the B.U.N.N.Y. atlas. It draws on trading card games like Magic: The Gathering. Each issue appears as a card, and each card's art comes from its issue's type label, so every `bug` shares one piece of art, every `enhancement` another, and so on, the way basic lands share art. Atlas component pages get the same card treatment, with art chosen by component category. Readers pick Neon or Cards with a skin picker, and the page remembers the choice.

This is the alternate skin and skin picker that [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) postponed "to a separate issue". Neon Geometry Wars stays the default.

Real setup: the generated guide (`docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html`) and atlas (`docs/system-design/`), read on a phone and a desktop. The guide covers Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo issues. No other hosts or services.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
**Satisfied required input: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85)** (merged PR [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251)). The card skin uses its role tokens, skin template and "how to add a skin" section, with the reduced-motion and five-second one-shot limit delivered by [#264](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/264). Read the current merged tokens and template at pickup.

- **Art mapping.** One small data file maps art keys to images and gives the precedence order. Issues are keyed by type label. The starting set covers every type label in the three repos' current snapshots, and the owner can rename or reassign any of it:

  | Label | Card "land" | Color |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `enhancement` | Forest | green |
  | `bug` | Mountain | red |
  | `documentation` | Island | blue |
  | `maintenance` | Swamp | black |
  | `accessibility` | Plains | white |
  | `hardware` | Artifact | colorless |

  Workflow labels (`status:*`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `priority:*`) never pick art. An issue with several type labels uses the first in precedence order. An issue with no mapped label gets a default card art. Atlas components are keyed by their category prefix (`API`, `CORE`, `DB`, `DEV`, `DEP`, `CH`, `ADR`, ...), and an unmapped prefix also gets the default.
- **One markup, two skins.** The generators (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`) write the art key into each issue link, brief and component panel, for example as a `data-art` attribute. The skins differ only in CSS, tokens and assets. Neon ignores the art key. Live GitHub status updates (#197) also update the art key when an issue's labels change.
- **Card anatomy.** In the Cards skin, the task brief dialog (#196) becomes a full card:
  - **Name line:** the issue title.
  - **Art box:** the label art.
  - **Type line:** type label and repository, for example "Enhancement - Hub".
  - **Set symbol:** a repository glyph. `priority:high` gets a "rare" treatment.
  - **Text box:** the existing brief content and copy buttons.

  Issue links in the guide tables become small mini-cards, using a type-colored frame and an art thumbnail or glyph. Atlas component panels use the card frame and category art. The table and page structure stays the same.
- **Art.** Original art made for this project and bundled in the repository, one piece per art key plus the default. Agent-drawn SVG is the default, and the owner can swap in raster images through the mapping later. Use no Wizards of the Coast art, card frames, mana symbols or logos, and do not use the Magic: The Gathering name in the UI. Record where each piece came from, and its license, in a short credits file beside the art. Keep all art to about 1 MB or less and make no remote requests.
- **Skin picker.** A small control in the guide and atlas headers switches between Neon and Cards. It stores the choice in `localStorage` (wrapped in try/catch) and applies it in the head script before first paint. If storage is unavailable, the page falls back to Neon.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- Status stays readable as text in both skins. Art and frame color never replace the status label, the blocked qualifier or the issue number. Text always sits on a solid panel, never directly on art.
- Fixed-meaning colors (the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repository colors and the status colors) come from #85's non-overridable token set. The card "land" colors are skin decoration only.
- Decorative motion in the Cards skin plays once and ends within five seconds of load; `prefers-reduced-motion` stops it. A skin introducing longer or repeating motion must supply an accessible motion control, as the shared style guide requires. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls. Print shows no decoration.
- The guide's issue totals, links, brief prompts, live GitHub status and existing checks behave as they do now. Change the generators and assets, not the generated output.
- The public guide carries only public issue data. Art and credits contain nothing private.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
1. **Cards render.** In the Cards skin at 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide's issue mini-cards, the brief card and the atlas component cards show the mapped art, type line, repository symbol and readable status text. Evidence: screenshots in the PR. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md#ui-approval-scope) requires. The guide needs no approval.
2. **Art is shared by label.** Two issues with the same type label use the same art. An issue with several type labels follows the precedence order. An unmapped label or category falls back to the default art. When a live status update changes an issue's labels, the art changes with them. Evidence: a guide check that every type label in the current snapshots, and every atlas category prefix, maps to art or explicitly to the default. The check must also cover a fixture issue with several labels and one with an unknown label.
3. **Picker works.** Switching skins changes the whole page without a reload and saves the choice. A seeded preference applies before first paint, and when storage is unavailable the page renders Neon. Evidence: browser check assertions. Seed the stored choice with `addInitScript`; do not assert storage across `page.reload()` (see the #85 CI lesson).
4. **Protections hold.** Status stays identifiable without color or art. Decorative motion runs once and ends within five seconds of load; with reduced motion enabled, nothing moves. Text contrast is checked on the card text panels. Nothing in the Cards skin adds a remote request. The color-literal check from #85 covers the new skin's files. Evidence: extended `check_guide.cjs` and `docs/system-design/check.cjs` assertions.
5. **Docs and credits.** The guide README's skin section lists the Cards skin, the mapping file and how to add or reassign art. The credits file lists each art piece's source and license.
6. **Existing checks pass:** `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`, `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`.

Delivery: follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas is outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies. There are no product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change is needed. Public publication follows the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md) and is separate from source delivery.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- **B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard, Nanoleaf and Pixoo apps.** They keep Neon only. Revisit after [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) lands the dashboard token layer.
- **Markdown documents rendered by GitHub** (READMEs, docs/*.md) and the nine Archify architecture viewers. These can't be skinned from our generators and stay as they are.
- **Deck view** (a card grid in place of each guide table), a rotated "tapped" look for blocked issues, gold frames for issues with several type labels, and flavor text. Revisit if the owner wants them after seeing the first candidate.
- **Per-issue custom art** (art keyed by issue rather than label). Revisit if the owner asks for it; the mapping file can grow an issue-key column.

issues.title: Prevent dashboard component aliases from colliding with built-in navigation
issues.body:
## Outcome

Give built-in dashboard pages and registered components distinct navigation identities. A component alias of `activity` or `connections` must open only that component while the Activity and Connections pages remain independently accessible.

## Problem and source evidence

[Dashboard PR #127](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/127) deferred **P3 F-STD-2** to hub frontend maintenance. The current [dashboard source at `28f7599`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L228-L258) still stores a built-in page name or component ID in the same `view` string. The navigation buttons, `aria-current` checks and visible sections compare against that shared string. An alias matching a built-in key selects both targets. Ordinary aliases are unaffected. The original review classified this as a nonblocking navigation defect, with no permission bypass or automatic device writes.

Reproduce with synthetic components whose IDs are `activity` and `connections`, alongside an ordinary component. Select each component and its similarly named built-in page. The selected navigation item and visible view must identify only the chosen target.

## Scope

Own this in `apps/dashboard`. Use a discriminated navigation value, or an equivalently unambiguous representation, that separates built-in page identity from component identity. Preserve registered aliases, display labels, API paths, credentials, capability gates, drafts and the existing component view. Coordinate with any active dashboard owner, including the separate styling work in [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Model navigation so every supported component alias remains distinct from built-in pages, including exactly `activity` and `connections`. Do not fix the collision by banning or renaming otherwise valid aliases.
- [ ] Each click or keyboard activation selects one navigation item with the correct `aria-current` and displays only its intended page or component. Both built-in pages remain reachable when both conflicting aliases exist together.
- [ ] Retain ordinary component navigation, read-only/unknown component views, drafts, focus and selection across normal snapshot refresh/reconnect. Component IDs sent to the owning APIs remain unchanged.
- [ ] Add a failing regression case before the fix, then cover both conflicting aliases, an ordinary alias and transitions to/from the built-in pages with synthetic browser fixtures. Assert selected navigation, visible sections and inspection without command requests.
- [ ] Run the dashboard and shared checks required by the current [development guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/development.md#dashboard-checks). Deliver through the [repository SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), including independent reviews, applicable current-head CI, required approval of the actual UI candidate and merged-main readback. Record the OpenSpec disposition for this bounded repair.

## Readiness and delivery boundary

Ready for a bounded source repair. The completed [dashboard issue #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6) and PR #127 are the delivered baseline, not unfinished prerequisites. There is no dependency on completing the style guide or a device integration.

This tracker publication does not implement the fix. Use fake components and isolated test state; installation, live device operations, new controls, source migration and public guide publication are outside this issue.

issues.title: Consolidate duplicated Pixoo and Nanoleaf integration-contract definitions
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Reduce the places that must change when an existing Pixoo or Nanoleaf integration contract changes, while retaining both native protocols. The affected consumers are the single-operator hub's controller client, MCP tool definitions and dashboard. No new controller or wire version is requested.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, protocol facts recur in [MCP schemas](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/mcp.ts#L69-L83), hub validators, and [dashboard types/builders](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L8-L25). [The pinned Nanoleaf contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/vendor/nanoleaf-integration.ts#L1-L13) already exports reusable types. Duplication is established; a current compatibility failure has not been demonstrated.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with a short contract/caller map in this issue: list duplicated declarations, their authoritative owner, intentional transport projections and actual imports. Identify the declarations that can be removed and the checks that show callers still accept/reject the same inputs. Use that map to settle the smallest browser-safe local module arrangement before implementation.

Then reuse owner-supplied types and consolidate shared facts per extension for the hub validators, MCP schema projections and dashboard request builders. Keep protocol-specific projections explicit and preserve validation at each trust boundary. Use existing packaging and build facilities; do not add a plugin system, schema framework, new distributable package or cross-repository migration merely for this refactor. Preserve the reviewed vendor bytes and provenance rather than editing an upstream-owned copy in place.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. Coordinate overlapping dashboard command work and any owner-contract revision at pickup. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/25 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26 own deferred source migrations and do not block local reuse. Prefer https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244, then https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245, then this work to reduce overlapping edits; that order is not a dependency.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (three consumers and two protocols); uncertainty **medium** (the reusable declarations and browser/package boundary need the map above); impact **high** because validation or guard drift can change admitted device commands. **Backlog.** Next action: complete the bounded map and update this assessment to ready when it shows a concrete reduction without changing accepted contracts. If a candidate declaration must differ by boundary, retain it and explain why. Reassess on upstream pin, wire or packaging changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Retain native API versions, different string/object request tickets, revision/generation meanings, configured target binding, strict unknown-field rejection, limits, mode semantics and configuration-versus-physical outcomes. Preserve HTTP/MCP authorization and ambiguous-write handling. Browser imports must not pull in Node transport, credential access or private configuration. Pixoo and Nanoleaf keep source and device-writer ownership.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**; readiness mapping comes before implementation. If the map finds no worthwhile consolidation that preserves the native boundaries, record the evidence and recommend closing without implementation. Do not force an abstraction to satisfy this issue. The implementation criteria below apply only when the map establishes a useful change.

- [ ] The map names each shared declaration's owner, callers, removed duplicate and any intentional projection. Review shows fewer independently maintained protocol facts, with no new wire acceptance or capability claim.
- [ ] The selected local definitions serve the current hub, MCP and dashboard callers. Type/build checks cover browser compatibility and installed hub packaging; source inspection confirms no dependency on device-application internals or Node-only code in the browser.
- [ ] Preserve vendor checksums and native fixture coverage. Feed relevant valid and invalid native requests through the MCP projection and owning validator, accounting for documented projections. Cover tickets, bounds, unknown/private fields, target binding and differing native receipt semantics; keep semantic validation that a schema cannot express.
- [ ] Preserve dashboard request guards and HTTP/MCP outcomes. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:mcp`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus shared contract/MCP/workflow checks required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Use the documented pinned owning-service checks for affected native boundaries. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] At pickup, record the issue-linked OpenSpec treatment for this intended behavior-preserving refactor. Any necessary wire or capability change requires reassessment before implementation. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI, conditional UI approval and merged-revision readback; review explicitly covers protocol compatibility and package contents.

## Meaningful deferrals

Source migrations remain in #25/#26; consumers continue using pinned owner contracts. A universal controller protocol and broad code generation have no demonstrated benefit here and are excluded; revisit only with a concrete new consumer requirement. No measured speed or memory improvement is claimed. Installation and device trials require a separate request.

## Execution recommendation

issues.body:
## Outcome

Add optional artwork to the shared playback service from [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), beginning with the Sony HT-A9 source. Acquire it once through the owning source/service so the BUNNY UI and display integrations can reuse it. Keep text-only now-playing and controls usable when artwork is missing.

Owner request, September 24, 2026: track artwork as a separate backlog story. This extracts the acquisition work previously described inside [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) and [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38); it is not a new requirement for the initial playback delivery.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] **AC1.** Define an optional source-scoped artwork reference/result in the shared contract. Sony-specific retrieval remains in the Sony module; shared consumers receive no private receiver URL. Keep the interface usable by future adapters and make unsupported/missing artwork explicit.
- [ ] **AC2.** Fetch only from the configured receiver under a documented size/time bound; validate the returned image bytes. The qualification observed JPEG bytes with `text/plain` and transient missing artwork, so do not require a correct MIME header or block metadata on artwork arrival.
- [ ] **AC3.** Keep only the current artwork or a small bounded cache. Do not attach delayed artwork from an earlier observation/source to the current track. Cover missing, delayed, invalid and oversized data and source/track changes with fake responses; no persistent artwork library is needed.
- [ ] **AC4.** Expose artwork through the existing authenticated playback boundary for UI/display consumers. [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) owns UI presentation and [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) owns Pixoo/Tidbyt sizing and rendering; neither duplicates acquisition. Refine the exact reference/serving format when selected.
- [ ] **AC5.** Run the owning hub/shared validation. Any real receiver trial needs separate target authorization; UI and physical-display acceptance remain with the consumer issues. One source read is not evidence of a rendered display result.

- [ ] **AC6.** Before closing this acquisition story, identify open work for visible artwork in the UI and on Pixoo/Tidbyt. Use [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) and [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) while they remain open; if their text-only deliveries have closed, create and link small rendering follow-ups. Those stories must explicitly cover current-track rendering, track/source changes, missing-artwork fallback and the appropriate browser/display acceptance. issues.title: Qualify Apple Music catalog search and chosen-item playback requests
issues.body:
## Outcome

Decide how BUNNY can find Apple Music content and request a specific song, album or playlist for playback through an agent tool or authenticated API. Qualify the actual player and output path before promising "play this" on the owner's iPhone or Windows PC. Return a recommended capability boundary and implementation issues; this investigation does not build or install a music connector.

## Delivery preference (September 24, 2026)

Prefer Linux/Docker-compatible paths and preserve the existing iPhone-to-HT-A9 output where possible. Basic now-playing and transport will come from the separate shared playback and Sony modules in [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175); those APIs do not select a catalog item. Windows-specific delivery [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is deferred. Music Assistant and MusicKit/browser alternatives remain research candidates, not adopted players or new prerequisites. Distinguish a server-owned queue/output from controlling the existing iPhone session.

## Questions to resolve

1. **Find music.** Compare Apple Music catalog search, charts and related content with personal-library search and recommendations. Record result IDs, storefront and availability, pagination, developer-token requirements, user authorization, subscription requirements where applicable, and any account or program cost. Separate public catalog results from personal data. Use Apple's current documentation and a bounded real query only when authorized credentials are available.
2. **Request a chosen item.** Compare (a) opening an Apple Music result for a user tap, (b) a Windows playback path, (c) MusicKit on the Web, (d) an iPhone MusicKit companion using `SystemMusicPlayer`, and (e) [Music Assistant’s Apple Music source](https://www.music-assistant.io/music-providers/apple-music/) with its [MCP plugin](https://www.music-assistant.io/plugins/fastmcp-server/) or [API](https://www.music-assistant.io/api/) and a server-owned player. For each, determine whether a selected catalog item can be queued and started, where audio originates, whether the owner's preferred iPhone-to-HT-A9 AirPlay route survives, and what happens when the app is backgrounded or absent. Check whether a request can reach the iPhone reliably; continuing audio after backgrounding alone does not prove remote command delivery. For Music Assistant, check its Apple Music playback support notice, authentication and token renewal, [Docker/player networking](https://www.music-assistant.io/installation/), HT-A9 compatibility, and how its server-owned queue differs from the current iPhone session. Record documented, live-tested, unsupported and unknown separately.
3. **Choose the command boundary.** Compare hub-owned MCP tools, a scoped authenticated HTTP API, Music Assistant’s own MCP/API, and provider hooks as entry points. In the accepted hub architecture, hooks are bounded observational emitters; deliberate music requests belong to an owning service reached through MCP or API. Define candidate `search_music`, `recommend_music` and `request_playback` inputs/outputs, read versus control scope, explicit target/source selection, request identity and sent/failed/uncertain outcomes. A dispatched request is not proof that the selected track played. Do not silently switch from the chosen output or retry an ambiguous play request.
4. **Recommend delivery.** Select the smallest supported search/discovery and playback-request paths, or recommend a link-and-tap handoff if direct playback is not qualified. State the needed implementation issues, fake-service tests, account setup and installed/physical acceptance gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A source-backed capability matrix distinguishes catalog search, personal-library search, recommendations, result links, queue/start, transport controls and now-playing observation. It records exact authentication and cost prerequisites, support status, output target, network requirements and confidence level for each candidate, including Music Assistant.
- [ ] **AC2.** A concrete "find this album and play it on my iPhone through the HT-A9" trace identifies the catalog item, chosen player, authorization, request delivery, playback receipt and observation that would confirm the intended item and output. A Windows-target trace is optional while Windows integration is deferred; the chosen Linux-compatible approach must state where audio originates and how it reaches the selected output.
- [ ] **AC3.** Hub MCP, Music Assistant MCP/API, authenticated HTTP and hooks are compared against the hub's current ownership and permission rules. The proposed tool/API contract distinguishes read from control, bounds result data, uses an explicit target and request ID, and reports unsupported/unavailable/uncertain without claiming playback success.
- [ ] **AC4.** Perform a bounded real catalog search and chosen-item playback trial on the intended target if the selected path's account, credentials, build/install path and separate device authorization are available. Record the tested app, output, account conditions and observed result without committing tokens, addresses or listening history. If a gate is unavailable, name it and leave that behavior unqualified; documentation or a fake does not establish a live playback result.
- [ ] **AC5.** Record a recommendation and file only the implementation issues justified by the result, with dependencies and fake-source tests. If direct selected-item playback remains unqualified, specify the manual handoff and the next live trial needed before implementation.

## Relationship to existing work

- [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) qualified now-playing and basic transport through the HT-A9 and Sonos Move; it did not select a catalog item.
- [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) delivers separate shared observation/transport and Sony source modules together. [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is deferred optional Windows integration. None is a prerequisite for this investigation; a later integrated command path should reuse the shared service. These basic transport adapters do not supply search, library or queue selection.
- [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) plans now-playing and basic UI/Codex controls. [#152](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/152) forwards saved device-playlist controls. This issue does not expand either into Apple Music catalog access.
- Part of the future music work in [#35](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/35). Source delivery, Apple account connection, companion installation, real-client qualification and speaker acceptance remain separate.

## Assessment and authority

**Complexity: medium.** Several distinct catalog and playback paths must be compared. **Uncertainty: high.** Apple documents catalog access and MusicKit playback, but remote request delivery to the owner's iPhone and preservation of its AirPlay output need a real trial. **Impact: low for document-only work; medium for an authorized playback trial.** The trial could replace the current queue or change the audible song. **Readiness:** documentation and interface investigation can start now. Live API and device checks are conditional on named credentials, installation authority and an explicit target/sequence; do not infer those permissions from this issue.

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This issue authorizes investigation and qualification planning, not account setup, installing an app, changing personal settings or sending music commands. Keep credentials, device addresses, private track data and listening history out of Git.

issues.body:
## Outcome
Provide an evidenced agent-event timeline independently of the best-effort current-status display. This is a deferred feature capability, not a v1 delivery requirement or a ready implementation story.

## Refinement required before implementation
- [ ] Define what reliability guarantees for the chosen provider: capture completeness, event identity, ordering, delivery gaps and supported client paths. Record unsupported guarantees rather than promising exactly-once or total order without evidence.
- [ ] Decide retention duration, storage limits, pruning/deletion behavior and the minimum history inspection interface.
- [ ] Define restart, replay and deduplication semantics, including incomplete or conflicting observations. Historical replay must not resend old effects to devices.
- [ ] Produce the issue-linked design and testable implementation scope, with an updated assessment. Resolve these decisions before treating this item as implementation-ready.

- [ ] Capture allowlisted lifecycle metadata durably with stable identity and explicit ordering provenance for qualified sources. Titles, project names, prompts and responses may be captured (#424, #425). Credentials and tokens stay out.

- [ ] Keep observed events separate from current-status calculations and manual task resets. A status reset does not erase history, and historical reconstruction does not control devices.
- [ ] Implement the agreed retention, restart and replay rules with bounded storage and documented recovery. Test duplicate delivery, gaps, reordering, interrupted writes, retention and privacy using isolated fixtures.
- [ ] Preserve compatibility with live best-effort monitoring. Existing v1 observations retain their original evidence limits; no retroactive reliability claim.

issues.title: Re-evaluate Linux performance budgets and reduce hub memory use
issues.body:
## Outcome
Re-evaluate the Linux/WSL performance budgets and reduce standalone hub memory use with reproducible measurements.

## Context and owner decision
During [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), the synthetic host workload completed 9,000 ingest/read pairs but reached 164.82 MiB peak RSS against the original 128 MiB service constraint. Four further diagnostic variants also exceeded that constraint. The receipts are retained in [PR #121](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/121), under `apps/hub/evidence/`.

The owner explicitly requested doubling the service RSS limit to **256 MiB** and creating this backlog item. This is a deliberate budget revision, not evidence that memory use improved. Preserve the original receipts and their failed results against 128 MiB. This follow-up is not a prerequisite for #5; that issue still requires its remaining functional acceptance and validation against the revised budget. Hook latency/CPU/child-RSS limits, queue/body limits and deadlines are unchanged by this decision.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Audit the scope and rationale of the existing budgets: service RSS versus JavaScript heap and native allocations, full-hook latency/CPU versus API timings, startup versus steady state, and isolated versus combined service memory.
- [ ] Define representative Linux/WSL workloads, including 1/10/50 sessions, longer-running steady state, bounded journal growth, SSE clients, replay retention and controller outages. Record versions, load, sampling and measurement boundaries.
- [ ] Profile allocations and retention to identify the causes of the observed memory use. Distinguish startup/JIT overhead, transient allocation, native SQLite/network allocations and leaks using evidence.
- [ ] Implement measured memory improvements without weakening durability, ownership, privacy, fail-open deadlines, retention or failure isolation. Retain before/after receipts and every failed trial.
- [ ] Propose justified service and end-to-end budgets with explicit headroom and regression checks. Retain 256 MiB until a separately reviewed change replaces it; do not silently rewrite historical results.
- [ ] Align the budget artifact, documentation and qualification checks with [integrated performance #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30). Distinguish partial API measurements from full integrated qualification.

## Scope and verification
Linux in WSL is primary. Native Windows qualification, installation, live state migration and physical-device testing are outside this source follow-up. Use disposable state and fake controllers. Require independent review and applicable CI for future implementation.

Related: [Pixoo performance hardening #61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61). Coordinate shared measurement boundaries without absorbing that separately owned work.

## Planning
Backlog only; this issue does not start its implementation. Before implementation, prepare an issue-linked OpenSpec change if required by `docs/sdlc.md`.

- **Impact: low.** Measurement and reduction on disposable state; no device effect.

issues.title: Add Music desk presets after playback and participation qualification
issues.body:
## Dependency clarification — October 1, 2026

The owner deferred #68 pending a later requirements reevaluation. Music presets do not require that control binding. Use #67 as the preset-service prerequisite; any binding or cycle integration remains optional future work under #68. This removes the blocking relationship without selecting a replacement control or reevaluating #68 now. This Music story remains deferred with its playback, participation-policy and selected presentation requirements intact.

## Outcome

Add Music as a later desk-preset option after the Work/Free/Quiet preset service and selected playback/presentation integrations are delivered. Reuse the preset service. A profile binding or cycle is an optional follow-up under deferred #68, not a requirement for this story.

## Further investigation and acceptance

- [ ] **AC1.** Use #40 as the owner of music participation, agent-alert interruption and restoration policy. Do not duplicate or reverse that dependency.
- [ ] **AC2.** Start with the selected Sony HT-A9 AirPlay source; refine per-device presentation mappings and entry/exit behavior closer to implementation. Cycle order is relevant only if a later binding/cycle integration is selected under #68. Playback controls remain separately selectable.
- [ ] **AC3.** Add the exact selected presentation dependencies before readiness: #38 for Pixoo/Tidbyt now-playing displays and/or #39 for qualified song-change/Nanoleaf scene behavior. Require only the branches actually selected.
- [ ] **AC4.** Keep audio-reactive effects behind #41 and their selected implementation/physical evidence. Track metadata or decorative motion is not measured audio.
- [ ] **AC5.** Retain native device modes, manual ownership, interruption priorities and restoration through existing controller services. Missing optional music devices must not break supported targets or the original three presets.
- [ ] **AC6.** Verify source behavior with fake playback/controllers, then separately authorize installation, real playback and visible-device acceptance. Do not claim Music readiness merely because a qualification ticket closed with an unsupported result.

This ticket consumes the shared playback and Sony modules from [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), and the selected playback/presentation/policy work in #37-#41. It does not own source adapters, playback controls, renderers or audio qualification. Deferred Windows integration [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is not a prerequisite. It remains deferred and does not block earlier mouse or desk-preset delivery.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 7, 2026. Source baseline: [hub main a7b1aa0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60), live prerequisite issues, and the user-confirmed decisions below. - **Uncertainty: high.** Music source/presentation branches and physical compatibility remain future qualifications.
- **Impact: medium.** Faults can interrupt playback or desk presentation; native ownership and restoration provide recovery.

**Evidence limits and unknowns:** Selected presentation branches, entry/exit behavior and qualified audio-reactive support. Resolve these later with #40 and the selected integration owners before readiness. A Music position in a cycle is only a future question if that optional #68 integration is selected.

**Readiness:** Blocked by preset-service delivery and #40 policy, with applicable playback qualification and selected presentation dependencies required before readiness. The deferred #68 binding is not a prerequisite. This issue remains deferred; no requirements investigation is selected now.

All checks below are planned and unexecuted. Proposed paths and commands are not delivery receipts.

| Criterion | Planned verification and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Review #40 policy links and dependency direction; assert the Music consumer does not become a prerequisite of its policy owner. |

## Accepted decisions

Owner revision, September 22, 2026: keyboard A/B and the attached Dual Super Buttons are managed directly on the keyboard, outside B.U.N.N.Y. This supersedes the earlier requirement for editable A/B bindings in #65 version 1 and their inclusion in #70. It changes scope, not delivery status.

issues.title: Verify desk preset switching, manual handoff and restoration
issues.body:
## Deferred verification follow-up — October 1, 2026

The owner deferred #68 and its requirements reevaluation. Keep the binding-specific verification in this issue deferred with that work. It is not a gate for Hub mode selection, device or companion modes, Music presets, or their source delivery.

The native blocking link from #68 is retired. The preset service in #67 remains a real source prerequisite. Before selecting this physical verification, reevaluate its request surface and binding-specific checks with the owner. The outcome and checklist below retain the earlier binding plan for that future discussion. In particular, the rapid-press and historical-press checks remain deferred; they are neither removed nor passed. No requirements reevaluation, installation or physical sequence is authorized now.

## Outcome

Verify the delivered configured preset-binding path across an explicitly identified set of supported devices after source delivery and separately authorized installation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Record participating devices, configured target identities/endpoints, supported operations, baseline presentation and installed versions. Authorize the exact sequence before physical changes.
- [ ] **AC2.** Verify Work, Free and Quiet visibly on each selected target, including status from authorized real agent sessions when testing the full lifecycle.
- [ ] **AC3.** Make a manual change in a vendor app. Confirm it remains until the next explicit configured preset request, then verify supported handoff and restoration.
- [ ] **AC4.** Verify one offline/slow device, mixed native modes, unknown/unsupported capabilities, rapid presses of the selected preset binding, concurrent frontend control, sleep/reconnect and restart. The display must show actual partial/uncertain outcomes.
- [ ] **AC5.** Confirm reconnect does not replay historical presses and source/transport success is not presented as optical confirmation.
- [ ] **AC6.** Confirm unrelated mouse input, normal typing, keyboard-owned A/B mappings and cooling controls remain untouched; no Wispr trial is required. Restore baseline presentation and record the result.
- [ ] **AC7.** Publish separate source, installation, real-client, transport and per-device visible/restoration evidence. Mark missing targets as unverified.

The source prerequisite on #8 supplies the shared producer setup for full installed agent-status acceptance. Additional device qualification/install gates remain conditional on the selected target set. Future PC/keyboard lighting participates only after its own capability and physical-acceptance work; it does not block the existing supported devices. Missing permissions or hardware are future acceptance gaps, not authority granted by this ticket.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 7, 2026. Source baseline: [hub main a7b1aa0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60), live prerequisite issues, and the user-confirmed decisions below. Uses the canonical [work-assessment contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/blob/22588b494cac646bd6eaa5e2f01b8d439ab6a60e/skills/deliver-work/references/work-assessment.md).

- **Complexity: high.** Several installed controllers and agent lifecycle sources must be observed through failures and manual changes.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The runbook can be bounded after source delivery, but actual target capabilities and physical outcomes remain unverified.
- **Impact: medium.** The sequence changes personal device presentation; each target needs a known restoration path.

**Evidence limits and unknowns:** Selected installed devices, current app/firmware versions, user-authorized sequence and per-target visible results.

**Readiness:** Deferred pending an owner-selected verification scope; source prerequisites are the preset service and shared producer setup. Binding-specific verification remains deferred with #68. Physical execution still needs selected devices, their applicable qualification/install gates, a named operator and explicit authorization.

### Planned acceptance evidence

All checks below are planned and unexecuted. Proposed paths and commands are not delivery receipts.

| Criterion | Planned verification and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Preflight the named operator, configured target inventory, qualified modes and baseline/rollback record before any authorized physical writes. |
| AC2 | User-observed Work/Free/Quiet sequence with authorized real agent activity verifies each target; keep optical outcomes distinct from producer and transport receipts. |
| AC3 | Change a scene/mode in the native app, wait to confirm it persists, then explicitly request the next preset and observe qualified handoff/restoration. |
| AC4 | Execute the approved failure/lifecycle matrix and compare visible behavior with per-device feedback. Record partial outcomes rather than treating the desk as atomic. |
| AC5 | Reconnect after an interrupted request and inspect fresh state; confirm no missed press is replayed and no sent receipt is labeled optical proof. |
| AC6 | Observe ordinary input and unaffected cooling controls, then restore the baseline. Do not record typed or dictated content. |
| AC7 | Audit the final matrix for separately named source, install, client, transport, visible and restoration evidence; retain missing-device gaps. |

**Review:** Qualified user/device owners confirm optical and restoration results; concurrency expertise reviews failure interpretation where the runbook cannot distinguish races. Preserve required independent source reviews.

**Operational handoff:** Deliver a per-device acceptance matrix, current limitations and recovery instructions to the installed hub owner. Unsupported/unverified targets remain excluded from support claims.

**Reassessment triggers:** Refresh on changed scope or source baseline, qualification results that alter the approach, changed dependencies, repeated failures without progress, or blocking review findings. Preserve existing review/acceptance requirements when reassessing.

issues.title: Implement Work, Free and Quiet desk preset coordination
issues.body:
## Outcome

Apply Work, Free or Quiet to explicitly configured Nanoleaf and Pixoo participants through the existing hub and owning controller services. Keep this personal-project feature small: fixed mode mappings, one active preset request, no saved restoration baseline and no background enforcement.

Owner-approved scope reduction, September 24, 2026. This replaces the earlier broad coordination investigation and rapid-replacement requirements. It changes the planned behavior, not delivery status.

## Fixed preset behavior

| Desk preset | Nanoleaf | Pixoo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work | Request native Work mode. | Request native Monitor mode. |
| Free | Request native Free mode. | Request native Media mode. |
| Quiet | Request native Quiet mode. | Request native Monitor mode; issue no additional brightness or animation commands. |

Use each controller's supported native API and exact wire values. The table names device behavior, not a new common controller mode enum. Native mode policies own brightness, presentation and any scene/media handoff. Quiet does not promise a subdued Pixoo presentation in this release.

Free delegates to native Free/Media behavior. The hub does not capture pre-Work settings, choose a saved scene or playlist, or guarantee restoration of arbitrary previous content. Manual device-app changes persist until the next explicit preset request and its supported ownership handoff; the service cannot bypass an external owner.

## Implementation boundary

- Add one small module inside the existing hub process. Expose the same operation through `POST /api/hub/v1/desk-preset` with `{preset: "Work" | "Free" | "Quiet"}` and an MCP `desk_preset_set` tool. Follow the host's existing authentication, request-validation and authorization conventions.
- Configure participation as an explicit list of existing registered device aliases in hub configuration. No discovery, new device destinations, participation editor or custom preset editor. Reject invalid participant configuration; do not invent failed rows for unknown devices.
- Require control authority for every configured participant before sending any device command. A caller lacking that authority receives a rejection with no device writes. Empty participation produces an explicit unavailable result, not successful application.
- Read each participant's current snapshot and capabilities, then submit its one native mode command with the owning API's request identity, revision and generation guards. Resolve exact API compatibility in the issue-linked specification before coding. Use existing controller clients and queues; introduce no physical writer or shared controller-database access.
- Process devices independently with bounded snapshot/command waits. Unsupported capabilities, an unavailable controller or a failed device request produce a per-device result without preventing supported participants from running. A capability declaration alone does not establish preset compatibility.
- Admit one preset invocation at a time across HTTP and MCP. Keep a process-local busy flag until that invocation's bounded per-device calls have settled; release it on all exit paths. Reject overlapping invocations as busy without queuing, cancelling or replacing them. Existing controller queues still own commands already admitted downstream. Do not promise atomic desk changes or last-request-wins behavior.
- Return per-device receipts or typed failures using their existing queued, sent, failed, partially-applied, uncertain and cancelled meanings. Do not collapse them to `ok/error`, claim all devices reached the requested state, or treat a timeout as proof that no command took effect. No new result taxonomy or operation-history service is needed.
- Retain no durable selected preset, restoration baseline or request history. No automatic retries, rollback, startup commands, reconnect replay, polling to enforce a preset or restart recovery of pending writes. New explicit requests read fresh state and respect controller conflicts or uncertainty holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Bounded specification.** Create issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts for the fixed matrix, participant configuration, native API mapping, shared HTTP/MCP operation, busy behavior and result contract. Record native Free/Media limitations. Update affected architecture/development documentation within implementation scope; the broad investigation backlog is superseded by these bounded decisions.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shared implementation.** HTTP and MCP call the same hub operation, use configured participants and existing authentication/guards/queues, and preserve independent device failures. No dashboard UI or additional device family is required.
- [ ] **AC3 — Focused fake-controller validation.** Cover the three mappings; both entry points; invalid input, empty participation and unauthorized requests with zero writes; unsupported and slow/offline participants; overlap returning busy and releasing the flag after failure; stale/manual-change conflicts without automatic overwrite; preservation of queued/partial/uncertain receipts; and restart/reconnect producing no commands. Exercise the new composition without duplicating the full downstream controller test suites.
- [ ] **AC4 — Delivery evidence.** Pass applicable repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, current-head hosted CI and merged-revision checks. Reviews cover the small module's authentication, ownership and concurrency behavior. Report source and transport outcomes separately from installation and physical observations.

All verification above is planned, not executed. Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md) and [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md).

## Scope and follow-up boundaries

- No dashboard controls in this issue. HTTP/MCP provide explicit preset selection. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695 owns the later Hub selector, individual overrides and visible per-device results. Physical binding remains deferred in [#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68).
- This issue retains no durable selected preset. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695 owns the later saved Hub selection and revisions. #68 is deferred pending an owner-requested requirements reevaluation; this work does not reopen that discussion and #68 blocks no delivery. Do not infer a desk-wide current preset from Nanoleaf or add an independent client counter.
- Installation, binding verification, manual handoff and visible restoration remain in [#69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/69). Do not fold or close that issue based on source tests or a three-mode smoke test. Device work requires its existing explicit target and operation authorization.
- Tidbyt, LIFX and PC lighting participation remain future work requiring their own supported hub integration and defined preset mapping. Existing controller availability does not automatically enroll a device family.
- Desktop-input decisions, including the exclusion of keyboard A/B and attached Super Buttons from preset bindings, remain in [desktop-controls.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-controls.md). This feature does not block independent Codex mouse delivery.
- Source delivery does not install software, alter personal configuration, launch agent sessions or contact physical devices. Keep credentials and private runtime state outside Git.

## Shared Hub mode follow-on — 2026-10-01

https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/695 is the selected-mode and individual-override owner. It consumes this issue's dispatcher and later routes Hub-wide preset entry points through that state owner. This issue still delivers the fixed, explicit per-request behavior without persistence; it has no dependency on the follow-on. #635 consumes the new owner for companion choices and retains behavior/permission policy. This supersedes only the selected-mode ownership described in the September 30 companion reconciliation comment. The fixed mappings, per-device failures, one-writer boundary, no-replay rules and deferred label remain unchanged.

All six recorded source prerequisites were verified closed on September 24, 2026:

- [Hub #63](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/63)
