The earlier dependency-blocked wording is superseded. Labels and native dependency relationships are unchanged by this tracker-only revision. The bounded specification and exact native API verification precede implementation; this update claims no source, installation or physical completion.

Reassessment: complexity medium, uncertainty low-to-medium, impact medium. Fixed one-command mappings and no persistent coordination reduce the work substantially; authorization, snapshot-to-command conflicts and partial results still require focused validation. Hub owns implementation and API notes; existing device owners retain their writers and native behavior. Reassess if scope expands to compound actions, durable cycling, automatic recovery or additional device families.

issues.title: Add B.U.N.N.Y. conversation and device tools through the LangGraph assistant
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498.

Lightweight backlog placeholder. Refine contracts, acceptance and operational choices before implementation. The owner selected LangGraph as the planned personal-agent engine on 2026-09-26.

## Outcome and real setup

The owner can converse with B.U.N.N.Y. in a local dashboard text view, ask about status and request supported device or dashboard actions.

## Smallest useful implementation

Requires https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499 for the LangGraph runtime. Reuse current Hub MCP/API discovery and scoped tools, with a small dashboard conversation/task surface. Keep device state changes in owning services and UI navigation in an explicit frontend interface. Proposed recurring rules use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45 and its follow-ups when available; that capability does not block basic status/control.

## Conversation continuity and tool discovery

Use https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/499's stable conversation/task records. The owner can return to a task after reload or restart, inspect its pending decision and continue it without accidentally starting another task. Pending decisions show their originating task and exact proposed action; dismissing a notification does not answer it.

Discover tools from the authorized service interfaces and declared capabilities, and refresh discovery when availability or permissions change. A new connector is usable only through its explicit authorized tool registration; the existence of a dashboard route does not grant assistant access. Missing or unsupported tools stay visible as unavailable, and server-side authorization is checked again at execution. Native assistant status reporting is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/505, and selected knowledge tools are https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/507; neither is a blanket prerequisite for the first status/control slice.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep the model provider replaceable, local controls available during model outage, and one state owner/device writer. Preserve manual modes, stale/unknown observations, command identity and partial/uncertain receipts. Reads do not acknowledge notices. A proposed recurring rule needs owner acceptance.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Synthetic tools demonstrate a status explanation and a permitted action against the correct configured target.
- [ ] Tests reject unsupported/unauthorized actions, preserve uncertainty after lost responses and avoid duplicate writes.
- [ ] Browser checks and current-candidate UI approval cover conversation, pending questions and clear outcomes.

- [ ] Browser reload and runtime restart reopen the same conversation/task and pending decision; answering correlates to the original action without a duplicate start.
- [ ] Adding/removing a fake capability or revoking permission updates available actions; a stale discovered tool cannot bypass current authorization.

Delivery target: source-only unless a later request explicitly names installation or live qualification. These checks are planned, not executed. Current SDLC, UI approval and physical-device authorization still apply.

## Meaningful deferrals

Voice, memory, coding and computer control are siblings under https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498. Phone/ambient access stays in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47 / https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/48. Until the automation service is ready, rule proposals remain drafts.

## Assessment

Planning refinement, 2026-09-26: expanded acceptance and integration boundaries at the owner's request. Remains backlog, not implementation-ready; select the bounded first case and settle the listed choices before delivery.

Complexity high (conversation, UI and tool effects); uncertainty high (model and first commands); impact high (device control and private conversation). Status: backlog; not implementation-ready. Reassess at pickup after the linked inputs and open choices are settled. Planning baseline: Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, 2026-09-26. issues.title: Run approved event rules and scheduled routines independently of conversation
issues.body:
> Refined on 2026-09-25 at the owner's direction. This replaces the placeholder text. It defines scope and acceptance; it does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes. Delivery is split into #358, #359 and #360 (see Child stories).

### Outcome and real setup

The hub runs owner-approved automation without an open conversation or a model call, in two forms:

1. **Event rules.** An event from a source (GitHub pull request or CI, calendar, agent lifecycle) maps to a moment, arbitrated by the hub and delivered through the contract `moment` command. #45 owns storing and editing these rules and the owner's interrupt set, and arbitrating the moments they trigger ([ADR 0006](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006-hub-moments-and-interludes.md)).
2. **Scheduled routines.** A time trigger, by time of day and day of week on the hub host's local clock, maps to typed device commands and scheduled moments through the existing hub routes: a desk preset (#67), a Pixoo playlist or single rendition (divoom-app-upgrade#13), screen power or brightness, a LIFX color, a Nanoleaf scene. Owner direction, 2026-09-25: "schedule routines throughout the day or week through B.U.N.N.Y.; they do not run while a device shows status, but do run in a content mode."

The owner inspects, enables, disables and revises both from a B.U.N.N.Y. Automation page and through MCP tools. The assistant may propose a rule or routine; it is created disabled and the owner accepts it before it runs (ADR 0004).

Setup is the installed hub with its registered controllers and the operator's browser. No new hosts or services. The hub already runs unattended, so no separate scheduler process is needed.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

**One rules store, two rule kinds.**

- A rule has a stable ID, a name, `enabled`, a trigger and an action. Stored in the hub's private SQLite alongside its existing state, edited only through hub routes and MCP tools. The interrupt set is the set of event kinds whose rules may set `coversStatus:true`; its default is a merged PR, a failed CI run and a meeting reminder, editable without a code change.
- **Event rule:** trigger is an event kind from a source (#293, #298, agent lifecycle). Action is a moment: mood, priority class, duration, optional palette, target devices. Arbitration and delivery follow ADR 0006 and the 1.1 contract (#292, closed).
- **Routine:** trigger is a weekly schedule. Actions are ordered existing typed operations or scheduled moments. Commands use `POST /api/hub/v1/desk-preset` (#67), `POST /api/controllers/v1/:id/commands`, `.../integration/commands` or `.../lighting/commands`; moments use #358 arbitration and #335's sender. Single-device actions name a registered alias; desk presets target #67's configured participant group. Obtain fresh request identities, revisions and generation guards at dispatch. No new device command kinds are introduced here.

**Local-clock routines (owner reduction, September 30, 2026).** #359 adds one timer in the existing hub and a small ordered executor. Weekly schedules contain `{days,time}` only. There is no timezone field, named-zone conversion, hard-coded Eastern zone, timezone library, custom DST behavior or zone-change test matrix. Keep valid occurrence/action IDs and minimal duplicate protection; submit an occurrence to its own routine only when due.

- **Restart and downtime:** future occurrences only. Never catch up or resume interrupted writes. Do not enumerate or collect missed occurrences, outage history or manual-command history.
- **One in flight:** at most one occurrence per routine. Overlap logs `busy` and drops; existing per-device bounds remain.
- **Scheduled moments remain included:** use #358 arbitration and #335's sender as `flourish` with `coversStatus:false`; retain existing switch, quiet-hours and budget policy without a new budget system.

**Preconditions instead of suspension.**

- Each routine action carries a mode precondition. Content actions (start a playlist, show a rendition, play a scene) default to "only while the device is in a content mode": Pixoo Media, Nanoleaf Free. Mode-changing actions (desk presets) carry no precondition. The owner can change the default per action.
- Where the device supports it, the precondition is sent with the command so the check and the admission are atomic (divoom-app-upgrade#13 adds `requireMode` for Pixoo). Where it is not, the hub reads the device snapshot immediately before sending and skips with a `skipped: mode` log entry; this is best-effort and the log says so.
- A manual command remains just a command. The next occurrence overrides it. There is no suspension, snooze or "resume schedule" state.
- A device paused on uncertainty or under external control rejects the command through its existing guards. The routine logs the typed failure and does not retry.

**Quiet hours.** Command actions run during quiet hours; moment actions use #358's existing arbitration. Leave the delivered daily quiet-hours settings intact. Sharing a new weekly compiler, timezone implementation or editor with routines is no longer required. #295 remains related agent-proposal/default-policy work.

**Execution.** A routine runs its actions in order through the existing hub routes with the existing authentication, admission and per-device bounds. Devices are independent: one device's failure or absence does not stop the others. No retries, no rollback, no restoration baseline. Per-action receipts keep their existing meanings; `sent` is transport evidence only.

**Log.** Reuse #358's bounded automation log for attempted actions and admission outcomes: occurrence/action/target, receipt or typed failure, blocked/skipped/busy. No `missed` records, historical reconstruction, manual-command audit or additional history store. Preserve event rows and correct flourish-budget accounting. Run-now returns an occurrence ID within the HTTP bound; the existing log supplies eventual results.

**Surfaces.**

- B.U.N.N.Y. Automation page: list rules and routines with enabled state, last outcome and next occurrence; create, edit, enable, disable and delete; edit the interrupt set and quiet hours; browse the log. Routine editing uses the device previews from #353 for Pixoo targets when that story is delivered, and plain IDs and names before it.
- MCP tools: list rules and routines, read the log, propose a rule or routine (created disabled), enable or disable. Proposing never enables. Tools follow the existing `read` and `control` scopes; enabling requires `control`.

**Dependencies.**

- Delivered at source level: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/335 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/358. The accepted #67 definition is not a delivered desk-preset operation; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67 still supplies that action.
- Event rules need at least one source: #293 or #298, or the existing agent lifecycle events.
- Existing Pixoo commands may use the accepted snapshot precondition until https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/13 supplies atomic admission. Its new show-rendition command also needs https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/96 and has no equivalent fallback.
- #358 delivered the bounded automation log. #359 and #296 extend that owner; no new history service is required here.
- #246 for the consolidated contract definitions.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One authoritative state owner and one writer per device. The hub routes typed intents; it never sends frames, raw protocol or device geometry, and never writes to a device directly.
- Existing request tickets, revisions, generations, receipts and admission limits. No new result taxonomy.
- No moment or routine changes a device's selected mode except an explicit desk-preset action the owner put in the routine. Content controls stay in Free or Media (ADR 0005, ADR 0006).
- A hub outage never blanks a status display; devices keep their base presentation. A model outage never stops rules or routines.
- Restarts, reconnects and historical replay (#139) never trigger a moment or a routine.
- Privacy: rules and the log hold event kinds, repository or calendar aliases, device aliases and receipts. Pull request, meeting and task titles may appear (#426). No credentials or tokens.
- The assistant proposes; the owner accepts. Nothing recurring runs without an explicit enable by the owner.
- Manual control in vendor apps keeps working with the existing ownership handoff.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] **AC1. Store and editing.** Rules and routines persist across a hub restart; create, edit, enable, disable and delete work from the page and MCP with the stated scopes; a proposal from MCP is stored disabled and is not scheduled until enabled. The interrupt set defaults to the three owner-approved kinds and is editable.
- [ ] **AC2. Event rules.** With a fake event source, an event in the interrupt set produces a moment with `coversStatus:true` to each target device via the 1.1 command; an event outside it produces a moment without cover; quiet hours, the global switch, budgets and current mode and alert state block or drop as ADR 0006 states, each with a log entry.
- [ ] **AC3. Local scheduling.** Focused controllable-clock tests cover weekday/local-minute selection, advancing to the next occurrence, and edit/disable/delete preventing stale dispatch. No timezone fields, custom DST rules, zone-change tests or exhaustive clock matrix.
- [ ] **AC4. No replay.** Restart after scheduled times have passed runs none of them and creates no missed-history rows; the next future occurrence runs once. Duplicate delivery and an inactive owner produce no new writes. No long-outage reconstruction is required.
- [ ] **AC5. Preconditions.** Against fake controllers: a content action with the Pixoo in Monitor is rejected by the device when `requireMode` is supported, and skipped by the hub with `skipped: mode` when it is not, with zero device writes either way; the same action in Media is applied; a desk-preset action applies regardless of mode.
- [ ] **AC6. Execution bounds.** Multi-device routine with one offline device: the others receive their commands, the offline one logs a typed failure, nothing retries. An occurrence arriving during a still-settling run is dropped as `busy`. Receipts keep `queued`, `sent`, `failed`, `partially-applied`, `uncertain` and `cancelled` meanings.
- [ ] **AC7. Log and page.** The Automation page shows each rule's enabled state, last outcome and next occurrence, and the log with the outcomes above; accessibility checks pass; explicit human UI approval is recorded in the PR under the SDLC UI approval scope.
- [ ] **AC8. Delivery.** Each child meets its retained issue-linked OpenSpec, applicable existing checks, independent Standards/Specification review and current-head/merged-revision CI gates. #359 uses its focused local-clock, no-replay, execution, moment-integration and persistence/run-now examples; no new endurance, timezone/device/failure matrix or duplicate sender conformance suite. #360 retains its existing UI acceptance and approval.

**Delivery target:** source-only. Installing on the owner's host and any live routine against the physical devices are separately authorized steps. Live acceptance proposal: one routine that starts a Pixoo playlist at a chosen minute while the Pixoo is in Media, then the same routine skipped while it is in Monitor, both visible in the log.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Timezone and custom clock-change behavior:** https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/674. Use the host's local clock; this follow-up does not block #45/#359/#360.

- **One-off dates, date ranges and holidays:** weekly schedules only. Manual alternative: enable or disable a routine by hand. Revisit when a real need appears.
- **Catch-up after downtime:** never. Manual alternative: run the routine now from the page. Revisit only if the owner finds devices in a stale state after outages.
- **Per-routine manual-override suspension:** not built; the next occurrence wins. Revisit if manual changes keep being overridden unexpectedly.
- **Conditions beyond mode** (presence, calendar busy, music playing): not built. #40 decides music precedence; a later story can add conditions to the same precondition slot.

### Child stories

Filed 2026-09-25, in delivery order. Each carries its own OpenSpec change and acceptance; this issue closes when all three are closed.

1. #358: delivered at source level in PR #650; installation and physical acceptance remain separate.
2. #359: local-clock weekly routines, ordered commands, scheduled moments and bounded attempted-action results. #358/#335 are delivered; unfinished action providers retain their own prerequisites. Timezone and missed-history follow-ups do not block it.
3. #360: Automation page and MCP tools; #358 is delivered, #359 remains an input. No routine zone editor or missed-history display.

Owner-approved planning reassessment, September 30, 2026. The parent remains a delivery envelope for its children, not a new combined implementation.

- **Complexity: medium per remaining child.** Reuse the delivered store/arbitration/sender; add local scheduling/execution and their UI. No timezone compiler, missed-history collector, automatic rollback or host-migration framework.
- **Uncertainty: medium across remaining integration work.** Scheduling policy is settled; exact unfinished action providers and the final #359 route shape remain their owners' work.
- **Impact: medium.** Unattended commands retain target authority, mode preconditions, bounded work, no replay/retry and truthful results.

**Readiness:** #358 is delivered; #359/#360 remain. Preserve their action/provider and UI gates. The timezone/history backlog items are optional future work, not additional required children. Reassess for changed action providers, a different host-clock need or repeated observed failures.

issues.title: Host the runtime on a Mac mini and plan the migration from the PC
issues.body:
> Rescoped on 2026-09-28 at the owner's request. The owner chose a Mac mini as the always-on host. **Nothing here blocks current work:** until the owner has the hardware, [ADR 0008](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0008-runtime-hosting.md)'s WSL hosting stays in force and development keeps targeting Linux in WSL. Publishing this authorizes no implementation, installation or device change.

### Outcome and real setup

The B.U.N.N.Y. runtime moves off the PC to an always-on Mac mini, so the PC no longer has to stay on for the lights, map, Pixoo, Tidbyt, LIFX and hub. Development stays on the Windows PC (WSL). The runtime is the same six services: the shared monitor, the Nanoleaf wall, controller and MCP, the Pixoo controller, and the Tidbyt and LIFX local controller host.

Hardware chosen by the owner on 2026-09-28: **Mac mini M6, 32 GB, 1 TB**, wired Ethernet. Not purchased yet. The Mac also runs the owner's Plex and the Apple integrations (Messages, Music), which are outside this issue.

### Smallest useful implementation

Record **hub ADR 0010**, which amends ADR 0008, and update the hosting text in `docs/architecture.md` and the READMEs that describe it. The ADR records:

1. **Host:** the Mac mini above, with a DHCP reservation and sleep off.
2. **Runtime:** one OrbStack Ubuntu (ARM64) Linux machine with systemd. It runs the existing Linux installers, user units and linger. State lives on the machine's own disk, never in a folder shared from macOS. Because the runtime stays Linux, current WSL development and Pixoo ADR 0021 remain valid.
3. **Restart:** FileVault stays on. After a power cut or macOS update, the runtime returns when the owner signs in, which starts OrbStack (owner decision, 2026-09-28). Unattended pre-login start is deferred.
4. **Network:** services stay on loopback inside the machine, and OrbStack's "Expose ports to LAN" is off. The only planned LAN-facing port is Tronbyt's, decided in #23.
5. **PC access:** PC hooks, the Windows browser and MCP clients reach the Mac-hosted runtime through an SSH tunnel from WSL (#566). A small WSL relay pushes Codex Desktop read state (#567). No LAN listener is added.
6. **Native Apple adapters:** Messages and Music run natively on macOS. The ADR settles how they connect to the hub. OrbStack machines reach macOS only at `host.orb.internal`, while macOS reaches machine services at `localhost`, and the hub today accepts only `127.0.0.1` controller endpoints.
7. **Amendments:**
   - drop ADR 0008's x86 default and its Docker packaging of the whole runtime (Docker stays only for Tronbyt);
   - ADR 0004's "Linux server" becomes "Linux host";
   - fix the stale "Windows Nanoleaf worker" text in ADRs 0001 and 0003.
8. **Rollback:** the WSL runtime ([#356](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/356)'s keep-alive) stays installed but disabled until the owner removes it after the cutover.

Then the migration follows the stories below.

### Plan (all deferred until the owner has the Mac)

| Story | What |
| --- | --- |
| #565 | Set up the Mac mini host |
| #566 | SSH tunnel from the PC |
| #567 | Codex Desktop read-state relay |
| [codex-nanoleaf#200](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/200) | Move the Nanoleaf installation (Nanoleaf ADR superseding its ADR 0011) |
| [divoom-app-upgrade#14](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/14) | Pixoo on ARM64 Linux |
| #568 | The cutover |
| #569, #570, #571, #572 | Messages, approved texts, Music and health, which follow the cutover |
| #23, #24 | Tronbyt |

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One agent-state owner and one writer per device. The WSL units are stopped and disabled before the Mac's units start.
- Controller databases stay private to their host. No SQLite file is shared across macOS, the machine or the PC.
- Credentials stay in private configuration.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- ADR 0010 and the architecture and README hosting text merge through a PR with the shared workflow checks.
- The migration stories carry their own acceptance.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Unattended start without a sign-in:** the owner accepted manual sign-in after restarts. Revisit if restarts leave the desk dark too often.
- **Docker packaging of the whole runtime (from #42):** not needed while an OrbStack Linux machine runs the existing installers. Revisit for a second host or an image-only service.
- **LAN discovery and events (mDNS, UPnP):** a machine behind OrbStack networking may not carry multicast, which is unverified. The first story that needs them qualifies it.

## Tronbyt workload (owner goal, 2026-09-25)

The owner wants the Tidbyt (a **Gen 1**) moved to a self-hosted Tronbyt server on the always-on host, not on the PC. That host is now the Mac mini: Tronbyt as a container in OrbStack, whose ARM64 image needs checking. The Tidbyt stays on the official cloud until then. [#23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23) owns the connection and [#24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/24) the transition. #24 is blocked by this issue.

Requirements this adds:

- **Always on.** With Tronbyt, the server decides every frame. A powered-off or asleep host leaves the whole Tidbyt stale, not just our tiles.
- **LAN-reachable.** The device connects in to the server over WiFi. The host needs a stable LAN address and one explicitly published port.
- **Isolation.** The server runs as its own container, with its own device and API keys.
- **Load.** Light: a Go service with a data directory, which needs backups.

Sources: [tronbyt/server](https://github.com/tronbyt/server) and [tronbyt/firmware-esp32](https://github.com/tronbyt/firmware-esp32).

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-28, from hub `origin/main` ADRs 0001-0009 and the codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade decisions. It draws on a read-only review of OS coupling across the three repositories and on the owner's answers of 2026-09-28.

- **Operating assumptions:**
  - one operator;
  - the PC stays the development machine;
  - the Mac mini is a single always-on host;
  - the hardware is not purchased yet.
- **Complexity: medium.** An ADR plus hosting text now; the migration is in the linked stories.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** These OrbStack behaviors are unverified on the owner's hardware: loopback forwarding to macOS, the machine's filesystem type, and multicast.
- **Impact: low for the ADR.** Its migration stories carry the high-impact steps.
- **Readiness:** backlog, deferred. It becomes ready when the owner has the Mac. The ADR may be written earlier, but nothing waits on it.
- **Reassess when:** the hardware arrives, the host choice changes, or OrbStack's behavior contradicts items 2-6.

- [ ] **AC2.** Define and test metadata comparison/track identity, duplicate reads, missing metadata and stale/recovered observations. Initial connection, reconnect and an explicit source switch initialize a baseline rather than firing an old effect. Start with title/artist/album comparison; same-song repeats and identical-metadata tracks may remain indistinguishable unless a qualified source supplies better identity. Refine required policy/scene dependencies before readiness; no automatic behavior is enabled by this issue update.

Separately qualify Nanoleaf Rhythm scenes where selected. Metadata-triggered lighting is decorative; measured audio response remains [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/41). issues.title: Verify the deferred Tidbyt-to-Tronbyt transition
issues.body:
## Outcome

Perform an explicitly authorized cloud-to-Tronbyt transition with one device writer and a tested recovery plan.

## Ownership and scope

Owner: `controllers/tidbyt`. Deferred; scheduling and implementation decisions remain open. This is a future deliverable created by #14. Bootstrap delivery does not implement or install it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm exact Tidbyt generation, hardware, target IP/ID and supported firmware/server versions. Obtain separate explicit authorization for firmware flashing, server installation and physical content replacement before any transition.
- [ ] Prepare a generation-specific runbook, power/network prerequisites, stock firmware recovery instructions and rollback criteria. Preserve old cloud configuration separately from Tronbyt credentials; do not commit secrets or backups.
- [ ] Stop the cloud controller’s writes and establish ownership before flashing or selecting Tronbyt. Never run competing backend writers or automatically fall back to an incompatible firmware/backend pair.
- [ ] Verify selected server identity, frame rendering, timing/rotation behavior, status semantics, disconnected/stale behavior and recovery. Compare against the previously accepted cloud baseline without assuming protocol acknowledgment proves pixels.
- [ ] Record server, firmware, transport and user-visible acceptance separately, including rollback verification or a documented blocker. Close only with the explicitly agreed physical evidence.

## Required issue prerequisites

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/44 (dedicated always-on host for the Tronbyt server)

Blocked until required source prerequisites are complete. Next action: complete those issues and resolve the readiness decisions above. Explicit installation and physical permissions are additional gates, never inferred from dependency closure.

## Verification

Future authorized hardware run only, after source compatibility and accepted cloud baseline. This backlog definition authorizes no flashing, server deployment or device contact.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Before behavior changes, create the exact issue-linked `gh-24-tronbyt-transition` OpenSpec change and proportionate executable checks. Documentation-only qualification needs a recorded no-product-delta rationale. Use isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep secrets, private paths, agent content and runtime state out of Git. This backlog issue does not authorize implementation, installation, device operations or settings changes.

## Owner decisions and research (2026-09-25)

**Settled facts**

- **Device:** Tidbyt **Gen 1**. The firmware target is `tidbyt-gen1`.
- **Host:** the Tronbyt server runs on **dedicated always-on hardware** ([#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/44)), not the PC. The owner chose to stay on the Tidbyt cloud until that hardware exists. This transition is therefore blocked by #44 as well as #23.

**Flashing and recovery facts**

- The project warns that flashing "could fatally damage your device" and voids the warranty ([firmware](https://github.com/tronbyt/firmware-esp32)).
- Reported problems were fixable. Some Gen 1 revisions swap color channels (build flag `SWAP_COLORS`), some units need a button press while flashing, and others were configuration typos. The thread reports no bricked devices ([forum thread](https://discuss.tidbyt.com/t/tronbyt-replacement-firmware-and-backend/7092)).
- **Stock restore:** use the web flasher (esptool-js) with the published `gen1_merged.bin` at address 0x0, with Erase Flash first. The runbook must include this before any flash.
- **Firmware updates:** the server can push them over the air. Pin firmware and server versions and disable automatic updates. Past regressions include a Gen 1 crash-and-reboot on 1.5.4 and brightness too high after 1.5.0, both fixed ([issues](https://github.com/tronbyt/firmware-esp32/issues?q=is%3Aissue)).

**Host prerequisites to settle in #44**

- The Tidbyt must reach the server over the LAN, so the host needs a stable address (DHCP reservation).
- Every router or firewall change needs explicit authorization.

**Context.** Tidbyt/Modal said on 2024-11-07 that the cloud "will remain running for everyone with existing devices", with no timeline ([Modal](https://modal.com/blog/tidbyt-is-joining-modal)).


## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** #23's pinned server and firmware compatibility record and the exact device generation, which decide what gets flashed and how rollback works.

**Reassess when:** #23 is delivered with its compatibility record.

issues.title: Implement the deferred Tronbyt connection
issues.body:
## Outcome

Add an explicitly selected Tronbyt server connection behind the Tidbyt controller’s existing rendering boundary.

## Ownership and scope

Owner: `controllers/tidbyt`. Deferred; scheduling and implementation decisions remain open. This is a future deliverable created by #14. Bootstrap delivery does not implement or install it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Refresh and pin the server API/firmware compatibility record before readiness. Resolve endpoint/authentication, installation identity, capabilities, interruption/background behavior, limits, observation semantics and delivery behavior in issue-linked OpenSpec design.
- [ ] Reuse existing frames and controller queues. Keep server URL, backend device ID, credentials and capability differences in connection configuration; never copy the status renderer or shared state reducer.
- [ ] Implement explicit backend selection with no automatic failover. Stop/drain or cancel the previous writer before enabling the selected connection; report uncertain old sends and prevent replay of expired frames.
- [ ] Test identical rendering fixtures through both connections and backend-specific authentication, errors, timeouts and capabilities. Do not claim API compatibility solely because an endpoint name matches.
- [ ] Document source configuration and operational prerequisites without deploying a server, installing firmware or migrating a live device. Hardware transition belongs to its separate issue.

## Required issue prerequisites

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/16
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4

Blocked until required source prerequisites are complete. Next action: complete those issues and resolve the readiness decisions above. Explicit installation and physical permissions are additional gates, never inferred from dependency closure.

## Verification

Use fake cloud/Tronbyt servers and fixture parity, then package and shared-consumer checks. An optional isolated server compatibility test needs no real display; firmware/physical evidence is separate.

## Sources to qualify

- https://github.com/tronbyt/server/blob/v2.3.7/API.md
- https://github.com/tronbyt/firmware-esp32/tree/v1.6.9

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Before behavior changes, create the exact issue-linked `gh-23-tronbyt-connection` OpenSpec change and proportionate executable checks. Documentation-only qualification needs a recorded no-product-delta rationale. Use isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep secrets, private paths, agent content and runtime state out of Git. This backlog issue does not authorize implementation, installation, device operations or settings changes.

## Home Assistant comparison — 2026-10-01

Compare [TronbytAssistant](https://github.com/tronbyt/TronbytAssistant) with direct server API access for administration/settings/app controls, using [#11](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11) for optional HA adoption.

- [ ] Pin server/firmware/integration versions and identify reusable operations while retaining frame delivery, priority, update gate and observation semantics.
- [ ] Show delegation to the existing Tidbyt owner or explicit handoff; HA must not become a competing frame/app writer.
- [ ] Preserve cloud-until-dedicated-host, #44's Mac/OrbStack qualification and #24's physical firmware transition. HA administration alone does not complete this connection.

## Work assessment

HA comparison reassessed on 2026-10-01 against the sources and acceptance above. Existing ratings and readiness remain; this adds candidate evidence, not adoption or physical qualification. Reassess on route/host selection or a failed required capability.

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** Explicit backend selection that drains the previous writer, isolated connection configuration and parity tests across both connections.
- **Uncertainty: high.** Endpoint, authentication, capability and observation semantics for the named server and firmware are unresolved.
- **Impact: medium.** Source-only with fakes, but a defect in writer handoff would reach the one-writer-per-device rule when installed.

## Owner decisions and research (2026-09-25)

**Decisions.** The owner settled these on 2026-09-25, during #38's installation.

- Stay on the official Tidbyt cloud for now.
- The goal is Tronbyt running on **dedicated always-on hardware**, planned in [#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/44), not on the PC.
- The owner's Tidbyt is a **Gen 1**.

**Why not the PC.** With Tronbyt, the server decides every frame. If its host is off, asleep or WSL isn't running, the whole Tidbyt stops updating, not just our tiles. The device also has to connect *into* the server over the LAN. WSL2's default networking doesn't allow that without mirrored networking or a port forward, plus a Windows firewall rule and a stable address. The hub deliberately listens only on loopback.

**What Tronbyt offers, from docs, not yet verified on this device:**

- **Display priority:** pushed images first, then the night-mode app, then a pinned app, then the normal rotation.
- **Delivery:** WebSocket delivery for current firmware, with HTTP polling of `/next` as a fallback.
- **Brightness and dwell:** the server controls both.
- **API:** token-authenticated `/v0` endpoints for push and installations, including pin and enable.
- **Management:** several devices and users, and Docker deployment.

Sources: [tronbyt/server](https://github.com/tronbyt/server), [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/tronbyt/server), [tronbyt/firmware-esp32](https://github.com/tronbyt/firmware-esp32).

**One known API gap.** An app pushed under a client-chosen installation ID could not be pinned, enabled or fetched by that ID. [tronbyt/server#910](https://github.com/tronbyt/server/pull/910) addresses it. Verify the pinned server version includes the fix.

**How this changes the connection.** Pushes become immediate interrupts, and pin/enable enables a "music mode" (for example, only the music and clock cards while music plays). The runner's 15 s write gate and 5 s playback read were chosen for the cloud; a local server makes a shorter gate reasonable. Prefer contributing any missing API upstream over forking the server or writing our own.

**Deferred alternative on the cloud.** A non-background push is "immediately prioritized for display" per Tidbyt staff, and frequent pushes block the rotation ([forum](https://discuss.tidbyt.com/t/device-showing-only-the-pushed-app/1160)). This is not qualified here (#16). Revisit trigger: the owner wants immediacy before Tronbyt hardware exists; start with a single qualification push.

**Coordination.** [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) would move the Tidbyt runner into one local controller host. Backend selection (cloud or Tronbyt) then lives in that host's Tidbyt connection configuration.

issues.title: Evaluate Home Assistant and MQTT for additional device integrations
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Determine where Home Assistant (HA) or MQTT can replace unbuilt device-access work for one operator and the existing Windows/WSL B.U.N.N.Y. installation, while preserving native Nanoleaf spatial behavior, Pixoo frame/playback behavior and designated writers. HA is not installed or selected. The future Mac mini host in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/44 is a separate deferred migration, not a prerequisite for this research.

## Smallest useful implementation

Reuse the existing qualification issues below. This issue owns the cross-device comparison, proposed shared routing and adoption decision; it is not a parent or universal prerequisite for every device.

1. Compare the existing direct-library route with HA for Wemo and LG, using Roborock as the observational case. Include Reachy's vendor integration and apartment sensing. This is a research order, not portfolio selection or installation authority.
2. Compare the operating burden for these candidates: host/runtime, maintenance, credentials, local/cloud dependencies, LAN discovery/events, Bluetooth/USB access and failure isolation. HA could serve several devices; the old one-vacuum cost assumption is no longer sufficient. Keep current WSL and possible future Mac/OrbStack qualification separate.
3. Propose the smallest authenticated HA-backed adapter through existing Hub/controller and typed-profile boundaries. Evaluate native WebSocket state subscriptions/action calls first; MQTT is optional where a selected producer uses it. Existing controllers remain the only writers for already integrated devices.
4. Return a bounded go/no-go and unresolved owner choices. After a route is accepted, refine existing source/installation stories; create a shared adapter story only if selected consumers actually need it. Do not prebuild a generic HA platform or create speculative implementation tickets.

Required source prerequisite: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4 (closed; retained as contract provenance). Device qualification issues are related independent work. Add a native prerequisite only when an accepted route creates an actual required input.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One active agent-state owner and one designated writer per physical device. HA must delegate to the existing controller or become the writer through an explicit controlled handoff. Preserve bounded queues, manual/vendor-app takeover and truthful external-state observations.

Retain Nanoleaf geometry, allocations, task/effect epochs, source reservations, unread policy, preferences, scenes and Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Retain Pixoo originals/renditions, simulator startup, frame/timing fidelity, playback recovery and Monitor/Media semantics. Ordinary power/brightness/effect support is not parity.

Use configured identities, allowlisted operations, private credentials and existing authorization. Preserve timestamps, availability, stale/unknown state, duplicate handling and no replay on reconnect. HA action success is not physical acceptance. Do not disguise robot motion, TV operations or heating as light commands.

The ambient recording/passive-transcription hold in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/634 remains in force. No installation, device contact, pairing, microphone/camera activation, procurement or network changes are authorized here.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Complete a cited capability/limit matrix for the named candidates and HA/MQTT contracts. Distinguish official/vendor integrations, community code, exact-model evidence and unknown physical behavior. The dated findings below are partial evidence, not hardware qualification.
- [ ] AC2: Compare direct and HA routes for Wemo/LG/Roborock and reuse prospects for Reachy/sensing. Name host requirements, local/cloud behavior, maintenance burden and missing capabilities; unknown effort stays unknown.
- [ ] AC3: Return synthetic contract examples for identity/capability mapping, observed state, stale/unavailable input, authentication failure, duplicate/ambiguous commands, restart/reconnect and manual takeover. Include allowlisted agent-status publication with stable identity, separate activity/attention and freshness, without exporting prompts/transcripts or making HA the state owner. For MQTT, distinguish discovery/state/availability from command freshness/replay rules. Show no second writer or automatic replay; no live broker/device is required.
- [ ] AC4: Separate reusable transport from retained B.U.N.N.Y. behavior. Any Nanoleaf/Pixoo replacement claim requires exact spatial/frame/timing and ownership evidence; otherwise retain native controllers.
- [ ] AC5: Return a bounded go/no-go with named owner decisions and affected existing stories. A viable option is not adoption. Reconcile source, installation and physical follow-ups after selection without changing unrelated commitments or protections.

Initial delivery: research, simulator/contract design and accepted planning record. The original source-only configuration/installation-tooling obligation is retained: after route selection, define its concrete acceptance and owning source follow-up(s), linked here before closure. Research alone does not satisfy those obligations. This tracker update delivers no product implementation or executable simulator. Future source changes retain issue-linked specifications, checks, independent review and CI. Installation and physical trials require separate authorization.

## Meaningful deferrals

HA installation, shared-adapter implementation and live trials wait for route/host selection. Direct qualification and vendor apps remain available meanwhile. Existing Nanoleaf, Pixoo, LIFX and Tidbyt integrations are not migration targets merely for uniformity. No all-vendor catalogue, new hardware purchase or portfolio reprioritization. Revisit candidates when their owning issues supply missing model/firmware/host evidence or the owner selects them.

- PC lighting: [icue2mqtt](https://github.com/tobinbrooke/icue2mqtt) documents loss of iCUE updates until its service stops; [HA OpenRGB](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/openrgb/) lacks per-zone/per-LED control. issues.title: Evaluate Effect for Hub status-subscription handling
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Decide whether Effect improves the existing TypeScript Hub status-subscription boundary enough to justify its dependency and maintenance cost. Compare it with the native approach under the same B.U.N.N.Y. contracts and #455 failure criteria. Effect remains a candidate, not an adopted foundation dependency.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with one read-only comparison of the current native feed/evaluation machinery and an exact pinned Effect release. Read official documentation/source for that release; do not mix v3/v4 APIs. Inspect stream cleanup, cancellation, reconnect/retry scheduling, coalescing, slow-consumer isolation, dependency/package compatibility, TypeScript/Python boundaries and available test support.

Compare the shared contract in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/701 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/455. Read-only research can start independently using accepted criteria and current code. An executable superiority claim requires a usable native baseline and any separately authorized comparison; prefer the delivered #455 baseline before that step. These are distinct from a native blocked-by relationship on the initial investigation.

Effect's bounded PubSub can suspend publishers behind slow subscribers; analyze that against B.U.N.N.Y.'s nonblocking intake and per-consumer isolation. An in-process PubSub is not durable transport. If discussing persisted queues, name the exact version, backing store, stability, retry/failed-item and acknowledgment semantics rather than attributing durability to the Effect dependency alone. Sources: https://effect.website/docs/v4/concurrency/pubsub and https://effect.website/docs/v4/api/effect/persistence/PersistedQueue.

Bound: one comparison report of these two approaches and, if runtime evidence is still needed, one proposed fake-stream comparison brief. Stop after that report; do not install dependencies, write or run a prototype, extend into a framework survey, start services or contact devices. The brief names inputs, allowed effects, finite scenarios/run bound, retained observations, stop conditions and the next decision for supported/refuted/inconclusive outcomes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Compare the same schema, cancellation, timeout, queue, stream and credential protections. Preserve fail-open hooks, one state owner/writer, latest-state status, live-only device effects, manual modes and the language-neutral contract. No Effect requirement is imposed on Python consumers. A convenience API is not evidence of preserved semantics.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: read-only investigation; no implementation or operational acceptance.

- [x] AC1: Return a source-backed API-to-requirement table identifying the exact release and distinguishing supported behavior from assumptions for native and Effect approaches.
- [x] AC2: Compare shutdown during a pending read, disconnect/reconnect/resync, malformed/oversized input, authorization failure, notices during evaluation, slow consumers and bounded resource cleanup. Name each invariant's enforcement owner and evidence limits.
- [x] AC3: Identify dependency/API-stability and maintenance implications, required integration changes and Python compatibility. Do not infer access or package/runtime results from documentation.
- [x] AC4: If inspection cannot settle suitability, propose one bounded comparison using synthetic SSE, fake clocks/controllers and the same #455 criteria. Explicitly identify any installation or other effects needing authorization. No experiment is executed under this read-only story.
- [x] AC5: Return adopt-locally, defer or inconclusive with supporting evidence, unresolved questions and the exact next owner decision. Adoption and implementation wait for needed executable evidence and a separate owner decision; a read-only report cannot prove runtime superiority.

Completion evidence is the inspectable report in this issue or linked permitted task evidence, with dated code/doc revisions and the next decision.

Completed investigation: [2026-10-02 pinned Effect 4.0.0 comparison report](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/702#issuecomment-5945410679). Recommendation: defer adoption; any fake-stream experiment or adoption needs a separate owner decision. This closes the investigation only; #701/#455 remain independently open. A report or checkbox is not implementation, installed-client, visible-device or physical evidence.

## Meaningful deferrals

Dependency installation, prototype execution, production changes, broker/store selection and mandatory adoption remain deferred. The next trigger is a report that identifies a concrete benefit or an unresolved scenario needing a bounded executable comparison. No publication of this investigation grants those effects. #455 may proceed with native primitives while this question is unresolved.

## Work assessment

Planning, 2026-10-01. One operator/current Windows/WSL Hub and its TypeScript status-feed seam; no new host or supported device family.

Complexity: medium, because the comparison crosses feed, evaluator and publisher lifecycles. Uncertainty: high, because benefit and equivalence have not been established. Impact: low for this read-only investigation; reassess impact before any implementation or adoption.

Readiness: ready to investigate, unselected backlog work. Implementation/adoption remains pending evidence and owner decision. Alignment: existing bounded feed/evaluation primitives provide the native baseline; shared events do not require a TypeScript library. issues.title: Start new stories with a descriptive headline and five bullets
issues.body:
## Understand each new story before its technical detail

- Give each new story a descriptive headline at the top of its body.
- Follow that headline with exactly five short bullets about the planned work.
- Use the same opening in the GitHub template and agent-written stories.
- Keep the detailed sections and strict Guide fields intact.
- Leave existing stories unchanged, including when they are picked up or edited.

## Outcome and real setup

Implement the owner's October 1 handoff in agent-device-hub: a separate level-two descriptive heading and exactly five top-level bullets before the five existing story sections. Apply the rule after adoption to new feature, maintenance, investigation and child stories written through GitHub, CLI or agents. An existing parent does not change when a new child uses the format.

## Smallest useful implementation

Update the new-story template and canonical guidance in docs/sdlc.md, reached through the existing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md paths. GitHub's YAML form adds fixed labels; use the smallest compatible template change that puts an author-selected headline first. A Markdown template preserves the chooser name and labels but gives up required-input validation. Verify local sample bodies rather than creating live test issues. Dependencies: none.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Do not backfill, rename, reformat or otherwise edit existing stories. Preserve recognized detailed headings, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria, Guide grammar, assessment and execution advice. The opening summarizes planned work and cannot imply installation, delivery or physical verification. Investigations promise findings or a decision; unresolved choices stay unresolved. No new wire field, readiness rule, prose-scoring system, shared-skill change, guide refresh, installation or device action.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only

- A local feature sample and a local investigation sample begin with a descriptive level-two headline and exactly five short bullets.
- The template path and agent-authored path put the opening before the existing detailed sections and Guide fields.
- Existing story content remains valid without an opening, and additional headings do not redefine parsed scope or readiness.
- Run Node 24 setup with npm ci, npm run check:workflow and npm run test:workflow from the isolated worktree, plus focused parser/record checks.
- Record changed files, a rendered example, rendering/authoring limitations, independent fixed-revision Standards and Specification reviews, and applicable PR/main CI. Obtain current-candidate UI approval before adopting the changed GitHub authoring interface.

This is a documentation/template change with no product behavior delta; no OpenSpec capability delta is needed.

## Meaningful deferrals

Automated prose scoring and retroactive enforcement are outside scope. Template authors must fill and check the Markdown prompts; required-input form validation is unavailable on that path.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Note:** Add the owner's headline-and-five-bullets opening to future story writing.

issues.title: Repair composed reset for default proof receipts
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make `verify:compose reset` work with the verification core's default storage and normal proof permissions on the owner's Windows/WSL development host. Hub #613 reproduced a failure before either consumer is paused, despite a healthy pinned composition. The owner approved this separate repair and delivery in the coordinating chat on 2026-09-29.

## Smallest useful implementation

Align `apps/hub/verify/feed-pause.mjs` receipt validation with the core's existing storage contract. Core receipts use mode 0644 and the default runtime label `~/.local/state/app-verify`; ordinary proof directories can be 0755/0775. Reset currently requires private proof files/directories and an absolute receipt runtime field. Independent probes reproduce each mismatch. This repairs the reset delivery in PR #600 (issue #557); it does not reopen its historical qualification receipts.

Use the existing core and reset driver. Add a real core-receipt regression that exercises default roots and ordinary proof permissions. Keep runtime controls private. No consumer package/pin or shared wire-format change is planned. This repair is required by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/613; source base is da5e4794d45f461bc583b1092b8ee1edeac07a94.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve one state owner and one writer per simulated device, drained-feed ordering, exact run/unit/PID/start-time and live-lease checks, owned paths, symlink and unsafe-file rejection, bounded reads, no replay, interruption recovery, and owner-first stop. Do not chmod existing proof, weaken private request/ack/release controls, rewrite frozen evidence, bypass permissions or mask the defect with root overrides. No installed services, personal configuration or physical devices change.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] A focused regression using a real core-generated receipt fails on the old implementation and passes after repair for default storage/normal proof permissions; explicit-root compatibility remains covered.
- [x] Invalid ownership/path/receipt/process/lease and nonprivate pause controls still fail before owner reset. Existing interruption and cleanup checks remain green.
- [x] At a clean committed candidate, start the actual pinned Hub/wall/Pixoo composition through the approved host route with default storage, change synthetic state through maintained captures, freeze proof, reset twice and verify seeded state restored with no replay, unchanged run IDs/ports/pairing/leases and frozen hashes, then stop cleanly.
- [x] Update the affected verification recipe and preserve the initial failure evidence. Independent Standards and Specification review, all applicable PR and merged-main CI, and issue readback pass before closure.

Delivery target: one reviewed PR and verified source/actual-host reset acceptance. #613 keeps its separate fresh-client, independent-session, configuration and browser acceptance obligations.

## Meaningful deferrals

No new host/client target, permissions profile, generalized receipt migration, consumer feature, service installation, device acceptance or recurring monitor. Revisit those only through their own selected work. Historical proof stays readable in place; no bulk rewrite.

## Work assessment

Source and named-host reset acceptance complete. Complexity medium, uncertainty medium at pickup, impact high because reset coordinates synthetic state ownership. Root implemented the bounded compatibility repair directly; two independent read-only reviewers found no defects. No new product capability, consumer pin or wire contract was introduced. Existing composed-preview-reset and core storage contracts remain authoritative. No OpenSpec delta was needed for this tooling compatibility repair.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

## Reset repair accepted — 2026-09-29

The owner approved the prepared repair. [#649 / PR #651](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/651) is accepted at `13fb6310f49d7c909744afc7db8dfdf77cb93ced`. [Independent Standards and Specification review](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/651#issuecomment-5903626917) found no defects in the reviewed comparison. All seven exact-head PR and seven merged-main Depot jobs succeeded with zero annotations. The merged tree matches the reviewed candidate.

Real core-written default and explicit-root receipt regressions passed, as did 37 focused tests, 24 broad validation commands, and seven actual-manager reset/failure/interruption cases. At the clean candidate, the actual pinned Hub/wall/Pixoo composition completed 14 host operations: captures, handoff, two resets, loss/replay/second-owner controls, doctor and owner-first stop. Seeded state returned without replay; IDs, ports, pairing, lease expiry and all 20 frozen-file hashes stayed unchanged. Installed service states match the baseline. Runtime cleanup and copied-proof checksum checks passed; evidence remains in the canonical local delivery directory. The repair made no personal configuration edit, installation or physical-device change.

#613 remains open: selected fresh-client launches, independent-session overlap and Linux Codex configuration metadata attribution are still required. The fresh Desktop ordinary approval-path retry returned supervisor-unavailable before any host command launched; zero starts and verified evidence checksums do not constitute preview success. Normal-terminal CLI/exec evidence is still missing. The source repair does not waive or replace those obligations. Existing operational approval remains valid.

#492's separate first-10-deliveries/14-day manual cohort and equal 14-day observation windows remain pending; actual cohort/window dates are not yet recorded, so no next maturity date can be asserted. #497's historical mixed qualification remains unchanged and agent-skills #44 stays postponed. Native dependency edges remain as provenance. No Project membership or publication expansion is selected.

issues.title: Qualify fresh and parallel Codex preview sessions on Windows/WSL
issues.body:
## Qualification accepted — 2026-10-01

Disposition: complete the named-host Codex qualification. The owner accepted the final integrated previews and screenshot, then accepted the accessible annotated walkthrough in the coordinating chat. The walkthrough shows cursor movement, target outlines, click rings, labels and pauses; the original frozen assertion evidence remains unchanged.

| Acceptance | Final evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Selected clients | Desktop/WSL, normal-terminal interactive WSL CLI 0.159.1 and normal-terminal codex exec 0.159.1 each passed standalone Hub, wall, Pixoo and integrated lifecycle: 33 assertions per client matrix. CLI and exec required ordinary per-command escalation after normal host access was refused; no persistent grant or settings edit was made. |
| Owner browser/chat handoff | Owner accepted the three integrated previews, screenshot and video. The final short actual exec composition passed 11 assertions, survived its client exit and supplied the accepted annotated walkthrough. |
| Independent sessions | Two independent Desktop chats passed separate Hub and integrated-composition overlap cases. Rebuild/reset/stop of A left B's identities, build, synthetic state, feed/writer state and frozen proof unchanged. Six simultaneous services establish this bounded case only. |
| Lifecycle and cleanup | Extension, expiry, restart, failed-start/partial-start cleanup and repaired aggregate reset are evidenced in the retained receipts. Final composition compose-20261001T211922Z-f6343f stopped cleanly; all three units, three lease timers and runtime directories were removed. Final proof checksums pass. The temporary video player also stopped; all five final preview/player listeners refuse connections. |
| Configuration and runbook | The named-host runbook records exact versions, startup checks, per-run ownership, rollback and manual smoke triggers. No configuration change was needed. Earlier metadata changes were attributed by the owner to intentional settings changes/resaves; this is not byte-level unchanged-file proof. |
| Installed system and parent | Final readback retains five active installed services and the owner's intentionally stopped Pixoo controller. No installed service or physical device was changed by this qualification. #492 and #488 retain their separate manual cohort and equal 14-day observation windows. |

Qualification pins: Hub `13fb6310f49d7c909744afc7db8dfdf77cb93ced`, wall `4ddf14bcec94abd145919c8f8d6de332a4b19b9c`, Pixoo `59a3eb71e2969a548b69fe6423a1cd9655624387`. A focused current-main smoke at `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` passed build, prerequisites, seven exact-revision Depot jobs and 11 integrated assertions, then stopped cleanly. Launcher/core/composition code is unchanged between the Hub pins; this does not qualify every intervening UI feature.

Accepted source PRs remain #618, #632 and #651, with retained independent Standards/Specification reviews and successful merged-main CI. No new source change or PR was needed for final acceptance. Existing historical failures remain in the evidence; #497 is not rewritten. Native dependency edges remain as provenance.

Limits: this qualifies the selected Windows/WSL clients on this host. It does not establish unattended approval-free exec, native Windows execution, arbitrary delegated workers, unlimited parallel capacity, or survival after Desktop shutdown/WSL restart. Separate checkouts and build outputs remain required.

Private receipt and runbook: `.local/evidence/codex-preview-delivery/613-final-handoff/result.md` and `613-host-runbook.md` in the canonical Hub checkout. Frozen proof, the accepted MP4, source/CI receipts and command logs are retained there. Live URLs are retired after acceptance. Qualification checkouts and their dependency environment are retained under the SDLC cleanup rules because their heads differ from the reviewed source PR heads; no forced removal or reset was used. Other sessions' resources remain untouched.

No further delivery session is recommended for this completed issue. The earlier execution recommendation below is retained only as dated history. Reassess a newly reported regression or changed client/profile/launcher against the runbook's smoke triggers; no recurring monitor is started.

## Outcome and real setup

Adopt the approved launch configuration on the owner's PC and demonstrate that every selected Codex development entrypoint can independently start, exercise, capture and hand off synthetic app previews. Demonstrate that two concurrent Codex sessions with separate worktrees and runs do not interfere. Report supported configurations and explicit limitations, never an unconditional promise about every future session.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: accepted scope/access decision https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/610, delivered launch/setup https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/611 and readiness check https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/612. These are native prerequisites. Read current source/counterpart pins and the prior [#497 mixed qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497#issuecomment-5881256819) before the run. The old failed receipt remains historical evidence, not a claim about the current version.

Before activation, record explicit owner authority for exact configuration changes, target clients, fresh agent sessions, supervised previews, browser checks and retention/cleanup. Prepare the reviewed configuration diff, backups, readback and rollback first. This planning request supplies none of that host-action authority. Activate only the selected development configuration; do not alter read-only/reviewer sessions or all unrelated Codex projects.

Use the accepted matrix from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/610: initially Desktop/WSL, interactive WSL CLI and `codex exec`, with delegated launches covered if included. Each fresh session starts in its own worktree and receives an ordinary verification request through the documented entrypoint. Record versions, effective permissions, source/build identities, manual intervention and failures. Qualify standalone Hub, wall and Pixoo plus the integrated composition. Use current reference scenarios, preserved controller queues and fake transports.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One active synthetic state owner per composition and one writer per simulated device, separate from the installed system. Distinct worktrees/build outputs, run IDs, state/proof directories, ports and units. One agent controls each run. No shared captures/reset, port/PID-based killing, real device writes, copied personal credentials, blanket sandbox bypass or scope change hidden as a successful retry.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] Each selected entrypoint passes its readiness checks and the single-app/integrated launch, reference capture and handoff paths, with versioned receipts. Missing host support stays failed/pending. Delegated agents' effective permissions and launch behavior are checked independently if selected; inheritance is not assumed.
- [x] From the actual Windows browser and chat surface, the owner opens each preview and its supported screenshot/video handoff. Optional programmatic Windows interop is recorded separately from human browser reachability. Preserve retained frozen files when an adapter does not serve proof URLs.
- [x] Two independent Codex development sessions overlap. Rebuild candidate A, reseed A and stop A while B's health, candidate digest and synthetic state remain unchanged. Verify distinct resources and repeat the relevant isolation case for integrated compositions with separate consumer checkouts. Record concurrent-session failures and correction attempts; a core unit test alone is not session-level proof.
- [x] After the originating session ends, preview extension, expiry, stop and restart work with recorded identity and cleanup. A failed start and partial composed start leave no unowned resources; frozen proof survives cleanup. Exercise current reset/loss/lease behavior through existing drivers without rewriting their tests.
- [x] A fresh session after activation uses the intended configuration without hidden setup. The runbook records the exact supported client/profile combinations, startup check, ownership, rollback and an event-triggered smoke check after relevant client/profile/launcher changes. Hardware exhaustion and broken candidates still fail honestly.
- [x] Read back unchanged installed services and excluded personal configuration, and each preview's final cleanup or explicit owner/expiry. Update the parent with qualified versus unsupported paths; preserve #497's historical result and #492's separate manual observation window.

Delivery target: named-host activation and actual Codex/Windows/parallel acceptance receipts. Closure requires all selected target paths to pass, or an explicit owner scope revision naming the unsupported paths and consequences. A failed trial is useful evidence but does not satisfy the promised usable outcome. This is operational qualification, not agent-skills #44's postponed comparative study.

## Meaningful deferrals

No native Windows execution, cloud/remote/LAN previews, physical-device qualification or performance capacity promise unless the owner adds a target. Two-session concurrency establishes the scoped isolation case, not unlimited scale. No recurring background monitor; rerun smoke checks at relevant upgrades or observed regressions.

## Work assessment

Qualification checkpoint, 2026-09-29. Complexity: high; uncertainty: high for unperformed fresh-client, host and concurrency behavior; impact: high because the accepted route uses Linux-user host authority. #610 is accepted and source prerequisites #611/#612 are delivered. Two isolated source/build sets, pinned consumers, local diagnostics and an exact operational brief are prepared. The owner has approved the named operational brief. Standalone current-Desktop and Hub human-browser evidence is recorded below; fresh-client, integrated and concurrent-session evidence remains pending. No personal configuration edit is proposed. One coordinator owns shared evidence; each parallel session owns only its assigned runs.

## Planning authority and ownership

The owner requested backlog planning on 2026-09-29. This record authorizes no implementation, personal permission changes, installation, service or browser launches, new agent sessions, or device actions. The later task must name its coordinator and applicable authority. issues.title: Check preview prerequisites before starting a verification run
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A Codex development session can check whether it can build, launch, capture and hand off the selected app preview before spending time on a full run. The result identifies the first actionable missing capability and never mistakes inability to inspect for success.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required input: the accepted capability requirements and launch boundary from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/610. Reuse app-verify's existing supervisor, build, path, tooling and diagnostic checks where practical. Keep this distinct from [delivery preflight #496](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/496), which checks source/review/acceptance evidence, and [#559](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/559), which already reports an unbuilt Hub verification core as JSON and serves frozen proof.

Add the smallest documented readiness operation to the existing verification interface; select its command and result shape at implementation pickup after inspecting current callers. Check the effective execution host, supervisor visibility, runtime/proof path usability, required runtimes, built artifacts, browser/capture tooling and any launch-boundary requirement selected upstream. Distinguish readiness to launch, ability to capture, and Windows/browser handoff qualification. A passing precheck is not a successful launch.

The default diagnostic does not start units, change permissions, install tools, contact devices or write application state. If an actual temporary write/bind or supervisor probe is required to establish a capability, report it as unproven in the read-only mode and define a separately authorized bounded probe with owned cleanup. Do not report access-test heuristics as proven filesystem writes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

No secret values or private configuration in output. Retain unavailable, failed and unknown distinctions, run/lease ownership, canonical evidence storage and synthetic-only boundaries. Existing start-time checks remain authoritative because capabilities can change after precheck. No automatic repair, package install or sandbox relaxation.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] A supported fixture reports the capabilities it checked, their scope and next command; it does not claim runtime or Windows-browser acceptance.
- [x] Missing supervisor, denied runtime/proof root, missing build/tool/browser and unavailable host evidence produce distinct actionable outcomes with deterministic tests and a known-failure control.
- [x] Tests verify default diagnostics create no service/run state and cannot reach installed services/devices. Any authorized probe variant cleans only its own artifacts on success and failure.
- [x] Hub and the declared Nanoleaf/Pixoo consumers can use the documented diagnostic or explicitly report unsupported capability until their owned adapters adopt it. Version/package compatibility and the affected feature maps are updated and checked; no duplicate implementation in each adapter.
- [ ] https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/613 runs the diagnostic from each actual Codex entrypoint and records whether its prediction matches launch/capture/handoff. Windows interop absence must not be confused with proof that a human cannot open the preview.

Delivery target: source-only shared capability and the declared consumer adoption. Run existing shared build/type, app-verify/package and affected adapter checks; add focused failure controls. Independent Standards/Specification review remains required. Host proof is separate.

## Meaningful deferrals

No always-on monitoring or automatic remediation. Read-only diagnostics cannot prove every future operation; use actual launch and browser checks in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/613. Defer unrelated machines and remote-network checks until explicitly selected.

## Work assessment

Source accepted 2026-09-29. Complexity: medium; uncertainty: medium at pickup; impact: medium. PR #632 delivered the shared read-only diagnostic, Hub build hook and standalone host routing at `da5e4794d45f461bc583b1092b8ee1edeac07a94`. Both independent review axes and all seven merged-main Depot jobs passed. The execution recommendation below records source pickup; no implementation remains in this closed source story. The final operational criterion remains unchecked and assigned to #613; source acceptance does not claim fresh-client or Windows qualification.

## Planning authority and ownership

The owner requested backlog planning on 2026-09-29. This record authorizes no implementation, personal permission changes, installation, service or browser launches, new agent sessions, or device actions. The later task must name its coordinator and applicable authority. One coordinator owns each deliverable; source changes follow the owning repository's PR, independent Standards and Specification review, CI and merged-revision readback gates. No Project membership or commitment is selected here.

Preserve [#497's mixed qualification result](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497#issuecomment-5881256819) as historical evidence; do not reopen it or claim that its closure qualified Codex. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: a change to the accepted host boundary, personal activation, fresh agent sessions or host/browser qualification; source delivery does not activate settings. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-29) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.

The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-29) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.

**Why:** Accepted requirements permit source delivery. The launcher crosses host authority and interruption/cleanup boundaries; readiness crosses shared CLI/plugin and consumer compatibility interfaces. Independent review covers the applicable impact and interacting behavior.
**Reassess when:** The accepted boundary, source ownership, caller compatibility or validation evidence changes.
