issues.title: Read multi-axis finding lines in the delivery preflight review parser
issues.body:
### Failure and reproduction

`scripts/delivery-preflight/reviews.mjs` (at `fb411f7`) parses each review-result finding line with `FINDING = /^- (\S+) \((P[0-3]), ([a-z]+), (unresolved|resolved|regression|accepted|deferred)\): /`, so the axis field accepts one lowercase word only. Since jimmie-potts/agent-skills#106 (merged as `c4fb878`), review-work's result contract (`skills/review-work/references/result-contract.md`) lists every axis whose reviewer raised a failure condition, joined by `+`, for example:

```text
- F1 (P2, standards+specification, resolved): src/export.ts:40, an empty filter exported every tenant's rows; first final 1, latest final 2
```

Such a line fails the regex, `parseReport` records `finding line <n> is unreadable`, and `judgeRound` turns that problem into a gate reason. A valid review round whose axes are both satisfied is then reported as not passing, and the multi-axis finding is dropped from the open-blocker check. Observed on PR #587, whose review report notes the lag. Found during the agent-skills#61 (close-work) closeout.

### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- A finding line whose axes field is one axis or several axes joined by `+` (`standards`, `specification` or `standards+specification`) parses. The parsed finding keeps every listed axis.
- The open P0-P2 blocker check still sees a multi-axis `unresolved` or `regression` finding.
- Malformed lines are still reported as unreadable, including `both` and a repeated axis, which the contract forbids.
- Tests cover a single-axis line, a `standards+specification` line in each state, and the rejected forms.

Related, not required here: jimmie-potts/agent-skills#109 proposes an alias form for coalesced finding IDs. If it lands first, read that form too, or record it as a separate follow-up.

### Dependencies, verification and delivery target

No blockers. Source delivery only: update the parser and its tests, then pass the repository's checks. No installation or physical verification.

### Guide placement

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

issues.title: Reconcile parent and dependent issue trackers at SDLC checkpoints
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Codex and Claude keep native issue trackers current when authorized work changes their evidence. A delivery coordinator reconciles the affected parent, ancestor and dependent issues as part of closeout, so completed children do not leave unexplained open phases and closed prerequisites do not remain listed as current holds.

The 2026-09-29 reconciliation of [PStack #488](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488) and [assessment pass #341](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/341) exposed the gap. Hub's SDLC defines leaf acceptance and readback, but no routine propagation checkpoint for those related records. [#536](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536) already requires parent outcomes to be accepted on their own evidence. This issue makes that maintenance responsibility explicit for ordinary repository work, whether or not a shared workflow skill is invoked.

## Smallest useful implementation

Update `docs/sdlc.md` and the minimal `AGENTS.md` pointer needed to make the checkpoint discoverable. Use the centrally installed writing-for-agents and unslop skills. Keep the procedure project-owned and consume existing GitHub CLI/API and recommendation tooling; do not copy shared skills or create a second status store.

- Trigger the checkpoint at accepted child completion, reopening, material scope or prerequisite change, and ownership handoff. The task's coordinating writer owns it before the final closeout report. Read-only work reports discrepancies; tracker-only work stays within its named scope; normal authorized delivery includes the affected routine reconciliation within existing repository authority.
- Bound discovery to the selected issue's native parent chain, native dependency/dependent links, and explicitly linked trackers whose acceptance or remaining work the change affects. Follow necessary pagination. An unavailable relationship read is unknown, not an empty graph. Do not scan every issue or treat every mention as a dependency.
- Map each affected acceptance criterion to delivered evidence or an explicit remaining obligation. Distinguish required and optional children, completed and not-planned closure, and source, installation, host, human and physical acceptance. Recheck the parent's own finish line before closing or reopening it; neither a checked child list nor a merged PR supplies that evidence.
- Re-read immediately before a write, compare the reviewed state, change only affected sections/checkboxes/labels/native dependencies, then read back the result. Preserve unrelated edits and one-writer ownership. On concurrent change, reassess before writing; after an ambiguous result, inspect the authoritative state before retrying. Repeated reconciliation of unchanged inputs is a no-op.
- Reassess affected execution recommendations when the story's scope or next step changes, using the canonical parser/upsert and current policy. Preserve insufficient assessments, record missing inputs, and never refresh a fingerprint merely to disguise stale advice. Held sections require the owning writer's handoff or owner-written update.
- Include a concise receipt in the existing closeout: affected trackers updated or already current; acceptance still pending; any blocked reconciliation with its owner, reason and next trigger. A coordination message is not acknowledgment or completed acceptance. A related tracker/access failure does not erase separately verified source delivery or justify a false parent closure.
- For time-dependent follow-up, name the evidence still needed and the next eligible checkpoint from the actual cohort/observation dates. Do not invent mature windows or automatic between-session execution.

Related work: [#538](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/538) owns Project-field projection and its live qualification; [#542](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542) owns contract-approval policy. Coordinate shared SDLC/AGENTS edits with their current writers. Neither is a prerequisite for this native-issue procedure; retain one canonical reconciliation rule and let #538 reference it once available. Sibling repositories and central skills retain their own instruction owners.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep acceptance, independent reviews, current-head CI, guarded merge and merged-main readback intact. Tracker maintenance must not waive installation/device authority, change the owner's portfolio selection, silently cut accepted behavior, reparent shared work, or revive postponed agent-skills #44. Unfinished source or operational acceptance stays visible.

The work guide remains a dated publication, and Project fields remain projections with their own field authority. This checkpoint neither requires a guide rebuild for each delivery nor grants publication, Project configuration or cross-repository policy-write authority.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] AC1: Both ordinary Codex and Claude repository workflows can discover one coordinator-owned checkpoint, with explicit triggers, bounded relationship discovery and read-only/tracker-only/delivery authority. Evidence: fresh-context walkthroughs of the candidate instructions using those three request types; no hypothetical mutation is executed.
- [x] AC2: Criterion-level examples distinguish a closeable parent from one whose children are closed but whose outcome is incomplete. Use the dated #489/#491 reconciliation and #490's retained #557/#560 obligations as evidence, preserving their current live state. Cover optional children, not-planned closure and separately pending installed/physical acceptance; do not operate those devices or implement those repairs.
- [x] AC3: A retired hold is removed while unresolved owner holds remain. Use #341's #497/#561 closures and the #45/#358/#359 handoff boundary. Include a changed recommendation, an insufficient story and a missing relationship read. Evidence: expected update/no-op/pending outcomes and canonical recommendation parsing; do not rewrite held sections for the test.
- [x] AC4: Walkthroughs cover concurrent owner edits, ambiguous write responses, repeat execution, an active writer and reopened acceptance. Each preserves unrelated data and distinguishes sent coordination from acknowledgment. A pending related update is reported without undoing valid source acceptance or claiming complete reconciliation.
- [x] AC5: A #492-style observation follow-up remains open with actual window dates, missingness and a next checkpoint; a successful guide refresh or Project update cannot substitute for the missing evidence. No scheduled scanner, new ledger or model study is introduced.
- [x] AC6: A separately authorized delivery qualifies one bounded reversible tracker edit or a genuine no-op against a selected live record, with before/after and authoritative readback evidence. Select the record and scope at pickup; no dummy closure, reparenting or interference with an active owner. Keep private receipts in the main checkout's ignored evidence area.
- [x] AC7: Deliver the instructions through an isolated PR with independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, all applicable current-head/main CI and guarded merge. Use Node 24, `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow`; report the actual OpenSpec inventory. Record why this policy-only change needs no product-spec delta. Preserve baseline gates when testing the new checkpoint.

Delivery target: merged repository instructions plus the bounded tracker-procedure qualification. Issue creation records the plan; it does not implement the policy or start its future runtime, review or live-write exercises. All evidence above is planned unless explicitly linked as historical evidence.

## Meaningful deferrals

No daemon, scheduler, whole-backlog repair pass or synchronization framework. Manual event-triggered reconciliation is the first implementation; revisit automation only after repeated missed updates or evidenced maintenance burden. Cross-repository instruction rollout needs a concrete owning delta and separate authorization. #538 retains Project projection; intentional guide updates and publication retain their existing process.

## Assessment and readiness

Assessed 2026-09-29 against Hub main and the live #538/#542 scopes. Complexity medium: native hierarchy, dependent records, recommendations and closeout semantics interact. Uncertainty low: the owner accepted the bounded checkpoint and its authority limits; remaining work is instruction design and verification. Impact medium: incorrect instructions could misstate several trackers' readiness or completion.

Ready for bounded source-instruction delivery when selected. No new dependency or portfolio commitment is implied. Search boundary: current SDLC, installed shared assessment/recommendation/review policy, #536/#538/#542, and the linked PStack/#341 reconciliation; repeat only changed sources at pickup. This is independently useful without Project access or the #538 live-field trial.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Note:** Reconcile parent acceptance, dependent holds and affected recommendations at SDLC checkpoints, with guarded writes and verified readbacks.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Implement the bounded instruction scope directly; retain two independent final reviewers and the issue’s qualification boundary.
**Work surface:** Backend

Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/579. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. ```

Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-sol reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: before changing accepted scope or touching an active writer’s files; qualify only the selected tracker/Project record within the delivery’s existing authority. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-29) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** The same bounded implementation, as a one-shot session in Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) `high`. Codex: none. Codex has no evidenced model or budget unavailability. The cheaper Claude start retains the recommended reviewers and all acceptance gates.

**Cheaper prompt (Claude Code):**

The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-29) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Why:** This bounded procedure crosses hierarchy, acceptance, recommendation freshness and concurrent-write recovery. Sol-level judgment and Sol/high reviews fit the interacting records; Claude uses high effort for verification and concurrency edge cases.
**Reassess when:** The scope or authority changes, a shared-file owner becomes active, required access is unavailable, or qualification exposes an unmet capability.

issues.title: Read registered controllers at contract 1.1 with a 1.0 fallback
issues.body:
> Split from #335 on 2026-09-28 at the owner's request. #335 keeps the moment sender and is blocked by this story. This story defines scope and acceptance; it does not authorize installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

The hub reads each registered controller at controller contract API 1.1 where the controller serves it, and falls back to 1.0 where it does not. Hub readers keep the 1.0 shape unless they ask for 1.1, and the per-device MCP `status` tool reads at 1.1. It is the hub-side reader that #335's sender needs before it sends anything. It is also what codex-nanoleaf#158 and divoom-app-upgrade#92 are checked against once a controller serves 1.1. Today the hub's controller client validates only 1.0 snapshots ([`controllers.ts`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/apps/hub/src/controllers.ts#L63-L69)).

Setup is the installed hub with its registered controllers. No registered controller serves 1.1 yet:
- The Nanoleaf controller and #318's local controller host answer a versioned read with `invalid-request`.
- Device adoption is codex-nanoleaf#158 and divoom-app-upgrade#92.

The [moment explainer](https://claude.ai/artifact/1LHU15QatQmMvbqcLAkTcx) diagrams the flow; this story is its read half.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- **Version negotiation per controller.** The hub reads a controller's snapshot with `apiVersion=1.1` and validates the answer against `snapshotV1_1`. An `invalid-request` answer means the controller serves only 1.0: the hub reads again without the parameter and records a `1.0-only` verdict for that controller's epoch. The hub probes again only when that epoch changes, and at hub start. Timeouts, 5xx answers and other failures never produce a 1.0-only verdict. The contract's rules govern: [negotiation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/docs/controller-contract.md#moments-api-11). The contract package already provides `negotiateApiVersion`, `downgradeSnapshot`, the 1.1 validators and fixtures; nothing changes under `packages/contracts`.
- **Hub reads keep 1.0 by default.** `GET /api/controllers/v1/:id/snapshot` without a parameter keeps returning the 1.0 shape, using `downgradeSnapshot` for a 1.1 controller. With `?apiVersion=1.1` it returns the 1.1 snapshot (including `capabilities.moments` and `state.moment`) for a 1.1 controller, and the 1.0 snapshot for a 1.0-only controller. The per-device MCP `status` tool reads at 1.1. The dashboard is unchanged, so this story is Backend only.
- **Shared fake controller.** A reusable fake 1.1 controller fixture under `apps/hub/tests`, built on the contract package's validators and fixtures: negotiation, a 1.0-only variant that answers `invalid-request`, and an epoch restart. Today each hub test spins its own ad hoc server. #335 extends this fixture with moment admission, a holdable slot and a command spy, and #358 reuses it.
- **No commands.** This story adds no command path, sender, route, tool or page.

Dependencies: #292 (closed; [`controller-contracts-v1.1.0`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/controller-contracts-v1.1.0) is released and the hub already pins `@jimmie-potts/device-contracts` 1.1.0). Nothing blocks this story. #335 is blocked by it.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- 1.0 controllers and 1.0 readers keep working unchanged: dashboard polls, MCP commands (which keep `apiVersion:'1.0'`), Tidbyt and LIFX through the local controller host, and every existing hub test.
- Reads, reconnects and dashboard polls never send commands.
- The existing one-slot-per-controller client stays in place. The fallback costs one extra read per controller epoch, not one per poll.
- Stored and returned data holds no credentials or tokens.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Evidence is hub tests over loopback HTTP against the fake 1.0-only and 1.1 controllers.

- [ ] **AC1. Negotiation and fallback.**
  - A 1.1 fake is read at 1.1 and validated against `snapshotV1_1`.
  - A 1.0-only fake that answers `invalid-request`, as Nanoleaf and the local controller host do today, gets exactly one fallback read and a `1.0-only` verdict.
  - Further reads in the same epoch do not probe again.

issues.title: Links from other local apps into B.U.N.N.Y. are refused as Forbidden
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Clicking a link from another local app into B.U.N.N.Y. shows a Forbidden error. The owner hit it on 2026-09-28 during Hub #497 qualification: in the integrated preview `compose-20260928T173157Z-7ab0f8`, the wall page's **B.U.N.N.Y.** link (`http://127.0.0.1:36385/`, the paired Hub run) opened a page reading `{"error":{"code":"forbidden"}}`.

**Cause.** The Hub serves `/`, `/dashboard.js` and `/dashboard.css` only when `sameOrigin(req)` passes (`apps/hub/src/server.ts:279`). That check accepts `Sec-Fetch-Site` of `none` or `same-origin` only (`server.ts:166-168`), and has since trusted-loopback sign-in (#419, `f69d6f4`, 2026-09-25). A link from another loopback port (wall on 8765, Pixoo, a verification preview) is `same-site`, so the browser's navigation gets 403. The orchestrator reproduced it against the preview's Hub:

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| No `Sec-Fetch-*` headers (typed address) | 200 |
| `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` | 200 |
| `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site`, `Mode: navigate`, `Dest: document` (a link click) | 403 |
| The same navigation to the wall and Pixoo previews | 200 |

**Installed impact (inferred from code, not probed).** The installed wall's B.U.N.N.Y. link to `http://127.0.0.1:8788/` (codex-nanoleaf #191, `30f1e2e`, 2026-09-26) meets the same rule on the installed Hub, so it very likely fails the same way. The orchestrator did not contact the installed Hub to confirm.

**The verification did not catch it.** Hub #495's `integrated-lifecycle` asserts that the wall's B.U.N.N.Y. `href` equals the Hub run's origin, but never follows the link. The broken behavior passed, against the owner's rule that a broken behavior must produce a failed result.

## Smallest useful implementation

1. **Page route.** Admit a top-level document navigation from a same-site loopback page (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`, no `Origin`, Host still one of the loopback names). Keep every API route, the session route and the launch exchange as strict as today. The page already signs in only through a same-origin `POST` with `x-pixoo-request`, so the navigation itself grants nothing. Consider `frame-ancestors 'none'` or `X-Frame-Options: DENY` so the admitted page cannot be framed. This relaxes a #276/#419 security boundary, so it needs the owner's decision and a Standards review of the threat model: another local service can already open a tab to the Hub, and the change only stops refusing it.
2. **Verification.** Make `integrated-lifecycle` click the wall's B.U.N.N.Y. link and assert that the Hub dashboard loads and signs in. Add the same for the Hub's Places link into the wall. Show the step failing on today's Hub before the fix.

## Observable acceptance

- Clicking B.U.N.N.Y. on the wall, installed or preview, opens the signed-in dashboard.
- A cross-site navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`) and every API request from another origin are still refused, with tests.
- The integrated step fails on the pre-fix Hub and passes after.
- Installation and a live check of the installed wall's link are separate, under the owner's installation request.

## Evidence

The owner's report and the orchestrator's reproduction during Hub #497 qualification.

issues.title: Keep a composed consumer's lease and thaw record truthful around the safety thaw
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The composition's safety thaw (Hub #495, PR #556) arms `app-verify-<run-id>-thaw.timer` before every freeze, because systemd 259 refuses to stop a frozen unit. The final reviews of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/556 found three edges around it. `doctor` reports each one as `stale` or leaves it harmless, and `stop` cleans up.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **A lease that ends during a freeze (S18, P-S12).** The one-shot lease timer fires while the consumer is frozen. systemd refuses the stop, and the timer is gone. After the thaw, the consumer runs with no lease. The reviewer reproduced this with `--lease 1` and an orchestrator killed mid-freeze. Either refuse a freeze when the target's remaining lease is shorter than `--thaw-after` plus a margin, or have the safety thaw also stop a unit whose `expiresAt` has passed. Then qualify the sentence in `docs/app-verification.md` that says the lease can still stop the consumer.
- **Who thawed the unit (S19, P-S11).** If the safety timer thaws first, the step's `thaw` still records `thawedBy: 'step'` with the current time. Read `FreezerState` before thawing: if the unit is already running, record `thawedBy: 'safety-timer'` and fail the injection with a problem. Also raise the `--thaw-after` floor from 10 s to above the loss step's worst-case frozen window, for example 60 s. The normal window is about 8 s, and the step allows 20 s for the stale mark.
- **A prompt stop leaves the thaw timer (S20).** After an orchestrator died mid-freeze, `stop` reports each run clean while the thaw timer and service stay loaded until they fire against a gone unit. Disarm the safety thaw for every service in `stopRuns`.

## Observable acceptance

- A freeze that would outlast the lease is refused, or the consumer is stopped once its lease has passed. A test covers it.
- An early safety thaw is recorded as such and fails the injection.
- After `stop`, no thaw timer of the composition remains.

## Evidence

The round 4 Standards review (probes H to K) and Specification review on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/556.

## Work assessment

Assessment for #341, 2026-09-28. Only previously missing ratings are added; scope, readiness and labels remain unchanged.

issues.title: Give an unbuilt verify wrapper a JSON result and hand off clickable proof links
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Hub #497 qualification sessions verified the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo apps from fresh worktrees. Two small gaps showed up in the Hub verification wrapper and in the handoff guidance.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **An unbuilt wrapper gives no JSON result.** In a fresh worktree after `npm ci` but before `npm run build`, `npm run -s verify -- start …` crashed with Node's `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `node_modules/@jimmie-potts/app-verify/dist/index.js`. It exited 1 with a stack trace and no JSON line, instead of the contract's `unavailable` result (exit 3) naming the missing build. `scripts/verify.mjs` (or the wrapper the `verify` script runs) should check that the core is built and print one JSON result saying to run `npm run build`.
- **Clickable proof links in the handoff.** The owner selected read-only HTTP links on the preview’s existing loopback origin, plus chat attachments where supported (2026-09-29). Serve the run’s frozen `verified/` proof outside the application’s routes, preserve its checksums, and name the links in the handoff. The caller walkthrough in `docs/app-verification.md` ("Agent: verify, retain proof, hand off") should show this approach. A filesystem path or `file://` link alone is not sufficient; the later owner report established that those links were not reliably accessible.

## Observable acceptance

- An unbuilt checkout's `verify start` prints one JSON line with state `unavailable` and exits 3.
- After handoff, frozen screenshots and videos are available through read-only `http://127.0.0.1:<preview-port>/…` links on the existing preview origin. The handoff and caller walkthrough name those links and attach files when the chat client supports it.
- Serving proof preserves the frozen set’s checksums. Only the selected run’s frozen proof is exposed: traversal, symlinks, mutations, live/private files and later captures are refused. Existing application routes retain their behavior.

issues.title: Reset a composed verification preview to its paired starting state
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A composed Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo preview (#495) can hand off, extend, stop, expire and restart as one unit, but it cannot reset. The composition's `handoff` never passes `--reset`: reseeding the Hub run on its own would restart the one agent-state owner under the paired consumers. Their feeds would then read a revision that went backwards, and the Hub's controller readings would be mid-flight.

Add an aggregate reset that returns all three runs to their paired starting state, preserving each run's ownership and retained evidence.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `verify:compose -- handoff <id> --reset` (and/or `reset <id>`) reseeds in a safe order:
  1. Stop the consumers' Hub polling. The consumers stay up.
  2. Reseed the Hub `integrated`, keeping its port and pairing inputs.
  3. Reseed each consumer `hub-paired`, so its feed resets against the new owner.
  4. Then check composition readiness again.
- Token files stay in place and are never printed. A failure at any step leaves a truthful per-service state, and `stop` can still clean up.

## Required consumer prerequisites

The accepted reset ordering needs a live polling pause in each paired consumer. Deliver those changes in their owning repositories, then pin their accepted merged revisions here, as #490 requires:

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/201 — pause and drain the disposable paired wall feed while its map/controller stay responsive.
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/127 — gate and drain the disposable paired Pixoo feed, including timer and read-triggered requests.

Both pauses must acknowledge drained requests before the Hub owner reseeds. After the owner reset succeeds, each consumer seed consumes a matching release authorization after its old unit stops and before the fresh process launches. This lets the new feed pass readiness without letting the old consumer observe a regressed owner. Ports, token files and frozen proof remain preserved. Aggregate operations must serialize and partial failures remain stoppable.

The active repair coordinator retains ownership. These are source-only prerequisites for the existing consumers-stay-up criterion; installed behavior and devices remain outside scope. Hub implementation waits for accepted consumer revisions; independent preparation can proceed.

## Observable acceptance

- After a reset, the Hub, wall and Pixoo pages show the scenario's initial state. Composition readiness passes, with feeds current at the new owner's revision.
- A reset that fails midway reports the failing service and leaves the composition stoppable.
- Captures from before the reset stay in the frozen proof, unchanged.

## Evidence

The #495 review on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/556 (Specification P-S5): the #495 acceptance lists aggregate reset, and the PR defers it for the reason above.

## Work assessment

Assessment for #341, 2026-09-28. Only previously missing ratings are added; scope, readiness and labels remain unchanged.

- **Complexity: high.** Reset coordinates owner and consumer state, polling, readiness and retained proof.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Partial reset and recovery need checks across real service boundaries.
- **Impact: medium.** Failure can leave a synthetic preview inconsistent or lose its retained proof.

issues.title: Define epic-based Guide records and reusable component contracts
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The public Guide and later local Ask the Guide use one versioned dataset and one reusable component catalog for the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repositories. GitHub issues, native relationships and the approved Project fields own the facts. This revision implements the owner's browser-first, epic-based rebuild decision; it replaces the old requirement to preserve topic sub-guides and the existing page layout.

## Smallest useful implementation

Define the next records version and component catalog together, with schemas/types, a field-source dictionary, producer/consumer responsibilities, compatibility rules and fixtures. Keep the approved `guide-records/1.0` artifacts unchanged until their consumers are retired. Name the new version from its actual compatibility impact; do not assume an incompatible revision is a minor release.

An explicit epic convention identifies epics; native parent/sub-issue links own membership. Specify how to resolve an issue's nearest containing epic, nested groups, deeper ancestry, cross-repository parents, unresolved parents and standalone work. A parent is not automatically an epic. Stable record IDs are separate from component instance IDs. Source closure reason, workflow, blockers, Phase, Commitment and unknown evidence stay distinct. There is one canonical issue record and primary placement even when several views display it.

The catalog defines reusable UI component inputs: an issue card accepts any issue kind through one normalized record, and an epic component accepts epic data and child references, composing the same issue cards or compact rows. Include dependencies, task briefs and board/phase presentation. Components receive data and view configuration; they do not fetch GitHub, parse issue bodies or call a model. The ordinary browser and later Ask use the same implementations, not separately built lookalikes. A deterministic composed fixture establishes the inputs before Jev exists.

When a user submits a request, later Jev selects existing record references and allowed component kinds; code validates the result and the shared renderer displays the corresponding cards and epic groups. Keep canonical facts in records and trusted links in code. Contract the data, component inputs, reference resolution, bounds and typed reason/evidence validation; leave spacing, styling and routine layout choices to the renderer. Reject arbitrary model-authored HTML, code, URLs and invented facts. Motion and interactive composition beyond this demonstrator remain later work.

Recently done means issues currently closed as completed within the seven days ending at the dataset's as-of time, using UTC timestamps. The collector must include that closed-issue slice as well as open issues and older parent/dependency records required for resolution. The seven-day display window must not prune required ancestry or dependency evidence. Specify the time boundary and fixtures; this is not a full historical archive.

Required accepted baseline: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/543. Consumers include https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/540, followed by the existing Ask work. This issue's new definitions require their own approval and source acceptance before consumers adopt them.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Owner instruction, 2026-09-30: UI changes no longer require human UI approval anywhere in this project, including Hub and Ask. This decision is effective now; #657 aligns source instructions and preflight. Contract approval in this issue remains required, as do independent review, applicable CI and UI verification for implementing consumers.

Keep complete pagination, identity, freshness, dependency and public-projection rules. Define the publication boundary explicitly: an incomplete required issue inventory blocks a new dataset; unavailable optional enrichment does not. Normalize missing/stale recommendations, malformed optional story sections and unavailable Project data to explicit gaps while keeping the issue browsable. Required-field/schema failures and unsafe public projection remain fatal. Specify completeness per collection, including the seven-day completion slice and required references; an unresolved reference allowed by the schema remains unknown and withholds dependent claims. A permitted cached Project snapshot keeps its original observation time and completeness, separate from the new issue collection/build time.

Separate the facts "no open native blocker" and "required outcome accepted." A closed prerequisite is not sufficient acceptance evidence. Owner decision at delivery (2026-09-30, recorded in the archived design): a prerequisite closed as completed accepts that issue's own stated scope; any further required gate is a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent, and not-planned, duplicate or unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until reconciled. A not-planned/cancelled/duplicate prerequisite requires reconciliation: an accepted replacement satisfying the same outcome, or an explicitly authorized change to the dependent scope. Missing/contradictory evidence withholds readiness. Define how existing tracker evidence establishes each required gate without introducing a new hand-maintained Guide ledger; keep source, installed/client and physical acceptance distinct.

Declare which arrays are unordered sets and which preserve meaningful order. Canonicalization may normalize issue enumeration, set membership and API pagination order; it must preserve owner-ordered Project phases and meaningful presentation sequences in their owning identities. Separate content identity from collection time and deployment release identity.

Define a release binding for pages, records, catalog and assets, with schema versions and generator provenance. Specify how consumers pin a compatible release, handle an unsupported records version and reject mixed-release input or obsolete replies. An already-open browser or older Hub must retain a validated compatible view or show an explicit update/unavailable state, without mixing releases or invoking Jev with unsupported data. #317 owns deployment ordering; #511 and #512 implement the consumer behavior. Missing required evidence prevents a readiness claim; unknown dependencies are not an empty list. Literal issue text remains untrusted data. Only explicitly allowed public planning data and the submitted question may reach a model. Credentials, private Project content and runtime/session data remain excluded. Ordinary browsing and generic Explain/Plan/Implement/Review briefs require no inference or current model recommendation.

Accepted history: #543 delivered `guide-records/1.0` in [PR #581](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/581), with [owner approval](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/543#issuecomment-5894188626). Its approved SHA-256 is `f2eea2bf8a737bbe3b5542ffbf2c04961e4564dd8fe27326464726f44a00e34d`. That approval does not approve this changed definition.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] AC1: The dictionary and schemas resolve epic membership, deeper ancestry, standalone work, native blockers, closure reasons and Project-owned values without duplicate authority. Positive and negative fixtures cover cross-repository links, unavailable ancestors, cycles, missing fields and version mismatch.
- [x] AC2: Ordinary and composed examples resolve the same component inputs and canonical identities, including one issue-card shape across issue kinds and an epic component containing child references. The #511 renderer must reuse actual implementations. Fixtures reject unknown references, duplicate instance IDs, excessive bounds, unsupported components and unsupported reason evidence. Seven-day Recently done fixtures cover the time boundary, reopened/not-planned issues and older records still required for parent/dependency resolution.
- [x] AC3: Public projection and literal rendering tests exclude credentials/unapproved data and preserve unknown or incomplete evidence. Generic briefs remain valid when an execution recommendation is absent or stale.
- [x] AC4: A complete reviewable candidate records its version, canonical artifacts, commit and digest. Jimmie's explicit approval names that candidate; no consumer adopts it before approval and merged-content readback. Changed normative definitions require renewed approval under the rules currently in force.
- [x] AC5: Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, relevant contract fixtures, workflow checks and all applicable source CI. Normal independent reviews and merged-main checks pass. Record the compatibility/migration obligations for both old and new consumers.

- [x] AC6: Collection/provenance fixtures distinguish fatal inventory truncation from missing recommendations, malformed optional sections, denied/partial Project reads and verified-empty Project data. Allowed fallback keeps all issues browsable and exposes the Project snapshot's actual age; invalid required records and unsafe public projection still fail validation.
- [x] AC7: Readiness fixtures distinguish completed-and-accepted prerequisites, completed-but-missing-required-acceptance, not-planned/cancelled closure, duplicates with unresolved or accepted replacements, reopened prerequisites and unknown closure reasons. No closed state or absence of open blockers silently proves a required outcome.
- [x] AC8: Identity fixtures prove that permutations of issue enumeration/set-valued relationships or API pages leave content identity unchanged, while reversing owner-ordered phases or another declared meaningful sequence changes its owning identity. Timestamp/release changes follow their separately documented rules.
- [x] AC9: Compatibility fixtures cover a supported pinned release, mixed page/data/catalog identities, an unsupported records version, an old client and a deployment during an outstanding request. Document safe retained-view/update behavior and rejection before model invocation; #511/#512/#317 supply browser and deployment evidence.

Delivery target: source-only contract definitions, specification and fixtures. Planned validation includes the new contract tests, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow` and affected checks in docs/development.md; commands are not executed by this planning update.

## Candidate and ownership

Delivered through [PR #645](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/645), squash-merged as `a0bb44ababf9cb30a6ee6df7ff14b2e5ee1d7949` on 2026-10-01 from reviewed head `155c1808c9dea916cf7389cdda870ebbe9782e88`. The owner approved bundle digest `78b941945fb2782e2033a5773c1ca978b70226d38e9f6969a3055315dd57a09b` ([renewed receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/545#issuecomment-5934967530)) after final review round 1 corrected the first approved candidate ([first receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/545#issuecomment-5924430458)). The merged files recompute the same digest. The definitions are `guide-records/2.0`, `guide-views/1.0` and `guide-release/1.0` in `docs/work-guide/contracts/epic-guide/` and `openspec/specs/epic-guide/spec.md`; `guide-records/1.0` is unchanged.

## Meaningful deferrals

No renderer, deployment, Jev endpoint, live model trial, generic widget platform or device operation. Broader policy changes in Hub #542 and agent-skills #87 remain separate. This issue does not wait for that automation.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium; impact medium. Ready for bounded candidate definition after the existing writer handoff; consumer adoption is blocked on this issue's own approval and source acceptance. Scope fits one shared browser boundary rather than separate tickets for each internal helper. Alignment: current #543 approval, #645 candidate, #511/#540 consumer seams, architecture, SDLC and Guide conventions. The added failure, acceptance, identity and compatibility cases remain within this contract definition; settle their evidence sources and fixtures before consumer adoption. Consumers include https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/540, followed by the existing Ask work. This issue's new definitions require their own approval and source acceptance before consumers adopt them.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
Owner instruction, 2026-09-30: UI changes no longer require human UI approval anywhere in this project, including Hub and Ask. This decision is effective now; #657 aligns source instructions and preflight. Contract approval in this issue remains required, as do independent review, applicable CI and UI verification for implementing consumers.

Keep complete pagination, identity, freshness, dependency and public-projection rules. Define the publication boundary explicitly: an incomplete required issue inventory blocks a new dataset; unavailable optional enrichment does not. Normalize missing/stale recommendations, malformed optional story sections and unavailable Project data to explicit gaps while keeping the issue browsable. Required-field/schema failures and unsafe public projection remain fatal. Specify completeness per collection, including the seven-day completion slice and required references; an unresolved reference allowed by the schema remains unknown and withholds dependent claims. A permitted cached Project snapshot keeps its original observation time and completeness, separate from the new issue collection/build time.

Separate the facts "no open native blocker" and "required outcome accepted." A closed prerequisite is not sufficient acceptance evidence. Owner decision at delivery (2026-09-30, recorded in the archived design): a prerequisite closed as completed accepts that issue's own stated scope; any further required gate is a separate issue that natively blocks the dependent, and not-planned, duplicate or unknown-reason closures withhold readiness until reconciled. A not-planned/cancelled/duplicate prerequisite requires reconciliation: an accepted replacement satisfying the same outcome, or an explicitly authorized change to the dependent scope. Missing/contradictory evidence withholds readiness. Define how existing tracker evidence establishes each required gate without introducing a new hand-maintained Guide ledger; keep source, installed/client and physical acceptance distinct.

Declare which arrays are unordered sets and which preserve meaningful order. Canonicalization may normalize issue enumeration, set membership and API pagination order; it must preserve owner-ordered Project phases and meaningful presentation sequences in their owning identities. Separate content identity from collection time and deployment release identity.

Define a release binding for pages, records, catalog and assets, with schema versions and generator provenance. Specify how consumers pin a compatible release, handle an unsupported records version and reject mixed-release input or obsolete replies. An already-open browser or older Hub must retain a validated compatible view or show an explicit update/unavailable state, without mixing releases or invoking Jev with unsupported data. #317 owns deployment ordering; #511 and #512 implement the consumer behavior. Missing required evidence prevents a readiness claim; unknown dependencies are not an empty list. Literal issue text remains untrusted data. Only explicitly allowed public planning data and the submitted question may reach a model. Credentials, private Project content and runtime/session data remain excluded. Ordinary browsing and generic Explain/Plan/Implement/Review briefs require no inference or current model recommendation.

Accepted history: #543 delivered `guide-records/1.0` in [PR #581](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/581), with [owner approval](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/543#issuecomment-5894188626). Its approved SHA-256 is `f2eea2bf8a737bbe3b5542ffbf2c04961e4564dd8fe27326464726f44a00e34d`. That approval does not approve this changed definition.

issues.title: Contract: Define guide issue and sub-guide records
issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509. Dedicated contract definition and approval work; this backlog publication does not approve the contract or start implementation.

## Outcome and real setup

Define and obtain human approval for the guide issue and sub-guide records boundary used by Ask the guide. One owner, the existing Hub and the three-repository guide are the supported setup.

## Smallest useful implementation

Define a small versioned, validated record shape for the guide renderer and composer, with a field-source dictionary: exact source/API or authored section, type, required/optional status, permitted values, update owner, precedence, freshness and missing/conflicting-value behavior. Reuse existing parsers and source rules. Jev receives an application-built projection of these records; it does not browse GitHub, infer the issue format or become the data authority.

| Data | Authoritative source and rule to define |
| --- | --- |
| Identity and basic facts | Native GitHub repository/issue identity, URL, title, body, state, closure reason and timestamps. Preserve identity across every view. |
| Workflow and descriptive tags | Native labels, interpreted by the SDLC and guide status rules: one workflow status on open delivery work; blocked/deferred and descriptive labels stay separate. Conflicting or absent status is reported, not guessed as ready. Explicit priority is distinct from model relevance. |
| Story content | The five feature-template sections: outcome/setup, implementation, protections, acceptance/evidence and deferrals. Document supported legacy heading aliases and parse provenance. A placeholder is not required to pretend it has implementation-ready acceptance. |
| Guide placement and ideas | Existing strict Guide fields: Topic, Note, Workaround, Highlight and Extends. Keep idea placement separate from workflow state and Extends separate from prerequisites. |
| Relationships | Native parent/sub-issue and blocked-by records. Compute inverse dependents and transitive paths in code, with pagination/completeness evidence. Related links or dependency-like prose do not silently become native blockers. |
| Sub-guides | Authored topic/track/section IDs, membership references, outcomes and next-step prose from the existing guide inputs, with their own source revision/date. |
| Optional planning/evidence | Existing assessment, execution recommendation and delivery/closeout records only through their defined parsers or explicit source links. Missing, outdated or unsupported records stay visibly unknown; closure does not prove installation. |
| Access and freshness | Per-repository fetch/snapshot time, issue update time, independent dependency freshness/completeness, schema version and source references. Specify the read-only adapter/interface the renderer and protected endpoint consume. |

Define which fields each operation requires: ordinary browsing, semantic discovery, prerequisite answers and ready-work recommendations need different evidence. Missing optional metadata must not erase an issue from the full guide. Missing required evidence prevents the affected recommendation/claim, with an explanation and source link.

Use the current topic vocabulary and native labels first. Add a controlled capability/domain field only if representative queries demonstrate a gap; define its allowed values and editing/validation path before use. Do not create one-off Jev tags or require guessed model summaries as authoritative fields.

Document how to maintain this contract in the existing story template/guide maintenance guidance during delivery. New stories and subsequent refreshes must use the same validation. Existing source references: [story template](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.yml), [SDLC labels](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299/docs/sdlc.md), and [Guide metadata](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299/docs/work-guide/README.md#guide-sections).

The data contract provides the field dictionary and maintenance requirements. #511 implements adapters, runs the complete inventory audit and wires repeatable data checks into refresh/rendering. This issue does not bulk-edit existing stories.

Provide a small canonical schema/type in the owning source/specification, a field-ownership dictionary, version/compatibility checks, one successful example and relevant invalid, unknown, stale and failure fixtures. Record exact producer and consumer responsibilities. No separate service, generic schema framework or new package is required. Cross-interface examples share stable record and catalog references rather than copying facts.

Required inputs: none for drafting this root contract. Downstream consumers: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/511, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/512, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/513, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/516. These relationships are native blocked-by links. Independent draft exploration may happen together; referenced definitions must be approved and delivered before this issue is accepted.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub owns work facts and native relationships; authored sub-guides retain dates/owners. Unknown evidence is not zero, success, freshness or readiness. Code computes graph facts and exact counts. Only the submitted question and allowlisted public planning data cross the Jev boundary. No agent prompts/transcripts, private paths, credentials, GitHub writes or device commands. The complete normal guide remains available without inference.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] The schema/type and field dictionary cover the boundary above, its owners, valid values, required/optional fields, source/version checks and missing/conflicting-data behavior.
- [x] Positive and negative fixtures exercise the stated boundary; a reviewer can trace input → validation → allowed output without filling gaps from model guesses.
- [x] Trace the normal guide → explicit query → validated composed view → refinement → Full guide across the referenced contracts. Include timeout, missing data, source/catalog mismatch, late responses after reset and reduced-motion equivalence where relevant. Use fake-provider examples; do not claim live model quality.
- [x] The human approval record binds the exact reviewed definition. Approval is pending until Jimmie explicitly approves it; changed definitions require renewed approval.
- [x] Normal source review and applicable CI pass, canonical merged artifacts match the approved content, and dependency/approval/source readback is recorded before closure and consumer unblock.

Delivery target: source-only definition, specification and fixtures. At pickup use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed product contracts and the owning guide/Hub plus shared checks in docs/development.md. Contract-only delivery does not implement consumers, install services, publish the guide or authorize paid inference.

## Human approval

**Owner:** Jimmie.
**Status:** Approved by Jimmie in the owner conversation at `2026-09-29T16:17:20.893Z`, with the explicit statement “Approved.” responding to this exact candidate/digest. [Approval receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/543#issuecomment-5894188626). Source delivery is complete in PR https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/581 at `69c02b5bd994ff4dfb5bf33b037d5db274178aa3`. Both independent review axes and all seven merged-main checks passed; the merged definition matches the approved content digest.

**Candidate commit:** `1d1087842417edb2d7ede8d24ab250e41986fab4`.
**Definition and examples:** [canonical contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/1d1087842417edb2d7ede8d24ab250e41986fab4/docs/work-guide/contracts/README.md).
**Content SHA-256:** `f2eea2bf8a737bbe3b5542ffbf2c04961e4564dd8fe27326464726f44a00e34d`.
**OpenSpec:** [gh-543-guide-records](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/1d1087842417edb2d7ede8d24ab250e41986fab4/openspec/changes/gh-543-guide-records).

Prepare the complete proposed definition and fixtures in a reviewable draft/PR before requesting approval. Record the contract issue, canonical artifact path, version, candidate commit and content digest, approver, explicit approval statement, timestamp and durable evidence link. Approval must come from the human owner through a verified channel; an agent-authored comment under shared credentials, issue closure, label, CI result, silence or approval of this backlog plan is insufficient.

Do not merge/adopt this contract or implement dependent behavior against it until the owner approves that exact candidate. Drafting and fixture exploration may proceed. A changed definition invalidates approval and requires renewed approval; an unchanged, already approved version can be reused with its evidence. Follow normal independent review and CI gates after approval. Close only after the approved definition is merged, merged content matches the approved digest, applicable main checks pass, and approval/source evidence is read back. Consumers remain blocked until this acceptance is complete. Contract approval applies to guide contracts even though guide UI itself is exempt from human UI approval.

## Meaningful deferrals

Saved/shared views, general widget APIs, voice/LangGraph handoff, external assets and device moments remain prospective work under #509. Shared policy automation is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/87 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542; drafting these Jev contracts does not wait for that automation, but their explicit human approval and source gates already apply procedurally.

## Assessment

Planning, 2026-09-26; Hub baseline 4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299. Complexity medium; uncertainty medium until examples and consumer seams agree; impact medium for contract correctness. Source delivery completed on 2026-09-29 in PR #581; exact-definition approval, adoption, independent review and merged-main CI are verified. Reassess at pickup or when definitions, hosting or data-sharing scope change.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Define guide issue and sub-guide records as an independently tracked, human-approved prerequisite for Ask the guide.
**Highlight:** decision, Approved guide-records/1.0 contract delivered with schema, source rules and validated examples.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: Claude Code on Opus at high effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at medium reasoning. Use the host prompt below; the issue's readiness and authority gates still apply.
**Work surface:** Backend

issues.title: Maintain GitHub Project state during the B.U.N.N.Y. SDLC
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Codex and Claude can keep the approved portfolio Project accurate during authorized planning and delivery without asking the owner to edit every card manually.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required inputs: the accepted rules from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536 and verified Project/field identities from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/537. Update Hub's existing SDLC instructions and their applicable references using writing-for-agents. Keep one project-owned policy; shared agent-skills remain generic and device repositories retain their own instructions. Do not silently modify sibling repositories or central skills. Coordinate shared docs/sdlc.md and instruction edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542, which owns the separate contract-approval policy. This is shared-file coordination, not a new prerequisite; preserve the current accepted gates and re-read both scopes at pickup.

Define the integration points: planning adds authorized selected issues and records approved Phase and Commitment values; implementation reflects the actual issue status; review reflects the actual review state; closeout projects completion only after the existing acceptance, independent review, applicable merged-revision CI and tracker-readback gates. Preserve Completed versus Closed/Not planned and source versus installation/physical acceptance. Epics close only against their accepted required-child and outcome criteria.

Specify field ownership and a bounded read/compare/write/readback procedure using existing GitHub CLI/API tools. Issue labels/native state own workflow; the only custom Project planning fields are Phase and Commitment. The owner selects those values; a child's Phase is a projection of its native parent, and standalone work stays blank until explicitly assigned. No Priority or Size field is in the pilot, and the procedure must not invent a priority label or guide ledger. The built-in Project Status is a projection of native workflow labels and closure, not authority to change them. On conflict, report the discrepancy and reconcile only within explicit field authority.

The procedure names allowed repositories, Project identity, mutation scope, an explicit no-op comparison, unrelated-field preservation, and timeout recovery by authoritative readback before retry. A missing scope, partial read or concurrent change leaves Project maintenance pending and visible; it must not fabricate Done, repeat ambiguous creates, or erase independent evidence that source delivery completed. Project maintenance itself never authorizes a feature, changes the owner's phase or commitment choices or exit criteria, grants credentials or bypasses gates.

Separate in-session maintenance from between-session automation. Use manual agent-driven updates first; no new daemon, scheduler, workflow token or synchronization framework in this story. Document event-triggered triage and replenishment when capacity opens, and outcome reviews at material learning, owner selection changes or phase entry/exit. Optional check-in reminders do not impose a delivery timebox. Link to the live Project rather than copying issue lists into docs. Maintain parent-derived phase membership under #536; a Project phase move never changes native prerequisites or drops unfinished acceptance. Require an explicit recorded proceed/hold/revise/stop decision at phase review, proportionate to the selected outcome.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

issues.title: Set up a cross-repository GitHub Project and seed the planning pilot
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner can inspect one GitHub Project across Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo and find the approved phase outcomes and selected work without maintaining a second backlog.

## Smallest useful implementation

Required input: the accepted field/visibility/selection contract from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536. First inspect existing Projects and reuse a matching one. Create a single user-owned Project only if no appropriate Project exists. Default to private owner-only visibility unless the accepted contract explicitly selects otherwise. Configure only the approved Phase and Commitment (Now/Next/Later/Ideas) custom planning fields; reuse native issue/parent/repository data. Link the authoritative phase definitions and entry/exit evidence from the Project description/README. Follow #536 for parent-derived story phase membership and explicit standalone/shared-work handling; do not duplicate issues to group them.

Create the five intended views: Phase map (epics grouped by outcome phase, with entry/exit references), Now / Next (committed work and ordered candidates, with Later accessible by filter), Delivery board (Now stories and projected workflow), Decisions and acceptance, and Ideas. Verify API support for each setting; use an authorized browser step for unsupported view settings and report any remaining manual operation truthfully. Use date-free table or board grouping for the phase map; a timeline layout is not required. Missing phase assignment remains visible. No invented date ranges, mandatory iteration field or calendar-based promotion is allowed.

Seed #498 and #509 plus their required children, and the owner-selected Nanoleaf #162 and Pixoo #96 examples, under https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536. Only #543 receives Commitment `Now`; #509 receives the current Phase; #498 and its children, Nanoleaf #162 and Pixoo #96 remain unselected with blank Phase and Commitment. #545 then #544 is a preferred order, not a `Next` assignment while blocked. This is membership, not automatic commitment: leave unselected ideas out of the delivery queue. Preserve cross-repository ownership, unrelated fields, assignees and existing parent relationships. Capture stable Project/field/item identities for later SDLC maintenance. Do not create duplicated draft issues for existing repository issues.

Project access was rechecked during the archival sweep on 2026-09-27 UTC: `gh project list --owner jimmie-potts` succeeded and returned zero Projects; the current authentication reports the `project` scope. The earlier missing-scope blocker is resolved for reading. Creation and field mutation have not been exercised, and no Project was configured by this task. Recheck effective access at pickup; request an authorization flow only if access is actually missing then. Setup still waits for the accepted planning decisions in #536.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep credentials outside Git, browser payloads and receipts. No public exposure, mass import, unrelated Project edits or automatic priority changes. Workflow fields reflect native status labels and closure reason; conflicting evidence is visible rather than overwritten. Disabling or removing the pilot Project must not delete its issues or their native relationships. GitHub view changes fall outside the guide-only UI exemption: retain applicable explicit current-candidate human UI approval.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] AC1: Exactly one selected Project has the intended owner, visibility, repository scope and fields. Evidence: authoritative API readback of identity and settings, with an existing-project search receipt and no duplicate creation.
- [x] AC2: The five views answer their named questions. Evidence: inspect filters/grouping/order in the live UI, including narrow-screen access where GitHub supports it; record any unavailable configuration instead of claiming it exists. Owner approves the current candidate.
- [x] AC3: Pilot membership and field values match https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536. Evidence: enumerate item IDs and linked issue URLs; verify no duplicate items, no accidental selection of optional ideas, correct parent-derived phase assignments and visible unassigned work, and a before/after comparison preserving unrelated fields and native issue ownership.
- [x] AC4: Repeat setup/reconciliation is a no-op for correct existing data. Evidence: a second read/compare identifies zero unintended changes; document how to remove only pilot membership/fields created by this work without deleting issues.
- [x] AC5: Access and visibility are verified without revealing secrets. Evidence: authenticated readback and an appropriate unauthenticated visibility check; distinguish configured Project access from future guide export permission.

Delivery target: live GitHub Project configuration and verified tracker membership. No product code, runtime installation or device acceptance. This work cannot complete on API acknowledgments alone. Any supporting repository changes require the normal PR/review/CI process; pure external configuration has no fabricated source revision or CI result.

## Meaningful deferrals

Do not migrate all 310 observed open issues or all personal repositories. Retain existing issue lists and expand only after the pilot. Built-in automations and scheduled workflows are deferred until a concrete recurring manual failure warrants them; manual SDLC updates are the initial alternative. No dependency on the Jev implementation or a custom guide board.

## Accepted setup input — 2026-09-27 UTC

The owner authorized Project creation using the [#536 decision record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/536) and the two-field pilot above. This authorization covers the private Project, its five planned views and bounded membership/field setup; it does not approve the current UI candidate before it exists or authorize product implementation, installation, publication or device actions. Read back the configured candidate, then obtain explicit owner approval of that candidate before #537 acceptance.

## Live setup receipt — 2026-09-27 UTC

The owner approved setup after #536 was accepted. The preflight search returned zero Projects; created one private user-owned Project, [B.U.N.N.Y. Portfolio](https://github.com/users/jimmie-potts/projects/1), number `1`, ID `PVT_kwHOAu24Wc4Bkz2N`. Authenticated readback reports `public:false`, owner `jimmie-potts`, `closed:false`, 28 items and 15 total fields. Thirteen are GitHub built-ins; only `Phase` (`PVTSSF_lAHOAu24Wc4Bkz2NzhjjE0g`) and `Commitment` (`PVTSSF_lAHOAu24Wc4Bkz2NzhjjE04`) are custom planning fields. Neither custom field has a default. Unauthenticated GET of the Project URL returned HTTP 404. The private Project is not authority to export its contents through the guide.

The Phase options are Ask the guide and Development activity at a glance. The Commitment options are Now, Next, Later and Ideas. The Project README links the accepted planning record and phase entry/exit sources. The 15 #509 family items project Ask the guide; #509 is the authoritative epic assignment, and its 14 child values are derived display values. #498 and ten required children plus Nanoleaf #162 and Pixoo #96 have blank Phase and Commitment. Only #543 is Now. There are no Next, Later or Ideas assignments. The built-in Status field was renamed to Backlog/Ready/In progress/Review/Done; its current 28 values were compared with native `status:*` labels, including Ready on #543, Nanoleaf #162 and Pixoo #96. Native labels, blocked relationships and issue closure remain authoritative.

The five saved view readbacks are: `Phase map` (#1, table, `is:issue`, grouped by Phase); `Now / Next` (#2, table, `commitment:Now,Next`, grouped by Commitment); `Delivery board` (#3, board, `commitment:Now`, columns by built-in Status); `Decisions and acceptance` (#4, table, `is:issue` with parent, progress, labels and closed fields); and `Ideas` (#5, table, `commitment:Ideas`, currently empty). Visible fields, filters and grouping were read back through GraphQL after the owner saved the UI configuration. Next has no assigned candidate, so no within-Next order is applicable. The owner stated that they inspected all five saved views and approved the current layout on 2026-09-27. A separate owner-provided phone screenshot verifies narrow-screen `Now / Next` legibility. GitHub's authenticated browser control was unavailable to this agent (`sandboxCwd is not a local file URI`), so direct agent visual inspection of the other views is not claimed; owner inspection and API readback provide the combined AC2 evidence.

A second read/compare found exactly 28 unique expected issue URLs, the selected Phase/Commitment values, zero unexpected idea items, and zero needed item/field edits. No repository issue identity, owner, parent link, assignee or source file was edited by Project setup. For rollback, remove only these 28 Project items and the two custom fields or delete this single Project after owner authorization; do not delete the linked repository issues or native relationships. The Status field is built-in and was configured only inside this Project.

### Owner-provided mobile view observation — 2026-09-27

The owner supplied a screenshot of GitHub's mobile `Now / Next` view. It visibly renders the Project title and one #543 card with `Status: Ready`, native `status:ready` label, Hub repository, `Phase: Ask the guide`, and `Commitment: Now`. This supports narrow-screen access and value legibility for this one view. The screenshot alone does not establish saved grouping or the behavior of the other views; the later saved-view readback and owner inspection/approval above supply those separate checks.
