issues.title: Define outcome phases and Now/Next/Later portfolio planning rules
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Give one owner a capability direction expressed as outcome phases and a small selected queue across Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo. This is a bounded planning/decision task, ready to start discovery; it does not select the product phases or make their implementation ready by itself. Other repositories join only when named by the owner.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use the existing GitHub issues and guide topics. Propose a few named outcome phases, detail the current phase, outline the next plausible phase and leave later possibilities coarse. Maintain a small ordered queue of ready issues. Phases have no mandatory start/end dates or elapsed-time gates. Reuse the assistant epic https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/498 and Jev epic https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509 as pilot examples, not automatic priority commitments.

Settle a concise planning contract in this issue's accepted decision record: themes are durable areas; epics are bounded outcomes; stories are independently verifiable increments; small implementation steps remain checklists. Use native parent/sub-issue relationships for membership and native blocked-by for required inputs. Device work stays in its owning repository. Preserve the existing Guide topics rather than inventing a second category taxonomy.

Accepted pilot defaults: one portfolio Project; a Phase field and a Commitment field (Now/Next/Later/Ideas), with no Priority or Size field; one major active epic plus a small maintenance stream. Ready is feasibility; Now is selected work within available implementation, review and acceptance capacity. Next is the small ordered candidate queue, Later is a plausible direction, and Ideas are uncommitted possibilities. These are selection categories, not workflow states or time periods. Native issue state and status labels remain workflow authority; Project workflow state is a projection.

A phase describes an observable capability or user outcome, such as a trustworthy daily control experience, rather than a calendar period or a universal design/build/test stage. Define its intended benefit, required and optional epics, entry conditions, exit evidence, exclusions and next decision. Entry needs an accepted bounded scope, its actual inputs and available capacity. Exit needs the required outcomes and their declared acceptance evidence, with an explicit proceed, hold, revise or stop decision. Test and accept each increment as it is delivered; do not defer testing until a separate global phase.

Keep the hierarchy shallow: native epic → story → checklist remains the delivery structure. Phase is portfolio grouping, not another mandatory parent issue. Record phase definitions once in the Project description/README, linked to the accepted decision record and owning epics. Epic phase assignment is authoritative; stories derive it through their native parent, with an explicit rule for standalone/shared work. A shared prerequisite keeps one issue and one native parent; other consumers link to it instead of duplicating or reparenting it. Missing phase membership stays visible as unassigned. Phase ordering is preferred sequence unless a native prerequisite records a true required input.

An epic carries outcome, smallest useful release, required versus optional scope, acceptance evidence, phase membership and the event that triggers reassessment. A phase may contain several epics, and independent work can proceed across phases when its actual inputs and capacity permit. Splitting or revising a phase requires an explicit scope decision; it cannot silently discard unfinished required work. Dates remain useful for evidence freshness and genuine external deadlines, never as prerequisites to starting or completing a phase. No deadline field or dated roadmap is required for the pilot.

Replenish Now from Next when capacity opens after acceptance or an explicit stop decision. Reassess scope/order when a blocker, material learning, changed priority or phase exit warrants it; do not wait for a scheduled planning meeting. Optional reminders can prevent neglect, but they are not delivery gates. Keep later phases and ideas lightly specified. Refine #498 with separately recognizable release goals without rewriting its accepted source or installed-acceptance boundaries; #509's required delivery and contract children remain distinct from its optional ideas; read its live native hierarchy rather than relying on a fixed child count. Record proposed amendments for scoped later application, preserving existing native parents.

The owner-selected outcomes, exclusions, initial queue, capacity and visibility policy are recorded in the dated decision below. Default recommendation is an owner-only private Project; public guide export requires an explicit allowlist. No dates, effort estimates or commitments are inferred from issue age or model judgment.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

GitHub issues own scope, acceptance, prerequisites and delivery state. Portfolio selection does not authorize implementation, installation or devices. No parallel backlog, forced story rewriting, mass reprioritization or replacement of existing review/CI gates. Source delivery and usable installed outcomes remain separate measures.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] AC1: The owner has selected the initial phase outcomes, the current phase, a coarse next-phase direction, exclusions and capacity. Evidence: an explicit dated decision record with measurable benefit, entry/exit criteria and linked existing epics; unanswered choices remain open. No mandatory date ranges are introduced.
- [x] AC2: Every proposed field has one owner, allowed values, edit authority and missing/conflict behavior. Evidence: a compact mapping that distinguishes native issue facts, portfolio fields and dated guide prose; examples cover Ready-but-unselected, Now-but-blocked, deferred ideas and closed-not-completed.
- [x] AC3: Epic closure and progress rules preserve required versus optional children and source versus installed acceptance. Evidence: apply the rubric to #498 and #509; child percentages are not effort forecasts and a merged PR alone cannot close a story.
- [x] AC4: The pilot selection and event-triggered replenishment/review procedure are concrete. Evidence: named issue candidates, an agreed WIP limit and value/prerequisite/effort/uncertainty criteria; walk through acceptance freeing capacity, a blocked Now item, a priority change and a phase exit. A blocked item still consumes its agreed WIP slot unless explicitly stopped or re-scoped; no automatic overfilling. Preserve unknown estimates.
- [x] AC5: Phase grouping, commitment and workflow have separate owners and meanings. Evidence: trace an epic, a child, standalone maintenance, a shared prerequisite and an unassigned item; show that a later-phase assignment alone blocks nothing. Phase completion requires its own evidence, not every backlog idea or an elapsed period.

Delivery target: accepted planning/tracker record only. Initial investigation is read-only; record decisions and amend named existing issues only within the authority granted at that pickup. No repository code, Project configuration or account authentication changes. No executable product tests are claimed.

## Meaningful deferrals

No full-backlog migration or new issues for every idea: pilot a small selected set first; broaden only after the pilot review. No story points or forecasting service: use observable completed increments, blocked age and waiting-for-acceptance work; revisit only if actual planning questions remain unanswered. The setup and SDLC children of this plan apply the accepted contract later.

## Assessment

Planning revision, 2026-09-26: the owner requested development phases driven by outcomes and evidence. Phase order is planning intent, not an additional native dependency.

Planning, 2026-09-26. Complexity medium (cross-repository planning and overlapping vocabularies); uncertainty high (phase outcomes and capacity require owner decisions); impact medium (incorrect commitments could misdirect several repositories). Ready for bounded discovery only. Implementation/adoption waits for the decisions above. Baseline Hub `4adfbf480a5bc3000cf99aec10226403d391a299`, live #498/#509 and current SDLC/guide conventions. Reassess if repository scope, audience or priorities change.

Planning evidence: current Hub source and live GitHub issues were inspected; this revision changes tracker planning only. No product checks, Project configuration or implementation ran. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated).

## Accepted owner decision record — 2026-09-27 UTC

The owner selected these rules in the planning conversation and authorized this tracker record and Project setup. This records portfolio intent only; it does not authorize #509, #498, #283, Nanoleaf or Pixoo product implementation, installation, publication or device actions.

### Outcome phases and finish lines

- **Current: Ask the guide.** Required outcome and scope: [Hub #509](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/509) and every child and approval that #509 requires for its own source acceptance. The benefit to demonstrate is a validated, sourced goal guide that supports the #509 Pixoo GIF journey, follow-up refinement and return to the ordinary full guide. Entry: this scope and one-child Now capacity are accepted; #543 is ready for bounded drafting, while contract approval remains pending. Exit: #509's required children meet source acceptance, its exact contract approvals and evaluation disposition are evidenced, and the owner records proceed, hold, revise or stop. Unqualified live-model results remain unknown. Installation, live-client use and public publication are separate acceptance targets. Optional #521/#522 and portfolio-guide #540 do not hold this phase or the #541 pilot open.
- **Coarse next direction: Development activity at a glance.** Anchor: the first, saved-GitHub-history Status-page slice in [Hub #283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283). The later live graphs requiring #282 are outside this provisional direction. Define the next phase's exact scope, entry and exit evidence before selecting it for delivery. Phase order is planning preference, not a native blocker or a date gate. #498 is not the next phase and has no near-term commitment.

### Field ownership and conflict rules

- Create one owner-only private Project across Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo. Its only custom planning fields are **Phase** (single select: `Ask the guide`, `Development activity at a glance`) and **Commitment** (single select: `Now`, `Next`, `Later`, `Ideas`). No Priority, Size, date or iteration field is selected for this pilot. Leave both fields without a default; blank means unassigned or unselected, never Ideas, Ready or Done.
- GitHub issues own scope, acceptance, open/closed state, workflow labels, native parent/sub-issue membership and blocked-by facts. Project Phase and Commitment own portfolio intent only. Any built-in Project workflow field is a projection of issue facts, not independent authority. The dated work guide is a consumer, not another status store.
- Assign Phase authoritatively on the epic; a child derives its phase from its one native parent. A standalone issue needs an explicit phase decision; otherwise leave Phase blank. A shared prerequisite remains one issue with one parent and links from other consumers. Do not duplicate or reparent it to make it appear in another phase. If a Project value conflicts with the native parent or issue facts, show the conflict and leave it for owner/coordinator review; do not guess, overwrite native facts or infer readiness from missing blockers.
- The owner chooses phase and selection changes. One authorized coordinator reads, compares, writes and reads back Project changes, preserving unrelated edits. A missing or partial read means unknown/pending synchronization, not an empty queue or permission to rewrite. `status:ready` without Commitment is ready-but-unselected; Now plus a native blocker stays blocked and occupies the selected slot; a deferred idea is not automatically a Project Ideas item; issue closure proves only that issue's stated acceptance, not installation or physical use.

### Pilot membership, capacity and replenishment

- Seed #509 and its required native children. #509 is the current Phase; #543 is the sole `Now` delivery child. Limit Now to one #509 child at a time. #545 then #544 is the preferred follow-on order, but both remain outside `Next` until their actual #543 prerequisite and other readiness decisions are cleared. `Next` is an ordered queue of ready, explicitly selected candidates; `Later` is a plausible but unselected direction; `Ideas` is a consciously retained possibility. Do not auto-fill any of them from labels, age or model judgment.
- Include #498 and its required children for visibility with blank Phase and Commitment; their presence promises no near-term work. Include [Nanoleaf #162](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/162) as standalone maintenance and [Pixoo #96](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/96) as a ready-but-unselected example, both with blank Phase and Commitment. #283 is a coarse future direction, not an initial Project item or Now/Next commitment. Do not seed optional #521/#522/#540 as required work.
- Choose work by owner-valued outcome, actual native prerequisites, implementation/review/acceptance capacity and known uncertainty; unknown effort remains unknown. If #543 is accepted, reopen capacity and check whether #545 is truly ready before selecting it. If #543 is blocked or waiting for approval, it keeps its slot unless the owner explicitly stops, pauses or re-scopes it. A newly important issue requires an explicit replacement decision, not an extra automatic Now slot. Reassess at accepted increments, blockers, material learning or phase review. No calendar cadence or elapsed-time promotion gate is required. A phase review may hold #509 while the planning pilot is evaluated.

### Closure and evidence examples

- #509 closes only on its required native children, human-approved contracts, source checks and explicit evaluation disposition. Its optional Jev ideas and #540 are excluded. #498 retains its own required source-child rubric; its separate installed daily-use follow-up #508 is not proof of, or a prerequisite for, source closure. Neither child percentages nor a merged PR alone estimate remaining effort or establish installed acceptance.
- Trace for the pilot: #509 is the epic with an authoritative current Phase; #543 is its parent-derived child and shared prerequisite for later consumers; Nanoleaf #162 is standalone maintenance; #498 and Pixoo #96 remain visible and unassigned. Assigning #283 a later phase in a future revision would not block its independent work without a native prerequisite. A phase is complete only on its declared outcome evidence and owner decision, not because every related backlog idea closes.

**Evidence and limits:** Owner selections were made in this conversation; this issue is the dated tracker record. Current issue bodies and native child lists supplied the acceptance and prerequisite boundaries. No product checks or source delivery were performed for this planning record. The Project and its live UI require separate #537 readback and current-candidate owner approval before setup acceptance.

## Owner-approved portfolio refresh — 2026-10-01

Decision: **revise** the current phase description to match #509's accepted browser-first direction and proceed with its next source increment. Retain the existing Phase option **Ask the guide**; no field rename or new phase is introduced. This decision supersedes the September 27 queue and its Pixoo GIF/follow-up release description, while preserving the original record as history.

Current outcome: deliver #509 Release 1, the epic Guide browser, before Release 2, ranked Ask. #509's current required-browser list and EP1–EP8 own the scope and evidence. #540 is now required for the browser release, while remaining outside the separate #541 planning-pilot closure. #655 is parallel mapping, not a release gate; #514/#515 and superseded planning records retain their current deferral/retirement rules. Retain a limit of one #509 delivery child in Now. #547 remains unselected, and #498 retains no near-term commitment. Next is a candidate, not an automatic promotion. A blocked Now item retains its slot until an explicit owner decision. #283 remains a coarse later direction, not a selected commitment.

These tracker changes authorize no source implementation, visibility change, publication, installation or device action.

Settle a concise planning contract in this issue's accepted decision record: themes are durable areas; epics are bounded outcomes; stories are independently verifiable increments; small implementation steps remain checklists. Use native parent/sub-issue relationships for membership and native blocked-by for required inputs. Device work stays in its owning repository. Preserve the existing Guide topics rather than inventing a second category taxonomy.

Accepted pilot defaults: one portfolio Project; a Phase field and a Commitment field (Now/Next/Later/Ideas), with no Priority or Size field; one major active epic plus a small maintenance stream. Ready is feasibility; Now is selected work within available implementation, review and acceptance capacity. Next is the small ordered candidate queue, Later is a plausible direction, and Ideas are uncommitted possibilities. These are selection categories, not workflow states or time periods. Native issue state and status labels remain workflow authority; Project workflow state is a projection.

A phase describes an observable capability or user outcome, such as a trustworthy daily control experience, rather than a calendar period or a universal design/build/test stage. Define its intended benefit, required and optional epics, entry conditions, exit evidence, exclusions and next decision. Entry needs an accepted bounded scope, its actual inputs and available capacity. Exit needs the required outcomes and their declared acceptance evidence, with an explicit proceed, hold, revise or stop decision. Test and accept each increment as it is delivered; do not defer testing until a separate global phase.

Keep the hierarchy shallow: native epic → story → checklist remains the delivery structure. Phase is portfolio grouping, not another mandatory parent issue. Record phase definitions once in the Project description/README, linked to the accepted decision record and owning epics. Epic phase assignment is authoritative; stories derive it through their native parent, with an explicit rule for standalone/shared work. A shared prerequisite keeps one issue and one native parent; other consumers link to it instead of duplicating or reparenting it. Missing phase membership stays visible as unassigned. Phase ordering is preferred sequence unless a native prerequisite records a true required input.

An epic carries outcome, smallest useful release, required versus optional scope, acceptance evidence, phase membership and the event that triggers reassessment. A phase may contain several epics, and independent work can proceed across phases when its actual inputs and capacity permit. Splitting or revising a phase requires an explicit scope decision; it cannot silently discard unfinished required work. Dates remain useful for evidence freshness and genuine external deadlines, never as prerequisites to starting or completing a phase. No deadline field or dated roadmap is required for the pilot.

Replenish Now from Next when capacity opens after acceptance or an explicit stop decision. Reassess scope/order when a blocker, material learning, changed priority or phase exit warrants it; do not wait for a scheduled planning meeting. Optional reminders can prevent neglect, but they are not delivery gates. Keep later phases and ideas lightly specified. Refine #498 with separately recognizable release goals without rewriting its accepted source or installed-acceptance boundaries; #509's required delivery and contract children remain distinct from its optional ideas; read its live native hierarchy rather than relying on a fixed child count. Record proposed amendments for scoped later application, preserving existing native parents.

The owner-selected outcomes, exclusions, initial queue, capacity and visibility policy are recorded in the dated decision below. Default recommendation is an owner-only private Project; public guide export requires an explicit allowlist. No dates, effort estimates or commitments are inferred from issue age or model judgment.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text: GitHub issues own scope, acceptance, prerequisites and delivery state. Portfolio selection does not authorize implementation, installation or devices. No parallel backlog, forced story rewriting, mass reprioritization or replacement of existing review/CI gates. Source delivery and usable installed outcomes remain separate measures.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
- [x] AC1: The owner has selected the initial phase outcomes, the current phase, a coarse next-phase direction, exclusions and capacity. Evidence: an explicit dated decision record with measurable benefit, entry/exit criteria and linked existing epics; unanswered choices remain open. No mandatory date ranges are introduced.
- [x] AC2: Every proposed field has one owner, allowed values, edit authority and missing/conflict behavior. Evidence: a compact mapping that distinguishes native issue facts, portfolio fields and dated guide prose; examples cover Ready-but-unselected, Now-but-blocked, deferred ideas and closed-not-completed.
- [x] AC3: Epic closure and progress rules preserve required versus optional children and source versus installed acceptance. Evidence: apply the rubric to #498 and #509; child percentages are not effort forecasts and a merged PR alone cannot close a story.
- [x] AC4: The pilot selection and event-triggered replenishment/review procedure are concrete. Evidence: named issue candidates, an agreed WIP limit and value/prerequisite/effort/uncertainty criteria; walk through acceptance freeing capacity, a blocked Now item, a priority change and a phase exit. A blocked item still consumes its agreed WIP slot unless explicitly stopped or re-scoped; no automatic overfilling. Preserve unknown estimates.
- [x] AC5: Phase grouping, commitment and workflow have separate owners and meanings. Evidence: trace an epic, a child, standalone maintenance, a shared prerequisite and an unassigned item; show that a later-phase assignment alone blocks nothing. Phase completion requires its own evidence, not every backlog idea or an elapsed period.

Delivery target: accepted planning/tracker record only. Initial investigation is read-only; record decisions and amend named existing issues only within the authority granted at that pickup. No repository code, Project configuration or account authentication changes. No executable product tests are claimed.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text: No full-backlog migration or new issues for every idea: pilot a small selected set first; broaden only after the pilot review. No story points or forecasting service: use observable completed increments, blocked age and waiting-for-acceptance work; revisit only if actual planning questions remain unanswered. The setup and SDLC children of this plan apply the accepted contract later.

issues.title: Qualify app verification and preview handoff on the owner’s Windows/WSL hosts
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

After source delivery, qualify the actual owner-host workflow: a fresh authorized Codex or Claude session uses documented verification tools, saves clickable proof and leaves a preview the owner can open in Windows. This is a host-adoption and acceptance issue, not another source implementation issue.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488
Phase: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/492

## Smallest useful implementation and dependencies

- Name each target host, installed skill/source revisions, application revisions and runtime owner before activation. Use the existing managed installation procedure and checkpoint; source issue closure alone does not authorize installation or launching sessions/services.
- Under a later explicit owner-host request, activate only the required merged methods/adapters and run the documented single-app and integrated scenarios. Qualify Codex and Claude separately; do not claim one host from the other's evidence.
- Exercise agent verification first, then a separate/reset hands-on preview with retained proof, expiry, extension, stop and reproducible restart. Verify links/artifacts in the actual Windows browser and chat surface, not only via Linux HTTP.
- Use fresh sessions without bespoke coordinator scripts or hidden knowledge. Record missing prerequisites, manual intervention, failures and recovery as adoption findings; route source defects back to their owning delivery rather than silently patching installed copies.
- Record installed versus recommended capabilities/settings honestly. Preserve private configuration and synthetic-only state; no physical-device sequence is included.
- Prepare an adoption readback: versions, qualified host/workflow paths, scenario evidence and limitations. This operational qualification is not a comparative model benchmark and does not require #44's postponed study preparation.

Required source prerequisites (native blocked-by links; independent investigation/preparation may proceed):

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/494
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/193
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/495
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/84
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/85
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/86

Use [installation checkpoint #69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/69) where applicable; coordinate reviewer host receipts with [#80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/80) without repeating its qualification. [Evaluation #44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/44) is postponed, including discovery, calibration, manifest preparation, fixture expansion and trials. It is not a qualification or completion prerequisite here; any later study needs a new scope decision and applicable authorization rather than an inherited allowance. Coordinate intended retained resources with the existing cleanup issues.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Explicit target/activation/launch authority and owner are recorded before host mutations or sessions; restore/stop procedures are available.
- [ ] The scoped Codex and Claude host paths each complete or explicitly fail qualification using documented entrypoints and current installed revisions.
- [ ] Actual Windows clicks open screenshots/video and each app preview; source/build and run identity match the receipt. Browser reachability is not inferred from a loopback unit test.
- [ ] Human exploration does not modify saved verification proof. Expiry/extend/stop/restart work after the originating agent finishes, including a failed-start case.
- [ ] No personal state, installed service or physical device is altered by synthetic runs; each retained preview has an owner, expiry and cleanup outcome.
- [ ] A concise handoff states what was verified, what remains unverified, the proof links, preview links, expiry and how the owner can validate it. Required product UI approval remains explicit.
- [ ] Qualification receipts declare the actual qualified host/workflow paths; missing host support and telemetry remain unknown/pending, not invented successes.
- [ ] Receipts preserve failed attempts, manual intervention and recovery for owned repairs and [Hub #492's operational follow-up](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/492), with truthful time and attribution limits. No #44 discovery or calibration package is required.

## Adoption findings and follow-up — updated 2026-09-28

For each qualified or attempted path, retain the task/scenario and source identity, expected versus observed behavior, first failing stage where known, manual intervention, recovery and final disposition. Record human active time only when measured or explicitly reported, separately from agent elapsed time and waiting; otherwise use unknown. Include failed and unsupported paths rather than only successful previews.

Keep these observations in the existing qualification receipt and link them to [#492's bounded manual follow-up](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/492) and applicable repair issues. An adoption observation is not a calibrated judgment or evidence of comparative improvement. [agent-skills #44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/44) may reuse suitable evidence only after a later owner decision; do not prepare its discovery sample now. Public readbacks omit private transcripts, raw identifiers and paths.

## Assessment and next action

Complexity: high; uncertainty: medium for actual host/browser/session controls; impact: high for installation and launch boundaries. Full qualification waits for applicable delivered sources and a later explicit owner-host request. Independent runbook/preflight preparation is available; per-host/per-app probes need only their applicable subset, not closure of unrelated work.

## Validation and finish line

Finish line: actual named-host adoption receipts and Windows/browser readback for the required app/workflow paths, or explicitly pending acceptance. Do not close this acceptance issue merely because source changes merged. If source fixes are needed, use owned source issues/PRs with their full reviews/CI; report their source completion separately from this host qualification.

## Meaningful deferrals

No paid API calls, new model comparison, changed model defaults, LAN/phone qualification, physical-device validation or daily automation. No study is launched by this issue or source delivery.

## Delivery boundary

This is planned work, not completed verification. Issue creation authorizes no implementation or launch. During later authorized source delivery, follow the owning repository's current instructions, preserve unrelated work, obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, require applicable current-head CI, use the guarded merge procedure and verify merged-main checks before source closure. Required UI approval remains separate from optional hands-on use.

issues.body:

- Report source/base/head identity, applicable configured CI jobs, actual results, independent reviewer coverage/results, proof artifact identity, required UI approval and requested installation/physical finish line.
- Missing, pending, skipped, failed or stale evidence stays explicit. Apply existing guide-only CI exceptions only when their actual scope/evidence requirements are met.
- Keep source/CI, UI approval, host activation, real-client and physical acceptance separate; do not demand installation for a source-only finish line.
- Consume reviewer evidence delivered by existing agent-skills #54. Retain source pointers/receipt IDs and read failures without publishing transcripts, tokens or private runtime data.

issues.title: Define the app verification interface and test preview lifecycle feasibility
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A delivery agent and the owner have one small, documented way to start a disposable app, establish what is running, exercise a scenario, collect proof and hand over a preview. Use Hub as the first caller and inspect Nanoleaf/Pixoo constraints before fixing the contract.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488
Phase: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/489

## Smallest useful implementation and dependencies

- Define project-owned operations for start, readiness/doctor, scenario/reset, browser drive/capture, handoff, extend, stop and expiry. Choose exact command names after the caller walkthrough; do not invent a new general orchestration protocol.
- Define a compact result/receipt using existing evidence conventions: run identity, source commit and build identity, scenario/version, actual versus simulated components, checks/outcomes, artifact paths, preview address, expiry, owned resource identities and cleanup result. A dirty or unknown build must be labelled, not presented as an exact candidate.
- Specify synthetic fixture ownership, port allocation, private runtime storage outside Git checkouts where required, artifact retention in the owning main checkout, and reset semantics. Reset can affect only this run's disposable state.
- Before implementing adapters, run bounded, authorized mechanics experiments for Windows-to-WSL loopback reachability, session-independent preview lifetime, browser screenshot/video capture and partial-start cleanup. Record hypothesis, smallest probe, stop condition and result. Do not start installed services, change networking settings or contact devices.
- Make the two-hour lease observable, extendable and stoppable. Cleanup identifies exact owned resources rather than killing by port or process name; an expired lease cannot kill a reused PID or another run.
- Work through concrete agent and human callers and a failed-start caller. Document accepted choices in the existing development/architecture owners only where needed; tracker status stays on GitHub.

No required source prerequisite blocks independent preparation. Coordinate overlapping files with their current owner.

Reference the existing Hub dashboard fixture/browser tests, Nanoleaf `scripts/demo.py`, Pixoo simulator and Hub standalone integration harness. Coordinate identity with [Hub #428](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/428), but wrapper-owned candidate identity must not wait for installed-runtime version UI.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A caller walkthrough covers verify → retain proof → hand off separate/reset state → human exploration → extend/stop/expiry → restart.
- [ ] A bounded feasibility receipt records actual host/browser access where authorized and marks any untested host behavior. Missing authorization leaves that probe pending; simulated success does not establish Windows access.
- [ ] The contract accounts for concurrent runs, occupied ports, stale builds, interrupted starts, agent exit, stale process identities, failed capture and unavailable browser tooling.
- [ ] Preserved proof cannot be overwritten by a subsequent reset/manual session; preview links identify their run and show expiry/staleness clearly.
- [ ] The contract identifies where auth secrets live, keeps tokens out of proof/URLs/logs, and defines a supported browser session establishment path rather than disabling authentication.
- [ ] The design is accepted and executable adapter acceptance is mapped to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/494, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/193 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118. No unsupported lifecycle promise remains hidden in prose.

## Assessment and next action

Complexity: medium; uncertainty: high around host reachability and supervisor lifetime; impact: medium because owned processes/state require reliable boundaries. Ready for design and bounded feasibility investigation when requested. Resolve factual mechanics here before committing dependent adapters to a mechanism; return only genuine product tradeoffs to the owner.

## Validation and finish line

Finish line: accepted source contract/design plus inspectable feasibility findings under an authorized delivery, with pending host probes explicit. Use proportionate doc/tooling checks and required workflow checks; runnable prototypes need focused lifecycle failure checks. Documentation-only work records why no product OpenSpec delta applies; behavior contracts use the repository's issue-linked OpenSpec process. Do not keep disposable prototype code merely because it ran.

## Meaningful deferrals

No LAN/phone hosting, remote fleet, continuous preview service, physical-device accuracy or general process-management platform. Revisit wider access only after the same-PC path is qualified.

## Delivery boundary

This is planned work, not completed verification. Issue creation authorizes no implementation or launch. During later authorized source delivery, follow the owning repository's current instructions, preserve unrelated work, obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, require applicable current-head CI, use the guarded merge procedure and verify merged-main checks before source closure. Required UI approval remains separate from optional hands-on use.

issues.title: Clear Claude Code approval attention once the prompt is answered
issues.body:
> Refined on 2026-09-30 from the read-only research handoff. The owner chose the retirement rules and accepted the one limitation below. Source-only; installation is a separate re-apply by a named owner.

### Outcome and real setup

When the owner answers a Claude Code dialog, the session's approval marker retires on the evidence that follows the answer, so devices stop showing attention within seconds instead of at the next prompt. Installed shared owner (hub 0.4.0), the Claude Code producer from #367, all status devices. Another session's attention still keeps devices amber; device repaint lag is #455.

### Smallest useful implementation

Why it lingers: the producer maps `PermissionRequest` to an `attention.approval` without an ID (`packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts`), and the reducer removes that marker only on a matching known-ID `attention.resolved` or when a newer turn retires its turn (`packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts`). No installed hook fires after an answer. The [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) (read 2026-09-30, identical in the 2026-09-25 archive) documents `PermissionRequest` "without tool_use_id", so no request-to-answer ID correlation exists on any version. AskUserQuestion dialogs take the same hook: the #22 trial showed attention for them and `PermissionRequest` is the only hook the producer maps to attention.

Two owner-policy rules. No envelope change: contract 1.0 and 1.1 already carry `attention.resolved` and `turn.ended`.

1. **Answered-tool evidence.** Setup adds `PostToolUse` and `PostToolUseFailure` (no matcher) to the generated Claude Code entries (`apps/hub/src/setup.ts`). The normalizer maps each to `attention.resolved {status:'known', id: tool_use_id}` with turn `prompt_id`, and returns null without either field. Reducer: a known-ID resolution on turn T removes a matching known-ID item as today, and also forgets every unknown-ID approval on turn T of that session. Questions, input markers, other turns and other sessions are untouched. Producer hooks block by default, so the resolution was emitted after a tool completed, and a tool completes only after its own dialog closed.
2. **Turn-end fallback.** `turn.ended` on turn T forgets that turn's unknown-ID approvals. This covers a denied dialog followed by nothing else, which produces no tool hook: `PostToolUseFailure` excludes "a permission denial" and `PermissionDenied` "doesn't run when you manually deny a permission dialog".

Also in scope: raise the packaged hook's 64 KiB stdin bound (`apps/hub/bin/monitor-hook.mjs`), because `PostToolUse` carries the whole `tool_response`; add the two events to `docs/provider-qualification.md`; update the agent-state-core spec requirement "Retired-turn approvals without a request ID" and the `attention.resolved` wording in `docs/agent-lifecycle-contract.md`; agent-state minor version. Re-applying setup on the `shared-monitor/claude` receipt adds the two events (`planSetup` re-adds missing owned entries).

**Accepted limitation (owner, 2026-09-30):** with several tool calls in flight in one Claude message, a completed auto-allowed tool can clear the marker a few seconds before the remaining dialog is answered; the device shows working until the next request creates a new marker. Rule 2 also applies to Codex no-ID approvals; Codex hooks are unchanged.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Hooks stay allowlisted metadata and fail open; `tool_response`, `tool_input` and `cwd` never enter the envelope. Missing evidence never clears attention: without `prompt_id` or `tool_use_id`, nothing is sent. Next-turn retirement (#225), explicit recovery (#185), known-ID markers on retired turns and every Codex hook are unchanged. Resolutions refresh session freshness like other lifecycle evidence.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, then a separate re-apply install by a named owner.

Reducer tests in `packages/agent-state/tests/approvals.test.mjs`, driven through `normalizeHook`:

- `UserPromptSubmit` P1, `PermissionRequest` P1, then `PostToolUse` P1 with `tool_use_id` X: marker gone, activity active, notices and acknowledgments unchanged. Same with `PostToolUseFailure`.
- `PostToolUse` on P1 with no marker: no attention change, no ambiguity added.
- `PostToolUse` carrying P2 while the marker is on P1, or from another session or source: marker stays.
- `PostToolUse` without `prompt_id` or without `tool_use_id`: normalizer returns null.
- `Stop` P1 after `PermissionRequest` P1: marker gone; `Stop` on P0 or an unknown turn leaves it.
- `PermissionRequest` P1 after a `PostToolUse` P1: a new marker exists.
- The same resolution twice: duplicate, no new revision.
- Known-ID approval on P1 plus resolution Y on P1: the known-ID item stays.
- Question and input markers on P1 survive both rules.

`packages/agent-state/tests/providers.test.mjs`: both hooks map for `claude`/`code`, are rejected for Codex, and canary content never enters the envelope. `apps/hub/tests/setup-hook.test.mjs`: a re-planned setup on an installed receipt adds exactly the two events; the packaged hook accepts a `PostToolUse` payload above 64 KiB.

Installed acceptance, after the re-apply: in the owner's ordinary sessions, an answered AskUserQuestion and an allowed Bash dialog clear attention before the next prompt, seen on `pendant-1` or the dashboard. The stacked-dialog case is observed there, not in a separate experiment. One comment records it.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Esc during a dialog: `Stop` "does not run if the stoppage occurred due to a user interrupt", so the marker stays until the next prompt, as today. Fallback: the next prompt or #185 recovery. Revisit when Claude Code documents an interrupt hook or a `tool_use_id` on `PermissionRequest`.
- Per-marker counts for stacked dialogs: the accepted window above. Revisit if the false clear is seen to matter in use.
- Async `PostToolUse` hook to remove per-tool latency: not chosen; it breaks the ordering argument and is documented as unenforced once backgrounded. Revisit if the synchronous hook's latency is noticeable.
- Codex answer evidence: none; #332 covers manual retirement.

### Evidence

In the #22 trial (2026-09-26), each answered Claude Code question dialog left the feed at attention: after answers at about 06:00:40 and 06:13, the state stayed attention until the next prompt (06:01:38, 06:17:36), so `pendant-1` stayed amber. Research on 2026-09-30 at main `641861b`: no `PostToolUse` hook is generated or accepted (`setup.ts`, `providers.ts`), the installed `~/.claude/settings.json` holds exactly the seven generated events, and the installed hub 0.4.0 hook is byte-identical to source.

## Guide

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#456](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/456) on 2026-09-30, from the story, the research handoff, source at main `641861b` and the Claude Code hooks reference.

issues.title: Keep LIFX status paints out of lighting.pending so the lighting snapshot stays valid
issues.body:
## Problem

During the #22 installed trial (2026-09-26, hub 0.3.12, host release `490ad5a`), B.U.N.N.Y.'s pendant-1 page intermittently showed `incompatible-controller` and "Controller observations are stale", reliably right after a mode change. A status paint sits in the bulb's queue for up to about a second, and the host lists it in `lighting.pending` with the private command kind `lifx.internal.status-paint` (wire-unit hue, saturation, brightness, kelvin). The `lifx-light` 1.0.0 snapshot allows only `lifx.color.set` and `lifx.temperature.set` there, so the hub's validator (`apps/hub/src/lifx-lighting.ts`) rejects any lighting read that lands during a paint, answers 502 and briefly marks the controller unavailable. The paints themselves were correct.

## Decision

The owner chose on 2026-09-26: an in-flight status paint is not listed in `lighting.pending`, so the lighting snapshot always stays valid `lifx-light` 1.0.0. This replaces #20's "shown in `lighting.pending` like a color command", which 1.0.0 cannot express. The paint keeps the bulb's queue, request identity namespace, receipts, `lastSuccessfulSend` and `lastOutcome`. No profile version change.

## Scope

- `controllers/lifx/src/controller.ts`: exclude status paints from `lighting.pending` (they are already excluded from controller v1 `state.pending`).
- Tests: a lighting snapshot taken while a paint is queued or in flight validates against the package's `lifx-light` 1.0.0 schema and the hub's lighting validator, and lists no paint.
- `controllers/lifx/README.md`, the `lifx-controller` spec (OpenSpec change) and any doc stating paints appear in `lighting.pending`.

Excluded: hub or dashboard changes, a profile bump, installation (the #22 session reinstalls the host and rechecks the page).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A lighting snapshot read while a status paint is queued or in flight passes the `lifx-light` 1.0.0 schema and the hub's `validateLightingSnapshot`, and its `lighting.pending` lists no paint.
- [ ] Paints still go through the bulb's queue with a receipt, update `lastSuccessfulSend` and `lastOutcome`, and are still cancelled by a generation cancel or a graceful close.
- [ ] Build, typecheck, `test:lifx`, `test:local-controllers`, `test:agent-status`, `test:hub`, the contract checks and the workflow checks exit zero on Node 24. The OpenSpec change is synced and archived.

Found by #22; fixes a behavior introduced by #20.

issues.title: Paint LIFX status from sessions with uncertain freshness
issues.body:
## Problem

#20 decided that the LIFX status publisher paints nothing while any shown root session has `uncertain` freshness. In agent-state, a session becomes `uncertain` after five minutes without new evidence, and sessions restored after a hub restart stay uncertain until their next event. A finished turn waiting to be read is idle by nature, so it is nearly always uncertain. On the installed setup during the #22 trial (2026-09-26, hub 0.3.12, host release `6b561ba`), 15 of the 16 shown root sessions were uncertain, and `highestStatus` returned `unknown` continuously. In Work or Quiet, `pendant-1` would therefore stay unpainted for up to the 24-hour evidence expiry.

## Decision

The owner chose on 2026-09-26: rank every shown root session by the state the shared owner reports, whatever its freshness. `highestStatus` returns `unknown` only when the feed is unavailable or the collector is not running. The other #20 rules are unchanged: attention before working before done before idle, done retired only by acknowledgment, silence never means done, paint only on transitions, and an unavailable feed never paints idle. The cost is the Tidbyt's existing behavior: a session that stopped silently stays working until it ends or expires.

## Scope

- `packages/agent-status` `highestStatus`: drop the uncertain-session rule; keep `unknown` for an unavailable feed or a collector that is not running.
- Tests in `packages/agent-status` and `controllers/lifx` that asserted the old rule now assert the new one, including a feed where every shown session is uncertain.
- `controllers/lifx/README.md`, the `lifx-controller` spec (through an OpenSpec change) and any other doc that states the old rule.
- The Tidbyt keeps its per-row dimming and is otherwise unchanged.

Excluded: installation and the physical check (#22 resumes after this merges), agent-state freshness itself, and #362.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A feed whose shown sessions are all uncertain yields their highest reported state, and the publisher paints it on the transition.
- [ ] An unavailable feed or a collector that is not running still yields `unknown` and no paint.
- [ ] The Tidbyt status tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Build, typecheck, `test:agent-status`, `test:lifx`, `test:local-controllers`, `test:tidbyt`, the contract checks and the workflow checks exit zero on Node 24. The OpenSpec change is synced and archived.

Found by #22; fixes a decision made in #20.

**Note:** Correct LIFX status painting for sessions with uncertain freshness before the #22 installation trial resumes.

issues.title: Carry session titles and project names in shared agent state
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-25 from the divoom-app-upgrade#98 follow-up, at the owner's request. On that date the owner retired the rule that titles, prompts, transcripts and paths never enter shared data. This issue does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes on its own.

### Outcome and real setup

Every device and B.U.N.N.Y. can show what each agent session is working on: the session's own title, such as `Redesign the Pixoo monitor layout`, and its project, such as `divoom-app-upgrade`. They no longer have to fall back to a session ID. This covers the hub's shared owner on the owner's WSL host, with its Codex CLI, Codex Desktop and Claude Code producers. Prompts and agent responses are #425, and are excluded here.

### Why

The exclusion entered in `ea5770f` (PR #12, 2026-09-06): `AGENTS.md:127-128` and `docs/architecture.md` "Only lifecycle metadata, identifiers, timestamps and explicit user-chosen labels enter the shared feed…". No commit, issue, PR, ADR or design records a reason. Every later statement repeats it: #2, PR #74, the `agent-lifecycle-contract` and `agent-state-core` specs, the Tidbyt README, and the Pixoo and Nanoleaf vocabularies. The owner has decided that titles, project names, prompts and transcripts are not a concern for them. Credentials and tokens remain excluded.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **Policy.** Replace the exclusion in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/agent-lifecycle-contract.md` with the new policy: session titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and agent output may enter shared data; credentials, tokens and secrets may not. Rewrite the privacy canaries: they keep credentials out and no longer reject titles or prompts.
- **Contract 1.1 (minor, additive).**
  - An optional `title` with its source (`provider` or `user`), separate from `label`, so an owner's label still wins.
  - An optional `project` display name. Either drop the "never derived from a path or title" rule for `projectId`, or add a separate project name. Record the choice in the design.
  - Existing 1.0 consumers ignore both fields.
- **Label bounds.** Align the label bound. The contract allows 80 characters while `hub_label` and the Pixoo input accept 160. Allow labels that are not user-set, which interacts with #372.
- **Producers** (`packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts`):
  - Codex title: `thread_name` for the session ID from `session_index.jsonl`, which exists in both the WSL and the Windows `.codex` homes. The hub already mounts the Windows home for unread state. The Nanoleaf wall already reads this file.
  - Claude Code title: the latest `custom-title`, else `ai-title`, entry from the hook's `transcript_path`. In a 2026-09-25 sample, 120 of 137 local transcripts had a `custom-title`. Lift the `codex-desktop.ts` "Never read a transcript" restriction to match.
  - Project name: the basename of the hook's `cwd`, or its git repository root.
- **State owner.** Persist `title` and `project`, update them when they change (renames), and expose them in `hub_sessions`, the `/api/monitor/v1` snapshot and B.U.N.N.Y. session tables.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Hooks stay bounded, observational and fail-open. A missing or unreadable title never blocks an event.
- The owner's explicit label always wins over a provider title.
- The closed schema and size bounds stay; new fields have explicit maximum lengths.
- Credentials and tokens stay excluded.
- Existing 1.0 consumers keep working until they adopt 1.1.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- A Codex Desktop session and a Claude Code session each appear in `hub_sessions` with their real title and project name. Verified by unit fixtures for both title sources and an installed observation on the owner's host.
- Renaming a session (Codex thread rename, Claude `/rename`) updates the shared title on a later event.
- A session with no title source still reports a neutral ID and never fails its hook.
- The rewritten canaries reject credentials and tokens, and accept titles and prompts.
- The delivery target is source-only unless the owner asks for installation.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Prompts and agent responses:** #425.
- **Pixoo and Nanoleaf display:** jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade#106 and jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#179.
- **Other hub surfaces that exclude titles** (moments, device controls, Tidbyt): #426.
- **Existing backlog items:** #364 (neutral alias) becomes the fallback for untitled sessions. #374 (story-key labels) is largely superseded. #372 (agent self-labels) stays relevant.

**Highlight:** idea, Devices show each session's real title and project instead of a UUID fragment, after the owner retired the unexplained title and prompt exclusion.

issues.title: Port the hub's Nanoleaf harness scripts to the split bridge modules before the next pin
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The hub's cross-repository Nanoleaf harnesses keep working when their Nanoleaf pin moves to jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf `f003a39` (#118, PR jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#173) or later. Setup: the hub checkout, a clean Nanoleaf source checkout at the pinned revision, isolated `/tmp` state and no device. Excluded: any Nanoleaf behavior change and any installation.

Three scripts drive Nanoleaf internals through the old bridge-module API that `f003a39` removed:
- `scripts/hub-shared-nanoleaf.py`, run by `check-hub-shared-consumers.mjs`: `shared.source_config(directory, bridge)`, `shared.accept(directory, bridge, …)`, `shared.command(command, bridge)` and `bridge.connect_state`. It also rebinds `bridge.launch_worker` and `bridge.data_dir`.
- `scripts/session-retirement-nanoleaf.py`, run by `check-session-retirement.mjs`: `shared_input.select_source(directory, b, 'shared', …)`.
- `scripts/performance/standalone-nanoleaf.py`: `shared.configure`, `select_source`, `Poller(directory, bridge)` and `source_config` with the bridge argument, `bridge.connect_state`, and the same rebinding.

The pins that gate them are `apps/hub/fixtures/nanoleaf-source.json` (now `0043456`, one commit before the change) and `apps/hub/fixtures/retirement-nanoleaf-source.json` (`f4ae77e`). All three work at those pins and fail at the first refresh past `f003a39`, with a `TypeError` (extra `bridge` argument) or an `AttributeError` (`bridge.connect_state`).

### Smallest useful implementation

When a pin next moves past `f003a39`, port each script to the Nanoleaf owners named in its [ADR 0016](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0016-module-ownership-and-dependency-direction.md):
- `shared_source.configure / select_source / accept / source_config / Poller / command` without the bridge argument (`command(argv, launch=…)` takes a launch seam).
- `database.connect_state`.
- Pass `--state-dir` in place of rebinding `data_dir`, and pass `launch=lambda _d: None` in place of rebinding `launch_worker`.

issues.title: Install stop-signal handlers before the hub and the Tidbyt runner announce they are ready
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The installed monitor (`codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service`, hub 0.3.7) and the standalone Tidbyt runner (the rollback path for the local controller host) both close gracefully on SIGINT and SIGTERM. But both announce they are ready before they install those handlers:

- `apps/hub/src/cli.ts` writes `{"ready":true,…}` at line 38 and registers `process.once('SIGTERM'|'SIGINT', stop)` at line 45, after `startHub` resolves.
- `controllers/tidbyt/src/cli.ts` prints `tidbyt-status-started` at line 7 and registers its handlers at lines 17–18.

A stop that arrives during startup, or in the gap after the ready line, uses the default action. The process dies without its graceful close. #351 fixed exactly this in the local controller host. That CLI's test failed once on `main` at `b5199f3` (Depot job `xr7jlbjl33`), and a local loop that sends SIGTERM as soon as the ready line appears killed the old CLI in 146 of 150 runs.

This matters for the installed monitor because systemd stops and restarts it on every update and, after #356, at boot. It matters for CI because any test that signals these CLIs right after the ready line can flake the same way.

### Smallest useful implementation

- Apply #351's pattern to both CLIs. Install the handlers first, record a stop that arrives during startup, and honor it as soon as startup finishes.
- Add one regression test per CLI: send SIGTERM the instant the ready line appears, 10 times, and require exit code 0 with no terminating signal. Wait on `close`, not `exit`.

Dependencies: none. Related: #351 (the same fix for the local host), #356 (boot-time start).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Keep the ready and stop lines, the exit codes and the hub's 5-second shutdown deadline.
- `serve-staged`, the migration fence and `open` are unchanged.
- One state owner and one Tidbyt writer: the leases and the owner store are released only through the existing close paths.
- No device contact in tests. The Tidbyt runner test keeps its fake connection.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Reinstalling the monitor is a separate step, on the owner's request.

- Both new tests fail against the current CLIs, reproducing the early-SIGTERM kill, and pass after the change.
- `test:hub`, `test:hub:package`, `test:setup`, `test:tidbyt` and the workflow checks pass.

### Meaningful deferrals

None. Until this is installed, the only manual workaround is not to stop the monitor in the first seconds after a start.

## Guide

**Topic:** hosting-migrations
**Note:** The stop-signal race #351 fixed in the local host is still in the hub and Tidbyt runner launchers.

issues.title: Store event rules and the interrupt set, and arbitrate the moments they trigger
issues.body:
> Child 1 of 3 of #45, filed 2026-09-25. Delivers the ADR 0006 assignment: the rules store, the interrupt set, event rules and moment arbitration. Routines are #359; the page and MCP tools are #360.

### Outcome and real setup

An owner-approved event rule turns a normalized event into a moment, arbitrated by the hub and delivered to each target device through the contract 1.1 `moment` command, without an open conversation or a model call. The owner's interrupt set (a merged pull request, a failed CI run, a meeting reminder) decides which event kinds may cover status presentation, and is stored data the owner can change without a code change.

Setup is the installed hub with its registered controllers. The first real source is the hub's existing agent lifecycle events; GitHub (#293) and calendar (#298) plug in when they land.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- **Rules store.** A `rules` table in the hub's private SQLite: stable ID, name, `enabled`, `kind` (`event` in this story; `routine` reserved for #359), trigger and action as validated JSON, created and updated timestamps. Edited only through typed hub routes; no page in this story. The interrupt set is a stored list of event kinds with the three owner-approved defaults seeded on first start.
- **Event rule.** Trigger: an event kind from a source, optionally narrowed by source alias. Action: a moment with mood, priority class (`event` or `flourish`), `durationMs`, optional palette, and target device aliases. `coversStatus` is derived: true only when the event kind is in the interrupt set and the class is `event`.
- **Event intake.** One internal interface that sources call with a normalized event carrying a stable ID and a kind. Duplicate IDs are dropped. Restart, reconnect and historical replay (#139) never reach the rules.
- **Arbitration.** For each matching enabled rule, check in order: the global "no flourishes" switch (flourish class only), quiet hours (#295, off by default), the per-agent and global budgets (#294, flourish class only), then each target's current mode and alert state from its snapshot. Blocked moments are logged with the blocking reason and not sent.
- **Delivery.** Hand each arbitrated moment to the shared sender from #335, which owns 1.1 negotiation, `start` computation from the device's `sampleClock`, and the per-device ticket, revision and generation guards. This story sends nothing itself. Devices are independent; one failure never blocks another.
- **Log.** A bounded `automation_log` table: rule, trigger event ID, each target, receipt or typed failure, and `blocked` with its reason. If #296 lands first, adopt its table and add the rule reference; otherwise #296 adopts this one.
- **Routes.** Typed hub routes for listing rules, creating, updating, enabling, disabling and deleting one, reading and replacing the interrupt set, and reading the log. `read` scope for reads, `control` for writes, `X-Pixoo-Request: 1` on mutations as the hub already requires.

Dependencies: #292 (closed, contract 1.1) and #335 (the shared moment sender; arbitration can be built and tested against a fake sender before it lands, but nothing reaches a device without it). Coordinate the rule and log schemas with #246. #293, #298 and #352 are sources, not prerequisites.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The hub sends semantic intents only; no frames, raw protocol or geometry.
- No moment changes a device's selected mode. Status presentation is covered only by an `event` moment whose kind is in the interrupt set (ADR 0006).
- One writer per device through its owning controller. Existing admission limits, tickets and receipt meanings.
- Restarts, reconnects and replay never trigger a moment.
- Privacy: rules and the log hold event kinds, source aliases, device aliases and receipts. Titles, project names and prompts may appear (#424, #425). No credentials or tokens.
- Rules created by anything other than the owner's explicit call are stored disabled.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] **AC1.** Rules and the interrupt set persist across a hub restart; the defaults are seeded exactly once; routes enforce scopes and reject invalid trigger or action JSON with typed errors.
- [x] **AC2.** With a fake source: an event in the interrupt set produces one 1.1 `moment` per target with `coversStatus:true`; an event outside it produces the moment with `coversStatus:false`; a disabled rule produces nothing; a duplicate event ID produces nothing.
- [x] **AC3.** Arbitration: the global switch, quiet hours, each budget, and a target in Quiet or with an active alert each block with the stated reason in the log and zero device writes.
- [x] **AC4.** Delivery: each arbitrated moment is handed to the #335 sender once per target; a target whose send fails or answers `moment-missed`, `moment-blocked` or `unsupported-capability` logs that failure while other targets are still handed over; nothing retries.
- [x] **AC5.** Restart and replay: events delivered before shutdown are not reprocessed after restart; a replayed history stream reaches no rule.
- [x] **AC6.** Issue-linked OpenSpec change; hub tests with fake controllers and a fake source; independent Standards and Specification reviews; current-head and merged-revision CI.

**Delivery target:** source-only. Enabling a rule on the owner's installed hub and any live moment on the physical devices are separately authorized steps.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Editing from B.U.N.N.Y. and MCP proposals: #360. Until then the owner edits through the typed routes with a token.
- GitHub and calendar sources: #293, #298.
- Scheduled routines and the clock source: #359.
- Choreographed multi-device palettes: #297.

### Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25. Complexity: medium. Uncertainty: low; the contract and arbitration inputs are decided. Impact: medium; a wrong arbitration can cover status, bounded by the interrupt set, receipts and the log.

**Readiness:** ready for the store, intake, arbitration and log against a fake sender; end-to-end delivery waits for #335. **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews with a privacy check on stored rule and log content.

Amended 2026-09-25 (closeout sweep): delivery goes through the #335 shared sender instead of this story sending moments itself.

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Note:** Rules store, interrupt set, event rules and moment arbitration, child 1 of #45.

issues.title: Keep the hub starting when its MCP tool catalog grows past the response limit
issues.body:
### Failure and reproduction

With `"mcp": true` in the installed hub's `host.json` (hub 0.3.7 from `68c9333`, on the Nanoleaf Linux installation), adding a sixth controller stops the hub from starting. The monitor exits with `hub-start-failed`, which takes every hub client offline until `host.json` is restored.

On 2026-09-25, codex-nanoleaf#167 added this entry:
- id `nanoleaf-panels`, kind `nanoleaf`
- the same endpoint and token as `nanoleaf-wall`
- `deviceId` `panels`

It follows `nanoleaf-wall`, `pixoo`, `tidbyt`, `beam` and `pendant-1`. The monitor failed twice under systemd. I restored the previous `host.json` within about 15 seconds, and the hub is healthy again.

I reproduced it on a private copy of the monitor's state outside any checkout, calling `startHub` from the installed `dist` on port 0:
- With the entry, startup throws `Tool catalog exceeds response limit` from `createMcpHandler` (`packages/mcp/src/http.ts:78`, `device-mcp/dist/http.js:115`), called from `createHubMcp`.
- The same configuration without the entry starts.
- The same configuration with the entry and `"mcp": false` also starts.

So the JSON tool catalog of six controllers plus the host service is over `maxResponseBytes` (1 MiB). Each device registers several tools, each carrying the full `$defs` schema. The catalog check runs at startup, so this doesn't depend on the Panels in particular: any sixth device fails the same way while MCP is on. Hub #319 (LIFX Beam) and later device additions would hit the same wall.

### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- The hub starts, with MCP enabled, with at least the owner's current device set plus the NL22 Panels, and with headroom for the devices already planned.
- A catalog that is too large degrades clearly instead of failing startup. For example: a clear startup error that names the limit, MCP disabled with a logged reason while the rest of the hub starts, or shared schema definitions so the catalog stays small.
- A test adds controllers until the old failure point and shows the hub still starts with MCP on.

### Dependencies, verification and delivery target

- Blocks the hub half of codex-nanoleaf#167: the Panels' hub controller entry and the hub brightness check. Dashboard controls for the Panels also need #323.
- Verification: a hub test at the failure point, then an installed restart with the `nanoleaf-panels` entry present and MCP on.
- Delivery target: hub source, then installation on the owner's request.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Note:** The hub's MCP tool catalog is over its 1 MiB response limit at six controllers, so adding a device while MCP is on stops the hub from starting.
