issues.title: Show Pixoo media and playlist previews on the B.U.N.N.Y. Pixoo page
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The operator browses the Pixoo's media and saved playlists from the B.U.N.N.Y. Pixoo page: a grid of renditions with still thumbnails, an animated preview on hover or selection, and each playlist as an ordered filmstrip of its items with duration or play count. Previews use the effective 64×64 rendition's exact cached PNG frames and timing manifest, matching the Pixoo web UI's pixels. Preview availability and compatibility with the configured device profile are separate; a preview is not evidence of physical playback. Owner direction, 2026-09-25: preview GIFs and playlists in B.U.N.N.Y. as well as in the Pixoo web UI, and schedule routines from B.U.N.N.Y. that name a playlist or a single rendition.

Setup is the installed hub with the registered Pixoo controller and the operator's browser. No new hosts, users or services.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Depends on divoom-app-upgrade#96, which adds a compatible minor version of `pixoo-integration` with a catalog capability flag and `catalogRevision` in the snapshot, paged rendition and playlist read routes, `preview.png`, an immutable `preview.json` frame/timing manifest, indexed frame PNGs, compatibility metadata and minimal current-media identity/playlist position. Owner-approved follow-up, 2026-09-30: use lossless frame-based animation and support complete admitted GIFs beyond the historical two-frame/500-ms smoke profile.
- `apps/hub`: accept the new minor version alongside `pixoo-integration/1.0` in `pixoo-integration.ts` and the pinned fixtures, reusing the Pixoo-owned contract. Coordinate with #246 only if its behavior-preserving refactor overlaps; it does not own or block this new wire version. Add read-only hub routes that forward to the Pixoo controller with the registered controller token:
  - `GET /api/controllers/v1/:id/integration/catalog/renditions`, `.../catalog/playlists` and `.../catalog/playlists/:playlistId`, paged with the Pixoo bounds (`limit` 1 to 100, default 25).
  - `GET /api/controllers/v1/:id/integration/renditions/:renditionId/preview.png`, `.../preview.json` and `.../frames/:index.png`, forwarding validated manifest/frame responses and their representation-specific strong ETags/cache headers. Conditional 304 handling retains authorization and current catalog-membership checks.
  These are typed per-route forwards, not a raw URL proxy, and they require `read` scope on the hub token. The browser never receives the Pixoo token.
- `apps/dashboard`: three widgets on the #277 widget interface, registered in the widget catalog (#366) and composed on the Pixoo component page by default:
  - **Pixoo media grid**: renditions with still thumbnails; selecting one animates its cached PNG frames using the effective timing manifest at native size with nearest-neighbor scaling. Use bounded frame buffering/prefetch, loading/error states and cancellation on selection change or widget unmount. Network arrival time must not become the intended frame delay; browser scheduling remains illustrative. Sizes medium and large.
  - **Pixoo playlists**: the playlist list; selecting one shows its filmstrip of items with duration or play count. Sizes medium and large.
  - **Pixoo now showing**: the current rendition's animated preview with the playlist name and position, resolved from the negotiated snapshot and catalog. Distinguish current/requested/last-sent/uncertain observations; unavailable or stale state is visible, and the widget does not claim optically observed output. Sizes small and medium. This is the card meant for the home grid.
  Playlist selection in the existing general controls shows names when present, and IDs otherwise. Each widget renders identically wherever the owner places it (#366).
- Read-only. Editing playlists and uploading media stay in the Pixoo web UI until #25 moves the Pixoo source into this repository, when the Pixoo page becomes the single UI (#271).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device. These routes and views issue no device commands and never touch the Pixoo adapter queue. The existing general controls, guards and command ledger are unchanged.
- Credentials stay with their owning services. The browser sees hub routes only; the Pixoo token stays in hub configuration.
- Strict contract validation in both directions. A 1.0 Pixoo keeps working with the catalog features hidden and a visible "not available on this Pixoo version" reason, following the disabled-control rule from #151.
- Revision consistency. Catalog JSON carries `catalogRevision`; detect a mismatch between related reads or a revision change observed in the periodic controller snapshot and refresh the affected view. Immutable rendition IDs bind frames to items. Do not promise atomicity across HTTP requests or discard valid immutable frame bytes solely because an unrelated catalog item changed.
- Bounded work. At most one active HTTP request per device, per the hub README, so preview fetches queue behind each other; the page shows a placeholder rather than firing parallel requests. Lists page at the stated bounds.
- Names include the Pixoo's user-entered names and, per #426/ADR 0005, media titles and filenames. Preserve explicit-label precedence and the existing Pixoo 120-character validation semantics; do not tighten entry to 80 or truncate stored data. No credentials, tokens or raw storage locations appear. Show profile incompatibility or unqualified playback separately from preview availability.
- Accessibility: keyboard access, contrast, reduced motion (animated previews do not autoplay when reduced motion is set) and narrow layouts pass the existing dashboard checks.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] **AC1.** With the fake Pixoo controller advertising the new minor version, the Pixoo page lists renditions and playlists, pages at the bounds, shows a still for each rendition and an animated preview on selection, and shows each playlist's items in order with their policy. Fixtures cover an empty catalog, a playlist without a name, the historical two-frame fixture, an admitted 20-frame GIF with variable non-500-ms delays, duplicate frames, more-than-256-color frames, and a previewable rendition incompatible with the configured device profile. Frame pixels/count/order/delays match the manifest; loading failure never passes as a complete preview.
- [x] **AC2.** Hub route tests: forwards carry the controller token and never expose it; a hub token without `read` gets 403; unknown device 404; unknown rendition forwarded as 404; representation-specific ETag forwarded and 304 returned on match after authorization/membership checks; invalid frame index rejected; no route reserves a controller ticket or writes to the command ledger.
- [x] **AC3.** With a 1.0 fixture, the page renders the general controls exactly as today and shows the catalog section as unavailable with its reason. Existing #151 browser fixtures pass unchanged.
- [x] **AC4.** A `catalogRevision` change observed through the existing periodic controller snapshot refreshes lists and thumbnails; a revision change between requests is detected and no item is paired with pixels belonging to a different rendition. Feed reconnect/resync coalesces to one controller/catalog refresh rather than replaying reads. No new feed event contract is required.
- [x] **AC5.** Accessibility and reduced-motion checks pass; animated previews respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; frame buffering is bounded, inactive/changed selections cancel pending reads, and the existing per-device request limit is preserved.
- [x] **AC6.** Issue-linked OpenSpec change for the `unified-dashboard` and hub contract deltas; `npm run test:dashboard`, `npm run test:dashboard:browser` and hub tests pass with the shared checks; independent Standards and Specification reviews; explicit human UI approval recorded in the PR under the SDLC UI approval scope.

**Delivery target:** source-only. Installing the new hub and Pixoo versions on the owner's host, and any live check against the physical Pixoo, are separately authorized steps. Any later live acceptance compares B.U.N.N.Y. and Pixoo web previews for the same rendition; display comparison uses an admitted historical profile or a broader profile qualified by divoom-app-upgrade#55. Preview/source completion does not imply broader hardware support.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Editing playlists or uploading media from B.U.N.N.Y.: use the Pixoo web UI. Add an "Open Pixoo app" link on the Pixoo page. Revisit when #25 moves the Pixoo source into this repository and #271 defines the device page.
- Previews of the original file rather than the effective rendition: not planned; previews show prepared 64×64 frames, with device compatibility reported separately.
- Rendition-level selection from the general controls, so a routine or the operator can show one GIF: divoom-app-upgrade#13 adds the command; this story only makes rendition IDs and previews visible.
- Routine and schedule authoring that uses these previews: #45.
- Broader device-mode import and physical GIF playback: divoom-app-upgrade#55. Preview every cataloged rendition within the application resource budget regardless of device-profile compatibility. Do not inherit the two-frame/500-ms smoke restriction in these widgets. #55 is not a prerequisite for read-only source acceptance here.

### Work assessment

Planning reassessment, 2026-09-30, after owner-approved preview/name corrections and expanded GIF direction; live Pixoo #96/#55 and current frame-based Pixoo preview implementation inspected.

- **Complexity: medium.** Typed catalog/manifest/frame forwards, version negotiation and three widgets with bounded animation loading and snapshot-driven catalog refresh and feed resync.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The revised producer contract is specified in #96 but not delivered; browser buffering and request serialization need consumer tests.
- **Impact: medium.** Authentication, strict proxy validation and bounded media reads affect the Hub and browser; no device writes are added.

**Readiness:** source delivery is accepted. [PR #676](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/676) merged at `782f25cb201d60947ec2526bf6cdfb89acc11bbd` after independent Standards and Specification reviews, all seven current-head CI jobs and explicit owner approval of the current UI. All seven merged-main Depot jobs passed. The owning-service check passed against delivered Pixoo #96 at `47c0fb2681ee27807f88a3a07bd713ab05bcdc81`; that native prerequisite remains as completed provenance. Installation and physical comparison remain outside this source-only finish line.

Related: #151, #154, #246, #271, #25, #45, #333, #277, #366, divoom-app-upgrade#96, divoom-app-upgrade#13.

Amended 2026-09-25: the dashboard work is three widgets on the #277 interface, placeable through #366, rather than a page section.

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match.

Delivery pickup, 2026-09-30: the owner explicitly requested coordinated delivery of Pixoo #96, Pixoo #55 and Hub #353. One coordinator owns durable repository and tracker writes; isolated workers prepare bounded proposals. This overrides the standalone-session execution recommendation for this active delivery. Source, UI, installation and physical evidence remain separate.

## Guide

**Topic:** pixoo-media
**Note:** Read-only Pixoo media grid, playlist filmstrips and animated previews on the B.U.N.N.Y. Pixoo page.

Delivery accepted, 2026-10-01: AC1–AC6 are satisfied by PR #676 and its recorded validation. No native parent, children or dependents were found; the completed #96 prerequisite is preserved. issues.title: Try a moment on a device from B.U.N.N.Y.
issues.body:
> Defined on 2026-09-29 with the owner through grilling; this replaces the 2026-09-25 placeholder and folds in the 2026-09-28 settled points. It defines scope and acceptance; it does not authorize installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

On a moment-capable device's B.U.N.N.Y. page, the owner plays one of the device's declared moods now, for example `celebrate`, and watches it play and end: completed, pre-empted, superseded or interrupted. The owner can see and feel an interlude before any rule, event source or persona exists.

Setup is the installed hub, the owner's browser and one registered controller that serves contract 1.1 with `moments` supported. None does yet; device adoption is codex-nanoleaf#158 and divoom-app-upgrade#92. The [moment explainer](https://claude.ai/artifact/1LHU15QatQmMvbqcLAkTcx) diagrams the flow.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- **Moments card.** A card on the device page, after the existing Mode, Power, Brightness, Media and Scene cards ([`main.tsx`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L84)). It targets that one device. It is shown only when the device's 1.1 snapshot declares `moments` supported, independent of whether the general cards show. Otherwise the card is hidden and the page's undeclared-capabilities line ([`main.tsx`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L85-L88)) names Moments. That line's list, `undeclaredCapabilities`, covers only power, brightness, media and scenes today, and its length check decides whether the general cards show. Adding Moments must not change that decision. The home widget is unchanged. The card follows the [style guide's](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/docs/application-ui-style-guide.md) card grid and density rule, with one short visible line and longer guidance behind Help.
- **Mood choice.** One button each for the three core moods every moment-capable device declares: `celebrate`, `setback` and `reminder`. Extra declared moods appear in a "More moods" menu, and choosing one sends it. Labels are title-cased IDs ("Celebrate"). The menu is absent when the device declares only the core three.
- **Options.**
  - Duration presets of 5, 10 and 30 s, default 10 s, showing only presets within the device's `maxDurationMs`.
  - A "Play over agent status" switch, default on, shown only when the device declares `coversStatus` supported. Otherwise the card sends `coversStatus:false`.
  - No palette: the device uses its own preset for the mood.
- **Send.** Each press sends exactly one moment through the shared command lifecycle ([`controls.tsx`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/dashboard/src/controls.tsx#L43)). It re-reads the device, sends once, shows the result and watches an accepted ticket. After an uncertain result it locks the card until "Reload current values", and it never resubmits. Pressing another mood while one is scheduled or playing sends a new moment, which supersedes the current one under the contract. The result lines keep receipts' transmission-only meaning:
  - "Celebrate: Scheduled on <device>." (`queued`)
  - "Not played: <device> is in Quiet." (`moment-blocked`)
  - "Not played: it missed its start window." (`moment-missed`)
  - "Not sent: this controller serves API 1.0." (the sender's not-sent reasons)
  - "Result unknown", with "Reload current values" (`uncertain`)
- **Live state.** A line from the 1.1 snapshot's `state.moment`:
  - "Scheduled: Celebrate";
  - "Playing Celebrate, 7 s left";
  - "Last moment: completed 4 s ago", or pre-empted by an alert, superseded or interrupted. The snapshot's `last` carries the moment ID and ending but no mood, so the line names the mood only when this page sent that moment ID ("Last: Celebrate, completed 4 s ago").

  While a moment is scheduled or playing, the page re-reads that one device every 1 s, stopping 5 s after the moment ends. Otherwise it keeps the normal 5 s poll. The card reads through #576's `GET /api/controllers/v1/:id/snapshot?apiVersion=1.1`.
- **Send route.** `POST /api/controllers/v1/:id/moment` with `control` scope and the hub's `X-Pixoo-Request: 1` mutation header. The body is `{mood, durationMs, coversStatus}`. The hub assigns a fresh `momentId` and `priorityClass:"event"`, uses the sender's default start of now, calls #335's single-device sender once and returns its typed result. The route is authorized for that one device like the existing controller routes ([`server.ts`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L314-L318)). The hub applies no arbitration: this is an explicit owner command, and the device's own precedence still applies (Quiet blocks it, an alert pre-empts it on status). There is no MCP tool, because an agent calling one would skip #295's arbitration.
- **Fixture and verification.**
  - [`apps/dashboard/tests/fixture.mjs`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/dashboard/tests/fixture.mjs) gains a moment-capable 1.1 fake, reusing #576's and #335's shared fake where practical.
  - [Hub verification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/apps/hub/verify/README.md) gains steps `moment-plays`, `moment-blocked-on-status` and `moment-uncertain-no-replay`. They are registered in `apps/hub/verify/plugin.mjs` and its step tests, and recorded in the feature map. The reference-step count in docs/development.md and docs/app-verification.md is updated to match.

Dependencies: #576 (the 1.1 snapshot route) and #335 (the sender). Both are open, and #336 is natively blocked by both. #292 is closed.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device: the send goes through #335's sender and the controller's own queue and ticket.
- Every press sends at most one moment. Reads, polls, the faster refresh, reloads and reconnects send nothing.
- Receipts never claim that the owner saw the moment. The live line reports the device's `state.moment`, not the hub's intent.
- 1.0 devices and 1.0 readers keep working unchanged. The home widget and other cards are unchanged.
- The browser never receives device credentials. Scope, origin and mutation-header checks apply to the new route as they do to existing control routes.
- Keyboard access, contrast, reduced motion and narrow layouts pass the existing dashboard checks.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Evidence is dashboard browser tests and hub route tests with fake controllers and a fake clock, plus a Hub verification run on the PR head.

- [ ] **AC1. Card presence.** The card appears for a moment-capable 1.1 fake. For a 1.0 fake it is absent and the undeclared-capabilities line names Moments. The home widget is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2. Moods, duration and switch.**
  - A fake declaring the core three plus two extras shows three buttons and a two-item "More moods" menu; a core-only fake shows no menu.
  - With `maxDurationMs: 20000`, only the 5 s and 10 s presets show.
  - The status switch shows, defaulting on, only when `coversStatus` is supported.
  - Requests never carry `palette`.
- [ ] **AC3. One send per press.** Each button, menu choice and preset sends exactly one moment with the chosen mood, duration and `coversStatus`. The command spy sees no command from browsing, polling, the faster refresh or a reload.
- [ ] **AC4. Outcomes and wording.**
  - Each result shows its line: `queued`, `moment-blocked` (with the switch off on a Work-mode fake, and in Quiet), `moment-missed`, the 1.0-only not-sent reason, and `uncertain`.
  - `uncertain` locks the card until "Reload current values" and is never resent.
  - A second press while a moment plays supersedes it, and the live line shows "superseded".
- [ ] **AC5. Live line and refresh.** On the fake clock the line moves from Scheduled to Playing to Last with the right ending. It names the mood only for a moment this page sent. The 1 s reads start only while a moment is current and stop within 5 s of its end. A hidden card makes no extra reads.
- [ ] **AC6. Route.**
  - `read` scope gets `forbidden`.
  - A missing mutation header, an undeclared mood or an out-of-range duration is rejected with a typed error and no send.
  - A valid request calls the sender exactly once and returns its typed result.
- [ ] **AC7. Verification and UI approval.** The new Hub verification steps pass in a run on the PR head. The owner approves the UI from that run's preview under the [UI approval scope](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/docs/sdlc.md#ui-approval-scope), and the approval names the run.
- [ ] **AC8. Delivery.**
  - An issue-linked OpenSpec change with deltas for `unified-dashboard` (the card) and `standalone-hub-host` (the route).
  - The [Dashboard checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/docs/development.md#dashboard-checks), including `npm run test:hub:verify`, plus the standalone hub and shared build, type, contract and workflow checks.
  - A PR walkthrough, as the [scope defaults](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/88dc56f/docs/sdlc.md#scope-defaults) require for device commands: writer ownership, the one-send rule, uncertain and restart behavior, the important failure test, and diagnosis.
  - Independent Standards and Specification reviews.
  - Current-head and merged-revision CI.

**Delivery target:** source-only. Installing the hub, and pressing a mood on the physical Lines or Pixoo, are separately authorized steps. They need codex-nanoleaf#158 or divoom-app-upgrade#92 installed.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Mood buttons on the home widget** (deferred). Revisit if the device page proves too far away for trying moods.
- **Several devices at once:** #297.
- **Palettes:** #297 and #400.
- **Durations above 30 s** (deferred). Revisit if a longer try is wanted; the contract allows up to 300 s.
- **An MCP send tool:** #295 owns agent proposals.
- **Showing the moment on the device art:** #432.
- **A history of more than the last moment:** #296.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-29, base `88dc56f`.

- **Operating assumptions:** one operator; the installed hub and browser; no 1.1 device yet (codex-nanoleaf#158, divoom-app-upgrade#92).
- **Complexity: medium.** One card with mood, duration and status controls, a bounded faster refresh, one control route, a fixture fake and three verification steps. All of it builds on the existing command lifecycle and #335's sender.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The owner settled placement, the controls, wording, refresh, the route and approval on 2026-09-29. The inputs come from #576 and #335.
- **Impact: medium.** It adds a new control route that sends an owner command to a device. Scope checks, one send per press, the uncertain lock and the device's own guards bound a defect.
- **Readiness:** defined; blocked by #576 and #335.
- **Portfolio:** standalone, with no parent epic, Phase or Commitment. The current phase is Ask the guide (#509), so delivery needs the owner's explicit selection.
- **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews, an accessibility check, and explicit owner UI approval.

**Settled 2026-09-28 (owner, #335 definition):** the owner's send skips hub arbitration, the device's own precedence applies, and reads go through #576's `?apiVersion=1.1` route. These points are now in the sections above.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Highlight:** idea, Try any declared mood on a device from B.U.N.N.Y. and watch how the moment ends.
**Extends:** H292, H296, H271

issues.title: Send moments from the hub through controller contract 1.1
issues.body:
> Defined on 2026-09-28 with the owner through plan-work and grilling, and rescoped the same day at the owner's request. Version negotiation and the 1.1 reads moved to #576, which blocks this story. It defines scope and acceptance; it does not authorize installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

The hub has one shared moment sender. A caller hands it one moment and one target device, and the sender delivers the moment through the contract 1.1 `moment` command and returns one typed result. Callers that address several devices call it once per device and fan out concurrently. The callers are rules and routines (#358, #359), agent proposals (#295), choreography (#297) and the owner's "try a mood" control (#336). Today the hub's controller client cannot send a moment: its command path validates only a 1.0 request ([`controllers.ts`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/apps/hub/src/controllers.ts#L71-L80)), and it rejects a busy slot immediately instead of waiting ([`controllers.ts`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/apps/hub/src/controllers.ts#L31)).

Setup is the installed hub with its registered controllers, read at 1.1 through #576. No registered controller serves 1.1 yet; device adoption is codex-nanoleaf#158 and divoom-app-upgrade#92.

The [moment explainer](https://claude.ai/artifact/1LHU15QatQmMvbqcLAkTcx) diagrams the flow.

### Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

In delivery order, each unit its own commit:

1. **Bounded slot wait.** An opt-in wait in the controller client of at most about 2.5 s for the controller's busy slot, used only by sends. Dashboard and MCP reads keep today's immediate `capacity` rejection. This is the one change to the existing one-slot-per-controller model, and it is testable with the existing 1.0 fakes before anything else lands. It is a candidate for its own small PR if the reviewer wants the concurrency change in isolation.
2. **Fake controller extensions.** #576's shared 1.1 fake under `apps/hub/tests` gains moment admission answers, a holdable slot and a command spy. #358 reuses it.
3. **1.1 command path.** The client gains a moment command: it validates `requestV1_1`, POSTs to `/commands` once, validates `receiptV1_1` and the echoed ticket, and reports `uncertain-result` on a mismatch or lost response. The 1.0 command path is unchanged.
4. **Moment sender.** An internal hub module; it adds no route, no MCP tool and no page. One call sends one moment to one device:
   1. Wait for that controller's busy slot for at most about 2.5 s.
   2. Read a fresh 1.1 snapshot through #576's negotiated read.
   3. Build one `requestV1_1`:
      - the ticket from `nextRequestId`;
      - `expectedConfigurationRevision` and `expectedGeneration` from that snapshot;
      - `start.epoch` from `sampleClock.epoch`;
      - `start.atMs` as `sampleClock.sampledAtMs` plus the difference, on the hub's monotonic clock, between the snapshot's arrival and the requested start instant;
      - `toleranceMs` defaulting to 10,000, which a caller may set up to the contract's 60,000.
   4. POST the request once.

   The caller supplies `momentId`, `mood`, optional `palette`, `durationMs`, `priorityClass` and `coversStatus`, and the sender passes them through unchanged. The caller may also give a start instant on the hub's monotonic clock. The default is now. A caller that sends one moment to several devices computes that instant once and passes it to each call, so every device gets the same hub instant in its own clock. A start more than 60,000 ms ahead is rejected locally.
5. **Typed per-device result.** Each call returns one of three results:
   - the controller's receipt (outcome and any typed failure);
   - a not-sent reason with zero POSTs: `1.0-only`, `moments-unsupported`, `unsupported-capability` (undeclared mood or a duration above `maxDurationMs`), `capacity` (slot wait expired) or `unavailable`;
   - `uncertain` after a timeout or lost response.

   Each result carries the `momentId` and computed `start`, so callers can log and display it.

- **No policy in the sender.** It applies no quiet hours, budgets, global switch or interrupt set; callers arbitrate. #358 arbitrates rules and routines, and #295 arbitrates agent proposals. An owner's explicit send (#336) is an explicit command: the hub applies no arbitration to it, and the device's own precedence still applies.
- **No durable state.** The sender keeps nothing queued and writes no SQLite table. The device's start window, clock epoch and `momentId` memory already make a stale or repeated delivery harmless. A history of sent moments is #296's.
- **No group send.** Independence between devices comes from the caller's concurrent fan-out (for example `Promise.allSettled` over one call per device), not from a batch entry point. #297 owns any group wrapper.

Dependencies: #576 (blocks this story; version negotiation, the per-controller verdict, the 1.1 reads and the shared fake) and #292 (closed; [`controller-contracts-v1.1.0`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/controller-contracts-v1.1.0) is released and the hub already pins `@jimmie-potts/device-contracts` 1.1.0). #358 builds against a fake sender until this lands. #336, #359's moment action (see the 2026-09-28 amendment there), #295, #297 and #432 consume it.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device. The hub goes through each controller's own queue and ticket sequence, and the existing one-slot-per-controller client stays in place. The wait applies only to sends; reads keep their immediate rejection.
- 1.0 controllers and 1.0 readers keep working unchanged: dashboard polls, MCP commands (which keep `apiVersion:'1.0'`), Tidbyt and LIFX through the local controller host, and every existing hub test.
- The hub never resends a moment, whether inside or after its start window, and never sends one after a hub restart.
- Reads, reconnects and dashboard polls never send commands.
- Semantic intents only: no frames, raw protocol or geometry.
- Receipts keep their transmission-only meaning. `queued` or `sent` never claims that a person saw the moment.
- Stored and returned data holds no credentials or tokens.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Acceptance examples for a consequential device-command change, per the [scope defaults](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/docs/sdlc.md#scope-defaults). Evidence is hub tests over loopback HTTP against the shared fake 1.0-only and 1.1 controllers from #576, with an injected monotonic clock and a command spy.

- [ ] **AC1. Slot wait.**
  - A send while a dashboard read holds the slot waits, then sends once.
  - A slot still held after the bound returns `capacity` with zero POSTs.
  - A dashboard read during a held slot still gets the immediate `capacity` rejection.
- [ ] **AC2. Request built from the snapshot.**
  - For a 1.1 fake declaring `moments`, one send produces exactly one POST.
  - The request validates as `requestV1_1`, and its ticket, expected revision and generation match the snapshot read just before it.
  - `start.epoch` equals `sampleClock.epoch`, and `start.atMs` equals `sampledAtMs` plus the injected hub-clock difference between the snapshot's arrival and the requested start instant.
  - Two calls given the same start instant for two fakes with different clocks produce the same hub instant in each device's clock.
  - `toleranceMs` defaults to 10,000; a caller value above 60,000 and a start more than 60,000 ms ahead are each rejected before any read.
  - Caller fields arrive unchanged, and a flourish with `coversStatus:true` is rejected locally.
- [ ] **AC3. Not sent, zero POSTs.** A 1.0-only target, a target declaring moments unsupported, an undeclared mood and a duration above `maxDurationMs` each return their typed not-sent reason. The command spy records no moment POST.
- [ ] **AC4. Ambiguity and receipts.**
  - A lost response or timeout returns `uncertain` after exactly one POST.
  - Device receipts return typed with no resend: `moment-missed`, `moment-blocked`, `moment-duplicate`, `revision-conflict`, `stale-generation` and `request-*`.
- [ ] **AC5. Independence.** Three concurrent single-device sends of one moment with one target offline: the other two are sent, and each call returns its own result.
- [ ] **AC6. No replay.** A hub restart sends nothing. Snapshot reads, reconnects and dashboard polls produce zero command POSTs, and the sender writes no durable state.
- [ ] **AC7. Delivery.**
  - An issue-linked OpenSpec change with a delta for `standalone-hub-host` (the bounded slot wait, the 1.1 command path and the moment sender).
  - The standalone hub and hub MCP checks in [docs/development.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/0b47580/docs/development.md), plus the shared build, type, contract and workflow checks.
  - A PR walkthrough, as the scope defaults require for device commands: writer ownership, timeout, restart and duplicate behavior, the important failure test, and diagnosis.
  - Independent Standards and Specification reviews.
  - Current-head and merged-revision CI.

**Delivery target:** source-only. Installing the hub and any live moment on a physical device are separately authorized steps. They also need a controller that serves 1.1 (codex-nanoleaf#158 or divoom-app-upgrade#92) and a caller (#336 or #358).

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Version negotiation, the versioned snapshot route, the MCP `status` read at 1.1 and controller feed reads.** #576, which also records the feed-read and timed re-probe deferrals.
- **A group send entry point** (deferred). Callers fan out per device; #297 owns choreography and any wrapper it needs. No current caller loses anything: #358 hands moments over per target and #336 sends to one device.
- **Showing moments in B.U.N.N.Y.** #336 adds "try a mood" and shows `state.moment`, #432 plays the moment on the device art, and #360's forms use the declared moods. Until then, moment state is visible through MCP `status` and the `?apiVersion=1.1` route from #576.
- **A send route or MCP tool.** #336 owns the owner's send, #295 agent proposals, and #358 and #359 rules and routines.
- **History of sent moments** (deferred). #296 owns it. `state.moment` shows the current moment (with mood) and the last ending.

issues.title: Show real LIFX power in B.U.N.N.Y. and stop presenting controls a device cannot use
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

These problems were found during #289's installed check on 2026-09-25. The setup was B.U.N.N.Y. on the installed hub 0.3.5, the LIFX A19 `pendant-1`, the LIFX Beam `beam` and the Tidbyt, all served by the local controller host.

- The bulb was off, but its Power control showed "On". Power was unknown, and the control starts at "On" as an unlabeled placeholder. Because the placeholder already read "On", turning the bulb on meant sending Off and then On. A brightness change does not turn a bulb on, so it had no visible effect until then.
- The Tidbyt page, and `beam`'s, shows four disabled general-control forms. They look clickable because disabled buttons are only drawn at half opacity.

Wanted: opening a LIFX bulb shows its actual on or off state within a few seconds. The Power control starts from what is known, or asks when nothing is. A device with no controls says so in one line. Disabled buttons look disabled everywhere in B.U.N.N.Y.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **Host, on-demand read.** When a qualified LIFX bulb's snapshot is read, through the v1 or the lighting route, and the bulb has no reading, or its last reading is 30 s old or more, the host queues one read-only `refresh()` (LightGet) through the bulb's queue. The snapshot answers at once from memory, and the next dashboard read, about 5 s later, shows the result. Reads are limited to one per bulb per 30 s, and happen only while something reads the snapshot. Unqualified bulbs such as `beam` are never read.
- **Dashboard Power control.** Start from desired power when known, otherwise from the observed power when known, otherwise from no selection, with a hint that current power is unknown. Show the last reading and its age in the hint.
- **Dashboard devices without controls.** General controls show a form only for each declared capability, plus one line naming the undeclared ones. A component that declares none of them, like the Tidbyt, shows one line only. This removes the same dead forms from the LIFX pages (media and scenes), the Pixoo (scenes) and the wall (media); it was refined during delivery on 2026-09-25. A LIFX bulb whose lighting capabilities declare neither color nor temperature gets one line for Lighting.
- **Disabled buttons,** across B.U.N.N.Y.: a clearly distinct disabled style from skin tokens, keeping contrast checks passing.

Dependencies: none. Related: #20 (automatic LIFX status, unchanged).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Reads only. The host sends no Set messages and never paints, and a manual change in the LIFX app stays until the next explicit command. Traffic goes only to configured, qualified bulbs, through each bulb's queue within `maxPending`. A read never reserves a request ID or changes a configuration revision or generation. A failed read keeps the last observation and its age.
- With no snapshot readers, the host sends no traffic.
- The Tidbyt stays status only. Pixoo and Nanoleaf controls are unchanged except for the Power starting rule and the disabled styling. A Nanoleaf whose power is unknown now also starts with no selection instead of "On".
- Command guards, receipts, locks and the shared command lifecycle are unchanged.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installation is a separate step, on the owner's explicit request.

- Host tests with fake transports:
  - A snapshot read of a bulb with no reading, or one 30 s old, queues exactly one LightGet.
  - Repeated reads inside 30 s, and reads while a read is queued, send nothing.
  - With no reads, there is no traffic, and an unqualified bulb is never read.
  - A failed read keeps the previous observation.
  - Request IDs are unchanged.
- Dashboard browser checks, with the real host and fakes:
  - With power unknown, both On and Off can be sent.
  - With an observed-off bulb, the control starts at Off and the hint shows the reading.
  - Tidbyt and `beam` each show one line and no forms.
  - LIFX, Pixoo and wall pages show no form for an undeclared capability.
  - Disabled buttons have a distinct computed style, and the accessibility scan passes.
- UI approval by the owner on the current candidate.
- After an authorized install: opening `pendant-1` shows its real power within a few seconds.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Beam support: multizone qualification of product 38 in the LIFX controller. Until then `beam` has no controls; manage it in the LIFX app. Revisit when the owner wants Beam controls.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `9f13c08`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One bounded, read-triggered refresh in the host; the Power starting rule, a no-controls line and disabled styling in the dashboard. The existing command lifecycle is untouched.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The LIFX controller already has a read-only `refresh()`. The owner asked for the on-load read on 2026-09-25, knowing it relaxes #289's "never reads on its own".
- **Impact: low to medium.** It adds bulb reads while B.U.N.N.Y. is open, and changes shared UI for every device.
- **Readiness: ready.**

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Real LIFX power on page load, no dead controls for status-only devices, and clearly disabled buttons.

issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Show the dashboard's general controls for the NL22 Light Panels. [codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113) ([PR #164](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/164)) makes the Panels a second Nanoleaf controller device. The Panels' `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot is read-only: it keeps the exact key set, but it marks `settings.set`, `elements.assign`, `task.assign` and `project.color` as `{supported: false, scope: "control"}` and lists no elements. Setup: one operator and the Linux Nanoleaf installation with the Lines (`wall`) and the Panels (`panels`) as two hub controller entries sharing one endpoint and credential.

Today two things block it:

- `validateIntegrationSnapshot` (`apps/hub/src/integration.ts:39`) requires `supported: true` for all four operations, so `integrationSnapshot()` throws `incompatible-controller` for the Panels.
- The dashboard (`apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx:270`) loads the v1 snapshot and the integration snapshot in one `try`. When the integration read fails, it never stores the v1 snapshot, so the Panels page shows "General controls unavailable: no controller snapshot". The hub's v1 routes work for the Panels.

### Smallest useful implementation

- Accept `supported: false` (with `scope: "control"`) for the four configuration operations in `validateIntegrationSnapshot`, and hide or disable the matching edit forms when an operation is unsupported.
- Optionally, keep the v1 snapshot and general controls when the integration snapshot fails.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The closed validation of every other key.
- The Lines' snapshot shape and editing.
- The hub browser never receives credentials.
- No new routes.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- A hub test fixture for a read-only Nanoleaf integration snapshot validates.
- The dashboard shows mode, power, brightness and scene controls for that component, with no configuration edit forms.
- Existing Nanoleaf and Pixoo fixtures still pass.

### Meaningful deferrals

Panels animations and configuration edits through the extension remain Nanoleaf-side work: the #92 follow-up and codex-nanoleaf#47.

### Guide placement

Nanoleaf devices: the Panels gain dashboard control once codex-nanoleaf#113 is installed.

## Guide

**Note:** Dashboard controls for a Nanoleaf device whose integration snapshot is read-only, so the Panels page shows mode, power, brightness and scenes.

issues.title: Refresh the work guide nightly into one rolling pull request
issues.body:
Owner: Hub `.github/workflows/` and guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

Every night a scheduled workflow refreshes the work guide's saved GitHub data, rebuilds the guide, runs its checks, and, when the committed output changed, opens or updates one rolling pull request with a plain report of what moved: stories opened, closed or relabelled, topic counts, recommendation labels that went stale, and whether the Direction narrative still fits. Today every one of those steps is manual: an "intentional guide revision" happens only when a session decides to run `refresh_backlogs.py`, hand-edits `work/history/github-history.json`, rebuilds and opens a PR. On 2026-09-25 the published guide's "Useful next steps" named three stories that had merged that day, and #290 and today's merges were absent until the next hand refresh.

The nightly PR is the starting point for the human step, not a replacement for it. The Direction narrative in `work/guide_direction.py` stays owner-written: when a cited story closed, the refresh check fails as #290 designed, the PR says so, and the owner rewrites the text before it can merge. Nothing merges or publishes on its own; that is [#317](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/317) gated by #240.

Setup: the hub repository on GitHub Actions with its `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the three public source repositories, the existing generator and checks. Excluded: merging, publishing the public edition, editing issues, re-rendering diagrams, and any change to the guide-only CI exception.

## Smallest useful implementation

issues.title: Record the 2026-09-25 delivery gotchas in the development and SDLC docs
issues.body:
Owner: `docs/development.md`, `docs/sdlc.md`, `docs/system-design/export_public.py`.

## Outcome and real setup

The gotchas that session closeouts on 2026-09-25 proposed for the docs are in the docs. Each was reported at least once as "worth adding", two of them by two different sessions, and none landed, because the only durable path a closeout had was memory.

Setup: the hub documentation read by every delivery session. Excluded: product behavior, CI changes, tooling.

## Smallest useful implementation

One docs-only PR:

- `docs/sdlc.md`, review and merge: pass an explicit `--body` to `gh pr merge --squash`; by default it copies the PR description into the commit and a "close #n" line closes the issue at merge, before post-merge checks (happened to #252).
- `docs/sdlc.md`, review and merge: a branch named `...issue-<n>...` can make GitHub close issue n at merge even when the body only says "Refs"; before merging when acceptance comes after the merge, read the PR's `closingIssuesReferences` and read back the issue state, not just its labels (happened to #87).
- `docs/development.md`, hub and setup checks: those suites refuse a `TMPDIR` inside any git checkout, so the global `.local/scratch` advice does not apply; use a folder under `~/.cache/agent-device-hub/`.
- `docs/development.md`, Tidbyt checks: the system Python lacks Pillow; create a venv and install `requirements-contracts.txt` before `npm run test:tidbyt:python` (reported by the #222 and #241 closeouts).
- `docs/development.md`, process checks: `pgrep -f <pattern>` matches the agent's own shell; inspect `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for node processes instead.
- `docs/development.md`, workflow section: OpenSpec 1.12 rejects a MODIFIED requirement that drops or renames a scenario; use REMOVED plus ADDED.
- `docs/system-design/export_public.py:58`: the comment still says "private Hub repository"; the repositories are public since #261.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Commands, contracts and evidence rules in both documents are unchanged; these are additions and one comment fix.
- Line length and wording follow the existing document style.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, one hub PR. Full CI applies because `docs/development.md` is outside the guide filter.

1. Each of the seven items appears in the named file, at the named section, with the trigger and the fix in one or two sentences.
2. `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero; the doc link check passes.
3. Independent Standards and Specification reviews; guarded squash merge with an explicit `--body`.

## Meaningful deferrals

- The codex-nanoleaf docs items (in-place upgrade, `codex exec` stdin, hand-listed bridge modules) are that repository's, filed separately.
- A general "closeout gotchas" page: not now; each item belongs beside the command it qualifies.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`. Complexity low. Uncertainty low, every item has a session transcript or issue behind it. Impact low. Readiness ready.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Note:** Seven closeout gotchas from 2026-09-25 that never left memory.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `medium` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/310. I started this session on Sonnet at medium effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/310. I started this session on gpt-6-luna at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-luna; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; the low-effort row fits only trivial, mechanical work.

issues.title: Show recommended creative and expansion stories in a guide Ideas section
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader of the cross-project work guide finds one **Ideas** section beside the Timeline and Direction sections. It lists every open story that its owners have marked as a creative or expansion idea: a new capability, a generalization across devices or repositories, or a user-visible win that recent work made cheap. Each entry shows the story with its live status relabel, the one-line observation that prompted it, the stories it would build on, and its existing scheduling state (candidate, blocked, deferred). Entries are grouped by the topic each story already lives in, so a reader sees where the idea lands without leaving the guide's vocabulary.

The mark lives in the story, not in a curated file. A story says `**Highlight:** idea, <what prompted it>` in its `## Guide` section and may add `**Extends:** <story keys>`. The Direction section's "Later ideas" list is derived from those marks instead of the hand-written `IDEAS` list in `work/guide_direction.py`, following the same move [#259](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/259) made for topics and highlights. Today the expansion stories filed on 2026-09-25 ([#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267), [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271), [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272), [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292) to [#298](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298), the Nanoleaf animation family and Pixoo #91 to #94) sit in their device topics with nothing that distinguishes a placeholder idea from a defect fix in the same table.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, snapshot inputs, checks and public edition. Excluded: a new GitHub label, tracker automation, changes to any session closeout prompt, ranking ideas by value, publication, and any product behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Grammar** in `work/guide_section.py`: a fourth `Highlight` kind, `idea`, with the same `<kind>, <reason>` shape; an optional `**Extends:** <keys>` line, valid only beside an `idea` highlight, whose keys use the guide's `H<n>`, `N<n>`, `P<n>` form and must exist in the snapshot. An `Extends` without `idea`, an unknown key, or a malformed line makes the section unreadable and fails the snapshot build naming the story, exactly like the existing rules. `work/story_sections.py` stays the shared engine. The three repositories' feature issue templates name `idea` and `Extends` in the Guide placement description (companion PRs in codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade, as #259 did).
- **Section** in `work/guide_ideas.py`, inserted by `build_guide.py` after Direction as `<details class="reference ideas" id="ideas">` with a sidebar entry "I · Ideas" whose count is the number of marked open stories. Entries group by topic in `guide_paths.TOPICS` order and, within a topic, by story key. Each entry renders the story through `issue_link`, the reason literally, the `Extends` keys through `issue_link`, and the scheduling state from the existing `guide_status.scheduling_state`. A note states that ideas are counted in their topics, not here, and that the mark is a placement, not a priority. The section joins search, Expand all and print, uses role tokens only, and has no decoration or motion.
- **Direction** in `work/guide_direction.py`: remove the curated `IDEAS` list; the "Later ideas" subsection renders the marked stories in compact form and links to the Ideas section. The existing `check()` also fails, naming the key, when a story in `SEQUENCE` carries an `idea` highlight, because "build next" and "later idea" are exclusive.
- **Live path** in `work/guide_overview.js`: the same grammar re-parses each successfully read repository's open bodies. A story newly marked or moved in since the snapshot lands in a "Newly added since the snapshot" block inside its topic group of the Ideas section; a story that closes live or loses its mark is removed; existing rows patch their reason and `Extends` in place. A repository whose read fails keeps the snapshot's rows. The freshness line names the Ideas section among the live parts.
- **Migration**, at an owner checkpoint: the delivery session reads the live tracker, proposes the exact list of stories to mark with a one-line reason drawn from each story's own text and its `Extends` keys from stated parents (for example #267 extends [#67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67); #271 and #272 extend codex-nanoleaf#47; Nanoleaf #158 and Pixoo #92 extend #292), and stops for approval before writing. Candidates: the seven keys the current curated `IDEAS` list cites, the 2026-09-25 placeholders, [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282), [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283), [#286](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/286) to [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289), the Nanoleaf animation stories and Pixoo #91 to #94. Writes go through the existing section render helper with a dry run first and receipts outside Git, the way #259 migrated topics.
- **Procedure**: `docs/work-guide/README.md` documents the `idea` kind, `Extends`, the Ideas section and the derived Later ideas; the Direction paragraph drops `IDEAS` from the saved-input list.

Dependencies: none required. [#290](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/290) (Direction) and #259 (guide sections) are delivered and are the seams this builds on. [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) edits the same sidebar; whichever lands second rebases. [#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) may later report an idea story that closed without its mark being reviewed.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- GitHub issues stay authoritative for scope and status. `idea` is a placement mark, not a status, a label or a priority. It never promotes a blocked, deferred or owner-later story, and the conservative scheduling rules are reused unchanged.
- Topic totals, exact-cover of topics, primary coverage, the archive, history, roadmap and diagram inputs are untouched. The Ideas section adds nothing to issue counts; the sidebar count is informational.
- No new labels, no tracker automation, no new endpoints. Migration writes are one-off, owner-approved edits to public issue bodies with receipts outside Git.
- Two consecutive builds produce identical HTML. Hostile text in a reason or `Extends` renders literally. The public export includes the section and holds only public keys and one-line prose.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. One hub PR under `docs/work-guide/` plus the hub feature template under `.github/`, so full CI applies and the guide-only exception does not; two companion template PRs in codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade. Guide UI needs no human approval under the SDLC UI approval scope.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: an `idea` highlight parses and renders; `Extends` without `idea`, an unknown `Extends` key and a malformed line each fail naming the story; a `SEQUENCE` key marked `idea` fails the direction check naming it; entries group in topic order; the Direction's Later ideas equal the marked set; hostile text is literal; repeated builds are identical.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: the section renders at 390 px and 1440 px without overflow, appears in search, Expand all and print, its links receive live status labels, and with the mocked live read a newly marked story appears in the Newly added block while a closed one is removed.
3. Guide commands pass under Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), the regenerated HTML is committed, and screenshots plus the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
4. Migration: the dry-run diff is reviewed and approved at the checkpoint, every write reads back equal to the rendered section, a rerun reports no change, and receipts are kept outside Git.
5. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the fixed candidate, all applicable CI jobs green on the hub PR and on the merged revision, and green companion PRs. Publication of the public edition is a separate authorized step.
6. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Ranking ideas by leverage, owner order or value: not now. Topic order and key order are enough for the current count; revisit when the section passes about forty entries.
- Filing ideas automatically from session closeouts: belongs to the closeout prompt, which is being revised separately; once it files placeholders with `Highlight: idea`, they appear here without a guide edit.
- An idea lifecycle or promotion state: not chosen. Promoting an idea means editing its story's highlight or adding it to the Direction sequence, and the new check keeps the two exclusive.
- Keeping a hand-written Later ideas list beside the derived one: rejected by the owner on 2026-09-25; derived only.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One grammar extension in an existing parser, one render module, one derived list replacing a curated one, live-path handling that mirrors the existing topic logic, tests, templates and a one-off migration.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The section engine, `issue_link`, scheduling state, the Direction check and the #259 migration pattern all exist; the owner has already settled derivation, migration approval and the `Extends` field.
- **Impact: low.** Documentation output and public issue-body edits; a fault fails the build loudly, and migration writes are reviewed before they happen.
- **Readiness: ready.** No open prerequisite.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Adds the Ideas section and the `idea` highlight kind; a one-off migration marks the existing expansion stories.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `medium` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |
| Checkpoints | the exact list of stories to mark and their Extends keys before any migration write; the Extends grammar if keys-only proves too narrow; the Direction check that rejects an idea in SEQUENCE before the curated list is removed | the exact list of stories to mark and their Extends keys before any migration write; the Extends grammar if keys-only proves too narrow; the Direction check that rejects an idea in SEQUENCE before the curated list is removed |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text

State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: the exact list of stories to mark and their Extends keys before any migration write; the Extends grammar if keys-only proves too narrow; the Direction check that rejects an idea in SEQUENCE before the curated list is removed. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

issues.title: Keep a story's recommendation current when only its Guide section changes
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The work guide shows "Needs reassessment (story text changed after 2026-09-25)" on every open story, and each task brief falls back to the generic Implement prompt. PR #281 wrote a `## Guide` section into all open stories after the #252 assessment pass had fingerprinted them, and `recommendations.fingerprint` hashes the body with only the Execution recommendation removed, so the placement section changed every fingerprint. Stripping the Guide section restores the recorded fingerprint for 110 of the 113 stale stories; the committed guide HTML carries 372 stale labels and 1 current one. Hub #37, Nanoleaf #44 and Nanoleaf #47 were edited after their assessment and are genuinely stale. Real setup: the saved backlogs in `docs/work-guide/work/backlogs/` and the maintainer's guide rebuild.

## Smallest useful implementation

- In `docs/work-guide/work/recommendations.py`, compute the fingerprint from the body with both the Execution recommendation and the Guide section removed, reusing `story_sections.without_section`.
- In `docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, add: a story that gains or edits a Guide section after assessment stays `recommended` with its original date; a scope edit still goes `stale`; `upsert` keeps the recorded date under the new fingerprint.
- Update the fingerprint paragraph in `docs/work-guide/README.md`: the Guide section is placement metadata and does not stale a recommendation, and notes must not carry scope.
- Rebuild the guide from the saved backlogs; run the maintenance tests and `check_guide.cjs`.
- Reassess Hub #37, Nanoleaf #44 and Nanoleaf #47 through `recommendations.py upsert`, dry run first. These three tracker writes are authorized by this story; no other story body changes.

Dependencies: none. Coordinate with any concurrent guide refresh, since both rebuild the same HTML.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

A real scope edit still stales the recommendation. The upsert `read_at` guard, the insufficient and unavailable states, the prompt-outside-fingerprint rule, live GitHub reads and every other guide widget stay as they are. Rerunning `upsert` over all #252 assessor entries is rejected: it would rewrite 110 bodies and move every assessment date to today.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: guide-only source change plus the three named tracker writes.

- [ ] A failing test shows a Guide-only edit staling a recommendation before the change and passing after it.
- [ ] The rebuilt guide shows the 110 affected stories as recommended with their original 2026-09-25 dates; only the three reassessed stories carry a new date, and no open story shows "Needs reassessment".
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py` and `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs` pass.
- [ ] Independent Standards and Specification reviews; the guide-only CI filter exception's evidence rules in docs/sdlc.md are followed for the merged revision.

No application UI change, so no human UI approval. No OpenSpec change.

## Meaningful deferrals

Recommended-versus-actual comparison per delivery is #307.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `f94e1f4`. Complexity low: one function, one test, one README paragraph. Uncertainty low: the cause is reproduced. Impact low: guide presentation. Ready.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Keep every story's starting-session recommendation current when only its Guide placement changes, and reassess the three stories that really changed.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `medium` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/304. I started this session on Sonnet at medium effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/304. I started this session on gpt-6-luna at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-luna; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; the low-effort row fits only trivial, mechanical work.

**Why:** One function, one test and one README paragraph with a reproduced cause, plus three named reassessments through the existing upsert tool. Policy row: bounded implementation with settled requirements and reliable checks.
**Reassess when:** The fingerprint rule changes for another reason, or the three named stories are reassessed elsewhere first.

issues.title: Add the Sonos Move as a selectable playback source with AirPlay play
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner's iPhone streams Apple Music over AirPlay to the Sonos Move, alone or grouped with the Sony HT-A9. The installed standalone hub reads what is playing from the Move and can pause, resume, skip forward and skip back. Resume is new: on 2026-09-25 the Move's local AVTransport `Play` resumed a paused phone session, and with both speakers in the group the HT-A9 followed within half a second; see the [play and resume check](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md#play-and-resume-check). No audio passes through the hub.

Excluded: native Sonos playback such as Apple Music favorites on the Move, position and duration in the snapshot, two concurrently observed sources, group creation from the hub, volume, and the Sonos cloud API.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Add a `sonos` source kind beside `sony` in `apps/hub/src`: `{"id": "...", "kind": "sonos", "endpoint": "http://<private IPv4>:1400"}` with the same ID and endpoint rules as the Sony entry. Poll `GetTransportInfo`, `GetPositionInfo` and `GetCurrentTransportActions` on the local AVTransport every two seconds with the existing timeout and reply bound, reusing a read in progress.
- Normalize: an `x-sonos-vli` track URI is the AirPlay session. `PLAYING`, `PAUSED_PLAYBACK` and `STOPPED` map to playing, paused and stopped; other transport states map to unknown; any other URI or no track is `inactive`. Title, artist and album come from the DIDL-Lite metadata with the same trimming and 256-character limit. Drop the album art URI and every other field.
- Controls: `pause`, `next` and `previous` while playing; `play`, `next` and `previous` while paused; each only when the Move's current transport actions list it. Commands are `Pause`, `Play` with speed 1, `Next` and `Previous`. HTTP 200 is `sent`, a SOAP fault is `failed`, anything else is uncertain. No retries.
- Let `playback.sources` hold up to one Sony and one Sonos entry, and let `selected` name the one the hub polls and commands. The other entry is validated but idle. Switching is a `host.json` edit and a restart. No UI selection and no automatic switching.
- Dependencies: none open. This builds on the [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) contract. The [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) view and MCP tools show `play` as soon as the snapshot declares it.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- One selected source per hub. No command is redirected to another source or address, one command runs at a time, request-ID receipts stay, and uncertain results are never retried.
- The Sony source is unchanged: pause, next and previous while playing, next and previous while paused, never play, per the [#242](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/242) evidence.
- Source-scoped `read` and `control` grants. The Move's address stays in the private configuration and the source ID never carries it.
- A Move that stops answering ages to stale and then unavailable as the Sony does, and a missing read never becomes paused.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

1. Fake AVTransport tests: AirPlay playing, paused and stopped; native content reported as inactive; missing metadata; a SOAP fault versus a timeout; controls following the action list; stale and unavailable aging; endpoint validation; a two-entry configuration where `selected` switches and the other entry stays idle.
2. The existing Hub, MCP and Dashboard suites pass. The hub README's Playback section documents the Sonos kind and the selection rule and links the qualification.
3. After merge, separately authorized: install, select the Move, then in the installed B.U.N.N.Y. and one Codex MCP session pause and resume the phone's stream with both speakers grouped. The owner confirms on the phone and the speakers. Record client behavior separately from receiver readings.

Delivery target: a source PR with independent reviews and CI. Installation and physical acceptance are separate requests.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Position and duration in the snapshot. The Move supplies them and the contract has no fields for them, so progress stays invisible. Revisit when a consumer such as [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) or [#39](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/39) asks for it.
- Sony visibility while the Move is selected. Phone-to-Sony-only playback is not observed until `selected` is switched back in `host.json`. Revisit if two concurrently observed sources become a requirement; the qualification doc's explicit-selection rules then apply.
- Native Sonos playback of Apple Music favorites: owned by [#178](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/178).
- UPnP event subscriptions: polling only. Callbacks across the WSL NAT were not qualified in [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158).
- Group creation, volume and the Sonos cloud API: no current requirement.

## Work assessment

- **Complexity: medium.** A second source kind and the two-entry selection in configuration. The shared playback module is unchanged.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Live-qualified on 2026-09-25 against the owner's Move alone and grouped with the HT-A9; the UPnP surface is documented and stable.
- **Impact: low.** Reversible transport commands to a speaker the owner already controls from the phone.

## Guide

**Topic:** controls-music
**Note:** Play and resume of the phone's AirPlay session through the Sonos Move, with a grouped Sony following. Successor to the [[H242]] qualification; the Sony source itself stays without play.
**Highlight:** next step, the qualified route to hub-issued play for the music controls in [[H37]].

issues.title: Release a controller contract version with a moment command and conformance cases
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-25 as a backlog placeholder at the owner's request. The owner started delivery with `deliver-work` on 2026-09-25 and approved the decisions below the same day.

### Outcome

Controllers receive coordinated moments through one shared, typed command instead of per-device extensions.

### Starting points

- Add a `moment` (or `interlude`) command and a `moments` capability declaring moods, limits and interlude support. The contents follow #291's decision.
- Extend the shared fixture inventory, which has 220 cases today, with moment cases:
  - precedence against alerts;
  - restore to the current base;
  - expiry;
  - a duplicate idempotency key;
  - a mode change mid-interlude;
  - hub-down behavior.
- Follow the contract's compatibility rules: a new version, with v1 consumers unaffected.

### Protections

- Typed commands only; no raw protocol or frames from the hub.
- Existing request tickets, generations and receipts.

### Accepted decisions (owner, 2026-09-25)

These settle the requirements in [ADR 0006](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006-hub-moments-and-interludes.md) and the review comments below.

1. **Start time.** `start` is required and uses the device's own clock: `{domain:"controller-monotonic", epoch, atMs, toleranceMs}`, with `toleranceMs` at most 60,000. The hub computes `atMs` from the device snapshot's `sampleClock` plus its own elapsed time. The device drops the moment with `moment-missed` when the clock epoch differs, when it would start more than `toleranceMs` late, or when `atMs` is more than 60 s ahead.
2. **Moods.** Moods are open neutral IDs that each device declares. Every device with `moments` supported must include the core set `celebrate` (PR merged), `setback` (CI failed) and `reminder` (meeting). An undeclared mood gets `unsupported-capability`.
3. **Priority class.** The classes are `event` and `flourish`. A newer moment replaces the scheduled or playing one when its class is the same or higher, and the replaced moment ends as `superseded`. A flourish that arrives during an event is dropped with a receipt. Only `event` moments may set `coversStatus:true`.
4. **Evidence.** Receipts keep their transmission-only meaning. Admission-time drops use the new 1.1 failure codes `moment-duplicate`, `moment-missed` and `moment-blocked`. The 1.1 snapshot adds `state.moment`, which holds the current moment and the last one that ended, with its reason: `completed`, `preempted`, `superseded` or `interrupted`.
5. **Duration.** The contract allows `durationMs` from 1,000 to 300,000. Each device declares a `maxDurationMs` within that range; a longer moment gets `unsupported-capability`.
6. **Release.** The artifact becomes 1.1.0 and serves API 1.0 and 1.1. The in-repo workspace pins move to 1.1.0 with no behavior change. The Device MCP 1.0.0 archive keeps bundling the released contracts 1.0.0. After merge and green main CI, the coordinator publishes the GitHub release `controller-contracts-v1.1.0` with the archive, its SHA-256 and a receipt, as was done for 1.0.0.

Accepted assumptions:

- Negotiation is opt-in. A client reads the snapshot at its highest version, and the controller answers with the highest version it supports. The client sends moments only after it has read a 1.1 snapshot. A 1.1 controller still accepts 1.0 requests on the same ticket sequence, and a 1.0-only controller rejects a 1.1 request before admission.
- `palette` is optional: 1 to 8 `#rrggbb` colors, which the device may approximate.
- 1.1 capabilities list `moments` explicitly.
- The device-neutral terms are presentation `status`, `content` or `quiet`, and alert `attention` or `failure`. Device mappings are examples: Nanoleaf Work, Free and Quiet with yellow and red alerts; Pixoo Monitor and Media.
- The device remembers at least the last 64 moment IDs for each controller epoch.
- A moment that is blocked when it is due to start is dropped, not deferred.
- Any explicit command or mode change ends an interlude, which ends as `interrupted`.

### Acceptance and planned evidence

- The 1.1 schema accepts the `moment` command, the `moments` capability, the new failure codes and `state.moment`, and rejects out-of-range, missing-core-mood, flourish-covering-status and raw-protocol payloads. Evidence: schema cases run in TypeScript and Python.
- The pure moment reference decides each of the following, as semantic cases run in both languages:
  - alert pre-emption on status, and no pre-emption over content;
  - return to the *current* base;
  - duration expiry;
  - a missed start window and a different clock epoch;
  - a duplicate moment ID;
  - a newer moment superseding, and a flourish dropped during an event;
  - a mode change or an explicit command mid-interlude;
  - skipping in Quiet;
  - hub-down behavior: the device ends its interlude on its own clock, and a late delivery is dropped;
  - a restart that does not replay.
- 1.0 is unaffected. All 220 existing cases pass unchanged, and 1.0 `validate`/`admit` reject a 1.1 request as before. The hub, MCP, Tidbyt and LIFX checks pass on the 1.1.0 workspace pin, and `npm run test:package` passes for the 1.1.0 archive.
- `docs/controller-contract.md` documents 1.1, and an OpenSpec change updates `controller-contracts`.
- After merge: main CI is green and the `controller-contracts-v1.1.0` release is published and read back.

### Deferred
