issues.title: Decide how hub moments and interludes work across devices
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome

One decision record defines how events become coordinated device "moments". The principle is **the hub decides, devices guarantee**:
- Rules, events and agent personality live in the hub.
- Rendering, safety, precedence at execution and restore live in each device controller.

The owner agreed this direction on 2026-09-25, during jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#92's follow-up planning.

### Proposed ADR 0006 outline (number confirmed at filing)

**Context.**
- Hooks and the shared monitor already feed the hub.
- Controller contract v1 is a closed command set, so jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#92 added a Nanoleaf-only `animation.play` extension.
- ADR 0005 keeps content Free/Media-only and forbids automatic restore.
- #45 (rules), #40 (interruption), #267 (coordinated looks) and #139 (event history) each touch part of this.

**Decision (draft).**
1. **Hub owns policy:**
   - event sources and normalization with stable event IDs;
   - rules (#45);
   - agent personas and flourish budgets;
   - quiet hours, rate limits, a global "no flourishes" switch;
   - cross-device choreography;
   - an explainable moment log.
2. **Devices own mechanism:**
   - translating a semantic intent (mood, palette, duration) into device output;
   - one writer per device, bounds and validation;
   - final precedence at execution (alerts > interludes > ambient);
   - saving and restoring the *current* base presentation;
   - truthful receipts and external-control reporting;
   - continuing status presentation when the hub is down.
3. **Contract:**
   - A shared `moment` command in a new controller contract version: intent, mood, palette, duration, priority class, idempotency key from the triggering event, start time.
   - Each device declares the moods and limits it supports.
   - It comes with conformance fixtures for precedence, restore, expiry, replay and duplicate events.
4. **Interludes:**
   - A moment may briefly take over Work/Monitor presentation only as a time-boxed interlude.
   - The device returns to the current base, a red or yellow alert always pre-empts it, and it is skipped in Quiet or do-not-disturb.
   - This revises ADR 0005's "nothing restores automatically" for interludes only.
5. **Agents propose, the hub disposes:** agents call a propose tool, and never command devices directly for flourishes.
6. **No replay:** historical replay (#139) and restarts never re-trigger moments.

**Consequences.** Contract release and conformance work; one interlude story per device; hub-side moment log and persona storage.

### Open questions for the owner

- Which events may interrupt Work: PR merged, CI failed, meetings, or none by default?
- Quiet hours and the default flourish budget per agent.
- Whether choreography needs synchronized start times, or best-effort is enough.

### Related

- #45, #40, #267, #139, #246.
- jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#146 and #158.
- jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade playback.

### Owner decisions (2026-09-25)

1. **Interrupting events.**
   - Default set: PR merged, CI failed, and meeting reminders (the calendar source is #298).
   - The set is owner-editable: events can be added or removed later without a code change.
   - Everything else plays only in Free or Media until the owner adds it.
2. **Quiet hours.**
   - Build them with an on/off switch and an editable schedule, defaulting to **off**.
   - The owner often works late at night. Revisit the default when their schedule settles.
3. **Flourish budget.**
   - Start conservative, test for a few days, then expand. Testing must not block other delivery.
   - Proposed starting defaults, all editable:
     - per agent: at most 1 flourish per completed task and 2 per hour;
     - across all agents: at most 6 per hour;
     - at least 5 minutes between flourishes on any one device.
4. **Timing.**
   - Best-effort start times are enough for now.
   - Revisit trigger: visible drift between devices during choreography, which would open a sync-qualification story.

**Readiness:** ready to draft the ADR.

issues.title: Record the product direction and highest-leverage next work in the work guide
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader of the cross-project work guide finds one dated **Direction** section beside the existing "Where we've been" and "Where we're going" panels. It answers, in the owner's words: where B.U.N.N.Y. stands on each surface, what it is becoming, what to build next and in what order, what to improve in what already exists, and which later ideas are worth keeping. Below the narrative, a computed **Least work, most unblocked** table ranks open stories by how many other open stories list them as a recorded prerequisite, so the owner can see which small items release the most work without re-deriving it each time.

Every intentional guide refresh re-validates the section. A story cited in the narrative that has since closed makes the maintenance check fail and name the story, so the direction text gets rewritten with the refresh rather than silently going stale, which is what happened to `docs/roadmap.md` before [#170](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/170) and to the "Useful next steps" list on 2026-09-25, when three of its four entries had merged that day. The leverage table is recomputed from the saved prerequisite records at every build and is never typed by hand.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, snapshot inputs, checks and public edition. Excluded: live GitHub reads of the direction text (it stays dated), new story fields or labels, automatic refresh, publication, and any product behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Saved input `work/guide_direction.py`**, the same pattern as `guide_paths.py`: `AS_OF` (date) and `REVISION` (the hub commit the text was written against); `STANDING`, one entry per surface (Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, Pixoo, Tidbyt, LIFX, PC lighting, playback, hub and dashboard, guide and atlas) with one or two sentences and the issue keys that evidence it; `BECOMING`, short paragraphs citing the direction placeholders [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267), [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) and [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272); `SEQUENCE`, an ordered list of (keys, why) for what to build next; `IMPROVEMENTS`, (text, keys) for changes to existing surfaces; `IDEAS`, later creative bets with keys; `DELIVERED_SINCE`, keys moved out of `SEQUENCE` at a refresh with the date, so the section can say what landed since the last direction rewrite. Text renders literally. Keys render through the existing `issue_link`, so they carry the same status icon and live GitHub relabel as every other link. First content: the 2026-09-25 assessment, pinned to hub `main` at `15c9c2a`.
- **Computed leverage** in `guide_status.py`: `leverage(issues, dependencies)` returns, for each open issue, the open issues whose native `blockedBy` records name it, direct and transitive, using the records `load_dependencies` already asserts complete. The renderer shows the top entries with at least one dependent: key, title, its existing scheduling state (candidate, active, blocked, deferred, later by owner), the direct and total counts, and the dependent keys. Stories in `DECISIONS` are marked "decision, no code". A `status:review` story is marked "in review" from its label; the PR snapshot is not parsed. The note states that counts come from recorded GitHub prerequisites only, that prose-only dependencies are not counted, and that a high count is not a priority.
- **Renderer** in `work/guide_direction.py`: one `<section id="direction">` inserted in `build_guide.py` after the timeline panels, with subsections "Where we stand", "What it is becoming", "Build next", "Least work, most unblocked", "Improve what exists" and "Later ideas". A dated line reads "Direction written <AS_OF> against hub <REVISION>; leverage computed from the <snapshot> prerequisite records." The section joins search, Expand all and print. It uses role tokens only, no decoration and no motion.
- **Refresh check** in `work/test_maintenance.py`: against the committed snapshot, every key in `STANDING`, `SEQUENCE`, `IMPROVEMENTS` and `IDEAS` must exist, and every `SEQUENCE` key must be open or listed in `DELIVERED_SINCE`; a violation fails naming the key. The same check covers `NEXT_STEPS` and `DECISIONS` in `guide_paths.py` until [#259](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/259) retires them.
- **Procedure**: `docs/work-guide/README.md` documents the section and its input, and step 1 of "Refresh and validate a guide revision" adds "review `work/guide_direction.py`; move delivered keys to `DELIVERED_SINCE` and rewrite the sequence". `docs/roadmap.md` gains one sentence pointing at the guide's Direction section as the dated narrative.

Dependencies: none required. Coordinate with #259, which moves curated per-story lists into story bodies: the direction narrative and the leverage table are guide structure and computed data, not story facts, so they stay in the repository. [#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) may later fold this input check into its CI drift report. [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201) can reuse `leverage()` for the mission map.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- GitHub issues stay authoritative for scope and status. The narrative is dated editorial text and never claims live state; the table is derived only from saved native records; nothing in it promotes a blocked, deferred or owner-later story, and the existing conservative scheduling rules are reused unchanged.
- Topic totals, primary coverage, the archive, history, roadmap and diagram inputs are untouched. The new section adds nothing to issue counts.
- No tracker writes, no new endpoints, no new JavaScript reads. The public export includes the section; the input holds only public issue keys and owner prose.
- Two consecutive builds produce identical HTML. Hostile text in the input renders literally.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, one hub PR entirely under `docs/work-guide/` plus the one-sentence pointer in `docs/roadmap.md`. Guide UI needs no human approval under the SDLC UI approval scope.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: leverage counts from a fixture prerequisite graph (direct, transitive, a cycle, a deferred blocker and a decision entry); an unknown cited key fails the build naming it; a closed `SEQUENCE` key fails unless recorded in `DELIVERED_SINCE`; the check also catches a closed `NEXT_STEPS` key; hostile text is literal; identical repeated builds.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: the section renders at 390 px and 1440 px without overflow, appears in search results and Expand all, prints, and its issue links receive live status labels with the mocked read.
3. Guide commands pass under Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), the regenerated HTML is committed, and screenshots plus the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
4. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the fixed candidate and a guarded squash merge under `docs/sdlc.md`, with the guide-only CI receipt if the filter applies. Publication of the public edition is a separate authorized step.
5. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Reading the direction text live from an issue or discussion: not now. The text changes only when the owner rewrites it, and the refresh check already forces that review. Revisit with #259.
- Generating the narrative automatically at refresh: not chosen, to keep the owner's voice. The check makes a human rewrite the stale parts instead.
- Counting prose dependencies ("required input", "after #n") that are not recorded as native prerequisites: not now; record them natively in the tracker instead. Consequence: an unrecorded dependency is invisible to the table.
- A leverage view inside the mission map: later, with #201.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `15c9c2a`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One input module, one render function, one graph computation over records the build already loads, tests and a README step.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Native prerequisite records, the PR snapshot, `issue_link` and the timeline panels all exist; nothing new is fetched.
- **Impact: low.** Documentation output only; a fault fails the build loudly.
- **Readiness: ready.** No open prerequisite.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `medium` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |
| Checkpoints | the transitive rule of the leverage count; the closed-key check failing on the committed snapshot before the section is rendered; the first direction text pinned to a hub revision | the transitive rule of the leverage count; the closed-key check failing on the committed snapshot before the section is rendered; the first direction text pinned to a hub revision |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/290. I started this session on Sonnet at medium effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: the transitive rule of the leverage count; the closed-key check failing on the committed snapshot before the section is rendered; the first direction text pinned to a hub revision. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/290. I started this session on gpt-6-luna at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-luna; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: the transitive rule of the leverage count; the closed-key check failing on the committed snapshot before the section is rendered; the first direction text pinned to a hub revision. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; the low-effort row fits only trivial, mechanical work.

**Why:** A bounded documentation-tooling change over records the build already loads, with named tests and no product behavior. Policy row: bounded implementation with settled requirements.
**Reassess when:** Guide inputs move into story bodies (#259), or the snapshot or native prerequisite record format changes.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text and dependencies read 2026-09-25 17:12 UTC at creation; ratings as recorded in the story's Work assessment · fingerprint: `f7d0a866a672`

issues.title: Connect Tidbyt and LIFX to the hub through one local controller host
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The Tidbyt and the LIFX bulbs appear in B.U.N.N.Y. like the wall and the Pixoo do: a component page, home widgets, history series, and `hub_devices` over MCP. Today the hub routes only controllers of kind `pixoo` and `nanoleaf`, each a separate HTTP service on loopback. Tidbyt (`controllers/tidbyt`) and LIFX (`controllers/lifx`) are in-process libraries with no listener, so no dashboard, widget, history or MCP path can reach them. The Tidbyt runner already consumes the shared feed on the installed hub; LIFX status is still open in [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20) and [#22](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/22). No backlog issue covers connecting either to the hub; [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) only documents connecting controllers that already speak the contract, and [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) does this for PC lighting later.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **One local controller host.** A small Node process in this repository, `apps/local-controllers` or similar, that loads the Tidbyt and LIFX libraries in-process and serves the existing controller v1 contract (`snapshot`, `commands`) for each on one loopback port with a bearer token, exactly as the Pixoo and Nanoleaf services do. It runs as one user service beside the hub and is the single writer for those devices. The Tidbyt runner's feed consumption moves into this host so there is one process, not two.
- **Two new kinds in the hub.** `ControllerConfig.kind` accepts `tidbyt` and `lifx`; the hub validates their capabilities from the snapshot (Tidbyt: power off is unsupported, status only; LIFX: power, brightness, color) and rejects unsupported commands with the owner's rejection, as the contract already requires. No integration route for either at first.
- **Registration.** `host.json` gains the two controller entries with their own `bunny-hub` principals, following the #154 and #155 pattern. The dashboard then shows both components with the generic controls, and [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) widgets, [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) series and MCP discovery follow without further work.

Read `docs/controller-contract.md` before touching wire values; this adds kinds and a service, not contract fields.

Dependencies: none for Tidbyt. LIFX control through the hub needs [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20)'s behavior decisions for automatic status, but manual power, brightness and color through the hub can land first. Related: [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) (setup docs), [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) (same pattern for PC lighting), [#23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23) (Tronbyt backend, unchanged by this).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device: the local host is the only Tidbyt and LIFX writer; the hub routes through it and never opens its state. The existing per-bulb queues, bounded retries and Tidbyt's classify-once results stay inside the libraries.
- Tidbyt credentials and bulb addresses stay in the host's private configuration, never in the hub's configuration or the browser.
- A manual change in the LIFX app is left alone until the next explicit command, as the LIFX README and #20 require. Nothing in this story adds automatic status painting.
- Contract rules: request tickets, configuration revisions, generations, typed outcomes, and unsupported capabilities reported rather than faked.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then installation on explicit request with a named owner.

- Contract tests run against the local host with fake Tidbyt and LIFX transports: snapshot shape, supported and rejected commands, ticket and revision guards. `npm run test:contracts`, `test:contracts:python`, `test:tidbyt`, the LIFX suite, and the hub, MCP and dashboard suites pass with the two kinds registered in fixtures.
- With fakes, the dashboard shows a `tidbyt` and a `lifx` component with the right controls available and unavailable, and `hub_devices` lists both.
- Installation gate: the owner registers the host in `host.json`, and a bulb responds to a brightness change from the dashboard; Tidbyt shows the same status it shows today. Physical checks need the explicit device addresses and permission, as always.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Automatic LIFX agent status: [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20) and [#22](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/22).
- Tidbyt media or playlists: Tidbyt shows status only; nothing else is qualified.
- Integration routes (mappings, monitor settings) for these devices: add when a page needs more than the generic controls.
- Tronbyt: [#23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23) and [#24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/24).

**Coordination with [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292) (checked 2026-09-25):** the host implements whichever controller contract version is current when it lands. If the moment command has shipped, the host declares the `moments` capability as unsupported for Tidbyt and LIFX until each has its own interlude story; v1 consumers stay unaffected either way.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: medium.** A new loopback host, two hub kinds, a LIFX lighting profile route, MCP tools and dashboard controls. The per-device queues already exist in the Tidbyt and LIFX libraries.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Owner decision on 2026-09-25: LIFX color and temperature go through the hub now, over the existing `lifx-light` 1.0.0 profile on a typed route for `lifx` components. Controller v1 is unchanged. #292 agreed that this lands on API 1.0 first; #292 bumps the host's contract pin when it rebases.
- **Impact: medium.** A new authenticated listener takes device commands. Device effects are reversible. Tidbyt credentials and bulb addresses stay in private host configuration.
- **Readiness: ready.** Source delivery first. Installation and the physical check stay a separate, owner-authorized step.
- **Delivery choices.** The host reads the existing Tidbyt runner JSON as-is, so status, now-playing and the device lease carry over. The standalone runner stays available for rollback, and the shared lease prevents both from running. Each bulb gets a writer lease keyed by its address. The host never polls bulbs.

## Guide

**Topic:** nanoleaf-devices
**Note:** One local controller host serving the contract for the in-process Tidbyt and LIFX libraries, registered in the hub as two new kinds.
**Highlight:** idea, Tidbyt and LIFX reachable from the hub through one controller host.

issues.title: Reach every B.U.N.N.Y. surface from one shared places navigation
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Every B.U.N.N.Y. surface reaches every other surface with one click, through the same navigation in the same order with the same labels. The surfaces are:

| Place | What it is today | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work guide | `docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html` | Public at https://jimmie-potts.github.io/agent-device-guide/ |
| Architecture | The nine Archify viewers, including the A2 system map ("the system") and the S4 walkthrough | Public under `/architecture/` |
| Atlas | The system design atlas: overview, walkthrough, 26 component pages, the complete reading view, the state and actions viewer | Public under `/atlas/` |
| Reference | The atlas API and database reference | Public under `/atlas/reference/` |
| B.U.N.N.Y. | The hub dashboard | Local only, `http://127.0.0.1:8788/` |
| Wall | The Nanoleaf wall map, owned by codex-nanoleaf | Local only, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` |

Today these sit on three islands with no shared navigation. The guide links to the atlas and the viewers, the atlas links back to the guide only in the public export, the viewers link nowhere, the dashboard links only to the optional advanced editor, and nothing links to the dashboard or the wall. Brand text differs on every surface ("AGENT DEVICE / WORK GUIDES", "B.U.N.N.Y. / SYSTEM DESIGN", "◈ B.U.N.N.Y. / LOCAL INTEGRATION", "Codex × Nanoleaf / Wall map").

Public surfaces stay public and keep working on the phone. Local surfaces stay loopback-only and appear in the navigation as local entries that open only on the PC.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **One places manifest.** A small committed file under `docs/skins/` (for example `places.json`) lists each place with its label, public URL, local URL and group (Public or Local). Every generator reads it; nothing hand-edits generated HTML.
2. **One shared strip on the documentation surfaces.** `build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py` and the reference build render the same "Places" strip in the shared documentation skin: the B.U.N.N.Y. wordmark, the current place name, and links to the other places. `architecture_diagrams.py` injects the same strip into each rendered viewer after Archify renders, since the viewers keep their own CSS. `export_public.py` uses the public URLs and keeps the local entries tagged "Local", so the phone sees them but knows they open on the PC. The existing local atlas gets its guide link, not only the public export.
3. **The same places in the dashboard.** The sidebar gains a "Places" group built from the manifest at bundle time: Wall on loopback, and the public guide, architecture, atlas and reference URLs. Links to public pages are ordinary anchors; local links keep the numeric-loopback rule the advanced editor link already enforces.
4. **One brand line.** Every surface shows the B.U.N.N.Y. wordmark and its place name, following style guide §10, with the wall keeping its own title until it merges under [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).
5. **Wall link back.** codex-nanoleaf adds a "B.U.N.N.Y." link in the wall map header to `http://127.0.0.1:8788/`. [codex-nanoleaf #189](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/189) owns this companion implementation.

Dependencies: none required. Related independent work: [#276](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/276) (so the dashboard link lands signed in), [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) (hash routes make deep links to a component possible later), [#254](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/254) (skin picker, which would read the same manifest), and [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Public pages never need a token, a local service or a private path. No local URL, credential or private runtime data enters the public export beyond the two loopback addresses, which carry nothing secret.
- The hub keeps serving only its three assets with the current CSP; the dashboard is not framed or embedded anywhere.
- The wall map's own CSRF token and loopback rule are untouched.
- The docs skin token check (`docs/skins/check_tokens.py`), the guide checks and the atlas checks keep passing. The viewer and reference styling exemption in the guide README stays; the injected strip uses the shared skin's fixed tokens only.
- Guide revisions still follow the guide maintenance procedure, and public publication still needs the owner's finish line and Pages receipts.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source, one guide revision, then public publication on the owner's request.

- From each of the six places, every other place is one click away, in the same order and with the same label. Checked by a browser script over the built local outputs and by hand on the running dashboard.
- On a phone over the public site, the guide, viewers, atlas and reference open and their strip fits at 390 px without horizontal overflow; local entries show the "Local" tag.
- `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `docs/system-design/check.py` and `check.cjs`, and `check_tokens.py` pass. `export_public.py` produces a manifest with the strip present in every exported page.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the new sidebar group; axe passes at desktop and 390 px.
- UI approval: the guide strip and its companion architecture viewers are exempt under the current [guide UI exception](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md#ui-approval-scope). The atlas, reference and dashboard changes need explicit owner approval of the current candidate, renewed after changes. The Nanoleaf wall link has its own approval gate in codex-nanoleaf #189.
- Publication: after the guide-only or mixed PR merges, the public edition is copied under the existing procedure with Pages receipts. Source merge alone does not claim the site is live.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Serving the guide and atlas from the hub so they work offline on the PC: not needed while the PC has internet; revisit if the hub moves to a host without it ([#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/42)).
- Reaching the dashboard or wall from the phone: excluded; [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47) and [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203).
- A shared dark and light toggle across origins: the `bunny-design-theme` key only works within one origin, and the dashboard is dark only. Revisit with [#254](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/254).
- Merging the wall map into the dashboard: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).

## Guide

**Note:** One places navigation across the guide, architecture viewers, atlas, reference, dashboard and wall.

issues.title: Make the dashboard a dense control surface instead of long single-column pages
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

Once signed in, the owner sees a dense control surface instead of a long column of forms. On the installed hub with the wall (Nanoleaf) and pixel (Pixoo) components, at 1440 px wide, a component page shows its status and every control without scrolling past about two screens, and the Activity page shows the sessions that matter in the first screen. The 390 px phone layout stays usable. Nothing about what the controls do changes.

What the pages look like today (full-page captures from the #245 candidate and the #182 approval set):

- The component page is one column: a 10-row fact list, then about twelve stacked forms (Mode, Reapply, Integration settings, Element, Task and Project mappings, Power, Brightness, Media, Scenes, Switch to Free), each with its own heading, one- to three-sentence hint, button and status line. The wall page is 3,827 px tall at 1280 wide and 4,933 px on a phone. Selects stop at half the column, so the right half is empty.
- The Activity page spends its first 400 px on a hero heading, a subtitle and a four-cell stats strip before any session appears. Each session is a full-width card with a six-item fact list, a label form and one form per notice.
- The Connections page is a hero, a six-item fact list and a few paragraphs.
- The login page is a two-line headline and two hint paragraphs.

Every hint is inline JSX in `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`, and the application skin defines no spacing or type tokens, so the layout reads as raw pixel values (style guide §4.1).

### Smallest useful implementation

**Owner direction (2026-09-25):** a dense control surface built as a dashboard of components and widgets, keeping the futuristic Neon Geometry Wars look from style guide §3. Decoration stays within the guide's rule of a calm surface with no glow on every card; the density comes from layout, not from more chrome. Whether every component ends up on one page or keeps its own page is open; the owner chose on 2026-09-25 to build modular widgets first and settle that from the built candidate.

**Recommendation for the page split.** Build every control and status block as a widget with one interface (component alias, capability, current snapshot, command action) that any page can place. The home grid shows every component's everyday widgets (status, mode, power, brightness, scenes) together, so one page is enough for daily use. Each component keeps a page that composes the same widgets plus its rare, larger forms (Nanoleaf assignments and mappings, the Pixoo Monitor view, media). A widget renders identically wherever it is placed, so moving one between pages is a placement change, not a rewrite. Decide the final split after the candidate exists.

Graph widgets (velocity and live series) belong to [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) and use this widget interface; their data comes from [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282).

Follow-on widget stories filed 2026-09-25: [#286](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/286) (wall miniature), [#287](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/287) (component inventory and widget ranking), [#288](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/288) (command palette and D-pad navigation). [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) brings Tidbyt and LIFX into the same component and widget set.

Work in two steps so the owner approves a design before code moves.

1. **Design candidate.** A static HTML mock in the application skin for the four views (login, Activity, component, Connections) at 1440 px and 390 px, using the Nanoleaf wall map's three-column density (rail, canvas, inspector) as the reference. Proposed changes:
   - Component page: a one-line status strip (health, mode, power, brightness, observation age, pending commands) replaces the fact list; the fact list moves into a "Details" disclosure. Controls become cards in a two- or three-column grid: Mode with Reapply, Power, Brightness, Scenes, Media. Nanoleaf mapping forms sit in one "Assignments" panel; the Pixoo Monitor form in one "Monitor" panel. Each card keeps one short label line; longer guidance moves behind a help control or a `title`.
   - Home: the Activity view becomes a widget grid. One widget per registered component shows its health, mode, power and brightness with its quick actions (apply mode, power, reapply), and links to the full component page. Sessions, attention and collector health are widgets in the same grid, so the first screen shows the whole installation at once.
   - Activity: drop the hero and subtitle for a page title and the stats strip in one row. Sessions become compact rows with the badge, identity and an inline label field; notices expand under their row.
   - Connections: fold into a compact status panel reachable from the sidebar footer, or a two-column card page.
   - Login: one line and one button (or nothing, once the sign-in story lands).
   - Spacing and type: add the `--space-*` and `--type-*` roles to the application skin and use them, so the dashboard and the documentation skin share one scale.
2. **Implementation.** Apply the approved candidate in `apps/dashboard`, add hash routes for the built-in views and components (`#/activity`, `#/component/<alias>`, `#/connections`) so pages have URLs and back-button history, and update the browser, matrix, retirement and lifecycle checks whose selectors and exact texts change.

Dependencies: land [#247](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/247) first or in the same change, because the routes need the discriminated navigation value it introduces. Related independent work: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) (device and group pages later) and [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) (shared colors). Do not choose a layout that blocks a group page.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Every control keeps its accessible name, its explicit apply action and its pending, unavailable, uncertain, error and stale states from the shared command lifecycle (#245). No control becomes implicit or auto-applied.
- Keyboard order, skip link, focus restoration after refresh and reconnect (the `.edit` group lookup), reduced motion, axe WCAG 2.1 AA at desktop and 390 px, and no horizontal overflow.
- Fixed-meaning status colors and the skin layer boundary from the style guide (§4.2, §4.3): a skin changes values, not layout semantics or which control is primary.
- Exact status sentences from `client.ts` and `lifecycle.ts`; shortening a hint must not change a status.
- The hub serves only `/`, `dashboard.js` and `dashboard.css` with the current CSP; no inline styles.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- The home view shows every registered component as a widget with its status and quick actions on the first screen at 1440 px.
- The owner approves the design candidate, then the implemented candidate (screenshots at 1440 px and 390 px for all four views and the wall and pixel components), renewed after any later UI change, recorded on the PR per docs/sdlc.md.
- Full-page height of the wall component page at 1280 px wide is under 2,000 px, down from 3,827 px, and no view has an empty right half at 1440 px.
- `npm run test:dashboard`, the browser and matrix checks, `retirement.mjs`, `style.test.mjs` (no raw colors outside `src/skins/`) and the hub dashboard test all pass. The style guide §7 and §12 checklists are updated with the new measurements.
- OpenSpec: the unified-dashboard spec gains the routing and layout requirements; the approval requirement is unchanged.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Device art, group page and wall-map merge: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).
- Light scheme and the Neon decoration layer for the dashboard (`data-skin`): deferred in #182; revisit after this layout lands.
- Glossary labels such as "Eyes" for freshness: the style guide §11 leaves these to the owning UI issue; not part of this change.

Related stories filed together on 2026-09-25: [#276](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/276) (sign-in without a token, which removes the login page this story would otherwise redesign) and [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) (shared places navigation, which adds a sidebar group this layout must leave room for). [#279](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/279) clears documentation leftovers. None block this one.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment on 2026-09-25 at pickup, from this story, the owner's 2026-09-25 comment, ADR 0007, the style guide and `apps/dashboard` at Hub `ba08043`. Operating assumptions: one operator, the installed hub with the wall, pixel, Tidbyt and LIFX components, opened through the launcher; source-only delivery; owner UI approval is a retained gate.

- **Complexity: medium.** Every view changes and hash routes plus a widget catalog are new; the command lifecycle and availability rules in `client.ts` and `lifecycle.ts` are untouched, and after the owner's no-Apply decision only the form wording in `lifecycle.ts` changed (a rejection no longer says the edit is kept).
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The layout is specified with a recommendation; the final page split is settled from the built candidate. The open item is the owner's approval, not a technical unknown.
- **Impact: medium.** Every control is re-rendered, so a regression could misrepresent a control's state; recovery is a source fix with no device or data effect.
- **Readiness: ready.** #247's discriminated navigation value lands in the same change, as this story allows.
- **Cuts:** the step 1 hand-built static mock is replaced by static HTML captures and screenshots of the built candidate (duplicated ceremony against the retained approval gate; the owner chose to settle the split from the built candidate). A home now-playing widget is not built (#287 owns the inventory).
- **Owner decision on the design candidate (2026-09-25):** the previews were accepted as a direction with one change to reduce clicks: no Apply button anywhere (a select or toggle sends on change, a text field on blur or Enter), sliders send once on release, and the on/off dropdown becomes a button. This replaces the "explicit apply action" protection above and the draft-and-conflict rule of the unified-dashboard spec; the fresh-read guard, one command per gesture, typed rejections and the uncertain lock stay. Delivered in the same PR.
- **Reassess when:** the owner rejects the candidate's page split, or #366 changes the widget catalog contract.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Turn the long single-column pages into a dense control surface with status strips, control cards and page URLs.
**Highlight:** next step, The dense home is where ADR 0007 settles the page split; the widget stories build on it.

issues.title: Open B.U.N.N.Y. from a bookmark without a token or launcher step
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner opens B.U.N.N.Y. on the PC by clicking one bookmark or shortcut and lands on the dashboard signed in. No token is generated, copied or pasted, and a reload or a second tab stays signed in. This applies to the one installed hub (`codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service`, loopback port 8788) used from the Windows browser and from WSL. Phone or LAN access is excluded; the hub stays loopback-only.

What exists today, from [#179](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/179) (PR #180): `node apps/hub/dist/cli.js open <config>` asks the hub over the owner-only socket `bunny-launch.sock` for a 30-second code, opens `http://127.0.0.1:8788/#launch=<code>`, and the page exchanges the code for an 8-hour browser session held only in page memory. The installed hub already serves that socket. What still hurts:

- No shortcut or bookmark runs the command, so the owner falls back to the collapsed "Use a separately provisioned access token" form, whose token is created by hand (README "Credentials").
- A reload or a new tab loses the session and shows the login page again.
- `http://localhost:8788/` is refused (the Host check expects `127.0.0.1`).

### Smallest useful implementation

**Decision (owner, 2026-09-25): Option 1.** Option 2 is kept below only as the rejected alternative.

**Option 1 (chosen): trusted-loopback sign-in.** A new optional private configuration field, for example `browserAccess: "trusted-loopback"`, off by default. When set, the page calls a new same-origin route (for example `POST /api/dashboard/v1/session`) on load and receives the same bounded browser session the launcher issues today: `read` and `control` on configured controller aliases, no `ingest`, `admin`, playback or MCP, 8-hour expiry, 16-session cap, retirement through the existing `retireBrowser` path. The route enforces the existing Host, Origin, `Sec-Fetch-Site` and `X-Pixoo-Request` checks. No cookie and no storage: a reload simply asks again, and `pagehide` logs the previous session out. The login page disappears when the option is on; a failed request shows the current launcher and manual-token fallbacks. The launcher and manual token keep working for configurations without the option.

**Option 2 (rejected): keep the code exchange, make it sticky.** Store the launched session in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, loopback-scoped cookie with a longer lifetime, add a Windows shortcut and a WSL alias for the `open` command, and accept `localhost` as a Host alias. The owner still runs the launcher after each expiry and on any machine reboot.

Also: accept `localhost:<port>` as well as `127.0.0.1:<port>` in the Host check, and document the bookmark URL in the hub README and `apps/hub/SETUP.md`. Blocked by nothing. Related independent work: [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) (setup guide), [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203) (owner sign-in for the future remote workspace, which this does not touch).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Loopback-only listener, exact Host and Origin checks, the `Sec-Fetch-Site` rule and the `X-Pixoo-Request` header on every write. These already stop cross-site pages and DNS rebinding and must stay.
- Machine credentials for ingest, admin, playback and MCP stay digest-only in the configuration; the browser session never gains them.
- Browser-session retirement from [#244](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244): expiry, eviction, logout and shutdown retire tickets, streams and replay entries.
- One state owner, one writer per device; the page only routes through the hub.

Assurance lost with Option 1, stated plainly: today a local program that is not the owner's browser needs a configured token or the owner-only socket to command devices. With the option on, any program on the PC that can send a same-origin-looking loopback request with the custom header can issue the same read and control commands. That matches the Nanoleaf wall map on port 8765, which has no sign-in and labels itself "Local to this PC". The devices are lights and displays. Reassess before any LAN, phone or second-operator exposure, as docs/sdlc.md already requires.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then the owner's installation on explicit request.

- Source: with the option on, opening `/` from a fresh browser context shows the dashboard with controls enabled, and a reload keeps it working. With the option off, behavior is unchanged. Hub unit tests cover: the route refused without the option, refused on a bad Host, Origin or missing header, sessions capped and retired, and MCP still refusing browser sessions. Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass, and `retirement.mjs` still passes.
- Acceptance examples for this credential change are written in the OpenSpec proposal before implementation, per docs/sdlc.md scope defaults, and the PR carries the short walkthrough (session ownership, expiry, reload, duplicate tab, failure case, recovery).
- Installation gate: a named owner adds the field to the installed `host.json`, updates the hub package under the existing backup and receipt procedure, and confirms the bookmark opens signed in. Source merge alone does not claim this.
- UI change: the login page and shell change, so the current candidate needs explicit owner approval before merge.

issues.title: Replace Pause motion with a one-shot circuit trace in the guide and atlas
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner found the Pause motion button confusing on a phone (#87's phone check): a second tap resumes only a slow top-bar streak, and the label never changes. The owner wants the button dropped from the work guide and the B.U.N.N.Y. atlas. The top-bar streak, which repeats every 25 s, becomes a single circuit trace that plays once on load. It runs down the screen through the page background as a branching, circuit-board pattern rather than one horizontal line.

Setup: the two generated documentation pages (guide and atlas) that share `docs/skins/`. They are read on desktop and phone, and published through agent-device-guide.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Skin template (`docs/skins/skin.py`):** stop supplying the `#motion-toggle` button, the stored `bunny-design-motion` preference and the `data-motion` attribute. Keep the theme toggle.
- **Neon skin (`docs/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css`):** replace the repeating streak with a one-shot circuit trace. It is CSS only, colored from existing tokens, sits behind content, runs top to bottom across the viewport width, and never repeats. The opening and the trace both finish within 5 s of load, so WCAG 2.2.2 needs no pause control.
- **Pages and checks:** remove the button from the guide and atlas generators, regenerate both, and update `check_skin.cjs`, `check_guide.cjs` and `docs/system-design/check.cjs`.
- **Docs:** update the style guide (`docs/application-ui-style-guide.md`) and `docs/work-guide/README.md` to drop the pause control from the skin rules.

No dependencies. The public republish follows the #87 procedure.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` still stops all decorative motion.
- Decoration stays out of the tab order, never covers text or controls, carries no meaning and prints as nothing.
- The token check still rejects color literals outside the token files.
- The theme toggle and its stored choice keep working across the guide and atlas.
- A stale stored `bunny-design-motion` value has no effect.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

1. Neither page has a Pause motion button, a `data-motion` attribute or motion storage.
2. On a fresh load, the circuit trace runs once, down and across the page background. The opening and the trace both finish within 5 s, with no infinite animation. Evidence: the browser checks assert that every animation is finite and ends by 5 s, plus screenshots mid-trace at 390 and 1440 px in dark and light.
3. Reduced motion runs no animation, the trace never intercepts pointer or keyboard input, and print has no decoration. Evidence: the extended skin check.
4. The guide and atlas builds, token check and browser checks pass, and full Depot CI passes.
5. The owner approves the atlas UI candidate, and the guide is published and hash-verified on Pages.

## Meaningful deferrals

- There is no user-facing way to stop the 5 s opening except the system Reduce Motion setting. That is acceptable under WCAG 2.2.2 for motion under 5 s. Revisit if a longer or repeating animation is proposed.
- #254 (Cards skin) and the style guide's skin template currently name the pause control. This issue updates the style guide and leaves a note on #254.

issues.title: Make the slow-device browser isolation check deterministic
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make the existing dashboard browser test for independent device progress reliable on Node 24 with Playwright and its fake controllers. During #218/#256 validation, the scenario “slow device serializes explicit commands while another device remains responsive” failed at `apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs:27` with `429 !== 200`. One unchanged-head rerun and an independent matrix run passed. This is separate from the corrected Start Monitor assertion in #256; no production defect is established.

Evidence: [the observed failure recorded in #256](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/256), [the test at the delivered revision](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/49b29d06caee71be61dd8cee93bbca0c746ca7e7/apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs#L24), and [the per-device capacity guard](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/49b29d06caee71be61dd8cee93bbca0c746ca7e7/apps/hub/src/controllers.ts#L26). The raw failure and successful rerun remain in the #218 delivery evidence. Priority: low; intermittent test maintenance, not a device incident.

## Smallest useful implementation

First reproduce the collision with controlled fake-controller/request ordering. The current test issues an extra wall read while browser polling can occupy that wall's single request slot. That is the leading explanation, not yet a deterministic diagnosis. Check `matrix.mjs`, `fixture.mjs` and the existing dashboard polling flow.

Then synchronize only the test/fixture so it measures a wall request admitted while the Pixoo request is still deliberately pending, without an unrelated wall poll consuming the slot. Prefer bounded observable barriers over fixed sleeps. Keep the fix within this test and the minimal supporting fixture. If the probe instead demonstrates a production defect, report it and obtain a scoped follow-up rather than relaxing the contract. Required source prerequisites: none. Coordinate if another delivery edits the matrix or fixture; shared files alone are not a dependency.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one bounded request slot per device and independent progress between devices. Preserve the successful wall response, the existing less-than-700-ms wall-read assertion while Pixoo is delayed 800 ms, serial explicit command behavior, exact write checks, and absence of capacity errors on the tested UI action. No production queue change, extra retries, assertion removal, increased threshold or disabled scenario merely to obtain green.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only test maintenance.

- [ ] A bounded controlled probe reproduces the original HTTP 429 assertion and identifies the competing read. Retain red evidence; a passing rerun alone is insufficient.
- [ ] After correction, the wall request succeeds while the slow Pixoo operation remains pending. A negative control that makes wall progress depend on Pixoo still fails the isolation check.
- [ ] The original status, timing, command and no-retry assertions remain; run the focused scenario through a small documented set of deliberately ordered interleavings, then the complete `npm run test:dashboard:browser` suite.
- [ ] Follow the Dashboard checks in `docs/development.md`, applicable shared checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all matching PR CI and merged-main CI. These are planned checks, not results from this planning task. Record any new failure separately rather than using blind reruns.

No product behavior delta is proposed, so an OpenSpec change is unnecessary unless diagnosis expands the scope. No application UI approval renewal is needed for a test-only correction; any actual UI change requires its normal approval.

## Meaningful deferrals

A general browser-flake framework, queue redesign, broad performance project and installed/hardware trial are excluded. They would add no evidence for this bounded scheduling defect. Reassess if the controlled probe implicates production routing or the required assertion itself is invalid.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded`. Complexity low: one scenario and its fixture. Uncertainty medium: the collision is observed but controlled reproduction remains the first task. Impact low: test-only correction; production scope expansion requires reassessment. Ready for bounded diagnosis followed by an evidenced test-only repair. No unfinished source dependency.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

issues.title: Move guide topic assignments and notes into the stories and read them live
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide source and story metadata. Blocked by [#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252), which supplies the section parser and the upsert helper this issue reuses.

## Outcome and real setup

A story carries its own guide placement: the topic guide that owns it, a one-line reading note, an optional workaround, and whether the owner highlights it as a next step, a decision or later work. The guide reads those from the story instead of from `guide-coverage.json`, `guide_details.py` and the curated lists in `guide_paths.py`. When the page opens, the browser reads current story bodies, so a story created or edited after the snapshot appears in its topic with its current note, and a story without a placement shows "topic assignment pending". Refreshing the guide then needs no manual coverage reconciliation.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, live-read script and checks. The eleven topic names, their outcomes, aliases and track groupings stay in the repository; they are the guide's structure, not story facts.

Excluded: history, roadmap and diagram inputs, which stay dated ([#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) reports their drift); automatic refresh PRs; publication; changing any story's scope or status.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **One `## Guide` section per story**, in the #252 style: `- **Topic:** <topic id>` (required, one of the eleven), `- **Note:** ...` (optional, replaces the per-issue reading note), `- **Workaround:** ...` (optional, defects only) and `- **Highlight:** next step | decision | later, with the reason` (optional, replaces the curated next-step, decision and owner-later lists). Reuse #252's parser and upsert helper by adding keys; do not write a second parser.
- **Generator.** `build_guide.py` derives coverage, notes, workarounds and highlights from the saved bodies. Retire `guide-coverage.json`, the `DETAILS` table and the `NEXT_STEPS`, `DECISIONS`, `OWNER_LATER` and `WORKAROUNDS` tables. The snapshot build still fails, naming the story, when an open story lacks a valid topic.
- **Live path.** `guide_overview.js` and the topic sections read the `Guide` section from live bodies with the shared parser. A story unknown to the snapshot but carrying a topic is placed in that topic with its note and gate; one without a topic stays under "Issues awaiting topic assignment". A note edited after the snapshot shows live. The freshness line names which parts are live and which stay dated.
- **Migration.** One idempotent pass writes the `Guide` section into every open story from the current files (116 stories on 2026-09-24): dry run first, read back each story, and a rerun on unchanged input writes nothing.
- **Templates.** Add the `Guide` block with the topic list to the feature and bug templates in all three repositories, so a new story carries its topic from creation. One small PR in each device repository.
- **Docs.** The guide README and the "dated publication" sentence in docs/sdlc.md say which parts are live and which stay dated.

Dependencies: required input #252 (parser, upsert helper, live-path conventions). Shared-file coordination with [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) on the generator and checks. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result later.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Every open story has exactly one topic in the snapshot build. Counts, reference links and the archive rules are unchanged. Live placement never counts a story twice or moves a closed one.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Guide` section. Everything else in a story is preserved: no label, status, assignee or closure changes. Reruns on unchanged input write nothing.
- The live read keeps its anonymous GET requests to the existing endpoint within the 60-per-hour limit; no new endpoints. A failed read keeps the snapshot, as today.
- Diagram, history and roadmap inputs and their receipts are untouched.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, meaning the hub PR, the migration edits and two template PRs.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: the `Guide` section parses from fixtures with each key; a missing or unknown topic fails the snapshot build naming the story; each highlight renders in its opening list; a story without a section is excluded from topic tables and listed as pending; hostile text renders literally; repeated builds produce identical HTML; the retired inputs are gone.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: with a mocked live body, a snapshot-unknown story appears in its topic with its note and the topic count updates; one without a section stays pending; a mocked note edit shows live; a failed read keeps the snapshot; the freshness line names the live parts; no page overflow at 390 px and 1440 px.
3. The migration report in the PR lists every open story with its topic and link, confirms each readback, and shows a second dry run writing nothing.
4. The guide procedure's commands pass with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots and the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
5. Independent Standards and Specification reviews and a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The hub PR touches `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and docs/sdlc.md, so normal CI applies. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Topic labels (`guide:<topic>`) instead of a body section: not chosen, to avoid 33 new labels and a second mechanism. Revisit if filtering stories by topic inside GitHub becomes a need.
- A generator for `github-history.json`, which is still refreshed by hand: separate small task when the manual refresh next hurts.
- Automatic refresh PRs and publication on merge: separate decisions after #240.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24, against Hub `main` [`73166b2`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/commit/73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d).

- **Complexity: medium.** A section parser shared by Python and JavaScript, a generator that drops four hand-maintained inputs, live placement of new stories, templates in three repositories and a 116-story migration.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Whether live placement changes topic counts or only lists the story is settled at the first checkpoint; the rest is observed in the current generator.
- **Impact: medium.** 116 body edits, reversible through GitHub edit history. A parser fault fails the build loudly through the exact-cover assertion rather than dropping stories silently.
- **Readiness: blocked** by #252. Placed in the backlog by the owner on 2026-09-24.
