outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
A story carries its own guide placement: the topic guide that owns it, a one-line reading note, an optional workaround, and whether the owner highlights it as a next step, a decision or later work. The guide reads those from the story instead of from `guide-coverage.json`, `guide_details.py` and the curated lists in `guide_paths.py`. When the page opens, the browser reads current story bodies, so a story created or edited after the snapshot appears in its topic with its current note, and a story without a placement shows "topic assignment pending". Refreshing the guide then needs no manual coverage reconciliation.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, live-read script and checks. The eleven topic names, their outcomes, aliases and track groupings stay in the repository; they are the guide's structure, not story facts.

Excluded: history, roadmap and diagram inputs, which stay dated ([#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) reports their drift); automatic refresh PRs; publication; changing any story's scope or status.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- **One `## Guide` section per story**, in the #252 style: `- **Topic:** <topic id>` (required, one of the eleven), `- **Note:** ...` (optional, replaces the per-issue reading note), `- **Workaround:** ...` (optional, defects only) and `- **Highlight:** next step | decision | later, with the reason` (optional, replaces the curated next-step, decision and owner-later lists). Reuse #252's parser and upsert helper by adding keys; do not write a second parser.
- **Generator.** `build_guide.py` derives coverage, notes, workarounds and highlights from the saved bodies. Retire `guide-coverage.json`, the `DETAILS` table and the `NEXT_STEPS`, `DECISIONS`, `OWNER_LATER` and `WORKAROUNDS` tables. The snapshot build still fails, naming the story, when an open story lacks a valid topic.
- **Live path.** `guide_overview.js` and the topic sections read the `Guide` section from live bodies with the shared parser. A story unknown to the snapshot but carrying a topic is placed in that topic with its note and gate; one without a topic stays under "Issues awaiting topic assignment". A note edited after the snapshot shows live. The freshness line names which parts are live and which stay dated.
- **Migration.** One idempotent pass writes the `Guide` section into every open story from the current files (116 stories on 2026-09-24): dry run first, read back each story, and a rerun on unchanged input writes nothing.
- **Templates.** Add the `Guide` block with the topic list to the feature and bug templates in all three repositories, so a new story carries its topic from creation. One small PR in each device repository.
- **Docs.** The guide README and the "dated publication" sentence in docs/sdlc.md say which parts are live and which stay dated.

Dependencies: required input #252 (parser, upsert helper, live-path conventions). Shared-file coordination with [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) on the generator and checks. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result later.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- Every open story has exactly one topic in the snapshot build. Counts, reference links and the archive rules are unchanged. Live placement never counts a story twice or moves a closed one.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Guide` section. Everything else in a story is preserved: no label, status, assignee or closure changes. Reruns on unchanged input write nothing.
- The live read keeps its anonymous GET requests to the existing endpoint within the 60-per-hour limit; no new endpoints. A failed read keeps the snapshot, as today.
- Diagram, history and roadmap inputs and their receipts are untouched.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
Delivery target: source-only, meaning the hub PR, the migration edits and two template PRs.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: the `Guide` section parses from fixtures with each key; a missing or unknown topic fails the snapshot build naming the story; each highlight renders in its opening list; a story without a section is excluded from topic tables and listed as pending; hostile text renders literally; repeated builds produce identical HTML; the retired inputs are gone.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: with a mocked live body, a snapshot-unknown story appears in its topic with its note and the topic count updates; one without a section stays pending; a mocked note edit shows live; a failed read keeps the snapshot; the freshness line names the live parts; no page overflow at 390 px and 1440 px.
3. The migration report in the PR lists every open story with its topic and link, confirms each readback, and shows a second dry run writing nothing.
4. The guide procedure's commands pass with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots and the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
5. Independent Standards and Specification reviews and a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The hub PR touches `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and docs/sdlc.md, so normal CI applies. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- Topic labels (`guide:<topic>`) instead of a body section: not chosen, to avoid 33 new labels and a second mechanism. Revisit if filtering stories by topic inside GitHub becomes a need.
- A generator for `github-history.json`, which is still refreshed by hand: separate small task when the manual refresh next hurts.
- Automatic refresh PRs and publication on merge: separate decisions after #240.

issues.title: Show starting model and thinking-level recommendations for each story in the work guide
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide source and story metadata. Policy: [agent-skills#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/56), merged in [PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/pull/57) as [`3e009e6`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/blob/3e009e6f71451bb8f6577d2250e6a0697d38528a/skills/plan-work/references/execution-recommendations.md).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader opens a story in the [work guide](https://jimmie-potts.github.io/agent-device-guide/) and sees, next to its complexity, uncertainty and impact, which model and thinking level to start with in Claude Code and in Codex, and whether that session implements bounded work, investigates, or orchestrates workers. The reader picks the model and effort in their host. The guide shows the saved recommendation; it never claims to launch or switch a model.

Each recommendation lives in its GitHub story as one `## Execution recommendation` section written under the policy above, together with the Implement prompts that carry it: one per host, plus a cheaper start when one exists. The saved backlog reproduces the section; the guide renders it and copies its prompts verbatim. Where the evidence is insufficient, the story and the guide say what is missing.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories (agent-device-hub, codex-nanoleaf, divoom-app-upgrade), the existing generator, checks and brief dialog. Stories stay authoritative in GitHub.

Excluded: implementing any assessed story; changing its scope, readiness, labels or status; installing skills; changing runtime model settings; operating devices; public publication, which #87 owns.

## Smallest useful implementation

Three internal tasks, one coordinator, one issue.

**A. Section convention and guide rendering**, all under `docs/work-guide/`.

- Document the section in `docs/work-guide/README.md` as the shape the installed plan-work policy defines once [agent-skills#58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/58) lands; until then this issue's own section is the interim reference. The README documents the parser's strictness, the guide-specific fingerprint and the rendering; it does not restate the policy. The interim shape: heading `## Execution recommendation`, then a `**Start with:**` line giving the one answer: which session type to open, on which model and thinking level in each host, and which prompt to paste. Then a two-host table with the rows `Model`, `Thinking level`, `Session type`, `Subagents` and `Availability` (evidence source and date per host, verified or provisional), plus an optional `Checkpoints` row naming decisions where a one-shot session stops to ask. Session type comes from a fixed vocabulary that maps one-to-one onto the policy's session roles: `One-shot` (one session implements directly, no subagents), `Pair` (one session delegates implementation to a single worker and advises it at approach, blockers and final review), `Orchestrate` (a stronger session breaks the story down, delegates bounded pieces to subagents and owns every write and review) and `Investigate first` (no implementation yet; a read-only session answers the named question, then the story is reassessed). Then `**Why:**`, `**Reassess when:**` and `**Assessed:**` (date, policy revision, evidence links, fingerprint) lines. After the table come the prompt blocks: `**Prompt (Claude Code):**` and `**Prompt (Codex):**`, each followed by one fenced `text` block, and optionally `**Cheaper start:**` (one line naming what it covers, its session type and each host's model and thinking level) followed by `**Cheaper prompt (Claude Code):**` and `**Cheaper prompt (Codex):**` blocks. Every prompt names the live issue URL, states the model and thinking level the reader selected, asks the agent to confirm the model and stop if it differs, tells it to take the thinking level as stated rather than guess it (Claude Code does not expose the effort level to the agent reliably: on 2026-09-24 an Opus session set to high reported low), states the session type and any subagent settings, points at the story's Execution recommendation with its assessment date, asks the agent to say so before changing strategy, and keeps the existing "if deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop" ending. `Investigate first` replaces the Implement prompts with read-only prompts that name the question. An insufficient story replaces the answer, table and prompts with `**Status:** insufficient` and `**Missing:**` (the exact input and the next question or evidence). One section per story. The parser is strict and never guesses. The vocabulary is a presentation label, not a second copy of the selection table.
- Add a parser and renderer module, for example `work/recommendations.py`, that `build_guide.py` feeds from the story bodies already saved in `work/backlogs/*-issues.json`. No new backlog file, tracker field, model registry or background assessor.
- Freshness. `Assessed` records a short SHA-256 fingerprint of the normalized story body with this section removed. The build recomputes it from the saved body; a mismatch renders "needs reassessment (story text changed after <date>)". Labels, state and dependencies never enter the fingerprint, so a status refresh can neither confirm nor stale a recommendation. Live GitHub reads in `guide_overview.js` keep each story's snapshot recommendation state and date. They may downgrade (a story absent from the snapshot shows "not yet assessed") and never upgrade. If the live path also checks the fingerprint, it shares fixtures with the Python check.
- Display. A compact text label per story in topic rows and opening cards, session type first, for example "Orchestrate · Opus high / Sol high", "One-shot · Sonnet medium / Luna medium" or "Investigate first · Sonnet medium / Luna medium", in both the snapshot renderer and the live renderer. In the brief dialog, a "Start with" block above the prompt actions shows the answer line, the two-host table with explicit model, thinking-level, session-type and subagent labels, the state, the assessment date and policy revision, and a `<details>` with why, availability and the reassessment trigger. One sentence tells the reader to choose the model and effort in their host before pasting, because the agent can confirm the model but not the thinking level. The Implement action gains two text toggles: host (Claude Code or Codex, remembered per viewer in browser storage with a safe fallback) and start (Recommended or Cheaper; Cheaper is disabled with a note when none is recorded). While the recommendation is current, Implement copies the story's saved prompt for that host and start. A stale, insufficient, unassessed or unreadable story gets the generic Implement prompt with its state notice, never a custom prompt. Explain, Plan and Review keep their current text. Every prompt names the live issue URL.
- States, in text rather than color: recommended, with date and provenance and a verified or provisional availability label per host; needs reassessment; insufficient information, with the missing input; not yet assessed; assessment unavailable, when a section is present but unreadable. Never a guessed default.
- An idempotent upsert helper, for example `work/recommendations.py upsert --dry-run`. It re-reads the live body, replaces only this section, writes nothing when the normalized section is unchanged, keeps the assessment date when the fingerprint and ratings are unchanged, and reads the result back. It renders the prompt blocks from the section's fields with one template per session type and host, so every story's prompts read the same way; a hand edit to a prompt in the issue wins on the next refresh, because the guide copies the saved text. The assessor's input stays outside Git in `.local/evidence/`. The helper writes what it is given; it does not assess.

**B. Initial assessment pass** over every open story in the three repositories. On 2026-09-24 that is 116 stories: Hub 66, Nanoleaf 30, Pixoo 20. The saved snapshot still lists 118; Nanoleaf #131, #132 and #135 have closed, and Pixoo #83 needs a primary guide.

- For each story, read the body, relevant comments, linked specification and dependencies.
- Reuse an existing `Work assessment` rating when its evidence is current. Derive a missing rating only when the sources support it, and record the rationale in that story's assessment section. Unknown stays unknown.
- Write both host recommendations for a sufficiently defined story, or `insufficient` with the exact missing input. Keep any blocker, deferral, readiness and status as they are.
- Assess children separately from parents. A high-impact story keeps the stronger capability floor even for a tiny diff.
- Re-read each body before writing. Coordinate with the owners of stories in progress or in review. Report permission failures and conflicting existing assessments as pending.

**C. Snapshot and guide revision.** After the tracker writes, run `refresh_backlogs.py`, reconcile primary coverage for new stories, rebuild, run the checks and deliver a Hub PR. Account for every inventoried story as recommended (new, updated or unchanged), insufficient, or pending, with links and reasons.

Dependencies: [agent-skills#58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/58) is a required input for the assessment pass (part B), so the 116 sections are written once in the canonical shape. Part A may proceed now against this issue's interim shape and adopts the merged revision. Shared-file coordination with [PR #251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) for #85, which changes `build_guide.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `test_maintenance.py`, `guide_brief.css` and the README: rebase onto main after it merges, or coordinate with its coordinator if it stalls on the atlas approval. [#240](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240) may change guide-only CI handling; confirm the policy at merge time. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the resulting guide revision later.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Stories remain authoritative; the guide is a dated projection. The three ratings stay model-neutral and are never averaged or derived from a title, label, file count or model choice. A recommendation grants no permission or readiness to start.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Execution recommendation` section and, where a rating is newly derived, the story's assessment section. Acceptance criteria, labels, status, assignees, priority, dependencies and other owners' text are preserved. No closing, reopening, native dependency edits or custom fields. Re-running the pass on unchanged evidence changes nothing.
- The existing brief actions (Explain, Plan, Implement, Review), their live issue URLs, focus handling, clipboard fallback, no-script GitHub link, keyboard access, phone-width fit, print and the anonymous GitHub read limits. This issue amends one rule from #196, "prompts embed no snapshot context": a custom Implement prompt embeds the model and strategy from a current recommendation, and only then. Every prompt still names the live URL and tells the agent to re-read the story. The prompt blocks sit inside the section and stay out of the freshness fingerprint.
- Generated HTML is never hand-edited. Architecture receipts and diagrams stay untouched. No credentials, private paths or transcripts enter the tracker or the guide.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, meaning the Hub PR plus the authorized story metadata edits. No installation, device or publication step.

1. `test_maintenance.py` covers the parser and renderer with fixtures: both hosts extracted and rendered; a missing host, duplicate section or unknown key rendering "assessment unavailable"; provisional availability rendered as unverified; a high-impact story whose ratings render unchanged beside its recommendation; a parent story typed Orchestrate and a child typed One-shot rendered independently; an unknown session type rendering "assessment unavailable"; a fingerprint mismatch rendering "needs reassessment"; a story without a section rendering "not yet assessed"; hostile text in every field and inside a prompt block rendered literally; prompts extracted per host and per start, with a missing cheaper start reported as absent rather than invented; two consecutive builds producing identical HTML.
2. The upsert helper is tested offline: unchanged content writes nothing and keeps the date; changed content replaces only the section; a body without a section gains exactly one; generated prompts follow one template per session type and host and survive a round trip through the parser.
3. `check_guide.cjs` shows the brief block with the answer line, both hosts and the session-type label as text at 390 px and 1440 px; a live status refresh that leaves the recommendation state and date unchanged; a live-only issue showing "not yet assessed"; one insufficient story showing its missing input; Implement copying the saved Claude Code and Codex prompts and the cheaper variant, the host choice persisting where storage allows, Cheaper disabled with a note where none is recorded, and a story mocked stale falling back to the generic prompt with its notice; print with the details expanded; the details control reachable by keyboard; no overflow.
4. The PR's assessment report lists every open story with its state and link, counts per state, the policy revision used, the stories left insufficient with their missing input, and any pending writes. The saved backlog reproduces every written section, and each story's readback matches.
5. The guide procedure's commands pass at the candidate with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`): `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots (both hosts, a missing-information case, phone width and print), the HTML hash and the check receipt go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/gh-<this issue>-<slug>/`.
6. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same fixed comparison, then a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). If every changed path stays under `docs/work-guide/`, record the guide-only CI exception evidence; otherwise normal CI applies. Guide UI needs no human approval. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

Limitations: recommendations are planning heuristics under the linked policy, not benchmarks. Codex availability cannot be inspected from a Claude Code session, nor the reverse, so the other host's choices carry a provisional label until a session on that host records evidence.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Live recomputation of the fingerprint in the browser: optional. Without it, a story edited after the snapshot keeps its snapshot state and date until the next guide refresh, and the dated label makes that visible. Revisit if a reader acts on a stale recommendation.
- Closed stories and other repositories: not assessed. No history backfill.
- Public publication: pending under #87 after this guide revision merges. A Hub merge alone does not update the website.
- Custom Explain, Plan and Review prompts: not done; they stay generic. Revisit if a story's planning session needs the recommendation in its prompt.
- A CI or scheduled reassessment: never. Reassessment happens at planning or delivery pickup under the existing policy.
- Policy enforcement in the helper, such as refusing Sonnet on a high-impact story: not built, to avoid a second maintained copy of the policy. The assessor applies it and the review checks it.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24, against Hub `main` [`73166b2`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/commit/73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d) and the policy revision above.

- **Complexity: medium.** A strict section parser, Python and JavaScript renderers that must agree, prompt templates per session type and host, a freshness rule across the snapshot and live paths, the brief dialog, print and phone layouts, and an idempotent tracker upsert across three repositories.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The section syntax and the freshness mechanism are proposed here and settled in delivery. How many stories have enough evidence is unknown until the pass runs. Codex availability is not inspectable from this host.
- **Impact: medium.** The guide is dated and reversible, but the pass edits about 116 issue bodies that other sessions own. A defective upsert damages acceptance text; GitHub's edit history is the recovery path. No product, device or credential effect.
- **Readiness: ready** for part A; part B waits for agent-skills#58. Shared-file coordination with PR #251 and a policy check against #240 at merge time.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** Orchestrate: one session breaks the work down and delegates bounded pieces. Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `high` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |
| Session type | Orchestrate | Orchestrate |
| Subagents | One read-only `sonnet` Explore scout per repository (two for Hub) that summarizes each story's outcome, checks, components and open decisions. The session writes the guide code and every tracker edit itself. | One read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) `medium` scout per repository, same brief. |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as an orchestrating session: break the work down, delegate the per-repository story reading to read-only `sonnet` Explore subagents, keep every write yourself, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252. I started this session on gpt-6-sol at high reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as an orchestrating session: break the work down, delegate the per-repository story reading to read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) scouts at medium reasoning, keep every write yourself, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; part A merged in #260, and the remaining assessment pass needs the orchestrating session.

**Why:** The remaining work is sustained judgment over about 125 stories with tracker writes other sessions own. The coordination row calls for an orchestrating Fable or Astra session; the breakdown is already written, so this recommendation deliberately starts one tier lower, on Opus or Sol at high. Policy row: substantial coordination across dependent work, one tier lower as stated.
**Reassess when:** The policy moves past `3746fab`, or #240 changes the CI exception.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text, comments and dependencies read 2026-09-25 04:51 UTC; ratings as recorded in the story · fingerprint: `e0a54c9d2c04`

The Implement action gains two text toggles: host (Claude Code or Codex, remembered per viewer in browser storage with a safe fallback) and start (Recommended or Cheaper; Cheaper is disabled with a note when none is recorded). While the recommendation is current, Implement copies the story's saved prompt for that host and start. A stale, insufficient, unassessed or unreadable story gets the generic Implement prompt with its state notice, never a custom prompt. Explain, Plan and Review keep their current text. Every prompt names the live issue URL.
- States, in text rather than color: recommended, with date and provenance and a verified or provisional availability label per host; needs reassessment; insufficient information, with the missing input; not yet assessed; assessment unavailable, when a section is present but unreadable. Never a guessed default.
- An idempotent upsert helper, for example `work/recommendations.py upsert --dry-run`. It re-reads the live body, replaces only this section, writes nothing when the normalized section is unchanged, keeps the assessment date when the fingerprint and ratings are unchanged, and reads the result back. It renders the prompt blocks from the section's fields with one template per session type and host, so every story's prompts read the same way; a hand edit to a prompt in the issue wins on the next refresh, because the guide copies the saved text. The assessor's input stays outside Git in `.local/evidence/`. The helper writes what it is given; it does not assess.

**B. Initial assessment pass** over every open story in the three repositories. On 2026-09-24 that is 116 stories: Hub 66, Nanoleaf 30, Pixoo 20. The saved snapshot still lists 118; Nanoleaf #131, #132 and #135 have closed, and Pixoo #83 needs a primary guide.

- For each story, read the body, relevant comments, linked specification and dependencies.
- Reuse an existing `Work assessment` rating when its evidence is current. Derive a missing rating only when the sources support it, and record the rationale in that story's assessment section. Unknown stays unknown.
- Write both host recommendations for a sufficiently defined story, or `insufficient` with the exact missing input. Keep any blocker, deferral, readiness and status as they are.
- Assess children separately from parents. A high-impact story keeps the stronger capability floor even for a tiny diff.
- Re-read each body before writing. Coordinate with the owners of stories in progress or in review. Report permission failures and conflicting existing assessments as pending.

**C. Snapshot and guide revision.** After the tracker writes, run `refresh_backlogs.py`, reconcile primary coverage for new stories, rebuild, run the checks and deliver a Hub PR. Account for every inventoried story as recommended (new, updated or unchanged), insufficient, or pending, with links and reasons.

Dependencies: [agent-skills#58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/58) is a required input for the assessment pass (part B), so the 116 sections are written once in the canonical shape. Part A may proceed now against this issue's interim shape and adopts the merged revision. Shared-file coordination with [PR #251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) for #85, which changes `build_guide.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `test_maintenance.py`, `guide_brief.css` and the README: rebase onto main after it merges, or coordinate with its coordinator if it stalls on the atlas approval. [#240](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240) may change guide-only CI handling; confirm the policy at merge time. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the resulting guide revision later.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- Stories remain authoritative; the guide is a dated projection. The three ratings stay model-neutral and are never averaged or derived from a title, label, file count or model choice. A recommendation grants no permission or readiness to start.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Execution recommendation` section and, where a rating is newly derived, the story's assessment section. Acceptance criteria, labels, status, assignees, priority, dependencies and other owners' text are preserved. No closing, reopening, native dependency edits or custom fields. Re-running the pass on unchanged evidence changes nothing.
- The existing brief actions (Explain, Plan, Implement, Review), their live issue URLs, focus handling, clipboard fallback, no-script GitHub link, keyboard access, phone-width fit, print and the anonymous GitHub read limits. This issue amends one rule from #196, "prompts embed no snapshot context": a custom Implement prompt embeds the model and strategy from a current recommendation, and only then. Every prompt still names the live URL and tells the agent to re-read the story. The prompt blocks sit inside the section and stay out of the freshness fingerprint.
- Generated HTML is never hand-edited. Architecture receipts and diagrams stay untouched. No credentials, private paths or transcripts enter the tracker or the guide.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
Delivery target: source-only, meaning the Hub PR plus the authorized story metadata edits. No installation, device or publication step.

1. `test_maintenance.py` covers the parser and renderer with fixtures: both hosts extracted and rendered; a missing host, duplicate section or unknown key rendering "assessment unavailable"; provisional availability rendered as unverified; a high-impact story whose ratings render unchanged beside its recommendation; a parent story typed Orchestrate and a child typed One-shot rendered independently; an unknown session type rendering "assessment unavailable"; a fingerprint mismatch rendering "needs reassessment"; a story without a section rendering "not yet assessed"; hostile text in every field and inside a prompt block rendered literally; prompts extracted per host and per start, with a missing cheaper start reported as absent rather than invented; two consecutive builds producing identical HTML.
2. The upsert helper is tested offline: unchanged content writes nothing and keeps the date; changed content replaces only the section; a body without a section gains exactly one; generated prompts follow one template per session type and host and survive a round trip through the parser.
3. `check_guide.cjs` shows the brief block with the answer line, both hosts and the session-type label as text at 390 px and 1440 px; a live status refresh that leaves the recommendation state and date unchanged; a live-only issue showing "not yet assessed"; one insufficient story showing its missing input; Implement copying the saved Claude Code and Codex prompts and the cheaper variant, the host choice persisting where storage allows, Cheaper disabled with a note where none is recorded, and a story mocked stale falling back to the generic prompt with its notice; print with the details expanded; the details control reachable by keyboard; no overflow.
4. The PR's assessment report lists every open story with its state and link, counts per state, the policy revision used, the stories left insufficient with their missing input, and any pending writes. The saved backlog reproduces every written section, and each story's readback matches.
5. The guide procedure's commands pass at the candidate with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`): `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots (both hosts, a missing-information case, phone width and print), the HTML hash and the check receipt go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/gh-<this issue>-<slug>/`.
6. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same fixed comparison, then a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). If every changed path stays under `docs/work-guide/`, record the guide-only CI exception evidence; otherwise normal CI applies. Guide UI needs no human approval. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

Limitations: recommendations are planning heuristics under the linked policy, not benchmarks. Codex availability cannot be inspected from a Claude Code session, nor the reverse, so the other host's choices carry a provisional label until a session on that host records evidence.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- Live recomputation of the fingerprint in the browser: optional. Without it, a story edited after the snapshot keeps its snapshot state and date until the next guide refresh, and the dated label makes that visible. Revisit if a reader acts on a stale recommendation.
- Closed stories and other repositories: not assessed. No history backfill.
- Public publication: pending under #87 after this guide revision merges. A Hub merge alone does not update the website.
- Custom Explain, Plan and Review prompts: not done; they stay generic. Revisit if a story's planning session needs the recommendation in its prompt.
- A CI or scheduled reassessment: never. Reassessment happens at planning or delivery pickup under the existing policy.
- Policy enforcement in the helper, such as refusing Sonnet on a high-impact story: not built, to avoid a second maintained copy of the policy. The assessor applies it and the review checks it.

issues.title: Share the dashboard command lifecycle between forms and actions
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

BUNNY's existing forms and one-click actions use one command lifecycle, so fixes to receipt handling, uncertainty and refresh ordering apply consistently. Preserve the current single-operator dashboard and its configured Pixoo/Nanoleaf controls, session labels and acknowledgments.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, [useCommand and EditForm](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L47-L98) separately maintain submission, receipt tracking, busy/locked state and refresh ordering. Both changed in [PR #239](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/239). This is maintenance work that preserves that delivered behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use one dashboard-local hook or reducer for the shared lifecycle, reusing `resultMessage`, `failureMessage`, `observedResult` and the focus helper. Forms retain draft values and configuration-revision conflicts; action buttons retain command preparation. Keep device-specific request construction and availability rules with their callers. Remove the duplicated orchestration after both callers use the common implementation; moving functions to separate files alone does not satisfy the outcome.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/231 is delivered behavior to preserve. Coordinate `apps/dashboard` edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182; skin work is independent and is not a blocker. Prefer https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244 before this work, then integration-contract consolidation; this is a preferred order, not a source dependency.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (two interaction models and asynchronous observations); uncertainty **low** (existing implementations and browser scenarios define the behavior); impact **high** because a lifecycle mistake could allow a duplicate or incorrectly guarded device command. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Reassess after command-policy or dashboard changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve fresh guards immediately before device submission, configuration-revision draft conflicts, generation-only advances, one explicit submission, no automatic retry, accepted-ticket-only receipt tracking, editable rejected drafts, and locks for uncertain/partial results until explicit reload. Keep mode-specific controls, memory-only credentials, scope checks, focus restoration and no-write inspection. Transport acceptance never establishes physical output. Keep existing wording and layout unless an additional change is explicitly scoped.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] Both `useCommand` and `EditForm` delegate shared transitions to one implementation. Code review identifies the removed duplicate logic and confirms that draft rules and device commands remain explicit at their existing boundaries.
- [ ] Focused transition tests cover prepare-blocked, accepted/queued, definite rejection, uncertain/partial, matching terminal receipt and explicit reload. A rejected ticket cannot adopt another client's receipt; no transition resubmits a command. Exercise both form and action consumers.
- [ ] Cover a preparation failure before submission and a failed refresh after a command result. Preparation failure sends no write; refresh failure preserves the original receipt/effect evidence and does not imply that nothing was sent. Neither path leaves the control permanently busy or retries automatically. Recovery must obtain current guards before another explicit device submission. Use controlled rejected promises and stale-read responses for both consumers.
- [ ] Preserve the browser matrix for fresh guards, generation races, successive power/brightness changes, retained drafts, mode reapply, Start Monitor, terminal outcomes, reconnect, focus and accessibility. Confirm each deliberate activation sends at most one write and passive reads send none.
- [ ] On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:dashboard`, `npm run typecheck:dashboard`, `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus the shared hub/contract/workflow checks required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Keep useful lower-level and browser tests. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] At pickup, record the issue-linked OpenSpec treatment under docs/sdlc.md; lifecycle/concurrency design must cover ordering and recovery even though intended behavior is unchanged. Preserve independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI and merged-revision readback. Apply the existing human approval requirement to any changed UI candidate. The PR walkthrough traces one accepted command and one uncertain command through the shared lifecycle.

## Meaningful deferrals

Visual restyling belongs to #182; this issue provides no new skin or controls. A framework-wide form system and generic device action engine have no current requirement and are excluded; revisit only if another real caller cannot use the bounded helper. Installation and physical acceptance remain separately authorized; fake/browser checks establish source behavior only.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `high` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Opus reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245. I started this session on gpt-6-sol at high reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-sol reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; high impact keeps the stronger capability floor.

**Why:** One shared command lifecycle for two interaction models, where a mistake could duplicate or misguard a device command. Policy row: high complexity or impact in a bounded outcome.
**Reassess when:** The command receipt or guard model changes.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text, comments and dependencies read 2026-09-25 03:10 UTC; ratings as recorded in the story · fingerprint: `a9d66a5b0904`

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Give B.U.N.N.Y. forms and one-click actions one command lifecycle, so receipt, uncertainty and refresh fixes apply to both. Preserve the behavior delivered in [[H231]]. Preferred after [[H244]].

issues.title: Bound browser-session resources and centralize retirement cleanup
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Repeatedly opening and closing BUNNY on the single-operator Linux/WSL hub releases each retired browser session's resources. Existing launcher, dashboard, HTTP and MCP access continue to work.

Source inspection at main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17` found that monitor reads allocate a principal ledger, while browser expiry, eviction and logout remove credentials without retiring that ledger. The 16-session cap therefore does not bound ledger entries across launches. This is a source finding; retained bytes and real-world memory growth have not been measured. See [ledger creation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L100-L140) and [launch/logout](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L218-L238).

## Smallest useful implementation

Keep the change inside the hub. Give browser-session resources one local lifecycle owner, using the existing maps where practical. Expiry, oldest-session eviction, logout, credential replacement and shutdown use one idempotent retirement path for credentials, streams and replay accounting. Retired sessions cannot admit new work; already admitted work stays tracked until settlement and is then released. Do not create a new service or persistent session store.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. The launcher from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/179 is delivered. Coordinate overlapping stream/server edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222; that is shared-file coordination, not a blocker. General memory profiling remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (session, stream and replay lifetimes); uncertainty **low** for the retention path, with exact cleanup scheduling to establish in focused tests; impact **high** because authorization and replay must remain correct. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Refresh this assessment if authentication, admission or stream ownership changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep current browser scope/alias limits, configured machine credentials, Host/Origin checks, authentication before replay, request identities, restart epochs, byte/entry limits and the rule that pending work cannot be evicted to admit more work. Retiring a browser session does not undo a submitted command, retry it, quiesce agent state or change a device writer. No credentials or private state enter test receipts.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] A focused regression covers repeated launch -> monitor read -> logout, expiry and oldest-session eviction. Session/ledger counts and replay accounting return to a documented bound after cleanup; no public diagnostics endpoint is needed. The existing repeat-launch test alone is insufficient because it does not read monitor sessions.
- [ ] Retirement closes that browser principal's streams and rejects its token and cached requests. Another browser session and configured HTTP/MCP principal remain usable. Logging out of a dashboard opened with a manually entered configured credential must not revoke that credential or reset its replay identity: reconnecting with it cannot execute an old request again. Verify both credential kinds with disposable-host authentication, replay and stream tests.
- [ ] A controlled pending command survives retirement without another execution or false cancellation. Its accounting remains charged until settlement and is then released; repeated retirement cannot double-release it. Verify with a deferred fake operation, including rejection and timeout paths.
- [ ] Preserve launcher, replay/revocation and restart tests. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:hub:mcp` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus the shared suites required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec lifecycle/concurrency design at pickup. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI and merged-revision readback. The PR walkthrough explains resource ownership, duplicate/restart behavior and the pending-retirement test; review explicitly covers authorization and replay.

## Meaningful deferrals

Process-wide profiling and performance-budget changes stay in #123; this issue proves bounded resource ownership, not an RSS improvement. Multi-operator or remote sessions are outside the selected setup and trigger reassessment if introduced. Installation and live-device trials require a separate request; source evidence does not update the installed hub.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `high` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244. I started this session on Opus at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Opus reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text

State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-sol reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; high impact keeps the stronger capability floor.

issues.title: Retire ended monitoring sessions consistently across Codex and Claude
issues.body:
## Outcome

Apply one shared-owner retirement rule to every currently supported provider/client: Codex Desktop (`codex`/`desktop`), Codex CLI (`codex`/`cli`) and Claude Code (`claude`/`code`). An accepted `runtime.ended` removes the known session and its known descendants in one durable update. Consumers reconcile the resulting snapshot.

User-approved planning, September 24, 2026. This extends [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218), whose completed delivery covers Codex Desktop. It removes the policy exception that would otherwise let an ended Claude or CLI record hold [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) in Work until expiry.

## Owner policy

- Reuse #218's atomic retirement, bounded delayed-event guards, fresh record generations and known-descendant handling. The shared owner interprets provider lifecycle evidence once; devices do not add their own end filters or timers.
- An accepted end retires monitoring even when notices or attention remain. This may discard task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state, as already accepted in #218. It does not acknowledge, mark read, report success, cancel work or terminate agents. Preserve unrelated sessions, global settings and device reservations.
- Ordinary `Stop`/`turn.ended`, `SubagentStop`, interruption, waiting, completed/read status and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not become session ends. Completed and waiting records remain until an accepted runtime end or their existing evidence expiry.
- Preserve the 24-hour fallback for absent/lost ends, using each record's evidence clock. Turn duration alone does not imply an end; add no universal 30-minute timer. A real run with no accepted lifecycle evidence for 24 hours can still expire.
- Qualify the end/start mappings for each supported path, including provider-specific exit, clear/switch and resume behavior where applicable. Missing or unqualified end evidence is a coverage gap, not an invented end. Keep hooks bounded, metadata-only and fail-open.
- An eligible new start after retirement creates a fresh record without old-effect replay. Preserve known identity/order protections across restart and missed consumer snapshots, and document their existing limits. Read evidence alone cannot recreate a record. Keep the Codex Desktop archive admission safeguard specific to that client.

## Bounded implementation

Generalize the owner path delivered by #218 and reuse its fixtures and consumer checks. Change a consumer only for a demonstrated gap. No new service, policy registry, provider watcher, historical event replay, cleanup UI or per-device cleanup command. Do not add new provider families or change native modes here.

Assess compatibility and the upgrade behavior of already-retained records using stored evidence; never infer an old end from idle/unknown activity or scan transcripts. Records without sufficient end evidence retain the existing expiry fallback. Document this transition without resetting evidence clocks or live databases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Parameterized owner/provider checks cover Codex Desktop, Codex CLI and Claude Code. An accepted known end atomically removes the record and known descendants, releases capacity and publishes one revision; unknown/repeated ends create nothing.
- [x] Mixed-provider checks preserve unrelated records. Ending one provider's last session cannot remove another provider's session, and no ended record survives merely because it is Claude or CLI.
- [x] Completion, waiting, interruption, read/acknowledgment, child turn completion, freshness uncertainty and turns over 30 minutes retain their existing semantics. Fake-clock checks preserve the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [x] Reuse focused delayed-event, fresh resume, recognizable old-end, restart, child-admission and missed-retirement checks for the newly covered paths; preserve #218's unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits.
- [x] Existing Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and dashboard checks confirm snapshot removal/fresh recreation without provider-specific cleanup. Preserve unavailable-feed handling, queues, native modes and each display's cadence.
- [x] Record provider mapping evidence and remaining installed-path gaps. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, lifecycle/state requirements, affected package/provider/setup guidance, compatibility assessment and applicable validation during implementation.
- [x] Document upgrade treatment of previously retained records and verify it with a legacy-state fixture; no fabricated end, acknowledgment, clock reset or old-effect replay.

## Verification and delivery target

Source-only. Extend existing fake-clock, provider, owner, persistence and consumer fixtures; run applicable repository checks. Synthetic events establish source behavior, not delivery from an installed client. Separately authorized installed qualification should observe a normal end and resume for each newly adopted CLI/Claude path, recording emitted events and owner removal/recreation. Named-device permission is required for any visible-light check; repeating every device's full hardware qualification is unnecessary.

#218 completed its accepted-end retirement and approved installed archive/presentation scope. Native Desktop idle/shutdown emission, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification now belong to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253). That investigation does not block this source-level generalization of accepted ends. This issue supplies owner removal to #110; it does not implement Work/Free automation or depend on #110.

## Dependencies and next action

- **Satisfied prerequisite: [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218)**, delivered through Hub #238 and Nanoleaf #116, with follow-up Hub #257 and successful merged-revision checks. Reuse its retirement contract, durable guards and consumer generation handling. The native dependency link remains as provenance; #218 is closed and no longer blocks readiness.
- [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) must validate the consistent owner policy before claiming automatic Work/Free behavior across supported providers.

Ready for source delivery. Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec change and focused provider mapping/owner tests; no unfinished source prerequisite is recorded. Installed provider qualification still needs its separate authorization and evidence. This planning update authorizes tracker changes only, not implementation, installation, settings changes, agent launches or device operations.

Planned downstream caller: [Hub #262](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/262) reuses the provider-neutral retirement guards for explicit Evict everywhere. That future command is not a prerequisite or scope expansion for this issue.

## Planning assessment

Refreshed September 25, 2026 after verified #218 completion; current Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded`. Complexity medium: provider mappings, durable owner transitions and consumer checks. Uncertainty medium: accepted-end policy is settled; actual installed emission coverage remains distinct. Impact high: incorrect identity/order handling could remove another live task's monitoring state. Ready for source work, with the existing criteria and protections retained. Reassess if provider qualification requires new collection mechanisms or changes accepted lifecycle meaning.

issues.title: Add the Sonos Move as a second playback source
issues.body:
## Outcome

When the iPhone plays Apple Music over AirPlay to the Sonos Move, alone or grouped with the Sony HT-A9, BUNNY shows what is playing and can send pause, play, next and previous. When the phone plays to the HT-A9 alone, the hub keeps showing the Sony as today. The hub picks the speaker itself: the Move whenever it reports an AirPlay session, otherwise the Sony. Today the hub sees nothing while the Move is playing; the HT-A9 reports AirPlay as `inactive`.

## Context

- [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) qualified the Move through its local UPnP AVTransport API ([qualification record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md#sonos-move-check)): title, artist, album, duration and position, plus phone-confirmed Pause, Next and Previous. Previous restarted the current song. UPnP event callbacks were not tested across WSL's NAT, so start with polling.
- [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) delivered the shared playback module with one source. Its archived design describes the two-source flow this issue would implement: each source keeps its own freshness, one explicitly selected source drives the snapshot and commands, commands never go to another source, and an unavailable selected source is shown as unavailable instead of switching silently.
- Decision, 2026-09-25, owner, in the delivery session: an ordered preference replaces the explicit `selected` source. The #175 design's no-silent-switch rule was written for a configuration-selected source; the phone chooses the output, so the owner wants the hub to follow it. The snapshot and receipts keep one stable client-facing playback ID, so B.U.N.N.Y., the MCP tools and the display cards need no change. The Tidbyt and Pixoo parsers reject unknown snapshot keys, so the 1.0 snapshot gains no field and does not say which speaker is active.

## Scope

- A Sonos source module implementing `PlaybackSource` over the Move's local UPnP AVTransport control URL at a private numeric IPv4 address. It polls `GetTransportInfo`, `GetPositionInfo` and `GetCurrentTransportActions` every two seconds; an `x-sonos-vli` track URI is the AirPlay session and any other URI is `inactive`. Controls intersect the advertised actions with the state: playing declares pause, next and previous; paused declares play, next and previous. `Play` uses speed 1. HTTP 200 is `sent`, a SOAP fault is `failed`, anything else is uncertain.
- Multi-source shared module and configuration: `playback` becomes `{"id": "...", "sources": [...]}` with the sources in preference order, at most one Sony and one Sonos. Every source is polled and keeps its own freshness. The presented source is ranked by reporting playing or paused, then freshness (available, stale, unavailable), then configured order. Snapshots and receipts carry the stable `id`. Commands go only to the presented source and only for its current controls; nothing is retried or redirected. The old `selected` form is rejected at startup and the upgrade is a documented edit.
- Position and duration stay out of the 1.0 snapshot; #38 and #39 are the revisit trigger.

Out of scope: discovery, UPnP event callbacks, artwork (#229), a runtime selection command, exposing the active speaker in the snapshot, and UI changes (#37 delivered the controls; a Play button appears when the presented source declares play).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fake-endpoint tests for the Sonos source: metadata, status, AirPlay session detection, controls by state, failed reads and sent, failed and uncertain commands.
- [ ] Fake-source tests for two sources with independent freshness and the preference rule: Move alone, grouped, Sony alone, Move offline mid-song (its last track stays visible as stale, then the Sony shows), and no command ever sent to a source that is not presented.
- [ ] Hub guide updated for the configuration change, the preference rule and the Sonos behavior; hub-playback spec, architecture guide and the qualification record updated; #301 links retargeted.
- [x] Live check with the owner: a track change on the Move reaches the hub; pause and play reach the phone; one paused next; with the phone on the Sony alone the hub shows the Sony. Passed 2026-09-26 on the installed hub 0.3.11; see the acceptance comment.

Only worth picking up if the owner plays to the Move regularly.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** A new Sonos source module and multi-source selection in the shared module and configuration.
- **Uncertainty: low.** #158 qualified the Move's UPnP API and #175 anticipates multiple sources.
- **Impact: low.** Media playback control only, with no credential or destructive effect.

issues.body:
## Outcome

An installation owner can enable BUNNY general controls on an installed hub by following the hub setup guide. They should not need to reconstruct the steps from source.

## Background

During [#154](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/154) and [#155](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/155) on September 24, 2026, the installed hub already contained the #151 and #153 UI. Its configuration had `"controllers": []`, so BUNNY could not command any device. [apps/hub/README.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/hub/README.md) describes the controller fields. Neither [SETUP.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/hub/SETUP.md) nor the [dashboard guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/dashboard/README.md) explains how to wire a device in. The coordinator worked out the steps from source and the device repositories.

## Scope

Add a "Connect device controllers for BUNNY" section to `apps/hub/SETUP.md` covering:

- **Prerequisites.** The device controller must be running and expose `/controller/v1` on numeric loopback. For Pixoo that means device mode and `PIXOO_CONTROLLER_ENABLED=1`. For Nanoleaf it means the controller service.
- **A dedicated principal per device**, created with each owner's command, so the hub never reuses another client's credential:
  - Nanoleaf: `nanoleaf controller-token --principal <id>`.
  - Pixoo: `npm run mcp:credentials -- add <data-dir> <id> control`.
- **The controller entry:** `id`, `kind`, `controllerId`, `deviceId`, `endpoint` and `token`. Show how to read `controllerId` and `deviceId` from a native snapshot. Keep tokens only in the owner-only config, and never print them.
- **Back up, then restart the hub service,** and verify: health lists each device, native snapshots validate, and the launcher session shows the controls.
- **Rollback:** restore the config, revoke each principal, restart.
- **Troubleshooting:**
  - A registered device shows `unknown` health until its first request.
  - Pixoo Monitor presentation needs an explicit mode command after an app start.
  - A controller stopped mid-session reports unavailable until it returns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SETUP.md has the section above, with placeholders instead of private paths, IPs or tokens.
- [ ] The dashboard guide links to it from "Build and access".
- [ ] A reviewer can follow the section against a disposable hub and the fake controllers used by the existing tests. No installed service or device is touched.

issues.title: Push hub change notifications when state commits
issues.body:
## Outcome

Readers of the hub's change stream learn about a new revision as soon as it commits, instead of up to a second later. The dashboard updates right after a hook event. Nanoleaf can later replace its once-a-second poll with this stream.

## Current behavior

`GET /api/monitor/v1/changes` is a Server-Sent Events stream. Each open stream runs its own 1-second timer. The timer reads the owner snapshot, compares a small fingerprint (revision, collector, loss count, rejected admissions, uncertain count) and writes a `state` event or a heartbeat ([server.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L262-L292)). A commit reaches readers 0 to 1 s later. The first stream whose timer fires also advances the shared feed state (fingerprint, sequence and 32-entry history) for all streams.

The agent-state core already signals every commit with `feeds.publish(revision)`, in `commit` and in `replaceSessions` ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L134), [index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L147)), but the hub doesn't listen. `owner.subscribe` doesn't fit: it takes a configured consumer ID and allows one subscription per ID, and the consumer list is part of durable state, so adding a hub consumer would make existing stores fail with `incompatible-state`.

Both call sites run inside `queue`'s try/catch ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L118-L121)). An error thrown there after the write is durable marks the collector `faulted` and stops ingest until restart.

Commits come from more than the events route:

- hook ingest
- the Codex Desktop read-state reader from #219, which calls `owner.ingest` in-process
- label, acknowledge and recovery commands
- maintenance: journal pruning, 24-hour session expiry and approval settlement

## Scope

- [ ] Give the hub a commit notification from the owner that needs no consumer ID. The core raises it at both `feeds.publish` call sites, after the in-memory state update. Hooking the core covers every commit source, including future ones, without wrapping each hub call. A listener on the owner API is one option. Another is an anonymous subscription that reuses the bounded channel in `subscriptions.ts`, which already delivers asynchronously.
- [ ] Keep the commit path isolated. The core catches listener errors. The hub schedules its fan-out outside the commit call, for example with `setImmediate`, instead of reading a snapshot for every stream synchronously inside the commit.
- [ ] Split the per-stream publish step. On each notification or timer tick, advance the shared feed state once, then flush each open stream. Coalesce a burst of commits into at most one write per stream.
- [ ] Keep the 1-second timer for heartbeats, the per-stream auth recheck and changes that don't commit (collector state, quiesce, loss count, rejected admissions, sessions turning uncertain).
- [ ] Add a test-only option for the timer interval, which is hard-coded at 1000 ms. Keep it out of the configuration file that `cli.ts` validates.
- [ ] Keep the wire format and limits as they are: event IDs, the 32-entry replay window, resync on an unknown cursor, the 16-stream cap and disconnecting a reader stalled for more than 5 s. Bursts now produce more events, so the window covers fewer seconds and a reconnecting reader gets `resync` more often. Both current clients refetch the snapshot on `resync`.
- [ ] A slow or paused reader must not delay ingest, commits or other readers.
- [ ] Add the issue-linked OpenSpec change `gh-222-<slug>` that docs/sdlc.md requires for a changed contract with timing and concurrency effects. Update `agent-state-core`, which currently allows subscriptions only for registered consumers, and `standalone-hub-host` for push on commit. The design covers commit-path isolation and the shorter replay horizon.
- [ ] Update the owner API table in the agent-state README and the `/changes` row in the hub README. Publish agent-state 3.1.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A hub test shows a committed event reaching an open stream without waiting for the timer, using a long test-only timer interval.
- [ ] Tests cover a burst of commits, a commit from the in-process read-state reader, a maintenance commit and a paused reader that doesn't delay ingest.
- [ ] An agent-state test shows a throwing listener leaves the collector `running` and the commit's outcome successful.
- [ ] The existing feed tests pass unchanged: hub HTTP, dashboard matrix and the performance stalled-reader check.
- [ ] The agent-state, standalone hub and workflow checks listed in AGENTS.md pass. The OpenSpec change is synced and archived on the delivery branch.
- [ ] Live, after the installed monitor is updated separately: watch `/changes` with `curl -N`, submit a Codex prompt and confirm the `state` event arrives within 250 ms of the hook's ingest. One comment records the result and how it was timed.

## Not included

- Nanoleaf reading the stream instead of polling. That is [codex-nanoleaf#90](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/90), which this issue blocks.
- Tidbyt's 30-second poll. Its writes are at least 15 s apart, so earlier notice doesn't help it.
- Session data in the stream, and any message broker.

## Readiness

Complexity low. Uncertainty low. Impact medium: the notification runs on the commit path every consumer depends on, and an unisolated listener error would stop ingest until restart. No blockers. The owner API addition is a minor agent-state version (3.1.0). Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md, including the OpenSpec change above.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: low.** The story calls it small: one listener on the existing feeds.publish signal.
- **Impact: medium.** Runs on the state owner's commit path that every consumer reads; listener errors must stay isolated.

issues.title: Apply the Neon skin foundation and B.U.N.N.Y. display name to the dashboard
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Move the dashboard's colors and fonts onto the role names in the accepted [application UI style guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/application-ui-style-guide.md) (section 4), held in one Neon Geometry Wars skin file, and change the visible name from `BUNNY` to `B.U.N.N.Y.`. Adding another skin later should then mean adding a file, not editing views. This is presentation work on the existing single-operator dashboard in `apps/dashboard`, not new device behavior.

The required input, [Hub #181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181), is delivered (`873041a`, PR #250). The documentation skin from [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) (PR #251) is a working model: `docs/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css` and the color checker `docs/skins/check_tokens.py`.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Skin file.** Add one application skin file, for example `apps/dashboard/src/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css`, that defines the section 4.1 roles and holds every color value. `style.css` uses only `var(--role)`. Remove the duplicated override rules at the end of `style.css` (focus outline, selected navigation, stats gradient) by folding the winning values into the tokens.
- **Keep the current look.** Use the dashboard's current values, not the Neon reference values, where they differ (link `#b6cdff`, accent-ink `#101724`, the slate edges). Use the dense pair (`--muted-dense`, `--edge-dense`) throughout. Apart from the name, the result should look the same as today.
- **Colors without a role.** Merge near-identical pale text shades (`#bac8de`, `#bdc9df`, `#b7c4da`, `#afbfda`, `#c7d8fc`, `#c6d8f9`, `#dbe5f6`) into `--text` or `--muted-dense` where the difference isn't visible. Component fills with no 4.1 role (badge fill and edge, stats gradient, secondary-button hover set, notice rule, empty-state border) become private tokens in the skin file. Section 4 needs no amendment.
- **Dark only.** The dashboard has always been dark (`color-scheme:dark`). The skin file defines dark values only; light values from guide step 4.4 are deferred.
- **Color check.** Add a small check to `npm run test:dashboard` that fails on any hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()` or named color in dashboard CSS outside the skin file, following `check_tokens.py`.
- **Rename.** Change every user-visible `BUNNY` to `B.U.N.N.Y.`: the shell wordmark, login eyebrow and "Open BUNNY with the Hub launcher.", footer, the status sentences in `client.ts` ("BUNNY can’t see the device…") and `main.tsx` ("BUNNY couldn’t read…"), and the hub CLI line "BUNNY opened in the browser." in `apps/hub/src/cli.ts`. Update the tests that assert these strings (`apps/dashboard/tests/*.mjs`). Package names, paths, API identifiers, environment variables and anchors such as `#open-bunny-without-typing-a-token` stay unchanged. No acronym expansion or logo.
- **README.** Replace the "until then" note in `apps/dashboard/README.md` with a link to the skin file and guide section 4.4.

Dependencies: none open. [#245](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245) and [#247](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/247) also edit `apps/dashboard`. They don't block this issue, but don't run them at the same time.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Pending (magenta), selection (cyan), device or task status and keyboard focus (white) stay visually and textually distinct. Capability and permission explanations, command guards, selection, drafts, focus recovery, pending and uncertain outcomes, stale evidence, and no-write inspection keep working as they do today. The layout and breakpoints stay the same. No decorative motion is added. The Nanoleaf wall map and its tokens stay in their own repository.

## Acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] **AC1 - Token layer.** Every dashboard color, font stack and radius comes from the skin file through a section 4.1 role, a dense variant or a private skin token. The new color check passes, and fails when a raw color is added to `style.css`. Evidence: the diff and the check's output.
- [ ] **AC2 - Same look, new name.** Re-capture the #181 frames (1440 and 390 px: login, login focus, activity, empty, component selected, primary focus, pending, unavailable, uncertain, error, stale) and compare them side by side with the originals in the owner's `.local/evidence/gh-181-ui-foundation/dashboard/`. The only intended difference is the name. Check contrast in the browser for any pair whose value changed.
- [ ] **AC3 - Behavior and accessibility unchanged.** The existing dashboard unit and browser checks pass, including the axe WCAG 2.1 AA scans, reduced motion, and the no-write, drafts, focus and uncertain-result scenarios. Fake controllers prove source behavior only.
- [ ] **AC4 - Name.** A search of dashboard and hub CLI user-facing strings finds no `BUNNY`, and the screenshots show `B.U.N.N.Y.` in both the logged-out and logged-in states.

Delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md, including the human approval of this UI candidate. With no product contract change, record that rationale instead of an OpenSpec change.

## Meaningful deferrals

- **Light scheme.** Revisit when the dashboard needs a light mode or a second skin; until then, the skin file is dark only.
- **Second skin, skin picker, saved preference, decoration.** Deferred until a second look is chosen (guide section 4.4 step 4).
- **Moving to the Neon reference values.** Revisit if the owner wants the dashboard to match the wall map exactly; that is a separate UI candidate.
- **Glossary labels in the UI** (for example "Eyes" for freshness). Owned by a later UI issue.

## Assessment and readiness

Refreshed 2026-09-25 against Hub `main` `d85b8b3` (the only change since #181 is guide decoration wording, which does not affect this issue). Scope was trimmed at the owner's request; the previous text is in the issue's edit history.
