- Complexity: **low**. One CSS file of about 50 raw colors, about 7 strings, and test text updates.

The required input, [Hub #181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181), is delivered (`873041a`, PR #250). The documentation skin from [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) (PR #251) is a working model: `docs/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css` and the color checker `docs/skins/check_tokens.py`.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- **Skin file.** Add one application skin file, for example `apps/dashboard/src/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css`, that defines the section 4.1 roles and holds every color value. `style.css` uses only `var(--role)`. Remove the duplicated override rules at the end of `style.css` (focus outline, selected navigation, stats gradient) by folding the winning values into the tokens.
- **Keep the current look.** Use the dashboard's current values, not the Neon reference values, where they differ (link `#b6cdff`, accent-ink `#101724`, the slate edges). Use the dense pair (`--muted-dense`, `--edge-dense`) throughout. Apart from the name, the result should look the same as today.
- **Colors without a role.** Merge near-identical pale text shades (`#bac8de`, `#bdc9df`, `#b7c4da`, `#afbfda`, `#c7d8fc`, `#c6d8f9`, `#dbe5f6`) into `--text` or `--muted-dense` where the difference isn't visible. Component fills with no 4.1 role (badge fill and edge, stats gradient, secondary-button hover set, notice rule, empty-state border) become private tokens in the skin file. Section 4 needs no amendment.
- **Dark only.** The dashboard has always been dark (`color-scheme:dark`). The skin file defines dark values only; light values from guide step 4.4 are deferred.
- **Color check.** Add a small check to `npm run test:dashboard` that fails on any hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()` or named color in dashboard CSS outside the skin file, following `check_tokens.py`.
- **Rename.** Change every user-visible `BUNNY` to `B.U.N.N.Y.`: the shell wordmark, login eyebrow and "Open BUNNY with the Hub launcher.", footer, the status sentences in `client.ts` ("BUNNY can’t see the device…") and `main.tsx` ("BUNNY couldn’t read…"), and the hub CLI line "BUNNY opened in the browser." in `apps/hub/src/cli.ts`. Update the tests that assert these strings (`apps/dashboard/tests/*.mjs`). Package names, paths, API identifiers, environment variables and anchors such as `#open-bunny-without-typing-a-token` stay unchanged. No acronym expansion or logo.
- **README.** Replace the "until then" note in `apps/dashboard/README.md` with a link to the skin file and guide section 4.4.

Dependencies: none open. [#245](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245) and [#247](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/247) also edit `apps/dashboard`. They don't block this issue, but don't run them at the same time.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text: Pending (magenta), selection (cyan), device or task status and keyboard focus (white) stay visually and textually distinct. Capability and permission explanations, command guards, selection, drafts, focus recovery, pending and uncertain outcomes, stale evidence, and no-write inspection keep working as they do today. The layout and breakpoints stay the same. No decorative motion is added. The Nanoleaf wall map and its tokens stay in their own repository.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- **Light scheme.** Revisit when the dashboard needs a light mode or a second skin; until then, the skin file is dark only.
- **Second skin, skin picker, saved preference, decoration.** Deferred until a second look is chosen (guide section 4.4 step 4).
- **Moving to the Neon reference values.** Revisit if the owner wants the dashboard to match the wall map exactly; that is a separate UI candidate.
- **Glossary labels in the UI** (for example "Eyes" for freshness). Owned by a later UI issue.

The initial music path uses the shared playback and Sony modules delivered together in [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), with no Windows executable or host music connector. Container migration does not block the first useful local release. Preserve controller-owned storage and a single writer per device.

For the selected Sony music path, verify outbound unicast HTTP from the actual container to the privately configured receiver and the authenticated hub routes used by clients. Do not add multicast discovery, audio-device mounts or Windows interoperability for this adapter. Ordinary bridge networking is a candidate to verify, not an installed guarantee; hub bind address, published ports, Host/Origin checks and credentials must be qualified together. Preserve existing access boundaries. Live receiver checks require explicit target/sequence authorization. This issue owns Docker evidence; [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175)'s WSL evidence is separate. General packaging can proceed independently; verifying the music feature waits for its service/adapter.

issues.title: Show Apple Music now-playing cards on Pixoo and Tidbyt
issues.body:
Add now-playing presentations for Pixoo and Tidbyt, using the source-independent playback interface from [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), initially backed by Sony, and each display's existing controller. Start with readable track and artist text. Artwork is optional: reuse [playback artwork story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) when available, then size/render it in each display owner. Text-only delivery does not depend on that extension or the deferred Windows source [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36). Poll the shared snapshot initially; no SSE requirement.

Qualify refresh cadence, stale playback behavior and restoration after alerts. Tidbyt begins with the accepted cloud connection. Keep rendering and physical writes with the owning controllers.

When artwork is added, acceptance must cover correctly sized, readable rendering on Pixoo and Tidbyt, updates after track/source changes and a text fallback when artwork is absent. Record renderer checks separately from separately authorized physical display acceptance. If this text-only issue closes first, [#229](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) must link open follow-up work for that rendering and acceptance; it must not be left as an optional note on a closed issue.

## Delivery scope (settled 2026-09-25)

The owner settled these at the delivery checkpoints on 2026-09-25. They replace the placeholder note above.

**Outcome and setup.** One operator, the installed hub with the Sony HT-A9 as playback source `ht-a9`, the installed Tidbyt runner (#21) and the installed Pixoo service. Both displays read `GET /api/playback/v1/snapshot` with a read credential that lists the source in `devices`. Text only: track and artist, no artwork.

**Smallest implementation.** Two PRs, Tidbyt first:

1. Hub (`controllers/tidbyt`): a now-playing publisher in the existing runner, opt-in through its private config. It writes through the same controller queue as the status tile.
2. Pixoo ([divoom-app-upgrade](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade)): a 64×64 card rendered and written by the Pixoo app's existing player and serialized writer.

**Tidbyt decisions**

- Placement and alerts: a second background installation beside the status tile, in the normal rotation. Alerts never interrupt it, so nothing needs restoring. Foreground takeover stays unqualified.
- Cadence: read the snapshot every 5 s. Push only when the card changes, at most once every 15 s, coalescing to the latest. Push an unchanged card again after 10 minutes.
- Stale: `available` with `playing` or `paused` shows the card, with a pause marker when paused. `stale` (5 to 30 s) keeps the last card dimmed and marked `?`. `unavailable`, `stopped`, `inactive` or `unknown` removes the tile. A failed read counts as stale until the last good observation is 30 s old. A missing read never becomes `paused`.

**Pixoo decisions**

- Monitor mode (agent dashboard): a new track, or playback starting, shows the card for 10 s, then the dashboard returns. If a session needs attention (approval, input or question), or attention arrives, the dashboard shows at once and the pop-up is dropped, not replayed.
- Media mode (playlists): a setting with Off (default, today's rule that nothing takes over Media), Pop-up (pause the playlist for the 10 s card, then resume it; the current item restarts) and Whole song (show the card while music plays or is paused, then resume the playlist when it stops or becomes unavailable). A manual player or mode action during a takeover cancels the automatic resume.
- The setting lives in the Pixoo settings UI and persists with the presentation configuration. That UI change needs the owner's approval of the current candidate.
- Cadence: read the snapshot every 2 s. Redraw only when the card changes, through the existing Monitor upload gate. Long text wraps or truncates; no scrolling.
- Stale: the same as Tidbyt, except that `unavailable`, `stopped` or `inactive` returns to the dashboard (Monitor) or resumes the playlist (Media).

**Preserve.** One writer per device through its existing queue. The Tidbyt status tile's behavior and cadence. Pixoo's Monitor/Media semantics outside the new setting, its playback recovery, originals and renditions. No hub changes to playback, credentials or controllers. Nothing contacts a device in tests.

**Acceptance and evidence**

- Tidbyt: fake hub and fake cloud tests for the card render (golden frame), the 5 s read, the change-only push with the 15 s gate and 10-minute refresh, the stale `?` card, removal on unavailable, stopped or inactive, the failed-read rule, installation targeting through the shared queue, the status tile unchanged, and the opt-in runner config. `npm run test:tidbyt`, `test:tidbyt:python` and the shared build, type, contract and workflow checks pass.
- Pixoo: fake hub tests for the card render, the Monitor pop-up with attention cut-short, the Media Off, Pop-up and Whole song behavior with resume and manual-cancel cases, stale handling and the persisted setting. Browser tests cover the settings control. Pixoo `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass. The owner approves the settings UI.
- Delivery target: both PRs merged with their CI read back. Installing the updated runner and Pixoo service and checking each physical display are separate steps that need their own go-ahead.

**Deferred**

- Artwork: [#229](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) keeps open follow-up work for sized rendering and acceptance on both displays.
- A Pixoo rotation slot in Media: revisit if the owner asks for it; it changes the playlist engine.
- A Tidbyt foreground or pop-up card: needs foreground push qualification first.
- Marquee scrolling for long titles: revisit if truncation proves unreadable on the device.
- Installation and physical checks: owner go-ahead after merge.

- **Uncertainty: low.** The comment names the credential and scope; refresh and stale policy are bounded choices.
- **Impact: low.** Read-only snapshot consumption and rendering through each display controller.

issues.body:
Show the active song, artist and playback status in the shared frontend. The first delivery is text-only. Expose supported play, pause and next-track commands through the UI and local Codex tools.

This extends the general device controls planned in [hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31).

## Required scope when refined

- Extend the existing authorization setup so intended browser-launch sessions and Codex MCP clients can read and, when granted, control their configured playback source. Browser-launch sessions currently have no playback grant. Keep browser sessions and machine credentials within their existing boundaries; grant only the required source-scoped read/control access, without broad device, ingestion or administrative access.
- Bind every command to the displayed/requested source. Show controls only when both source capability and client permission allow them. Cover read-only access, denied source access and unsupported commands with focused tests using the existing authorization model.

## Guide

**Topic:** controls-music
**Note:** Text-only now-playing and the Sony-qualified controls (pause, next, previous) in B.U.N.N.Y. and Codex tools, using shared playback from [[H175]]. B.U.N.N.Y. sessions need a small hub change to read the playback source. Sony play/resume is qualified separately in [[H242]].

## Acceptance (refined at delivery pickup, 2026-09-25)

Setup: one operator, the installed standalone hub with the `ht-a9` Sony source, launcher-opened B.U.N.N.Y. sessions and the Codex MCP client. Smallest implementation: extend the existing hub grants, MCP registration and dashboard; no new service, feed or source selection.

1. **Browser grant.** A launcher-issued browser session gets `read` and `control` on the configured playback source ID as well as the controller aliases, and nothing more (no ingest, admin or MCP). The dashboard context names the playback source only when the caller's credential grants it.
2. **Now playing view.** B.U.N.N.Y. shows the granted source's title, artist, optional album, status, availability and observation age by polling the snapshot. Stale shows the last values marked stale; unavailable shows no track and says so; `inactive` says AirPlay is not the receiver's input.
3. **Controls.** Buttons appear only for actions the snapshot currently declares, and only for a control-scoped client while the source is available. The view names why the others are missing: read-only access, a stale or unavailable source, or an action the source does not declare (play/resume waits for #242). Each press reads the snapshot again, then sends one command bound to the displayed source ID with a new request ID. The view shows sent, refused and uncertain results; an uncertain result locks until an explicit reload and nothing retries.
4. **Codex tools.** The hub MCP registers a read-scope playback status tool and a control-scope playback command tool bound to the source ID. They are listed and callable only for credentials with that source in `devices` and the matching scope. The command tool takes a request ID and action. Rejections are typed with no prior effects, an uncertain result reports possible effects, nothing retries, and a staged hub refuses commands.
5. **Paused controls.** Owner live check on 2026-09-25 (receiver acknowledgments plus the owner's phone observation): with AirPlay paused, `setPlayNextContent` and `setPlayPreviousContent` changed the phone's track without resuming, but the receiver kept reporting the old title. The Sony source therefore declares `next` and `previous` (not `pause` or `play`) while paused. The UI and tool descriptions warn that the title may lag until playback resumes.
6. **Evidence.** Focused fake-service tests cover the browser grant, a credential without the source, read-only access, unsupported and unavailable controls, MCP discovery and calls, the paused declaration and a dashboard browser scenario. Existing Hub, MCP and Dashboard CI jobs run them.
7. **After merge, separately authorized.** Install the merged hub, then in the installed B.U.N.N.Y. and in a real Codex MCP session read the current snapshot and send one supported command to `ht-a9`. Record real client behavior separately from fake-service tests and transport acknowledgments. UI approval of the current candidate is required before merge.

Deferred: artwork presentation (#229 keeps the UI rendering story), source-selection UI (until a second real source), an SSE playback feed and play/resume (#242).

issues.title: Defer Windows Apple Music as an optional playback source
issues.body:
## Outcome and priority

Deferred: add the native Windows Apple Music app as an optional later source of the [shared playback and Sony delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175). The initial music delivery uses the Sony HT-A9 through [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) and requires no Windows helper or program.

Owner decision, September 24, 2026: Linux/Docker-compatible playback service first, Sony first real adapter, Windows integration later only if still wanted. This issue no longer owns the shared service and does not block UI, displays, lighting, Music presets or Sony delivery.

## Boundary to revisit before implementation

- Keep Windows-specific access behind a source adapter and reuse the shared snapshot/command contract. A Linux container cannot directly consume the native Windows media-session API; any later Windows-local helper or remote producer needs an explicit placement decision and installed qualification.
- Do not preselect Python/pywinrt, PowerShell subprocess supervision, login startup, a tray application or a connector push protocol. Qualify the smallest approach from the actual host environment when this deferred work is selected.
- Select Apple Music by `GetSessions()` and its qualified `SourceAppUserModelId`, never the system's current-session heuristic. Test alongside another media app and with Apple Music in the background.
- Report available metadata and controls without requiring duration, progress or artwork. Retain unavailable/stale observations, exact command targeting, unsupported controls, request correlation and no automatic retry of uncertain writes.
- If this becomes the second source, implement the minimum coexistence/selection behavior through the shared service, with an explicit selection that never changes merely because another source updates or the selected source disappears. Coordinate any selection UI with [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37); do not duplicate the playback service.

## Acceptance to refine when selected

- [ ] **AC1.** Record the chosen placement, installed Windows/app versions, exact session identity, useful fields and isolated supported-control results in the issue-linked OpenSpec design. Historical probe evidence is not current app qualification.

issues.title: Add automatic agent status to LIFX
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The qualified LIFX A19 `pendant-1` shows shared agent status from the installed hub. It turns amber when any session needs the owner, blue while a session works, green while a finished turn is unacknowledged, and warm white when nothing is outstanding. Manual control stays predictable: a change made in the LIFX app stays until the next status change, and the owner can switch the bulb to Free from B.U.N.N.Y. to stop painting.

Setup: one operator, the installed hub, Codex and Claude sessions on the shared state owner, and the [local controller host](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/local-controllers/README.md) from #289, which is the single LIFX writer. Excluded: the Beam (#319, #327), lighting effects (none are supported), Nanoleaf and Pixoo behavior, installation and the physical check (#22).

### Decisions

The owner settled these on 2026-09-25. They replace the four open questions this story carried since 2026-09-24.

1. **Bulbs, colors and brightness.** Only `pendant-1`, the one qualified bulb. Attention is amber, working is blue and done is green, with the same meanings as the Tidbyt tile's `ASK`, `RUN` and `DONE`; start from `STATUS_COLORS` in `controllers/tidbyt/src/status.ts`. Idle, meaning no session has anything outstanding, is warm white at 2700 K with zero saturation. Every paint uses a per-bulb brightness cap from the host configuration, default 50%; Quiet uses a lower quiet cap, default 20%. #267 and #373 may later replace these fixed values.
2. **Sessions.** One bulb shows the highest-priority state across root sessions: attention, then working, then done, then idle. A root whose child is active is working, as on the Tidbyt. Read evidence does not retire done; any consumer's acknowledgment does. Session ends and retirement follow the shared owner (#312, #241, #195). Silence never means done.
3. **Modes.** Each qualified bulb has a mode, `Work`, `Quiet` or `Free`, advertised through the controller v1 `modes` capability and set from B.U.N.N.Y. with `mode.set`. Work paints every state at the cap. Quiet paints only attention, at the quiet cap, and otherwise leaves the bulb alone. Free paints nothing and enables the color and temperature controls. The mode persists per bulb in the host's state directory under `~/.local/state/agent-device-hub/lifx/` and starts as Free until the owner sets it. Painting never changes power: a bulb the owner turned off stays off. Stopping the host retires pending automation and leaves the bulb as it is; a request already sent may finish. Starting the host in Work paints the current state once; Quiet paints once only if attention is outstanding.
4. **Manual change.** The host paints only when the shown state changes, never on a heartbeat, an unchanged snapshot or a repeated read, and never on a timer. A change made in the LIFX app therefore stays until the next transition, and nothing restores an earlier appearance. A failed paint is not replayed; the next transition is a fresh request for the current state. When the feed is unavailable or a session's freshness is uncertain, the host paints nothing and the last appearance stays. Detection of an outside change and the B.U.N.N.Y. hint stay in #362, which is not a prerequisite.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Status publisher in the host.** Add a LIFX status publisher, in `controllers/lifx` beside the controller and started by the local controller host the way the host starts the Tidbyt runner. It reads the hub's `/api/monitor/v1/sessions` with the Tidbyt runner's cadence (every 30 s and on each change notice) using the same read-only hub credential pattern. `HubStatusFeed` and the per-session state ranking live in `controllers/tidbyt/src/runner.ts` and `status.ts` today; share them from one place both consumers use rather than copying them, so the Tidbyt and the bulb never disagree about a session's state.
- **One absolute write per paint.** A paint is one zero-duration `LightSetColor` with the full HSBK, through the bulb's existing queue and request namespace, shown in `lighting.pending` like a color command. It does not use the public read-modify-write color and brightness commands, which would take two transitions per paint.
- **Modes in the controller.** `LifxController` advertises `modes` with `Work`, `Quiet` and `Free` for qualified bulbs, accepts `mode.set`, reports the desired mode in the snapshot and reads the persisted mode at start. Unqualified bulbs such as the Beam advertise no modes and are never painted.
- **Host configuration.** A per-bulb `status` block with the brightness cap and quiet cap, plus the hub URL, owner ID and read-only token for the feed, in the existing private host JSON.
- **B.U.N.N.Y.** The LIFX page shows the mode control for these three modes (today `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx` allows modes only for Nanoleaf and Pixoo). In Work and Quiet the color and temperature controls are disabled with the ADR 0005 reason and a one-click Switch to Free, as the Nanoleaf page does for scenes. Power and brightness stay mode-independent.
- **Docs and specs.** Record the decisions in `controllers/lifx/README.md`, the configuration in `apps/local-controllers/README.md`, and the story's OpenSpec change. The existing `test:lifx`, `test:local-controllers` and dashboard checks cover the new tests; add commands to `docs/development.md` only if a new package script is needed.

Required issues: none open. #18, #3 and divoom-app-upgrade#31 are closed; #289 and #330 are delivered and installed.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per bulb: the host and its lease. The hub routes; it never writes to a bulb directly. No second lifecycle reducer: the publisher reads the shared owner's snapshot, never acknowledges notices and never infers a state the owner did not report.
- Missing or stale evidence never means done, read or connected. An unavailable feed never paints idle.
- The controller's bounded queue, retries, cancellation and shutdown. Cancelling never claims to undo a physical write.
- Manual control: painting never changes power, nothing restores automatically, and an unchanged feed never repaints.
- The #330 on-demand reads and their limits. Painting adds no polling and never reads the Beam.
- Only a color reaches the bulb. That is a display limit, not a privacy rule.
- ADR 0005 and ADR 0006 semantics: Work and Quiet are status presentation, Free is content, and the painted state is the base presentation a later #337 moment returns to.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. Fake feed and fake transport tests, no bulb traffic.

- [ ] **Mapping.** A fake feed with sessions in each state paints the expected HSBK at the cap; several sessions paint the highest-priority state; no outstanding session paints warm white; Quiet paints attention at the quiet cap and nothing else.
- [ ] **Transitions only.** The same snapshot repeated, a heartbeat and a read with new evidence but the same state send no write. A different HSBK reported by the fake transport, standing in for an app change, survives them and is repainted only at the next transition.
- [ ] **Stale input.** An unavailable feed and an uncertain session send no write and leave the last appearance. Recovery paints only if the state differs from the last painted state.
- [ ] **Offline bulb.** With two fake bulbs, one that times out does not stop the other. The failed paint is not replayed; the next transition paints both.
- [ ] **Modes.** `mode.set` receipts for the three modes; Free stops painting and leaves the bulb; returning to Work paints the current state once; the mode survives a host restart through the state directory; a bulb with no recorded mode starts in Free.
- [ ] **Stop.** Closing the host with paints queued cancels them, sends nothing more and leaves the bulb; a write already in flight completes and its receipt says so.
- [ ] **B.U.N.N.Y.** The LIFX page shows the mode control; color and temperature are disabled in Work and Quiet with the reason and Switch to Free, and enabled in Free. This is a UI change outside the work guide, so it needs the owner's explicit approval of the candidate under the docs/sdlc.md UI approval scope.
- [ ] **Checks.** `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:lifx`, `npm run test:local-controllers`, the dashboard checks, the contract checks and the workflow checks exit zero from the worktree root on Node 24. The OpenSpec change is synchronized and archived on the delivery branch.

Installed visual acceptance, including the real app change, unplugging a bulb and stopping the host, belongs to #22.

## Meaningful deferrals

- **Outside-change detection and hint:** #362. Consequence: B.U.N.N.Y. keeps reporting external control as unknown; the manual-change policy needs no detection because painting happens only on transitions.
- **Beam:** #319 for control and #327 for the per-session zone strip. Consequence: the Beam stays untouched by status.
- **Shared and provider colors:** #267 and #373. Consequence: fixed default colors until then.
- **Moments on LIFX:** #337, which returns to the base this story paints.
- **LIFX in the desk presets:** an extension of #67 after this story.
- **A brightness or power override that lasts until the next mode command, as on Nanoleaf:** not adopted. The next transition repaints brightness at the cap. Revisit if #22 finds this surprising.
- **Every-client compatibility and long-running reliability:** not claimed. A repeatable observed defect gets a focused follow-up.

## Prerequisites

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/18 (closed)
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3 (closed)
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31 (closed)
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/330 (closed, installed)

Personal-project scope retained from 2026-09-23; behavior boundaries clarified on 2026-09-24; decisions recorded and the story rewritten in the feature form on 2026-09-25. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This issue does not authorize installation or bulb writes.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `a6aa402`.

- **Complexity: medium.** A feed consumer and state mapper in the host, a per-bulb mode with persistence in the controller, one new internal write through the existing queue, and a dashboard mode control with ADR 0005 gating. The queue, leases, feed reader and state ranking already exist.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The four behavior decisions are recorded above. The consumption pattern is the installed Tidbyt runner, and the writer is the installed host.
- **Impact: medium.** Automatic writes to a physical bulb the owner also uses as a lamp. Effects are reversible from B.U.N.N.Y. or the LIFX app, painting never changes power, and no credential or data changes beyond one more read-only hub token in the private host file.
- **Readiness: ready.** Source delivery first; the B.U.N.N.Y. change needs the owner's UI approval, and installation and the physical check stay with #22.

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match.

outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
The qualified LIFX A19 `pendant-1` shows shared agent status from the installed hub. It turns amber when any session needs the owner, blue while a session works, green while a finished turn is unacknowledged, and warm white when nothing is outstanding. Manual control stays predictable: a change made in the LIFX app stays until the next status change, and the owner can switch the bulb to Free from B.U.N.N.Y. to stop painting.

Setup: one operator, the installed hub, Codex and Claude sessions on the shared state owner, and the [local controller host](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/local-controllers/README.md) from #289, which is the single LIFX writer. Excluded: the Beam (#319, #327), lighting effects (none are supported), Nanoleaf and Pixoo behavior, installation and the physical check (#22).

### Decisions

The owner settled these on 2026-09-25. They replace the four open questions this story carried since 2026-09-24.

1. **Bulbs, colors and brightness.** Only `pendant-1`, the one qualified bulb. Attention is amber, working is blue and done is green, with the same meanings as the Tidbyt tile's `ASK`, `RUN` and `DONE`; start from `STATUS_COLORS` in `controllers/tidbyt/src/status.ts`. Idle, meaning no session has anything outstanding, is warm white at 2700 K with zero saturation. Every paint uses a per-bulb brightness cap from the host configuration, default 50%; Quiet uses a lower quiet cap, default 20%. #267 and #373 may later replace these fixed values.
2. **Sessions.** One bulb shows the highest-priority state across root sessions: attention, then working, then done, then idle. A root whose child is active is working, as on the Tidbyt. Read evidence does not retire done; any consumer's acknowledgment does. Session ends and retirement follow the shared owner (#312, #241, #195). Silence never means done.
3. **Modes.** Each qualified bulb has a mode, `Work`, `Quiet` or `Free`, advertised through the controller v1 `modes` capability and set from B.U.N.N.Y. with `mode.set`. Work paints every state at the cap. Quiet paints only attention, at the quiet cap, and otherwise leaves the bulb alone. Free paints nothing and enables the color and temperature controls. The mode persists per bulb in the host's state directory under `~/.local/state/agent-device-hub/lifx/` and starts as Free until the owner sets it. Painting never changes power: a bulb the owner turned off stays off. Stopping the host retires pending automation and leaves the bulb as it is; a request already sent may finish. Starting the host in Work paints the current state once; Quiet paints once only if attention is outstanding.
4. **Manual change.** The host paints only when the shown state changes, never on a heartbeat, an unchanged snapshot or a repeated read, and never on a timer. A change made in the LIFX app therefore stays until the next transition, and nothing restores an earlier appearance. A failed paint is not replayed; the next transition is a fresh request for the current state. When the feed is unavailable or a session's freshness is uncertain, the host paints nothing and the last appearance stays. Detection of an outside change and the B.U.N.N.Y. hint stay in #362, which is not a prerequisite.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- **Status publisher in the host.** Add a LIFX status publisher, in `controllers/lifx` beside the controller and started by the local controller host the way the host starts the Tidbyt runner. It reads the hub's `/api/monitor/v1/sessions` with the Tidbyt runner's cadence (every 30 s and on each change notice) using the same read-only hub credential pattern. `HubStatusFeed` and the per-session state ranking live in `controllers/tidbyt/src/runner.ts` and `status.ts` today; share them from one place both consumers use rather than copying them, so the Tidbyt and the bulb never disagree about a session's state.
- **One absolute write per paint.** A paint is one zero-duration `LightSetColor` with the full HSBK, through the bulb's existing queue and request namespace, shown in `lighting.pending` like a color command. It does not use the public read-modify-write color and brightness commands, which would take two transitions per paint.
- **Modes in the controller.** `LifxController` advertises `modes` with `Work`, `Quiet` and `Free` for qualified bulbs, accepts `mode.set`, reports the desired mode in the snapshot and reads the persisted mode at start. Unqualified bulbs such as the Beam advertise no modes and are never painted.
- **Host configuration.** A per-bulb `status` block with the brightness cap and quiet cap, plus the hub URL, owner ID and read-only token for the feed, in the existing private host JSON.
- **B.U.N.N.Y.** The LIFX page shows the mode control for these three modes (today `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx` allows modes only for Nanoleaf and Pixoo). In Work and Quiet the color and temperature controls are disabled with the ADR 0005 reason and a one-click Switch to Free, as the Nanoleaf page does for scenes. Power and brightness stay mode-independent.
- **Docs and specs.** Record the decisions in `controllers/lifx/README.md`, the configuration in `apps/local-controllers/README.md`, and the story's OpenSpec change. The existing `test:lifx`, `test:local-controllers` and dashboard checks cover the new tests; add commands to `docs/development.md` only if a new package script is needed.

Required issues: none open. #18, #3 and divoom-app-upgrade#31 are closed; #289 and #330 are delivered and installed.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- One writer per bulb: the host and its lease. The hub routes; it never writes to a bulb directly. No second lifecycle reducer: the publisher reads the shared owner's snapshot, never acknowledges notices and never infers a state the owner did not report.
- Missing or stale evidence never means done, read or connected. An unavailable feed never paints idle.
- The controller's bounded queue, retries, cancellation and shutdown. Cancelling never claims to undo a physical write.
- Manual control: painting never changes power, nothing restores automatically, and an unchanged feed never repaints.
- The #330 on-demand reads and their limits. Painting adds no polling and never reads the Beam.
- Only a color reaches the bulb. That is a display limit, not a privacy rule.
- ADR 0005 and ADR 0006 semantics: Work and Quiet are status presentation, Free is content, and the painted state is the base presentation a later #337 moment returns to.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
Delivery target: source-only. Fake feed and fake transport tests, no bulb traffic.

- [ ] **Mapping.** A fake feed with sessions in each state paints the expected HSBK at the cap; several sessions paint the highest-priority state; no outstanding session paints warm white; Quiet paints attention at the quiet cap and nothing else.
- [ ] **Transitions only.** The same snapshot repeated, a heartbeat and a read with new evidence but the same state send no write. A different HSBK reported by the fake transport, standing in for an app change, survives them and is repainted only at the next transition.
- [ ] **Stale input.** An unavailable feed and an uncertain session send no write and leave the last appearance. Recovery paints only if the state differs from the last painted state.
- [ ] **Offline bulb.** With two fake bulbs, one that times out does not stop the other. The failed paint is not replayed; the next transition paints both.
- [ ] **Modes.** `mode.set` receipts for the three modes; Free stops painting and leaves the bulb; returning to Work paints the current state once; the mode survives a host restart through the state directory; a bulb with no recorded mode starts in Free.
- [ ] **Stop.** Closing the host with paints queued cancels them, sends nothing more and leaves the bulb; a write already in flight completes and its receipt says so.
- [ ] **B.U.N.N.Y.** The LIFX page shows the mode control; color and temperature are disabled in Work and Quiet with the reason and Switch to Free, and enabled in Free. This is a UI change outside the work guide, so it needs the owner's explicit approval of the candidate under the docs/sdlc.md UI approval scope.
- [ ] **Checks.** `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:lifx`, `npm run test:local-controllers`, the dashboard checks, the contract checks and the workflow checks exit zero from the worktree root on Node 24. The OpenSpec change is synchronized and archived on the delivery branch.

Installed visual acceptance, including the real app change, unplugging a bulb and stopping the host, belongs to #22.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
- **Outside-change detection and hint:** #362. Consequence: B.U.N.N.Y. keeps reporting external control as unknown; the manual-change policy needs no detection because painting happens only on transitions.
- **Beam:** #319 for control and #327 for the per-session zone strip. Consequence: the Beam stays untouched by status.
- **Shared and provider colors:** #267 and #373. Consequence: fixed default colors until then.
- **Moments on LIFX:** #337, which returns to the base this story paints.
- **LIFX in the desk presets:** an extension of #67 after this story.
- **A brightness or power override that lasts until the next mode command, as on Nanoleaf:** not adopted. The next transition repaints brightness at the cap. Revisit if #22 finds this surprising.
- **Every-client compatibility and long-running reliability:** not claimed. A repeatable observed defect gets a focused follow-up.

issues.title: Pin the layout-read spacing constant and cover the remaining rebinding-guard forms
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The final review of #196 ([PR #203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/203)) passed both axes with P3 observations only. These are the test-hardening follow-ups it deferred. None of them affects the demo, the map or the installed runtime; they tighten tests that guard the verification runner.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Pin the layout-read spacing constant.** `LAYOUT_READS.apartMs` is 9000 in `scripts/verify/steps.mjs`, but any value from 3001 to 9500 passes `tests/verify_checks.mjs`. Add boundary cases for an 8999 ms gap that fails and a 9000 ms gap that passes. Drop or relabel the repeated four-reads case.
- **Cover the untested guard branches.** In `tests/test_module_dependencies.py`, no mutation exercises a direct `delattr(...)`, a rebound `delattr` or a walrus alias. Removing any of those rules still passes the suite. Add a permanent failing case for each.
- **Ordinary alias and root spellings the guard still misses.** Each of these returned `[]` from `rebinding_problems` when inserted into `scripts/demo.py`:
  - `m, _ = wall_server, None`, then `m.x = None` (tuple alias)
  - `for m in (wall_server,): m.x = None` (loop alias)
  - `import importlib as il`, then `il.import_module('wall_server').x = None`
  - `from importlib import import_module as im`, then `im('wall_server').x = None`
  - `sys.modules.get('wall_server').x = None`
  - `getattr(wall_server, 'App').state = None`
  - `(m := wall_server).x = None` (walrus as the target's base)
  - `wall_server.TABLE['k'] = 1` (item store under a module)

  Either cover the ones judged ordinary code, or narrow the docstring so it no longer claims more than the guard checks.
- **Wording.** The guard's docstring and the archived gh-196 proposal say `setattr` and `delattr` "may only be called by name". The code rejects every `delattr` call, which is the stricter rule. Correct the docstring; the archived proposal is history.

## Behavior to preserve

- `scripts/demo.py` passes the guard, including its single `setattr` loop over `UNAUDITED`.
- The existing mutations, from #195 rounds 2 and 3 and from #196, keep failing.
- The bounded-read rule: at most three reads, endpoint `''`, recorded at least 9 s apart.

## Observable acceptance

- A test fails when `apartMs` is set to 8999 or 9001.
- Each added mutation fails the guard, and removing the rule it exercises makes the test fail.

## Deferrals

- A static AST check cannot be complete. Parameter aliases (`def f(m): m.x = None` then `f(wall_server)`), `with nullcontext(wall_server) as m`, `exec` and computed names stay out of scope.
- Known limitation, accepted in #196: the alias analysis is flow-insensitive. A local name assigned from a module anywhere in the file is treated as a module in every scope, so a harmless refactor can trip the guard. It fails loudly, never silently. Revisit if it blocks a real change to `demo.py`.

issues.title: Move the Nanoleaf installation to the Mac mini's Linux host
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-28 from the hub's Mac mini hosting plan ([agent-device-hub#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/44)). Deferred until the owner has the Mac; it changes nothing in the current WSL installation or its development.

### Outcome and real setup

The Nanoleaf wall, controller and MCP services run in the Mac mini's OrbStack Ubuntu (ARM64) machine, with their device state and favorites preserved. Availability follows that always-on host instead of WSL. The physical check happens in the hub's cutover ([agent-device-hub#568](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/568)).

### Smallest useful implementation

- **An ADR superseding ADR 0011** ("runtime availability follows WSL") and the WSL-lifetime clause of ADR 0007 and the `linux-runtime` spec. The installation is still Linux with user systemd units, so everything else in ADR 0007 and ADR 0012 stands.
- **A documented move of a stopped installation to another Linux host,** consistent with the state rules: no whole-database restore over a live installation, and no fresh setup. It also regenerates units and paths.
- **Checks on ARM64:**
  - `install_linux.py`, its filesystem check and the Node 24 and Python 3.12 requirements;
  - the `rpds-py` wheel;
  - the B.U.N.N.Y. link on the wall map, which works through macOS `localhost` and the PC tunnel.
- **Coordinate with the hub:** the hub runtime currently lives inside `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf`.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device.
- SQLite stays on the machine's own disk.
- The shared-input selection and favorites are preserved.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- The ADR and move procedure merge with this repository's checks.
- A dry run of the move against a copy on the Mac starts all three services with the preserved state, before the hub cutover.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **A macOS-native (launchd) installation:** not needed while the host runs Linux.

**Readiness:** deferred until the hardware arrives and hub #44's ADR is merged.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-28, from the current issue body, comments and native prerequisites; the owning repository's single-operator scope and delivery boundaries apply. No scope cuts or readiness promotion are proposed.

- **Complexity: medium.** The stopped-installation procedure crosses the installer, user units, SQLite state and Hub-owned runtime paths.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** ARM64 package support, filesystem behavior and the eventual host remain to be checked by the defined rehearsal.
- **Impact: high.** A bad migration procedure can lose private device state or favorites or create competing writers; recovery must be demonstrated against a copy.
- **Readiness:** Deferred until the hardware arrives and Hub #44's ADR is merged, exactly as the issue states; this recommendation does not authorize the move.
- **Planned evidence:** Review the superseding ADR and stopped-installation procedure, run installer/filesystem/native-package checks on ARM64, and rehearse all three services against copied state with favorites and shared-input selection preserved. Hub #568 owns the physical cutover. Existing repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI remain required; these checks have not been run for this story.
- **Reassess when:** the stated prerequisite, acceptance boundary or isolated verification assumptions change.

issues.title: Finish owned local branch and worktree cleanup with a verified outcome
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A completed delivery removes its eligible owned local branch, worktree and scratch resources, or records why each is retained and who acts next. This applies to ordinary authorized delivery as well as explicit deliver-work.

The existing [cleanup policy](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/30f1e2e77d5467178e5100e8112cdeb2426b84ea/docs/sdlc.md#cleanup-after-delivery), delivered through [#82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/82), already protects exact PR heads, ignored evidence, other owners and tool-managed worktrees. It still prohibits manual delivery-branch deletion and does not consistently require a visible cleanup result.

Owner decision, 2026-09-26: routine delivery may remove its own verified local branch automatically after the cleanup gates pass. Existing accumulated branches require a separately approved candidate list. This issue defines the future rule; planning it does not authorize deleting anything now.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Keep the procedure in docs/sdlc.md. Add only a short completion requirement and conditional pointer in AGENTS.md, using writing-for-agents.
- Separate remote and local branch lifecycle. [Hub #309](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/309) owns GitHub automatic deletion and the old remote-branch prune. A missing remote branch does not prove local cleanup or authorize deleting local work.
- After the repository's existing merge, merged-main CI (or applicable documented exception), issue readback and evidence gates, remove the delivery's eligible owned worktree through its designated lifecycle. Remove its local branch only when it still points exactly at the reviewed merged PR head, no worktree or session uses it, and no remaining consumer needs it.
- Establish squash-merge delivery from the merged PR and exact reviewed head, not commit ancestry or git branch --merged. A moved tip is unfinished/unknown work and must be retained.
- Recheck branch identity, expected tip and worktree/ownership state immediately before removal. Use an exact-ref expected-head guard for branch removal; never perform a broad forced branch sweep. Any refusal or changed state retains the resource and records the next action.
- Account for owned scratch, independent temporary clones, review copies and staging directories, including locations outside the registry. Preserve required ignored/private evidence in a surviving private location before cleanup.
- Require a concise cleanup result in existing delivery evidence: removed with readback, retained with reason and owner/next action, or not applicable. A tool exit flow that this session cannot run is retained, not completed.

Required inputs: none; the accepted local-branch policy is specified here. Coordinate shared docs/sdlc.md edits with Hub #309 and sibling cleanup-policy deliveries. The shared-skill checkpoint [agent-skills#83](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/83) and global storage updates [dotfiles#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/dotfiles/issues/4) are related improvements, not required inputs: this repository must enforce its own completion rule without invoking a skill. Remote deletion need not be enabled to verify and clean an eligible local branch.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep other sessions' branches, worktrees and installations untouched. Never force worktree removal, reset, clean or discard files to make cleanup pass. Unknown ownership, locks, dirty state, unreviewed commits, unavailable CI, needed ignored files and active consumers all retain the affected resources. A lack of visible processes is not proof that a session has released a worktree. Failed/abandoned work and the historical backlog keep their separate owner-decision boundary. Source delivery does not install hooks, change live state or contact devices.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: reviewed documentation/instruction PR merged to this repository's main, with required local checks, hosted CI and issue readback. No product behavior delta or invented OpenSpec capability.

1. A completed ordinary delivery and an explicitly invoked deliver-work both produce a cleanup outcome. An eligible squash-merged local branch is removed only after its worktree is gone and the exact-head/ownership checks pass.
2. Read-only simulations cover a moved branch tip, another registered worktree, an active/unknown session, ignored evidence, lock/dirty state, incomplete CI and a remaining installation/publication consumer. Each retains the resource and names the next action.
3. A clean tool-managed worktree uses its exit flow; unavailable flow is reported pending. A standalone clone is discovered through task ownership rather than the Git worktree registry.
4. Source/CI completion and cleanup outcome remain distinct; no claim of removed resources without a current readback. Public receipts do not expose private paths, configurations or runtime metadata.
5. With Node 24, run npm ci, npm run check:workflow and npm run test:workflow from the isolated delivery root; both checks must exit zero and report the actual specification inventory. Preserve all applicable current-head and merged-main CI and independent Standards/Specification reviews. Use this repository's current validation and merge procedure.

## Meaningful deferrals

No retroactive artifact deletion, GitHub setting changes, scheduled cleanup, evidence expiry, runtime/cache cleanup or installation. The existing remote-branch backlog remains Hub #309; a separate approved local-maintenance issue handles old local artifacts. Manual retention with a named next action is the fallback when safe cleanup cannot be established.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26, against codex-nanoleaf main 30f1e2e and the owner's accepted local-branch policy. Complexity: medium, because Git refs, worktree lifecycles, evidence and consumers interact. Uncertainty: low; the decision and existing retention gates are explicit. Impact: high, because incorrect removal can lose unmerged or private work. Readiness: ready. Shared-file coordination is not a required-input dependency. Reassess on policy/head changes, tool-lifecycle differences, or new cleanup consumers. Planning-session reasoning: unknown.

issues.title: Check a saved animation against the current Lines layout before playing it
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 during the animation-bundle archive sweep. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

From Codex, the owner can ask whether a saved favorite still fits the current Lines layout and see a concise explanation before requesting playback. The check changes no mode, favorite, queue or lights and does not claim physical success.

Observation: #154 freezes recipes across database reopen and source upgrades, but ADR 0017 explicitly allows a later layout to make a saved recipe exceed current encoder bounds. Today the owner learns that when play is rejected. #151 and #153 already provide deterministic bounded encoding. A read-only check can reuse it.

### Smallest useful implementation

Not yet defined. Starting point: resolve one named favorite through the existing owner and run the same pure encoder/validation against the saved current layout, reporting a bounded summary or the existing typed reason for rejection. Settle whether this fits an existing options tool or needs a new tool before coding; the complete catalog is already 493,877 bytes against its 524,288-byte regression budget at `da5f9d3`.

This is distinct from #156's animated wall-map preview: no rendered browser playback or frame export is proposed. It does not replace play-time validation.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Private favorite data stays behind the existing authenticated boundary and out of browser/Hub snapshots. Use the same recipe resolution and encoder; no parallel validation policy, ticket allocation, device request, mode switch or second writer. A successful check describes one layout revision and can become stale before play.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Not yet defined. Delivery target: source-only first. Candidate evidence: a valid recipe, a favorite made too large by a layout change, zero state/queue/device writes, truthful stale-result behavior, and unchanged final playback admission. Resolve the returned summary and revision semantics during planning.

### Meaningful deferrals

Later idea. The work guide's Direction favors fixed desk presets (H67), boot availability (H356), and visible wall hold/completion fixes first. This small assistant interaction extends existing animation control without promoting it ahead of those priorities. Graphical preview stays #156; exporting favorites is separate and has no current delivery request.

issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

P2 follow-up from the 2026-09-26 animation-bundle archive sweep. Put the source-delivered #174, #150, #151, #153 and #154 features on the owner's selected Linux installation, then separately verify real-client and visible Lines behavior. The source finish line is complete; this issue owns the installation and physical evidence that was explicitly excluded.

Baseline to include: `da5f9d3c8155b5a6ac25bc1f3e60f41fea2d2073` (PRs #182–#186). Device MCP 1.0.1 was published in jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#407 and adopted in #174. Live GitHub readback on 2026-09-26 confirms all source issues are closed and all five exact merged-revision jobs passed for each PR. This sweep did not inspect or change the running installation, so its current revision must be established at pickup.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. Obtain an explicit installation request and identify the installation owner. Read current instructions and coordinate with any active runtime owner. Read the actual installed revision first; if another authorized session already installed the bundle, verify it instead of reinstalling.
2. Select an exact approved committed revision containing the baseline, verify its applicable CI, and follow the existing guarded in-place upgrade procedure with backup and rollback receipts. Preserve the current private database; do not fresh-install over it. #140 owns an upgrade command and #162 owns procedure documentation; neither needs to be implemented merely to run an already supported manual upgrade.
3. Verify installed MCP discovery and typed receipts from an explicitly selected real client. Permanent Codex registration remains #159; reuse an approved existing or per-run attachment when suitable rather than silently editing personal settings.
4. Obtain a separate named Lines target/IP and permission for the precise playback/restoration sequence before physical commands. Record source, installed, client, transport and visible results separately.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one writer per device, Free-only playback, existing Work/Quiet behavior, task state, reservations, credentials, remembered scenes and brightness policy. Do not alter Panels output. Favorite saves are create-only; rename rejects occupied names atomically; supplied recipes and defaults are frozen. Preserve existing favorites through upgrade/restart. Do not restore an old database over newer favorites as an automatic rollback step; follow ADR 0017.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: authorized installation plus separately authorized client and physical acceptance; no new source feature.

- Record installed revision, selected source revision, backup/rollback location privately, service and worker readiness, and the Device MCP archive checksum. Do not publish private state or credentials.
- Real client discovers the expected tools; supplied-field and preset saves send no light command, collisions preserve both records, and a chosen favorite survives restart and replays with the same recipe. Preserve original request identities for receipt lookup/replay.
- With explicit target permission, observe clockwise and counterclockwise waves, the faster setting, representative named moods and favorite replay. Record the owner's palette assessment separately from transport receipts; select the exact sequence with the owner before it runs.
- Play an animation and invoke `nanoleaf_scene_restore`; observe the remembered scene return. Confirm Work/Quiet and missing-target failures remain typed without unintended light commands. This is scene restoration, not a new brightness-restoration promise.
- Record persistence, restoration, unchanged unrelated device state, and any discrepancies. File a source bug if a reproducible mismatch appears; do not broaden this installation task silently.

### Meaningful deferrals

Permanent registration: #159. Flash-rate cap remains optional under the owner decision in #149. Panels animations: #157. Saved firmware scenes: #155. Source tests and loopback receipts do not establish physical output.

Readiness: backlog until the owner selects the installation, owner, real client and authorized physical target/sequence. Filing this issue grants none of those permissions.

issues.title: Play hub moments as interludes on the Lines, then restore the current presentation
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A hub moment briefly plays on the Lines as an *interlude*, then returns to what is showing now: Work status, the remembered scene, or the Free content. This covers both "play this for 30 seconds, then restore" and event moments such as a merged PR.

This is the Nanoleaf side of the hub-decides/devices-guarantee plan in jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#291. It was reshaped on 2026-09-25 from "Play an animation for a set time, then restore".

## Smallest useful implementation

- Implement the `moment` command from the shared contract release, jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#292. Resolve its mood and palette to a Lines preset (#153), or render the palette with the requested pattern.
- The Lines worker saves the current base presentation, plays at most one interlude, and restores the current base when it ends.
- Any explicit command, a red or yellow alert, or a mode change ends the interlude early.
- Skip interludes in Quiet.
- Stopping and restoring the scene reuses #150's path.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer.
- Alerts always win.
- Completed comets are never restarted, and task pulse epochs are kept.
- No restore of a stale snapshot, and no replay after a restart.
- The remembered scene and brightness are unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Fake-clock tests cover:
- interlude then restore, in Work and in Free;
- pre-emption by an alert;
- a mode change mid-interlude;

issues.title: Save a requested animation as a Nanoleaf scene
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

An animation the owner likes can be saved on the Lines as a real Nanoleaf scene, so it appears in the Nanoleaf app and can be selected from a phone.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Use the Nanoleaf effect write commands to add, update and delete saved scenes. `add` stores the encoded display effect under a chosen name.
- This changes a standing rule in the bridge guide: no saved Nanoleaf scenes are added, edited or deleted.
- The owner authorized this on 2026-09-25 (see Decision below). Record the policy change in an ADR and in the bridge guide. Settle in the design: naming, collision handling, and how discovery then advertises the new scene.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Editing or deleting a scene happens only on an explicit request that names that scene. There is no bulk or implied deletion, and the remembered scene is never changed as a side effect.
- The remembered-scene policy.
- The single writer.
- Scene IDs stay opaque in shared v1.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- A fake-device test of the `add` payload.
- A collision refusal test.
- Discovery picks up the new scene.
- A live check that it shows in the Nanoleaf app, when requested.

## Meaningful deferrals

- None beyond the design questions above.


## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, from #92's delivery and the live session. Source-only delivery unless stated.

- **Complexity: medium.**
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The policy is decided. The firmware behavior of `add`, update and delete for custom effects is unverified; the first delivery step is a bounded live qualification, which needs the owner's go-ahead for device writes at that time.
- **Impact: high.** It writes persistent data on the device that the user also manages.
- **Readiness:** backlog. It is ready to plan once a qualification step is scheduled.

## Decision (owner, 2026-09-25)

The bridge may add, edit and delete scenes on the owner's Nanoleaf device. This replaces the bridge guide's rule that no saved scenes are added, edited or deleted, for this capability.

Follows #92 and complements #146.

**Missing:** A separately authorized firmware qualification plan and its add/update/delete evidence, followed by accepted scene naming, collision and discovery rules.

**Why:** The owner approved the capability in principle, but the story still names unverified persistent firmware operations and unresolved design choices. Policy approval is not permission for a device-writing qualification sequence.

issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A light runs from Line to Line along the physical connections of the owner's Lines wall, following the shape instead of an axis or the center.

## Smallest useful implementation

- The layout and device state specs.
- Free-only gating and the encoder bounds.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Topology fixture tests on the 15-Line layout, including a branching point.

- Bounds tests.

issues.title: Cap how fast animations can flash
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Requested animations on the Lines never flash faster than a safe rate unless the owner opts in. It is a photosensitivity safeguard that must be in place before faster speeds or new patterns land (see #151).

Measured on 2026-09-25 against the 15-Line fixture at `fast`, the worst per-Line brightness peak rate today is `pulse` at 2.0 per second. `wave` with 8 colors reaches 1.7 and everything else stays below 1. All of these are under the common 3-flashes-per-second guideline (WCAG 2.3.1), so this protects future speeds and patterns rather than fixing a current defect.

## Smallest useful implementation

- A shared check in `bridge/effects.py` that computes each Line's peak rate from the encoded frames and rejects an effect above the limit with `capacity` before queueing. This is the same admission point as the byte and frame bounds.
- A pure frame property that needs no device.
- The animation options route and `nanoleaf_animations_list` report the limit.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- All five current patterns, at every speed, stay allowed.
- Status animations, comets and alerts are not subject to this check.
- The frame and byte bounds and the Free-only gate stay as they are.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Tests compute peak rates for every pattern, speed and color count on the fixtures, and assert that none exceeds the limit.
- A synthetic too-fast frame list is rejected before queueing and consumes no ticket.
- The options route reports the limit.

## Meaningful deferrals

- An owner opt-in to exceed the limit is deferred until someone asks for it. The manual alternative is none, by design.


## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, from #92's delivery and the live session. Source-only delivery unless stated.

- **Complexity: low.** One pure function and a limit field.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The threshold and how "flash" is measured (luminance delta, area) need an owner decision. Default proposal: at most 3 peaks per second per Line, with at least a 2:1 luminance change.
- **Impact: medium.** It is a safety property on a physical device.
- **Readiness:** deferred. The owner decision below removes the need for a cap on this installation.

## Decision (owner, 2026-09-25)

The owner is not sensitive to flashing and asked to be lax here. No flash-rate cap is enforced on this installation. The device's one-decisecond frame resolution already bounds any pattern at about 5 flashes per second, and the frame and byte bounds still apply. This story stays as an optional guard. Revisit it if someone who may be sensitive shares the room, or if the wall becomes visible to others (for example a stream or a shared space). It no longer blocks #151.

Follows #92 and complements #146.

**Note:** Cap how fast requested animations can flash.

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** An owner decision to activate this optional guard, followed by an accepted threshold and definition of a flash, and updated fixture expectations for the delivered faster speed.

**Why:** The explicit owner decision leaves the cap deferred and removes its prerequisite on #151. This assessment does not reverse that decision or treat the old safeguard wording as current readiness.
**Reassess when:** The owner records the missing decision or evidence and the remaining acceptance is defined; preserve existing scope and authorization gates.

outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text:
Requested animations on the Lines never flash faster than a safe rate unless the owner opts in. It is a photosensitivity safeguard that must be in place before faster speeds or new patterns land (see #151).

Measured on 2026-09-25 against the 15-Line fixture at `fast`, the worst per-Line brightness peak rate today is `pulse` at 2.0 per second. `wave` with 8 colors reaches 1.7 and everything else stays below 1. All of these are under the common 3-flashes-per-second guideline (WCAG 2.3.1), so this protects future speeds and patterns rather than fixing a current defect.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- A shared check in `bridge/effects.py` that computes each Line's peak rate from the encoded frames and rejects an effect above the limit with `capacity` before queueing. This is the same admission point as the byte and frame bounds.
- A pure frame property that needs no device.
- The animation options route and `nanoleaf_animations_list` report the limit.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
- All five current patterns, at every speed, stay allowed.
- Status animations, comets and alerts are not subject to this check.
- The frame and byte bounds and the Free-only gate stay as they are.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
- Tests compute peak rates for every pattern, speed and color count on the fixtures, and assert that none exceeds the limit.
- A synthetic too-fast frame list is rejected before queueing and consumes no ticket.
- The options route reports the limit.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text: - An owner opt-in to exceed the limit is deferred until someone asks for it. The manual alternative is none, by design.

issues.title: Play custom animations for different events
issues.body:
## Outcome

Different events play their own animation on the Lines. For example, a green sweep when CI passes, a red ripple when it fails, or a slow sunrise in the morning. The user picks which events get an animation and what it looks like.

Placeholder for future refinement. Set scope, dependencies and acceptance criteria before implementation.

## Starting point

#92 delivered `animation.play`. It has five patterns: `wave`, `gradient`, `pulse`, `breathe` and `sparkle`. Each takes 1 to 8 colors, a speed (`slow`, `medium` or `fast`), a direction (`left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, `outward` or `inward`) and a loop or play-once choice. Animations play only in Free and stay until something replaces them. The suggestions below reuse those patterns unless marked *new*.

### Suggested events and animations

| Event | Suggested animation | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI passed on a PR | `gradient` up, green → teal, `medium`, once | Development workflow |
| CI failed | `wave` outward, red → orange, `fast`, once | Must not hide a real blocked task |
| PR merged | `sparkle`, blue, green and gold, `medium`, once | |
| Review requested or changes requested | `pulse`, purple, `medium`, a few cycles | |
| Installation or deploy finished | `wave` outward, teal → white, `medium`, once | |
| Start of day | `gradient` up, deep orange → pink → warm yellow, `slow` | Scheduled |
| Focus timer ended | `breathe`, soft green, `slow`, a few cycles | Scheduled |
| Meeting in five minutes | `pulse`, amber, `medium` | Needs a calendar source |
| End of work day | `wave` inward, warm amber → dim red, `slow`, then Free or Quiet | Scheduled |
| Device, controller or MCP error | `breathe`, dim red, `slow` | Local health events |
| Codex task completed | Covered by #19 (celebration presets) | Link, don't duplicate |
| Codex needs approval or is blocked | Covered by #20 (per-status presets) | Link, don't duplicate |

Pattern ideas that would help, each needing its own design:
- *New* `spin`: a sweep that rotates around the wall's center. The current layout surrounds its center, so this would suit it.
- *New* `chase`: a light that runs along physically connected Lines.
- *New* speed: one step faster than `fast`.

All of these must stay within the envelope #92 qualified, 20 frames per zone and 8,192 bytes, unless a live probe raises it.

## Open questions

- **Over Work status.** An animation that plays over Work status needs its own hub ADR 0005 decision, including how and when status resumes. Free-only events avoid that decision. hub [#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45) records the same open question.
- **Rules.** Where do event-to-animation rules live and run without a conversation? hub #45 owns approved automation rules; this issue could own the Nanoleaf presets those rules call.
- **Restoring.** After a play-once animation, return to the scene or status that was showing before it, not to a stale snapshot. Loops need an explicit stop.
- **Precedence.** Red and yellow alerts, completed comets and unread state must never be erased or restarted. Decide what happens when two events collide, and how duplicates are rate-limited.
- **Event sources.** GitHub events need polling or a webhook. Remote ingress is deferred by hub ADR 0004. Calendar and timer sources are undecided.
- **Preferences.** Where per-event choices are stored, how they're previewed, and whether the wall map needs UI for them (a UI change needs human approval).

## Related

- #92: the typed animation command and MCP tools this builds on.
- #19 and #20: completion and per-status presets, which cover the task-lifecycle events.
- hub [#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45): approved alert and device automation rules.
- hub [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md): Free-only content and no automatic restore.

## Guide

**Topic:** nanoleaf-presentation
**Highlight:** idea, Per-event animations such as CI passed, PR merged and start of day.
**Extends:** N92

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The remaining Nanoleaf-owned outcome and acceptance after the comment moved event rules to Hub #45 and split presets, interludes and external-control work into #153, #158 and #161.

**Why:** The body remains a placeholder with obsolete open questions; the settled hub ownership and delivered animation bundle do not define a separate implementation for this parent idea.
**Reassess when:** The owner records the missing decision or evidence and the remaining acceptance is defined; preserve existing scope and authorization gates.
