issues.body:
> Scope narrowed on 2026-09-24. [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/139) now owns the configurable base and status palette: the color choices, defaults, persistence, reset, validation, status-based priority, physical output, Project halves and the current map's artwork and legend. This issue keeps only the part that depends on the live renderer from #17. The original scope is in this issue's edit history.

## Shared-hub ownership

Use shared semantic identifiers from [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2) with an explicit mapping for current working/question/blocked/unread behavior. Palettes and brightness stay device presentation preferences. Priority cannot derive from RGB; clients consume effective colors.

## Desired outcome

Once #17 draws the wall from the worker's sent frames, every color the regular app shows agrees with the palette the worker is using, including while a palette change is still being applied.

## Scope

After #17, the map has two color sources: the worker's sent frames from #15 and the effective palette from #139, which colors the legend and task status markers. Make them agree, and show a palette change as pending until the worker has sent frames with it. Palette editing, storage, defaults and physical output stay with #139. On-screen previews belong to #19 and #20, which take their colors from #139. Exposing the palette to the CLI, controller API, MCP or integration settings API stays deferred under #139's revisit trigger.

If #17's delivery already meets these criteria, close this issue with that evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: With a custom palette, the live view's Line colors match the worker's sent frames, and the legend and task status markers use the same effective palette.
- AC2: After a palette change, the live view keeps the previously sent colors and marks the change pending until the worker sends frames with the new palette. A failed send shows as failed, not as the requested colors.
- AC3: The browser keeps no fixed status-color table. Wherever #17's renderer draws a status color that does not come from a frame, it reads the effective palette from #139.
- AC4: Viewing the live wall and changing the palette do not restart status epochs, replay waves or completions, change task/Line assignments or mark tasks read. Work, Quiet and Free behavior and saved scenes are unchanged.

## Verification approach

Browser tests with a custom palette cover a pending palette change, a failed send, the legend and task status markers. Compare live-view colors with frame colors from the fake worker. Record software evidence separately from physical observations.

issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Keep the reusable Nanoleaf visual renderer here. Future hub previews may consume this timeline after parity verification; [agent-device-hub#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6)'s overview does not depend on it. Do not add a device writer or status interpreter.

## Desired outcome

Make the regular app's wall visualization track bridge-controlled physical lights in real time, including animation rather than only one-second status-color updates.

## Scope

Consume #15's rendering contract in a reusable visual renderer for the current map. Match task pulses and waves, per-project halves, completion effects, Locate, and physical previews. Make the renderer reusable by the inspection-only wallpaper and future ambient view without requiring either deliverable to finish first.

Keep on-screen effect demonstrations visibly separate from the live wall visualization. External Nanoleaf scenes are a separate investigation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: For bridge-controlled output, the correct physical zones show the same encoded colors, relative brightness, frame transitions, looping, and timing as the worker output. Project/status halves and physical Line numbering remain correct after rotation and flips.
- AC2: Verify a maximum visual phase difference of 250 ms in the agreed visible-app acceptance scenarios on the user's PC. Record actual measurements and the measurement method. This measures UI-versus-wall alignment, not the separate delay before a task-status event reaches the worker. A failure to meet the target remains an acceptance gap unless the user explicitly revises it.
- AC3: Rendering follows successfully sent output and exposes pending, failed/uncertain, stale, and externally controlled states. Do not present requested-but-unsent settings or arbitrary scene guesses as current physical output.

- AC5: Selecting Lines/tasks and observing the live view do not mutate task state, mark tasks read, start animations, or send light writes. Existing editing actions remain explicit in the regular map; the wallpaper remains inspection-only.

- AC7: Physical comparison covers Work and Quiet, overlapping blocked/question alerts, split halves, an existing completion comet, and Locate. Extend frame-parity and device scenarios when the linked new palettes and effects become available. Free and idle external scenes display their known control state without claiming unverified per-zone mirroring.
- AC8: Preserve keyboard focus and selection during updates, and record CPU/GPU/memory behavior while visible and paused. No second animation scheduler or light writer is introduced.

Use deterministic frame/timing browser scenarios against #15, including failed/partial sends and restart/no-replay cases. issues.title: Pause a paired verification feed while the Hub owner resets
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Hub's composed disposable preview must reset its one synthetic state owner while consumer pages remain responsive. Hub #557 cannot safely reseed the owner while this consumer is still polling. This source-only prerequisite supplies the consumer-owned pause boundary required by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/557. It preserves the repository split required by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/490.

## Smallest useful implementation

Add a private, per-run feed-pause control only to the `hub-paired` verification launch. The composition writes a bounded versioned request with run identity and a fresh nonce in the run's existing private runtime directory. The running consumer stops admitting Hub requests, drains those already in flight, then writes an atomic mode-0600 acknowledgment with the same run/nonce and its process identity. The pages, health route and controller remain responsive.

The request stays active while Hub reseeds its owner. Only after that succeeds, the composition authorizes this consumer's reseed with the matching nonce. The adapter consumes that authorization in seed after the old unit has stopped and fresh state has been written, before the replacement launches. Its fresh source can then poll the reset owner and pass readiness. An unrelated reseed must not silently release an outstanding pause. Missing, stale or malformed control state produces a fixed actionable failure rather than an acknowledgment.

The protocol is verification-only: no new public controller or shared core API, installed setting, service or agent-state owner. Hub owns orchestration, validation of process identity, partial failure reporting, manifest pin updates and complete aggregate qualification in #557. These files are private controls, never captured proof or browser output.


Implementation seam: the paired demo worker serializes `Poller.tick`; pause before its next feed pass, acknowledge only after the previous pass drains, and keep its map/controller servers and local worker operations available. Update `scripts/demo.py`, the verification plug-in, focused tests and the owning verification guide/specification.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve the existing simulator/no-device boundary, credential confinement, one selected state owner, request identities, no automatic command replay, normal startup behavior, ports, token files and retained frozen proof. Timer-driven and read-triggered requests must obey the same pause boundary. Device/controller reads continue to answer. A paused browser read reports retained state with truthful freshness and never initiates a new Hub request. Stop remains available at every phase.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Hold a Hub read in flight: acknowledgment waits until it finishes; after acknowledgment, timer and browser/controller activity issue no further Hub requests while pages remain responsive.
- Reject stale nonce/run/process acknowledgments and malformed or linked control files. The control directory is enabled only by an explicit disposable paired launch, never inherited into ordinary startup.
- Reseed after matching release authorization: old process stops before authorization is consumed, token files and ports persist, a fresh lower owner revision becomes current, and frozen proof bytes are unchanged. A reseed without release authorization fails closed.
- Removing an unused pause request resumes the still-running paired consumer without replaying commands. Partial failure remains stoppable.
- Run the repository's full applicable source/browser/workflow checks and focused real-user-systemd adapter qualification. Keep source, installed runtime and device acceptance separate. Delivery target: source-only PR, independent Standards/Specification reviews, all PR and merged-main CI.

## Meaningful deferrals

Aggregate reset and its complete real-consumer evidence remain Hub #557, which will pin this merged revision. Installed pause controls, physical-device behavior and a general distributed coordination service are outside this disposable-preview requirement. Existing unrelated verification follow-ups retain their own scope.

## Work assessment

One operator on the existing Linux/WSL verification host, with disposable state and synthetic transport. Complexity medium; uncertainty medium until drain and reseed negative controls pass; impact medium because incorrect timing can leave the preview stale. The required interface is a bounded prerequisite of the already accepted aggregate reset, with no change to its consumers-stay-up criterion.

issues.title: Widen the wall verification read-spacing margin and harden the rebinding guard
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The wall verification adapter from [#193](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/193) (PR #195) left two small follow-ups from its final reviews. Neither affects the current demo.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Layout-read spacing margin (review P-S8):** `scripts/verify/steps.mjs` requires tolerated layout reads to be at least 9.9 s apart, which leaves about 100 ms of slack against the map's 10 s cadence (measured gaps: 10003-10010 ms). A read recorded more than about 100 ms late would make a correct map fail `device-read-refused`, and would make `doctor` report `device-boundary: failed` on a long-lived `layout-unavailable` preview. That is a false failure, never a false pass. Widen `apartMs` to about 9 s, or record a monotonic time in each boundary entry, and update the spec and guide.
- **Rebinding guard coverage (review S8):** `tests/test_module_dependencies.py` `rebinding_problems` misses some ordinary spellings:
  - `importlib.import_module(...)` and `sys.modules[...]` roots;
  - a module aliased to a local name;
  - class attributes reached through a module, such as `wall_server.App.state = ...`;
  - `setattr` bound to another name or reached through `getattr`.

  Resolve each assignment target's attribute chain to its root, flag rebinding of `setattr`, and add the class-attribute and `import_module` forms as permanent failing cases.

## Behavior to preserve

- The existing boundary.
- The bounded-read rule (at most 3 reads, endpoint `''`).
- The single allowed `setattr` loop over `UNAUDITED`.

## Observable acceptance

- A read delayed by 500 ms still passes.
- The every-poll and no-limit maps still fail.
- Each new rebinding form fails the guard test.

## Deferrals

A static AST check cannot be complete. Deliberately obfuscated rebinding stays out of scope.

Observation from the same review, not part of this issue: `tests/line_identity_checks.cjs:152` ("Unchanged polling preserves badge focus") failed once locally and passed on rerun, with no related change.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-28, from the current issue body, comments and native prerequisites; the owning repository's single-operator scope and delivery boundaries apply. No scope cuts or readiness promotion are proposed.

- **Complexity: medium.** Timing tolerance and AST root/alias resolution cross the verification runner, dependency guard, specifications and tests.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The 500 ms delayed-read case and the forbidden rebinding forms define the required behavior; deliberately obfuscated code remains excluded.
- **Impact: medium.** A guard regression could admit prohibited rebinding or make bounded-read evidence misleading, even though product behavior does not change.
- **Readiness:** Remains backlog; implementation strategy does not change the issue status or its exclusions.
- **Planned evidence:** Delayed reads pass while every-poll/no-limit maps fail; each added alias, class-attribute and import-module form fails the guard and the single UNAUDITED exception remains accepted. Existing repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI remain required; these checks have not been run for this story.
- **Reassess when:** the stated prerequisite, acceptance boundary or isolated verification assumptions change.

issues.title: Add a hub-paired wall verification scenario for the integrated preview
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The integrated verification preview in [Hub #495](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/495) pairs one disposable wall run with one disposable Hub run. The wall must then act as a real Hub consumer: it serves the controller API the Hub calls and polls the Hub's shared session feed. Today's wall verification run from [#193](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/193) serves only the map page. Its device boundary refuses every socket connect, loopback included.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

Add a `hub-paired` scenario to the wall verification adapter:

- **Seed.** Register the Hub's controller credential from a run-supplied token file, and configure shared input with the paired Hub feed URL. The URL arrives as a non-secret run input through core `@jimmie-potts/app-verify` 1.1 `--input`, which is Hub #495's core change.
- **Serve.** Start the real `controller_server` listener in a thread, alongside the map page, and announce its endpoint through the core's `ReadyLine.endpoints`.
- **Worker stand-in.** Run the real shared-input `Poller` and integration processing once per second.
- **Boundary.** Allow `socket.connect` only to `127.0.0.1:<paired Hub port>`. That port comes from the run input and is refused if it is an installed port. Log each allowed connect as `allowed`. Every light request and every other target stays refused, and the `device-boundary` check still fails on any light request or any unexpected target.
- **Checks and steps.** Add a doctor check that the paired feed is current and its revision matches, plus one capture step.

Dependencies:

- Required: #193 merged, and app-verify 1.1 released under Hub #495.
- Hub #495 consumes this change.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- No light request ever leaves a run.
- One writer and one agent-state owner: the Hub is the only owner, and the wall consumes its feed.
- The standalone wall scenarios and their boundary proof are unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- In a paired run the Hub's controller calls reach the wall's real controller API.

## Outcome and real setup

An agent starts the real Nanoleaf wall using synthetic Lines/Panels layouts and tasks, exercises current presentation/configuration/animation states, captures proof and hands over a disposable preview without communicating with physical lights.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488

## Smallest useful implementation and dependencies

- Extend the existing `scripts/demo.py` and browser tooling behind the accepted interface. Reuse its actual wall server and no-device boundary; prove that all relevant transport paths remain simulated.
- Give each run its own state, port, identity and owned process lifetime. Support repeatable fixtures, capture, reset, handoff, extend, stop and expiry.
- Map current Lines/Panels task presentation, applicable configuration and animation states to reproducible browser actions and expected observations. Clearly identify which server/controller components are real or simulated.
- Retain screenshots/video and a source-labelled receipt in the main checkout's ignored evidence area. Keep runtime state in an approved private location.
- Design adapter seams needed by the combined preview; do not claim the wall demo alone proves the real shared-input/controller integration.

Required source prerequisites (native blocked-by links; independent investigation/preparation may proceed):

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/493

[Animation preview #156](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/156) remains a separate product capability. Coordinate retained previews with [cleanup #192](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/192); neither issue grants device-control permission.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Fresh documented runs cover Lines and Panels, task transitions, a representative configuration action and available animation states.
- [ ] Device-request traps or equivalent observable confinement fail on attempted physical requests; a pretty wall screenshot is insufficient proof of isolation.
- [ ] Two independent runs do not share state or reset one another. Failed starts and expired leases clean only owned resources.
- [ ] Screenshot and short interaction video are inspectable; a handoff is reproducible after expiry without modifying retained proof.
- [ ] A relevant known presentation/transition defect is detected by the scenario assertions, and reference behavior passes.
- [ ] Feature map, fixture and driver instructions are maintained with the affected behavior. Unsupported cases are explicitly identified.
- [ ] Current-candidate human approval is recorded for any changed product UI; actual Windows access is qualified under https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497.

## Assessment and next action

Complexity: medium; uncertainty: medium for demo versus full integration seams; impact: medium. Blocked for implementation on the accepted interface; independent source inspection is available. Coordinate with current wall retirement/direction before investing in new permanent wall UI.

Finish line: merged adapter and meaningful isolated/browser evidence. Follow current Nanoleaf AGENTS/SDLC with supported Python and Node versions; run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser` and affected consumer/workflow checks. Keep source delivery distinct from owner-host qualification and device acceptance.

## Meaningful deferrals

No light uploads, layout discovery from a physical target, legacy/shared-input cutover, runtime migration or new wall editor. Simulated wall output does not prove physical color or timing.

This is planned work, not completed verification. Issue creation authorizes no implementation or launch. During later authorized source delivery, follow the owning repository's current instructions, preserve unrelated work, obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, require applicable current-head CI, use the guarded merge procedure and verify merged-main checks before source closure. Required UI approval remains separate from optional hands-on use.

issues.title: Restore the shared-consumer measurement script to the current owners and feed contract
issues.body:
### Observed and expected behavior

`docs/shared-input.md` (Verification) documents `python3 scripts/measure-shared.py --output /tmp/shared-consumer.json`. It is supposed to measure 900 synthetic Linux shared-consumer operations across the 1-, 10- and 50-session profiles and write a receipt like `docs/performance/gh29-shared-consumer.json`. It fails before measuring anything.

- **Current main (`f3c1384`):** `AttributeError: module 'shared_input' has no attribute 'configure'` at `shared.configure(directory,b,config)`. Since #118, `configure`, `select_source` and `accept` live in `shared_source` and no longer take a bridge module. The script also calls `b.connect_state`, which is now `database.connect_state`.
- **Before #118 (`f003a39^`):** it already failed, with `shared_input.FeedError: feed-rejected`. The cause, inferred from the code: #116 (`7a030ac`) made the consumer request `/sessions?snapshotVersion=1.1`, but the script's fake host accepts only the exact path `/api/monitor/v1/sessions`. It also serves 1.0 snapshots without the per-session `generation` that the 1.1 contract requires.

CI does not run the script, so neither break was caught. The checked receipt in `docs/performance/gh29-shared-consumer.json` names source hashes from #62 and is otherwise unaffected.

### Reproduction

From a checkout of current main, with Node 24 on PATH:

```sh
python3 scripts/measure-shared.py --output /tmp/shared-consumer.json
```

It exits with the `AttributeError` above. To see the earlier failure, run the same command from `git archive f003a39^ bridge scripts tests/fixtures`; it ends in `FeedError: feed-rejected`. Neither run touches a device, Codex state or the installation.

### Scope

Bring `scripts/measure-shared.py` back in line with the current owners and feed contract:

- Call `shared_source.configure`, `select_source` and `accept` with their current signatures, and use `database.connect_state`.
- Make the fake loopback host serve the `snapshotVersion=1.1` request with valid 1.1 snapshots, including `generation`.
- Keep the measured work the same: loopback fetch, released validation, SQLite projection, allocation and pure effect construction. Keep the receipt schema and the stated limitations.

Out of scope:
- Refreshing or reinterpreting the committed #29 receipt, unless the owner asks for new measurements.
- Changing consumer behavior or performance.
- Hub #30 qualification.
- Adding the full measurement run to CI.

### Acceptance criteria

- AC1: On current main, `python3 scripts/measure-shared.py --output <file>` exits 0 and writes a receipt with the 1-, 10- and 50-session profiles. It uses isolated state, contacts no device and touches no Codex state.
- AC2: The script reaches shared operations only through their owning modules. It passes no bridge module, which keeps ADR 0016's rule for scripts as well as bridge modules.
- AC3: A fast regression check runs in `python3 scripts/check.py`, for example one profile with a small sample count. It fails if the script's calls or its fake host drift from the owners' signatures or the feed contract again.
- AC4: The command in `docs/shared-input.md` stays accurate. If the receipt is not refreshed, the doc says the committed receipt came from the #62 source hashes.

### Verification approach

Run the script end to end on current main and inspect the receipt shape. Add the reduced-sample check to the Python suite, and show it failing against the current script before the fix. Run `python3 scripts/check.py`. No device verification is needed.

### Dependencies

None. Found during #120 (PR #176); the breakage predates it.

### Delivery target

Source-only

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

issues.title: Expose element geometry read-only on the integration route for the Lines and Panels
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

The hub can draw the real shape of the Lines and the Panels without opening Nanoleaf state. The integration route exposes each registered device's element geometry read-only, and the hub passes it through the integration snapshot. Hub #286's second phase and the shared device art in hub ADR 0007 (B.U.N.N.Y. is the shell; the wall map is Nanoleaf's advanced editor) both need it. One operator, the installed Linux runtime, the Lines and the NL22 Panels.

### Smallest useful implementation

- Add a read-only geometry view to `nanoleaf.integration` for the requesting device: element ids in the existing order, each with its physical id, zone list and the positions and orientation the wall map already draws from (`layout.json` version 2 and `panel_geometry`, ADR 0009 and ADR 0010). No new state, no write.
- Keep the snapshot shape strict-compatible with the installed hub: publish geometry on a separate versioned route or a new extension minor with the hub's `validateIntegrationSnapshot` updated in the same delivery, as ADR 0014 did for animations.
- Dependencies: none. The Panels already answer as a controller device (#113).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device; this route reads only.
- No private paths, addresses or tokens in the payload; ids stay the existing opaque local ids.
- The wall map keeps drawing from its own files until it retires (hub ADR 0007).

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Fake-device tests: the Lines and the Panels each return their geometry, a device without a layout returns an explicit empty result, and a request for an unknown device fails as today.
- Hub consumer fixture: the hub reads the geometry through its integration snapshot with fakes. Delivery target: source only; the installed hub picks it up at its next upgrade.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Orientation, palette, Locate, device-only eviction and the Panels' configuration operations: a separate Nanoleaf issue filed with this one.
- Physical-layout rendering in the hub: hub #286 phase 2 and the hub's shared device art issue.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment, 2026-09-25, against `main` at 88831e4. Source-only delivery.

- **Operating assumptions:** one operator, the installed Linux runtime with the Lines (`wall`) and the NL22 Panels registered (this issue, SDLC scope defaults). The installed hub validates the `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot exactly (`apps/hub/src/integration.ts`), so the snapshot keeps its shape.
- **Decision (owner, 2026-09-25):** Nanoleaf publishes geometry on a separate read route, `GET /controller/integration/v1/geometry?deviceId=`, as ADR 0014 did for animations. The hub companion adds a sibling route, `GET /api/controllers/v1/:id/integration/geometry`, with a closed validator and a fake-controller fixture, rather than merging geometry into the hub's polled integration snapshot.
- **Cuts:** none. Map drawing caches (`connector-geometry.json`) and device discovery stay out: the route reads the saved `layout.json` only. Revisit if a Lines layout lacks saved connector geometry.
- **Complexity: medium.** One pure read route over existing geometry functions, a TypeScript consumer validator and a hub companion in a second repository.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The wall map's pure geometry functions and the ADR 0014 route pattern already exist.
- **Impact: medium.** Read-only, but two consumers (hub, future shell art) depend on the shape, and the payload must carry no private paths, addresses or tokens.
- **Readiness:** ready. No blockers.
- **Acceptance mapping:** controller tests with the fake Lines and Panels layouts (each returns its geometry; no layout gives an explicit empty result; unknown device fails with `unknown-device`; read is byte-pure and sends no light request); HTTP route guards; Python/TypeScript consumer fixtures; hub companion fixture test through the hub route with a fake controller.
- **Reviews:** independent Standards and Specification reviews in both repositories. No UI change, so no human UI approval.

## Guide

**Topic:** nanoleaf-devices
**Note:** Read-only element geometry for the Lines and Panels on the integration route, so the hub's shell and home widget can draw the real wall shape.
**Highlight:** next step, Read-only geometry that the shell art (hub #355) and the home miniature (hub #286) draw from.

issues.title: Save and replay favorite animations by name
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

After an animation the owner likes, Codex can save it under a name (for example, "my ripple") and replay it later by name.

## Smallest useful implementation

- The extension stores named favorites (validated `animation.play` fields) in the installation's private SQLite, bounded (for example, 32).
- New extension commands save and delete favorites. They are configuration edits with `applied` receipts.
- `animation.play` accepts `favorite: <name>`.
- MCP adds `nanoleaf_animation_save` and `nanoleaf_animation_forget`, and the options listing includes favorites.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Favorites are local state and must survive upgrades.
- Private data stays out of Git and the browser.
- The frame and byte bounds apply at play time. No flash cap applies (owner decision in #149).
- The snapshot shape stays unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Save, replay, rename collision, delete and bound tests.
- A persistence test across a database reopen.
- MCP save and replay tests.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Sharing favorites with the hub or across devices is deferred to the hub.


## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, from #92's delivery and the live session. Source-only delivery unless stated.

- **Complexity: medium.** New persistent state and commands.
- **Uncertainty: low.**
- **Impact: medium.** User data integrity.
- **Readiness:** backlog.

Follows #92 and complements #146.

issues.title: Offer a mood library of named animation presets
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

When asked for something like "cozy", "ocean", "sunset", "aurora", "campfire" or "forest", Codex picks from a curated library of named presets (pattern, colors, speed, direction) instead of improvising palettes.

## Smallest useful implementation

- A static preset table in `bridge/effects.py`, reported by the animation options route and `nanoleaf_animations_list`.
- `animation.play` accepts either explicit fields or `preset: <name>`, resolved server-side to the same encoded effect.
- Start with about 8 presets.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Explicit animation requests keep working unchanged.
- Presets must pass the frame and byte bounds. No flash cap applies (owner decision in #149).
- The extension snapshot shape stays unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Every preset validates and renders within bounds.
- A preset request produces the same frames as the equivalent explicit request.
- MCP lists the presets.
- The owner reviews the palettes live when requested.

issues.title: Add a rotating spin direction and a faster speed for animations
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Codex can play a sweep that rotates around the wall's center, clockwise or counterclockwise, and can pick a speed one step faster than `fast`. On the owner's 15-Line wall the Lines surround the centroid (angles cover the full circle), so a rotation reads clearly.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `bridge/effects.py` `phases()` gains `clockwise` and `counterclockwise`, computed from each Line's angle around the centroid. The spatial patterns (`wave`, `gradient`) accept them.
- A new speed, for example `faster`, uses a shorter keyframe step, still within 20 frames per zone and 8,192 bytes.
- Validation, the TypeScript consumer and fixtures, and the MCP enums are updated. Specs and docs follow.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Existing directions and speeds keep their frames byte for byte.
- Free-only gating, receipts and the single writer are unchanged.
- The faster speed may go down to the device's one-decisecond keyframe step; no flash cap applies (owner decision in #149).

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Encoder tests: crest order follows angle for both rotations on the 15-Line and two-Line fixtures; the faster speed produces a shorter cycle; every combination stays within the frame and byte bounds.
- MCP tests list the new values.
- Live, when requested: play a clockwise wave and confirm the rotation.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Choosing a custom rotation center is deferred. The centroid is used. Revisit if the owner's wall shape makes it look off-center.


## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, from #92's delivery and the live session. Source-only delivery unless stated.

- **Complexity: low.** Encoder and enum changes.
- **Uncertainty: low.**
- **Impact: medium.** Physical output.
- **Readiness:** ready. The owner relaxed the flash cap on 2026-09-25 (#149), so the faster speed is unblocked.

Follows #92 and complements #146.

issues.title: Stop an animation and restore the remembered scene through MCP
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

From Codex, "stop the animation" returns the Lines to the scene the bridge remembers (for example, Cozy Blaze at its remembered brightness) with one explicit command. After the #92 live check, stopping a looping animation took a manual `scene.activate` of the remembered scene.

## Smallest useful implementation

- The animation options route (`GET /controller/integration/v1/animations`) adds `rememberedSceneId`, the opaque ID of the remembered scene, or null when none is remembered or it is no longer advertised.
- A new MCP control tool, `nanoleaf_scene_restore`, reads that ID and sends one existing v1 `scene.activate` through the same path as `nanoleaf_scene_activate`. It never switches mode.
- No controller v1 change and no extension snapshot change (the hub validates the snapshot exactly).

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Hub ADR 0005: this is an explicit command, and nothing restores automatically. The tool is Free-only, like `scene.activate`, and the Work/Quiet rejection message says to switch to Free.
- Scene names stay out of the shared v1 snapshot.
- The remembered scene and its brightness are unchanged by the tool; only the worker's existing restore policy writes them.
- There is one light writer.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Controller tests: the options route reports the remembered scene ID; the ID is null when nothing is remembered and null when the scene disappeared.
- MCP tests: restore sends exactly one `scene.activate` with the caller's request identity; Work/Quiet is rejected with the switch message; a null ID gives a typed failure with no dispatch.
- Live, when requested: play an animation, ask Codex to stop it, and confirm the remembered scene returns.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Restoring brightness as well as the scene is deferred. Today's Free handoff already restores it, and the #92 live check found it unchanged. Revisit if an override leaves it different.


## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, from #92's delivery and the live session. Source-only delivery unless stated.

- **Complexity: low.** One read field and one tool reusing `scene.activate`.
- **Uncertainty: low.**
- **Impact: medium.** It writes to a physical device through an existing command.
- **Readiness:** ready.
- **Acceptance mapping:** controller and MCP unit tests plus the protocol test; live check optional.

Follows #92 and complements #146.

## Guide

issues.title: Customize Work-mode light colors so unread tasks stand out from the base
issues.body:
### Outcome and real setup

One operator, the Linux installation, the registered Lines wall and, when registered, the NL22 Light Panels. In Work mode the operator can tell at a glance which Lines carry a finished task waiting for review ("ready"; the bridge calls it unread) and which are unused. The operator can also choose the colors used for the base and for each status.

Today unused Lines and read or interrupted task Lines are steady blue `#193CFF`, and unread tasks pulse between 20% and 100% of the same blue (`BASELINE` and `COLORS['unread']` in `bridge/bridge.py`). At the 30% Work brightness the unread pulse is hard to tell apart from the base. The completion comet tail is blue too, and the map draws empty Lines and unread tasks with the same `--wall-unread` token. Status colors are fixed constants in `bridge/bridge.py` and CSS tokens in `bridge/wall.html`; only project colors can be edited.

Excluded: animation style per status (#20), completion celebration choice (#19), the live renderer (#17), Free mode and the Nanoleaf app's own scenes.

### Palette and options

Default palette, accepted by the owner on 2026-09-24:

| Role | Today | New default | Suggested alternatives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base (unused and read Lines) | Blue `#193CFF` | Dim blue `#0A1866` (about 40% of today's blue) | Today's blue, dim warm white `#4D3F2A`, Off `#000000` |
| Working | Green `#00FF00` | Unchanged | - |
| Question | Yellow `#FFFF00` | Unchanged | Amber `#FFB000` |
| Blocked | Red `#FF0000` | Unchanged | - |
| Unread (ready) | Blue `#193CFF` | Violet `#9B30FF` | Magenta `#FF00C0`, cyan `#00E5FF`, warm white `#FFE0B0` |

Unread shares the base hue today. The fix gives Unread a hue no other role uses and makes the base dimmer than the task Lines. Violet is far from the blue base and from green, yellow and red. White is not the default because the comet head and the Locate flash are already white. Off makes task Lines stand out most but leaves a mostly dark wall, so it is offered as a swatch to try.

Customization in this issue:

1. A color choice for each of the five roles: Base, Working, Question, Blocked and Unread. Each offers the suggested swatches above and a custom color.
2. Reset colors, which restores the defaults and nothing else.
3. A warning in the Colors group when two roles are too similar to tell apart, such as Unread and Base today. It does not block saving.
4. One palette for every registered device, so Lines and Panels agree.

Where the palette applies:

- Work: the base for unused Lines and for read or interrupted task Lines; status colors for pulses and outward waves. The comet tail uses the Unread color, because the Line settles into Unread afterward. The comet head stays white.
- Quiet: the same colors, steady at 10%.
- Project layout: the status half of an unused reserved Line and empty Shared Lines use the base. Project halves keep their project colors, and animation coverage is unchanged.
- Wall map: the wall artwork and legend use the effective colors, including the Project halves sample.
- Unchanged: Free, the white Locate flash, the white comet head, the remembered scene and the steady blue fallback shown before any scene has been remembered.

### Smallest useful implementation

Store one palette in private SQLite. The worker reads it for each frame in place of the fixed `BASELINE` and `COLORS` values, and `PRIORITY` stays keyed by status. Expose the effective palette in `/api/state` and accept changes through the existing validated settings write, with the page origin and request token. Add a Colors group to the wall map's Options menu with the five choices, swatches and Reset colors, and replace the map's fixed status tokens with the effective palette. Prerequisites: none. This does not wait for #17.

Planning: an issue-linked OpenSpec change. Task-light colors have no capability spec yet, so the change migrates the relevant bridge guide contract (status table, pulses, waves, comet colors and Project halves) into a new capability spec alongside the delta. It also adds a `wall-map-hierarchy` delta for the Options group.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

The worker stays the only light writer for each device. Alert priority comes from status, not color: blocked stays on top even when set to violet. A color change applies within about two seconds without restarting pulse epochs, replaying outward waves or comets, moving tasks between Lines or releasing comet source reservations. Mode, scene selection and brightness, project colors, reservations, halves, coverage, orientation, and task and unread state are unchanged. Opening the Colors group sends no request. Invalid colors and unknown roles are rejected without a partial update. The Nanoleaf token never reaches the browser.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- [ ] The Options menu has a Colors group with Base, Working, Question, Blocked and Unread choices, each with suggested swatches and a custom color, plus Reset colors. Choices survive a restart (browser check; isolated persistence test).
- [ ] In Work, unused and read Lines use the base color. An unread task pulses in the Unread color, and the comet tail uses the Unread color with a white head. Working, question and blocked use their chosen colors for pulses and waves (fake-clock frame tests on `zone_color` and `effect_payload`).
- [ ] Quiet shows the chosen colors steady at 10%; Free is unchanged (frame tests).
- [ ] In Project layout the status half and empty Shared Lines use the base, and project halves keep their colors under both coverage settings (frame tests).
- [ ] With blocked set to violet and unread set to red, blocked still overrides question, working and unread in overlapping waves and comets (frame tests).
- [ ] Applying or resetting colors mid-pulse and mid-comet restarts no epoch, replays no wave or comet and changes no assignment (fake-clock test).
- [ ] With the base set to Off, unused Lines stay dark while indicators show, and the remembered scene still returns when the last indicator clears (frame and worker tests).
- [ ] The wall artwork and legend use the effective colors, and status labels stay readable whatever colors are chosen (browser check with screenshots).
- [ ] A similar-color warning appears when Unread equals Base and clears when they differ (browser check).
- [ ] Invalid hex values, unknown roles and missing request tokens are rejected with nothing applied (API tests).
- [ ] Upgrading an existing installation keeps project colors, reservations, map settings, mode and scene, and starts with the new default palette (migration test with isolated state).
- [ ] Registered Panels use the same palette for their status display (frame test with the synthetic NL22 layout).
- [ ] Explicit human approval of the current UI candidate before merge.

Checks: `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow`. A physical side-by-side check of the default Unread and Base colors on the Lines with `setup --demo` needs an explicit request and the installation owner. Record it separately from the software evidence.

### Decisions

Settled with the owner on 2026-09-24, who accepted each recommendation:

1. Unread default: violet `#9B30FF`. LED color at 30% brightness can look different from the screen. If violet reads poorly on the Lines, the owner picks another swatch; no code change is needed. The physical check is optional and needs an explicit request.
2. Base default: dim blue `#0A1866`.
3. Existing installation: adopts the new defaults on upgrade, because no status colors have been saved and today's default is the problem.

issues.title: Contain SQLite backup, fixture and operation knowledge within state owners
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Concentrate schema knowledge where it causes demonstrated maintenance coupling: shared-input backup/restore, synthetic demo seeding, and selected multi-table state operations. Callers express those operations without reconstructing column order or backup row formats.

The objective is a smaller change surface for schema evolution, not a wrapper for every SQL statement or a ban on all cross-module reads.

## Evidence

At `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e`:

- [devices.py](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/devices.py#L14-L33) preserves legacy column order for positional shared-input backups.
- [shared_input._dump_tables/_restore_tables](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/shared_input.py#L253-L266) use SELECT * and interpret legacy row lengths.
- [scripts/demo.py](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/scripts/demo.py#L43-L55) seeds several tables with positional tuples; browser checks depend on that fixture.
- Shared-input projection and wall configuration edits span task, placement and project state. The useful boundary is a coherent operation, including its transaction, rather than individual SQL statements.

## Scope

- Put legacy/current backup encoding and restoration behind the modules that own the relevant state and compatibility rules. Preserve the supported backup format and restore behavior.
- Provide a state/map-owned synthetic seeding operation used by the demo and browser fixtures.
- Inventory the cross-module state operations affected by those changes and #118's configuration-operation boundary. Move a bounded operation where doing so removes column/layout or invariant knowledge from callers.
- Keep multi-table changes on the caller's transaction. Owner helpers must not open independent connections or commit behind the caller.
- Retain justified SQL projections where an owner wrapper would add no information hiding; document those choices.

Out of scope: an ORM, generic query/repository framework, schema migration, new backup format, allocation changes, moving already-owned controller/integration journals, or a repository-wide SQL rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The delivery records the bounded operations being changed, their owners, callers and invariants. Completion is measured by removed schema/row-format knowledge, not grep counts or a universal no-cross-table rule.
- AC2: The demo seeds through the owning operation. A focused Python test verifies its tasks, activity epochs, projects, metadata and applied-mode state before the browser suite uses it.
- AC3: Existing legacy and device-aware backup data restore correctly without callers inferring compatibility from tuple length. Repeated initialization and source rollback preserve current modes/scenes, manual preferences, bound placements, task epochs and each device's comet reservations.
- AC4: Failure partway through a multi-table operation rolls back as a unit; no new connection or hidden commit breaks the caller's transaction. Preserve existing source-generation checks and concurrency behavior.
- AC5: Tests for migrations, source rollback, pending edits and reservations retain their assertions. Python and browser suites pass with no behavior or wire-contract change.
- AC6: The PR explains retained cross-module SQL and why each new operation hides meaningful policy or representation. Verify affected specs and record why no capability delta is needed if requirements remain unchanged.

## Verification approach

Start with characterization of synthetic seeding and existing backup/restore behavior using isolated fixtures. Use the existing Linux pre-migration fixture, repeated-initialization, shared-input rollback, project-map and comet tests. Add only missing operation-level compatibility/atomicity coverage; do not remove distinct lower-level tests.

Run python3 scripts/check.py and npm run test:browser, plus required workflow checks for any planning/specification changes. No installed database or physical device is needed.

## Dependencies and readiness

- #118 first: use the settled application/runtime ownership rather than moving SQL twice.
- #127 and #128 address render inputs and wall refresh/projection separately; this issue changes neither rendering policy nor refresh scheduling.
- Coordinate any change to shared-input projection with #122 and active source-input fixes; this issue does not depend on extracting a pure shared reducer.
- Worth exploring, with high confidence in the observed coupling and moderate confidence in broad payoff. Keep the initial scope on backups and seeding, expanding only when a named caller demonstrably loses schema knowledge.

issues.title: Separate shared configuration operations, runtime primitives and hook management
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Shared configuration behavior, runtime primitives and hook-file management have explicit owners beneath the CLI and HTTP entry points. Servers and installers import focused operations instead of receiving the bridge module or a namespace of its globals.

Start with the configuration-edit boundary: browser routes and machine commands call the same transaction-level operations without translating machine commands into browser URLs. Continue with hook management and the remaining runtime dependencies. Preserve current process and state ownership.

## Evidence

Source baseline: `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e` (2026-09-24).

- [integration_api.operation/process](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/integration_api.py#L181-L245) translates commands into /api/... routes and imports wall_server to apply them.
- [wall_server.apply_operation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/wall_server.py#L125-L157) owns shared configuration validation/application beneath browser routing.
- [The CLI](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L1534-L1541) passes a bridge namespace to shared-input and controller commands. Other server/installer callers also receive broad bridge dependencies.
- Hook-file management and its span-preserving JSON parser reside in bridge.py despite callers in shared input, installation and hook tests.
- [ADR 0008](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/docs/decisions/0008-integration-settings-extension.md#L19-L23) calls for shared transaction-level application operations and atomic configuration receipts.

## Scope and implementation sequence

1. Extract focused configuration operations independent of HTTP and the CLI. Browser routes decode browser payloads; the machine adapter validates its own contract and resolves opaque IDs. Neither the worker nor the integration application path depends on wall_server or /api/... strings.
2. Move hook management and the JSON span parser into a focused module. Preserve supported commands, bytes/positions of unrelated hooks, trust boundaries and private backups; temporary re-exports are allowed where existing callers need a staged migration.
3. Give shared runtime primitives explicit homes and dependencies: state initialization, mode changes, config/geometry loading, JSON writes, device requests and worker launch. Avoid replacing bridge.py with another catch-all runtime module.
4. Remove whole-module b/bridge arguments and the SimpleNamespace(**globals()) hand-off. Retain explicit request/send/launch/clock seams appropriate to each operation. Device reads and enrollment requests are not interchangeable with rendered-effect sends.
5. Update installation packaging for every new module. The Linux installer is the only installation path after #131.
6. Keep launch_worker spawning bridge.py worker and preserve every documented CLI command and argument.

Keep browser Host/Origin/edit-token handling and machine authentication, strict request validation, opaque IDs and request journals in their respective adapters.

Out of scope: new daemon/process ownership, schema or public API changes, rendering policy, input selection, wall-page scheduling (#119), device context (#121), transaction-duration changes, installations or device operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: No caller receives the bridge module or SimpleNamespace(**globals()). Imports needed only to break entry-point cycles are removed; deliberate lazy imports for optional dependencies remain allowed and documented.
- AC2: Hook management is exercised through its owning module or documented temporary re-exports. Registration/removal/rollback preserve unrelated hook text, positions, commands and trust behavior.
- AC3: Demo and affected tests inject device request/send and worker-launch dependencies through explicit seams rather than mutating the bridge module. Necessary failure injection at an owning boundary remains allowed; a blanket ban on mocking is not an objective.
- AC4: An isolated Linux runtime-copy test proves `install_linux.copy_runtime` includes every shared runtime module this change adds, and that the copied `bridge.py` imports them and starts its documented commands outside the source tree. (Refreshed 2026-09-25: #131 / PR #138 removed the Windows installer, so Linux is the only installation path.)
- AC5: The Python, browser, MCP and required workflow suites pass. CLI smoke coverage verifies documented command names/arguments and optional-dependency startup behavior; record the actual suite count at the delivery revision.
- AC6: Isolated Linux setup with fake device transport, run against the copied runtime, verifies packaging. No Windows PowerShell validation remains after #131. This evidence does not claim an installed upgrade. (Refreshed 2026-09-25.)
- AC7: A decision record using the next available number describes application-operation, runtime, hook, CLI and worker ownership and the permitted dependency direction.
- AC8: The integration/worker configuration application path imports neither wall_server nor browser route names. Both adapters invoke the same configuration operations; no duplicate edit implementation replaces the removed coupling.
- AC9: Caller-owned transactions, exactly-once revision/dirty notifications per existing edit semantics, and atomic configuration-plus-receipt commits are preserved. Cancellation, revocation, expiry and cross-client revision conflicts retain their existing outcomes.
- AC10: Browser edits retain selective active-comet deferral; machine execution retains its wait for an active comet or existing pending wall edit. Equivalent eligible edits through both adapters produce equivalent saved settings/assignments without resetting task epochs, replaying effects, changing source/mode/scene, or touching unrelated reservations.

## Verification approach

Use existing isolated SQLite, fake clocks and fake device transport. Preserve hook, source-switching, cancellation/recovery and device-isolation tests. Add focused browser/machine operation-parity checks covering deferred and conflict cases, installer packaging coverage and CLI compatibility coverage before moving the corresponding code.

Run python3 scripts/check.py, npm run test:browser, npm run test:mcp, and the workflow checks required by repository policy. Windows checks run in Windows PowerShell. Keep tests for distinct algorithms and race conditions.

This is intended to preserve behavior. Apply the SDLC's significant-design planning requirements, verify affected specs and record why no capability delta is needed if contracts remain unchanged.

## Dependencies and readiness

Strong recommendation; high confidence. Ready for source delivery. The configuration-operation extraction is the first bounded step. Coordinate the remaining broad module moves with active controller/worker owners and merge in a quiet window; do not absorb behavior fixes.

#119 is independent frontend work. #120 follows this module ownership work. #121 remains a separate device-context decision, and #122 investigates shared-input projection. #127 owns the device-render input; #128 investigates backend wall refresh/projection. #129 investigates execution ownership while preserving locks, and #130 measures contention before considering shorter lock windows.

## Delivery target

Source-only through reviewed PR delivery. This issue does not authorize installation, physical-light changes or changes to another task's worktree.

## Agreed architecture work order

1. This issue: extract shared configuration operations first, then hook management and the remaining runtime dependencies in bounded steps.
2. #119 (browser coordinator) and #127 (device-render input) are separate next candidates; neither replaces the other.
3. #120 targets backup/fixture/operation schema coupling after this issue. #128 first settles the backend refresh/freshness question.
4. #129 is a later execution-ownership investigation. #130 independently measures whether shorter lock windows are justified; no lock-duration change is implied by this refactor.

#121 and #122 keep their existing device-context and shared-projection scopes. They are related work, not additional prerequisites for the first configuration extraction. This ordering supersedes the earlier sequencing comment on this issue; issue-specific dependencies and active ownership still govern delivery.

## Work assessment

issues.title: Change a registered Nanoleaf device's address without re-enrolling
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Let the operator change the address of a registered Nanoleaf device, such as the NL22 Light Panels after a new DHCP lease, without removing and re-enrolling it. The device keeps its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that.

## Background

`device-enroll` ([#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/45), PR #79) refuses an existing id at a new address, so it never silently redirects an identity. The only way to change a Panels address today is `device-remove` followed by `device-enroll`, which clears the device's reservations. The [device-state specification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/device-state/spec.md) already says a configured address change keeps a device's identity and saved state. The Linux guide documents the current workaround.

## Scope

An explicit command or option that changes one registered device's address. Before writing, it verifies the device at the new address with the stored credential, the same way enrollment does: model NL22 and a layout whose triangles match the saved geometry. The Lines device (`wall`) may be covered if that is simple; otherwise it is out of scope.

Out of scope: automatic discovery or following the device on the network, and changing a device's kind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The operator can change a registered Panels device's address. Its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene are unchanged, and it is never registered twice.
- [ ] AC2: Before any write, the new address is checked: it must be a private IPv4 address, unused by another registered device, and answering as the same kind of device with a layout matching the saved one. A mismatch is refused with nothing changed.
- [ ] AC3: The change sends no light write. A running worker for the device picks up the new address on its next pass or retry, without a service restart.
- [ ] AC4: Credentials stay out of output and errors, as with enrollment.

issues.title: Control the NL22 Panels through the controller and local MCP server
issues.body:
## Problem

The protected controller and the local MCP server reach only the Lines (`wall`). The controller has one device identity. Under ADR 0010, only the `wall` worker runs controller and integration work, including overrides, the hold and scene discovery. The NL22 Panels can be controlled only from the CLI (`mode … --device panels`).

So the hub, the dashboard and Codex can't turn the Panels on or off, set their brightness or mode, or play their scenes. #91 and #92 cover the Lines only.

## Outcome

The Panels are a second controller device. The hub, the dashboard and Codex (through MCP) control them the same way as the Lines, and each device keeps its own single writer.

## Scope

- [ ] `/controller/v1/devices` lists both devices. The snapshot, commands, feed and integration routes accept the Panels' `deviceId`, with their own identity, revisions, request journal, overrides, hold and discovered scenes.
- [ ] The Panels worker runs the Panels' controller work and stays the only writer to the Panels. The `wall` worker never writes to them. Update ADR 0010, which assigns all controller work to `wall`.
- [ ] Power, brightness, mode and `scene.activate` work for the Panels under the same mode rules as the Lines.
- [ ] The local MCP server can bind the Panels as a second fixed target. Callers can't choose other devices.
- [ ] Record whether the Panels accept `display` version 2.0 effects, which ADR 0010 lists as unknown. #92 needs that answer before animations can extend to the Panels.

issues.title: Keep following the hub feed when it contains an undeclared source
issues.body:
## Problem

Nanoleaf rejects the whole hub snapshot when any session comes from a source that isn't in `qualifiedSources`. `check_envelope` in `bridge/shared_input.py` raises `unqualified-source`. The feed then counts as failed: tasks are marked stale, colors hold and the wall stops following every agent, not just the new one. It stays that way until someone edits the consumer configuration.

The installed configuration declares only Codex Desktop and Codex CLI. The hub has no Claude Code sessions today, but the first Claude Code hook that posts to it would stop the wall. #100 expects Claude Code tasks on the wall.

## Outcome

A session from a source Nanoleaf hasn't declared stays off the wall, and every other session keeps updating. Once you declare a Claude Code source, its sessions appear.

## Scope

- [ ] Skip sessions from undeclared sources instead of rejecting the snapshot. A skipped session gets no slot, wave, comet or acknowledgment, and takes no part in parent and subagent grouping.
- [ ] Envelope checks still reject the whole snapshot: authentication, version, owner, schema and revision.
- [ ] `shared-status` reports how many sessions were skipped and their source identities, so a missing declaration is visible.
- [ ] Declaring a source later with `shared-configure` doesn't replay old comets or waves for its existing sessions.
- [ ] Test that `qualifiedSources` accepts a Claude Code source identity. Update `docs/shared-input.md`, which says every source in the feed must be declared, and describe how to declare one.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `shared-session-consumer` spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover:
  - one undeclared session among declared ones
  - a snapshot with only undeclared sessions, which leaves the wall idle and the connection current
  - a declared Claude Code source
  - declaring a source after its sessions already exist
  - a declared subagent whose parent is undeclared, which follows the existing missing-parent rule
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes.

## Dependencies

Installing Claude Code hooks for the hub, and any hub change.

issues.title: Play custom animations on the Lines when Codex asks for them
issues.body:
## Outcome

You can describe an animation to Codex, such as "a slow blue-green ocean wave". Codex switches the wall to Free and plays it on the Lines through the local MCP server.

## Background

A custom Nanoleaf animation is a `display` effect: frames for each panel, uploaded once with `PUT /effects` and then looped by the device. The worker already builds and uploads this kind of effect for status (`effect_payload` in `bridge/bridge.py`). A requested animation reuses the same path and the same single writer, with no per-frame streaming.

Nothing accepts animation input today. Controller v1 has no animation command. The hub architecture requires typed-extension work for arbitrary color or timeline input and rules out raw protocol commands.

## Decision

The owner chose Free-mode content on September 23, 2026. When you ask for an animation in conversation, the agent switches the wall to Free with `nanoleaf_mode_set`, then plays the animation. It stays until the next mode command, animation or scene. This fits hub [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md) as written: switching to Free is its own command, and nothing restores automatically.

Animations that play over Work status to get your attention are wanted too, but as scheduled or routine behavior, not on request. They are out of scope here (see Not included).

## Scope

- [ ] A typed `animation.play` command in the Nanoleaf extension, not a controller v1 change. Parameters: a pattern from a fixed set (for example wave, pulse, breathe, sparkle and gradient), 1 to 8 `#rrggbb` colors, speed, direction for spatial patterns, and whether it loops or plays once. The controller validates everything before queueing.
- [ ] The worker separates the frame encoder from the status color logic, and renders each pattern with the Lines geometry it already uses for waves and comets.
- [ ] Commands use the existing queue and receipts: sent, failed or uncertain, with physical outcome unknown. Like `scene.activate`, the command is accepted only in Free. In Work or Quiet the controller rejects it before any write, and the MCP tool's message says to switch to Free first.
- [ ] The local MCP server gets a read tool that lists patterns and limits, and a control tool, `nanoleaf_animation_play`.
- [ ] Qualify the firmware's limits on effect size and frame count, and keep requests within the controller's 64 KiB limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover validation bounds, encoder output for each pattern on fixture layouts, acceptance in Free and rejection in Work and Quiet, receipts and the MCP tools.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass. OpenSpec changes update the affected controller, worker and MCP specs.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests it: ask Codex for two different animations, and confirm it switches the wall to Free before each one plays. One comment records it.

## Related

- #91 lets Codex play saved scenes and sets up the same MCP connection.
- #19 and #20 (status animation presets) could reuse the new encoder.
- #15 (authoritative rendering state).
- [agent-device-hub#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/41) needs real-time streaming for music visualizers. This issue doesn't.

## Not included

Per-panel keyframes, the NL22 Panels, audio-reactive or streamed effects, and the hub's MCP route. Also attention animations over Work status: they belong with scheduled or routine behavior under [agent-device-hub#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45), and playing over status will need its own ADR 0005 decision. They can reuse this issue's encoder. Also ChatGPT and other remote clients: ChatGPT connects to MCP servers only over remote HTTPS, which depends on the remote access that hub ADR 0004 defers.

## Readiness

Complexity medium. Uncertainty low; the firmware limits are the main unknown. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

## Work assessment

issues.title: Let Codex play saved Nanoleaf scenes through the local MCP server
issues.body:
## Outcome

You can ask Codex to play a scene you saved in the Nanoleaf app, for example "switch the wall to Free and play Aurora", through the local MCP server.

## Current behavior

The controller already supports `scene.activate` for discovered scenes, in Free mode only (#64). The local MCP server exposes only `nanoleaf_status` and `nanoleaf_mode_set`, and the `local-mcp-bindings` spec forbids scene tools. Scene IDs are opaque. The names you chose in the Nanoleaf app travel in the `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot. Codex isn't configured to use the MCP server yet.

## Scope

- [ ] A read tool lists the advertised scenes with their IDs and names.
- [ ] A control tool, `nanoleaf_scene_activate`, sends one `scene.activate` through the controller. Like `nanoleaf_mode_set`, it passes the caller's request ID and expected revisions through unchanged.
- [ ] Following hub ADR 0005, activation stays a separate command. The tool doesn't switch to Free itself. In Work or Quiet it returns the controller's rejection with a message to switch to Free first.
- [ ] An unknown scene ID is rejected before dispatch. The tools appear only for credentials with the matching read or control scope.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `local-mcp-bindings` spec, and `docs/local-mcp.md` describes the tools.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fake-controller tests cover:

  - receipts preserved without claiming visible output

issues.title: Switch the wall map between Lines and Light Panels
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Let the existing wall map show and edit one Nanoleaf device at a time, with a selector that switches between the original Lines and the NL22 Light Panels.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. The Linux runtime has no tray, so this issue covers the browser map and its API only.

## Scope

Add a device selector to the existing map. The selected device drives the page: its layout, mode, layout settings, reservations, pending state and Locate. Lines keep their current presentation. NL22 triangles render as plain SVG triangles with static status colours, drawn from the cached geometry delivered by [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43). This is the existing Nanoleaf editor, not a new hub dashboard.

Out of scope here: showing both devices at once, a "Both devices" mode action, Prism styling or simulated pulse, wave and comet animation for triangles, a triangle assembly animation, the retired Windows tray, and a combined allocation pool ([#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) is deferred).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The map opens on Lines. A labelled selector lists the registered devices and switches the page to the chosen one. The selection is kept in the URL, so a reload stays on the same device. With only Lines registered, the page behaves as it does today.
- [ ] AC2: Device-scoped reads and actions (state, mode, layout settings, assignment and Locate) address the selected device. Project colours and task project assignment stay shared. Requests that name no device address Lines, so existing browser and CLI callers behave as before. Unknown devices are rejected rather than falling back to Lines. The protected controller API stays Lines-only per #43.
- [ ] AC3: For the selected device, the page shows its mode with Work/Quiet/Free controls, its pending state and last error, its reservations and its waiting count. Changing one device's mode leaves the other device's mode and saved scene alone.
- [ ] AC4: Triangles support selection, multi-selection, project reservation, Shared release, inspector information and Locate. Triangles are numbered in the order #43's geometry reader returns them. Split-half and half-swap controls are hidden for triangles, and the backend rejects those settings for one-zone elements. Lines keep them.
- [ ] AC5: Rotation and flip apply to the selected device and are saved per device.
- [ ] AC6: Existing protections hold. Selection, refresh and switching devices send no physical Locate or effect. Display reads use cached geometry. Request-origin and edit-token checks remain, and browser responses never include Nanoleaf credentials.
- [ ] AC7: Keyboard selection and focus, reduced motion and the existing supported viewport sizes work on the triangle view. The Lines assembly behaviour delivered by #38 is unchanged, and switching to Panels plays no assembly.
- [ ] AC8: Record explicit human approval of the current UI candidate before merge. Agent review and successful CI do not substitute for that approval; changed UI requires renewed approval.

## Verification approach

Use deterministic browser fixtures with Lines and #43's synthetic 18-triangle NL22 fixture. Cover switching and URL persistence, targeted actions on each device, rejection of unknown devices, the Lines default for untargeted calls, triangle selection, reservation and Locate, and rejected split-half settings. Assert that selection and switching send no Locate. Keep #38's browser checks passing. Run the Python, browser and OpenSpec/workflow suites. Personal installation remains separate.

## Dependencies

- [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) is delivered. #38 is delivered and merged.
- Sequenced after [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) by choice. The Panels were enrolled (#45) and trialled (#46, closed 2026-09-24) with CLI mode controls, so nothing here is blocked.
- #45 promises that enrollment needs no service restart. The selector must therefore read the device registry on each request, not once at map startup, or a newly enrolled device would not appear until the map service restarts. The running map currently caches only the Lines configuration (`wall_server.App.config`).
- #29 and #33 are related consumers, not prerequisites. Exact animation parity from #15 and #17 is not part of this completion gate.

## Delivery target

Source-only map and API changes with a human-approved UI candidate. Installing the updated map on the Linux runtime needs a separate explicit request.

## Long-term direction

On 2026-09-25 the owner set a long-term direction: a B.U.N.N.Y. interface with device pages and a group page that shows every device ([agent-device-hub#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271)). This story still shows one device at a time, and its scope and acceptance criteria are unchanged. Two implementation choices keep that path open. They are design notes, not acceptance criteria:

- Draw each device through one renderer that takes a device and its cached geometry, instead of branching the page on Lines versus Panels. A later page can then show several devices or reuse the art.
- Key the page's device-scoped state by device, so showing two devices later adds entries rather than changing the model. [#119](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/119), which moves the page's rebuild policy behind a view model, makes this easier if it lands first.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge, and main-CI readback. UI changes require human approval of the current candidate.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-44-wall-map-device-selector/`. Check active and archived changes for this exact issue before creating or reusing it.

## Revision note

Scope reduced on 2026-09-22 for a single-operator Linux installation, matching the same-day trim of #41 through #43.

Rewritten on 2026-09-23 as a device selector and moved after #46. I removed the side-by-side sections and their responsive stacking, the global count that deduplicated tasks across sections, the "Both devices" action, focus and selection kept across two sections, the six-triangle region case, the numbering scheme based on geometry and device identity, and the requirement that triangle animation in the map stay honest (triangles now show static colours). The edit history holds the prior text.

Update 2026-09-24: #46 is complete. Added the requirement to read the device registry per request, so enrollment keeps working without a map restart.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** Device-scoped state and per-request registry reads in the map and API.

issues.title: Name non-connection Hub feed failures and document the hub-sessions command rules
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Round 2 of the review of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/124 (hub-paired verification, #120) left three small diagnosis and documentation gaps. Each case still fails when it should.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Name non-connection fetch failures (S5):** `readHubFeed` (`scripts/verify/pairing.ts:96-100`) classifies every rejected fetch as `unreachable`, so a redirect or a non-HTTP answer on the `hub-feed` port reads `skipped: … not reachable (no connection)` for 60 s, then fails with that same misleading reason. Treat only `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET` or `UND_ERR_SOCKET` (and a connect timeout) as unreachable. Report any other failure as an error with a fixed reason, such as "the Hub answered with a redirect", which fails at once. Add the case to `verify-paired.test.ts`.
- **The `fresh` rule in the guide (S6):** `docs/development.md:244-245` says steps that change state are marked `fresh`. `hub-sessions` now sends one `brightness.set` and asserts deltas instead. Amend the sentence, and note that the step leaves brightness at 25.
- **`hub-sessions` inside a live composition (P-S5):** the step sends one command as the Hub, outside the Hub's queue. Say in "Hub-paired runs" to run it only against a stand-in or an idle pairing, never while a Hub #495 composition is driving the Hub.

## Observable acceptance

- A redirect on the `hub-feed` port fails `hub-feed` at once with a reason naming the redirect.
- The guide states both rules.

## Evidence

The round 2 Standards and Specification reviews on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/124.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-28, from the current issue body, comments and native prerequisites; the owning repository's single-operator scope and delivery boundaries apply. No scope cuts or readiness promotion are proposed.

- **Complexity: medium.** Fetch-failure classification crosses error causes, retry timing, paired verification and its command-use documentation.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The issue lists the connection failures that may wait and requires redirects to fail immediately with a fixed reason.
- **Impact: medium.** Misclassification can misrepresent verification health; the documented command must stay outside a live Hub-driven composition.
- **Readiness:** Remains backlog; no installed run or live composition is authorized by this recommendation.
- **Planned evidence:** A redirect fails hub-feed immediately with its named reason; retained connection failures use the bounded waiting path. Review both documented hub-sessions rules, including brightness 25 and the stand-in/idle-only boundary. Existing repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI remain required; these checks have not been run for this story.
