issues.title: Keep test-launched Pixoo servers and guarded listeners off installed ports
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Tests that launch a Pixoo server, or open a guarded listener, on port 0 can be handed 41230 or 41231 by the kernel. Both are installed-service ports inside Linux's ephemeral range. A test that receives one is refused by the verification guard (`port-reserved` in supervised runs, a refused connection back to its own listener in unsupervised ones), so the test fails for a reason unrelated to the behavior it checks.

The CI failure at divoom-app-upgrade `74b20d8` (PR #124, Simulator browser checks) shows CI hands out these ports. That failure came from a stand-in Hub, which `bace2fd` fixed with `listenLoopback`'s retry. The same risk remains for test-launched Pixoo servers and for the guarded listeners that predate #124.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Route every test listener through the `listenLoopback` retry that `bace2fd` added.
- Make the test launch helper retry a launch whose ready line names an installed port.

## Observable acceptance

A unit test hands the launch helper 41231 and 41230 before a free port, and the launch succeeds on the free one.

## Evidence

The round 2 Standards review on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/124, which puts the risk at about 2 in 28,232 per listen.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-28, from the current issue body, comments and native prerequisites; the owning repository's single-operator scope and delivery boundaries apply. No scope cuts or readiness promotion are proposed.

- **Complexity: medium.** Listener allocation and the subprocess launch/ready-line retry need to agree across test helpers.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Reserved ports 41230 and 41231 and the existing listenLoopback retry define the bounded fix.
- **Impact: medium.** A faulty retry can leave test processes/listeners running or collide with installed-service ports; isolation must remain enforced.
- **Readiness:** Remains backlog; only isolated test listeners and launch helpers are in scope.
- **Planned evidence:** Inject ready lines naming 41231 and 41230 before a free port; require success on the free port and clean termination of rejected launches. Existing guard refusals and listener cleanup still pass. Existing repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI remain required; these checks have not been run for this story.
- **Reassess when:** the stated prerequisite, acceptance boundary or isolated verification assumptions change.

Tests that launch a Pixoo server, or open a guarded listener, on port 0 can be handed 41230 or 41231 by the kernel. Both are installed-service ports inside Linux's ephemeral range. A test that receives one is refused by the verification guard (`port-reserved` in supervised runs, a refused connection back to its own listener in unsupervised ones), so the test fails for a reason unrelated to the behavior it checks.

The CI failure at divoom-app-upgrade `74b20d8` (PR #124, Simulator browser checks) shows CI hands out these ports. That failure came from a stand-in Hub, which `bace2fd` fixed with `listenLoopback`'s retry. The same risk remains for test-launched Pixoo servers and for the guarded listeners that predate #124.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- Route every test listener through the `listenLoopback` retry that `bace2fd` added.
- Make the test launch helper retry a launch whose ready line names an installed port.

issues.title: Finish owned local branch and worktree cleanup with a verified outcome
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A completed delivery removes its eligible owned local branch, worktree and scratch resources, or records why each is retained and who acts next. This applies to ordinary authorized delivery as well as explicit deliver-work.

The existing [cleanup policy](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/9467f90cafe0bdf774eec2d75f66edc9e3bccaaf/docs/sdlc.md#cleanup-after-delivery), delivered through [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/70), already protects exact PR heads, ignored evidence, other owners and tool-managed worktrees. It still prohibits manual delivery-branch deletion and does not consistently require a visible cleanup result.

Owner decision, 2026-09-26: routine delivery may remove its own verified local branch automatically after the cleanup gates pass. Existing accumulated branches require a separately approved candidate list. This issue defines the future rule; planning it does not authorize deleting anything now.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

- Keep the procedure in docs/sdlc.md. Add only a short completion requirement and conditional pointer in AGENTS.md, using writing-for-agents.
- Separate remote and local branch lifecycle. [Hub #309](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/309) owns GitHub automatic deletion and the old remote-branch prune. A missing remote branch does not prove local cleanup or authorize deleting local work.
- After the repository's existing merge, merged-main CI (or applicable documented exception), issue readback and evidence gates, remove the delivery's eligible owned worktree through its designated lifecycle. Remove its local branch only when it still points exactly at the reviewed merged PR head, no worktree or session uses it, and no remaining consumer needs it.
- Establish squash-merge delivery from the merged PR and exact reviewed head, not commit ancestry or git branch --merged. A moved tip is unfinished/unknown work and must be retained.
- Recheck branch identity, expected tip and worktree/ownership state immediately before removal. Use an exact-ref expected-head guard for branch removal; never perform a broad forced branch sweep. Any refusal or changed state retains the resource and records the next action.
- Account for owned scratch, independent temporary clones, review copies and staging directories, including locations outside the registry. Preserve required ignored/private evidence in a surviving private location before cleanup.
- Require a concise cleanup result in existing delivery evidence: removed with readback, retained with reason and owner/next action, or not applicable. A tool exit flow that this session cannot run is retained, not completed.

Required inputs: none; the accepted local-branch policy is specified here. Coordinate shared docs/sdlc.md edits with Hub #309 and sibling cleanup-policy deliveries. The shared-skill checkpoint [agent-skills#83](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/83) and global storage updates [dotfiles#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/dotfiles/issues/4) are related improvements, not required inputs: this repository must enforce its own completion rule without invoking a skill. Remote deletion need not be enabled to verify and clean an eligible local branch.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep other sessions' branches, worktrees and installations untouched. Never force worktree removal, reset, clean or discard files to make cleanup pass. Unknown ownership, locks, dirty state, unreviewed commits, unavailable CI, needed ignored files and active consumers all retain the affected resources. A lack of visible processes is not proof that a session has released a worktree. Failed/abandoned work and the historical backlog keep their separate owner-decision boundary. Source delivery does not install hooks, change live state or contact devices.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: reviewed documentation/instruction PR merged to this repository's main, with required local checks, hosted CI and issue readback. No product behavior delta or invented OpenSpec capability.

1. A completed ordinary delivery and an explicitly invoked deliver-work both produce a cleanup outcome. An eligible squash-merged local branch is removed only after its worktree is gone and the exact-head/ownership checks pass.
2. Read-only simulations cover a moved branch tip, another registered worktree, an active/unknown session, ignored evidence, lock/dirty state, incomplete CI and a remaining installation/publication consumer. Each retains the resource and names the next action.
3. A clean tool-managed worktree uses its exit flow; unavailable flow is reported pending. A standalone clone is discovered through task ownership rather than the Git worktree registry.
4. Source/CI completion and cleanup outcome remain distinct; no claim of removed resources without a current readback. Public receipts do not expose private paths, configurations or runtime metadata.
5. With Node 24, run npm ci, npm run check:workflow and npm run test:workflow from the isolated delivery root; both checks must exit zero and report the actual specification inventory. Preserve all applicable current-head and merged-main CI and independent Standards/Specification reviews. Use this repository's current validation and merge procedure.

## Meaningful deferrals

No retroactive artifact deletion, GitHub setting changes, scheduled cleanup, evidence expiry, runtime/cache cleanup or installation. The existing remote-branch backlog remains Hub #309; a separate approved local-maintenance issue handles old local artifacts. Manual retention with a named next action is the fallback when safe cleanup cannot be established.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-26, against divoom-app-upgrade main 9467f90 and the owner's accepted local-branch policy. Complexity: medium, because Git refs, worktree lifecycles, evidence and consumers interact. Uncertainty: low; the decision and existing retention gates are explicit. Impact: high, because incorrect removal can lose unmerged or private work. Readiness: ready. Shared-file coordination is not a required-input dependency. Reassess on policy/head changes, tool-lifecycle differences, or new cleanup consumers. Planning-session reasoning: unknown.

issues.title: Upgrade and roll back the Pixoo user service with one command under the install contract
issues.body:
> Filed on 2026-09-26 from an owner-requested review of how the hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo runtimes are installed. Publishing it authorizes no implementation, installation or device change.

### Outcome and real setup

The owner, or an agent the owner approves at a checkpoint, upgrades or rolls back the Pixoo user service with one command that implements the hub's [install contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/465). Agents find it through one pointer in `AGENTS.md`.

Setup: one operator; `pixoo-playlist-controller.service` running a `git archive` copy under `~/.local/share/pixoo-playlist-controller-runtime/<sha>/`. Settings come from `~/.config/pixoo-playlist-controller/service.env`.

Today each upgrade:
- is done by hand following #100 and #98 (`git archive` a reviewed SHA, build beside the running copy, back up, edit `ExecStart`, restart);
- keeps its backups under `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/install-backups/`;
- records its revision only in a private `source-receipt.json` and in issue comments.

`docs/local-operations.md` (L120-139) still describes an in-place `git checkout`. #101 duplicated #100 because the install was a manual task, and the installed copy is behind `main` (#113).

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Command.** Add `plan`, `upgrade <sha>`, `rollback [<sha>]` and `status`, run from a clean checkout, following the contract. The command:
   - builds `releases/<sha>/` beside the running service (`npm ci`, `npm run build`, Node 24);
   - takes the installation lock and makes an offline `npm run backup` of the library;
   - switches the `current` link and restarts the unit;
   - waits until `/api/health` reports the target `build.sourceRevision` (#114) and the device reconnects;
   - rolls back automatically on failure;
   - writes the receipt under `~/.local/share/pixoo-playlist-controller-runtime/receipts/` and prunes releases per the contract.
2. **One-time migration.** Move the existing per-SHA copies under `releases/`, add the `current` link, and point the unit's `ExecStart` at it once with `systemd-analyze --user verify` and `daemon-reload`. `service.env` is unchanged.
3. **Procedure document.** Replace the in-place section of `docs/local-operations.md` with the command, what it touches and how to roll back. Correct the stale installed-revision statements in `docs/agent-monitoring.md` (L547-548, L578-580).
4. **Declaration.** Add the contract's declaration to `AGENTS.md`.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One local backend and one serialized operation queue write to the device. A service restart replays startup restore, which can change the display, so the checkpoint names that effect.
- Private media, credentials, device details, databases and runtime state stay outside Git. Originals and referenced renditions are preserved.
- Linger and boot start are unchanged (#356 owns boot start).

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] `plan` changes nothing. `upgrade`, `rollback`, a dirty checkout, a failed build and a failed health check (which must roll back automatically) are covered with fake service control in an isolated state directory (server or scripts tests).
- [ ] Receipts validate against the vendored contracts 1.2.0 schema.
- [ ] At the owner's checkpoint, the migration and one real upgrade to current `main` record a receipt, health reports the target build, and the owner confirms the display. Physical checks beyond that stay separate.

issues.title: Characterize native SSE disconnect during registration and verify reservation release
issues.body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-26 from the #80–#82 final sweep. It holds the investigation until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

Priority: P2 investigation. Establish whether disconnecting a native SSE client while registration awaits catalog or authentication work can retain a feed-local reservation or attempt delivery after the socket closes. Use the simulator, synthetic credentials and disposable state. No runtime regression is claimed.

At `9467f90cafe0bdf774eec2d75f66edc9e3bccaaf`, `apps/server/src/controller-events.ts:27–34` reserves before asynchronous work; `apps/server/src/sse-delivery.ts:18–23` attaches the close listener only at activation. The HTTP security layer has separate early close cleanup. This ordering predates #81 and was deliberately preserved in PR #110. Persistent exhaustion and actual socket behavior have not been reproduced.

### Smallest useful implementation

Not yet defined. First hold catalog/authentication promises, disconnect a real loopback client before activation, then settle or reject the promises. Observe feed-local and global admission separately. Only if a defect is reproduced, specify the smallest cleanup correction and add its regression test. Related: #81 and ADR 0023; no unfinished prerequisite.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

Reserve before asynchronous registration; write SSE headers before publication; preserve authentication, replay cursors, 16 mixed-feed/HEAD streams, 32 requests and existing queue/drain policies. Disconnect cannot stop playback or cause commands. Keep one state owner and one device writer.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. Final criteria are not yet defined. The investigation must record both resolving and rejecting registration, shutdown during registration, repeated early disconnects and whether the local reservation remains occupied. issues.title: Every monitor row is marked uncertain because hook sources never supply ordering evidence
issues.body:
## Observed and expected behavior

Observed on the installed service on 2026-09-25 23:55Z: every monitor row carries the amber `?` uncertainty mark, including Claude Code rows whose activity is `active`, freshness `current` and turn known. The live snapshot showed `evidence.unavailable` with dimension `ordering`, reason `missing` on all ten sessions from all three producers (Codex CLI, Codex Desktop, Claude Code).

`DashboardPager.layout()` in `apps/server/src/agent-dashboard.ts` sets `uncertain` when `s.unavailable.length>0` or `s.ordering.status==='unknown'`. `docs/agent-monitoring.md` records that documented hook fields never establish native event IDs or total ordering, and that unknown ordering is never filled in from arrival order. So no hook-based source can ever produce a row without the mark, and the mark carries no information.

Expected: the `?` mark means something. A row with current freshness, a known turn and a known activity is not marked uncertain merely because ordering is unknown; ordering uncertainty is shown only where it changes what the owner should do, or not at all on the 64x64 frame.

## Reproduction

1. Run the installed service in Monitor with the remote owner, or the simulator with `apps/server/src/dashboard-examples.ts` after adding `unavailable:[{kind:'evidence.unavailable',dimension:'ordering',reason:'missing'}]` and `ordering:{status:'unknown'}` to a current, active session.
2. Read `GET /api/integration/v1/rendition`: `rows[].uncertain` is true for every row.
3. The frame shows `?` at x=56 on every row.

## Scope

Decide which evidence dimensions make a row uncertain on the frame: freshness, connection, activity unknown and parent unknown stay; `ordering` and other dimensions that no supported source can supply do not. Keep the full `unavailable` list in the Monitor tab. Update the row rule, the layout table in `docs/agent-monitoring.md`, the synthetic examples and the frame hashes. Out of scope: hub changes to the ordering contract (Hub #139 owns event history and ordering guarantees).

## Acceptance criteria

- A current, active, known-turn session with only `ordering` unavailable renders without the uncertainty mark.
- A session with stale freshness, unknown activity, an unknown parent or a non-current connection still renders with it.
- The Monitor tab still lists every `unavailable` entry.
- `docs/agent-monitoring.md` names the dimensions that set the mark.

## Verification approach

Unit tests in `tests/unit/agent-dashboard.test.ts` for both cases, updated synthetic frame hashes, `npm run check`.

## Dependencies

Related: #98 (layout redesign shows uncertainty visibly), Hub #139 (ordering guarantees). Neither blocks.

## Delivery target

Source-only. Installing follows #100's pattern.

<!-- bunny-art-planning-20261001:pixoo -->

Part of https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/677. Required first-release outcome.

## Outcome and real setup

Refine the existing generated-art story for B.U.N.N.Y.: accept validated 64×64 stills or short animations, preserve their provenance, and make immutable native rendition IDs available for approved art presentation or explicit library reuse. Generation is owned by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/680; Pixoo continues to own media ingestion, catalog, playback and its one device writer.

## Smallest useful implementation

Extend the existing bounded media/API or integration seam with the smallest qualified generated-art admission path from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678. Reuse original preservation, byte/pixel/frame/duration/profile validation, immutable rendition identity, authenticated reads/commands and reference-safe cleanup. Private temporary staging has bounded retention; saving to the permanent library/favorites is explicit. The accepted art policy may admit ephemeral display assets automatically after validation; it does not enable indiscriminate permanent library imports.

Return stable asset/rendition references and preview/compatibility evidence. Exact-art moment playback integrates with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92 and the qualified handoff; staging alone never plays an asset. Reuse existing catalog and preview work rather than duplicating it: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/96 and Hub https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/353 (preview PR https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/676 is merged; refresh its separate closeout/installation evidence at pickup). Separate staging delivery from unfinished moment consumption.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve originals, referenced renditions, simulator startup, Monitor/Media ownership, playback recovery and existing queue/admission guards. Generated provenance is not an automatic licensing, originality or content-suitability guarantee; replace the old placeholder's unsupported assurance with truthful attribution. No credential/path exposure or direct hardware writes. Permanent library admission and transient presentation remain distinct.

Required inputs: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/679. The linked accepted output, not a closed label alone, is the prerequisite.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: A bounded still and short-animation fixture imports to immutable native media, preserves original bytes and reports the effective 64×64 frames/timing/profile.
  Planned evidence: Existing media/library/API tests plus generated-art cases; an independent preview matches effective pixels.

- [ ] AC2: Invalid signatures, excessive resources, unsupported profiles and unauthorized callers produce zero playback or device commands.
  Planned evidence: Negative ingestion/authentication tests and a command spy; limits reuse the current renderer profile.

- [ ] AC3: Duplicate admission reuses the same result; failed staging and retention cleanup cannot remove originals or referenced/favorited media.
  Planned evidence: Persistence, restart, reference and cleanup tests.

- [ ] AC4: An admitted rendition is consumable by the qualified hub/art integration; admission by itself never shows it.
  Planned evidence: Owning-service integration fixture; exact interlude/current-base restoration belongs to https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/684.

Planned validation (not executed): on the owning Pixoo worktree, Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run check`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, plus the affected controller/Hub consumer checks from its live development guidance. No real device is required for source checks.

Delivery target: source-only; installation and optical acceptance are tracked in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

Planning publication only. Implementation follows the owning repository's live AGENTS.md/SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec, applicable package/consumer tests and CI, independent Standards and Specification review of the same committed comparison, and current UI policy. Any new executable surface must first have documented build/type/test coverage and CI. All tests here are planned, not run. Installation and device contact remain separately authorized through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687.

## Meaningful deferrals

No generator, daily scheduler or new general media store here. Moment playback remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92; physical qualification is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/687 and existing Pixoo device-profile work. Semantic ranking remains Hub https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/530. Higher-resolution desktop assets are https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/685.

## Work assessment

Complexity: medium (bounded interfaces and evidence). Uncertainty: high (Accepted generated-art admission/provenance interface from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/678; refresh the native media profile and active producer/preview work before implementation.). Impact: high (private data, counted external requests or device effects).

Readiness: backlog; dependent source work waits for the named accepted inputs and installed acceptance remains separate.

Alignment: aligned. Inspected Hub main `782f25cb201d60947ec2526bf6cdfb89acc11bbd`, controller contract 1.1, ADRs 0004/0006/0007, app/controller guides and the directly linked live backlog on 2026-10-01 UTC. Main advanced during planning through Pixoo preview PR #676; its merged widget/media interfaces were reread before final publication. Flexible art sizing and runtime themes are owner-selected extensions of earlier fixed-layout/single-skin scope; update their owning specifications during delivery. Reuse existing state/layout/palette/media owners. Search was limited to these art, automation, UI and occupancy seams, including relevant open/closed work and the preview merge.

Scope fit: one operator, existing installation and configured surfaces. Desktop and presence are accepted deferrals with owning children; no extra host, generic job platform or second general memory/scheduler is introduced. Required data/ownership/queue protections remain. Reassess after producer/contract changes, provider findings, owner policy changes, or contradictory installed evidence.

Planning evidence: 2026-10-01 UTC; user decisions in the art grilling session; live linked issues and source reads. Shared policy `agent-skills@bd50cfc896a4db4c188a9f2047c9ff038b03b4be`. issues.title: Disconnect the Pixoo from Divoom's cloud while keeping local control
issues.body:
## Outcome

The owner's Pixoo cannot reach Divoom's cloud, and this app keeps controlling it over the LAN. The device stops fetching the cloud gallery, cloud-fed faces and firmware updates. The owner knows which default-content behavior the disconnect removes and which stays with #76 and #77. Real setup: one Pixoo64 on the home Wi-Fi, one router, one backend on the WSL host.

## Background

Owner intent, September 24, 2026: do everything possible to keep the Pixoo's default content off the display, including cutting the device off from Divoom's cloud.

#76 records what the device does today: after an app-issued screen-on it shows its native random GIFs, and after a power cycle it booted to the Faces channel with a cloud-fed dial. #76 listed blocking the Pixoo's internet at the router and clearing uploads, likes and Custom pages in the Divoom app as owner actions to document. This issue now owns those actions, their verification and their documentation. #76 keeps the app-side screen-on, reboot and idle-display behavior, and #77 the startup restore.

Known cloud dependencies, from #76 and the vendor pages it links: reboot is an MQTT command through Divoom's server, and the uploaded and liked image lists come from `app.divoom-gz.com`. Unknown: the device's full host list, whether it takes time from NTP or from Divoom, how it behaves at boot without the cloud, and whether the native random GIFs are stored on the device. Firmware remains unknown.

The likely limit: the native GIFs after screen-on and at boot probably live on the device, so a network block alone will not remove them. The block removes cloud-fed content and firmware updates. The app's presentation, restored at startup (#77) and after screen-on or reboot (#76), remains what keeps this app's content on the display.

## Scope

Owner steps, in order, each with its own receipt:

1. **Address reservation.** Give the Pixoo a DHCP reservation so the router rule and the app's configured private IPv4 target stay on the same device. If the reserved address differs from the configured target, update the app settings and restart the backend.
2. **Internet block.** In the router, block the Pixoo's internet access and leave LAN traffic allowed. A per-device block is the simplest complete option. A DNS-only block depends on the device resolving every host by name and is a fallback.
3. **Divoom app cleanup.** Clear uploads, likes and Custom pages in the Divoom app before the block, because the phone app may reach the device through the cloud and lose control afterwards.
4. **Verification from the WSL host.** The app's read-only device probe succeeds and an explicit Monitor mode command presents. Then power-cycle the device and record the boot state: channel, face or GIF, any on-screen network indicator, and whether the native GIFs still appear. Watch for a stated window, for example five minutes, for reboots or retry loops.
5. **Documentation.** Local operations describes the owner-only network and Divoom-account actions and their effects, including the re-pairing consequence below. The hardware notes record the observations. This is the source-only part; no application change is planned.

Prerequisites: none. #77 and #76 supply the app-side recovery and can proceed independently.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Local HTTP control on the explicit private IPv4 target, with one backend and one serialized device writer.
- The app never contacts the router, changes firmware or sends requests to any address except the configured target. This issue adds no network or router authority to the app or to agents.
- Wi-Fi provisioning goes through the Divoom app and the cloud. Re-pairing after a factory reset or a Wi-Fi change needs the block lifted temporarily.
- The Divoom phone app may stop controlling the device after the block. The owner accepts that or finishes the cleanup first.
- Device time: the app has no time command today. `Device/SetUTC` and `Sys/TimeZone` are manual alternatives if a clock is ever shown.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Pixoo has a DHCP reservation matching the app's configured target, or the settings were updated to the reserved address and the backend restarted.
- [ ] The router blocks the Pixoo's internet access with LAN allowed. The receipt names the router feature used and the date.
- [ ] With the block in place, the app's read-only probe succeeds from the WSL host and an explicit Monitor mode command presents.
- [ ] After a device power cycle with the block in place, the boot state is recorded, including whether native GIFs still appear and any retry or reboot behavior in the observation window.
- [ ] Local operations covers the owner-only network and Divoom-account actions and their effects. The hardware notes record the observations.
- [ ] Every router, Divoom-account and device power action is owner-performed and separately authorized, with its own receipt.

Evidence: owner receipts for steps 1 to 3, owner observation plus the backend's diagnostics output for step 4, and the documentation diff reviewed against the receipts for step 5. Delivery target: source-only for the documentation. The network and account steps are owner actions, not delivery steps.

## Out of scope and deferrals

- **Native on-device GIFs at boot and after screen-on.** The block probably does not remove them. #77 owns startup restore; #76 owns screen-on, reboot and idle-display behavior.
- **A separate IoT VLAN or DNS sinkhole.** Not needed for one device on one home router. Revisit if the router cannot block a single device.
- **Removing the device from the Divoom account or a factory reset.** Not planned. Both would require re-provisioning through the cloud.
- **Device time.** No application change. Manual `Device/SetUTC` and `Sys/TimeZone` if needed.
- **Firmware changes.** Never performed by agents. Blocking the cloud also freezes firmware, which keeps device behavior stable.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 24, 2026.

Operating assumptions: one owner, one Pixoo64 on home Wi-Fi with a router that can block a single device, one WSL backend, device firmware unknown. Sources: docs/sdlc.md scope defaults, #76 and the hardware validation notes.

- **Complexity: low.** Router configuration and documentation. No code and no new state.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The host list, the device's time source, boot behavior without the cloud and the location of the native GIFs are unknown. Step 4 answers the last two by observation.
- **Impact: low to medium.** Reversible by removing the router rule. The Divoom phone app may lose control of the device, and re-pairing needs the block lifted.

**Readiness:** backlog. Waiting on the owner to schedule the router change and record the receipts. The documentation delivery follows the observed outcome.

Reassess if the router cannot block a single device, if the device misbehaves without the cloud (reboots, retry loops, a persistent network banner), or if firmware turns out to behave differently from the September 24 observations in #76.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Source delivery is documentation only. This issue grants no permission to change router or firewall settings, contact the device, change firmware or edit the Divoom account. Those are owner actions with receipts.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below. The owner performs the router, DHCP and Divoom app steps; the session records receipts and documents the effects.

issues.title: Keep Divoom cloud content off the Pixoo after screen-on and device reboots
issues.body:
## Outcome

The Pixoo shows only this app's content, or a black screen, and never Divoom cloud content, including after a screen-on or a device reboot. Owner actions that cut the device off from Divoom's cloud are documented alongside.

## Background and evidence

Found during [hub #154](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/154) hardware acceptance and a follow-up check on September 24, 2026. The owner wants the Pixoo disconnected from every backend except this one.

**What the app does today:**

- Startup never activates Monitor presentation.
- Screen-off pauses, and screen-on does not resume. See [controller UI](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/controller-ui.md).
- After an app-issued screen off/on, the device shows its native random GIFs. This happened during #154 and matches the earlier "Random GIFs return" note in [hardware validation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/hardware-validation.md).

**What Divoom's local API offers:**

- `Channel/SetIndex` selects 0 Faces, 1 Cloud Channel, 2 Visualizer, 3 Custom or 4 black screen. The same [official page](https://doc.divoom-gz.com/web/#/12?page_id=89) also says "channel id 0~3", so black-screen support may depend on firmware.
- `Channel/GetAllConf` reports `PowerOnChannelId`, described as the channel shown at power-on ([get all setting](https://doc.divoom-gz.com/web/#/12?page_id=243)). No documented command sets it.
- No documented command deletes stored content.
- The device keeps cloud links. Reboot is documented as an MQTT command through Divoom's server ([System reboots](https://doc.divoom-gz.com/web/#/12?page_id=610)), and the uploaded and liked image lists are served from `app.divoom-gz.com`.

**What the device did on September 24, 2026 (firmware unknown):**

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before any change | `SelectIndex` 1 (Cloud), `PowerOnChannelId` 1, `RotationFlag` 0 |
| `Channel/SetIndex` 4, with the app stopped so it was the only writer | `error_code` 0, `SelectIndex` 4. `PowerOnChannelId` still 1 after 10 seconds |
| Unplug and replug | Booted to `SelectIndex` 0 (Faces), face 38 ("YouTube Account", a cloud-fed dial). Brightness reset from 80 to 100. `PowerOnChannelId` still 1 |
| App restarted and an explicit Monitor mode command sent | Presentation active, first frame `sent` |

The black-screen channel therefore does not survive a power cycle, and `PowerOnChannelId` does not predict the boot channel. Only this app, while presenting, keeps Divoom content off the display.

## Scope

- **Screen-on:** an app-issued screen-on resumes Monitor presentation when the saved mode is Monitor. Owner decision, September 24, 2026 (see the decision comment). This reverses the accepted "screen-on does not resume" rule for Monitor mode only. Media playback stays paused after screen-on until explicit resume.
- **Device reboot:** detect a device reboot or an external channel change, for example with a bounded `Channel/GetIndex` probe after reconnect or on an interval. Then restore Monitor presentation when the saved mode is Monitor. Owner decision, September 24, 2026. Use the existing serialized adapter queue with no automatic retry storms, and run it only in device mode. Share the restore path with the startup restore in #77: one rule, three triggers.
- **Idle display:** select the black-screen channel (`Channel/SetIndex` 4) when nothing is presented, meaning Media is stopped and Monitor is inactive, rather than leaving firmware content on screen. Owner decision, September 24, 2026 (see the decision comment). Send it once per idle transition through the serialized queue, device mode only. Black-screen support may depend on firmware; the September 24 observation returned `error_code` 0 and `SelectIndex` 4. A rejected command is recorded and not retried. Define the exact idle predicate in the OpenSpec delta. Screen-off and shutdown behavior are unchanged.
- **Documentation:**
  - Record the observations above in the hardware notes.
  - The owner-only network and Divoom-account actions (router block with LAN allowed, clearing uploads, likes and Custom pages), their verification and their documentation moved to #83 on September 24, 2026.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The owner's decisions on screen-on behavior and reboot recovery are recorded: resume Monitor presentation when the saved mode is Monitor.
- [ ] After an app-issued screen-on with the saved mode Monitor, the display shows Monitor presentation, not firmware content. With the saved mode Media, playback stays paused.
- [ ] After a device power cycle while the app runs with the saved mode Monitor, the app restores Monitor presentation within a stated bound, without an app restart.
- [ ] When Media is stopped and Monitor is inactive, the app selects the black-screen channel once per idle transition through the serialized queue, device mode only. A rejected command is recorded and not retried. Covered by fake-adapter tests.
- [ ] Any new device probe is bounded, serialized through the adapter queue, device-mode only and covered by fake-adapter tests.
- [ ] The hardware notes cover the observations above. The owner-only network and Divoom-account actions are documented under #83.
- [ ] A separately authorized physical check on the owner's Pixoo confirms the three display criteria: screen-on, power cycle and idle.

## Out of scope

Router or firewall changes, firmware changes, factory reset and Divoom account edits are owner actions, tracked and documented under #83. This issue does not perform them.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 24, 2026.

- **Complexity: medium.** Screen, presentation and player state interact with a new recovery path.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Boot behavior and black-screen support vary with firmware, and the boot face appeared to change on its own (from 144 to 38).
- **Impact: medium.** The change affects what the physical display shows. Recovery is an explicit mode command.

**Readiness:** ready. Screen-on, reboot and idle-display decisions recorded September 24, 2026. The physical check on the owner's Pixoo remains separately authorized.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md, including an issue-linked OpenSpec change for the behavior delta. This issue grants no permission to change network settings, contact devices or install software.

issues.title: Fix rapid extra GIF flashes before the next still image
issues.body:
## Observed and expected behavior

During physical acceptance for #12 on September 8, 2026, the owner observed three normal red 1 / green 2 cycles, followed by several rapid extra cycles before the blue 30 still appeared. The rapid burst repeated in one separately authorized traced run. Expected behavior is the requested normal cadence followed by the still, without the rapid extra flashing.

The owner accepted this as a known defect and explicitly said it must not block continuing #12. Preserve the failed observation in acceptance evidence. This issue tracks investigation and correction; it does not claim a firmware cause or a completed fix.

## Reproduction

1. With separately authorized access to a Pixoo64, run one device-mode application backend using the normal target lock and an isolated synthetic library.
2. Use application source `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`, Node 24.20.0 and profile `pixoo64-smoke-2026-09-06`. Firmware was unknown. The observed session used the configured HTTP proxy.
3. Play a two-frame 64x64 GIF with red 1 and green 2, each delayed 500 ms, using a three-total-plays policy. Follow it with a blue 30 still with a 30-second duration, repeat off.
4. Observe the transition after the three normal cycles. The owner reported rapid extra flashes before the still on both runs. Their duration has not been visually measured.

The traced repeat sent exactly five requests: `Draw/GetHttpGifId`, two `Draw/SendHttpGif` frames, another ID query, then one still frame. The GIF used returned ID 6 and the still ID 7. Every frame used `PicSpeed:500` and the expected rendered RGB hash. All responses reported `error_code:0`; no retries or rejected requests occurred. The second ID query began 3004.108 ms after the last GIF response. The ID query plus still upload took 205.987 ms, including tracing and HTTP completion. These are request timings, not visible-burst measurements.

A local full-application fixture likewise sent the expected five requests. No duplicate application upload, changed requested speed or reused animation ID explains the traced run. The display's internal behavior remains unknown.

## Scope

Diagnose and correct the rapid flashing during the two-frame GIF to one-frame still handoff. Preserve the serialized writer, fresh-intent recovery, immutable media and truthful timing estimates. Assess any protocol/profile change against physical evidence before implementation. Do not assume that resetting IDs, changing firmware or adding arbitrary delays is a valid fix.

Broader transition improvements remain in #16. This is a specific reproduced defect, not a duplicate of that exploratory enhancement. Private device addresses, runtime libraries and raw receipts stay outside Git.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the reported burst with separately authorized physical observation and identify its cause or document an evidence-supported device limitation.
- [ ] If a supported correction exists, implement it with a meaningful regression check covering the identified cause and adjacent handoffs.
- [ ] Observe one-, three- and five-play sequences followed by the still without the rapid burst after the correction; report visible timing separately from HTTP success and state timing.
- [ ] Preserve cancellation, one-writer ownership, supported frame delays and failure handling; pass required source checks and independent reviews.
- [ ] Update dated hardware evidence with source revision, observed results and remaining limitations. If no supported fix exists, obtain an explicit disposition instead of claiming a pass.

## Verification approach

Use the synthetic reproduction and a bounded request trace. Pair software checks with owner-observed physical transitions. Any further physical session needs its own applicable authorization. Issue creation authorizes no display changes or firmware/network changes.

## Dependencies and priority

Found during #12; related to #16. This defect is backlog work and is explicitly nonblocking for #12 under the owner's September 8 decision. No prerequisite implementation issue is currently identified. Reassess scope and the causal evidence before marking ready.

## Delivery target

Source plus separately authorized physical-device verification.


## Further owner observation, September 8, 2026

During the approved #12 soak, the owner clarified that blue 30 briefly interleaves with the red 1 / green 2 frames before the display settles on solid blue 30. The two items retain 30-second duration policies and the GIF uses two 500 ms frames. This describes the recurring accepted transition burst; no root cause or correction is established.

Two subsequent owner stopwatch readings, from solid blue appearance until the numbered GIF replaced it, were 30.3 seconds each. An earlier approximate reading was 28 seconds. Preserve all three readings and their human measurement limits. These visible readings are separate from backend SSE dwell measurements.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

issues.title: Connect ChatGPT to the local MCP server through a private tunnel
issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Keep remote connectivity deferred. Reuse [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7) through a qualified Pixoo-local endpoint or explicitly selected hub gateway. Document the deployment before implementation. A tunnel is not needed for local hooks, monitoring or the unified local UI.

## Outcome
Connect ChatGPT web to the local Pixoo application's MCP tools through an authenticated private connection.

## Scope and source
Refine the existing remote-control backlog issue for the requested ChatGPT integration. Reuse the MCP endpoint from #24 and its shared application services. Prefer OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel, with a client running beside the local backend and reaching OpenAI through outbound HTTPS. The local app and Pixoo remain private.

This is follow-on work outside the mixed-playlist MVP. #11 continues to own authenticated browser LAN access; [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) owns remote browser acceptance and #12 owns local physical playback/soak. Neither a LAN listener nor completion of physical soak testing is required to develop this outbound MCP path. Public plugin distribution, general remote browser control, and other VPN/hosting options remain outside this implementation slice.

Official documentation checked September 6, 2026: [Secure MCP Tunnel](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels), [ChatGPT developer mode](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode), and [MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp). Recheck these sources when implementation starts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Resolve the connection/authentication design before marking ready. Document target ChatGPT developer-mode availability, Platform tunnel permissions and organization/workspace association, runtime credential handling, and how the tunnel authenticates to the local MCP endpoint. If the supported route is unavailable, record the exact missing prerequisite and proposed alternative for user decision.
- [ ] Provide the source/configuration templates and runbook needed to connect a developer-mode app to the running backend through the selected private tunnel. Reuse the same MCP tools and backend queue as Codex; the bridge never talks directly to the Pixoo or launches another device-writing backend.
- [ ] Preserve loopback defaults and require an explicitly configured endpoint and credentials. Expose only the intended MCP path through the tunnel, not the rest of the web server or private media directory. Verify the bridge can authenticate locally without weakening the local MCP access checks.
- [ ] Define and test authorization at both the remote connection and local app boundary. Keep runtime keys, local credentials, private IPs, and media paths out of Git, URLs, tool results, and routine logs. Treat read-only/write annotations as client guidance, with server authorization enforced independently.
- [ ] Document start, health/readiness checks, failure diagnosis, credential rotation/revocation, disconnect, and cleanup. A stopped or revoked tunnel rejects new remote work; local app use continues. Reconnect must not blindly replay uncertain writes.
- [ ] Document that the host/backend/tunnel must remain running for ChatGPT calls. Client disconnection does not own or stop playback. Keep app deployment and persistent host startup aligned with #10 without adding an always-on installation to source delivery.
- [ ] Provide a simulator-only end-to-end runbook for tool discovery, approved writes, failures, and disconnect/reconnect. Actual ChatGPT account setup and live client/device evidence are completed in [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44), with unavailable access recorded there rather than claimed from mocks.
- [ ] Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec proposal, affected capability deltas, tasks, design, and ADR for the transport/auth boundary before implementation. Do not add public ingress or change router/firewall settings as an automatic fallback.

Planned OpenSpec change: `gh-17-chatgpt-private-mcp`.

## Verification approach
Use isolated test credentials, a local MCP test server/client, and a fake tunnel transport where practical to verify target restriction, authentication, disconnects, revocation, and duplicate-request behavior. Separate tests of our wrapper/configuration from claims about the external tunnel service. Source tests must pass without external accounts or a device.

Run Node 24 `npm ci` and all repository checks applicable to changed source, HTTP/startup behavior, and OpenSpec artifacts, including `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` for application changes. Require all configured PR/main CI. Live ChatGPT setup and acceptance belong to [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44).

## Dependencies
- #24 for the authenticated local MCP endpoint.
- Verified target account/workspace permissions and a settled transport/auth design before readiness.

Additional shared prerequisites:
- [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7)

## Related work
#25 adds media/playlist tools and can proceed independently of this connection work. #10 supplies shared deployment guidance when available; this issue owns tunnel-specific lifecycle instructions. [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44) owns remote client/device verification and depends on this issue. Source-only. Account registration, key creation, tunnel installation, personal app configuration, and hardware actions require the later explicitly authorized setup/acceptance work.

issues.title: Let hub routines play a playlist or one rendition only while the Pixoo is in Media mode
issues.body:
## Outcome

A B.U.N.N.Y. routine can start a saved playlist or show one rendition on the Pixoo, and it does so only while the Pixoo is in Media mode. A routine that arrives during Monitor mode is rejected with a typed receipt and never switches the display away from agent status.

## Why

The owner wants to schedule routines throughout the day and week from B.U.N.N.Y., for example "every evening at five, play this playlist" or "show this GIF", and those routines must not run while the Pixoo is in Monitor mode (owner direction, 2026-09-25). Scheduling, routines, timezone and DST handling and the editor belong in the hub (jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#45). The Pixoo only needs to act on commands and to make the mode rule atomic.

Today a `media.start` from the hub selects Media through the same service as the browser, so a scheduled playlist would displace agent status. The hub can read the mode from the integration snapshot before sending, but only the Pixoo can check the mode and admit the command in one step. Controller v1 also has no rendition-selection command; only the browser and the local MCP `show_media` tool can show one rendition.

This story replaces the original "timezone-aware playlist schedules" placeholder from the September 5 handoff, section 12. That scope now lives in the hub.

## Scope

1. **Mode precondition.** An additive optional field on the shared controller command envelope, for example `requireMode: "media"`, honored by `media.start` and `media.control`. When the current mode is not the required one, the command is rejected before admission with a typed conflict receipt, reusing the existing receipt taxonomy. No device write, no mode change, no queuing or deferral. A command without the field behaves exactly as today.
2. **Show one rendition.** A command on the Pixoo integration extension that shows a single rendition by id with an optional playback policy, using the same show-media service and temporary-session semantics as the local MCP tool. It honors the same mode precondition. Rendition ids come from the catalog discovery in #96, so this part depends on #96.
3. Contract minor versions for both, an issue-linked OpenSpec delta, and a linked hub PR updating the pinned fixtures and compatibility record.

## Out of scope

- Schedules, routines, timezone, DST and missed-firing policy: jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#45.
- Previews and catalog discovery: #96 and jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#353.
- Coordinated scenes and desk presets: jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#267 and #67.
- Any change to Monitor/Media ownership rules in ADR 0018, the uncertainty pause in ADR 0012, or startup restore from #84.

## Behavior to preserve

- One backend, one serialized adapter queue, one writer. Native, browser and MCP commands keep one shared epoch and sequence.
- A manual command remains just a command. A later routine overrides it at its scheduled time; there is no suspension logic on the Pixoo side.
- A player paused on uncertainty is never resumed by a routine. The existing conflict rejection covers it; the routine fails with a receipt.
- Screen-off pauses and screen-on does not resume media, unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** `media.start` and `media.control` without the precondition field behave exactly as today; existing hub fixtures pass unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2.** With the field and Media active, the command is applied normally and the receipt is unchanged in shape.
- [ ] **AC3.** With the field and Monitor active, the command is rejected before admission: no adapter operation, no mode change, a typed conflict receipt, and the command ledger records the rejection.
- [ ] **AC4.** Race coverage: a mode change admitted immediately before the command still yields a rejection or a clean apply, never a partial apply, in simulator and device modes.
- [ ] **AC5.** The show-rendition command shows the rendition through the existing show-media service, restores paused like the MCP tool, honors the precondition, and rejects an unknown or unreferenced rendition id with a typed failure.
- [ ] **AC6.** A player paused on uncertainty rejects both commands without resuming.
- [ ] **AC7.** Contract minor versions recorded, OpenSpec delta archived, `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass, and a linked hub PR updates the pinned fixtures and compatibility record.

## Dependencies

- #96 for rendition discovery (part 2 only). Part 1 has no open dependency.
- jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#45 consumes this; jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#353 makes rendition ids visible to the operator.
- #12 is closed and no longer blocks this.

## Verification approach

Route and service tests with the fake adapter for admission, rejection, race and zero-write cases. Existing browser suite for regression. Repository CI on the PR head and merged revision. No hardware or installation side effects are authorized by this story.

## Delivery target

Source-only.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against `main` at 5004b35.

- **Complexity: low.** One optional envelope field checked at admission, one command that wraps an existing service.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Mode is already tracked by the presentation service and reported in the extension snapshot.
- **Impact: low to medium.** A wrong admission could displace Monitor mode; the tests in AC3 and AC4 bound that.

**Readiness:** part 1 is ready now. Part 2 waits for #96. Deliver together once #96 merges, or split part 1 out if hub #45 becomes ready first.

## Guide

**Topic:** pixoo-media
**Note:** Media-mode precondition on hub media commands, plus show-one-rendition, so B.U.N.N.Y. routines never displace agent status.

issues.title: Drain a paired verification feed before aggregate reset
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Hub's composed disposable preview must reset its one synthetic state owner while consumer pages remain responsive. Hub #557 cannot safely reseed the owner while this consumer is still polling. This source-only prerequisite supplies the consumer-owned pause boundary required by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/557. It preserves the repository split required by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/490.

## Smallest useful implementation

Add a private, per-run feed-pause control only to the `hub-paired` verification launch. The composition writes a bounded versioned request with run identity and a fresh nonce in the run's existing private runtime directory. The running consumer stops admitting Hub requests, drains those already in flight, then writes an atomic mode-0600 acknowledgment with the same run/nonce and its process identity. The pages, health route and controller remain responsive.

The request stays active while Hub reseeds its owner. Only after that succeeds, the composition authorizes this consumer's reseed with the matching nonce. The adapter consumes that authorization in seed after the old unit has stopped and fresh state has been written, before the replacement launches. Its fresh source can then poll the reset owner and pass readiness. An unrelated reseed must not silently release an outstanding pause. Missing, stale or malformed control state produces a fixed actionable failure rather than an acknowledgment.

The protocol is verification-only: no new public controller or shared core API, installed setting, service or agent-state owner. Hub owns orchestration, validation of process identity, partial failure reporting, manifest pin updates and complete aggregate qualification in #557. These files are private controls, never captured proof or browser output.


Implementation seam: the remote monitor source is shared by its timer, browser reads and remote commands. Gate all Hub requests at that source, supply the gate only through the simulator verification launcher/guard, and preserve ordinary source behavior when absent. Update the source seam, verification adapter/environment, focused tests and the owning verification guide/specification.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve the existing simulator/no-device boundary, credential confinement, one selected state owner, request identities, no automatic command replay, normal startup behavior, ports, token files and retained frozen proof. Timer-driven and read-triggered requests must obey the same pause boundary. Device/controller reads continue to answer. A paused browser read reports retained state with truthful freshness and never initiates a new Hub request. Stop remains available at every phase.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Hold a Hub read in flight: acknowledgment waits until it finishes; after acknowledgment, timer and browser/controller activity issue no further Hub requests while pages remain responsive.
- Reject stale nonce/run/process acknowledgments and malformed or linked control files. The control directory is enabled only by an explicit disposable paired launch, never inherited into ordinary startup.
- Reseed after matching release authorization: old process stops before authorization is consumed, token files and ports persist, a fresh lower owner revision becomes current, and frozen proof bytes are unchanged. A reseed without release authorization fails closed.
- Removing an unused pause request resumes the still-running paired consumer without replaying commands. Partial failure remains stoppable.
- Run the repository's full applicable source/browser/workflow checks and focused real-user-systemd adapter qualification. Keep source, installed runtime and device acceptance separate. Delivery target: source-only PR, independent Standards/Specification reviews, all PR and merged-main CI.

## Meaningful deferrals

Aggregate reset and its complete real-consumer evidence remain Hub #557, which will pin this merged revision. Installed pause controls, physical-device behavior and a general distributed coordination service are outside this disposable-preview requirement. Existing unrelated verification follow-ups retain their own scope.

## Work assessment

One operator on the existing Linux/WSL verification host, with disposable state and synthetic transport. Complexity medium; uncertainty medium until drain and reseed negative controls pass; impact medium because incorrect timing can leave the preview stale. The required interface is a bounded prerequisite of the already accepted aggregate reset, with no change to its consumers-stay-up criterion.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: implement the bounded private feed pause and authorized reseed boundary with Sol at high reasoning, then independent Standards and Specification review. This active batch uses the owner-requested Astra/xhigh coordinator and read-only consumer proposals.
**Work surface:** Backend

issues.title: Close three small verification transport guard edges
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The simulator verification transport guard from [#118](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118) (PR #121) guards public Node.js API use by the app and its dependencies. The final PR #121 reviews left three small edges, none of which the served app reaches today.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Writable `process.execPath`:** a fork falls back to `process.execPath`, which code can overwrite with another program. Capture `process.execPath` when the guard loads, and compare `options.execPath || process.execPath` against the captured value, or always pass the captured value. (Review P-S6.)
- **Empty `execPath`:** `execPath: ''` or `null` is refused, but Node treats a falsy value as `process.execPath`. The same normalization fixes this. (Review R4-S2; it currently fails closed.)
- **`data:` URL workers:** a `data:` URL worker's `worker` record stores the URL-encoded source in the private runtime transport log. Record `<data-url>`, or only the scheme, for any worker URL that is not `file:`. (Reviews R4-S1 and P-S7.)

## Behavior to preserve

- Guarded forks of Node.
- Symlinked Node binaries allowed.
- File-based workers guarded.
- Every refusal recorded by name only.

## Observable acceptance

outcome.heading: Outcome and real setup
outcome.text: The simulator verification transport guard from [#118](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118) (PR #121) guards public Node.js API use by the app and its dependencies. The final PR #121 reviews left three small edges, none of which the served app reaches today.

implementation.heading: Smallest useful implementation
implementation.text:
- **Writable `process.execPath`:** a fork falls back to `process.execPath`, which code can overwrite with another program. Capture `process.execPath` when the guard loads, and compare `options.execPath || process.execPath` against the captured value, or always pass the captured value. (Review P-S6.)
- **Empty `execPath`:** `execPath: ''` or `null` is refused, but Node treats a falsy value as `process.execPath`. The same normalization fixes this. (Review R4-S2; it currently fails closed.)
- **`data:` URL workers:** a `data:` URL worker's `worker` record stores the URL-encoded source in the private runtime transport log. Record `<data-url>`, or only the scheme, for any worker URL that is not `file:`. (Reviews R4-S1 and P-S7.)

issues.title: Add a hub-paired Pixoo verification scenario for the integrated preview
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The integrated verification preview in [Hub #495](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/495) pairs one disposable Pixoo run with one disposable Hub run. Pixoo must then act as a real Hub consumer: it serves its controller API to the Hub and reads the Hub's session feed as a `remote` owner. Today's simulator verification run from [#118](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118) seeds its own embedded owner and keeps the controller API off. Its transport guard allows only the run's own port.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

Add a `hub-paired` scenario to the simulator verification adapter:

- **Seed.** Write a `mode: remote` monitor configuration: the Hub owner id, plus the paired Hub feed URL as a non-secret run input through core `@jimmie-potts/app-verify` 1.1 `--input`. Register the Hub's controller credential from a run-supplied token file. Skip the embedded session seed.
- **Launch.** Add `PIXOO_CONTROLLER_ENABLED=1` and `APP_VERIFY_PAIRED_PORTS=<Hub port>`. The guard already refuses an installed port there.
- **Guard check.** `no-physical-transport` accepts `paired` connections only in this scenario and only to the declared port. It still fails on any blocked or other attempt.
- **Checks and steps.** Add a doctor check that the remote feed is current and its revision matches, plus one capture step.

Dependencies:

- Required: #118 merged, and app-verify 1.1 released under Hub #495.
- Hub #495 consumes this change.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Simulator mode is enforced, and no physical transport is used.
- A private data root.
- One agent-state owner: the Hub.
- The standalone scenarios and their guard proof are unchanged.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- In a paired run the Hub's controller calls reach Pixoo's real controller API.
- The Pixoo Monitor shows Hub-fed sessions.
- The transport log shows only the paired port as allowed.
- A negative control fails: a connect to an installed port, or a device request, is refused and fails the check.
- Source finish line. Adapter tests and a local paired run, with Hub #495 owning the integrated evidence.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Media and playback commands from the Hub beyond one representative command.
- Moments and interludes (#92).
- Restarting one consumer while the pairing continues.

issues.title: Add a Pixoo simulator verification adapter with media and Monitor proof
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

An agent starts the real Pixoo application/server in explicit simulator mode with synthetic media, drives library/playlist/playback and Monitor/Media behavior, captures proof and leaves a disposable preview.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488
Phase: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/490

## Smallest useful implementation and dependencies

- Wrap the existing simulator/browser entrypoints with the accepted interface. Force simulator transport explicitly: an inherited `PIXOO_MODE` must never select a real device.
- Use an explicit private `PIXOO_DATA_DIR` outside all Git checkouts, including symlink aliases, and an ephemeral loopback port. Never fall back to the owner's normal data directory or personal media library.
- Seed small synthetic image/animation assets, playlists and monitoring transitions. Preserve simulator startup, originals/renditions, playback recovery and explicit Monitor/Media semantics.
- Add a compact feature map for library, playlist, playback, 64×64 rendering and Monitor/Media, with deterministic actions and expected observations.
- Implement capture, separate/reset handoff, extend, stop, expiry and restart while retaining proof outside disposable worktrees.

Required source prerequisites (native blocked-by links; independent investigation/preparation may proceed):

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/493

[Catalog previews #96](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/96) remains separate product integration work. Coordinate retained-preview cleanup with [#117](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/117).

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Start under an ambient physical-mode setting and prove that the created run remains simulator-only with no physical transport requests.
- [ ] Reject unsafe data roots/aliases and occupied or unrelated resources; never mutate normal installed state.
- [ ] Drive actual browser/server behavior through synthetic library selection, playlist progression, playback controls and Monitor/Media transitions, including recovery from an injected failure without stale replay.
- [ ] Save an inspectable 64×64 result, browser screenshot and short interaction video with candidate/scenario identity. Simulator rendering is labelled as such.
- [ ] Concurrent runs, reset, failed startup, stop, extension and expiry affect only their own processes/state. Artifacts survive cleanup and are not overwritten by manual exploration.
- [ ] A relevant known transition/rendering failure is detected and the reference passes. Feature map and fixtures remain consistent with the tested behavior.
- [ ] Product UI changes retain current-candidate human approval; https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497 owns actual Windows-host access.

## Assessment and next action

Complexity: medium; uncertainty: medium for transport-mode enforcement and media fixtures; impact: medium. Source implementation depends on https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/493; repo inspection can proceed independently.

## Validation and finish line

Finish line: merged adapter and isolated simulator/browser evidence. Follow current Pixoo AGENTS/SDLC, `npm run check`, `npm run test:browser` and affected contract-consumer checks. Check transport isolation as executable behavior, not solely an environment string assertion.

## Meaningful deferrals

No physical Pixoo IP, upload, personal media scan, installed-app restart or new catalog/product feature. Visible-device animation acceptance needs separate named-target authority.

## Delivery boundary

This is planned work, not completed verification. Issue creation authorizes no implementation or launch. During later authorized source delivery, follow the owning repository's current instructions, preserve unrelated work, obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, require applicable current-head CI, use the guarded merge procedure and verify merged-main checks before source closure. Required UI approval remains separate from optional hands-on use.

The installed Pixoo monitor names each session by what it is working on. ### Why

On 2026-09-25 the installed monitor showed 44 sessions, none with a label, so every card read like `…F-B214-CF114BD23343`. The rule behind that has no recorded reason, and the owner retired it (jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#424). The Pixoo copies of the rule are:

issues.title: Redesign the Pixoo monitor layout for readability and motion
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

The installed Pixoo (device mode, user service, Monitor selected) shows agent sessions in a layout a person can read from across the room, with visible motion, instead of a dense grid of letter codes. The simulator preview shows the same bytes. Excluded: alert interruptions and moments (#92), the identifier fallback rule (#87), page cadence changes.

## Problem

The current 64x64 layout (`apps/server/src/dashboard-pixels.ts`, documented in `docs/agent-monitoring.md`) packs four sessions per page in a 3x5 font. Each row is a run of single-letter codes: provider `C`/`L`, activity `>`/`=`/`X`/`]`/`?`, attention `A`/`!`/`?`, a six-character label, a child count and two amber flags. On the installed service on September 25, 2026, every row read `C? 01A0D+ +0? ?T`. The codes need a legend, the label budget is too small to be useful, and the only change over time is the page number every ten seconds.

## Smallest useful implementation

One session per screen, cycling, instead of four rows. Proposed layout, to be refined in the preview before code changes:

- **Label** in a larger font over up to two lines, with room for roughly ten characters per line. Full labels stay in the Monitor tab. The shared `apps/server/src/pixel-font.ts` from #89 and the now-playing card's wrapping rules are the starting point.
- **Provider and state as icons and color**, not letters: a provider mark, a state color (active, idle, attention, ended, unknown) and a distinct attention badge.
- **An activity bar** that pulses while the session is active and holds still when idle, giving motion without hiding information.
- **A summary strip** at the bottom: total sessions, sessions needing attention, and page dots instead of `4/5`. Connection and collector health stay visible as a small indicator.
- **Attention-first ordering** is preserved, and sessions with attention may blink slowly.
- **Empty and uncertain states** stay explicit: an empty view shows the summary strip; an uncertain row shows its uncertainty visibly rather than as a trailing `?`.

Steps: sketch two or three candidate layouts in `docs/examples/agent-dashboard.html` through `scripts/dashboard-preview.mjs` and pick one with the owner; replace the row renderer with the chosen layout; keep the `DashboardPager` sort, filter and paging contracts, with rows-per-page set to one; update the layout table and legend in `docs/agent-monitoring.md`, `apps/server/src/dashboard-examples.ts`, the frame hashes in `tests/unit/agent-dashboard.test.ts` and the qualification fixtures in `packages/device/src/dashboard-fixtures.ts`. Choose the identifier width once so #87 and this layout agree. Prerequisite: none; #87 is related.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

The 64x64 complete RGB upload, coalescing and the minimum cadence from ADR 0015 and ADR 0018; the single writer and generation guards; the Monitor tab preview as the same RGB bytes, nearest-neighbor scaled; the now-playing card precedence from ADR 0019. Motion within one screen is delivered as a multi-frame upload at the adapter's supported timing where the device profile allows it, or as successive frames at the configured cadence otherwise; record which of those the qualification evidence supports.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- The chosen layout is recorded in the preview HTML and `docs/agent-monitoring.md` with a legend that fits in one short table.
- Synthetic scenarios (attention first, overflow, stale source, empty) render deterministically with updated hashes, and every state in the legend appears in at least one scenario.
- The Monitor tab preview and the device rendition remain byte-identical for the same layout.
- Browser tests for the Monitor tab pass, and `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass.
- Physical readability on the Pixoo64 needs an explicit request and an owner, and is reported separately.

## Meaningful deferrals

Alert interruptions and moments: #92 and Hub #358. Identifier fallback: #87. Stale rows: Hub #241 and Hub #332 reduce them but are not required.

## Guide

**Topic:** shared-codex
**Note:** One session per screen with icons, a pulsing activity bar and a summary strip, replacing the four-row letter grid.
