issues.title: Amend ADR 0018 to allow opt-in alert interruptions on the Pixoo display
issues.body:
## Outcome

Let the user opt in to short display interruptions on the Pixoo for chosen events, such as a task completing, an approval request or a new email, and have the display return to whatever owned it before. Amend ADR 0018 so this is an explicit, user-configured policy rather than a rejected alternative.

## Background

ADR 0018 (`docs/decisions/0018-monitor-display-ownership.md`) states that automatic attention takeover would violate Media intent, and the `agent-monitor-controls` specification requires that unsolicited events never take over Media. Both restate an acceptance criterion from #33. That criterion was scoped to the first Monitor mode delivery. It was not a product decision that the screen must stay quiet for every event.

Hub ADR 0004 already names alert interruption per device, preserving mode intent and restoring prior presentation, as product direction ([Hub #40](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/40), [Hub #45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45)). This issue defines the Pixoo side of that policy.

## Decision to record

Amend ADR 0018 in the same form as the #77 amendment. Keep:

- one backend, one adapter, one serialized operation queue
- explicit Monitor and Media modes selected only by user commands
- generation guards, coalescing, no automatic retry and no replay
- raw hook events never change the mode on their own

Add an **alert interruption** as a third, transient presentation:

- An alert is a bounded animation or picture with a maximum duration, played through Player's sole adapter under its own generation.
- Alerts run only when the user has enabled an alert policy. The policy names the event kinds, which modes may be interrupted (Monitor, Media, both or neither), a cooldown, and whether screen-off suppresses alerts.
- When an alert ends, is cancelled by an explicit command, or fails, the backend restores the prior owner: the current Monitor rendition, or paused Media context resumed only if it was playing before the alert.
- Alerts coalesce. A burst of events yields one alert per cooldown; missed alerts are not replayed.
- An alert never acknowledges a notice, marks chat read, approves work or changes a tracker.
- Simulator mode renders alerts to the preview only.

## Scope

- Amend ADR 0018 and the `agent-monitor-controls` spec; add the alert scenarios to OpenSpec.
- Add persisted alert policy to `agent-monitor/presentation.json` (new version) with atomic replacement and startup validation.
- Add a bounded alert operation to the Pixoo integration extension so the hub can trigger an alert with a named kind and optional label, under the existing request identity and revision guards.
- Add a browser control to enable, configure and test the alert policy, and a preview of the alert animation.
- Ship a small built-in animation set (task complete, attention needed, message arrived) rendered as multi-frame uploads at the adapter's supported timing.

Event sources other than agent lifecycle, such as email, are hub work; see [Hub #352](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/352). Pixoo receives an alert command, it does not poll mail.

## Dependencies

- #87 so an alert can name the task it is about.
- [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) and [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253) so stale sessions do not fire alerts.
- [Hub #352](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/352) for the email event source and per-device alert routing.

## Acceptance

- ADR 0018 carries the amendment with the date and owner decision; the spec's "Attention while Media owns the display" scenario is updated to distinguish an enabled alert policy from raw events.
- With the policy disabled, behavior is unchanged and existing presentation tests pass.
- With the policy enabled for Media, a triggered alert plays, then playback resumes from its captured context; with it enabled for Monitor, the current rendition returns after the alert.
- A mode command during an alert cancels it and wins; a late alert completion cannot reclaim the display.
- Screen-off, restart and shutdown retire pending alerts; no alert replays after restart.
- `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass. Physical acceptance follows the device profile and is reported separately.

issues.title: Expose the media catalog, playlist items and previews through the Pixoo integration extension
issues.body:
## Outcome

B.U.N.N.Y. can browse the local Pixoo application's media catalog and saved playlists, inspect ordered playlist items and playback policies, and preview complete 64×64 renditions with their effective frame timings. Reads do not change playback or the display. Preview availability and compatibility with the configured device profile are separate facts.

## Why and media ownership

Owner direction, 2026-09-25: preview GIFs and playlists in B.U.N.N.Y. and use their identities when authoring routines. Owner follow-up, 2026-09-30: proceed with the drift-review recommendations and support useful animated GIFs beyond the two-frame, uniform-500-ms smoke profile.

The source is media imported into the existing local Pixoo application: PNG, JPEG and GIF uploads. The application preserves originals and renders immutable 64×64 frames. This story supplies no stock collection, cloud gallery, GIF-provider search or generated artwork. Public-provider staging remains #94 and generated art remains #93.

Pixoo retains its private `PIXOO_DATA_DIR`: catalog and playlists in `library/catalog.sqlite`, byte-identical originals in `library/media/originals/<content-hash>`, and manifests/RGB/PNG frames in `library/media/renditions/<rendition-id>/`. The Hub reads the owning API; it neither opens that database nor creates a second authoritative media library.

Controller v1 exposes playlist IDs and declares preview unavailable. The strict `pixoo-integration/1.0` snapshot has no catalog. Extend it compatibly for the consumer in jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#353. This story absorbs #67's undelivered catalog/name work, with its old filename exclusion superseded by Hub #424/#426 and ADR 0005.

## Scope

- Advertise a new compatible minor version of the Pixoo integration extension with explicit consumer negotiation. Existing 1.0 consumers receive unchanged 1.0 snapshots. Keep lists and frame bytes outside snapshots.
- Add catalog capability and `catalogRevision` to the negotiated snapshot. Also expose the minimal nullable current-media identity and playlist position needed by Hub #353's now-showing widget, from existing player state. Keep desired/current/last-sent/uncertain meanings explicit; never label a successful read or upload as observed physical output.
- Read routes under `/controller/pixoo-integration/v1/`:
  - `catalog/renditions`: rendition and asset identities, display name when available, source format, effective frame count/duration, and compatibility with the configured playback profile. Compatibility does not certify visible device behavior.
  - `catalog/playlists` and `catalog/playlists/:id`: saved playlist identity/name/revision, repeat/shuffle, and ordered item identities with `renditionId` and duration-ms or total-plays policy. Reuse existing per-playlist item bounds.
  - Page list routes with `limit` 1–100, default 25, nonnegative safe-integer `offset`, and `total`. Preserve controller v1's existing 100-ID discovery behavior; do not impose a new 100-playlist storage limit.
  - `renditions/:id/preview.png`: the first effective frame.
  - `renditions/:id/preview.json`: an immutable, bounded manifest of the effective frame count, ordered indexes and delays, dimensions, duration and existing timing warnings. Stills retain null frame delay/duration where playlist policy supplies timing.
  - `renditions/:id/frames/:index.png`: the corresponding cached effective frame, pixel-identical to the existing browser route. The client animates these frames using the manifest. No original-file decode or palette quantization occurs on reads.
- This frame sequence replaces the proposed `preview.gif` encoding. A GIF file is limited to palette-based colors and cannot promise pixel identity for all existing RGB renditions. GIF input and animated previews remain supported; a downloadable GIF export is not required here.
- Expose existing useful media titles and filenames under the owner-approved policy, with explicit owner labels taking precedence when available. Reuse Pixoo's current name validation and 120-character bound, including its counting semantics; do not tighten browser/MCP/library input to 80 or truncate stored names. Missing names use neutral ID fallbacks. Credentials, tokens, secrets and raw storage locations remain excluded; no arbitrary filesystem access is introduced.
- Use immutable rendition IDs to bind previews to items. JSON catalog reads report `catalogRevision`; increment it on catalog membership, display-name, playlist or item changes. A client that observes different revisions refreshes the affected view. Specify/read-test the consistency check in the issue-linked contract; do not promise an atomic snapshot across unrelated HTTP requests. Immutable frame identity stays valid across unrelated catalog edits.
- Give each immutable preview representation a strong ETag identifying its actual bytes, plus long-lived cache headers and matching `If-None-Match` handling. Frame/format variants must not share an incorrect validator. Check current authorization and catalog membership before returning bytes or 304; unknown or no-longer-cataloged renditions return 404. A rendition need not belong to a playlist to be previewable.
- Require read scope using existing authorization rules. No preview/list read reserves a command ticket, changes the command ledger or touches the device adapter queue. Bound queued work, frame reads and request duration with existing safeguards and typed failures.
- Support every cataloged rendition admitted by the application resource profile, including more than two frames and nonuniform delays. The historical device smoke profile is not a preview limit. #55 owns separating device-mode import from playback qualification and broadening physical GIF support. Retain existing application resource bounds as the starting point (500 frames, 10 MiB uploads, 50 million composed source pixels, 30-second media-job deadline); these are software safeguards, not Pixoo hardware claims. This read interface adds no smaller animation cap.
- Existing browser and local MCP routes retain their behavior. Hub #353 owns authenticated forwarding and the B.U.N.N.Y. widgets; Pixoo credentials never reach the browser.

## Out of scope

Uploads/edits or rendition-selection writes through this extension (#13 owns selection), original downloads, external asset sourcing (#93/#94), Hub UI/proxy implementation (#353), routine scheduling (Hub #45), and device profile changes or physical GIF qualification (#55). Source delivery does not install or operate the device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** The new minor version is negotiated alongside 1.0. Existing 1.0 fixtures pass unchanged. The issue-linked OpenSpec delta and pinned consumer contract specify the new catalog, preview and current-media fields, including unavailable/uncertain state.
- [x] **AC2.** List paging validates bounds and reports totals. Cover empty catalogs, multiple pages, unnamed fallback, filename-derived names, explicit-label precedence when present, preserved 81–120-character names and the existing rejection above 120. Existing browser/MCP name validation is unchanged.
- [x] **AC3.** Catalog mutations advance `catalogRevision`; a mutation between list/playlist reads is detectable and refreshes without pairing one rendition's pixels with another's metadata. Current-media identity/position matches the existing player observation and has honest absent/uncertain cases.
- [x] **AC4.** `preview.png` and every frame PNG decode to the exact cached effective RGB pixels. Manifest frame count, order, repeated frames, delays, duration and warnings match the owning rendition. Cover PNG/JPEG stills, a one-frame GIF, the historical two-frame fixture, at least a 20-frame GIF with non-500-ms variable delays, duplicate frames, and a frame with more than 256 colors. All admitted frames remain present. These are source fixtures, not physical qualification.
- [x] **AC5.** Test representation-specific ETags, conditional 304, unknown/deleted rendition 404, invalid frame index, a cataloged rendition with no playlist reference, read-scope rejection and existing control-only credential rules. No credential or raw storage path is exposed.
- [x] **AC6.** Fake-adapter and ledger tests show zero device operations/tickets across catalog and preview reads in simulator and device configurations, including a previewable rendition incompatible with the current device profile. Exercise queue/timeout failures and prevent partial responses being accepted as complete previews.
- [x] **AC7.** `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass; required PR and merged-revision CI and independent Standards/Specification review pass. Coordinate a linked Hub contract/fixture compatibility PR with #353. #246 may reuse the definitions if its refactor overlaps; its completion is not a prerequisite for this feature.

## Dependencies and delivery

#37 and #33 supply the delivered API foundation; #67 is absorbed. No new hard dependency on #55: read-only previews can ship using existing cataloged renditions and synthetic fixtures before broader device playback is qualified. #55 owns normal device-host import/preview support and broader physical playback; do not claim that outcome from #96 acceptance. Hub #353 consumes this extension and depends on #96. #13 and Hub #45 consume discovery for selection/routine authoring.

Delivery target: source-only, including the linked Hub compatibility update. Installation and physical observation require separate authorization. Without this story, the Pixoo web UI remains the manual media browser.

## Work assessment

Planning reassessment, 2026-09-30, following the owner's accepted drift corrections and GIF direction. Sources: live #96/#55/Hub #353/#426/#246, Pixoo main `0d18b7fa0cc42ed576b25f8d5c24259a89fc05e3`, existing renderer/library/browser contracts, and Hub ADR 0005.

- **Complexity: medium.** Version negotiation, catalog revisions, bounded frame reads and the Hub consumer contract cross existing interfaces.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Cached PNG frames and delays already support exact previews; the owner accepted that approach and existing-name compatibility. Physical frame/timing uncertainty remains isolated in #55.
- **Impact: medium.** Incorrect catalog identity, authorization or resource handling affects multiple readers; device writes remain excluded.

**Readiness:** source delivery accepted in [PR #130](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/130), merged as `47c0fb2681ee27807f88a3a07bd713ab05bcdc81`. Both independent reviews passed; all three configured PR and merged-main CI jobs succeeded. [Hub compatibility PR #676](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/676) contains pinned fixtures, and its owning-service check passed against the merged producer. No runtime installation or broader physical playback is claimed; #55 remains open for that evidence.

Delivery pickup, 2026-09-30: the owner explicitly requested coordinated delivery of Pixoo #96, Pixoo #55 and Hub #353. One coordinator owns durable repository and tracker writes; isolated workers prepare bounded proposals. This overrides the standalone-session execution recommendation for this active delivery. Source, UI, installation and physical evidence remain separate.

issues.title: Show hub now-playing cards on the Pixoo
issues.body:
Pixoo half of [agent-device-hub#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38). The hub issue owns the overall outcome and records the owner's settled decisions (2026-09-25) in its "Delivery scope" section. The Tidbyt half is [agent-device-hub#280](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/280).

## Outcome and real setup

One operator, the installed Pixoo app (device mode, user service), and the installed hub with the Sony HT-A9 playback source. The Pixoo reads the hub's shared playback snapshot, `GET /api/playback/v1/snapshot` on loopback, with a private read credential that lists the source in `devices`. It shows a 64×64 now-playing card with the track and artist. Text only, no artwork.

## Smallest useful implementation

- An opt-in private playback configuration in the backend's data directory: the hub endpoint, the token and the source ID. Without it, nothing changes.
- A playback reader that polls every 2 s, validates the envelope strictly and keeps the last good read.
- A 64×64 card renderer: a play or pause marker, the title and the artist, wrapped or truncated with no scrolling. A stale card is dimmed and marked `?`.
- **Monitor mode:** a new track, or playback starting, shows the card for 10 s, then the dashboard returns. If a session needs attention (approval, input or question), or attention arrives, the dashboard shows at once and the pop-up is dropped, not replayed.
- **Media mode:** a Pixoo-local setting.
  - Off (default): today's rule; nothing takes over Media.
  - Pop-up: pause the playlist for the 10 s card, then resume it; the current item restarts.
  - Whole song: show the card while music plays or is paused, then resume the playlist when it stops or becomes unavailable.
  - A takeover happens only while a playlist is actively playing and the screen is on. Otherwise there is nothing to restore, and the card is not shown.
  - Any manual player, mode or screen action during a takeover cancels the automatic resume.
- The setting lives in the browser settings UI and persists in its own file. The shared `pixoo-integration/1.0` snapshot and configuration are unchanged, because the hub validates them strictly.
- All writes go through the existing player and serialized adapter. Redraws happen only when the card changes, through the existing Monitor upload gate.

Stale rules match the Tidbyt:

- `playing` or `paused` shows the card.
- `stale` (5 to 30 s), or a failed read, keeps it dimmed with `?`.
- `unavailable`, `stopped`, `inactive` or `unknown` returns to the dashboard in Monitor mode, or resumes the playlist in Media mode. A failed read counts as stale until the last good observation is 30 s old.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

One serialized device writer. Monitor/Media semantics outside the new setting, including "screen-on alone never resumes playback". Playback recovery, originals and referenced renditions. The integration contract the hub consumes. No hub changes. Tests never contact a device or the hub.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Fake hub and fake player tests cover:
  - the card render;
  - the Monitor pop-up and its attention cut-short;
  - Media Off, Pop-up and Whole song, with resume, manual-cancel, screen-off and not-playing cases;
  - stale and failed-read handling;
  - the persisted setting and the unchanged integration snapshot.
- Browser tests cover the settings control.
- `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass.
- The owner approves the settings UI.
- Delivery target: source-only. Installing the updated app and checking the physical Pixoo need the owner's separate go-ahead.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Artwork: agent-device-hub#229.
- A rotation slot in Media: revisit if the owner asks for it; it changes the playlist engine.
- Marquee scrolling: revisit if truncation proves unreadable on the device.

issues.title: Pixoo monitor rows all show the same truncated session ID prefix
issues.body:
## Problem

Every row on the installed Pixoo monitor shows the same task identifier, `01A0D+`, so sessions cannot be told apart on the device.

Observed on September 25, 2026 against the installed user service (revision `690f14d`, device mode, remote owner `personal-shared-monitor` on port 8788). The rendition layout listed 19 matching top-level rows over 5 pages. All rows were Codex Desktop sessions (`codex`/`desktop`, host `wsl-ubuntu`), none had a label, and every `shortLabel` was `01A0D+`.

Cause, in the current code:

- `DashboardRow.label` falls back to `identity.sessionId` when no label is set (`apps/server/src/agent-dashboard.ts`).
- `shortLabel()` keeps the first five characters and appends `+` when the label is longer than six characters.
- Codex session IDs are time-ordered UUIDs, so every session created in the same period shares the prefix `01a0d…`. The five kept characters carry no identifying information.
- No session has a label because the shared vocabulary only allows user-chosen labels (`label.origin: 'user'`); the hub hook normalizer never sets one, and none were saved through the Monitor tab.

The `+` is a truncation marker, not part of the identifier. Together with the six-character budget, the row cannot show either a meaningful name or a distinguishing part of the ID.

## Outcome

A Pixoo monitor row identifies its session at a glance. Two sessions visible at the same time never show the same identifier unless they share a label.

## Scope

- Choose a distinguishing fallback when no label exists, for example the last characters of the session ID or a short per-owner ordinal assigned by the renderer, and record the choice in `docs/agent-monitoring.md`.
- Truncate labels so the marker cannot be mistaken for content, for example by shortening without a suffix when the row budget is fixed, or by using a distinct glyph.
- Keep the Monitor tab showing the full label or ID beside the truncated glyphs.
- Keep the shared vocabulary: no automatic titles, prompts or paths become labels in Pixoo. If an automatic neutral label is wanted, that is a hub owner change and needs its own hub issue.

Any change to the row layout should be coordinated with the monitor readability redesign if that is planned separately, so the identifier width is chosen once.

## Acceptance

- With the synthetic examples in `apps/server/src/dashboard-examples.ts` and a fixture of four unlabeled sessions whose IDs share a prefix, the rendered rows show four different identifiers.
- Unit tests for `shortLabel` and the fallback cover the shared-prefix case and a labeled case.
- `docs/agent-monitoring.md` describes the identifier rule and the truncation marker.
- `npm run check` passes. Physical acceptance follows the existing device profile and is reported separately.

## Related

- Hub #241 retires ended sessions across Codex and Claude; fewer stale rows reduces, but does not remove, the collision.
- Labels: the Monitor tab `Save label` command remains the only way to name a session today.


## Evidence update, 2026-09-25 sweep

After the hub's session retirement (Hub #241, installed with Hub 0.3.5) the shared owner dropped from 29 to 3 Codex Desktop sessions during the day, so fewer rows collide. The fallback is unchanged: an unlabeled row still shows the first five characters of a time-ordered UUID. Hub #312 qualifies Claude Code and Codex CLI ends; Hub #332 retires stale attention from B.U.N.N.Y. Neither changes the identifier rule.

## Guide

**Topic:** shared-codex
**Note:** Unlabeled Pixoo rows show a five-character UUID prefix plus `+`, identical for every session from the same period.


## Delivery assessment

Refreshed 2026-09-25 at pickup against `main` 2d7e954; stage: delivery.

- **Assumptions:** one owner, one local backend, installed service reads the shared owner (AGENTS.md, docs/sdlc.md). Hub #364 (shared alias) is backlog, so the fallback stays in Pixoo. #98 will choose its own width; the rule here is width-independent.
- **Decision:** an unlabeled row shows `…` plus the last five ID characters; a long label keeps its first three and last two characters around `…`. The marker glyph is outside the label alphabet. Rationale and rejected options: OpenSpec change `gh-87-distinct-row-identifiers`.
- **Residual:** different IDs sharing their last five characters, or labels sharing three leading and two trailing characters, still collide (about 1 in 175,000 for four visible UUIDs). Revisit trigger: Hub #364 landing, or an observed collision.
- **Ratings:** complexity low (pure identifier function, one glyph); uncertainty low (fallback decision delegated by the resume note); impact low (display only, no persistence, device commands or credentials).
- **Readiness:** ready; no blockers.
- **Verification:** unit tests for the shared-prefix, labeled, short and unsupported cases; a synthetic four-session example with distinct identifiers and updated hashes; browser preview byte equality; docs by inspection; `npm run check`, `npm run test:browser` and both workflow checks. Physical acceptance needs a separate request.

issues.title: Retire native Windows support and the flaky Windows CI jobs
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

`Application checks on windows-latest` fails now and then because an integration test exceeds Vitest's default 5000 ms timeout. Reruns pass with no code change, and the same suite passes on Ubuntu. The failures block merges and turn main CI red (most recently main push run [36207958108](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/36207958108) for #98, three attempts).

The app actually runs in WSL: the owner selected WSL as the primary workflow (docs/hardware-validation.md) and the installed backend is a systemd user service there. Native Windows was only a documented fallback for when a Windows browser cannot reach WSL loopback (#10). Nothing in current use depends on it.

**Scope decision (owner, 2026-09-25):** instead of raising timeouts, retire native Windows as a supported runtime and remove both Windows CI jobs. This replaces the original timeout plan below.

Observed Windows failures:

| Run | Date | Context | Tests that timed out | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [36086733786](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/36086733786) | 2026-09-25 | push to main (#84) | `device-runtime` "applies smoke limits at import…" (8.6 s), `media-admission` "bounds multiple rendition rows…" (5.3 s) | passed on attempt 2 |
| [36065641254](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/36065641254) | 2026-09-24 | PR #78 | `monitor-failures` "preserves unavailable child rollup…", `playback-context` "captures immutable context…" | failed |
| [35545831662](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/35545831662) | 2026-09-20 | PR (gh-32) | `diagnostics` "reports private-safe simulator diagnostics…" | passed on attempt 2 |
| [35544559191](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/35544559191) | 2026-09-20 | PR (gh-30 acceptance) | `diagnostics` (same test) | passed on attempt 2 |
| [35530830998](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/35530830998) | 2026-09-20 | PR (gh-30 qualification) | `media-admission` "checks cancellation inside the real library queue…" (both attempts) | failed |
| [34530647127](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34530647127) | 2026-09-10 | push to main | most of `device-runtime` and two `mcp` tests; hooks also hit the 10000 ms timeout | passed on attempt 2 |

## Smallest useful implementation

- Remove `windows-latest` from the Workflow and Application jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. CI keeps three Ubuntu jobs: Workflow checks, Application checks and Simulator browser checks.
- Remove native Windows runtime instructions (PowerShell startup, backup/restore, MCP startup, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` default) from README and docs. Keep the Windows-browser-to-WSL reachability checks, since the owner uses a Windows browser against the WSL backend.
- Update the `local-operations` spec clause that requires documenting "native Windows as an alternative", through an OpenSpec change, and record the decision in an ADR.
- Update CI job lists in docs/development.md, docs/sdlc.md and the issue templates.
- Leave existing `win32` code branches and their unit test in place. They are harmless, and removing them would add churn without a current benefit.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Linux/WSL behavior, tests and assertions are unchanged. No test is skipped, weakened or retried.
- All remaining configured jobs stay required.
- Windows-browser-to-WSL reachability diagnostics and the "do not share a live SQLite directory across hosts" guidance stay.
- Agent-client routes (Codex or Claude on Windows reaching the WSL backend) are unaffected; they are documented in docs/agent-monitoring.md and docs/local-mcp.md.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] CI defines no Windows job; the PR run and the merged main run show exactly three jobs, all successful.
- [x] README and docs no longer present native Windows as a supported runtime; a repository search for PowerShell runtime steps finds none. Windows-to-WSL reachability guidance remains.
- [x] The `local-operations` spec no longer requires a native Windows alternative; the OpenSpec change is synced and archived, and `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` pass.
- [x] `npm run check` passes locally.

Source-only delivery; no device or installation.

## Meaningful deferrals and cuts

| Cut | Class | Lost assurance | Manual alternative | Revisit trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native Windows runtime | Unnecessary capability | No documented or CI-verified way to run the backend natively on Windows; `win32` code paths become unverified | Run the backend in WSL and reach it from Windows over loopback | A Windows host that cannot run WSL, or a need for a second native host |
| Windows CI jobs | Unnecessary capability (follows the runtime cut) | Windows-specific path, file-lock and process regressions go undetected | none needed while WSL is the only host | Same as above |
| Timeout tuning | Deferred | Slow Ubuntu runners could still hit the 5 s default | Rerun | An Ubuntu job times out |

## Work assessment

Delivery refresh, 2026-09-25, base `fec2e2d`. Original planning assessment (raise timeouts) superseded by the owner's scope decision above.

- **Complexity: low.** CI config, docs, one spec clause, one ADR.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Current runtime is WSL (hardware-validation.md, installed user service).
- **Impact: low.** Only CI coverage and documentation; revert restores both.

**Readiness:** ready. Operating assumption: one operator, backend in WSL (docs/sdlc.md scope defaults, docs/hardware-validation.md).

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow

issues.title: Reconcile product and hub-integration docs with delivered runtime behavior
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make the current-facing product and hub-integration guidance accurately describe the implemented local Pixoo application: one operator, one backend, simulator by default, and explicit validated device activation. This is a low-priority documentation-only cleanup.

Planning baseline: `0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf`, verified as current main on 2026-09-24.

Two concrete inconsistencies:
- [Product guidance](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/product.md#L62) says startup stays simulator-only, while its earlier runtime description and [README configuration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/README.md#L50) support explicit device mode.
- [Hub integration guidance](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/hub-integration.md#L94) says Monitor/Media and filter extensions remain unavailable pending issue 33, although the extension is implemented. The same document also retains broad statements that shared monitoring and native controller integration remain planned.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

Reconcile these two documents against current main, the owning implementation/specifications and issue-linked delivery evidence. Update current-facing statements and links; identify historical planning context as historical where it must remain. Inspect directly linked guidance only to resolve affected claims rather than expanding into a repository-wide documentation rewrite or another status ledger.

Keep shared controller v1's advertised capabilities distinct from the implemented Pixoo-specific integration extension.

Required input dependencies: **none outstanding**. Existing ownership records include [monitor host](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31), [Monitor/Media controls](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33), [native controller](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [explicit device activation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42). Refresh their supporting evidence at pickup; issue closure alone is not proof of every acceptance stage.

This cleanup is independent of [typed evidence](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/79), [typed command observations](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/80) and [shared SSE delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/81). Do not describe those planned improvements as delivered.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve the single selected agent-state owner, single serialized device writer, simulator default, explicit target/activation and Monitor/Media intent. Enabling monitoring alone must not be described as activating presentation; screen-on alone does not resume playback or monitoring.

Keep source/CI, installation, actual-client, transport and visible-device evidence separate. Preserve immutable handoff material, archived OpenSpec changes, historical ADR decisions and dated acceptance receipts. Do not rewrite requirements or remove acceptance gates to make prose agree.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] **AC1 — Startup wording.** Both documents consistently distinguish simulator default from supported explicit device activation. Evidence: compare each affected claim with current README, runtime selection and device-application requirements.
- [x] **AC2 — Delivered integration.** Current-facing text no longer calls implemented monitoring, native-controller or Pixoo Monitor/Media/filter capabilities unavailable or merely planned. Native v1 and the Pixoo extension remain clearly distinguished. Evidence: trace the statements to current registration/command code, specifications and linked delivery records.
- [x] **AC3 — Evidence boundaries.** Source availability does not imply a current personal installation or fresh physical acceptance. Any installation/client/device statement cites its dated evidence and retains its limits. Historical source text remains intact. Evidence: focused documentation review and diff inspection.
- [x] **AC4 — References and consistency.** Affected links and anchors resolve, issue references identify the correct work, and version references distinguish source pins from separately recorded installed versions. Evidence: link/anchor inspection and comparison with authoritative manifests/receipts; avoid changing a version merely to match another environment.
- [x] **AC5 — Documentation-only delivery.** No application, configuration, credential, runtime-state or device behavior changes. Evidence: reviewed changed-file list, `git diff --check`, applicable repository checks and configured CI.

Delivery target: **source-only documentation**.

## Meaningful deferrals

No cross-project guide refresh or public-site publication is needed under current policy. This item changes repository guidance only; separately requested publication follows the hub's existing procedure.

Broader architecture refactoring, performance qualification, installation and physical tests remain in their owning issues. There is no new runtime assurance from this cleanup.

## Work assessment and delivery

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24. Complexity: **low**, focused edits to two current-facing documents. Uncertainty: **low**, concrete contradictions have been identified and authoritative source is available. Impact: **low**, with no executable behavior change. Readiness: **ready**. No unresolved product decision or blocking dependency. Session reasoning setting: **unknown**.

Reassess if source behavior changes or supporting delivery evidence conflicts. Record why no product specification delta is required; this issue corrects descriptions, not contracts.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/AGENTS.md) and [the SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/sdlc.md): isolated documentation delivery, the required unslop editorial pass, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, configured PR checks, guarded merge and merged-main CI readback. No validation has been run for a candidate. Publishing this issue does not begin documentation edits or implementation.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `low` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `low` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) |
| Thinking level | `low` | `low` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**


issues.title: Share SSE client delivery while preserving browser and native feed contracts
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Planning baseline: `0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf`. Changes require maintaining both implementations. This is a maintenance improvement; no existing combined-capacity bug or measured performance gain is claimed.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

Characterize the two implementations' readiness, authentication and blocked-write behavior first. Extract a private client-delivery component that accepts already encoded messages and the existing authentication callback where applicable. Migrate both feed classes in one passing candidate, removing their duplicated delivery machinery.

Keep snapshot selection, signatures, event history, cursor namespaces/parsing, replay/resync decisions and wire envelopes with the existing feed owners. Keep native stream reservation before asynchronous catalog/authentication work and ensure headers are sent before publication can write to the connection.

Required input dependencies: **none outstanding**. Preferred order is [evidence/MCP fix](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/79), [typed command observations](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/80), then this item. Neither is a blocked-by dependency. Coordinate any overlapping event publication or controller-registration changes at integration.

[Embedded monitor performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61) retains its own benchmarks and acceptance; it is not a prerequisite for this extraction.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Browser feeds retain `state`/`resync` behavior; released native controller feeds retain their versioned envelopes and contract-driven replay. Preserve each feed's existing authentication policy, including behavior where no continuous authentication callback is configured.

Keep per-delivery authorization and one-second credential rechecks for native streams, 15-second heartbeats, 32-entry delivery bounds, five-second drain ceilings and bounded disconnect handling. The global 16-stream admission budget remains owned by the existing HTTP security layer and covers mixed feeds and HEAD requests. Preserve the overall HTTP request limit and release resources on rejected registration, disconnect and shutdown.

No new transport, endpoint, state owner, database, device adapter or writer. Stream reconnection must never replay commands, stop backend playback or refresh physical evidence.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] **AC1 — Characterized delivery.** Capture readiness/header ordering, queue/authentication sequencing, blocked writes and shutdown behavior before extraction. Evidence: focused lifecycle tests; record intentional implementation differences instead of assuming equivalence.
- [x] **AC2 — One delivery implementation.** Both feed classes use the same private queue/authentication/backpressure/cleanup component; duplicated mechanics are removed while protocol decisions remain local. Evidence: source inspection and focused component tests.
- [x] **AC3 — Protocol compatibility.** Preserve browser and native envelopes, event IDs, retained-cursor replay, invalid/expired/future cursor resync and current-state reconciliation. Evidence: retain separate browser/native/monitor integration suites and browser reconnect tests.
- [x] **AC4 — Authorization and cleanup.** Revoked or rejected credentials stop protected delivery. Shutdown during authentication and rejection with queued messages leave no late protected writes, dangling timers or occupied stream slots. Evidence: controlled authentication promises, revocation tests and repeated connect/disconnect/shutdown checks.
- [x] **AC5 — Bounds and backpressure.** Mixed feeds and HEAD connections respect the global 16-stream limit; queue bounds, heartbeat/recheck intervals and drain deadlines remain unchanged. Drain followed by another publication preserves ordering and cleanup. Evidence: controlled-clock/socket tests plus existing mixed-feed capacity tests.
- [x] **AC6 — Client independence.** Stalled/disconnected consumers do not delay command completion, ingestion or healthy consumers; disconnect does not stop playback. Evidence: retain existing slow-socket, health/command and playback-continuity tests.
- [x] **AC7 — Whole application compatibility.** Application, controller compatibility and browser checks pass without any public schema or device-ownership change. Evidence: required local checks and all configured PR/main CI jobs.

Delivery target: **source-only**.

## Meaningful deferrals

Numeric performance qualification remains in [issue 61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61); this item makes no latency/resource-budget claim. Benchmark expansion is unnecessary for a behavior-preserving extraction unless testing reveals a material regression.

Public protocol unification and a reusable cross-project transport package are unnecessary capabilities here. Keep the component private; revisit only when a named consumer needs a shared package or a separately reviewed versioned protocol change. Preserve all separate end-to-end protocol tests.

## Work assessment and delivery

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24. Complexity: **high**, because authentication, asynchronous registration, publication, backpressure and shutdown interact across feed implementations. Uncertainty: **medium**; characterization must resolve their lifecycle differences. Impact: **high**, since regressions could disclose protected stream data or exhaust local request capacity. Readiness: **ready, with characterization first**. No unresolved product decision or blocking prerequisite. Session reasoning setting: **unknown**.

Reassess if current source changes, characterization exposes incompatible delivery policies, or extraction would require changing authentication, limits or public feed semantics. Record necessary protocol-specific hooks rather than silently changing supported behavior.

Before implementation, check active/archive collisions and prepare issue-linked design/failure scenarios and tasks using the local OpenSpec workflow, plus an ADR for the shared delivery boundary. Document why public contracts are unchanged. Preserve [controller API requirements](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/openspec/specs/controller-api/spec.md), [native feed requirements](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/openspec/specs/hub-controller-api/spec.md), [shared host ownership](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/decisions/0016-shared-monitor-host.md), and [Monitor/Media behavior](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/decisions/0018-monitor-display-ownership.md).

Use documented fnm/shared caches and run workflow checks for OpenSpec changes. None has run for this issue.

Follow [the SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/sdlc.md): independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, with concurrency and authorization inspection; all five configured PR CI jobs; guarded merge; merged-main CI readback. issues.title: Separate typed command observations from replay payloads
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make command producers and observers share typed operation metadata so changes expose affected consumers during typechecking. Keep the existing one-operator, one-backend setup and the same behavior for browser, MCP and native-controller clients.

Planning baseline: `0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf`. [Commands](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/apps/server/src/commands.ts#L4) publishes unknown payloads/results; [ControllerState.observe](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/apps/server/src/controller-state.ts#L88) interprets positional tuples, recognizes transport-specific payloads and casts results. This couples observation to replay serialization. No runtime defect or performance improvement is claimed.

## Smallest useful implementation, with dependencies

Separate typed observation metadata from the replay fingerprint. Use discriminated event types and exhaustive handling at the existing application boundary; migrate producers and ControllerState together. Keep the existing ledger, execution helpers, AsyncLocalStorage request context and pending-slot accounting. No event bus or new coordinator framework is needed.

Start by characterizing pending, completion, failure and replay behavior. Preserve the recorded behavior while changing the internal representation. Keep the consumer migration in one passing candidate.

Required input dependencies: **none outstanding**. Prefer [the evidence/MCP fix](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/79) first, then this item, then [shared SSE delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/81); this is preferred order, not blocked-by. Coordinate overlapping controller code with [playlist-name extension work](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/67); neither consumes the other's unfinished result.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one command owner and device writer, exact target selection, synchronous cancellation boundaries, native revision/generation guards, guard-sensitive native fingerprints, HTTP/MCP cross-route replay, retained failures and immutable receipts. Preserve 32 pending request slots and 256 completed receipts.

Late uploads must retain their initiating request and generation without reviving obsolete work or transferring effects to a later pause/stop. Preserve identity through automatic traversal, retry and probe-triggered recovery. Shared monitor labels/notices remain with the selected shared-state owner and are not absorbed into this ledger.

No public payload, response, scheduling, persistence, authorization or screen-off/on behavior changes. Keep local operations that cannot be represented by controller v1 from acquiring an invented native command representation.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [x] **AC1 — Characterized boundary.** Record pending/completion/error ordering, replay behavior and observer isolation before refactoring. Evidence: focused tests at the existing ledger/service boundary; do not invent a failing test for a behavior-preserving refactor.
- [x] **AC2 — Typed observation.** Producers provide typed operation metadata separately from the existing fingerprint, and ControllerState handles tagged variants without positional replay-tuple or unchecked result casts. Evidence: TypeScript checks, focused event tests and inspection of all producers/consumers.
- [x] **AC3 — Replay compatibility.** Matching requests execute once and retain original outcomes; changed payloads/guards conflict; schema failures do not reserve IDs; admitted failures remain replayable; expired epochs/IDs never execute. Replay emits no second execution lifecycle. Evidence: HTTP, MCP and native integration/compatibility suites.
- [x] **AC4 — Attribution and ordering.** Cancellation, late completion, traversal, retries and probe recovery retain the original request/generation and do not mutate a queued receipt or reactivate obsolete output. Evidence: preserve asynchronous/retired-upload and probe-recovery cases in the [controller compatibility suite](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/tests/integration/hub-controller-compatibility.test.ts#L116).
- [x] **AC5 — Capacity and isolation.** Existing pending-slot lifetime, 32-slot admission and 256-result retention remain unchanged; observer failure cannot interrupt command execution. Evidence: focused ledger tests and existing capacity tests, with representative checks when the native endpoint is enabled and disabled.
- [x] **AC6 — Whole application compatibility.** Browser, MCP, native controller and Monitor/Media behavior pass their existing owning checks without a second writer or state owner. Evidence: required application, controller and browser checks.

Delivery target: **source-only**.

## Meaningful deferrals

Moving pending-slot accounting out of ControllerState is deferred. Its current endpoint-dependent ownership stays unchanged; revisit only if a concrete capacity inconsistency is reproduced. This item adds no new guarantee for that question.

A general event bus, public event API and new coordinator are unnecessary capabilities for this outcome. Direct typed events suffice; revisit only for a concrete additional consumer requirement. Retain all existing lower-level tests with distinct coverage.

Make command producers and observers share typed operation metadata so changes expose affected consumers during typechecking. Keep the existing one-operator, one-backend setup and the same behavior for browser, MCP and native-controller clients.

Planning baseline: `0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf`. [Commands](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/apps/server/src/commands.ts#L4) publishes unknown payloads/results; [ControllerState.observe](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/apps/server/src/controller-state.ts#L88) interprets positional tuples, recognizes transport-specific payloads and casts results. This couples observation to replay serialization. No runtime defect or performance improvement is claimed.

protections.heading: Behavior and protections to preserve
protections.text:
Keep one command owner and device writer, exact target selection, synchronous cancellation boundaries, native revision/generation guards, guard-sensitive native fingerprints, HTTP/MCP cross-route replay, retained failures and immutable receipts. Preserve 32 pending request slots and 256 completed receipts.

Late uploads must retain their initiating request and generation without reviving obsolete work or transferring effects to a later pause/stop. Preserve identity through automatic traversal, retry and probe-triggered recovery. Shared monitor labels/notices remain with the selected shared-state owner and are not absorbed into this ledger.

No public payload, response, scheduling, persistence, authorization or screen-off/on behavior changes. Keep local operations that cannot be represented by controller v1 from acquiring an invented native command representation.

acceptance.heading: Observable acceptance and planned evidence
acceptance.text:
- [x] **AC1 — Characterized boundary.** Record pending/completion/error ordering, replay behavior and observer isolation before refactoring. Evidence: focused tests at the existing ledger/service boundary; do not invent a failing test for a behavior-preserving refactor.
- [x] **AC2 — Typed observation.** Producers provide typed operation metadata separately from the existing fingerprint, and ControllerState handles tagged variants without positional replay-tuple or unchecked result casts. Evidence: TypeScript checks, focused event tests and inspection of all producers/consumers.
- [x] **AC3 — Replay compatibility.** Matching requests execute once and retain original outcomes; changed payloads/guards conflict; schema failures do not reserve IDs; admitted failures remain replayable; expired epochs/IDs never execute. Replay emits no second execution lifecycle. Evidence: HTTP, MCP and native integration/compatibility suites.
- [x] **AC4 — Attribution and ordering.** Cancellation, late completion, traversal, retries and probe recovery retain the original request/generation and do not mutate a queued receipt or reactivate obsolete output. Evidence: preserve asynchronous/retired-upload and probe-recovery cases in the [controller compatibility suite](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/tests/integration/hub-controller-compatibility.test.ts#L116).
- [x] **AC5 — Capacity and isolation.** Existing pending-slot lifetime, 32-slot admission and 256-result retention remain unchanged; observer failure cannot interrupt command execution. Evidence: focused ledger tests and existing capacity tests, with representative checks when the native endpoint is enabled and disabled.
- [x] **AC6 — Whole application compatibility.** Browser, MCP, native controller and Monitor/Media behavior pass their existing owning checks without a second writer or state owner. Evidence: required application, controller and browser checks.

Delivery target: **source-only**.

deferrals.heading: Meaningful deferrals
deferrals.text:
Moving pending-slot accounting out of ControllerState is deferred. Its current endpoint-dependent ownership stays unchanged; revisit only if a concrete capacity inconsistency is reproduced. This item adds no new guarantee for that question.

A general event bus, public event API and new coordinator are unnecessary capabilities for this outcome. Direct typed events suffice; revisit only for a concrete additional consumer requirement. Retain all existing lower-level tests with distinct coverage.

issues.title: Keep MCP status valid after dashboard uploads with typed display evidence
issues.body:
## Observed and expected behavior

At planning baseline `0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf`, Player records completed dashboard transport evidence with source `dashboard`, while the MCP status schema accepts only `brightness`, `screen`, `probe`, and `upload`. ControlService passes the evidence through, so the traced `get_status` path reaches a schema rejection. This is a source-backed finding; no runtime reproduction has been executed for this issue.

Expected: with monitoring and MCP enabled together, status stays valid after a dashboard upload and continues to distinguish requested, acknowledged and observed state.

Sources: [Player evidence](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/packages/playback/src/player.ts#L39), [dashboard upload](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/packages/playback/src/player.ts#L147), [MCP status schema and projection](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/apps/server/src/mcp-tools.ts#L20), and [honest status requirements](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/openspec/specs/local-mcp-controls/spec.md#L59).

## Reproduction

Planned regression: start the built simulator with monitoring and MCP enabled using isolated configuration and synthetic credentials; explicitly activate Monitor; complete a synthetic dashboard upload; call `get_status` through a real MCP protocol client and validate it against the advertised output schema. Capture the current failing result before implementing the fix. No physical device or installed client is needed.

## Scope

Give Player's display evidence a finite source type and add an exhaustive MCP projection. Keep internal `dashboard` evidence distinct, but map it to the existing public `upload` value. Preserve the advertised MCP schema, existing tool set and evidence ownership inside Player.

Keep the current single operator/backend setup, simulator default, explicit configured device target, one serialized writer, generation guards, nullable observations, monotonic timestamps, sanitized results and read/control authorization. Status reads remain free of catalog names, private paths and device addresses.

## Acceptance criteria and planned evidence

- [ ] **AC1 — Combined feature regression.** The reproduction above fails on the baseline and passes after the change; status after a current-generation dashboard upload is schema-valid and exposes public source `upload`. Evidence: built-server MCP integration test with a deterministic synthetic upload.
- [ ] **AC2 — Complete evidence mapping.** Every finite producer source has an explicit, typechecked projection; unavailable evidence remains null. Evidence: focused mapping tests plus typecheck, with no unrestricted source string or fallback that silently accepts new producer values.
- [ ] **AC3 — Honest reads.** Repeated status calls add no device operations, advance no generation and do not refresh evidence timestamps; simulator connectivity remains false and possible prior effects remain explicit. Evidence: controlled-clock/evidence tests and protocol assertions.
- [ ] **AC4 — Retired work.** An obsolete dashboard completion cannot replace current evidence or reactivate presentation. Evidence: preserve and extend existing retired-generation tests where needed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Compatibility.** Existing HTTP/MCP display replay, privacy, authentication, explicit activation and screen-off/on behavior remain intact. Evidence: preserve existing MCP, display-evidence and monitor-presentation suites and run the full required checks.

## Dependencies and order

No unfinished input dependency. The delivered MCP and Monitor boundaries are already present in the pinned baseline. Prefer this fix before [typed command observations](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/80) and [shared SSE delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/81); that is priority, not a blocked-by relationship.

## Meaningful deferrals

A new public `dashboard` evidence value is deferred: MCP callers continue to see an upload without a new schema value. Revisit only when a consumer needs the distinction and compatibility/versioning is specified. No new status framework, tool, state store or device operation is needed.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24. Complexity: **medium**, covering Player evidence, its MCP projection and combined feature tests. Uncertainty: **low**; the static mismatch is clear, but the first delivery step must reproduce it. Impact: **medium**; incorrect status disrupts multiple consumers without requiring changes to device control. Readiness: **ready**. No unresolved product decision or blocking prerequisite. Session reasoning setting: **unknown**.

Reassess if the baseline changes, the failing path cannot be reproduced, or preserving the public schema requires a different semantic mapping. This is a contract-preserving bug fix: record why no product specification delta is required, linking the existing honest-status requirements. Preserve [the accepted evidence owner](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/decisions/0013-local-mcp-controls.md).

## Verification and delivery target

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/AGENTS.md) and the [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0ca009c828fb90f278469302d367f1ac9f9ab4bf/docs/sdlc.md). Delivery uses an isolated worktree, Node 24, synthetic credentials, disposable runtime data and fake/injected device transport. Planned checks are `npm ci`, focused tests, `npm run check`, and Chromium installation followed by `npm run test:browser`; use the documented fnm/shared-cache setup. Run current workflow checks for any OpenSpec changes. Require independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, all five configured PR CI jobs, guarded merge and merged-main CI verification. These checks have not run for this issue.

Delivery target: **source-only**. Publication of this issue authorizes tracking only; it does not start implementation, installation, personal-client configuration or physical tests. Current policy requires no cross-project guide refresh for this scope.

issues.title: Run the installed Pixoo app as a user service with hub settings
issues.body:
## Outcome

The installed Pixoo app keeps running across PC and WSL restarts, with the settings the shared hub needs, so BUNNY controls and agent-status presentation come back without manual steps.

## Background

Found during [hub #154](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/154) on September 24, 2026.

- The installed app runs as a detached manual process. [Local operations](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/local-operations.md) says no startup or restart service is installed. After a PC or WSL restart the app is gone: BUNNY reports the Pixoo controller unavailable, and agent status stops.
- The hub needs `PIXOO_CONTROLLER_ENABLED=1` and device mode. #154 added the flag to the owner's private start script, but the packaged operator runbook from #65 does not mention it. A reinstall from the runbook would drop it.
- Even after a manual restart, startup never activates Monitor presentation. Someone still has to send an explicit Monitor mode command.

The Nanoleaf installation already runs as user services on the same host, so a user service is a proven pattern there.

## Scope

- Provide a supported user-service setup for the installed app: start on login or boot, restart on failure, and stop gracefully with SIGTERM so the player drains. Keep one backend per data directory.
- Put device mode, monitoring, the controller flag and the stable controller identity in that setup and in the operator runbook.
- Restore Monitor presentation at startup when the saved mode is Monitor. Owner decision, September 24, 2026 (see the decision comment). This reverses the accepted "startup never activates presentation" rule in ADR 0018 and the agent-monitor-controls spec, so delivery includes the issue-linked OpenSpec delta and an ADR amendment. Coordinate with [#76](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/76), which covers screen-on and device-reboot recovery. Cloud isolation is #83.
- Document install, upgrade, rollback and removal of the service.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The service setup and runbook exist, including the controller flag and device mode.
- [x] After a WSL restart, the app is running and the hub reports the Pixoo controller ready without manual steps. *(Accepted by the owner on proxy evidence, September 25, 2026; see the closing comment.)*
- [x] The startup-presentation decision is recorded: restore Monitor presentation at startup when the saved mode is Monitor.
- [x] Startup restores Monitor presentation when the saved mode is Monitor, in device mode only, through the serialized adapter, with a failed transmission suspending monitoring until explicit activation.
- [x] Graceful stop is verified: the player drains and the catalog closes.
- [x] Installing the service on the owner's host is a separately authorized step, with its own backup and receipt.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 24, 2026.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** Service wiring and documentation, plus one optional startup behavior change.
- **Uncertainty: low.** A matching user-service pattern already runs on the host.
- **Impact: medium.** It affects display ownership after restarts. Rollback means disabling the service.

**Readiness:** ready. The startup-presentation decision is recorded. Installing the service on the owner's host remains a separately authorized step.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Source delivery does not install the service or contact the device.

issues.title: Expose user-entered playlist names through the Pixoo integration extension
issues.body:
## Outcome

Expose the user-entered name of each discoverable saved playlist through the Pixoo integration extension, so the shared BUNNY frontend can label playlist selection instead of showing bare IDs.

## Scope and accepted definition

The accepted general-control definition is [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in the hub as ADR 0005 (`docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`). Controller v1 exposes up to the first 100 saved playlist IDs without names and remains unchanged. This issue adds an additive field to the Pixoo-owned `pixoo-integration` extension under a new compatible minor version, with explicit consumer negotiation.

This issue is non-blocking for the hub's Pixoo general-control UI. That UI is accepted with IDs alone and shows names only after it consumes the new extension version.

## Accepted behavior

- A playlist name is included only when it was entered by the user in the Pixoo application. Names derived from filenames, media titles or paths are omitted, not substituted.
- Names follow the shared label bound of at most 80 Unicode characters and contain no credentials, paths or private metadata.
- The mapping is keyed by the same playlist IDs and catalog revision that controller v1 discovery uses, so a stale name cannot be paired with a different playlist.
- Browser and local MCP routes are unchanged. Reads add no device writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The extension snapshot carries the additive name field under a new minor version; existing consumers of the current version keep working. The exact issue-linked OpenSpec change records the delta.
- [ ] **AC2.** Validation rejects names above the bound and never includes names that are not user-entered; tests cover a playlist without a user-entered name.
- [ ] **AC3.** Names and IDs are consistent with the catalog revision in the same snapshot; a catalog change advances the revision.
- [ ] **AC4.** A linked Hub companion PR updates the hub's pinned Pixoo integration fixtures and compatibility record.

## Required source prerequisites

- [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31): general-control definition, accepted 2026-09-22.
- [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [#33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33): controller API and integration extension, closed.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-22, against divoom-app-upgrade `main` and the accepted Hub #31 decisions.

- **Complexity: low.** One additive read field on an existing versioned extension.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Whether Pixoo stores an explicit user-entered playlist name must be confirmed in the code before the field is specified; if names are ever auto-derived, the omission rule applies.
- **Impact: low.** Read-only data; a wrong name is a labeling defect, not a device effect.

**Readiness:** ready. **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews with a privacy check on name provenance.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Use the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, proportionate executable checks, isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep private media, credentials and runtime state out of Git. This issue does not authorize installation or device operations.

issues.title: Harden and qualify embedded shared-monitor performance
issues.body:
## Outcome
Qualify and improve embedded shared-monitor performance with reproducible measurements, while allowing feature delivery to progress independently.

## Scope and authority
On September 20, 2026, the owner explicitly moved the performance measurements and numeric performance-acceptance requirement out of #31 into this hardening story. This story owns the embedded-host measurement helper, benchmark comparability, diagnosis, optimization and qualification evidence previously blocking PR #60. It is not a prerequisite for merging #31 or progressing dependent features. This defers performance acceptance; it does not claim that existing measurements pass or change frozen limits.

[Hub #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) continues to own cross-repository and later integrated performance qualification. This story supplies its embedded-host evidence and does not duplicate standalone, installed-client or physical acceptance work.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Audit `scripts/measure-monitor.mjs` against the frozen [Linux budget definitions](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/1fd353215532a5d0220b99d9b35b6da0436221cc/docs/performance/linux-budgets.json). Document applicable measurement boundaries, latency/cold-start/max-return limits, CPU/RSS scopes, overload accounting, isolation and cleanup evidence. Do not mistake the current partial helper for complete qualification.
- [ ] Instrument process startup, configuration/normalization, HTTP authentication/admission, queueing, durable commit and publication. Establish the cause of slow calls using controlled, recorded host/load conditions; compare the same runtime/source boundaries.
- [ ] Improve measured bottlenecks without weakening privacy, authentication, durable commits, exclusive ownership, bounded queues/streams, explicit loss reporting or fail-open deadlines.
- [ ] Qualify a pinned final revision with 1, 10 and 50 concurrent hooks, three repetitions of 1,000 warm calls per profile, first-call measurements and all applicable resource/failure checks. Every repetition and pooled latency must meet the applicable ceilings; retain failures and do not select favorable reruns.
- [ ] Exercise stalled/disconnected consumers, overload, host outage and descendant cleanup using synthetic input and disposable isolated state. No installed hooks, private databases, device traffic or Windows executable forwarding.
- [ ] Preserve the three failed 9,000-call receipts in `docs/performance/gh-31-embedded-host.json`. Retain their limitations and distinguish them from later accepted evidence. No discarded failures or post-failure limit relaxation; any justified material rebaselining needs a separately documented reviewed decision.
- [ ] Publish reproducible commands, per-phase results and acceptance receipts; synchronize Hub #30 and the work guide. Keep source qualification separate from installed-client, transport and physical acceptance.

## Starting evidence
PR #60 at `ae25a76bb6c597c96e1f08b81300878932ca46b9` passed 535 application tests, 52 browser tests and all five CI jobs. Its retained performance runs failed. The latest retained run's worst p99 values were 104.3/170.7/716.9 ms against 65/87/396 ms for concurrency 1/10/50. Other host workloads were uncontrolled; the cause is not established.
