issues.title: Support complete GIF imports and qualify longer Pixoo64 animations and timing
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Support useful animated GIFs in the local Pixoo application and on the owner's Pixoo64, beyond the historical one/two-frame, uniform-500-ms smoke profile. Preserve complete admitted animations and their effective timing in library previews, and establish a tested device playback profile with honest compatibility reporting.

Owner direction, 2026-09-30: support GIFs with more frames and varied timing; use technical resource safeguards where justified, without treating the smoke-test bounds as product requirements or proven hardware maxima. This expands the former variable-timing-only story to include frame-count qualification and separation of application import/preview from physical playback admission.

Owner disposition, 2026-10-01: physical animations use one fixed delay for every frame. Pauses use repeated identical frames, which count toward the frame limit. Keep complete mixed-delay imports and previews, but reject their physical playback; do not silently convert or retime them. Retain the bounded raw-upload profile; the subsequent owner-authorized hosted integration adds a distinct profile as described below. Automatic conversion is deferred until an owner request and reviewed conversion design. The blue-transition investigation remains open.

## Existing evidence

Continue the variable-timing qualification left open by #12. Its September 8
trial requested red/green delays of 500/1000 ms, then 1000/500 ms, followed by
an equal-500-ms control. A was uncertain, B looked equal and the control looked
equal. The requests preserved the expected frame order, bytes and delay fields;
HTTP success did not establish asymmetric visible timing. Firmware was unknown.

At planning pickup, the renderer supported up to 500 frames with variable delays under its application/simulator profile, but explicit device mode applied the two-frame smoke profile to imports and playback. That coupling prevents useful library imports before playback qualification. No universal maximum for this Pixoo/firmware has been established. Published community observations about roughly 40 frames are investigation leads, not a supported limit for this device. See the [existing protocol evidence](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0d18b7fa0cc42ed576b25f8d5c24259a89fc05e3/docs/protocol-spike.md) and [dated hardware record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/0d18b7fa0cc42ed576b25f8d5c24259a89fc05e3/docs/hardware-validation.md).

## Scope and sequence

1. Separate library import/render/preview admissibility from device playback compatibility. Permit complete GIF imports and effective previews within the application resource budget even when the current physical profile cannot play them. Use the existing rendition/profile and compatibility concepts; preserve original files, immutable identities, saved playlist references and old renditions. New rendering creates a new rendition instead of rewriting an old one.
2. Keep practical application safeguards. Start from the existing 10 MiB upload, 50-million composed-source-pixel, 500-frame and 30-second media-job bounds, with existing concurrency/queue protection. These are adjustable software budgets, not Pixoo hardware specifications. Account for decoded source canvases as well as 64×64 output: a small compressed GIF can expand substantially. Give a specific rejection reason, retain existing files and never silently truncate, drop frames or force all delays to 500 ms. Reassess a resource limit against a representative rejected owner GIF and measured resource use before increasing it; do not promise unlimited memory or processing. No arbitrary animation-duration cap is requested.
3. Prepare a bounded device qualification plan that tests frame count and timing separately. Begin with a reviewed multi-frame sequence above two frames and equal timing, then test faster uniform delays and asymmetric delays with a control. The plan names fixture frame counts/delays, source revision, model/firmware or unknown, request/time bounds, observation method, loading behavior, stop conditions and final display disposition. This issue does not prescribe a guessed maximum or authorize crash-limit probing.
4. After explicit target and sequence authorization, observe frame order/completeness, loop behavior and timing on the actual display. Distinguish bytes sent, HTTP acknowledgment and visible behavior. Preserve the prior inconclusive timing evidence. Inspect the current transport's total-upload deadline and sequential-frame behavior; increasing a profile count alone may not suffice for longer uploads.
5. Implement the owner-selected `pixoo64-gif-2026-10-01` physical profile: at most 20 frames, with one fixed 100–800 ms effective delay per animation. Preserve the historical smoke profile and explicit restart-only selection. Repeated identical frames express pauses and remain separate, counting toward the limit. Reject mixed effective delays before replacing playback context or queueing device work. Preserve complete imports/previews and original timing without automatic conversion, truncation or deduplication. Hosted integration is separately authorized below. The earlier unreleased September 30 candidate is superseded by the recorded evidence.

Library/source work can proceed independently of physical measurements. The full issue remains open until its required physical outcome is accepted or the owner explicitly disposes an evidenced limitation. Keep the transition-flashing defect #52 separate unless evidence shows a necessary shared fix and scope is reassessed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Meaningful source tests and the Pixoo UI show import, restart persistence and full preview of an admitted GIF with at least 20 frames and varied non-500-ms delays in both simulator and device-mode configurations, with no device write from import/preview. Unqualified physical playback remains visibly unavailable and rejects before adapter work.
- [x] **AC2.** Tests cover the application frame/byte/composed-pixel/deadline boundaries, cancellation, queue bounds, clear failure reasons, no partial/truncated publication, original preservation and unchanged referenced renditions. Existing zero/missing-delay normalization remains explicit.
- [x] **AC3.** A bounded, owner-approved physical sequence records the explicit target privately, revision, model/firmware, request traces, control, observed frame sequence/loops/timing and measurement uncertainty. Evidence demonstrates useful playback beyond two frames and evaluates non-500-ms and nonuniform delays separately; request acknowledgment alone is insufficient.
- [x] **AC4.** Reconcile source/effective/requested/visible timing and supported frame counts. An issue-linked OpenSpec change preserves the uniform-only raw profile and defines the separately selected lossless hosted profile and observable compatibility, including rejection of mixed delays and preservation of repeated pause frames, without recasting a tested bound as a universal hardware maximum. If a target behavior fails or remains ambiguous, retain the evidence and obtain explicit owner disposition before closure.
- [x] **AC5.** Normal application playback through the existing single writer demonstrates the accepted profile, transition/cancellation behavior and relevant playback policies. No firmware/router/firewall changes, guessed targets, unsolicited resets or alternate writers. Hosted file transport is authorized by the wrap-up request and must follow its scoped design. Lossy conversion remains unapproved.
- [x] **AC6.** Preserve existing browser/MCP/controller behavior, originals, immutable rendition IDs and playlist/session references. Run `npm run check`, `npm run test:browser`, relevant profile/adapter/player regressions, independent Standards/Specification reviews, required head/main CI and current-candidate human approval for UI changes. Record source, installation and physical evidence separately; ordinary delivery follows current guide-maintenance policy and does not require a companion Guide PR.

## Dependencies and consumers

Completed #12 supplies the historical physical evidence; #5/#42 own existing renderer/device application contracts. #96 and jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#353 expose previews and compatibility but do not qualify hardware. Their read-only source work need not wait for this issue's measurements. #13 and future routines must preserve playback admission. This story owns the broader import/profile work so it does not expand #96 into device control.

## Delivery target

Source delivery plus the owner-authorized bounded normal-application physical validation. Permanent installation and persistent network routing are outside this wrap-up; the installed service remains stopped. The wrap-up handoff supplies the explicit target, synthetic content sequence and cleanup authority.

## Approved deferral from #12

The owner approved moving only effective variable-timing qualification to this follow-up after completing the September 8 experiments. Issue #12 closes against the existing uniform-500-ms profile with its recorded tolerances and accepted limitations. This disposition does not turn the uncertain timing observations into a pass and authorizes no further device operation.

## Hosted integration authorization and assessment

October 1 wrap-up request authorizes production hosted GIF integration and bounded normal-application physical validation on the previously named device. Five-second (100×50 ms) and thirty-second (500×60 ms) standalone runs are complete; they are not normal-player acceptance. The controlled 20×100 ms palette-only experiment supports using one global palette with no local palettes.

Preserve both existing profiles. Add `pixoo64-hosted-2026-10-01`, admitting up to the existing 500-frame software budget and uniform 50–800 ms whole-centisecond delays. This is an admission envelope, not exhaustive qualification or a hardware maximum; no duration cap is added. Multi-frame effective RGB must fit a lossless global palette of at most 256 colors. Reject other content before replacing context, while preserving full import/preview and originals. Single-frame RGB uploads retain full color fidelity. No lossy conversion is authorized.

The existing queued writer sends one file-play command, with no uncertain retry or automatic fallback. An application-owned, bounded, expiring capability URL exposes only prepared bytes. Transfer completion and estimated readiness remain distinct from camera evidence. The private startup configuration must name a device-reachable route. WSL acceptance may use an owned temporary file-only Windows relay; persistent installation/routing requires its separate authorization and deployment plan. Existing control authentication, Stop semantics, restart behavior and one-writer ownership remain required.

Complexity: high, because encoding admission, queued device work, file transfer and player timing interact. Uncertainty: bounded application observations are now recorded; arbitrary media, every frame, exact finite plays and the full admission envelope remain unqualified. Impact: medium, with bounded synthetic display replacement and reversible source/runtime changes; no persistent installation is included. The completed design is `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-01-gh-55-gif-profiles/design.md`; all six capability deltas are synchronized.

AC1/AC2/AC6 require source/browser checks and preserved import/reference behavior. AC3/AC4 combine the completed experiments with lossless encoder/admission regressions. AC5 requires final-candidate normal-player recordings for both long fixtures, GIF-to-still and GIF-to-GIF advancement, relevant timing policies, replacement, cancellation/Stop, restart without replay and owned cleanup. Automatically review the recordings and retain ambiguous observations as unqualified. Issue #52 is not resolved by a clean loop and remains separate. Current hosted Settings UI approval and final archive are complete. Independent reviews and all three head/main CI jobs passed. Bounded application physical acceptance is recorded below.

Delivery pickup, 2026-09-30: the owner explicitly requested coordinated delivery of Pixoo #96, Pixoo #55 and Hub #353. One coordinator owns durable repository and tracker writes; isolated workers prepare bounded proposals. This overrides the standalone-session execution recommendation for this active delivery. Source, UI, installation and physical evidence remain separate.

## Guide

**Topic:** pixoo-media
**Note:** Support complete GIF imports/previews and qualify useful Pixoo frame counts and timing beyond the two-frame smoke profile. Physical tests need separate authorization.

Owner-approved Settings refinement, 2026-10-01: keep the saved IP and playback profile visible; put optional model and firmware notes under a collapsed Device details disclosure with simpler labels. These notes do not select the profile or gate GIF import/preview. Preserve their values when saving with the disclosure collapsed. The owner approved the Library UI, Hub preview UI and revised Settings candidate. This presentation change does not expand physical playback admission.

## Recorded timing investigation, October 1, 2026

The owner ran the camera-assisted timing-only sequence against candidate `47c6551535f642b4dde7f3fd066e8278fb033b83`. Each case uploaded one 20-frame animation through the normal application, then sent no further display frames. All three 23-request traces completed successfully with exact expected frame hashes, offsets and requested delays. Recordings contain approximately 65 seconds each at about 30 fps; originals and private device details remain outside Git.

| Case | Requested delays | Predicted loop with individual delays | Observed mean loop |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A | All 500 ms | 10 s | 10.048 s, four measured cycles |
| B | 100/200/500/800 ms, repeated five times | 8 s | 16.048 s, two measured cycles |
| C | 800/500/200/100 ms, repeated five times | 8 s | 2.049 s, 26 measured cycles |

Two independent methods tracked the moving diamond and progress bar against original video timestamps. Selected digit contact sheets verify all frames 01–20 in order. Allow approximately 0.1 second uncertainty at individual visual boundaries because of camera sampling and panel scanning. This establishes behavior for these cases and transport, not firmware internals or a universal frame limit. The later measured evidence supersedes the earlier qualitative interpretation of variable-delay support without deleting those observations. These recordings intentionally contain no GIF-to-still handoff, so they do not resolve BLUE flashing or settling.

## Execution recommendation

PR #131 is merged after clear independent Standards/Specification reviews and successful head/main CI. No implementation work remains for this issue. Source/browser checks, bounded application physical acceptance and current Settings UI approval are complete. Keep source, installation and physical evidence separate. The earlier raw-upload BLUE investigation remains in #52; clean hosted transitions do not prove that historical transport fixed.

The previous recommendation was based on qualitative timing observations; the October 1 recordings supersede that basis. Automatic conversion, transports beyond the approved hosted path and firmware changes remain outside this scope.

## Hosted application acceptance, October 1, 2026

The normal API/player at `84e24c2df6afecb8228afb008d2050641323fb1f` imported, saved, previewed and restarted without device writes, rejected mixed timing before context replacement, and exercised five/ thirty-second playback, GIF-to-GIF and GIF-to-still advancement, replacement, Stop and paused restart. Eleven device commands and five complete hosted responses completed without retries or resets. The installed service stayed inactive; the temporary backend, relay and camera were cleaned up, leaving the authorized BLUE still.

Automatic video analysis measured five-second intervals averaging 5.0112 s (five intervals) and one internal thirty-second interval of 29.984 s. Both thirty-second restart boundaries showed 500 → 001 → 002. The first BLUE hold stayed BLUE for all 261 samples over 13.024 s; no animation flashback was observed. Camera gaps reached 192 ms. These samples do not prove every frame or exact finite plays: the third long loop was replaced near its end, consistent with total-plays being estimated dwell. No new arbitrary duration cap or claim of exhaustive hardware qualification is made.

Sanitized evidence: `docs/hardware-validation.md`, “Hosted application playback — October 1, 2026.” Raw recordings and receipts remain private. Source checks: 772 passed/1 expected skip; browser: 79 passed/3 skipped; workflow: 10 passed. The owner approved the current hosted Settings desktop/mobile candidate. Permanent installation requires a separate request and reviewed deployment/rollback plan.

## Delivery completed

[PR #131](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/131) merged as `9c84321280ac6e1a478c348cbf9d40621c5f46e7`. All three [head CI jobs](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/36948279945) and all three [merged-main CI jobs](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/36948747866) passed. The merged tree matches the reviewed candidate, and production bytes match the physically tested revision. [Sanitized physical evidence](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/9c84321280ac6e1a478c348cbf9d40621c5f46e7/docs/hardware-validation.md#hosted-application-playback--october-1-2026). Source and bounded physical acceptance are complete; permanent installation remains unchanged.

issues.title: Support proportionate planning and review with structured evidence
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Shared planning and delivery skills scale their paperwork and review effort to the work while preserving evidence and each project's stronger rules. Routine work can use a concise plan and, only when its project explicitly adopts the policy, one independent reviewer covering both Standards and Specification.

## Smallest useful implementation

Update the owning plan-work, deliver-work, review-work, assessment and execution-record instructions together. Define explicit eligibility for routine bounded work; consequential changes, unresolved uncertainty, security/authentication, contracts, CI/policy, state ownership and device effects retain stronger review. The implementer never acts as their own independent reviewer. Existing project floors override a shared default.

Use a small structured review/delivery result for repeatable facts such as revision, axes inspected, findings and disposition. Keep raw findings and evidence links; do not substitute a claimed summary for a review or claim that shared GitHub credentials prove human authorship. Provide migration/compatibility guidance for existing readers and records rather than silently breaking them.

Make detailed execution recommendations selective: prepare them for selected work or on request, with generic work prompts available for unassessed backlog items. Keep named missing inputs and truthful uncertainty. Remove any shared expectation to maintain a current model recommendation on every open issue. Let small tasks use short outcome/acceptance definitions and conditional sections; use full OpenSpec/design work when behavior or uncertainty warrants it or the project requires it.

Coordinate https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/87: independently approved contracts are for real shared/external boundaries when required, not every internal helper. Do not adopt an unapproved definition or silently rewrite that existing issue's accepted scope. Keep repository authority explicit and avoid imposing Hub-specific fields, schemas or process on unrelated projects.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Planning remains read-only unless tracker/document writes are named. Source work does not install software or operate devices by implication. Current-candidate evidence, unresolved findings, exact source provenance, truthful unavailable status and stronger project gates remain intact. No governance service, parallel tracker or new approval authority.

Installation is part of completion under this repository's AGENTS.md. Before the catalog fast-forward or install, read README's installed-catalog procedure and present the required owner checkpoint. Installed links share the canonical checkout with active Codex/Claude/Pi sessions; do not update them mid-session without the applicable handoff. Record exactly which changed skills were installed and verify source/installed readback. If installation is deferred, keep this issue open with its owner and next action.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] AC1: Behavioral fixtures distinguish an explicitly opted-in low-risk project from stronger/default project policy, high-impact work and unknown risk. Only eligible work may use one fresh independent reviewer covering both axes.
- [ ] AC2: Negative cases reject self-review, missing axes, stale/wrong-head evidence, fabricated human approval, unresolved blocking findings and missing CI. This policy change itself uses the pre-existing stronger review requirements.
- [ ] AC3: Structured outputs preserve findings/provenance and can be consumed alongside existing records during migration. No reader silently treats absent evidence as success.
- [ ] AC4: Planning examples show concise routine work, conditional detail, recommendations only when useful/selected and a valid generic start when no recommendation exists. Material uncertainty and project-required specifications still receive full treatment.
- [ ] AC5: Run the complete current AGENTS.md check list, including skill validation, plan-work/deliver-work/review-work/workflow-evaluation tests, catalog-installation tests and diff checks. Record host-specific reviewer restrictions accurately; no fixture-only result is claimed as live delivery evidence.
- [ ] AC6: After authorized installation, verify the intended source revision, installed links/content and affected host discovery. Source acceptance and installed acceptance are separately recorded.

Delivery target: reviewed shared skill source, required validation, authorized installation and readback. The commands and scenarios are planned; this planning issue installs nothing.

## Meaningful deferrals

No automatic review service, new model benchmark, bulk issue rewrite or project-rule adoption. Hub adoption and the bounded Guide pilot live in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/657. Existing #70/#74/#77/#87/#103 retain their distinct measurement, review orchestration and findings work.

## Assessment

Complexity medium; uncertainty medium; impact high because shared workflow instructions affect delivery across projects. Ready for bounded policy definition and behavioral fixtures; project adoption waits for accepted source and installed readback. Scope is one coherent portable planning/review change with consumer compatibility, not a new governance framework. Alignment: current installed shared skills, README/AGENTS installation and reviewer rules, open #70/#74/#77/#87/#103, and the requested friction reduction. Reassess if a consumer requires stronger rules or installation includes unrelated changes.

Planning evidence: refreshed live issue/source records on 2026-09-30. Hub main `6654d0238429fcd5c85b567eb28ac9cba125d0e5`; shared policy `agent-skills@70037e79c489ffce4b687112b588fce4f6eef512`. This update is tracker planning only; no implementation checks ran. Planner reasoning setting: unknown (not exposed or user-stated).

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot. Claude Code: Opus at high effort; Codex: Sol at high reasoning. Start only the permitted next step after verifying the issue’s prerequisites.
**Work surface:** Backend

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Opus (`opus`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `high` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Opus (`opus`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Astra (`gpt-6-astra`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: verify the Claude Code model picker, effort and reviewer profiles at pickup; no Claude session was inspected. | Verified: current tool schema lists the selected model and level; future start-session access and reviewer restrictions remain provisional until pickup. |
| Checkpoints | Before fast-forwarding the installed catalog or installing skills, follow the owning repository's checkpoint and present affected running sessions and changes; do not lower the review rules used for this change | Before fast-forwarding the installed catalog or installing skills, follow the owning repository's checkpoint and present affected running sessions and changes; do not lower the review rules used for this change |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/113. I started this session on Opus at high effort. issues.title: Require separately tracked contracts and explicit human approval in planning and delivery
```
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make new or changed boundary contracts visible as separate GitHub issues, with human approval of the exact candidate before adoption or dependent implementation. Apply a portable procedure in shared planning/delivery guidance; consuming repositories retain their contract formats and validation commands. This is selected backlog work, not an installed policy.

## Smallest useful implementation

Update the canonical planning/delivery references used by plan-work, deliver-work and ordinary repository workflows. At scope assessment, identify new or changed APIs, shared data/event formats, persisted schemas and inter-module/provider boundaries. Reuse an unchanged approved contract; otherwise create one dedicated issue per coherent contract, identify its canonical artifact/version, owner and consumers, and add native blocked-by links from consumers. Keep contract definitions in their canonical source, with issue links and acceptance instead of conflicting copies.

Use the lifecycle: identify → dedicated issue → draft definition and examples → explicit human approval of exact candidate → normal source review/CI/merge → readback and consumer unblock. Draft preparation is permitted before approval; adoption and dependent product behavior are not. Record artifact path, version, candidate commit/content digest, human approver, approval statement/time and durable evidence. Definition changes invalidate approval; unchanged approved content can be reused. The approved policy must define compatibility/versioning expectations and how amendments/supersession remain traceable.

Do not accept issue closure, labels, agent review, silence or general implementation authorization as contract approval. Shared user/agent GitHub credentials do not independently prove human authorship. Specify a verifiable approval channel and its trust requirements; where enforcement is procedural, say so. A future machine-readable approval record or trusted check has its own defined owner and schema before use. Reuse consuming-repository enforcement findings rather than inventing a shared service.

Coordinate with architecture/backlog alignment in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/72. Trusted review-check investigation https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/77 is related, not a requirement to introduce unattended orchestration. Hub adoption/enforcement is https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep plan-work/deliver-work explicit-invocation behavior. Respect tracker-write authority; read-only work proposes the issue and dependencies without creating them. No auto-installation of skills, policy rollout to unrelated repositories, agent sessions, account changes or live protection changes. Human contract approval does not waive independent source review, CI, UI approval where applicable, installation or device authority. A repository's guide UI exemption does not imply contract approval.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] Shared guidance defines contract triggers, unchanged reuse, separate issue ownership, native dependencies, exact-version human approval, invalidation and source/readback closure rules.
- [ ] Each contract issue has outcome/scope, producers/consumers, canonical artifact/version, examples, compatibility/unknown/failure behavior, human approval pending/evidence and source acceptance. Label names remain repository conventions; no label alone grants approval.
- [ ] Behavioral scenarios cover missing contract issue, missing/stale/agent-authored approval, amended definition, unchanged reuse, an undeclared boundary discovered during delivery, unavailable approval evidence and read-only tracker authority. They also cover the guide UI exemption without bypassing contract approval.
- [ ] Reconcile planning and delivery guidance so both stop dependent adoption at the same gate and prepare a concrete candidate before asking the owner. Record any bootstrap approval requirement for new approval-record schemas without circular self-approval.
- [ ] Run current agent-skills AGENTS validation and relevant workflow behavior tests from an isolated delivery worktree; independently review the same committed candidate. Report source validation separately from fresh-host behavioral qualification, which needs authorization to launch/install.
- [ ] The owner approves the proposed policy wording and approval mechanism before it is put into effect. Record its exact revision. Source delivery does not imply personal skill installation.

Delivery target: source-only shared guidance and tests, through the repository's normal delivery gates. All acceptance is planned.

## Meaningful deferrals

Do not build a generic governance service or deploy credentials/check publishers. Hub owns its local qualification and enforcement through https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/542 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240. Other repositories adopt the portable rule through separately authorized local changes.

## Assessment

Planning, 2026-09-26. Canonical agent-skills main: 97cd2316d3d0f55f96b0328a89bea1741d725b89. Complexity medium; uncertainty medium around verifiable approval with shared credentials; impact high because the rule changes delivery authority. Backlog, ready for policy design; dependent adoption waits for an accepted mechanism. Reassess at pickup against current guidance and related issues.

issues.title: Keep feature maps current and verify that checks detect meaningful failures
issues.body:
## Outcome and real setup

A behavior change updates the verification knowledge needed to inspect it, and important checks demonstrate that they catch the relevant failure. Agents can distinguish a product defect from missing or stale verification support.

Initiative: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/488
Phase: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/492

## Smallest useful implementation and dependencies

- Add a concise verification-maintenance checkpoint to existing planning/delivery methods and conditional references, using `writing-for-agents`.
- For changed behavior, locate the owning feature map/recipe and update affected entrypoints, fixtures, actions, observations and artifact expectations in the same authorized source delivery. Keep product acceptance and issue status in their current owners; do not create a central duplicate feature database.
- Classify failed verification as product behavior, harness/tooling, stale instructions, unavailable environment or unmet acceptance. Preserve uncertainty when evidence does not distinguish them.
- Use focused negative controls for high-value changed behavior: a known bad result must fail and a correct reference must pass. Select checks by risk rather than requiring mutation of every edit or duplicating implementation details.
- For repeated mistakes, prefer a proportionate type constraint, lint/check, boundary test or driver capability where it prevents the cause. Avoid growing rules indefinitely or silently broadening a task to fix unrelated failures.
- Keep maintenance ownership in each app. Initial feature maps/negative controls are accepted in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/494, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/193, https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/118 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/495; subsequent product changes maintain those artifacts.

No required source prerequisite blocks independent preparation. Coordinate overlapping files with their current owner.

[Boundary checks #81](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/81) owns the particular SDLC entrypoint guard. [Grader isolation #82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/82) owns access-based evaluation isolation. Reuse their outcomes where applicable without expanding those issues here.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- [ ] A changed-feature scenario updates only affected verification knowledge and preserves authoritative acceptance ownership.
- [ ] Product failure, stale recipe, missing harness capability and unavailable host produce distinct truthful outcomes.
- [ ] A meaningful negative control fails; the reference passes. A low-impact prose change avoids unnecessary executable tests.
- [ ] Repeated-failure guidance selects a structural prevention mechanism where justified and returns unrelated repairs for separate scope.
- [ ] A case selected from real delivery evidence is traced to its human disposition and an appropriate maintained check, or a recorded deferral; tuning examples are not reported as unseen evaluation cases.
- [ ] Missing proof does not become success, screenshots do not replace assertions, and simulated transport does not become physical acceptance.
- [ ] Project details load conditionally; the shared method does not copy app commands into a competing source.

## Feed observed failures into maintained checks — clarified 2026-09-28

Post-delivery clarification: consume selected failures from authorized ordinary delivery evidence and [Hub #492's independently scoped manual follow-up](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/492). [#44's formal discovery and comparison](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/44) are postponed and are not an input dependency or active work under this issue. This clarifies future use without changing the completed source delivery or its recorded acceptance. For each accepted case, retain its source revision, expected versus observed behavior, evidence pointer and human disposition in existing verification evidence. Choose a proportionate product test, driver assertion, instruction scenario or reviewer-calibration case according to what failed; do not turn every user correction into a new global rule. A reference to a calibration case does not authorize the postponed #44 calibration exercise.

A selected deterministic check must reject the evidenced bad behavior and accept a valid reference. Judgment-dependent failures retain the human criterion and scoring limits. Cases used to tune a workflow or grader are development/regression evidence, not untouched holdouts. Record a reason when a case is deferred or unsupported. Source guidance and illustrative fixtures can ship before real discovery/adoption results; later product deliveries apply the checkpoint. It applies within authorized work and routes unrelated repairs to their owner; it grants no transcript access, model calls or automatic retrospective scan.

## Assessment and next action

Complexity: medium; uncertainty: low; impact: medium. Ready for source work when requested. Source guidance can proceed independently; actual application-map adoption is evidenced by the adapter deliveries and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/497.

## Validation and finish line

Finish line: merged method/reference changes with focused scenario and structural checks plus the full current agent-skills suite. Do not execute catalog-bundled scripts merely for validation or claim that static fixtures measure runtime effectiveness.

## Meaningful deferrals

No full mutation-testing rollout, periodic whole-repository scan, global lint rewrite or new feature-management service. Revisit broader automation after repeated observed failures justify it.

## Delivery boundary

This is planned work, not completed verification. Issue creation authorizes no implementation or launch. During later authorized source delivery, follow the owning repository's current instructions, preserve unrelated work, obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, require applicable current-head CI, use the guarded merge procedure and verify merged-main checks before source closure. Required UI approval remains separate from optional hands-on use.

issues.title: Restyle the guide and atlas in the Neon skin
issues.body:
Owner: Hub guide and atlas source.

## Outcome

Restyle the public work guide and the atlas in the Neon Geometry Wars skin, readable on a phone. Build it so a later skin is a new set of token values, not new templates or generator changes.

V1 ships one skin. The alternate skin and a skin picker with a saved preference are deferred to a separate issue.

## Scope

- **Tokens.** Guide and atlas styles use CSS custom properties named for their roles (surfaces, text, borders, selection, pending, status, diagram edges, radius, type scale, spacing). The Neon skin supplies their values for dark and light. Fixed-meaning colors (cyan Hub, magenta Nanoleaf, lime Pixoo, status colors) live in a separate token set that skins don't override.
- **Decoration.** Neon's artwork, glow, opening and streak are scoped to the skin. CSS animations only, with no JavaScript render loop or timers. Decoration sits on borders and artwork, never on text or dependency edges, and never signals live agent or device activity. Starting values: a ~2 s opening and a ~1 s streak every 25 s; tune by eye.
- **Motion off.** A pause control and `prefers-reduced-motion` stop all decorative motion. Print shows no decoration.
- Change the generators and assets (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`), not generated output. Bundle artwork; add no remote requests.
- If [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196)'s brief dialog or [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197)'s status line has merged, style it too. Neither blocks this issue.

## Acceptance

1. At 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide (header, navigation, cards, issue badges, status, inline diagrams) and the atlas use the Neon skin. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as `docs/sdlc.md` requires; the guide needs no approval.
2. Colors in guide and atlas styles come from tokens. A check fails on color literals outside the token files.
3. Pause and reduced motion stop all decorative motion. Every page stays readable and usable with motion off. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls.
4. The guide README has a short section listing the tokens and how to add a skin.
5. Existing checks pass, plus the checks in AC2 and AC3.

Evidence: before/after screenshots at 390 and 1440 px in the PR, and these runs:
- guide: `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`
- atlas: `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas lives outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies. No product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result.

This issue absorbs #86. [#181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181) is not a prerequisite; it can adopt these token names for the apps later.

Out of scope: the nine Archify architecture viewers (they keep Archify's styling), the alternate skin and picker, composition comparisons, the finish-kit fingerprint, frame-rate budgets and phone measurements, the [#73](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/73) connector fix, React adoption ([#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182)) and publication (#87).

Assessment: complexity medium (two generators, token conversion, motion), uncertainty low, impact low (reversible styling). Ready.

issues.title: Deliver shared Linux playback with a separate Sony HT-A9 source
issues.body:
## Outcome

Deliver the Linux-native shared playback module and the first Sony HT-A9 source module together, in one issue and PR. The iPhone continues playing Apple Music to the HT-A9 over AirPlay; BUNNY reads metadata and sends qualified controls. No Windows helper or audio routing through the hub is needed.

Owner decision, September 24, 2026: consolidate [#228](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/228) here while preserving separate modules and an architecture that supports future music sources. This combines delivery, not the two responsibilities. [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) remains deferred Windows integration.

## Architecture to preserve

- **Shared playback module:** owns the normalized snapshot, observation freshness, authenticated snapshot/command routes and command results. It accepts source observations and delegates commands through a small typed interface. It must not import Sony protocol code or interpret Sony response fields.
- **Sony source module:** owns the configured receiver endpoint, polling, Sony field normalization and supported command calls. Endpoint details and raw Sony responses stay inside this module. The hub composes and stops both modules.
- **Future sources:** retain stable neutral source ids, source-scoped observations, optional metadata and declared controls. Bind commands to the requested source id; consumers must not depend on Sony fields or receiver URLs. The design must show how another adapter can keep its own snapshot/freshness and how one explicit selection controls presentation and routing. When multiple sources arrive, a newer observation or unavailable selected source must never silently select another source. Adding an adapter must not require rewriting the shared service or consumer contract.
- **First implementation:** one configured Sony source, selected explicitly by configuration. Keep the interface small and the snapshot in memory. No plugin discovery, generic source manager, dynamic switching UI, separate daemon or playback database. A second real adapter and multi-source runtime/selection behavior are deferred; the architecture must leave room for them.

## Initial behavior

- Poll `getPlayingContentInfo` around every two seconds, with a documented timeout and no overlapping reads. Normalize title, artist, optional album, playback status and supported controls. A successful unchanged read refreshes observation time; failures do not. Use documented available/stale/unavailable rules and start unavailable until the first successful observation.
- Expose authenticated `GET /api/playback/v1/snapshot` and `POST /api/playback/v1/commands` through existing hub read/control and request-validation boundaries. The snapshot includes its source id and observation time/age. Preserve current controller-registration restrictions; the privately configured Sony endpoint is not a client-supplied URL proxy. Playback remains separate from agent lifecycle/state exports.
- Implement qualified pause, next and previous. Play/resume stays unsupported until separately qualified. Preserve sent/failed/uncertain outcomes, unsupported/unavailable failures, request correlation, small bounded duplicate suppression and one command at a time. No automatic write retries or pending-command replay after restart.
- Start with text metadata and snapshot polling. [#39](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/39) owns song-transition detection, track comparison/identity and lighting effects. [playback artwork story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) owns artwork acquisition. Neither feature blocks this delivery. Subscriptions, SSE, precise progress and repeat detection are outside this first version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Source and the issue-linked design preserve the module boundary above. Document a concrete future two-source flow: independent freshness, explicit selection, source-bound commands and no silent fallback. A simple non-Sony fake can use the same interface without changing the shared module; no second production integration is required.
- [x] **AC2.** One focused suite using a fake Sony endpoint covers metadata/status, missing fields, unchanged observations, unavailable/non-AirPlay input, timeout and reconnect. Use controlled-clock checks for freshness; avoid duplicating the same scenarios in separate service and adapter suites.
- [x] **AC3.** Verify authentication, the configured source target, unsupported controls, duplicate next, concurrent commands and uncertain outcomes. No command is redirected or automatically resent.
- [x] **AC4.** Add proportionate playback validation to docs/development.md and CI and pass the required hub/shared checks. Document configuration, the API and module extension points; correct Windows-first architecture wording, including ADR 0004. Preserve historical qualification facts. Atlas regeneration and work-guide publication are not completion gates for this feature.
- [x] **AC5.** After separate installation/control authorization, verify a real iPhone AirPlay track change reaches the hub within a few seconds and pause reaches the phone. Record actual effects and timing separately from fake/HTTP evidence.

## Evidence, dependencies and follow-ups

Completed input: [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) and the [HT-A9 qualification record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md). It established WSL HTTP/WebSocket access, metadata, optional artwork and phone-confirmed pause/next/previous. Previous restarted the current song; selecting the preceding song, play/resume and Docker behavior were not established. Position/duration were absent. This covers the tested AirPlay path, not other receiver inputs or arbitrary Windows playback.

Outcome: open any issue in the guide on a phone or desktop, pick an action and copy a short prompt that starts that work in an existing Codex or Claude app. Plan starts the `plan-work` skill; Implement starts `deliver-work`.

## Scope

- Selecting an issue badge (`a.issue[data-issue]`) opens one native `<dialog>` with the repository, number, title, a GitHub link and four actions: Explain, Plan, Implement and Review. Each action shows its prompt in a read-only textarea with a Copy button. Update the search hint that says issue links open GitHub.
- Build prompts in the browser from the badge's existing key, URL and title. Reference the full issue URL and embed no snapshot context: the agent reads the live issue and the repository's AGENTS.md.
- Prompt templates. Delivery may tune the wording but keeps the skill names and scope limits:
  - Explain: `Explain <issue URL> ("<title>"). Read the issue and the repository's AGENTS.md first. Read-only: don't change files, branches or GitHub.`
  - Plan: `Use the plan-work skill for <issue URL>. Planning only: return proposals and don't change the tracker until I approve. If plan-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Implement: `Use the deliver-work skill to deliver <issue URL>. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Review: `Review the open pull request for <issue URL>. If there isn't exactly one, ask me which revision to review. Read-only: report findings without changing files or GitHub.`

2. Each prompt uses the full issue URL. Explain and Review state read-only scope; Plan names `plan-work` and planning-only scope; Implement names `deliver-work`. Titles render as text, not markup.
3. Copy writes the prompt to the clipboard. If the Clipboard API is denied or unavailable, including when the guide is opened from `file://`, the textarea text is selected for manual copying.

Evidence: one new `check_guide.cjs` case covering these criteria at 390 px, plus the existing `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` runs. No live agent or device test.

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md) and the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). issues.title: Support best-effort Codex current status across successive turns
issues.body:
## Outcome
Make ordinary successive Codex Desktop turns in Ubuntu WSL show Working, Finished and Working again through the shared monitor. V1 uses explicitly best-effort current status; reliable event history is a separate future capability.

## Evidence and accepted policy
The installed provider emits unknown ordering; the reducer intentionally makes successive unordered turns ambiguous. The source reproduction start(turn-one), stop(turn-one), start(turn-two) leaves activity unknown and the previous notice uncleared. Synthetic qualified ordering makes the same sequence pass. See [Pixoo #34 diagnosis](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34#issuecomment-5769993937).

The owner accepted receipt order as a best-effort choice for a previously unseen valid turn start. This is a deliberate revision of the current conservative policy, not authoritative provider order. A delayed unseen start can temporarily select the wrong turn or prematurely clear a notice. Native turn IDs remain opaque. Do not fabricate provider sequence numbers or imply reliable history.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- [x] A valid start with usable session/turn identity for a previously unseen turn selects that turn and sets activity active. A matching stop completes it and retains a completion notice without claiming success or readership.
- [x] A new selected turn clears only previous completion notices covered by each consumer's clearOnNewTurn policy. Manual dismissal remains notice/consumer-scoped; unresolved approval/input attention remains independent.
- [x] Known superseded-turn events and unchanged duplicates cannot overwrite current activity or restore cleared notices. Bound remembered identities; specify behavior when that bound is exhausted, including limits on rejecting very old events.
- [x] Missing identity or contradictory evidence remains visibly unknown. Preserve freshness timeout, restart uncertainty and session separation. Document the limitation for previously unseen delayed starts.
- [x] Existing sessions stuck in ambiguity recover through a valid fresh start under the new policy without deleting the database, labels, unrelated notices or attention. Provide a supported compatibility path if persisted format changes are needed.
- [x] Preserve available event/session/turn identity and genuine ordering evidence. Clearly separate observations, best-effort current-state calculation and the bounded diagnostic journal. No claim of complete durable event history or retroactive reliability.
- [x] Both Pixoo and Nanoleaf consume the shared result with their existing independent policies. Hooks remain silent, private, bounded, fail-open and independent of devices; preserve existing CLI/Claude compatibility through regression checks without expanding live-client qualification.
- [x] Package the fix reproducibly with version/hash/source receipt and concise installed-update instructions. No new installer, runtime-owner relocation or live database reset.

## Verification
Map the criteria to provider-to-reducer and packaged-hook regressions covering start/stop/next-start, delayed starts and stops, duplicate delivery, two sessions, bounded identity retention, restart, recovery from existing ambiguity, acknowledgment isolation and differing consumer policies. Retain privacy, authentication and hook-deadline checks. Use real consumer code with fake device transports. Synthetic ordering alone cannot satisfy the ordinary provider-path regression. Installation and the short real Desktop/Pixoo retest remain in Pixoo #34.

## Dependencies and coordination
Delivered Hub #2/#3/#8 contracts/state/setup are inputs; this is a focused follow-up, not a reopening of those deliveries. [Pixoo #34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34) consumes this fix and an installed update before resuming its lifecycle acceptance. Manual task reset and reliable history do not block #34.

Coordinate shared tests, packages and guide inputs with [Hub PR #135](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/135). Shared files are coordination, not a dependency on performance qualification. No required input from future history work.

## Exclusions
Reliable event capture/history/replay, new client/platform certification, frontend redesign, device rendering changes and an extended performance programme. Per-task manual reset is a separate follow-up.

## Assessment and readiness
Planning baseline: Hub main 25590e9c95ce334a516d2de0494584d67ea15a26 and observed installed failure, September 22, 2026. Complexity high: cross-process events, persisted state and two consumers. Uncertainty medium: bounded retention and compatibility details require design, while product tradeoff and reproduction are established. Impact medium: shared displayed status and notices; permission boundaries unchanged. Ready for implementation planning. Review transition/concurrency and persistence behavior within independent reviews. Reassess if required client identity is absent, a storage migration is necessary, or scope/base changes.

## Delivery and planning
Source-only delivery. Publication does not start implementation, installation, agent sessions or device operations. Use the assigned issue number for a new OpenSpec change under `openspec/changes/`; revise affected specifications and document consequential policy decisions before implementation. Preserve the archived earlier changes. Follow current AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: isolated work, relevant tests, independent Standards and Specification reviews, applicable CI, guarded merge and merged-main verification. Publish new versioned artifacts rather than replacing released bytes. Synchronize the maintained Hub work guide during delivery; public publication remains separate.

Planning reasoning setting: unknown. No agents were dispatched for this planning publication.

## Delivery evidence
Source delivery completed in [PR #144](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/144), merged as `013b829a851277cd0cfbaeaba6d6d0dfc32727c7`. Its tree matches reviewed head `b1eff926ed56a8264881023c814291da8d92b7c0`. Both independent reviews passed after the documented corrections; all six PR and all six merged-main jobs passed. Main receipts: [Checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35682328106) and [Work guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35682328098). GitHub recorded closure at merge time; this completion update follows verified main CI and artifact publication.

Published [agent-state 2.0.0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/agent-state-v2.0.0) and [Hub 0.2.0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/hub-v0.2.0), each with archive, checksum and merged-source receipt. Fresh merged-source builds and both CI Python jobs reproduce the reviewed hashes; downloaded release assets were verified byte for byte. Snapshot and storage formats remain 1.0.

Evidence includes 113 state tests, 70 Hub tests, both-language contract consumers, protected packaged hooks, reproducible isolated archives, real Pixoo/Nanoleaf projections and the 12-scenario compatibility check. The 11-task OpenSpec change is synchronized and archived. Private guide completion merged in [PR #146](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/146) at `2855be7af01265e82012e131838e94d45c83e62f`. Its tree matches the independently reviewed candidate; local generation, five maintenance tests, browser/print and no-drift checks pass. All 13 paths are guide-only and both PR/main workflow filters were verified under the documented CI exception. Public guide publication, installation and the real Desktop/Pixoo retest remain separate. Pixoo #34 owns installed acceptance; reset #138 and history #139 are excluded.

issues.body:
## Outcome
Install or remove shared monitoring reversibly while preserving unrelated hooks and existing Nanoleaf behavior.

## Scope
Deliver source tooling and a runbook for optional Windows/WSL installation, producer credentials and embedded-to-standalone migration. Live installation requires separate explicit authorization; Pixoo [divoom-app-upgrade#34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34) and Nanoleaf [codex-nanoleaf#30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30) own device acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Provide inspect/plan/apply/remove operations with a reviewable configuration diff, ownership markers, backups outside Git and idempotent fixtures for every qualified client.
- [x] Install one owned producer configuration per provider/source that feeds the chosen shared state owner. Preserve unrelated hooks/trust settings and do not weaken agent permission policies.
- [x] Preserve Nanoleaf's legacy hook path until an explicitly selected shared-input cutover passes its prerequisites. Cutover disables only owned duplicate ingestion paths; rollback restores the latest user configuration without resurrecting unrelated removed entries.
- [x] Coordinate a quiesced embedded-to-standalone state handoff with export/import, session/notice/revision preservation, producer endpoint updates and rollback. Verify no simultaneous state owners or competing device writers.
- [x] Document actual supported client versions, Windows/WSL invocation and reachability, trust review, credentials, startup/shutdown and failure recovery. No implicit host move or router/firewall changes.
- [x] Removal revokes owned producer access and removes only still-owned entries. Monitoring absence cannot block agents, ordinary media use or the legacy bridge after rollback.
- [x] Separate source tests, installation, real-client event coverage and visible-device receipts. Require a named installation owner and explicit future authorization before personal changes.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5)
- [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31)
- [codex-nanoleaf#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29)

## Verification
Isolated config merge/removal, ownership conflict, auth revocation, interrupted migration, state preservation, platform command and rollback fixtures. Do not run personal installation.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-8-shared-monitor-installation/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Prioritize qualified Windows/WSL Codex hook setup and expose inspectable, sanitized source/consumer configuration and health for the integration frontend. Reading setup status must not install hooks, change source ownership or start device activity.
- [x] Verify one identified event updates both consumers after explicit cutover, and rollback restores the selected legacy or embedded path without duplicate ingestion. Device participation/mode changes never disable agent permission safeguards or silently redirect the shared state owner.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.


## Owner delivery decision, September 21, 2026

The owner explicitly invoked deliver-work and selected Linux/WSL setup, matching the delivered host and current CI. Windows clients may use an explicitly configured WSL producer command; native Windows installation is outside this delivery. Preserve existing Windows hooks. Source delivery does not authorize personal installation, client launches, live state migration or device operation.

This task owns branch `codex/gh-8-shared-monitor-installation`, based on `a639e0a8ca79c1651e3acb9190c565af1c9c7fa9`, and OpenSpec `gh-8-shared-monitor-installation`. All three source prerequisites are closed. Assessment: high complexity and impact from reversible configuration, credentials and state-owner handoff; bounded compatibility questions will be tested against the released owning services. Independent Standards and Specification reviews, applicable CI and guide reconciliation remain required.


Source candidate: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/129. Independent review and current-head CI are in progress. Installation, real-client qualification and device acceptance remain separate.


## Source delivery verified, September 21, 2026

PR #129 merged as `f6bee907e06177c6dc8abde0075d73cc391784e9` after independent Standards and Specification approval and all five current-head CI jobs. All five merged-main jobs passed (Checks run 35659013909; Work guide run 35659013921). Local validation includes 64 hub tests, reproducible offline package tests, and pinned real Pixoo/Nanoleaf source checks for both projections, credentials, fenced handoff and rollback. OpenSpec is synchronized and archived.

Acceptance is source-only. No personal hooks, client sessions, live databases or physical devices were changed. Installed-client qualification and device acceptance remain separately authorized, with Pixoo #34 and Nanoleaf #30 owning device acceptance. Public guide publication remains pending separate authority. A linked guide follow-up will reconcile this saved completion state.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Record the accepted 8BitDo desktop-control direction and link the implementation and investigation backlog. This is a documentation deliverable; it does not implement the controls.

## Exact documentation scope

- Add `/home/jimmie/projects/agent-device-hub/docs/desktop-controls.md` with accepted defaults, vocabulary, ownership, qualification questions, delivery sequence and evidence boundaries.
- Update `/home/jimmie/projects/agent-device-hub/docs/architecture.md` with control profiles, button bindings, desk presets and Windows-local input handling through existing command owners.
- Update `/home/jimmie/projects/agent-device-hub/docs/roadmap.md` with required versus conditional prerequisites and the independent shortcut path.
- Add a discovery link in `/home/jimmie/projects/agent-device-hub/README.md` while retaining the actual implementation status.
- Link the resulting work from future-work guide #35; cross-reference #31 and #40 without duplicating their scopes or reversing dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Record the accepted decisions below and distinguish supported facts from future qualification.
- [x] **AC2.** Link all desktop-control tickets and explain the Codex-first gate for shared presets, without making basic Codex mouse shortcuts depend on shared monitoring, general controls or Music.
- [x] **AC3.** Preserve Nanoleaf Work/Quiet/Free and Pixoo Monitor/Media semantics. Desk presets orchestrate configured actions; they introduce no common device-mode enum or silent controller takeover.
- [x] **AC4.** Record hardware/input, app, transport and visible-device evidence separately.
- [x] **AC5.** Reconcile concurrent documentation changes, including PC lighting PR #59; preserve its separate scope and do not make it a prerequisite for desktop controls.
- [x] **AC6.** Validate links and applicable repository checks, obtain required independent reviews and deliver through the repository's guarded PR/main-CI process.

Documentation and backlog only: no product behavior or wire-contract delta, so no new OpenSpec capability is needed for this documentation ticket. Source packages, runtime code and installation paths are selected in their owning future implementation tickets.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 7, 2026. Source baseline: [hub main a7b1aa0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60), live prerequisite issues, and the user-confirmed decisions below. Uses the canonical [work-assessment contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/blob/22588b494cac646bd6eaa5e2f01b8d439ab6a60e/skills/deliver-work/references/work-assessment.md).

- **Complexity: low.** Four documentation files and tracker links, with no runtime behavior.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Accepted decisions and authoritative documentation paths are established.
- **Impact: low.** Documentation changes are reversible and cause no device/input operations.

**Evidence limits and unknowns:** Intervening documentation edits and current PR/main-CI status must be refreshed at delivery.

**Readiness:** Ready for documentation delivery when selected; no unfinished source prerequisite. This publication does not start that delivery.

### Planned acceptance evidence

All checks below are planned and unexecuted. Proposed paths and commands are not delivery receipts.

| Criterion | Planned verification and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Document review against the accepted decision list and official-source evidence; verify unknown hardware is still labeled unknown. |
| AC2 | Check each live issue link and both ends of required dependencies; ensure the shortcut path has no hub/general-control prerequisite. |
| AC3 | Compare proposed terms and examples with controller-contract.md and the native mode owners; reject invented global wire values. |
| AC4 | Review every evidence claim for its source, installation, input/app, transport or visible-device level; documentation alone proves none of the latter. |
| AC5 | Refresh base/head and inspect the four-file diff against concurrent PC-lighting documentation; independent review checks unrelated content is preserved. |
| AC6 | Run applicable Node 24 workflow checks and a local Markdown-link/whitespace check during delivery, then independent review, current-head CI and merged-revision main CI. These checks are planned and have not run for this ticket. |

**Review:** Independent Standards and Specification reviews; reconcile shared documentation with the owner of PR #59. No device specialist or physical acceptance is needed for prose.

**Operational handoff:** Repository documentation owner verifies the reviewed merge and main CI; revert documentation through normal review if needed.

**Reassessment triggers:** Refresh on changed scope or source baseline, qualification results that alter the approach, changed dependencies, repeated failures without progress, or blocking review findings. Preserve existing review/acceptance requirements when reassessing.

### Authoritative scope sources

- [Repository instructions](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md).
- [Architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md) and [accepted assistant direction](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-local-first-personal-assistant.md).

## Accepted decisions

Owner revision, September 22, 2026: keyboard A/B and the attached Dual Super Buttons are managed directly on the keyboard, outside B.U.N.N.Y. This supersedes the earlier requirement for editable A/B bindings in #65 version 1 and their inclusion in #70. It changes scope, not delivery status.

- The owner's preferred keyboard assignments are B=Wispr Ctrl+Win hold/release and A=Enter on a separate press. The authorized trial succeeded and both temporary assignments were cleared afterward. These are personal setup choices, not B.U.N.N.Y. defaults or installed-state claims.
- B.U.N.N.Y. does not discover, store, edit, dispatch, restore or use keyboard A/B or the attached Super Buttons as preset bindings. Wispr retains its own settings and speech processing. No further A/B integration or acceptance work is required.
- The first mouse mapping provides next task needing attention, command menu, previous task and next task within Codex. Preserve ordinary behavior outside Codex.
- Basic Codex mouse shortcuts can ship independently of the hub. Shared desk presets follow the Codex-first milestone and general-control definition, using an explicitly selected qualified control other than keyboard A/B or the attached Super Buttons.
- A manual change in a device's own app remains until the next explicit preset request. That request applies the next preset to participating supported devices.
- A control profile maps supported physical controls and gestures to actions, including application scope. A button binding is one such assignment. A desk preset defines explicit actions on participating lights and displays. Selecting a control profile alone sends no device commands.
- The later #70 editor covers qualified remappable controls within this boundary, with saved profiles, supported app/hub actions and custom keyboard shortcuts. Keyboard A/B and the attached Super Buttons remain excluded. Arbitrary scripts and multi-step macros remain outside the first customization release.

Preserve the existing CHOMPI bridge and vendor mappings; reuse its approach without treating its three MIDI bindings as an implemented 8BitDo/profile system. Keyboard A/B and the attached Super Buttons remain keyboard-owned and outside this integration.

Follow `AGENTS.md` and `docs/sdlc.md`. This ticket is future backlog definition. Creation authorizes no implementation, installation, startup registration, personal configuration, agent sessions, input injection or device operation. Future behavior changes require refined issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts, proportionate executable validation, independent reviews and the repository delivery gates. Installation and physical acceptance require a named owner and explicit authorization. Keep private settings, recordings, dictated/typed content and credentials outside Git and shared agent-state payloads.

## Required source prerequisites

None. This work can be selected independently of unfinished shared-hub delivery.

## Readiness

Ready to select later within the assessment boundary. Perform the listed investigations in a future session; their answers are not claimed here. Negative or incomplete qualification does not enable unsupported behavior.
