issues.title: Qualify N30 mouse controls for Codex
issues.body:
## Outcome

Qualify an existing supported route for the N30 mouse's four Codex actions. Keyboard A/B and the attached Super Buttons are outside B.U.N.N.Y.; their completed personal mapping trial is historical evidence only.

## Investigation scope

- Packaging identifies N30 model 85CA using 2.4 GHz. Operator unplug/reconnect inventory associates its receiver with `VID_062A&PID_4101`, with normal operation restored. The reported Codex package is `OpenAI.Codex` version `26.917.6896.0`.
- Use the existing PageUp/PageDown/Back/Forward outputs and an application-scoped Windows mapper. The owner accepted that those signals from other keyboards and mice also map within Codex. Preserve clicks, touch scrolling, typing, vendor configuration and the existing CHOMPI bridge. No receiver-specific suppression claim is required or made.
- Select one mapping owner, verify four Codex actions, normal behavior outside Codex and stop/restoration. Do not replace firmware, add a driver or invent a custom USB protocol.
- Record firmware, per-device attribution, controlled hold timing, reconnect/sleep recovery and CHOMPI coexistence as unknown. Persistent implementation and proportionate installation/lifecycle checks remain in #65/#66; no broader trial is required to close this personal-project research.
- Collect no typed/dictated content, arbitrary keystrokes, window titles or audio. No Wispr configuration or A/B mapping work remains.

## Expected evidence

- [x] **AC1.** A sourced per-control/per-connection capability matrix with supported, unsupported and unknown results.
- [x] **AC2.** A selected existing supported input/mapping route, action ownership and reversible setup plan.
- [x] **AC3.** Separate documentation/source evidence from authorized input-event and application acceptance results.
- [x] **AC4.** Explicit gaps and follow-up work for unsupported controls. A negative qualification may close research but does not make dependent support ready.

## Sources and current evidence

- [N30 product page](https://www.8bitdo.com/n30-wireless-mouse/) and [manual](https://download.8bitdo.com/Manual/Other/N30-Mouse/N30_Mouse_Manual.pdf?20220513=)
- [Codex command reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/commands#keyboard-shortcuts)
- [AutoHotkey 2.0.28 official release](https://github.com/AutoHotkey/AutoHotkey/releases/tag/v2.0.28)
- [Qualification candidate PR #143](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/143)
- [Dated trial receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/64#issuecomment-5770483024)

On September 23, 2026, after the corrected portable launcher was staged, the owner reported: "Everything passed and looks good." The requested checks were Up→next attention task, Down→command menu, Left/Right→previous/next task/tab, normal scrolling/Back/Forward in a separate browser, and stopping the trial so Down no longer opened the Codex menu. No exception or unavailable action was reported. This is aggregate owner acceptance, not a retained per-action trace. No reusable mapper, installer or startup entry was delivered by the trial.

The first native observer stopped before events on a device-change notification. Its correction was not run after the owner chose the simpler route. The first AutoHotkey launcher also stopped before mappings because it expected one manifest executable. The corrected launcher resolves a running window executable inside the installed package directory. Seven local selection fixtures and both scoped reviews passed; those are separate from the owner's subsequent Windows result. Failures remain recorded rather than treated as hardware rejection.

## Work assessment

Reassessed September 23, 2026 against the owner's accepted shared-key boundary, successful brief trial and main `a76b22db3497bcc1c92f6445add1356f8eb1820e`.

- **Complexity: medium.** Foreground targeting, shared input signals and mapping ownership still interact.
- **Uncertainty: low for this bounded route.** The four actions, outside-app behavior and stop/restoration passed; persistent lifecycle and other configurations remain unqualified.
- **Impact: medium.** Enabled hotkeys affect the same signals from all devices inside Codex and require a clear stop path.

**Readiness:** Qualification source delivered in [PR #143](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/143) at `c646f15edc508a9ebebd134809050dbe6f947f7a`. Independent Standards and Specification reviews approved the candidate; all six Depot checks passed on both the reviewed head and the merged revision. The owner authorized verifying Depot results through GitHub for this delivery because the job pages require sign-in. This completes #64, not implementation or installation of #65/#66.

### Acceptance evidence

| Criterion | Evidence and remaining condition |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Sourced matrix, partial browser traces, receiver inventory and installed version. Unknown firmware/per-device/hold and lifecycle details remain labeled. |
| AC2 | AutoHotkey 2.0.28 route selected. One Windows-local owner maps shared keys only while the installed Codex executable is active. Four actions, outside-app behavior and stop/restoration passed. |
| AC3 | Official docs, inspected source, synthetic selection fixtures and owner-reported live results remain separate. No task or dictated content retained. |
| AC4 | Explicit unqualified capabilities and downstream implementation/installation work; keyboard A/B excluded by owner choice rather than a negative hardware finding. |

**Review:** Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison. The operator supplied live results; no further input trial is pending for #64.

**Operational handoff:** #65 can use the selected shared-key route after this source delivery, with explicit scope disclosure and enable/disable behavior. #66 owns persistent installation and proportionate lifecycle acceptance. Preserve CHOMPI and vendor ownership.

**Reassessment triggers:** New firmware/app versions, connection or shortcut changes, a request for per-device isolation, conflicting events or review findings.

### Authoritative scope sources

- [Repository instructions](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md).
- [Desktop controls](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-controls.md) and [architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/architecture.md).

## Accepted decisions

Owner revision, September 23, 2026: use application-scoped shared keys for this personal project. PageUp/PageDown and Back/Forward from other input devices share the N30 mappings while Codex is active. Preserve normal behavior elsewhere. Per-device filtering and its wider qualification campaign are not required for this route. The owner authorized the brief trial and then reported that everything passed. This supersedes the earlier per-device route requirement; it does not prove receiver isolation or complete installation.

Owner revision, September 22, 2026: keyboard A/B and the attached Dual Super Buttons are managed directly on the keyboard, outside B.U.N.N.Y. This supersedes the earlier requirement for editable A/B bindings in #65 version 1 and their inclusion in #70. It changes scope, not delivery status.

- The owner's preferred keyboard assignments are B=Wispr Ctrl+Win hold/release and A=Enter on a separate press. The authorized trial succeeded and both temporary assignments were cleared afterward. These are personal setup choices, not B.U.N.N.Y. defaults or installed-state claims.
- B.U.N.N.Y. does not discover, store, edit, dispatch, restore or use keyboard A/B or the attached Super Buttons as preset bindings. Wispr retains its own settings and speech processing. No further A/B integration or acceptance work is required.
- The first mouse mapping provides next task needing attention, command menu, previous task and next task within Codex. Preserve ordinary behavior outside Codex.
- Basic Codex mouse shortcuts can ship independently of the hub. Shared desk presets follow the Codex-first milestone and general-control definition, using an explicitly selected qualified control other than keyboard A/B or the attached Super Buttons.
- A manual change in a device's own app remains until the next explicit preset request. That request applies the next preset to participating supported devices.
- A control profile maps supported physical controls and gestures to actions, including application scope. A button binding is one such assignment. A desk preset defines explicit actions on participating lights and displays. Selecting a control profile alone sends no device commands.
- The later #70 editor covers qualified remappable controls within this boundary, with saved profiles, supported app/hub actions and custom keyboard shortcuts. Keyboard A/B and the attached Super Buttons remain excluded. Arbitrary scripts and multi-step macros remain outside the first customization release.

## Ownership and delivery boundary

Owner: `agent-device-hub`, with Windows-local input handling and commands routed through the owning app/controller services. Preserve the existing CHOMPI bridge and vendor mappings; reuse its approach without treating its three MIDI bindings as an implemented 8BitDo/profile system. Keyboard A/B and the attached Super Buttons remain keyboard-owned and outside this integration.

Follow `AGENTS.md` and `docs/sdlc.md`. The owner selected this qualification for delivery. That authorizes its source work and scoped tracker updates, not installation, startup registration, new personal configuration, agent sessions or unapproved input injection/device operation. Future behavior changes require refined issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts, proportionate executable validation, independent reviews and the repository delivery gates. Installation and physical acceptance require a named owner and explicit authorization. Keep private settings, recordings, dictated/typed content and credentials outside Git and shared agent-state payloads.

## Required source prerequisites

None. This work can be selected independently of unfinished shared-hub delivery.

## Readiness

The accepted shared-key route passed the brief owner-operated Windows trial. Source review, current-head CI and merged-revision checks are complete. Reusable implementation (#65) and persistent installation (#66) remain separate; unsupported or untested capabilities do not become enabled by this qualification.

issues.title: Deliver Codex-first shared monitoring and integration controls
issues.body:
## Outcome
One qualified Codex lifecycle event reaches one shared state owner and produces consistent task status on Pixoo and Nanoleaf. A common frontend lets the user inspect and manage those Codex integrations. General device control without agent interaction is a later goal.

## Accepted direction
- Keep Node.js/TypeScript shared services and Pixoo, and the Python Windows Nanoleaf worker. Preserve performance through measured release budgets.
- Shared state code belongs in this repo from the start, initially packaged into Pixoo's backend and later run by a standalone host. The frontend belongs here in apps/dashboard, using the delivered Nanoleaf visual language and useful interaction patterns as its starting point.
- Each device integration consumes the shared feed and retains its own rendering policy, private state and designated writer. One stalled device must not delay another or block Codex.
- Preserve existing local MCP delivery and other coordinators' work. This planning goal does not take over their issues or installed state.

## First-phase frontend
Show Codex sessions, attention, retained notices, freshness, collector/consumer health and device integration state. Support explicit user labels, monitor-only notice dismissal, supported per-device participation/modes and task/project mappings. Device modes keep their existing meanings. Existing advanced editors remain usable; full wall-map/playlist-editor migration, custom effects and exact optical previews are not initial gates.

## Delivery stages
1. Qualify Codex Desktop/CLI and Windows/WSL paths in #2; retain provider-neutral contracts and existing Claude source fixtures without making a new Claude installed rollout the Codex milestone.
2. Deliver #3 and Pixoo #29/#31/#37, then Pixoo #32/#33 and Nanoleaf #29/#49 after their prerequisites.
3. Deliver standalone hosting #5 and reversible owned-hook setup/migration #8. Prove one active state owner and no duplicate legacy/shared ingestion.
4. Deliver #6's Codex-integration frontend using the owning controller APIs; deliver #13's shared MCP composition without duplicating existing local tools.
5. Pass the cross-repository source suite #9 and performance qualification. Then use the separately authorized Pixoo #34 and Nanoleaf #30 acceptance stages for real Codex hooks and visible behavior.

## Completion criteria
- [x] Existing issue scope, live prerequisites and ownership are refreshed. Issue bodies/specs/docs are reconciled before implementation; completed or independently active work is preserved.
- [x] All first-phase source features have reviewed merged revisions and applicable validation evidence. UI candidates have explicit human approval.
- [x] The same synthetic task sequence reaches both consumers and the common frontend through embedded and standalone hosts; duplicates/outages/reconnect cannot invent success, repeat expired effects or take over Media/Free behavior.
- [x] Frontend integration controls use protected owning services, preserve identity/revisions and show pending/conflict/uncertain results. Inspection is free of device mutations.
- [x] Performance budgets pass across required source/runtime profiles; a third fake consumer demonstrates extensibility without adding new production hardware.
- [x] Source completion is reported separately from installed acceptance. Full Codex-first acceptance needs the approved real Windows/WSL client and device evidence. Claude-specific outstanding criteria remain tracked and are not falsely closed by the Codex milestone.
- [x] General agent-independent controls remain deferred; no implementation goal or installation is silently started by backlog definition.

## Scope ownership
This is the cross-repository goal and priority record. Child issues retain their own acceptance, OpenSpec identity, review and completion conditions. This record does not waive a child's remaining Claude, physical, UI or prerequisite criteria. No giant cross-repository implementation PR is intended.

## Dependencies and delivery target
Planning is complete only when the bounded source stories and missing API/performance work are linked. Runtime completion depends on their source and separately authorized acceptance evidence. Current action is backlog alignment only.

## Delivery and authority
Planning/backlog definition only under the user's 2026-09-07 request. Do not start implementation, personal setup, agent sessions, hook changes or device operations from this issue publication. Future source work follows the repository's current AGENTS.md and SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, applicable checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, human approval for UI candidates, guarded merge and merged-source readback. Preserve other coordinators' work. Installation and physical acceptance require their separately scoped authorization.

issues.title: Define agent-independent device controls after Codex integration acceptance
issues.body:
## Outcome
In a second phase, expand the shared frontend into a general device-control application that works without an agent session.

## Scope and priority
The user selected Codex integration and manual frontend controls for that integration as the first goal. This issue records later planning for general power, brightness, scenes, media and other device-native controls. Preserve controls already delivered in device apps or local MCP work; do not postpone or undo that independent delivery.

## Acceptance criteria for planning
- [x] Begin after the Codex-first goal has its source, shared-frontend and authorized installed acceptance evidence; record any remaining gaps before advancing.
- [x] Inventory existing controller capabilities and choose the supported initial general-control set with the user. Identify missing device API work in the owning repositories instead of assuming every light/display supports every operation.
- [x] Define explicit manual takeover, restoration and interaction with ongoing Codex monitoring and device-specific modes. No global mode may silently overwrite all device intent.
- [x] Define frontend pages and narrow controller extensions using the same protected command owners, identity/replay rules and failure evidence. The frontend must not become another physical writer.
- [x] Reuse delivered visual components and domain editors as appropriate; define any integration or migration work separately. Exact live rendering, phone/remote access and language/repository migrations retain their own scope.
- [x] Create or refine bounded implementation issues in the hub and affected device repos only after the feature set is settled. Define source tests, human UI approval and separately authorized physical acceptance.

## Dependencies and readiness
Deferred until Codex-first shared monitoring and integration controls are accepted. The later feature set remains a user decision. Do not implement this phase or mark it ready as part of the current backlog alignment.

## Delivery target
Deferred planning definition; no new physical controls are implemented by this issue.

## Delivery and authority
Planning/backlog definition only under the user's 2026-09-07 request. Do not start implementation, personal setup, agent sessions, hook changes or device operations from this issue publication. Future source work follows the repository's current AGENTS.md and SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, applicable checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, human approval for UI candidates, guarded merge and merged-source readback. Preserve other coordinators' work. Installation and physical acceptance require their separately scoped authorization.

## Blocking goal
[Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32) owns the prior Codex-first goal and its acceptance milestone. Remain deferred until that milestone passes. This planning-only backlog item has no product spec delta yet; define issue-linked implementation changes after the later feature set is accepted.

## Desktop-control consumer

The accepted desk presets and explicitly configured preset bindings are defined in [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67) and [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68). They remain downstream of this general-control definition and the Codex-first milestone. Control profiles map inputs to actions; desk presets apply configured device actions without redefining native modes. Manual device changes remain until the next explicit preset request. Early Codex mouse delivery in [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#65](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/65) is independent of this milestone. These links define future consumers and add no implementation scope to the current milestone.

## Central BUNNY UI and future components, 2026-09-21

The user confirmed that general device control should extend the same central BUNNY application established by [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6). Preserve its Nanoleaf-derived visual language and reusable integration views.

- [x] Plan general controls within the existing shared navigation and component status/settings/control views, including operation without an active agent session. Each later user-facing BUNNY integration must adopt that same view pattern as its supported capabilities are delivered.
- [x] For each selected feature, record the component's capability and permission matrix, owning API/service, required UI work and verification. Unsupported capabilities remain explicit; a new component does not imply support for every lighting or media operation.
- [x] Keep routine supported controls in the central UI and define bounded follow-on issues for specialized editor integration where needed. Preserve existing editor links until their replacements are delivered and accepted.
- [x] Carry the reusable integration-view acceptance criteria from Hub #6 into the later implementation issues, including differing component capabilities, unavailable states, concurrent edits and inspection without writes. Retain the existing manual takeover, restoration and designated-writer boundaries.

This is an authorized planning refinement. The issue remains deferred behind [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32); choosing and implementing the later control set retains its existing acceptance and authorization requirements.


## Accepted definition, 2026-09-22

The user resolved the planning decisions in a grouped question round on 2026-09-22 and authorized the tracker changes and documentation PR below. The durable record is ADR 0005, `docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`, delivered with the linked hub PR. This section is the tracker summary; the ADR and the linked issues own the details.

**Codex-first gap record.** Hub #32 closed 2026-09-22. Nanoleaf #30 and Pixoo #34 installed acceptance, and Hub #8, #9 and #30, are closed. No remaining gap blocks this definition. The public guide edition is behind the merged source, which is a separate publication stage.

**Capability inventory at definition time.**

| Device | Native controller v1 capabilities declared | Delivered extension | General-control status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pixoo | Screen power (off pauses, on does not resume), brightness 0–100, media: playlist selection by ID (up to 100 IDs, no names) and pause/resume/stop/next/previous/clear. Scenes, zones, preview and modes unsupported. | Monitor/Media mode, filters, cadence | Supported now; UI in #151, names in Pixoo #67 |
| Nanoleaf | Mode set Work/Quiet/Free only. Power, brightness, media, zones, scenes and preview unsupported. | Layout, coverage, element/task assignment, project colors | Needs Nanoleaf #64 before UI in #153 |
| Tidbyt, LIFX, PC lighting | No controller delivered (#15/#16, #17/#18, #51/#53) | none | Unavailable; join through their existing issues and #56 |

**Initial general-control set.** Pixoo: power, brightness, playlist selection and the six playback actions, one guarded v1 command each; rendition selection stays an editor link. Nanoleaf: power, brightness and saved-scene activation after Nanoleaf #64 declares them. Hub MCP media tools are a separate issue, #152.

**Takeover, restoration and mode rules.**
- Power and brightness are mode-independent. The owning controller keeps its policies: Pixoo screen-off pauses; a Nanoleaf brightness command is an override that persists until the next explicit mode command.
- Content controls (Pixoo playlist and playback, Nanoleaf scenes) are disabled while the device presents agent status, with the reason and a one-click explicit switch to Media or Free through the existing mode control. No user action changes a mode as a side effect of another command, and no compound writes are submitted.
- Nothing restores automatically. Restoration is the existing mode command. The hub stores no baseline and runs no timer. Free-mode restoration baselines for presets remain #67.
- Nanoleaf scene activation is accepted only in Free, as a one-shot worker write with no polling after handoff.

**Pages and permissions.** Controls live only in each component's existing view; navigation is unchanged and no page commands more than one device. Availability is the product of controller-declared capability and the credential's existing control scope and device aliases; every disabled control names the missing capability or scope. The frontend remains a client of the hub route and never a physical writer.

**Vocabulary.** *General control*: an explicit user-issued supported device operation through the owning controller, independent of any agent session (avoid "manual control", "agent-independent control"). *Status presentation*: a device rendering agent status (Pixoo Monitor, Nanoleaf Work or Quiet). *Takeover*: the user selecting the device's content mode (Pixoo Media, Nanoleaf Free) so content controls apply; distinct from the contract's *external control*, a change made outside the controller. *Restoration*: an explicit return to status presentation through the existing mode command.

**Bounded implementation issues.**

| --- | --- | --- |
| [#151](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/151) | Pixoo general controls in the BUNNY component view | Ready |
| [Nanoleaf #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/64) | Native power, brightness and scene capabilities on the protected controller API | Ready |
| [#153](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/153) | Nanoleaf general controls in the BUNNY component view | Blocked by Nanoleaf #64 |
| [Pixoo #67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/67) | User-entered playlist names in the Pixoo integration extension, non-blocking | Ready |
| [#152](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/152) | Hub MCP media tools | Backlog, not blocked |
| [#154](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/154) | Pixoo hardware acceptance | Blocked by #151 |
| [#155](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/155) | Nanoleaf hardware acceptance | Blocked by #153 and Nanoleaf #64 |

Each implementation issue defines source tests, human UI approval where UI changes, and separately authorized physical acceptance. This definition authorizes none of that implementation, installation or device operation.

issues.body:
## Outcome
Provide one optional standalone hub host for shared agent state, registered controllers, APIs and future clients.

## Scope
Compose the shared state core and controller clients. Before this migration the state core can remain embedded in Pixoo. Standalone hosting is an explicit source/deployment stage, not a second simultaneously active collector.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Serve authenticated loopback APIs and revisioned snapshot/change feeds using the shared contracts. Keep agent-state health and each device's health independent.
- [x] Connect the Pixoo and Linux/WSL Nanoleaf controller APIs through bounded clients; support simulators and deterministic outages without credentials.
- [x] Route all commands to their existing owner. Isolate queues/failures per device so an offline Pixoo cannot block Nanoleaf; no direct protocol writer is added.
- [x] Implement one authoritative agent-state owner, whether embedded or standalone. Specify a quiesced, versioned export/import that preserves identities and revisions, switches producers and consumer endpoints, and supports rollback without two active owners or duplicate notices/effects. Exercise Pixoo #31's embedded/remote session-source facade: its renderer/browser must receive the new feed, and shared label/acknowledgment writes must reach the selected owner. Resume ingestion only after the selected owner and consumer routes are ready; fail explicitly if readiness or migration fails.
- [x] Preserve private data ownership across host changes; do not mount a shared SQLite database between Windows and WSL. Resolve reachability through explicit supported local endpoints without router/firewall changes or an implicit host switch.
- [x] On restart/reconnect, recover current snapshots and uncertain observations without replaying expired animations, missed pictures or ambiguous sent commands.
- [x] Package a reproducible host with isolated runtime storage, readiness, graceful shutdown and a controller compatibility matrix. Source completion does not install or start it on the user's machine.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3)
- [agent-device-hub#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4)
- [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37)
- [codex-nanoleaf#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28)
- [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31)

## Verification
Local integration with both fake controller clients, slow/offline isolation, auth, recovery, quiesced migration/rollback and one-owner checks. Verify Pixoo feed and acknowledgment routing through cutover, interrupted cutover and rollback; separately validate the installed Nanoleaf consumer cutover under [agent-device-hub#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8).

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-5-hub-host/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Planned after the local Codex control path. Shared monitoring, standalone hosting, collector migration, and the unified dashboard remain useful follow-on work; none is a prerequisite for the reusable local MCP module or device-local Codex acceptance. Preserve the existing behavior until any separately authorized migration.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Serve a common integration-management API for the shared frontend: source/consumer health, current task state, user labels and monitor acknowledgment, registered device capabilities, integration modes and controller-owned mappings/settings.
- [x] Route Pixoo monitor filters/modes and Nanoleaf supported integration settings through their owning APIs. Specify finite versioned integration extensions and compatibility fixtures; do not silently broaden released device API v1, pass native credentials to the browser or add a second device writer.
- [x] Keep shared source/package ownership in this repository across embedded and standalone hosting. The standalone application composes the same engine; Pixoo's backend remains a device service using its selected session-source facade.
- [x] Validate source/consumer/API responsiveness against the early budget artifact from [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) and preserve Linux-owned Nanoleaf state and its designated writer.

### Additional required dependencies
- [Nanoleaf integration-settings API](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/49) for the completed integration-management adapter.
- [Pixoo #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33) for completed monitor settings/mode operations. Host/core work with fakes can proceed independently; do not claim final controller integration until these APIs are delivered.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

## Owner delivery decision, September 21, 2026

The owner explicitly invoked deliver-work for this issue and selected Linux in WSL as the primary runtime. Native Windows runtime implementation and qualification are outside this delivery. Use configured authenticated local controller endpoints and private Linux storage; do not share controller databases, change a live installation or operate devices. This supersedes the earlier Windows-only wording and planning-only authority for this issue.

Host/core work may proceed while Pixoo #33 remains open. Nanoleaf #49 is now source-delivered through PR #63. Final Pixoo settings integration remains blocked on its owning API; do not invent or silently widen a controller contract.


## Owner memory-budget decision, September 21, 2026

The owner explicitly requested doubling the service RSS budget from 128 MiB to **256 MiB** and deferring budget re-evaluation and memory improvements to [Hub #123](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123). That follow-up is backlog work and does not block this issue. Preserve all original measurements and their failures against 128 MiB; a budget increase is not evidence of optimization. Other budgets, functional acceptance and integrated qualification remain unchanged.

Pixoo #33 has since closed through [PR #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/64). Its delivered API can now be integrated; this does not complete the host adapter or migration acceptance.

## Source acceptance, September 21, 2026

[PR #121](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/121) merged as `2c3bb4117bab0f845a95048b4ce72a49e915cfdc`. Both independent Standards and Specification reviewers approved final head `fdc277392179b7a6a7e7825566faada7cfb624c9`. All five PR jobs and all five merged-main jobs passed. Main evidence: [shared/product checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35653288866), [guide checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35653288926). The merged tree matches the reviewed candidate.

The Linux host provides scoped authenticated monitor/management APIs, independent bounded controller clients, Pixoo and Nanoleaf settings adapters, private durable ownership and supervised migration. The real pinned Pixoo simulator verified producer switching, its selected-source facade, label/acknowledgment routing, renderer revision and fresh-store rollback after accepted writes. Migration recovery tests preserve fences and original producer policy across failures. Readiness is bound to the live supervised Pixoo child and its selected configuration. Nanoleaf's actual owning controller fixture verified queued settings, application and replay.

Local validation includes 29 host tests, shared build/type/contract/state/MCP checks, reproducible offline package installation, seven specifications and six archived changes, 15 workflow tests and guide checks. The final synthetic API receipt retains 9,000 samples, zero failures and peak RSS 165.44 MiB against 256 MiB. It remains `qualified: false` for full integration. Original failed receipts and the earlier CI fixture failure remain recorded; the corrected current-head run passed.

This closes source delivery only. Nothing was installed, no live state was migrated and no device was operated. Installed cutover remains #8; full integrated qualification remains #30; budget reassessment and memory optimization remain nonblocking #123. [Guide companion #125](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/125) merged as `a639e0a8ca79c1651e3acb9190c565af1c9c7fa9` after both independent reviews, local guide checks and verified guide-only CI filtering. Guide-source synchronization is complete; public publication remains pending.

issues.title: Expose Nanoleaf integration settings and assignments to the shared frontend
issues.body:
## Outcome
Let the shared Codex-integration frontend inspect and change the existing Nanoleaf task-display configuration through the native Linux controller and retained Windows controller.

## Scope
Add a bounded, versioned machine API for existing integration settings and assignments that the mode-only API in [#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28) does not expose. Reuse the wall editor's application operations and the shared-session identity mapping from [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29). The shared frontend belongs to [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6); this issue owns Nanoleaf behavior and its adapter.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Publish a capability and permission matrix for current Work/Quiet/Free modes, Classic/Project layout, existing coverage settings, project-to-element reservations, task-to-project association and saved project colors. Only existing supported operations are in the first release; new animation presets, general power/brightness/scene control and preview playback are outside scope.
- [x] Expose a sanitized revisioned configuration/assignment projection with configured device IDs, stable element IDs, neutral shared task/project identities or explicit user-chosen labels, desired/pending state and bounded outcomes. Do not export local paths, automatic conversation titles, credentials or raw Codex metadata.
- [x] Route protected writes through the same application operations and Windows database coordination as wall/tray controls. Preserve request identity, principal/target scope, revisions, duplicate/conflict rejection, cancellation and possible prior effects. Do not silently widen the released shared controller v1 schema; specify a versioned extension and consumer fixtures.
- [x] Mode and assignment changes preserve task/effect epochs, reservations, current scene, pending edits and legacy/shared input selection. Inspecting or selecting an element cannot clear notices, mark a Codex task read, advance work or send a light command.
- [x] Validate cross-client edits against current revisions. Return actionable pending/conflict/unsupported/uncertain results; reconnect never automatically retries a write. The hub frontend cannot receive or borrow wall-editor/native credentials.
- [x] Support current Lines without waiting for the separate NL22 release. Coordinate with #41/#44 when their device identity and UI work lands; preserve per-device identity and modes, and require qualified support before exposing additional devices or combined-layout features.
- [x] Verify through isolated Python and shared consumer fixtures, concurrent wall/hub requests, synthetic identity mapping, privacy canaries and Windows/WSL forwarding. Run affected browser, workflow and Windows checks. Record source and physical evidence separately.
- [x] Update controller/integration guides and issue-linked OpenSpec scenarios, including the finite supported-operation matrix and versioning/rollback behavior.

## Dependencies
- [#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28): existing protected controller API.
- [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29): shared session identities and selected feed.
- [Hub #4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4): released controller contract.
- Related independent work: #18/#19/#20 advanced presentation, #41/#44 multi-device state/UI. Do not absorb those stories or require unimplemented presentation capabilities.

## Readiness and verification
Delivered through [PR #63](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/63), merged as `f12ac6653a9f3267fa9ef62a2d6667072183d8b3`. All nine PR jobs and all nine merged-main jobs passed. Independent Standards and Specification reviews found no actionable findings. Local validation passed 231 Python tests, including 15 integration-extension tests, 26 cross-language request fixtures and four receipt mappings, plus browser and workflow checks.

The selected contract is the Nanoleaf-owned `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` extension; released shared controller v1 remains unchanged. ADR 0007 governs native Linux ownership and retained Windows compatibility. The issue-linked OpenSpec change is synchronized and archived at `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-20-gh-49-integration-settings-api/`.

## Delivery and authority
The original September 7 publication authorized planning only. The subsequent explicit `$deliver-work` request authorized this source delivery, and the user accepted the Nanoleaf-owned extension recommendation. Source and tracker acceptance are complete. Guide-source synchronization is tracked in [Hub PR #118](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/118). Installation, frontend integration, physical acceptance and public guide publication remain separately scoped work; none was performed by this delivery.

## Goal and consumers
Part of [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5) integrates the adapter; [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6) owns the shared frontend. [Hub #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) verifies performance. General device controls remain [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31).

issues.title: Add monitor controls and shared Monitor/Media display ownership
issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Use #31's embedded/remote session-source facade for monitor rendering, browser state and shared label/acknowledgment operations, and expose effective Monitor/Media capabilities through [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37). Pixoo keeps mode policy, renderer, player and its serialized writer. Hub/browser/MCP clients use those commands. [agent-device-hub#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6) independently owns the shared overview.

## Outcome
Let the user manage agent monitoring in the app and choose whether the Pixoo displays monitoring or media, with one backend controlling all writes.

## Scope and source
Extend the existing browser, HTTP/SSE services, and player. Integrate the dashboard's selected device-rendering method only after qualification. Hooks continue observing in both display modes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Add a monitor panel with full session labels, provider/state, timestamps and observation age, collector health, short-label editing, project/session filters, retained-notice dismissal, and an exact 64×64 preview. Make filter effects and empty results clear. Apply the selected monitor view consistently to preview and display.
- [x] Label assignment is an explicit user action. Do not automatically copy prompts, titles, tool output, or private paths. Retained-notice dismissal changes monitor state only and cannot mark a chat read, approve an action, or close a GitHub issue.
- [x] Expose explicit Monitor and Media modes. Entering Monitor pauses playlist advancement. Starting media selects Media. Leaving Monitor leaves the playlist paused until the user explicitly resumes or starts media. Starting a media item/playlist is explicit playback intent.
- [x] Keep collecting agent events in either mode. Questions, approvals, turn ends, and errors never take over Media mode or send unsolicited monitor alerts to the display.
- [x] Route browser, player, dashboard, HTTP, and any MCP device operations through the same backend adapter and serialized operation queue. Mode switches invalidate obsolete generations, timers, and pending picture updates; a late completion cannot reclaim display ownership.
- [x] Use the rendering method and measured configurable cadence from the qualification issue. Coalesce updates to the latest desired view. Screen-off pauses/cancels display work according to #7; screen-on alone does not resume playback or trigger an unrequested monitor refresh.
- [x] On backend restart, retain the chosen view/mode and paused playback context, mark previously active sessions uncertain, and wait for explicit display activation before new physical writes. Bound reconnect retries and never replay missed dashboard pictures or old mode transitions.
- [x] Extend #8's validated commands, request IDs, revision handling, authoritative snapshots, and sequence-aware SSE reconnect/resync. Reject stale updates and conflicting duplicate commands. Preserve loopback defaults and the existing authenticated access boundaries; no generic raw-device endpoint.
- [x] Keep normal startup simulator-only. Document mode switching, paused playback, preview fidelity, recovery, and display ownership in `docs/agent-monitoring.md`, with affected product/ADR/OpenSpec links.

## Dependencies
- #31 and #32 provide session state and layout.
- #30 must resolve the supported method/cadence before final device integration is accepted. Browser and simulator work can proceed while those measurements are pending.
- #7 owns playback, generations, pause/resume, screen control, and recovery.
- #8 owns shared HTTP/SSE and command semantics; #9 owns the app UI being extended.
- #24 can later expose monitor controls through MCP. MCP and #17 are not prerequisites.

Additional shared prerequisites:
- [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37)

## Related monitoring work
Personal setup and end-to-end client/device acceptance belong to #34. This issue does not expand the existing MCP issues.

## Verification approach
Verify that the monitor view and shared label/acknowledgment operations continue through #31's owner cutover and rollback without creating local agent-state authority. Use browser tests with synthetic sessions and fake-device integration tests covering mode changes during upload, event bursts, attention during Media, explicit resume, screen-off/on, reconnect, restart, stale SSE, duplicate requests, and multiple clients. Prove one writer and no delayed upload from an obsolete mode.
Use isolated runtime data and the deterministic fake device. For executable changes, retain focused red/green evidence and run Node 24 `npm ci` and `npm run check`. For HTTP, UI, or startup changes, install Playwright Chromium and run `npm run test:browser`. OpenSpec/workflow changes also require `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow`. No real account or display is needed for source checks.

## Delivery target
Source-only. Physical qualification is a prerequisite for the final transport choice, not permission to operate the display during this issue. Installed-client and end-to-end physical acceptance remain separate.

## Planning and delivery
Before implementation, prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec proposal, affected capability deltas, tasks, and applicable design using the local planning root `openspec/changes/`. GitHub owns acceptance and delivery status; the specification owns capability scenarios. Follow [the repository SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), including isolated work, independent review, and current PR/main CI. This publication authorizes backlog records only.

Planned OpenSpec change: `gh-33-agent-monitor-controls`.
Local planning root: `openspec/changes/gh-33-agent-monitor-controls/`. Check active and archived changes for collisions before creating it.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Own the Pixoo integration operations used by both the existing app and Hub #6: monitor view/filter configuration, selected integration mode and effective participation. Shared user labels and notice acknowledgment still belong to the selected state owner.
- [x] Expose a finite protected versioned extension or existing compatible API for these operations through the controller boundary in #37. Preserve request/revision identity, replay/conflict behavior and sanitized snapshots; do not silently widen released shared device API v1.
- [x] Verify the shared frontend adapter with capability, current/pending mode, filter and conflict fixtures. Choosing Media is explicit non-participation in monitor presentation while collection continues; task events cannot take it over. The new frontend need not implement a general media-library/player UI for this goal.
- [x] Keep existing app controls and local MCP media delivery intact. This issue adds integration controls and preserves playback ownership; it does not absorb a later general device-control frontend.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

issues.title: Define versioned controller capabilities and integration APIs
issues.body:
## Outcome
Give shared clients a stable way to inspect and command existing device owners without erasing device-specific behavior.

## Scope
Own schemas and cross-language fixtures for device identity, capabilities, observations, commands and feeds. Device implementations remain in [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [codex-nanoleaf#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). This contract can be defined independently of provider qualification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define a stable configured device ID and controller/source identity. Register only explicitly configured destinations; callers cannot choose raw IPs, URLs, filesystem paths, firmware/reset operations or arbitrary device commands.
- [ ] Describe supported capabilities and typed operations for power/brightness and optional device-specific media, zones, scenes and previews. Unsupported capabilities are explicit; ordinary lights do not implement Pixoo's RGB animation interface.
- [ ] Separate desired configuration, queued/pending work, last successful send, failed/partially applied or uncertain work, external control, and observation age from service health. Transport acknowledgment is never optical proof.
- [ ] Version request/result and snapshot/change-feed envelopes. Include request identity, configuration revision, output generation, typed failure and possible prior effects; define bounded replay, conflicting duplicates, cursor expiry and full resync.
- [ ] Define a machine-client authentication boundary distinct from browser Origin/editing tokens, loopback defaults, credential rotation/revocation and bounded admission. Do not weaken existing browser protections.
- [ ] Keep one designated writer per physical device. Clients delegate through its services/queue; expired generations and reconnects cannot replay stale commands or reclaim ownership.
- [ ] Specify renderer metadata with explicit clock domain, epochs, compatibility and update outcomes. Device payloads may contain Pixoo frames or Nanoleaf zone timelines; no universal animation scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Define package/API compatibility policy and shared fixtures consumed by Python and TypeScript. Keep databases private to their owners; Windows and WSL must never coordinate by concurrently opening a mounted SQLite file.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema and contract-consumer fixtures covering unsupported capabilities, replay/conflicts, stale generations/cursors, authentication, unknown telemetry and cross-process clock interpretation.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-4-controller-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. This contract is the shared source prerequisite for the local MCP module in #7 and [Nanoleaf controller #28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). Provider qualification and standalone hosting are independent.

- [ ] Version request/result and snapshot/change-feed envelopes. Include request identity, configuration revision, output generation, typed failure and possible prior effects; define bounded replay, conflicting duplicates, cursor expiry and full resync.
- [ ] Define a machine-client authentication boundary distinct from browser Origin/editing tokens, loopback defaults, credential rotation/revocation and bounded admission. Do not weaken existing browser protections.
- [ ] Keep one designated writer per physical device. Clients delegate through its services/queue; expired generations and reconnects cannot replay stale commands or reclaim ownership.
- [ ] Specify renderer metadata with explicit clock domain, epochs, compatibility and update outcomes. Device payloads may contain Pixoo frames or Nanoleaf zone timelines; no universal animation scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Define package/API compatibility policy and shared fixtures consumed by Python and TypeScript. Keep databases private to their owners; Windows and WSL must never coordinate by concurrently opening a mounted SQLite file.

issues.title: Provide reusable local MCP transport and device tools
issues.body:
## Outcome
Provide reusable authenticated MCP infrastructure for local Codex device control, with protocol compatibility fixtures for Codex and Claude.

## Scope
Provide a reusable MCP module embeddable by local device integrations. Standalone hosting, aggregate device discovery, and agent/session tools move to [agent-device-hub#13](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/13); they do not gate this module. Pixoo [divoom-app-upgrade#24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/24) preserves its optional local /mcp entry point through this module; [divoom-app-upgrade#25](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/25) owns its media tool implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Implement opt-in authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP initialization, discovery and typed tools over registered controller/service interfaces with fake-backed fixtures, with a pinned compatible SDK/license and no second device writer.
- [ ] Provide registration/discovery primitives and capability-aware device status/power/brightness operations. Standalone aggregate discovery and qualified agent/session status are owned by [agent-device-hub#13](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/13). Device-specific tools bind server-controlled IDs and delegate to registered controller commands.
- [ ] Export reusable transport/authentication, tool/result and registration code for separate repository consumers. Device endpoints may use explicit default-device bindings without duplicating common MCP infrastructure.
- [ ] Preserve command request IDs, revisions, cancellation, replay/conflict handling and possible prior effects across browser, HTTP and MCP. A disconnected client cannot stop backend playback or create an automatic retry of an ambiguous write.
- [ ] Apply credentials, Host and supplied-Origin validation, bounded admission and accurate read/write annotations. Tool descriptions cannot imply telemetry certainty, raw device access, permissions bypass or task success.
- [ ] Test Codex/Claude protocol clients with fakes; document installed-client compatibility gaps for acceptance. Hosted ChatGPT/tunnels remain separately gated by Pixoo [divoom-app-upgrade#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/17).

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4) for controller contracts; no dependency on the standalone host or monitoring core.

## Verification
MCP protocol/consumer fixtures, authentication, concurrent UI/MCP commands, unsupported capability, replay, cancellation and offline-controller checks.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-7-shared-mcp-gateway/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. Deliver consumable versioned artifacts for [Pixoo #24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/24) and [codex-nanoleaf#33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/33) without worktree-relative imports. A fake controller satisfies module source validation; installed-client/physical acceptance remains in the device repositories. The existing planned OpenSpec identifier is retained; reconcile its scope before creating artifacts.

issues.title: Implement the reusable agent-state core and provider emitters
issues.body:
## Outcome
Interpret agent observations once and expose durable, trustworthy session snapshots to multiple device consumers.

## Scope
Implement shared TypeScript packages and bounded provider emitters from [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2). The first production host is Pixoo's existing backend in [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31); this issue does not create a second backend or install hooks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Implement the qualified provider mappings and deterministic reducer with injectable time. Namespace state by provider/source/session and retain available turn and evidenced child identity.
- [x] Preserve continuing questions, blocked attention, turn-ended notices, interruption and unavailable evidence independently. A new turn or explicit monitor acknowledgment clears only the intended monitor notice.
- [x] Reject stale prior-turn changes, deduplicate retries and make child counts stable under concurrent, missing-ID and reordered observations. Unknown ordering remains visible as uncertainty.
- [x] Expose session observation age separately from collector health. Five minutes without session evidence marks observations uncertain, not failed. Restart restores previously active sessions as uncertain until fresh evidence.
- [x] Persist state, chosen labels and undismissed notices through the host's storage boundary. Bound the diagnostic journal to 24 hours or 10,000 events, whichever comes first, without deleting current state or notices.
- [x] Validate/strip non-allowlisted fields before delivery and persistence. Privacy-canary tests must prove excluded payloads do not appear in transport, storage, diagnostics or errors.
- [x] Export an embedding API for ingest, snapshots/change subscriptions, acknowledgment, shutdown, and migrations. Version the package/contracts and test the TypeScript and Python consumer fixtures; no per-device copy of the reducer.
- [x] Keep provider emitters fail-open with bounded latency, payloads and queues during collector outages. State collection never commands a device, including in Media/Free modes.
- [x] Document immutable snapshot revisions, compatibility, storage ownership, source installation identity and one active state owner. Publish reproducible package artifacts usable by a separate repository without checkout-relative imports.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2)

## Verification
Fake-clock reducer, privacy, deduplication, retention, migration, interrupted-write, restart, concurrent-producer and package-consumer checks without credentials or devices.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-3-agent-state-core/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

- [x] Keep the shared source in packages/agent-state and provider integration modules in this repository. Publish immutable artifacts for initial embedding in Pixoo and later standalone reuse; do not move or duplicate the reducer into device repositories.
- [x] Expose one current-state feed to independent registered consumers. Bound each consumer's delivery/history and isolate stalls; recover from snapshots after expired cursors without replaying old effects. Verify two device consumers plus a stalled third fake consumer.
- [x] Use the baseline and frozen numeric budget artifact from [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) before implementation. Event collection and hook return remain independent of UI visibility, device availability and selected device mode. This is an early design input, not a dependency on that issue's integrated completion.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

## Source delivery completed, 2026-09-20

PR #105 merged as `f550bcd6b7d3b7da0f34c90c622b343afe2b25fb`, with the same tree as independently reviewed head `ab6c7f5`. The source acceptance criteria and applicable merged-main CI requirement are met. Guide-source reconciliation merged in [PR #109](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/109) at `1ea93eebc13ee818962053daa7cb690c5735c59a`. Its tree exactly matches independently reviewed head `8a21efe`; all 13 changed paths are under `docs/work-guide/`. Local generation, five maintenance tests and six-width browser/print checks pass. issues.title: Verify Lines and NL22 Panels together on the installed Linux runtime
issues.body:
## Desired outcome

Confirm that Lines and original NL22 Light Panels display useful task status together on the existing Linux installation, operate independently, and restore their own scenes and brightness.

## Scope

One installation and everyday-use trial for one operator in Ubuntu WSL. Source prerequisites [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41), [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43), and [#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/45) are delivered. The wall map remains Lines-only; use the CLI `--device` target for Panels until [#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44).

A later explicit installation task must authorize the intended devices, installation update, and bounded light sequence. Updating this issue does not authorize installation, pairing, or device operation.

Use the existing private Linux installation and [Linux installation guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/linux-install.md). Never run fresh setup to update it. Updating installed source may require restarting affected processes; enrollment itself requires no service restart. No backup, upgrade, or rollback tooling is added here.

User-reported Panels hardware is NL22, firmware 5.2.2, hardware 1.6.2, with 18 triangles arranged as three connected hexagons and the middle hexagon raised. Treat this as an expectation to check against the device, not a source of panel identities. Obtain addresses and credentials from private configuration; keep the original photo private.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — Identify the trial: record the delivered source revision, confirm both intended device identities, and read the NL22 model, firmware, and layout. Check the expected triangle count and plausible physical arrangement using reported geometry and representative visible placement. Resolve a material mismatch before dependent tests; do not guess panel identities or change firmware.
- [x] AC2 — Update and enroll: update the existing Linux installation without fresh setup and enroll Panels in Free using the delivered command. Confirm existing Lines tasks, reservations and preferences remain available and normal task display through the existing input source still works. Keep the selected shared-monitoring source; do not switch back to legacy hooks for this trial. Preserve credentials and trusted hooks. Restart only processes needed for the source update; enrollment alone needs no restart.
- [x] AC3 — Check task display: use representative tasks and the existing synthetic effect previews to confirm a task appears once on each device, representative triangle placement makes sense, and shared completion/read evidence clears the corresponding indications on both. Observe working green, question yellow, blocked red, unread blue, a status pulse, an outward wave, and a completion effect. Confirm red/yellow alerts remain visible and Lines retain split-half behavior. This is a visual functional check, not precise timing or exhaustive transition testing. Do not mark Codex tasks read through the map or by editing Codex state.
- [x] AC4 — Check modes and restoration: briefly exercise Work, Quiet, and Free on each device. Confirm Quiet is steady at its intended brightness, changing one device's mode leaves the other alone, and each device restores its own saved scene and brightness at the agreed idle or Free boundary. Use targeted CLI commands for Panels; a full matrix of mixed-mode combinations is unnecessary.
- [x] AC5 — Check the existing map: confirm the wall map opens, still shows Lines, and one targeted Lines control works with Panels enrolled. Panels selection and triangle reservations remain outside this trial; the map selector follows in #44.
- [x] AC6 — Finish and record: keep the installed worker as the only light writer for each device throughout the trial. Restore the user-selected modes and scene preferences at the end. Record a concise result with the source revision, installation outcome, visible observations, scene restoration, final modes, and remaining problems. Separate transport acknowledgments from the user's visible-light confirmation. Exclude credentials, private addresses and paths, raw task/device data, and the original photo. Close only when the retained criteria pass and the user confirms the visible result; otherwise keep the issue open with the specific next action.

## Verification approach

Reuse source-test evidence from #41, #43, and #45. Perform the separately authorized installation and one bounded visual sequence, using synthetic tasks where possible, plus a normal task check through the installed shared-monitoring source. No new test harness, soak period, or production qualification exercise is required.

The NL22 payload version, logical-panel flag, and orientation semantics were left physically unconfirmed by [#43's delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43#issuecomment-5789645955). Successful visible task placement and effects must establish that the delivered behavior works on this device; API acceptance alone is insufficient.

Out of scope for this completion gate: locating every Line, exhaustive capacity/waiting-list tests, precise optical timing, every animation/mode transition, deliberate outage injection, reconnect/restart matrices, uncertain machine-request replay testing, firmware qualification, Windows support, rollback tooling, and exact UI-to-light frame synchronization. Record and investigate failures encountered during ordinary use; do not silently waive a failed retained criterion.

## Dependencies and next action

- No open source blockers. #41 and #43 are closed; #45 was delivered in [PR #79](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/79) and closed on 2026-09-23.
- Installation and visible-light trial completed with the operator on 2026-09-24 UTC. See the acceptance receipt below. Final modes: Lines Work, Panels Free with their saved scene and brightness restored.
- Use `blocked` only when a concrete required dependency, decision, or verification is unavailable, and state the obstacle and next action. An unscheduled trial alone is not a source blocker.
- #44 follows this trial by choice and does not block it. #47 remains future work.
- #34 owns local MCP acceptance; #30 owns shared-monitoring migration. This trial does not wait for #29 or #33. #15 and #17 retain authoritative rendering and exact parity scope.

## Delivery target

Installed and visibly confirmed behavior, not another source implementation project. A successful trial needs a concise acceptance comment; source delivery alone cannot close this issue.

If the trial discovers a source defect, scope the repair and follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md, including applicable planning, tests, independent review, CI, and PR delivery. UI changes require approval of the current candidate. Those repair steps are conditional on an actual source change.

## Revision note

Reduced to a personal-project installation and everyday-use trial. Removed the satisfied #45 blocker and changed backlog status to ready while retaining the hardware label and explicit operation-authorization boundary. The earlier Linux-only and CLI-first decisions remain; the edit history preserves the previous nine-criterion scope. Deferred regression exercises are not prerequisites for this issue's completion.
