issues.title: Clear Codex Desktop tasks and Line assignments when sessions end
issues.body:
## Outcome

Retire an ended Codex Desktop session and its known descendants from the shared owner in one durable update. Existing consumers remove the task: Nanoleaf releases its Line assignments, Tidbyt and Pixoo update their monitoring displays, and the dashboard removes its row.

The owner retires within seconds of accepting `runtime.ended`. Displays follow their existing polling, write cadence and transport availability; this is not a promise that all physical devices clear simultaneously.

Scope simplified with the user on September 24, 2026. The agreed retirement behavior and safeguards remain.

## Policy

The [Codex hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#sessionend) documents `SessionEnd` for archive/delete of an open conversation, normal shutdown, and a conversation idle and unopened in any connected client for 30 minutes. The existing normalizer maps these to the same `runtime.ended` event; its reason is currently `"other"`. No new idle timer or cause detection is needed.

- Apply retirement to `provider: codex`, `client: desktop`. Keep other provider/client policies unchanged in this delivery; [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) extends the same owner rule to Codex CLI and Claude Code afterward.
- Remove the parent and descendants linked by known parent identities together. Do not guess relationships or terminate agents.
- Use [#195's forgetting policy](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195): notices, attention, task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state may be discarded. This is not acknowledgment, readership, success or cancellation. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects, colors, reservations, scenes, settings and conversations.
- Ordinary turn completion, waiting for input, read/acknowledgment changes and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not retire sessions. A turn exceeding 30 minutes does not trigger cleanup just because of its duration.
- Keep the 24-hour evidence expiry as the fallback for absent/lost ends, with each record's existing expiry clock.
- Eligible new work after resume or unarchive creates a fresh monitoring record with defaults, without old-effect replay. Retain protection against recognizable delayed events and document unknown-ordering limits.

## Bounded implementation

1. Extend the owner's existing atomic session-removal path from #195 and publish the normal snapshot revision. No new cleanup service or physical writer. The explicitly approved local presentation control below is a separate Nanoleaf operation.
2. Reuse consumer reconciliation. Add focused checks for Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and the dashboard; change a consumer only where a check demonstrates a gap. Retain device queues, native modes, scene restoration, cadence and resynchronization behavior. Report unrelated existing animation limitations separately.
3. Keep archive lookup out of retirement. Cleanup works without Codex-home configuration or a readable archive folder. Retain read-only archive evidence solely as an admission safeguard against archived tasks returning through delayed events, using [#191's configuration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191). Missing/unreadable files supply no evidence; never write or move Codex files.
4. Keep retirement/resume handling bounded and durable across restart. Resolve the case where a consumer misses retirement and sees the same conversation identity recreated at its next read. Preserve fresh-record semantics without assuming every intermediate snapshot was observed.
5. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, affected lifecycle/state contract and guide, compatibility assessment and required checks. Use the smallest change demonstrated necessary by the focused scenarios below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One normalized `runtime.ended` scenario verifies atomic parent/known-descendant retirement, capacity release and one published revision. Retain provider-mapping coverage; do not duplicate identical unit tests for the four documented end causes.
- [x] Unknown/repeated ends create nothing. Unrelated sessions and global settings survive.
- [x] Ordinary completion, waiting, read/acknowledgment changes, freshness uncertainty and a turn lasting over 30 minutes retain the session; fake-clock coverage preserves the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [x] Archive admission tests cover available archive evidence, absent configuration, missing/unreadable folders, delayed events and new work after unarchive.
- [x] Focused tests cover recognizable delayed events, same-identity resume, a recognizable old end after resume, owner restart and a consumer missing the entire retirement between reads. New monitoring records start fresh and old effects do not replay.
- [x] Cover child events after parent retirement and state the admission rule and limits of missing identity/order evidence.
- [x] Existing-consumer checks verify Nanoleaf assignment release, Tidbyt/Pixoo monitoring updates and dashboard removal, including reconnect. If nothing remains to display, preserve each consumer's existing idle behavior. Fix change-caused regressions without redesigning unrelated effects.
- [x] Qualify the separately authorized installed archive-end path with a throwaway conversation. Record accepted owner retirement, dashboard removal and visible Nanoleaf Line release separately from source checks; preserve the timing evidence. Other consumer checks do not repeat complete hardware qualification.

The user approved moving the remaining native non-archive end, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253). The idle/shutdown trials did not establish reliable end emission. That investigation is not a blocker for this accepted-end retirement delivery; no automatic cleanup on quit or after thirty minutes is claimed. Source-level fresh-resume and read-only admission safeguards remain required and verified above.

## Dependencies and boundaries

[#195](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195) is complete. [#191](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191) supplies the archive safeguard's Codex-home context, not a prerequisite for receiving ends.

[Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) follows this delivery and generalizes accepted-end retirement across the supported providers. It is not a blocker for #218 and does not expand #218's active PRs or acceptance scope.

[Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) is a downstream consumer of authoritative session presence/removal, with #241 as an additional prerequisite for consistent provider behavior. It owns automatic Work/Free switching and manual override; this issue issues no mode commands. An unavailable feed must not be represented as a healthy empty snapshot.

No archive polling, App Server client, Windows watcher, archive browser, restoration history, new dashboard feature, Claude/CLI policy change or future LIFX/PC-lighting integration. Those future consumers do not block delivery. This issue does not block completed [Tidbyt #21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21).

## Installed-trial presentation expansion

The user approved these additions on September 24 after observing the installed wall:

- [x] Shared completed/read tasks retain both their wall row and assigned Line until authoritative removal or explicit eviction. Reading ends the unread pulse; idle is steady blue. Preserve legacy input and orphan-child behavior.
- [x] The selected wall task offers **Evict** for the current Nanoleaf device. Remove its local row, allocation and task effects without changing the conversation, shared owner, other devices, global preferences or mode. Keep it suppressed through polling, read/acknowledgment changes and restart. An identifiable new turn or generation may appear again; reject controls from an older turn/generation/source selection.
- [x] Verify the new UI in isolated browser/Python scenarios and obtain renewed human approval of the concrete candidate before merge. Installation and visible-device checks remain separate.

Device-only eviction is the accepted first version. Eviction across every device is deferred until an explicit shared-owner command is introduced; revisit when another consumer needs the control. Local eviction leaves the owner record present, so it still counts toward Nanoleaf #110's future Work/Free policy. No owner timer, forged SessionEnd, manual database deletion or Codex-state write is added.

This expansion adds a Nanoleaf wall control; the shared-owner API and Hub dashboard controls remain unchanged. Native idle/shutdown emission and subsequent reopen/live-resume qualification now belong to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253), under the user-approved scope split. The temporary diagnostic hook was restored byte-for-byte. Ends observed during manual task cleanup do not establish normal-shutdown acceptance. The user accepted installed retention and Evict at Nanoleaf `0865a73` and approved the combined UI at `f1fc8e8`. Final head `f4ae77e` changes specifications only; the approval remains applicable. The final integrated source has not been installed.

## Delivered

Delivered through [Hub #238](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/238) and [Nanoleaf #116](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/116). The identified Tidbyt test lifetime defect is repaired in Hub #238 ([#255](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/255)); [Hub #257](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/257) repairs the pre-existing Start Monitor browser-test ordering failure ([#256](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/256)). Both repairs are test-only.

Final Hub main `49b29d06caee71be61dd8cee93bbca0c746ca7e7` has all six required Depot jobs passing. Nanoleaf main `7a030aca690f7d73dfe9960ccadd17599cbe0fd3` has all five passing. Matching PR checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, guarded squash merges and exact resulting-tree readbacks are recorded. Original implementation and consumer validation, specification sync/archive, installed archive/presentation acceptance and explicit UI approval remain complete.

Installed Hub remains 0.3.0 (source `6acc747`), with Nanoleaf `0865a73`; the final integrated source has not been installed. No additional runtime change or database restore occurred. Native idle/shutdown, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification remains open in #253. No automatic cleanup on quit or after thirty minutes is claimed.

issues.title: Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients
issues.body:
## Ownership

The fresh Linux installation's existing worker owns light writes and the timeline it sends. This issue exposes a read-only snapshot of that worker output. The wall map's live renderer and physical parity belong to [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17); this issue does not change current wall-map animation. Legacy Windows installations keep their existing path; adding Windows-specific behavior is outside scope.

Reuse relevant fields from [agent-device-hub#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4) where useful. The shared overview and basic controls do not wait for this work.

## Desired outcome

Provide display clients with enough last-sent rendering data to reproduce bridge-controlled output without inferring it from task status or scheduling effects themselves.

## Scope

Add a read-only `GET /api/rendering` route to the existing loopback wall-map server for the current Linux-owned Lines worker. Read directly from private state without refreshing metadata, acquiring device geometry, contacting the controller, or starting a worker. Include physical zone identity, encoded colors and frame durations, loop/effect phase, effective brightness and a compact outcome: pending, last successfully sent, failed/partial, or externally controlled/unknown.

Retain only the latest output receipt needed to describe the current worker output; do not add output history, subscriptions, replay queues, a new listener/authentication system, or a second writer. Preserve existing task/effect epochs and the current palette, one outward pulse with its two-second cycle, completion comet defaults, split project/status halves, and Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Future palettes and effects remain with #18-#20.

A successful HTTP command means the device accepted the command; it does not prove what the lights visibly produced. Scenes or streams whose frames are unavailable remain externally controlled/unknown. A simulated on-screen preview is not live worker output.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A rendering read provides the worker's last successfully accepted encoded frames, physical zone identity, frame durations, looping/phase and brightness needed by a display client to reproduce bridge-controlled output.
- AC2: The response distinguishes pending work, last successful output, failed or partially accepted updates, and external/unknown output. It does not describe command acceptance as optical confirmation.
- AC3: Reads do not refresh task metadata, advance effects, reserve sources, clear unread state, change assignments/preferences, acquire device geometry, contact the controller, start a worker, or write lights. Reads and reconnects do not replay expired effects.
- AC4: The latest output receipt and timing remain available after worker or map-server restart without resetting task, scene or project preferences. Existing installations acquire receipt storage without destructive migration.
- AC5: The endpoint reads through the existing loopback server and retains its Host and no-store protections. It contains no Nanoleaf credentials. Current wall-map rendering remains unchanged; #17 consumes this data.

## Verification

Use the fake controller, isolated database and fake clock to compare representative worker payloads for a two-second pulse and completion comet. Check pending and failed/partial outcomes, repeated reads, restart recovery, and that the GET-only rendering endpoint rejects writes without changing the last-sent worker receipt. The renderer-specific check that an on-screen-only preview stays separate from live worker output belongs to #17.

For implementation, run `python3 scripts/check.py`. The wall map itself is unchanged, so browser rendering checks belong with #17. Physical comparison and installation remain separate, explicitly authorized work under #17/#55.

## Dependencies

None. The shared envelope in agent-device-hub#4 is available for alignment; it does not block this work. The ambient-view decision and Lively prototype do not gate it.

## Follow-up work

- [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17) - Render bridge-controlled lights live and verify physical parity.
- [#18](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18) - Configure project and status colors.
- [#19](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/19) - Choose and preview completion celebrations.
- [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/20) - Customize animation for each status.
- [#16](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/16) - Build the deferred ambient view.
- [#21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/21) - Investigate mirroring externally controlled Nanoleaf scenes.

issues.title: Qualify and version the shared agent lifecycle contract
issues.body:
## Outcome
Define one evidence-backed event and session vocabulary for local Codex Desktop, Codex CLI, and Claude Code that every device integration can consume.

## Scope
This owns shared provider qualification previously planned in Pixoo #29. Pixoo retains consumer adoption in [divoom-app-upgrade#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/29). Use the existing Nanoleaf behavior and tests as evidence, without treating its Codex-specific assumptions as universal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record accessible installed client versions, primary documentation, event/payload/ordering identifiers, delivery support, and parent/subagent evidence. Distinguish documented, observed, unsupported and inaccessible signals; documentation/fixtures do not establish live compatibility.
- [ ] Define a versioned runtime-validated metadata envelope with provider, host/source, session and available turn identity, event identity or deterministic deduplication fallback, event kind, observation time and evidenced parent relationships.
- [ ] Keep activity, continuing questions, blocked input/approval, turn-ended notices, interruption/runtime end, acknowledgment and freshness distinct. A turn ending proves neither success nor readership.
- [ ] Represent each top-level session separately, including concurrent sessions in one project. Aggregate only attributable children; unknown parentage and unavailable counts stay explicit.
- [ ] Define optional Codex Desktop unread evidence and per-consumer notice policies. Preserve Nanoleaf's existing read behavior during migration; Pixoo dismissal remains monitor-only and never edits agent read state.
- [ ] Allow only lifecycle metadata, identifiers, timestamps and explicit user-chosen labels. Exclude prompts, transcripts, tool arguments/results, auto-copied titles, credentials and unrelated private paths before transmission and persistence.
- [ ] Specify bounded nonblocking fail-open producer delivery, timeout/overflow behavior and silent observational output. Monitoring cannot approve, deny, change permissions or hold an agent action waiting.
- [ ] Provide fixtures for new/old turns, ongoing questions, blocked input, resolution, turn end, interruption, children, duplicates, missing IDs, late events and unsupported evidence. Define required-client stop conditions.
- [ ] Publish vocabulary, schema compatibility rules and source/version evidence in hub documentation and issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts. Mark all live-client gaps for [agent-device-hub#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8) and device acceptance.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema/fixture validation and a primary-source capability matrix using synthetic metadata. Inspect accessible installed client artifacts read-only; no settings changes or agent launches.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-2-agent-lifecycle-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Qualify Codex Desktop and CLI on the supported Windows/WSL paths first, including installed-version gaps. Define shared labels, task/project identity and notice acknowledgment needed by manual integration controls without exporting private Codex metadata.
- [ ] Supply the event semantics and supported path matrix needed to establish cold/warm hook baselines in [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30); document hard fail-open behavior before runtime implementation.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

issues.title: Add local MCP status and display controls for Codex
issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Consume the reusable MCP transport, authentication, schemas and registration module from [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7). This issue owns optional Pixoo-local `/mcp` bindings to existing services. The hub registers the same capabilities with explicit device IDs. Do not implement another common MCP layer or device writer.

## Outcome
Control the app from local Codex through MCP tools for status, brightness, and screen on/off.

## Scope and source
Add an opt-in Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `/mcp` in the existing Fastify backend. Delegate to the shared device and player services delivered by #8. The backend owns one adapter instance and one serialized device queue across HTTP, browser, playback, and MCP callers.

This issue is the first MCP implementation slice. #25 adds media and playlist tools, #17 connects ChatGPT, and #26 records local Codex acceptance. No raw device commands, caller-selected IPs, filesystem access, firmware/reset tools, or second device-writing process.

[Product direction](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/product.md), [device adapter contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/openspec/specs/device-adapter/spec.md), and #8 own the underlying application behavior. Historical source reference: `bebc61efa4ec8c9e620e005754e16ba958b1b49b`. OpenAI documentation checked September 6, 2026: [MCP transports, authentication, and Codex configuration](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An MCP client can initialize, discover tools, and call `get_status()`, `set_brightness(percent, request_id)`, and `set_screen(on, request_id)` through the built application. Pin the shared MCP module and its compatible SDK/license record.
- [ ] `get_status` reports server readiness separately from configured mode, observed device connectivity, brightness, screen state, and player state. Identify observation freshness and unavailable values. Simulator results never report a connected physical display; transport acknowledgment never implies visual confirmation.
- [ ] Validate brightness as an integer 0-100 and screen state as a boolean. Reject invalid inputs before side effects. Return structured outcomes using the shared application's errors, request IDs, timing, and possible prior effects.
- [ ] All mutations use the same service and queue as #8. Screen-off follows the player's pause/cancellation semantics; screen-on does not resume playback. Concurrent MCP sessions and HTTP commands cannot interleave uploads or create another adapter.
- [ ] Preserve #8's duplicate-request handling and generation rules. Repeating a request ID does not execute it again; conflicting reuse is rejected. Define bounded retention and timeout/cancellation behavior in the shared command contract. Ambiguous sent commands are not automatically replayed.
- [ ] MCP is disabled unless explicitly enabled and remains loopback-bound. Require a locally provisioned credential outside Git, validate host and any supplied Origin, and reject unauthorized requests before app effects. Authenticated native clients without an Origin can connect. Credentials and private device/media details stay out of tool results and logs.
- [ ] Tool descriptions and schemas distinguish observations from writes. Mark status read-only and display controls as writes so client approval policies apply. Discovery and connection never mutate the device.
- [ ] Document local Codex Streamable HTTP configuration, credential setup/revocation, start/stop, and WSL reachability diagnostics. Normal startup remains simulator-only; MCP follows the app's explicitly selected mode and never enables hardware or LAN access itself. Disconnecting Codex leaves the backend running.
- [ ] Before implementation, prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec proposal, affected capability deltas, tasks, and design; record the shared-service placement and transport/auth decision in an ADR. Follow repository delivery and review requirements.

Planned OpenSpec change: `gh-24-local-mcp-controls`.

## Verification approach
Use a real MCP client against the built server with the fake device, isolated runtime data, and temporary test credentials. Cover discovery, valid/invalid calls, unauthorized and cross-origin requests, duplicate IDs, overlapping clients/HTTP commands, upload serialization, timeouts, cancellation, and backend continuity after disconnect. Existing browser behavior and simulator defaults must remain covered.

Run Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run check`, and `npm run test:browser` after Playwright Chromium installation; current workflow/spec checks and all configured PR/main CI jobs must pass. Source checks require no real device or external account. Actual Codex and physical acceptance remain in #26.

## Dependencies
- #8 for the shared validated device/player application services and command contract.
- #2 and #3 provide the delivered server and adapter foundations.
- #4 supplies bounded physical protocol evidence for future authorized device acceptance, not blanket firmware or timing guarantees.

Additional shared prerequisites:
- [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7)

## Delivery target
Source-only. This issue does not install the integration, change personal Codex settings, or authorize physical-device commands.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. Source work uses the fake adapter and does not wait on #11, #17, a standalone hub, or monitoring. [divoom-app-upgrade#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42) is a prerequisite of physical acceptance in #26, not simulator-backed MCP development.

issues.title: Add MCP media selection and playlist playback tools
issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Own Pixoo media/playlist tool handlers and register them through [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7)'s shared module. Preserve local default-device and hub device-ID bindings with the same services, request identity and queue.

## Outcome
Ask local Codex to find existing media, show an item, start a saved playlist, and control playback through the app.

## Scope and source
Extend the MCP interface from #24 with library and player tools. Reuse rendering from #5, persistence from #6, playback from #7, and shared APIs/services from #8. MCP translates user requests into those application operations; the backend owns all playback timing and device writes.

Suggested tool contract: `list_media`, `show_media`, `list_playlists`, `play_playlist`, and `control_playback`. Tool names and schemas must be finalized in the issue-linked OpenSpec change. Upload/import, AI image generation, playlist editing/deletion, scheduling, and cloud-gallery access are outside this slice.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `list_media` and `list_playlists` provide bounded, paginated/searchable results with stable IDs and enough metadata to choose an item. Duplicate names remain distinguishable. Return app IDs and approved metadata without local paths or raw originals.
- [ ] `show_media` selects existing media and an effective rendition through the shared player. Start an ephemeral single-item session without creating or editing a saved playlist. If a shared single-item command is missing, add it once to the application layer with tests. Apply established playback defaults unless an explicitly validated policy is supplied.
- [ ] `play_playlist` validates the chosen playlist and expected revision before starting its immutable session snapshot. Return an actionable conflict if the selection changed. Starting new content retires prior work through the existing generation mechanism.
- [ ] `control_playback` supports an explicit enum of pause, resume, stop, next, and previous. Preserve #7 semantics: pause stops advancement, resume restarts the item, stop leaves the last content, and previous follows actual history. Do not invent device playback-complete events.
- [ ] Mutations require request IDs and inherit #24/#8 replay, cancellation, and error rules. Unknown IDs, stale revisions, unsupported renditions, and invalid playback policies produce typed errors without unintended changes.
- [ ] Tool results expose the authoritative session/revision/state and identify loading, estimated timing, unsupported capabilities, and possible prior effects. Reads and writes have accurate MCP annotations and descriptions.
- [ ] Playback continues under the backend after MCP client disconnection. Concurrent browser and MCP controls observe the same session and queue. Playlist edits during playback retain the existing snapshot/restart rules.
- [ ] Media remains subject to rendering limits, reference retention, and the selected device profile. A successful simulator or HTTP result cannot widen hardware capability limits.
- [ ] Prepare issue-linked OpenSpec proposal, capability deltas, tasks, and the required design for temporary sessions, concurrency, and error handling before implementation.

Planned OpenSpec change: `gh-25-mcp-media-playback`.

## Verification approach
Exercise the built MCP endpoint with a real MCP client, fake device/clock, and isolated media/playlist fixtures. Cover repeated names, pagination, missing IDs, revision races, repeated commands, single-item sessions, pause/resume/skip during loading, concurrent HTTP/MCP controls, and playback after disconnect. Assert saved playlists and referenced renditions remain intact.

Run Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run check`, and `npm run test:browser` after installing Playwright Chromium. Require current workflow/spec validation and every configured PR/main CI job. Actual client/device observations are recorded in #26.

## Dependencies
- #24 for MCP transport, authentication, and tool/result conventions.
- #8 for the shared library/player services, with #5, #6, and #7 as its existing prerequisites.

## Related work
#17 connects these tools to ChatGPT web; local source implementation does not depend on it.

## Delivery target
Source-only. No installation, private-media ingestion, or physical-device operation is authorized by issue creation.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. #26 owns local Codex acceptance. [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44) preserves future ChatGPT acceptance. Source tests use the simulator; physical acceptance also needs [divoom-app-upgrade#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42).

issues.title: Verify local Codex control on the Pixoo
issues.body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Verify interactive Pixoo commands through the shared MCP module and configured endpoint. Reuse common fixtures from [agent-device-hub#7](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/7). #34 owns observational monitoring; [agent-device-hub#9](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/9) owns cross-repository source compatibility.

## Outcome
Demonstrate that local Codex can control the configured Pixoo through the same application backend, and retain reproducible evidence.

## Scope and source
Verify the delivered MCP tools in the actual local Codex client, then perform separately authorized physical checks. The September 6 bounded smoke evidence in #4 is the protocol baseline; it does not prove MCP or application integration.

#12 retains broad local physical playback timing, recovery, and soak acceptance. [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) owns future browser LAN acceptance; [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44) owns future ChatGPT web acceptance. This issue owns the additional local Codex command path, client approval behavior, and integration installation evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Identify the installation/test owner, source revision, actual local Codex clients, host/network path, and rollback steps before setup. Keep configuration and credentials outside Git; use WSL as the primary existing workflow and record reachability failures without silently switching hosts.
- [ ] In local Codex, discover and exercise status, brightness, screen control, media selection, playlist start, and playback controls against simulator fixtures. Record tool inputs/results and confirm write classification and the selected approval policy.
- [ ] Before physical calls, obtain the exact private device IP and explicit permission for the test sequence and display replacement. Record initial brightness/screen state and restoration limits. Use synthetic or separately authorized existing media within the supported profile.
- [ ] From local Codex, observe a read-only status/probe, approved brightness and screen changes, one still/short animation, and a short playlist with pause/resume/skip/stop. Record user-visible results separately from transport acknowledgments and estimated timing. Restore known brightness/screen settings; do not promise restoration of unknown prior artwork.
- [ ] Verify browser and MCP callers share one backend/queue, screen-off pauses advancement, screen-on does not resume, and playback continues after the chat disconnects. A failed or stale request must not produce a later unexpected command.
- [ ] Disable the integration and verify access is revoked while ordinary local app use remains available. Document local service startup and shutdown without changing router/firewall settings.
- [ ] Record dated, redacted pass/fail/blocked results and source revision in the repository's hardware-validation documentation, linking this issue and the originating feature issues. Leave missing client or physical observations open; simulator and source success cannot close this acceptance issue.

## Verification approach
Use the runbooks from #24 and #25. Keep real client, installation, transport, and physical/user evidence separate. No soak or crash-limit experiment is included. Reuse the current source/CI evidence; run applicable checks again only for resulting source or documentation changes. Any implementation defect returns to a scoped source fix and its required checks.

## Dependencies
- [divoom-app-upgrade#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42) for application-integrated physical control.
- #24 for local MCP status/display control.
- #25 for media and playlist tools.
- #4 for the bounded protocol baseline.
- Future explicit installation and physical-test authorization, named owner, available local client, and configured device.

## Related work
#12 remains a separate acceptance obligation; completion here does not close it.

## Delivery target
Includes installation and its verification plus explicitly authorized physical-device verification. This backlog entry records the required future gates; it does not itself authorize installation, account changes, or hardware actions.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. The ChatGPT checks moved to [divoom-app-upgrade#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/44). Unavailable remote clients/account access cannot block this local issue. Keep separately authorized local-client installation and user-observed physical checks open until complete.

issues.title: Validate local physical playback, recovery, and soak reliability
issues.body:
## Outcome
Validate local physical playback, recovery, and soak reliability.

## Scope and source
[September 5 handoff](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/blob/main/docs/reference/2026-09-05-agent-handoff.md), sections 9-11. Preserve its evidence boundaries. This issue delivers the scoped portion of M6; other milestone work stays in linked issues.

## Current approved disposition

The owner approved the prepared narrow deferral after asking to wrap up visual testing. [#55](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/55) now owns effective variable GIF timing qualification. A remained ambiguous, B looked equal despite asymmetric requested delays, and the equal-500-ms control looked equal. These observations remain unverified timing evidence, not a pass. The normal application profile stays uniform 500 ms; no application behavior or product specification changes with this disposition.

All remaining physical observations for this issue are complete. The recorded approximate 28-second still reading remains outside the agreed 29-31-second tolerance; two later readings were 30.3 seconds. The failed three-play transition and later known flashing remain accepted under #52. Screen-on content retention remains a separately accepted limitation with an observed explicit-Resume recovery. The approved deferral changes only the variable-timing component. It preserves every other criterion, tolerance, observation and delivery gate.

All physical helpers are closed, with final blue 30 owner-confirmed. No additional physical operation is part of closeout. Final hardware documentation is committed in candidate `267df1d6aa05032c54cea1a3f9f856b7fe2a3fa0`. Both independent reviews found no P0-P3 findings, and all five current-head PR jobs passed in [run 34293736877](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34293736877). [PR #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/54) merged at `7c1204fd2516df86c706bae7c9498a5ee1bb749b`, with a tree identical to reviewed head. [Merged-main run 34294175210](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34294175210) passed all five configured jobs. Source and scoped physical acceptance are complete. [Final guide PR #79](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/79) merged at `8064537639d7a91a66657cdbce9a63654e41b80c`, preserving the independently reviewed tree. All twelve merged-main jobs passed in [run 34295211810](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34295211810). The guide records completed #12 and open timing follow-up #55. Guide synchronization and the authorized delivery are complete. The records below are dated execution history; earlier pending-approval or blocker statements describe those earlier checkpoints.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Obtain user approval for display-changing tests and a normal-cadence soak. Capture model/firmware and tested profile without committing private identifiers.
- [x] Observe 30-second image dwell, numbered GIFs at several total-play counts, upload gaps and play-boundary error under the current uniform-500-ms profile; retain the agreed tolerances and accepted defect #52. Effective variable timing is deferred by explicit owner approval to #55.
- [x] Validate pause/resume restart, skip during loading, stop, brightness, screen off/on, user-assisted disconnect/reconnect and server restart without stale commands.
- [x] Run a user-approved soak of at least 60 minutes AND 100 transitions; report latency distribution, artifacts, freezes/recoveries and server resource growth.
- [x] Record dated user-observed local playback results and source revision in hardware-validation documentation. Authenticated phone access and continued playback after phone close/lock are preserved in [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43) and do not block this local acceptance issue.
- [x] Report every check pass/fail/blocked. Keep this issue open if hardware acceptance is pending; describe simulator-only completion as software complete with hardware verification pending.

## Dependencies
- #4
- [divoom-app-upgrade#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/42) for physical adapter integration in the application.
- #10 for local startup/operations.

## Verification approach
Record dated device/user observations and separate automated source checks as specified above. No hardware actions are authorized by issue creation.

## Delivery target
Source plus separately authorized physical acceptance.

## Priority and access decision
Prioritize local playback and recovery; perform the normal-cadence soak only after the user approves its schedule and limits. Local Codex command-path acceptance is #26 and can complete independently of this broad soak. Remote browser acceptance is deferred in [divoom-app-upgrade#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/43); #11 is no longer a prerequisite here.

## Earlier delivery assessment, September 8, 2026

Coordinator: current authorized deliver-work session. Fresh base: `d51ce01dbe7be66322f58f333465d49f405bdd6d`; branch: `codex/gh-12-physical-acceptance`. The pre-start audit found no dedicated #12 branch, PR, OpenSpec change or execution record. #4, #42 and #10 are complete; #26 is narrower prior acceptance.

The owner supplied the exact target privately, identified Pixoo64, accepted the staged tests and proposed timing tolerances, and is available for the observation checkpoints. Firmware remains unknown. Use synthetic content, one WSL backend/writer, private runtime storage, and the existing profile for initial checks. Restore known brightness/screen state when reachable; prior artwork is not guaranteed recoverable.

Complexity medium: playback/control/restart and prolonged observations. Uncertainty high: visible timing and variable-delay qualification remain unmeasured. Impact medium: temporary visible content/settings changes and owner-assisted recovery. Supported-profile checks are ready; variable timing is a bounded investigation before any expanded-profile operation. No incompatible profile or unsupported hardware behavior is assumed.

Evidence mapping: criterion 1 uses this session authorization plus private target/profile records; criterion 2 uses generated fixtures, measured state timing and dated user observations; criterion 3 uses staged controls and owner-assisted device/backend recovery; criterion 4 requires both 60 minutes and 100 transitions, a 75-minute cap, latency/artifact records and resource samples; criteria 5-6 use a reviewed hardware-validation update with explicit pass/fail/blocked dispositions. Accepted proposed tolerances: 30-second dwell within 1 second; GIF play boundary within one 500 ms frame; loading interruptions require separate owner assessment.

Physical results remain pending. The user reports Actions budget restored; rerun and verify all configured jobs, preserving independent Standards/Specification review and guarded squash merge. Deliver-work is the installed successor to the retired github-delivery name. Reassess on profile discoveries, unacceptable output, uncertain writes or changed scope. Final source delivery includes the required linked hub guide synchronization.

## Validation checkpoint, September 8, 2026

The Actions budget fix is verified: [main run 34255897665, attempt 2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/actions/runs/34255897665) passed all five configured jobs at `d51ce01dbe7be66322f58f333465d49f405bdd6d`. Local Node 24.20.0 `npm ci` and `npm run check` passed, including 270 application tests, 10 workflow tests, 11 specifications and 12 archives. Local HTTP checks require command-local loopback proxy exclusions in this execution environment; no product tests were changed.

Original synthetic 64x64 fixtures and the staged playlists were prepared. Independent fixture decoding confirmed two 500 ms GIF frames; simulator import and a one-play-to-still transition succeeded. Source remains unchanged at the base revision.

The physical application backend acquired the standard exclusive target lock and passed startup health. Its one read-only probe failed with `offline`, `priorEffects:none`. Direct TCP diagnosis returned `ENETUNREACH`; a final read-only proxy request was explicitly blocked because the session sandbox rejects local/private network addresses, including after an escalation request. The backend was stopped cleanly. No display-changing command was sent. This does not establish a device or LAN failure outside the session.

Permission retry: after the owner selected the device-development profile, the approved target answered a read-only channel request through the configured proxy with HTTP 200 and device error_code 0. The previous private-address permission block is cleared.

Execution blocker resolved: Codex ran the normal rebuilt application's read-only probe successfully at clean commit `b490290d4896065253571dbcf39c3a78d74b0949`. The application returned `available:true` and `connected:true`, read the channel and known display settings, and closed cleanly. No display-changing command was sent. The owner no longer needs to run the manual terminal probe. Existing hardware authorization remains valid; visible timing, controls/recovery, variable-delay qualification and soak acceptance remain pending.

The pinned local Chromium download is separately allowlist-blocked, and cached Chrome cannot launch under the session socket restriction. Hosted pinned-browser checks passed; no local visual pass is claimed. Keep #12 open. Independent final reviews, candidate PR/main checks, physical acceptance and companion guide synchronization remain future delivery gates.


## Codex execution compatibility, September 8, 2026

The owner requested that Codex run the commands without a manual terminal handoff. The approved read-only application probe still fails after escalation. The transport creates an unconfigured per-request HTTP agent, which omits Node's explicitly enabled environment proxy. Implement a bounded compatibility fix that inherits the configured Node proxy while preserving fresh request connections, fixed private device destination/port/path, response validation, cancellation and the serialized writer. Test proxy opt-in, direct operation and NO_PROXY with isolated loopback fixtures, then repeat the normal application's read-only probe from Codex.

No product specification delta is required: this restores execution through operator-configured networking while preserving the existing device command, admission, lifecycle and evidence contracts. Document the connection route and its cancellation limits. No Codex permission policy, router/firewall, firmware, automatic retry or display-changing scope is added. Broader #12 hardware acceptance and normal delivery gates remain pending.


The connection fix is committed on `codex/gh-12-physical-acceptance`; latest head is `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`. The follow-up commit only declares Node >=24.5 <25 in package metadata and documentation, matching the introduction of Node HTTP proxy support. The lockfile was regenerated with npm; the installed runtime was not changed. `npm ci` and the full `npm run check` passed on Node 24.20.0 at this head: 273 application tests, 10 workflow tests, 11 specifications and 12 archives. The new test reproduced the incorrect direct route before the fix and now verifies proxy opt-in, direct operation, NO_PROXY and separate connections.

This resolves the Codex execution compatibility substep. It does not complete #12 or establish physical playback accuracy. Candidate hosted CI, final acceptance/review, publication/merge and companion hub guide synchronization remain pending. The remaining variable-timing qualification requires a bounded observed profile before that criterion can pass.


## Physical acceptance checkpoint, September 8, 2026 UTC

Tested application source: `15b0820eaf14e6d61da44e299b2407f339bfe6c1`, Node 24.20.0, existing Pixoo64 smoke profile through the approved command proxy and one normal application writer. The owner confirmed the expected white 30/border on blue and one red 1 / green 2 cycle followed by the still.

The three-play test exposed unexpected output. The owner reported three complete cycles followed by several rapid extra 1 / 2 cycles before the blue still. The expected visible sequence failed. Recorded backend intervals were 3000.159 ms playing and 195.791 ms transitioning to still readiness; these are state-derived intervals, not visible-burst measurements. No session error or reconnect appeared. Playback was stopped and the physical backend closed. Brightness and screen state were not changed.

At the initial stop, five plays, controls, recovery and soak had not run. The owner has since accepted the transition artifact as nonblocking, as recorded below. Variable timing remains separately unqualified. The hardware-validation draft retains the failed visible observation; it is not promoted to a pass.

A local full-application reproduction with the same assets/policy issued exactly five requests: ID query, two GIF frames, ID query, one still frame. All uploaded frames retained 500 ms timing and the expected RGB hashes/ID association. This software run does not explain the physical burst. Independent inspection and 53 relevant source tests likewise found no duplicate upload or deliberate speed change. No firmware defect is asserted.

The owner authorized one bounded traced repeat and reported the rapid burst again. Exactly five physical requests completed with error_code 0 and no retry: an ID query, two GIF frames under returned ID 6, another query and the still under ID 7. Every frame used PicSpeed 500 and the expected rendered RGB hash. The second query began 3004.108 ms after the final GIF response; the query/still-upload interval was 205.987 ms. These include trace overhead and HTTP completion, not visible timing. The backend stopped and closed. Extra application uploads, changed requested speed and reused IDs do not explain this recorded run.


## Accepted defect and continuation decision, September 8, 2026

The owner requested a backlog defect and explicitly accepted the rapid GIF-to-still flashing as nonblocking for moving forward. [Defect #52](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/52) now owns investigation and correction. The observed three-play sequence remains failed with this accepted known-defect disposition; no root cause or fix is claimed.

Continue the remaining approved supported-profile tests, including five plays, controls, recovery and the bounded soak after the shorter checks. Recurrence of the same known burst will be recorded without reopening that resolved continuation decision. New uncertain writes, conflicting writers or other unexpected output still require assessment. All other acceptance criteria remain unchanged. Variable timing is still a separate qualification gap; final evidence, independent reviews, candidate/main CI and guide synchronization remain required.


## Resumed tests and new observation checkpoint, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed five normal 1 / 2 cycles followed by blue 30 with the known flashing. Backend GIF dwell was 5000.601 ms and still loading was 199.978 ms. Defect #52 remains accepted and nonblocking.

The owner also confirmed blue remained during pause, changed to the numbered GIF about 30 seconds after resume, and GIF content remained after Stop. Backend pause lasted 50.877 seconds; resume gave the still a fresh 30.002 seconds, followed by 366.962 ms GIF loading. Exact visible dwell was not measured.

The next batch submitted Skip 4.459 ms after the GIF entered loading; that GIF never reached backend playing. The API then accepted 20% brightness, screen off/on and restoration to 100%. Screen-on left playback paused, and the device probe returned brightness 100%, screen on and channel 1. The owning backend closed cleanly; a new backend restored the same session/item paused with connectivity unknown and performed only local health/status/catalog reads.

The owner subsequently reported random GIFs and said they did not see the last test execute. Skip, brightness/screen and unchanged physical content across backend restart are therefore unconfirmed. The restarted backend was closed immediately without another device command. The onset and cause of the non-test content are unknown; API success is not a visual pass.

Current physical checkpoint: resolve or explicitly disposition this separate unexpected-content observation before more display commands. It is not covered by the accepted rapid-flashing defect. Device disconnect/reconnect, variable timing and soak remain unexecuted. Confirmed observations are retained; no additional acceptance criterion is marked complete.


## Isolated screen off/on observation, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner reports the Divoom app closed and no known active external controller. They authorized a step-by-step repeat that omitted Skip, brightness changes and backend restart during the observation interval. The same application source and normal exclusive backend were used.

The blue still was uploaded once. Its still-only playlist completed after a 30001.476 ms backend playing-to-idle interval, and the owner confirmed blue 30 was still visible afterward. The owner confirmed a dark screen after Off, then reported "Random GIFs return." after On. The player remained paused and no replacement artwork was submitted. The backend closed after the final observation. Brightness was unchanged.

This isolates screen off/on as a sufficient trigger for the content change in the observed sequence. The internal device cause and precise return timing remain unknown. The screen controls visibly operated, but uploaded content was not retained across the cycle. Source behavior follows the current contract: screen-on does not resume playback or upload artwork. The earlier missed Skip/brightness test remains unconfirmed.

This finding is separate from accepted flashing defect #52. The owner explicitly accepted screen-on returning random GIFs while the player stays paused as a known limitation for #12, and authorized one explicit Resume to reload the retained content. This resolves the screen-retention continuation decision. The observed loss of uploaded content remains recorded; automatic artwork restoration is not added. Device disconnect/reconnect, variable timing and soak remain pending, along with final delivery gates.


## Supported-profile controls and recovery complete, September 8, 2026 UTC

The owner confirmed explicit Resume restored blue 30 after the accepted screen-on limitation. The same retained session resumed, with a 223.047 ms backend loading interval. Separate observed brightness checks confirmed dimming at requested 20% and restoration; the device probe reported 100%, screen on.
